In its own reckoning the dragon believed that it ought to swallow the entire human race; but the devil did not know this, because he never began to serve you.

In all that you did with the flood, when you submerged humankind, you showed the ruin of the wandering multitude. For you, holy Divinity, planted a new offspring in Noah, just as the earth, overturned into another condition, produced new juice of wine. Abraham was the first root [Col. 0239C] which flowered in the branches of his race, as Aaron’s rod, cut from the root, put forth leaves (Num. XVII). In it you prefigured the Incarnation of your Only-Begotten, who flowered in the chaste womb of the Virgin through your power, holy Divinity, without any fleshly conception.

O pure Divinity, you observed the malicious hearing of the first woman, deceived through the serpent; and you caused the most noble rod, Mary, to flower through your power. She received the archangel’s message with the hearing of true humility and obeyed you in true faith (Luke I). You raised her, your unique mother of another nature, above the stars into heaven, where Eve had not come. Those things which Eve lost for us have through the mother of salvation been restored and reserved for us, together with all the adornments of paradise.

Now, O praiseworthy Divinity, let praise be to you, because [Col. 0239D] you repaired every malicious thing in humanity, and in your knowledge wrote how you would overcome your enemy. To proclaim this Scripture you chose men, among whom these were foremost. In them you showed that all the evils of Adam’s fall were to be restored for the better through your Son, just as after the flood the earth and human beings were renewed for the better by a certain newness, and as disobedience was erased through obedience in Abraham.

Abraham was the root of beginning holiness: through obedience he kept God’s command and offered to almighty God a sacrifice of good will. Therefore he is deservedly called the father of many nations (Gen. XVII), because by these things—namely obedience and the observance of God’s commands—he touched and marked you, holy Divinity. Thus noble Mary also proceeded from his stock, [Col. 0240A] and bore the noble shoot, the Son of God, who illumined the whole world and crushed the serpent’s head.

O gentle Wisdom, whose ordering in all your creatures is just and true, save that person who has seen and heard this Scripture, and make him a chief in the redemption of your Son, so that he may never be separated from the number of those who rejoice in your kingdom. Deliver me from every deceit of evil spirits, who hate me together with all humankind, lest, by consenting to them, I become defiled. May you grant this to me through holy Mary, star of the sea, and through your Son. Amen.

Divine Deity, who fly with the other powers of your might upon the wings of the winds (Ps. XVII), whose lifting and flight exist through your power: through your strength rationality flies in angels and human beings, who are your work. And you are Wisdom, who gives knowledge to their rationality, so that they may recognize what sort of works theirs are, and, like the wise man, build their house upon the rock, namely Christ. Human rationality, together with wisdom, digs deeply into the earth so that it may build its house upon the rock (Matt. VII). Hence whoever flies with wisdom toward the heavenly love of the eternal God despises the vain way of living in sins.

But the weary and foolish person, who is weary of digging the earth deeply and founding a house upon the rock, cultivates the desires of his flesh and will be mocked. You, pure Divinity, [Col. 0240C] preserved Moses, drawn from the waters, whom Pharaoh’s daughter reared as her own son, so that he might not be choked by death (Exod. II).

Water pertains to the Holy Spirit, because through it every fornication and form is emptied out; moisture belongs to it, because all things are tempered, just as fire also tempers all things by its mastery. Wisdom is joined to rationality, and the body is the garment of that rationality. O holy Divinity, by these three powers you completed all your work in that unity in which there is no division and none of them unjustly excels another. But you are all in all (I Cor. XV). In the possibility of your power you multiplied your creature, which has many senses in one form.

You also foresaw your Incarnation in the vision of the ancient saints and in the saints of the New Testament, [Col. 0240D] who are present to it, as you acted through the cloud in Noah, through the ram in Abraham, and in Moses, whom you drew from the waters. In him you wrote your legal foundation, and in your wonders you performed hidden mysteries and miracles unknown to human beings. For by the key of the clouds you poured out the waters; through circumcision you showed Abraham’s baptism, whose binding you sanctified through Moses, whom Pharaoh’s daughter preserved after drawing him from the waters.

Pharaoh’s daughter signifies the Church, which, having come from Gentiles who worshipped idols, was converted to God through the washing of baptism and the anointing of the Holy Spirit—to whom water especially pertains. You foresaw future miracles in Moses, who led the Israelite people by a fiery pillar at night [Col. 0241A] and divided the Red Sea (Exod. XIV). Through what it signifies, the devil, with all his followers, was drowned. But the rod by which he caused the divided waters to flow together signifies the legal correction by which he established the first full number; he shall complete this through his Son.

For the Church suffers many persecutions through the burning of vices, just as Israel endured many disturbances in the wilderness while murmuring against God. To Moses, who saw the bush burn without being burned (Exod. III), you announced that the Israelite people would be saved. That fire signified that the Virgin, through the Holy Spirit and without any union with a man, would bear your Son, through whom you sanctified in the waters the Israelite people whom you planted in Abraham.

You also showed your back to Moses, your most devoted [Col. 0241B] friend, when he desired to see your face (Exod. XXIV). This shows that your eternity cannot be seen by a living human being upon this earth, except insofar as it is known in faith. For he received your secret miracles more fully in human understanding than other human beings; hence he too was terrified and shaken, and people do not know what you did with his body.

O holy Divinity, praise to you in all the works which you performed in these three pillars, and for all the miracles which you shall perform for the last human being. For through the Holy Spirit, in these three men all the other prophets have been given wings and fly with them. Now preserve the great and the small who have written from your Spirit, and me, a little one, who have laboured on this writing from the breath of your Spirit. Joshua made Moses’ flying wings, because he received wings from him. Abraham likewise, after Noah, inspired by the Holy Spirit, brought forth the new law (Gen. XVII), namely circumcision; and the entire philosophy of the prophets sprang and was generated from him alone.

God also, when he created heaven and earth, adorned heaven with heavenly signs, earth with plants and beasts, and finally created the human being (Gen. I), marked by every creature and capable of understanding every kind of knowledge.

All the miracles before Jesus—namely, those through the sign of circumcision—and every prophecy of the prophets, were all fulfilled and established in him, because a new human being came into the world in another nature. For God sent him into unploughed earth and earth not overturned by a plough, in which he, the most noble flower, grew and gave the sweetest fragrance to the whole world, just as noble flowers grow in unploughed earth.

In his flowering a new world came forth in likeness, as God said to Adam: “Increase and multiply, and fill the earth” (Gen. I). But because that shoot perished through the deception of the ancient serpent, so that it did not proceed in its first beginning, afterwards the Son of God choked the death of the first human being and planted great clusters in the new vineyard. They gave the best wine, from which all were made drunk with great joy.

This vineyard signifies the faith which flowed from the Word, namely the Son of God, whose procession the whole world [Col. 0242A] could not recount. The finest wine of the clusters signifies his sweetest teaching, by which he taught people in parables. For divine mysteries are not to be seen by a race darkened through the serpent’s counsel, except as a human face shines in a mirror, though it is not itself in the mirror. For how could life be seen by a mortal human being?

He spoke obscure words to people, namely parables, because those conceived in sins could not otherwise receive the words of life. The Son of God, who is divine life, came into the world, which is the tabernacle of the human being deceived by the harmful apple, in order to call that person back to life by the words of his teaching—the person whom he saw in a human form that veiled his divinity.

The fountain of power, whose divinity no one can behold, is almighty God. In his foreknowledge he predestined that his Son would be incarnate from the human being whom he created in his own image and likeness, so that through that Son’s holy humanity lost humanity might be delivered from eternal death, from which it could in no other way be freed.

For the Son of God, the one life existing without beginning or end, raised mortal humanity to life and resurrected it from eternal death. He created humanity in two natures: from earthly matter, whence it experiences sins; and from a soul, through which it understands almighty and invisible God, who is the highest mountain, to which no creature can ascend. Therefore it was fitting that he from whom all creation descends and moves should free humanity through his Son—God, that is, and human being—so that [Col. 0242C] the empty angelic choir might be filled through him.

For God established heaven and earth, as Moses, inspired by the Holy Spirit, wrote. He designated this in the earthen vessel, namely the human being, whom the devil did not fully recognize as one established in God’s miracles, just as divinity was hidden and concealed in humanity. For if he had known him perfectly, he would never have undertaken to deceive him.

Indeed, even before his own fall the devil never saw him, because he was blind through lack of charity, which exists in all things like soul and eye. He perceived that Jesus Christ was without sin, and perceived in him the works through which humankind rises to life. Therefore, remembering the first human being whom he had deceived, he wished also to deceive him after he had been tempted, and, so that his memory might be erased, he labours in every way, though in vain.

But when he saw himself defeated, he was altogether terrified and ashamed; yet he trusts in his wickedness that through Antichrist he must put God to shame in his work. For from the strong vein of the first deception he trusts that he can accomplish in an earthly human being what he could not accomplish in inextinguishable light. Job, who was overwhelmed in his suffering, understood this in his prophecy when he said: “The devil has confidence that Jordan may flow into his mouth” (Job XL).

For he especially hates fire and water, because all creatures are strengthened and animated through them. But the fire in which he burns according to his impiety lacks all light; he is also devoid of all greenness, and therefore has no share in light and moisture. The most noble flower of Aaron’s rod choked death through fire in its flower and in water; from it sprang the flowering of holiness and heavenly virtues. For it is the noble shoot that descended from the high mountain, and it also planted a new race.

The prophetic words which sounded in the shadow of report then appeared in formed reality, when the Son of God descended from the high mountain, namely from his Father’s heart, to put on humanity. He called every creature and placed it in the cavern of his nature, because it was fitting for him, clothed in new humanity, to clothe human beings with the new holiness of heavenly virtues.

For, according to John, they “were born not of bloods, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of [Col. 0243B] God” (John I). For as the virgin Mary, contrary to nature, bore God and human being, so these people, contrary to the nature of fleshly concupiscence, by imitating him were born into the new holiness which they drew from him.

The Son of God, like a good and wise gardener, gathers good herbs, perfect and suited to the use of each: that is, good and perfect human beings, who were like good grass in good soil because they heard him and, hearing his words, willingly obeyed his commands in faith and charity. He also chose the twelve apostles (Matt. X), corresponding to the number of the twelve prophets, who were Christ’s shadow, as a shadow displays a body.

## EPISTLE XLVIII

### PHILIP, DEAN, AND THE CLERGY OF COLOGNE TO HILDEGARD

They request her prayers. They ask her to commit to writing and send them what she had previously told them orally.

[Col. 0243C]

PHILIP, dean, although most unworthy, of the greater church, and the entire clergy of Cologne, to HILDEGARD of Saint Robert in *Pinguia*, venerable follower of that portion which Mary chose (Luke X), and now able through purity of heart, and hereafter face to face, to behold God.

Because we love your maternal compassion, we make known to you that, after you departed from us—when by divine command you had come to us and opened to us words of life as God inspired you [Col. 0243D]—we were led into the greatest admiration because God accomplishes such wondrous secrets of his in so fragile a vessel, in so frail a sex of humanity. But “the Spirit breathes where it wills” (John III).

For from many indications it becomes evident that he has chosen a dwelling pleasing to himself in your inmost heart. Rightly, therefore, we too approach you in our admiration as if to the living temple of God, to offer prayers; and from your heart, truly as from God’s oracle, we request answers of truth.

We most earnestly beseech your blessedness to commend our desires to God more intently, since they concern the care of souls. And if, while adhering to God, your mind should, as is its custom, perceive anything concerning us in a true vision, may you take care to disclose it to us in writing [Col. 0244A]. We also ask that you commit to writing and send us those things which you previously told us orally. For, while we are devoted to carnal desires, we easily through negligence consign to oblivion spiritual things which we neither see nor hear.

May your love prosper, and may he whom you love with your whole heart be with you.

### HILDEGARD’S REPLY

In very grave words and in God’s name she rebukes the clergy’s negligence in the care of souls and their other vices; she gives many admonitions and also intermingles many predictions.

“He who was, and who is, and who is to come” (Rev. I) says to the shepherds of the Church:

He who was was about to make the creature, so that he held the testimony of testimonies in himself, making all his works as he willed. For he who made every creature showed the testimony of testimonies in all his works, so that each of the forms appeared. He who is to come shall purge all things and repeat them anew in another alternation; he shall wipe away every wrinkle of times and seasons, make all things new together, and after the purification show things unknown.

From him the wind blew, saying: “I established the firmament with all its adornments, lacking no power. It has eyes, as if for seeing; ears, for hearing; nostrils, for smelling; and a mouth, for tasting. For the sun is like the light of its eyes; the wind, the hearing of its ears; the air, its fragrance; the dew, its taste, sweating forth greenness as [Col. 0244C] the breath of its mouth. The moon gives the periods of times and thus displays knowledge to human beings. The stars too are as though rational, because they have a circuit; and rationality likewise comprehends many things.

“I established the four corners of the world by fire, cloud, and water, and thus joined all the boundaries of the earth as veins. I poured forth stones from fire and water as bones, and made the earth from moisture and greenness as marrow. I stretched out the abysses in a fixed arrangement, as those which support a body; around them are sweating waters for their firmament. Thus all things have been established so that they do not fail. If clouds did not have fire and water, they would be like ashes. But if the other luminaries did not have light from the fire of the sun, they would not flash through the waters, [Col. 0244D] but would be blind.

“These too are instruments for the building-up of humanity, which humanity grasps by touching, kissing, and embracing, when they minister to it—by touching, namely, because it exercises noble power with them. And a human being would have no licence of capacity if these were not with him. Thus these are with humanity and humanity with them.

“O little sons, you who pasture my flocks: why, at the pressing instruction of the Lord’s speaking voice, are you not ashamed, when other creatures do not abandon but fulfil the commands which they have from their master? I established you like the sun and the other luminaries, that you might shine for human beings, flashing with the fire of teaching in good report and preparing burning hearts.

“I did this in the first age of the world. For I chose Abel, loved Noah, showed myself to Abraham [Col. 0245A] (Gen. IV, VI, XII), instructed Moses for the institution of the law, and appointed the prophets as my most beloved friends (Exod. III, IV, V). Thus Abel prefigured the priesthood, Noah the chief teaching office, Abraham the renewal of offspring, Moses the royal message, and the prophets many ministries.

“But Abel, like the moon, poured out his radiance because he showed the time of obedience in his offering; Noah was like the sun because he completed the structure of obedience; Abraham was like the strong planets when he brought circumcision; Moses was like the other stars when through obedience he gathered the law; and the prophets, like the four corners supporting the bounds of the earth, stood firm in strength when they rebuked the world because of its pressing wickedness, and thereby showed God.

“But your tongues are mute amid the crying voice of the Lord’s sounding trumpet, since you do not love holy rationality, which, like the stars, has the circle of its orbit. The Lord’s trumpet is God’s justice, which you ought to ponder with great zeal, repeating it to the peoples in the official law and obedience, with holy discernment and at fitting times, and not driving it into them excessively. But you do not do this because of the obstinacy of your own will.

“Therefore the luminaries are absent from your tongues in the firmament of God’s justice, as when stars do not shine. For you are night breathing darkness, and like a people neither labouring nor walking in the light because of weariness. Rather, as a naked serpent hides itself in a cave, so you enter into filth among the baseness of beasts. [Col. 0245C]

“Ah, ah! You ought to be what was said: ‘Mount Zion, wherein you dwelt’ (Ps. LXXIII). For, blessed and marked among heavenly persons, you ought to have been a dwelling-place fragrant with myrrh and incense, in which God himself might dwell. But you are not this. Instead you are swift toward the wantonness of childish age, namely of those who do not know how to speak of their salvation. You also do whatever your flesh demands.

“Therefore it is said of you: ‘Lift up your hands against their pride unto the end: how greatly has the enemy acted wickedly in the sanctuary!’ (ibid.). For the power of God shall cast down your necks raised in iniquity, and shall bring to nothing those things puffed up as in a blast of wind, since you do not know God, do not fear humankind, and do not despise iniquity so as to desire it to end within you. You do not see God, nor do you desire to see him. Rather, you regard your own works and judge them in yourselves, doing and leaving undone whatever you please according to your own will.

“O how great is this malice and enmity: that a human being wishes to live in no good conduct either for God’s sake or for another human being’s, but desires honour without labour and eternal rewards without abstinence, and wishes only to make an empty sound as though in holiness, according to what the devil says: ‘I am good and holy.’ But he is not.

“What do you now say? You have no eyes, since your works do not shine before human beings in the fire of the Holy Spirit and since you do not ponder good examples for them. Therefore the firmament of God’s justice in you lacks the sun’s light, and the air lacks the sweet fragrance of the edifice of virtues. Hence it was said: ‘They have eyes and shall not see; they have nostrils and shall not smell’ (Ps. CXIII).

“For as winds blow and suffuse the whole world, so you ought to be swift winds to the whole people with your teaching, as it was said: ‘Their sound has gone forth into all the earth’ (Ps. XVIII). But in every flying worldly reputation you are already wearied, so that at times you are soldiers, at times servants, at times mocking singers; yet by your fabled offices you sometimes drive away flies in summer.

“Through the teaching of the Scriptures, which were composed from the fire of the Holy Spirit, you ought to be the corners of the Church’s strength, supporting it as the corners support the ends of the earth. But you have fallen down and do not hold the Church; [Col. 0246B] rather, you flee into the cave of your pleasure. Because of weariness from riches, avarice, and other vanities, you do not instruct those subject to you, nor do you allow them to seek teaching from you, saying: ‘We cannot work out everything.’

“For you ought to suffuse and bind them by the commands of the law, lest any one of them through weakness should do, as through marrow, what he chooses for himself—just as the earth is suffused and bound by moisture and greenness lest it become ash. But because of you they are scattered and do what they wish in every matter. You ought to be a fiery pillar, leading them, crying out to them, performing good works before them, and saying: ‘Lay hold of discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry and you perish from the right way’ (Ps. II).

“For the Lord’s law is full of discipline through love and fear; and therefore every nature, spiritual and fleshly alike, must be exercised in the straight path, lest the Creator threaten those whom he created because they do not walk in his ways. But you deceive yourselves, saying: ‘We cannot overcome either these people or those.’ Yet if, through the rationality which God gave you, you truly rebuked those subject to you, they would not dare resist the truth, but would say that your words were true to the extent of their ability.

“But because you do not do this, it is said of you: ‘They were troubled and moved as a drunken man, and all their wisdom was swallowed up’ (Ps. CVI). This is what it means: you are troubled when you possess no regard for the good within yourselves by which you may walk rightly. You are also moved in great uncertainty when your works give you no right answer, as though you did not know what you are doing—like a drunkard when you do those things which the choice of your mind and your own will desire. Therefore all the wisdom which you have sought everywhere from Scriptures and teaching has been swallowed up in the well of your own will, when you did in your full desires and in the fatness of your flesh what you knew by touching and tasting, like a child who in childhood does not know what he is doing.

“Therefore it is said to you: ‘You do not have moral conduct for the people in right firmness, as feet support the rest of the body, so that you might surround them with Scriptures, as the abyss is surrounded on every side by sweating waters.’ But you say: ‘We do not now have time to speak, nor is this now a time when we are heard, as it was in earlier times.’

“But I say: Abel, because of his brother’s hatred, did not abandon his offering, but offered it to his Lord, although on account of it he was killed (Gen. IV). Noah, distressed amid the fearful judgment of the suffocation of creatures, poured forth much sweat when he greatly feared death, yet there fulfilled God’s commands (Gen. VI). Certain other people said: ‘What is this fool doing? The winds will destroy him.’ Yet he fulfilled what the Lord had commanded him.

“Abraham neither because of his heart’s pain nor because of love for his son ceased from binding that same son as a burnt offering (Gen. XXII). Moses also, the lawgiver, suffered hard and bitter things in great anguish from his brothers and neighbours; nevertheless, he did not forsake the law but fulfilled God’s commands. The prophets too were killed by unbelieving people, as by ravening wolves, while obeying God.

“But you do not wish to endure injuries from the people during a brief and suitable time, and therefore gather innumerable and endless torments into your bosom. You ought to be day, but you are night. For you will be either night or day. Choose for yourselves in which part you wish to stand. Yet in the firmament of God’s justice and law you are neither sun nor moon nor stars, but darkness, in which you lie as dead.

“Therefore I say again: God sets before those who turn away from him the works which he himself has made, because they do not rightly bear sheaves of good fruits. Just as a father shows his children his works of integrity when they depart from him, where they do not walk well in honourableness.

“Adam received God’s command in good will, but failed through the devil’s counsel. Hence he lost the brightness which he had as a shining garment and the inheritance of paradise, put on a lamentable garment, and went into the dark earth. Then the devil rejoiced because he had mocked humanity; and he did this until Abel, who loved God with good will and showed that will by good work. But there the devil attacked Cain, so that he killed his brother (Gen. IV).

“God looked upon these things written in his mind as in a book; mysteries which the devil did not know, because they appeared only in holy divinity. For virginity was adorned in Abel by priestly office and the blood of martyrdom; and this was afterwards wholly fulfilled in the Son of God.

“Then through Noah, in the building of the ark, God prefigured the heavenly foundation, where he brought forth a new world. Then the earth gave new juice, namely wine, in which are death and life. There also the devil persuaded Noah’s son to dishonour his father because of his nakedness (Gen. IX); hence that same son, stripped of the blessing of freedom, was made a slave as well (Gen. XVII).

“Afterwards Divinity displayed in Abraham, through circumcision and true manifestation, the walls of that same foundation, and also in the barren woman. For circumcision was the serpent’s confusion and death’s wound. The first woman too was barren of life; but the Church was a fruitful vine through faith. [Col. 0248A]

“But in certain persons among Abraham’s race the devil wrought, with the curse, mockery through homicide and other wicked deeds; hence they fell from God’s blessing. Yet God’s finger wrote Moses’ law, where it raised high the towers of the aforesaid foundation. Therefore the same devil there openly displayed the worst and supreme evil which he had previously devised, when he declared himself to be God in Baal. Hence God struck the children of Israel with many plagues (III Kings XVIII).

“Then the unicorn came and slept in the Virgin’s womb, when the Word of God was made flesh (John I), and wholly completed the heavenly foundation. For in virginal nature he was fully made the sacrifice of Abel through the blood of martyrdom.

“The ancient serpent lay in wait for him because it did not know who he was, and because [Col. 0248B] it did not know those mysteries which were in God’s mind. It urged the Jewish people not to listen to him in his wonders, but to seize him when he had been sold by his disciple. Therefore they themselves were sold into diverse regions and lost their own land.

“But the Son of God placed the Church like Noah’s ark upon the other high mountains when, through his disciples, princes, leaders, and kings, he taught the faith. There he also filled it with all kinds: namely, just persons, tax collectors, and sinners. He likewise began obedience in Abraham when, incarnate, he obeyed his Father unto death (Phil. II); and in circumcision he gave baptism in the name of the holy Trinity, when he commanded his disciples to baptize believers (Matt. XXVIII).

“In that same baptism [Col. 0248C] the serpent was choked in confusion, and death was conquered and wounded. Hence the Church bore a new generation by another way, because Eve was barren of life, while Mary bestowed greater grace than Eve had inflicted harm.

But the ancient serpent persuaded the Jews and unbelieving people to persecute and kill God’s saints. Yet the Son of God bore the banner of victory in all his works, and, as he gave Moses the Law, so he gave his disciples the Law: that they should teach all peoples, appoint teachers, and adorn the Church in all its orders. They accomplished this through the inspiration of God’s Spirit, who wrote true teaching in their hearts. And because the Word of God had become incarnate, it pleased God that all the orders of angels, [Col. 0248D] known to human beings by their names, should be spiritually signified in the spiritual people, as in priests and bishops and the other such spiritual orders.

Then the Church appeared in spiritual persons like the dawn, and shone so brightly in virtues because amid their tribulations it possessed defence as a shield and protection as a breastplate. Thus the spiritual people stood in great honour before God and human beings, until a certain tyrant began to be Baal-like, with the bondage of idols. Seeing this, the spiritual people first sighed and trembled. Yet afterwards that same spiritual people adopted singularity and individual self-will in its conduct; it departed from the covenant which it had promised God through the Holy Spirit. And, just as the Jews had done, they abandoned commandment after commandment, one after another; each order made a law for itself according to the desire of its own self-will, and turned away from good conduct and sound teaching.

Then they too were stripped of the garment of obedience, as Adam was, and began to live according to the will of the flesh. They did this in a land of darkness, just as Adam, after his disobedience, was called dark by God. And the Churches, which had previously shone, no longer gave light, but became like the darkening of a storm. So too Adam, clouded because of disobedience, gave light neither to himself nor to others; rather, they walked in darkness.

And again I heard a voice from the living light saying:

“O daughter of Zion, the crown of honour upon the heads of your children shall be bowed down, and the mantle of the abundance of their riches shall be diminished, because they did not recognize the time which I gave them for seeing and for teaching those subject to them. For breasts were also given them to nourish my little ones, but they do not offer them at the right and fitting time. Thus many children, like strangers, have perished from hunger because they are not refreshed by sound teaching. They have a voice, yet do not cry out; works too were given them, yet they do not work. They wish to possess glory without merit, and merit without work. Whoever wishes to have glory with God must cut away his self-will; and whoever desires to possess merit before God must provide the work for it.

“But [Col. 0249C] because you do not do this, you shall be reckoned among the servants of servants; they themselves shall be your judges, and your freedom shall depart from you, as the blessing departed from Canaan. These scourges shall come first; then others shall come, and afterwards still others, worse ones. For the devil says of you within himself: ‘In these I find the food of banqueters and feasts suited to all my desire. My eyes, my ears, my belly, and my veins are filled with the froth of these people; and my breasts are full of their vices. For they refuse to labour in their God, but count him as nothing. Therefore I shall begin to wage war against them and sport with them in play, because I do not find them labouring in the field of their Lord, as their Lord commands them.’

“But, O my disciples and subjects, you are far more disciplined than they before the people. Since you are such, rise up above them; strip from them all their riches and all their honour, and, having wholly despoiled them, suffocate them.”

The devil says these things within himself; and God’s judgment will indeed bring them to fulfilment in many cases. But I, who am, say to those who hear me: In that time, when this happens, ruin shall fall upon you through a certain wandering people, worse than the wandering people now existing—transgressors upon you who transgress—who will persecute you everywhere and will not conceal your deeds. Instead, they will lay them bare and say of you: “These are scorpions in their customs and serpents in their works.” And, as though with zeal for the Lord, they will invoke a curse upon you: “The way of the wicked shall perish” (Psalm 1). For they will deride and mock your ways in your iniquity, to your destruction.

But this people, which will do this, deceived and sent by the devil, will come with a pale face, fashioning itself as if in every holiness, and will join itself to the greater secular princes. To them they will say concerning you: “Why do you keep these people with you? Why do you allow them to remain with you, when they pollute the whole earth by their foul iniquities? For they are drunken and lustful; unless you cast them away from yourselves, the whole Church will be destroyed.”

The people who says this of you will wear cheap cowls of unfamiliar colour; it will walk with a proper tonsure and show itself to human beings gentle and quiet in all its behaviour. It will not love avarice or possess money, and in its hidden practices it will imitate such great abstinence that scarcely any one among them can be reproached. For the devil is with these people, revealing himself to them in a hidden radiance, just as he was in the ordering of the world before his fall. He makes himself somewhat like the prophets and says:

“The people speak jestingly—namely, that I show myself to them as raging and unclean animals and as flies. But now I wish to fly upon the wings of the winds with flashing thunder, and to pour myself into them in every way, so that they may accomplish my whole will. Thus I shall make my signs in these people resemble the signs of almighty God.”

For the devil accomplishes these things through aerial spirits. Because of the wicked deeds of human beings, these spirits move about in the breath of wind and air, innumerable around certain people, like flies and gnats that torment people by their multitude in the heat of summer. Thus he pours himself into these people: he does not take chastity from them, but permits them to be chaste when they wish to possess chastity. And again he says within himself: “God loves chastity and continence; I too shall imitate this in these people.” Thus the same ancient enemy inflates these people through aerial spirits, so that they abstain from incestuous sins. Hence they do not love women, but flee from them. In this way they will display themselves to people as though in every holiness, and with mocking words they will say:

“The other people who before us wished to have chastity roasted themselves like a dried fish. But no pollution of flesh or lust dares touch us, because we are holy and are filled with the Holy Spirit. Alas! The wandering people now living do not know what they are doing, just as those who preceded us in earlier times did not know.”

For other people who at that time stray within the Catholic faith will fear these people, minister to them in servile submission, and imitate them as much as they can. Then the people will rejoice over the way of life of these persons, because they will seem righteous to them.

When these people have thus established the course of their error, they will drive out teachers and wise persons who then remain faithfully in the Catholic faith, pursuing them from every side. Yet they will not drive out all of them, for some of them are most valiant soldiers in God’s righteousness. Nor will they be able to move certain congregations of saints whose conduct is holy. Therefore they will advise princes and the wealthy to restrain these teachers of the Church and the rest of their spiritual people—that is, those subject to them—with rods and clubs, so that they may become righteous. This will be fulfilled in some cases, and others will tremble in fear.

Nevertheless, as was said to Elijah, many righteous people will be preserved; they will not be confounded in these errors nor destroyed from their foundations (3 Kings 19). At the beginning of their deceptive error, however, these seducers will say to women: “You may not be with us. But because you have no upright teachers, obey us; do whatever we tell and command you, and you shall be saved.” In this way they will draw women to themselves and lead them into their error. Hence they themselves, swollen with pride of heart, will say: “We have overcome everyone.” Yet afterwards they will engage those same women in secret lust; thus their iniquity and sect will be exposed.

But I, who am, say: Thus an iniquity which will purge iniquity shall be brought upon you, as it is written: “He made darkness his hiding-place; around him was his tabernacle, dark water in clouds of air” (Psalm 17). For God will appoint your wicked deeds, which are without light, for vengeance; in it he will hide himself from you without aid, because he will not proclaim equity over you, but will declare you wicked. For law and teaching are from heaven, in which they ought to have dwelt among you, had you been an adornment of virtues and a fragrant garden of delights. But you are an evil example in human minds, since no stream of good repute flows from you; so that [Col. 0251C] you have neither food to eat nor clothing to cover yourselves in the proper care of the soul, but unjust works without the good of knowledge. Therefore your honour shall perish and the crown shall fall from your head.

Thus righteousness summons righteousness, seeking and examining every scandal (Matthew 13), as it is written: “Nevertheless, woe to the man through whom scandal comes” (Matthew 18). For the wicked works of human beings must be purged through tribulations and crushing. Yet many hardships are also heaped upon those who inflict miseries upon others in their impiety. These unbelieving people, deceived by the devil, will be your broom for chastising you, because you do not worship God purely; they will torment you until your righteousnesses and iniquities are purged.

These deceivers, however, are not those who will come before the last day, when the devil shall fly aloft, as he began to fight against the Lord in the beginning (Isaiah 14); rather, they are their forerunning shoot. Yet after they have been found in the perversities of Baal and other wicked works, princes and other great persons will rush upon them and kill them like rabid wolves wherever they find them.

Then your dawn of righteousness and your latter state will be better than the former; you will be made fearful by all that has passed, will shine like the purest gold, and will endure thus for a long time. For then the first dawn of righteousness will rise in the spiritual people. As it first began with a small number, so they will not wish to possess many goods or great riches, which kill souls, but will say: “Woe to us, for we have sinned!” (Lamentations 5). For through past fear and past sorrow they will be strengthened toward righteousness, as the angels were strengthened in the love of God by the fall of the devil. Afterwards they will live in humility and will not desire to rebel against God by wicked works. Purified from many errors, they will henceforth persevere in the strongest power of rectitude. Many people will marvel that so fierce a storm preceded this gentleness.

The people who lived before these times endured many fierce struggles against their own wills amid dangers to their bodies, from which they could not free themselves. But in your times you have many restless wars because of your own wills and disordered customs, in which [Col. 0252B] you shall suffer many tribulations.

Therefore, whoever wishes to escape these dangers must beware lest his eyes be so darkened that he is caught in the nets of these hardships. Rather, each person, as far as he is able, should flee them through good works and regard for good will; and God will provide that person with his help.

For the devil brought error into God’s work; he began even in the first human being, and from this he spat the froth of his vices over the spiritual people. But God will preserve in rectitude the people whom he has chosen, just as he preserves certain people against the final error so that they may scatter it. Thus the devil will be confounded in the tail of this error, and will hide in a cave like a serpent, just as he will be brought to confusion in the final error.

For God foresaw his works in Adam, whose flesh and bones he made from clay when he breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 1–2). But when the human spirit departs from him, flesh and bones turn into ashes; nevertheless, they will be renewed on the last day. That God made the human being from clay prefigured the giving of the old Law to humanity. But that this same human being rose from clay into flesh and bones signified the spiritual Law which the Son of God brought through himself. This human being too will be renewed after ashes and will be eternal; in him it will be shown that, with the reward of holiness and the reward of the true Law, he will see the face of the Creator, because there he is truly renewed, as it is written: “Send forth your Spirit, and they shall be created; and you shall renew the face of the earth” (Psalm 103).

This means: You, God, who created all things, will send forth your Spirit at the last trumpet, and human beings will rise in immortality; they will neither grow in that manner nor wither nor be turned into any corruption. Thus you will renew the face of the earth: that is, body and soul will be in one knowledge and one perfection. God will do this—he in whom there is neither beginning nor end. For God looks toward no one, because he himself is complete. He created the human being, in whom he placed his work and miracles, and to whom he entrusted every edifice of virtues, by which the person may tend toward that very thing which God greatly loves, because God is love (1 John 4).

For God acts like a householder who entrusts his goods to a familiar friend so that, for the good work done with those goods, he may receive a reward from him. Now, O children of God, hear and understand what the Spirit of God says to you, lest you perish from the better part. The Spirit of God says to you:

“Look to your city and region, and cast out from yourselves the wicked people who are worse than the Jews and like the Sadducees. For as long as they remain with you, you cannot be safe. The Church weeps and mourns over their iniquity, because her children are defiled by it. Therefore cast them out from yourselves, lest your congregation and city perish. For long ago in Cologne a feast of royal nuptials was prepared, and its streets still flash with lightning.

“But I, a timid and poor little woman, was greatly wearied for two years, that I might utter this message in a living voice before masters, teachers, and other wise persons in certain principal places where they dwell. But because the Church was divided, I withdrew this voice for the present.”

## LETTER XLIX

### The provost of Saint Peter and the whole clergy of Trier to Hildegard

They ask that what she had recently foretold to them during the days of Pentecost be committed to writing and sent to them.

R., a sinner and provost of the greater church of Saint Peter, and the whole clergy of Trier, to HILDEGARD, handmaid of God and knower of very many of his mysteries, living devoutly in the monastery of Blessed Robert: with thanksgiving, hands outstretched in prayer for her.

Since, by divine permission, the thoughts of many hearts are revealed (Luke 2), we love you, by the divine will, with the full striving of our bodies and the whole devotion of our minds. For we know that the Holy Spirit dwells in you (Romans 8), and that through him many things unknown to other people are made manifest to you. Since you departed from us—after you had recently come to us during the days of Pentecost by heavenly dispensation, when you foretold that God’s threat was hanging over us—we have seen and experienced many losses of churches and many dangers to people around us and among us. This happened because we neglected to placate God’s wrath in accordance with the good counsel which you gave us. Unless his vengeance had been withdrawn through God’s mercy, perhaps, with those same dangers impending, we should have succumbed in despair.

And because God is in you and his words sound from your mouth, we most earnestly beseech your motherly love: send to us in writing, through the present bearer, the things which you then disclosed to us in a living voice, so that succeeding posterity may see both God’s vengeance and his mercy directed upon us, and may know that you are a true and beloved knower of his secrets. May the Lord’s protection always remain over you, and may he bring to a good end in you what he has begun.

### Hildegard’s reply

After severely rebuking the negligence of pastors and prelates, she proceeds to predictions of future good and evil.

[Col. 0254A]

I, a poor little figure, who possess in myself neither health nor strength nor might nor learning, but who am subject to masters, heard these words from the mystical light of the true vision, addressed to the prelates and clergy of Trier:

Teachers and masters refuse to sound the trumpet of righteousness; therefore the east of good works, which illumines the whole world and is like a mirror of light, has been extinguished in them. This east ought to shine in them through teaching, which would govern diverse commandments, just as the sphere of the sun is diverse. The south wind of virtues, too, is as cold as winter within them, because they possess no good works kindled from the fiery Holy Spirit and are dry for lack of greenness. The west of mercy has been turned into the blackness of a hair-shirt (Revelation 6), because by living well they do not honour Christ’s Passion—he who descended through humility into humanity and veiled his divinity, just as the sun is sometimes hidden. But the north, with its north wind, works in them, where each turns the breadth of his self-will into punishments for souls, just as haircloth constricts a human body.

For they do not rise with the east through good works, do not burn with the sun’s heat, nor turn away from evils with the west. Instead, with the northern wind they hide themselves in the self-will of their hearts. Therefore the devil truly sends three black winds from the north with playful hissing: the first, with pride and hatred, against the east that has been extinguished; the second, with forgetfulness of God, against the south; the third, with unbelief, against the west. For when teachers and masters rightly walked in imitation of God, the east constrained the north so that it could not even sigh; the south burned it within them by good works; and the west cast down its powers into darkness, when they, following the Lamb, abandoned the world and themselves.

But now the manly strength of fortitude has bent into feminine weakness, which ought not to fight with manly strength, because the man is the head (Ephesians 5). This feminine time began with a certain tyrant, when every evil arose.

In the true vision I have learned that very often any householder, who is the mighty Lord, sets before his children and servants—who displease him because they have transgressed his commandments—his own goodness, power, and ability; then, stretching out his hand with the rod of correction, he bows and scatters them according to their condition, saying: “Whence do you come, and what are you without me?” And I heard concerning the Lord’s zeal that God does not leave the transgression of his commandments unpunished.

For Adam transgressed God’s commandments, lost the vision of heavenly things and his bright garment, and was sent into a place of misery. Through the Lord’s zeal Cain was likewise driven out because he shed the blood of his brother whom he killed (Genesis 4). Very many peoples also arose from Adam’s children, who forgot God so thoroughly that they would not acknowledge themselves to be human; hence, sinning shamefully, they lived according to the habits of beasts—except for the children of God, who separated themselves from those people and their loves, and from whom Noah was born.

Then the Lord’s zeal was raised up; the Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters (Genesis 1), split the clouds, and released the waters in the flood. Thus the earth was cleansed from criminal sins and from Abel’s blood which it had drunk. God did these things. Thus the neck of the ancient serpent’s covetousness was crushed. Then the earth, which had previously been violated by Abel’s blood, produced the new sap of wine, and wisdom began to work again.

But the devil committed wickedness with mockery in Noah’s son. Therefore the Lord’s zeal consigned the sinner to slavery, withdrew blessing from him, and delivered sinners to the curse of slavery. Thus new wisdom worked in heaven and on earth. Afterwards the Holy Trinity displayed a great work in Abraham, prefiguring and showing obedience: when he left his homeland, when he was circumcised, and when in obedience he prefigured those of whom it was said: “Who are these that fly like clouds?” (Isaiah 60). In circumcision he received the wound that brought confusion upon the ancient serpent.

But the woman, with laughter, followed the folly of the first woman; yet in her fruitfulness the Son of God was prefigured. For in Abraham’s obedience God transformed Adam’s transgression; in Abraham’s circumcision he struck death; and in the fruitfulness of the barren woman he foresaw that another woman would bear another son, because the Son of God fulfilled all this prefiguration in his birth.

Moses the lawgiver came as an aid to circumcision and gave the Law, which too was brought about by God. But his people perished in idols and other sins because of their many transgressions of God’s commandments. The Lord’s zeal will work purgations of this kind until the end of the world. Yet God sends forth his vengeance and often foretells it through a human being or some other creature, so that people may have no excuse for their evils. Therefore often many among them arise and do penance, as happened in Jonah. Thus God is praised through his friends and proclaimed through his enemies.

For God often touched the form of his finger in men and women with the aforesaid manifestation, as it is written: “Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy” (Joel 2). After God had prefigured what he wished to do, he remembered what he had said: that he would crush the serpent’s head. He filled a certain woman, namely the Virgin, with obedience, chastity, and every honour; he filled her with every good, so that the pride which was in Eve dried up in her. But this Virgin conceived the Son of God by the Holy Spirit; he came forth wondrously from her and entered the world with miracles.

Then God ceased from that work which he had carried out in so fleshly a manner. And he gave this Son of his the task of recalling all carnal things to spiritual things, because he is the flesh of holiness, which came forth through another nature and which the serpent’s counsel never violated. Therefore the same Son of God watered the old Law when, in baptism, through faith and obedience and abstinence from carnal desires, he showed the way of holiness; when he gave repentance to human beings; when he confirmed all these things in a mortal body by his death; and when he gave his disciples miracles and signs, just as the Father had given them to him.

Then God appeared as a human being. With the thunder of divinity he sent into his disciples a new fire that had never previously appeared, and the disciples were filled with new fiery tongues and new knowledge (Acts 2), which taught human beings to live according to heavenly harmony. Then the east shone in its power, the south burned in its heat, the west was not deadly, and the north with its north wind did not rage, because through Christ’s Passion they were tempered—until a certain tyrant, from whose time every evil, injustice, and transgression arose.

Yet these things were brought low by famine and pestilence, bent down by wars and battles, and purged by the penalties of penance. But now the Law is neglected among the spiritual people, who despise doing and teaching what is good. Masters and prelates too, having abandoned righteousness, sleep. Therefore I heard this voice saying from heaven:

“O daughter of Zion, the crown shall be bowed down from your head, and the mantle of the abundance of your riches shall be diminished for you, reduced to a small number, and you shall be driven from region to region. For through powerful people very many cities and monasteries must be devastated. And princes will say: ‘Let us remove from them the iniquity which overturns the whole world within them.’”

And I saw and heard that these dangers and crushing trials will come upon regions and monasteries because of transgression of obedience and of other commandments established by law. I saw that amid such transgressions some will cling to God and pant after him, as happened in Elijah’s time (3 Kings 18). These will persevere with great honour and be regarded as God’s whole burnt offering, because they withdrew from evils, like Noah and Lot.

This same purification will begin on a small scale in this feminine time, later become greater, and then a manly time will come, in which wars and battles will occur by God’s just judgment. But this feminine time will not last as long as it has endured up to now. Then God’s righteousness and judgments will arise; discipline and the fear of God will be among the people; and righteous and good people will arise in the spiritual people. Yet they will remain few in number because of humility, and will return to the first dawn like hermits. They will do this also out of fear of the former times, which they saw had been hostile to them.

People will not have the folly of wanton manners, like children, but will endure sorrow because of the unknown times that are to come. Then strong men will arise and prophesy; they will gather all things old and new in the Scriptures, and all sayings poured out through the Holy Spirit, and will adorn their meaning like a necklace with precious stones. Through them and other wise persons, very many secular people will become good and live holy lives.

This pursuit of holiness will not quickly wither, but will endure for a long time, because all these things will take place owing to the wandering time, when many will be martyrs in the faith. For the warrior-man will do these things, who considers in them the beginning and end of his works, in order to withstand the wandering people in this matter. For he first established prophets as a head, wise persons as eyes, and teachers as a mouth, just as all things were made through the Word of God. And because the remaining members—that is, the faithful—will afterwards perform good works, God places the head in their bosom: that is, he will open prophecy to their understanding.

Then princes will turn harps and drums into hardship and sorrow, as the children of Israel did when they were taken captive (Psalm 136). After all these things, spiritual matters will be strengthened without weariness or failure, and people will look upon the pupil of the living Book. Then power, strength, and health will arise among the people, because the warrior-man will fill the air with health and bring forth the greenness of virtues, lest the faithful fail in body and soul during the wandering time. This will endure until the wandering time, in which the faithful people will hasten to death as though to a banquet.

But this time will maintain error in this way until God examines it in his grace, mercy, and zeal. In all these matters the gardener will cast useless things out of his garden and gather the useful things to himself, as it is written: “The God of vengeances, the Lord; the God of vengeances has acted freely” (Psalm 93). This means: God in his zeal crushes the head of iniquity, and the Lord throws it down in its fall, because all iniquity is from the devil, who is buried in hell. For he is the God of vengeances, because he looked toward or regarded no one from whom he might take anything to add to himself. Rather, within himself he distributes, establishes, and does every thing; and he acted freely in this manner because he alone is just, good, and to be feared in all his judgments.

For God acts in vengeance against those who perish because they refused the good, and therefore condemns them with the devil. He also freely bows many down through suffering, whom he afterwards raises again, so that through good works they may be like pillars of heaven, just as he made many saints out of tax collectors and sinners. Then the devil, raising himself up in his lost son, wishes to fly upon the wings of the winds. But God disposes within himself what he wills, because no one can overcome him; he scatters all the devil’s power, like a smith who reduces everything useless in his workshop and stretches out his hand in zeal. So he did when he cast that same Satan into the abyss from his first love. Therefore Satan enters his hole like a serpent and hides himself in the abyss; he will rise no more, because he is now wholly deceived.

Afterwards the divinity unknown to every creature will act, because it is unknown to every human being when the purification of the world by fire will occur. And I saw Trier, first among the faithful, greatly adorned with the new fire which appeared to the disciples in fiery tongues (Acts 2), so that all its streets were then spread abroad in golden faith with miracles. But now, surrounded by the wandering of squalid customs with weariness, as though it did not know God, and defiled with many other evils, it has grown old in weariness and the failure of the joy and beauty of its chief and honourable institutions, and has declined into forgetfulness of many sins. Therefore fiery vengeances shall come upon them from enemies unless they are erased through repentance, as happened in Jonah (Jonah 2–3).

## LETTER L

[Col. 0258B]

### The dean of the Church of the Holy Apostles at Cologne, chief master of the schools, to Hildegard

Concerning a demon-possessed woman delivered by Hildegard.

T., by God’s grace called dean and chief master of the schools of the Church of the Holy Apostles at Cologne, together with all the brethren of that church, to Lady HILDEGARD and all those serving Christ on the Mount of Saint Robert: devoted prayer in the Lord, and salvation in the true Saviour.

From the day it became known to us that you had admitted our sister—or rather our special daughter—Lady Sigewiz into the fellowship of your blessed community, not only we, but indeed the whole city of Cologne, have by God’s prompting been inflamed with love of devotion. Hence it is now openly proclaimed by all throughout every region of our land: “Behold, the fragrance of the ladies of Saint Robert is like the fragrance of a full field which the Lord has blessed” (Genesis 27).

Blessed therefore are you by the Lord, who on your small and humble hill have performed works of mercy which, we do not say, all the heights of our mountains and all the expanses of our valleys have been unable to perform, but rather have neglected. For we have heard very recently, as report tells, that the ancient enemy was cast out through your prayers. If this is so, we beseech you to inform us in writing of the manner and order of that expulsion, so that we may rejoice with you and praise God with you in perpetual devotion.

We also greet Lady Sigewiz with special affection, as we know her more familiarly, renewing the devoted prayers promised in Christ and awaiting the same from her. Farewell.

### Hildegard’s reply

She replies most humbly, attributing the expulsion of the demon to the combined good works of many. She treats of how God directs the various good works of different people to one end.

God made his work, but he did not establish it in one uniform manner. For Adam perished, since he did not complete the course of his circuit. Yet he was sought after noon. But God sent his breath into the prophets, that they might proclaim the truth; and thus Wisdom spoke in the mouths of those whom she herself established, so that they might bring forth miracles. The apostles too, through the Holy Spirit, carried God’s work onward in faith. Their martyrdom, and that of others, showed God; and the Holy Spirit also inspired the spiritual people, who bring the world to an end in themselves and cultivate the angelic order—if God’s work is like a day. For all spoke one thing, yet each cried out individually.

For at the rising of day dawn precedes the sun; in the morning the sun’s ray shines forth; at the third hour it burns fully in its heat; about the ninth it declines in heat; and toward evening it ends the heat which it had during the day and hides itself before night. Thus the day is completed and rests from its works. If these things were completed in one manner, they would displease humankind. Hence God also bears the name Sabaoth, because every course of this world has its full office.

[Col. 0259B] God works in this manner in all his works. Thus it also happened in the case of this woman about whom you inquire. For her, the high and higher, the small and smaller, with labours and prayers, spoke one thing and cried out individually, according as the Holy Spirit taught them this office. Some laboured for her through sighs of mercy; others through prayers and vigils; some also endured fasts and bodily discipline; many moreover gave alms for her; and a great multitude, with the help of every good thing that each could do, bent itself toward her. Some accomplished this with great zeal and without weariness. Thus all together looked to God on her behalf, just as the day completes its circuit.

Now let us say together in praise: “Glory to you, Lord.” May God’s blessing in his grace be upon you and upon all who were moved by mercy toward her; for the Lord himself says: “I desire mercy and not sacrifice” (Hos. VI; Matt. IX; XII).

## LETTER LI

### MEFFRID, PRIOR OF EBERBACH, TO HILDEGARD

They request the prayers of the holy woman and the letter which, they had heard, she had written “about those converted from secular life to the spiritual way of life—whom we call conversi.”

To the God-beloved, God-chosen, venerable lady HILDEGARD: M., prior, and the whole congregation of brothers at Eberbach, everlasting enjoyment of delights in the chamber of the supreme King.

[Col. 0259D] Having often heard the fragrant and most sweet report, worthy of God, of your holiness, we who are idle and unworthy have rejoiced with ineffable joy of spirit because almighty God, in grace and mercy, has bestowed upon you such wondrous gifts of his generosity. For it is clearer than light that the Lord loves you among those human beings who love him, since you are so worthy, so welcome, so lovable, so venerable to all those in whom he dwells that no one can doubt that he is in you and remains with you.

And to one upon whom such great benefits of virtues have been bestowed, we do not doubt that the gifts of holy mercy also dwell in you, and that the bowels of devout charity and devout compassion are not lacking.

[Col. 0260A] Therefore we humbly entreat the abundance of your mercy: since the Lord was born in the flesh from blessed Mary ever-virgin in order to redeem and save sinners, have mercy upon us for the love of that same almighty Lord, our Creator and most merciful Redeemer, and deign to make us sharers in your prayers.

Moreover, we earnestly ask that you do not hesitate graciously to send us the letter which, as we have heard, you wrote by the Holy Spirit concerning persons from secular life and without learning who have been converted to the spiritual way of life, whom we call conversi. Thus may we see in them God’s wondrous works and his will, and, so far as we can, follow and fulfil these things with the whole affection of good works. Farewell.

### HILDEGARD’S REPLY TO THE MONKS OF CRISEOS  
[Note: [Col. 0259D] That is, the Cistercians.]

Hildegard praises the Cistercian order, but reproves those “whom they themselves call conversi, many of whom do not turn themselves toward God in their conduct.” She adds further instruction.

[Col. 0260B]

I, a little poor woman, having lain in a bed of sickness for more than two years, saw these things and heard a voice from heaven speaking to me thus: “Write to the spiritual people, whom God in his foreknowledge, with miracles of prophecy, foreknew according to his good pleasure, what you see and hear, beginning in this manner:

God prefigured through four creatures of God’s hidden mysteries certain virtuous works which he performed in his saints and elect. Through these creatures and through other miracles he makes his hidden mysteries known to humankind, just as he showed Ezekiel the prophet and John his beloved through these same creatures (Ezek. I) that he wished the spiritual people to be separated and gathered from the common people.

For John says: ‘In the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes before and behind’ (Rev. IV). What is said? Within the strength of God’s power—he who is God and man—and in every region to which his power extends, faithful persons instructed by the four Evangelists ought to be meditating upon God’s commandments and possess the fullness of the watchfulness of virtues, so that they may see whence they came into being and also what they shall become.

For God is fire (Deut. IV), and the angels, who are burning spirits, often announce his miracles and the wonders of his throne to human beings (Heb. I). They shine before his face and burn so in his love that they will nothing but what he wills. Of them it is said: ‘You make your angels spirits, and your ministers a burning fire’ (Ps. CIII).

[Col. 0260D] What is said? Almighty One, you are he who makes your messengers—namely, those sent by you for the salvation of humankind—spirits with a sending forth; while they rest in unfailing life before your sight, they are again spirits, your messengers, when they become messengers for the fulfilment of your commands. For angels are messengers because they report to God every inspiration of that breath which God sent into the human being (Gen. II). In this way they perform offices on account of human beings: because of their works they gather and discern; and because of human works which are wrought through the Spirit, they too are called spirits and angels, since they are often sent by the heavenly ruler to carry out his judgments.

But you make your ministers, who serve your will everywhere, a burning fire when they burn in your love; and in that ardour they again minister to you with unwearied praise. For God’s ministers, who always behold his face, shine like flame; and in that radiance they see his miracles, recognize them in wonder and praise, and therefore are also a burning fire (Deut. IV). Through God, who is fire, they burn; they can neither be kindled nor extinguished by another. Rather, they burn unquenchably in his love, because he, clothed in the mantle of humanity, always leads them into wondrous miracles.

[Col. 0261B] For God girded himself with the mantle of his strength (Ps. XCI), through which he established the human being as a mirror of his honour and miracles, so that the human being might fight against the devil and overcome him, and thus always continue in divine praise.

In the same way God makes those who are his messengers, proclaiming words of salvation to the children of the Church, into spirits when he commands them to resist their flesh and serve the spirit. Having made them spiritual in this way with their whole heart, he then trains them to reveal his commandments to the people with so much greater confidence. He also causes those who labour for him day and night in service to burn in his love and thus to be a burning fire; and, having become fire, they again sweat at his service without weariness.

For in his foreknowledge God had preordained that he would significantly work in human beings also the miracles and secrets that are in angels. Hence he made angels speak to human beings, as happened with Abraham and Jacob, just as Balaam’s ass also spoke (Num. XXII). He covers, as it were with a garment, the angelic spirits who minister to him, praising and honouring his face, with his hidden things; and therefore they too are called a burning fire.

[Col. 0261C] Through these fiery ministers, covered as with a garment by God’s secrets, hermits are signified: denying themselves, they live as though they were not human beings and flee human companionship. For through his work, which is the human being, God performs great wonders, which he predestined in angelic spirits and which flash before him with praise and wondrous honour.

But, as was said above, “around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes before and behind” (Rev. IV). This means all the holy works which God performs in those people who look to him and to his throne: east through faith; south through hope; west through remembrance of the Fall which occurred in the first parent, as though looking backward; and north through directing their eyes ahead with forethought, lest the warrior of the north bring them down by the falling sickness of pride and the burning flame of unchastity.

Therefore, with these eyes which they have on every side, they ought to pant after God, lest they be extinguished from faith, separated from the light, and so draw near to the north that they are choked by eternal death. This indeed is what “around the throne” means: east, south, and west show God; but the north, wholly overcome by him, is subjected to him as the footstool of his feet.

[Col. 0262A] Then it is written: ‘The first living creature was like a lion, the second like a calf, the third had as it were the face of a human being, and the fourth was like a flying eagle’ (Rev. IV). What is said?

This first creature signifies hooded men, who first, in the strength of the lion, withdraw themselves altogether from the world. Hence they are also likened to those fiery beings who are covered as with a garment by God’s hidden things and who always behold God’s face. Their clothing is not from the world, but wondrously from God, as God ordained in those who first brought it forth by showing and teaching it.

For their cowl was prefigured by the angelic spirits, who look upon God’s face and not upon another; and its width extends in the likeness of a cloud, because angels have often appeared in clouds, and because Adam’s garment of innocence was like a bright cloud. Thus these men cover their heads with the cowl, lest, turning to the left or to the right, they fail to walk straight ahead in the impulse of the spirit, always looking upon God and not turning back from good works.

[Col. 0262C] All this ought to be done in the obedience which the Son of Man showed through himself, so that the commands of masters may be kept in the fear of God; and so that, just as a person fears to perish at the sound of thunder, so also he may fear sins. For as the lion surpasses other beasts in strength, so these surpass other people in the most powerful force of divinity, because, though they are human beings, they do not live as human beings do.

For when a person, renouncing the world, offers himself to God, he condemns the world, so that it is in all things useless to him, and thus raises his mind, as Daniel says: ‘I was watching in the visions of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a Son of Man was coming, and he came unto the Ancient of Days’ (Dan. VII).

What is said? When I raised my mind upward to heavenly things, I saw, in the contemplation of very many adversities, that all the heavenly and divine miracles which God worked in angelic spirits were prefigured by him through his Son in human beings. Thus that same Son came unto the Ancient of Days, because the Son of God is God and man; and thus God and man are one God. For God is man, and this man is God. The good works of human beings and the praises of angels are also joined together and are one in God.

[Col. 0262D] To these hooded men is joined a multitude of virgins, who leave behind husband, love, riches, and the whole world. For just as a virgin ought to be removed from worldly delights lest she suck the breasts of pleasure, so too the hooded multitude ought to be separated from the world, lest it carry on any secular business with it. And the virgin is left by her husband, so that she is not under his care and power but is free from him; so too the monk, having left the world, ought not to be subjected to it but should remain free from it.

Virginity also signifies the sun, which illumines the whole world, because God joined virginity to himself; leaving a husband, it bore him whom the ray of divinity flooded and who rules all things. For the king who rules all things is God; and that virginity was united with him when God and man was born from the Virgin. Thus “the queen stood at his right hand in clothing of gold, surrounded by variety” (Ps. XLIV), because virginity, resisting the devil, stood beside the power of divinity in a shining work, encompassed everywhere by a multitude of diverse virtues.

[Col. 0263A] Divinity betrothed virginity to itself when the first angel fell to the left, and then also chose for itself in Adam the people of salvation, whom it called its right hand. From that people it joined virginity to itself, which brought forth the greatest work. For as God created all things through his Word, so virginity, through the heat of holy divinity, bore the Son of God. Thus virginity is not without fruitfulness, because the Virgin bore God and man, through whom all things were made.

And in this way all the virtues of the Old and New Testaments, which God worked in his saints, are gilded like a garment adorned with gold. The virgin will freely gather these to herself, because a husband’s bond will not constrain her. The wheel which Ezekiel saw (Ezek. I) also prefigured virginity, because this same virginity was prefigured in the Law before the Incarnation of the Son of God.

[Col. 0263C] After his Incarnation, however, it works wondrously many miracles, because through it God cleansed every expiation and rightly ordered every institution. For virginity bears the old and sustains the new; it is itself the root and foundation of every good, because it has always and ever been with him who is without beginning and without end. For the nature of the human being, which had been lost through sins, revived in salvation through it, when through an alien nature it removed sins from human beings.

But the second creature, like a calf, shows those in clerical dress who devote themselves to divine sacrifice: namely, those who dig around the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth and everywhere turn up by ploughing the field of God’s commandments; and also those who are called angels of the Lord of hosts. These too must gird themselves with the girdle of chastity, lest they walk in the vanity of carnal pleasures, but may vigorously turn over the field with the plough. They will also have the circumcision of sobriety, because through them the sins of human beings are washed away; and this will be done in mercy, because they perceive sins in themselves.

[Col. 0263D] These noble kinds—that is, the people signified by the lion and the calf—draw to themselves another kind of persons, whom they themselves call conversi. Many of these do not turn themselves toward God in their conduct, because they love opposition rather than rectitude and perform their works with the clamour of recklessness, saying of their prelates: “Who are these men, and what are they? And what were we, or what are we?” Because they act thus, they are like false prophets; and because they do not judge rightly how God established his people.

Therefore you who fear God, hear the Spirit of the Lord speaking to you: Remove these evils mentioned above from yourselves, and cleanse yourselves before those days of tribulation, when the enemies of God and of ourselves will drive you away and turn you back to the straight place of humility and poverty, lest henceforth you remain in such great spaciousness as you have hitherto enjoyed. Thus God also changed the old Law from its customary practice into spiritual life, and purified every earlier institution for more useful ends.

[Col. 0264A] At the first beginning God granted Adam to cultivate the earth, Abel to sacrifice, Noah to build; and this continued up to the high priesthood which arose in Christ’s Incarnation, which Abraham earlier prefigured by circumcision and Moses by legislation. But the same Son of God afterward fulfilled all these things in his humanity; hence they are to be understood in relation to human beings.

After Adam’s fall, God rightly prefigured his ordering both in human beings and in angels. It would by no means be fitting for a priest to pursue the offices of a farmer, or a disciple the offices of a master, since the farmer ought to imitate the priest and the disciple the master in fear and humble patience. For almighty God is known in his works, as he began to work in Adam, to whom he gave cultivation of the earth and the care of human beings; since God himself created all things. Through Abel’s sacrifice he prefigured that his Son was to be sacrificed for the redemption of the people; and through Noah, who built the ark (Gen. VI), he prefigured that teachers were to be established among the spiritual people.

[Col. 0264C] Now you masters, rebuke and correct the persons named above, namely the conversi, in your order; for the greater part of them work neither by day nor by night, since they serve neither God nor the world perfectly. Rouse them from this ignorance, as a good gardener clears useless herbs from his garden.
