Therefore a woman who has impaired the integrity of her virginity with a man must abstain, on account of the bruise of her wound by which she has been impaired, from entering my temple until the wound of that injury is healed, according as ecclesiastical discipline most certainly shows her in this matter.

For when the bride of my Son had been joined to him on the wood [Col. 0397D] of the cross, she kept herself hidden until my Son commanded his disciples to spread the truth of the Gospel throughout the world; afterward she rose openly and publicly proclaimed the glory of her bridegroom in the begetting of Spirit and water. So too let a virgin who is joined to a man act with chaste modesty: until the time prescribed for her by ecclesiastical ruling, let her remain hidden; and, when this has been completed, passing out of her seclusion into love for her bridegroom, let her come forth openly.

Nor do I will the aforesaid work of man and woman to be performed once the root of a little child has been placed in the woman, lest the coagulation of the child be defiled by superfluous and wasted seed, until the purification after its birth [Col. 0398A]. Afterward this is not forbidden when it is done again for love of children in uprightness and not in wantonness. Thus the human race has been established to proceed in its procreation in the honour of human discipline, and not as the empty talk of foolish persons cries out, those who say that it is lawful for them to exercise their lust according to their own will, saying: “How can we restrain ourselves so inhumanly?”

O human being, if you look toward the devil, he stirs you up to every evil and kills you with his deadly poison; but if you raise your eyes toward God, he gives you help and makes you chaste. Do you not seek lust more than chastity in your work? A woman is subject to a man, in whom he sows his seed, just as he also tills the earth so that it may bear fruit. Does a man [Col. 0398B] till the earth in order that it may produce thorns and briars? Certainly not, but that it may yield worthy fruit. Thus this endeavour of humankind too must be in love of children, not in wantonness of lust.

Therefore, O human beings, weep and howl to your God, whom you so often despise in your sins when you emit your seed in most evil fornication. There you are not merely fornicators, but murderers also, because you reject regard for God and fulfill your lust according to your own will. Thus the devil also always pursues you in this work, knowing that you pursue your desire more than you behold the joy of children.

Hear, then, you who are in the towers of the Church. Do not accuse me in your fornication [Col. 0398C], but look upon yourselves. For when you run to the devil, despising me, you do unlawful works, and therefore do not wish to be chaste, as my servant Hosea speaks of the defiled people, saying: “Their thoughts will not permit them to return to their God, because a spirit of fornication is in their midst, and they have not known God” (Hosea 5:4).

This means: malignant people who do not know God hide the face of their heart, not turning it amid the various twists of their contrivance so as to return to true brightness. With a discerning eye they do not distinguish the things that are God’s, but nourish evil within themselves. For the breath of wanton uncleanness, through diabolical suggestion, softens the manly strength [Col. 0398D] which they ought to possess in themselves, not allowing them to place their good conscience in God, while the adversary turns them away from the life of blessedness.

But now I shall turn to my most beloved sheep, planted in my heart and constituting the seed of chastity. For virginity was planted by me, because my Son too was born of a virgin. Thus virginity is the most beautiful fruit among all the fruits of the valleys, and a great person among all persons who are in the palace of the unfailing King, because it is not subject to the command of the Law, since it brought my Only-Begotten into the world.

Therefore let those hear who wish to follow the Son of God in the innocence of free chastity and in the separation of mourning widowhood. For virginity, unpolluted [Col. 0399A] from the beginning, is nobler than widowhood oppressed beneath a man’s yoke, although widowhood, after its grief in which it lost its husband, follows virginity. For my Son endured many pains in his body and underwent the death of the cross. Thus you too will suffer many distresses in love for him, when you overcome within yourselves that which was sown in sinful lust through the tasting of the fruit.

Yet when you endure the flowing streams of lust’s burning in your seed, since you cannot be so chaste that the frailty of human weakness does not secretly show itself in you, you ought in this to imitate the Passion of my Son: by resisting yourselves, extinguishing within you the burning flame of lust, and restraining the other worldly things that belong to the world—namely anger, pride, sensual excess [Col. 0399B], and the other vices of this sort—and accomplishing this victory in great struggle. Then these battles appear before me, with great beauty and much fruit, brighter than the sun and sweeter than the fragrance of spices, because you imitate my Only-Begotten in his sufferings when you trample burning lust within yourselves by so strong a contest. And when you persevere in this way, you shall obtain great glory from it in the heavenly kingdom.

O most flourishing flowers, my angels marvel at your struggle: that you escape death; that you are not defiled in the poisonous mud of the world, though you bear a fleshly body; and that by trampling it down in this manner you shall be glorious in their company, [Col. 0399C] because you appear undefiled according to their likeness. Therefore rejoice when you persevere thus, for then I am with you, when you faithfully receive me and fulfill my voice with the joy of your heart, as I show in the secret vision of my beloved John, saying: “Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice, I shall enter in to him and dine with him, and he with me” (Revelation 3:20).

This means: you who faithfully love me, your Saviour, see that, wishing to help you, I wait at the dwelling-place of your heart, considering what your conscience contains in the treasury of its heart. And, through the inspiration of your mind’s remembrance, I admonish your spirit to open itself in welcoming good will. If then the faithful heart [Col. 0399D] perceives the sound of my fear, I join myself to it, embracing it and taking unfailing food with it, when it offers itself to me as a sweet taste in good works. So it too will receive in me the food of life, because it loves that which brings life to those who desire righteousness.

But, as you see, after Adam and Eve had been expelled from Paradise, a most radiant splendour surrounded that same region. For, after they had left the place of delight because of their transgression, the power of divine majesty removed every stain of all defilement from that place and so fortified it by its brightness that it should henceforth be touched by no contrary thing. It also showed that the transgression committed there would one day be mercifully and compassionately abolished.

And so all the [Col. 0400A] elements of the world, which had previously existed in great tranquillity, were turned into the greatest unrest and displayed dreadful terrors. For the creation which had been made for humankind’s service, and which had felt no adversity within itself, when humankind embraced disobedience and became disobedient to its Creator, abandoned its tranquillity and received unrest, bringing very great and numerous adversities upon humankind, so that humankind, having bent itself toward worse things, might be restrained by them. What does this mean? Because humankind was rebellious against God in the place of delights, that creation which had been subjected in service to humankind set itself in opposition to humankind.

And Paradise is a place of delight, flourishing in the greenness of flowers and herbs and the pleasures of every spice, filled with the finest odours and endowed [Col. 0400B] with the joy of blessed souls. It gives most fruitful fertility to the dry earth because it grants the earth its greatest power, just as the soul supplies strength to the body; for Paradise is not darkened in the shadow and perdition of sins.

Therefore hear and understand, you who say in your hearts: “What are these things, and why are they so?” O why are you so foolish in your hearts, you who were made in the image and likeness of God? How could such great glory and such great honour, given to you, exist without testing, when gold, which is as though nothing and an empty thing, ought to be tested in fire; when precious stones must be polished in purification; and when all such things must everywhere be examined?

Therefore, O foolish human beings, how could that which was made in the image and likeness [Col. 0400C] of God endure without testing? For humankind must be examined above every creature, and therefore must be tested through every creature. How? Spirit by spirit, flesh by flesh, earth by air, fire by water, battle by peace, good by evil, beauty by ugliness, poverty by riches, sweetness by bitterness, health by sickness, the long by the short, the hard by the soft, height by depth, light by darkness, life by death, Paradise by punishments, the heavenly kingdom by Gehenna, earthly things by earthly things, and heavenly things by heavenly things. Thus humankind was tested in every creature: in Paradise, on earth, and [Col. 0400D] in hell; afterward it was placed in heaven.

You plainly see a few things out of many which are hidden before your eyes. Why do you ridicule things that are upright, plain, just, and good in every good thing before God? Why are you indignant at these? God is just; but the human race is unjust in transgressing God’s commandments when it strives to be wiser than God.

Now tell me, O human being: what do you think you were when you did not yet exist in soul and body? You do not know how you were created. Yet now, O human being, you wish to search out heaven and earth, judge their justice in relation to God’s ordering, and discern the highest things, when you cannot even examine the lowest things: for you do not know how you live in the body or how you are stripped from the body. He who created you in the first human being foresaw all these things.

[Col. 0401A] Likewise, the most gentle Father sent his Only-Begotten to die for the people, so that he might free humankind from diabolical power. Thus the liberated human being shines in God, and God in the human being; and humankind, having fellowship with God, possesses in heaven a more brilliant splendour than it had before. This would not have been so if the Son of God had not put on flesh; for if humankind had remained in Paradise, the Son would not have suffered on the cross.

But when humankind was deceived by the cunning serpent, God, moved by true mercy, willed that his Only-Begotten be incarnate in a most pure virgin. Thus, after humankind’s fall, many shining virtues were raised up in heaven—such as humility, the queen of virtues, which flowered in virginal birth, and likewise the other virtues which lead God’s elect to heavenly things. [Col. 0401B] For when a field is cultivated with much labour, it yields much fruit, as was shown in the human race; because after humankind’s fall many virtues arose for its raising up.

But, O human beings, weighed down by bodily heaviness, you do not see that great glory prepared for you in the full justice of God, without stain and without any contempt, and which no one can take away. For before the fabric of the world had been established, God foresaw all these things in true justice. Therefore, O human being, consider this comparison.

A lord who wishes with much care to make a garden first establishes a suitable site for the garden. Then, arranging the place of each planting, he considers the usefulness, flavour, and fragrance of the fruit of good trees [Col. 0401C], and the spices of diverse kinds. Thus the great and profound craftsman-lord arranges each of his plantings in it so that it may be properly distinguished in its usefulness. He then considers with what defence he may surround it so that none of its enemies can destroy his planting. He also appoints his spice-makers, who know how to water that garden, gather its fruit, and make from it diverse spices.

Therefore, O human being, consider carefully: if that lord foresees that his garden, bearing no fruit and no utility, is to be destroyed, why then does so great and profound a craftsman construct [Col. 0401D], plant, water, and fortify that garden with such great care and labour? Hear, then, and understand. God, who is the sun of righteousness, sent his splendour upon the mud that is human transgression; and that splendour shone in great brightness because that mud was exceedingly foul and dark. For the sun shone in its brightness, while the mud rotted in its foulness; therefore the sun was embraced with greater delight by those who saw it than if mud had not been placed beside it.

But just as mud is foul in comparison with the sun, so human transgression is unjust in comparison with God’s justice. Therefore righteousness, because it is beautiful, must be loved; and iniquity, because it is foul, must be hated. Into this foulness fell the sheep of the Lord who had planted the garden. This sheep was taken away from the Lord through its own consent, not through the Lord’s negligence; [Col. 0402A] afterward the Lord sought it with much care and justice.

Therefore the choir of angels was enlightened in the greatest joy when the angels saw humankind in heaven. What does this mean? When the innocent Lamb was suspended on the cross, the elements trembled, because the most noble son of the Virgin was bodily slain by the hands of murderers. In his death, the lost sheep was brought back to the pastures of life.

For after the ancient persecutor saw that he had to lose that sheep because of the blood of the innocent Lamb, which the Lamb had poured out for the remission of human sins, he then first learned who that Lamb was. Previously he could not know how the heavenly Lamb was incarnate of a virgin, without male seed and without any desire of sin, under the [Col. 0402B] overshadowing of the Holy Spirit. For that same persecutor, at the beginning of his creation, raised himself in the breath of pride, casting himself down into death and throwing humankind out of the glory of Paradise. God did not will to resist him in his power, but overcame him in humility through his Son. And because Lucifer despised the justice of God, by God’s just judgment he could not know the incarnation of the Only-Begotten Son of God.

For through this hidden counsel the lost sheep was restored to life. Therefore, O rebellious human beings, why do you assume such hardness? God did not will to abandon humankind, but sent his Son for its salvation; for in this way God crushed the head of pride in the ancient serpent. In the deliverance of humankind from death, hell opened its enclosure while Satan cried: [Col. 0402C] “Woe, woe! Who will help me?” And the entire diabolical troop, in great raging, tore itself apart, marvelling what that great power could be which it, together with the prince of wickedness, could not resist, when it saw faithful souls being taken away from it.

Thus humankind was raised above the heavens, because God in humankind and humankind in God appeared through the Son of God. That same Lord who had lost the sheep but had brought it back to life so gloriously also possessed a precious pearl in the same likeness, which, being lost, fell into much filth. But he did not permit it to lie thus in filth: he sought it, joyfully drew it out when found, and so cleansed it after drawing it out from the filth in which it had lain—as gold is usually purified in a furnace—that he restored it to its former [Col. 0402D] honour with greater glory.

For God created humankind, but it fell into death through diabolical persuasion. From this the Son of God rescued it through his blood and gloriously led it to heavenly honour. How? Through humility and charity. For humility caused the Son of God to be born of a virgin. That humility was found neither in the embraces of a husband, nor in the curiosity of flesh, nor in earthly riches, nor in golden ornaments, nor in worldly honours; rather, the Son of God lay in a manger because his mother was poor. Humility always groans, weeps, and destroys all crimes: this is its work.

Therefore, whoever wishes to overcome the devil must fortify and arm himself with humility, because Lucifer flees from it so greatly and [Col. 0403A] hides himself before it in a cave like a serpent. Wherever humility catches him, it quickly breaks him like a most fragile thread. Charity likewise holds the Only-Begotten Son of God in the Father’s bosom in heaven and sent him down into his mother’s womb on earth; for it does not despise sinners or tax collectors, but intends to save all. Therefore, often drawing a fountain of tears from the eyes of the faithful, it softens the heart’s hardness.

In this, humility and charity are brighter than the other virtues, since humility and charity are like body and soul, possessing stronger powers than the other powers of the soul and members of the body. How? Humility is as though the body, and charity as though the soul. They cannot be separated from one another but work together, [Col. 0404A] just as soul and body cannot be separated but cooperate while a human being lives in the body. And just as the diverse members of the body are subject to soul and body according to their powers, so the other virtues cooperate with humility and charity according to their righteousness.

Therefore, O human beings, pursue humility and charity for the glory of God and for your salvation. Armed with them, you shall not fear diabolical snares, but shall possess unfailing life. Therefore whoever has knowledge in the Holy Spirit and wings in faith must not transgress my admonition, but receive it by embracing it in the taste of his soul.

## THIRD VISION

[Col. 0403]

### Summary

That invisible and eternal things are manifested through visible and temporal things. Concerning the firmament made in the likeness of an egg. Concerning the bright fire and the shadowy skin. Concerning the position of the sun and three stars. Concerning the sun’s ascent. Concerning its descent and what it signifies. Words of the Acts of the Apostles on the same subject. Concerning the first wind and its whirlwinds. Concerning the second wind and its whirlwinds. Concerning the dark fire, its sound, and its sharp stones. Concerning the most pure ether and the position of the moon and two stars. Concerning the position of the other stars. Concerning the third wind and its whirlwinds. Concerning the watery air and the white skin. Concerning the fourth wind and its whirlwinds. Concerning the sandy globe of the earth. Words of David concerning the same matter. Concerning the earthquake and what it signifies. Concerning the greatest mountain between north and east. Concerning those who investigate future events in created things by perverse art. Words of the Gospel. How the devil deceives human beings through magical art. A parable concerning the same subject. When human salvation and usefulness have been fulfilled, the world will be changed. Words of Job concerning the same matter. Words of God concerning the same. That God no longer wishes to tolerate divinations in the stars and other created things. Concerning human folly and obstinacy. A comparison concerning a goat, a stag, and a wolf. A comparison concerning a physician. Words of John.

[Col. 0403B] After this I saw a vast structure, round and shadowy, in the likeness of an egg: narrow above, broad in the middle, and constricted below. Around its outer surface was a bright fire, as though it had beneath it a shadowy skin. Within that fire was a globe of glowing fire, so great that the entire structure was illuminated by it. Above it were three lamps, visibly arranged upright, which by their fire held that globe so that it did not slip. At times that globe raised itself upward, and a great abundance of fire met it, so that it extended its flames farther; and at times it bent downward, and much cold came against it, wherefore it withdrew its flames more quickly.

Moreover, from the fire which encircled the structure [Col. 0403C] there issued a blast with its whirlwinds; and from the skin lying beneath it another blast boiled up with its whirlwinds, spreading throughout that structure in every direction. In that same skin there was a certain dark fire, so terrible that I could not look at it. It shook the entire skin with its force and was full of noises, storms, and exceedingly sharp stones, greater and smaller. When it raised its noise, that bright fire, the winds, and the air were set in motion, so that flashes of lightning preceded the sound itself, because that fire first felt within itself the agitation of that same sound.

But beneath that skin was a most pure ether, with no skin beneath itself. [Col. 0403D] In it I also beheld a globe of blazing fire, exceedingly great, having above itself two lamps [Col. 0404B] visibly set upright and holding the globe so that it did not exceed the measure of its course. In that same ether many bright spheres were set everywhere. The same globe, sometimes diminishing itself a little, sent its brightness into these spheres; then, returning beneath the aforesaid red and fiery globe and restoring its flames from it, it breathed them forth again into those same spheres.

From that ether also a blast burst forth with its whirlwinds, spreading everywhere throughout the aforesaid structure. Beneath that ether I saw watery air, having beneath itself a white skin; spreading here and there, it supplied moisture to that whole structure. When it sometimes suddenly gathered itself together, it poured out a sudden rain with great crashing; and when [Col. 0404C] it spread itself gently, it shed a mild rain with gentle movement. A blast also went out from it with its whirlwinds and spread everywhere through the aforesaid structure.

In the midst of these elements was a very large sandy globe. These elements surrounded it in such a way that it could not slip away either this way or that. Yet when the same elements, with the aforesaid blasts, sometimes shook one another, they compelled the globe itself to move slightly by their force.

And I saw, between north and east, something like a very great mountain, which held much darkness toward the north and much light toward the east; yet neither could that light reach the darkness nor the darkness the light.

[Col. 0404D] And again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: God, who created all things by his will, created them [Col. 0405A] for the knowledge and honour of his name, showing in them not only those things which are visible and temporal, but also making manifest in them those which are invisible and eternal. This vision which you see demonstrates this.

For this vast structure which you see—round and shadowy, like an egg, narrow above, broad in the middle, and constricted below—faithfully declares almighty God, incomprehensible in his majesty, immeasurable in his mysteries, and the hope of all the faithful: since at first human beings were uncultivated and simple in their actions; later, instructed more fully in the Old and New Law, they trouble and afflict one another; and at last, near the end of the world, they will suffer many miseries in their straits. [Col. 0405B]

Around its outer surface is a bright fire, as though it had a shadowy skin beneath it. This signifies that God everywhere burns up by the fire of his vengeance those who are outside the true faith, while everywhere he purifies by the fire of his consolation those who remain within the Catholic faith; thus he casts down the darkness of diabolical perversity, as also happened when the devil, created by God, wished to set himself against God and fell, defeated, into perdition.

And in this fire is a globe of glowing fire so great that the whole structure is illuminated by it. By the splendour of its brightness it shows that in God the Father is his ineffable Only-Begotten Son, the sun of righteousness, possessing the radiance of burning love and being of such glory that every creature [Col. 0405C] is enlightened by the brightness of his light. Above itself it has three lamps arranged upright, which by their fire hold the globe so that it does not slip. By their governance these signify the Trinity, which contains all things, and show that the Son of God, descending from heaven to earth, left the angels in heaven and revealed heavenly things also to human beings, who subsist in soul and body. Glorifying him by the benefit of his brightness, they cast away every harmful error, when they magnified him as the true Son of God incarnate from a true Virgin—after an angel had announced him to them, and after a human being living in soul and body received him with faithful joy.

Therefore the same globe sometimes [Col. 0405D] rises upward, and much fire meets it, so that it extends its flames farther. This signifies that, when the time came in which God’s Only-Begotten Son was to be incarnate, by the Father’s will, for the redemption and raising up of humankind, the Holy Spirit, in the power of the Father, wondrously worked the heavenly mysteries in the blessed Virgin. Thus, as the same Son of God gave miraculous radiance in virginal chastity through fruitful virginity, virginity was made glorious. For in the most noble Virgin the incarnation most supremely to be desired was revealed.

Likewise, it sometimes inclines downward, and much cold comes against it; for which reason it withdraws its flames more quickly. This declares that the same Only-Begotten Son of God, born from a virgin and thus mercifully inclining himself to the poverty of human beings, endured many bodily distresses when many miseries met him. When he had shown himself bodily to the world, he passed from the world and returned to the Father, while his disciples also stood by, as it is written: “While they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud received him from their eyes” (Acts 1). [Col. 0406A]

This means: when the children of the Church receive the Son of God in the inward knowledge of their heart, the holiness of his body was lifted up in the power of his divinity, and in a mystical miracle a cloud of hidden mystery received him, concealing him from mortal eyes, while the gusts of winds ministered to him.

But, as you see, a blast with its whirlwinds issued from that fire which encircled the same structure. This shows that from almighty God, filling the whole world with his power, a true proclamation went forth in righteous words, when he himself, the living and true God, was manifested to human beings in truth. And another blast boils up with its whirlwinds from the skin beneath it, because from diabolical rage also—which neither knows nor fears God—there goes out an evil report with wicked utterances. These spread through the structure here and there, because in the world useful and useless rumours mingle among peoples in diverse ways.

Moreover, in that same skin there is a dark fire so terrible that you cannot look upon it. This declares that within the worst and most wicked snares of the ancient betrayer there bursts forth the most hideous murder with such heat that human understanding [Col. 0406C] cannot discern its madness. It shakes the whole skin with its force, because murder embraces in its horror every diabolical malice, since in the firstborn, hatred boiling up from wrath perpetrated fratricide.

That fire was full of noises, storms, and very sharp stones, greater and smaller, because murder is full of greed, drunkenness, and most savage wickednesses, which rage without mercy in great murders as well as in lesser vices. When it raises its noise, that bright fire, the winds, and the air are moved, because when murder shrieks in the desire for the shedding of blood, heavenly judgments, swift reports, and preparations for the murderer’s ruin, stretched out everywhere in the vengeance of righteous judgment, are stirred up. Thus lightning flashes precede the sound itself, because that fire first feels within itself the agitation of that same sound. For the severity of divine judgment overwhelms and crushes that crime, since divine majesty openly foresees, with the eye to which all things are naked, before the rumbling of that madness is publicly revealed. [Col. 0406D]

But beneath that skin is most pure ether, with no skin beneath it, because beneath the snares of the ancient betrayer shines the most serene faith, in which no uncertainty of unbelief lies hidden: not founded upon itself, but sustained in Christ. In it you also see a globe of blazing fire, exceedingly great, which truly signifies the united Church, displaying to you in faith the whiteness of innocent brightness [Col. 0407A] and of very great honour. It has above itself two lamps visibly set upright, holding the globe so that it does not exceed the measure of its course. By their meaning they show that the two Testaments, namely the authority of the Old and New, given from above, draw the Church toward the divine commands of heavenly mysteries. They restrain her so that she does not rashly extend herself into diversity of morals; and both the Old and the New testimony show her the blessedness of the heavenly inheritance.

Therefore, in that same ether many bright spheres are set everywhere, into which the same globe, sometimes diminishing itself a little, sends out its brightness. For in the purity of faith very many splendid works [Col. 0407B] of piety appear everywhere. At a certain time the Church endured some oppression, and the beauty of her wonders faded somewhat; yet, lying as though in grief, she nevertheless admired the brightness of her former works in perfect human beings. Then, returning beneath the aforesaid red and fiery globe and restoring her flames from it, she again breathes them forth into the same spheres. For, placed in affliction, she hastens under the protection of the Only-Begotten Son of God and receives from him the endurance of divine strengthening, declaring love of heavenly things in blessed works.

Hence a blast with its whirlwinds bursts out from that ether and spreads everywhere through the aforesaid structure, because from [Col. 0407C] the unity of faith a most powerful report, with true and perfect assertions flowing forth to aid human beings, has struck the bounds of the whole world with great swiftness.

Beneath that ether you see watery air having beneath itself a white skin, which, spreading in every direction, gives moisture to the whole structure. For beneath the faith which existed both among the ancient and the new fathers, baptism in the Church, for the salvation of believers—as is most truly shown to you—was founded in the innocence of most blessed steadfastness; spreading everywhere by divine inspiration, it brought to the whole world the irrigation of salvation among believers. When it sometimes suddenly gathers itself, it sends out a sudden rain with much cold; and when it gently spreads itself, it gives a mild rain with gentle movement. For when baptism was at times multiplied through defenders of truth, in the speed of their preaching and the depth of their minds, it was made manifest to astonished people in a swift abundance of words, in the flood of their preaching. At other times baptism, extended through preaching in gentle moderation, was revealed in sweet irrigation, with the aid of discernment drawing peoples in. [Col. 0407D]

Therefore a blast with its whirlwinds, going out from it, spreads everywhere through the aforesaid structure, because from the flood of baptism which brings salvation to believers a most true report, going out with the words of most powerful discourses, has flooded the whole world with the manifestation of its blessedness, as is now openly declared among peoples abandoning unbelief [Col. 0408A] and seeking the Catholic faith.

And in the midst of these elements is a very large sandy globe, which the elements surround so that it cannot slip away either this way or that. It plainly shows the human being who lives in profound reflection: made in a wonderful manner from the clay of the earth with much glory, and so surrounded by the power of God’s creatures that he cannot in any way be separated from them. For the elements of the world were created for the service of human beings and render service to them, while the human being, sitting as it were in their midst, presides over them by divine disposition. Thus David, inspired even through me, says: “You crowned him with glory and honour, and set him over the works of your hands” (Psalm 8).

This means: O [Col. 0408B] God, who made all things wonderfully, you crowned the human being with the golden and purple crown of understanding and with the most worthy garment of visible form, setting him as a prince over the height of your perfect works, which you justly and well disposed among your creatures. For you bestowed upon the human being, above your other creatures, great and marvellous dignities.

But, as you see, when those elements, together with the aforesaid blasts, sometimes shake one another, they compel the globe itself to move a little by their force. For when, at a fitting time, God’s creatures encounter one another with the report of their Creator’s miracles, so that miracle is enfolded in miracle with the great thunder of words, the human being, struck by the greatness of those miracles, [Col. 0408C] feels a shaking of mind and body, while in astonishment at those wonders he considers the weakness of his own frailty.

And you see between north and east something like a very great mountain, which has much darkness toward the north and much light toward the east. For between diabolical impiety and divine goodness there appears the great fall of humanity: through the most evil deception of the wicked one it holds many miseries of damnation among the reprobate, and through desirable salvation very great happiness of redemption among the elect. Yet neither that light can reach the darkness nor that darkness the light, because works of light do not intermingle with works of darkness, nor do works of darkness rise to works of light—although the devil [Col. 0408D] often strives to obscure the latter through evil people, as happens among pagans, heretics, false prophets, and those whom these try to draw after themselves by their deceitful deception.

How? Because they wish to know what they ought not to know, imitating him who wished to be like the Most High. And because they follow him, he shows them falsehood as though it were truth, according to their will. Therefore they are not with me, nor am I with them, because they do not walk in my ways but love strange paths, seeking what the foolish creature may deceitfully show them concerning future events. They wish to know this according to the perversity with which they investigate it, despising me and rejecting my saints, who love me with a sincere heart.

But can such people [Col. 0409A], who test me so obstinately by perverse art that they scrutinize the creature made for their service, asking it to show them, according to their own will, the thing which they wish to know—can they, in their investigation of this art, lengthen or shorten the time of life appointed for them by their Creator? Certainly they have power to do neither this nor to make a day or an hour. Or can they turn aside God’s predestination? By no means, O miserable people. Do I not sometimes allow creatures to reveal your sufferings to you? They then have signs because they fear me, God, just as a servant sometimes displays his master’s resources, and as an ox, an ass, and other animals make known the will of their masters [Col. 0409B] when they faithfully fulfil it in their service.

O fools: when you consign me to oblivion, neither looking to me nor worshipping me, but looking to the creature subject to you to see what it may foretell and show—then you obstinately reject me, worshipping a weak creature in place of your Creator. Therefore I also say to you, O human being: why do you worship that creature which can neither console nor help you, and which brings you no prosperity or happiness? Yet instructors in death—the astrologers—and followers of Gentile unbelief rashly assert that the stars grant life to human beings and dispose all your actions. O miserable people, who made the stars?

But by my permission stars are sometimes shown to human beings with certain signs, as my Son also shows in the Gospel, where he says: “There will be signs in sun, moon, and stars” (Luke 21). This means: through the light of these luminaries service is rendered to human beings, and through their circuit the seasons of times are shown. Thus in the last times mournful and perilous times will, by my permission, be shown in them, so that the ray of the sun, the brightness of the moon, and the radiance of the stars will sometimes be withdrawn, in order that human hearts may be shaken by this. Thus also the incarnation of my Son was shown by a star, by my will.

But a human being does not have a particular star which orders his life, as a foolish and erring people attempts to assert. Rather, all stars are held in common for the service of all people. But the reason that that star shone more brightly than the other stars [Col. 0409D] is that my Only-Begotten was born above all other human beings by virginal birth, without sin. That star brought no other assistance to my Son than faithfully announcing his incarnation alone to the people. For all stars and creatures, fearing me, accomplish only my command and have no signification of anything in any creature.

For when it pleases me, creatures show my command, just as, when a craftsman makes a coin, he engraves on it a form pleasing to himself. Then the coin displays the form imposed upon it, having no power of its own over that matter. For it does not know when the craftsman may wish to impose another form on it, because it discerns neither the long nor the short duration of its form.

[Col. 0410A] What is this? O human being, if a stone lay before you, in which, carefully examining it, you conjectured certain signs of your sufferings, then, according to your deceitful judgment, either saddened by your misfortune or puffed up by your prosperity, you would say in your delusion: “Ah! I shall die!” or “Hurrah! I shall live!” or “Alas, how great is my misfortune!” or “Hurrah, how great is my prosperity!” And what would that stone then contribute to you? Would it take anything from you or give anything to you? It would have no power either to harm or to benefit you. So too neither stars nor fire nor birds nor any other such creature can harm or help you in the signs investigated from them.

But if you put your trust in this creature, made for your service, rejecting me, then I also cast you from my sight by my just judgment, taking away from you the blessedness of my kingdom. For I do not wish you to investigate stars, fire, birds, or other such creatures concerning future events; for if you look into them obstinately, your eyes are hateful to me, and I cast you down as a lost angel who abandoned truth and hurled himself into damnation.

O human being, when the stars and the other creatures were made, where were you? Did you give counsel regarding their institution? Rather, the presumption of such inquiry arose in the first schism: namely, when people had so consigned God to oblivion that nation after nation proudly examined different creatures and sought in them various signs concerning future events. Thus that error also arose in Baal: people, deceived, worshipped God’s creature as God. Diabolical mockery further incited them to this, because they looked more to the creature than to their Creator, desiring to know what they ought not to have known. [Col. 0410C]

Hence worse things also appeared, when people began, through the devil, to rage by the art of magic, so that they see and hear the devil, while he deceitfully speaks to them and shows them that they are looking at one creature when something else is present. But it should be left unspoken how the first seducers were taught by the devil; in the same way, those who seek in this manner see and hear him. Yet they themselves are greatly blameworthy for this wickedness, since in this way they deny me, their God, and follow the ancient seducer.

O human being, I sought you in the blood of my Son, not with malice [Col. 0410D] and iniquity, but with great equity; nevertheless, you abandon me, the true God, and follow him who is a liar. I am justice and truth; therefore I admonish you in faith, exhort you in love, and lead you back in repentance, so that, although you are bloodstained in the pollutions of sins, you may nevertheless rise from the fall of your ruin. But if you despise me, you will experience in yourself the parable of this likeness.

A certain lord had many servants under him. To each of them he gave very many weapons of war, saying: “Be upright and strong, casting away slowness and idleness.” But while those servants were travelling along a certain road with him, they saw beside the road a certain deceiver and most evil inventor of an alien art. Some of them, deceived, said: [Col. 0411A] “We wish to learn this man’s arts.” Throwing away the weapons they had, they ran to him. Others said to them: “What are you doing, following this deceiver and provoking your lord to anger?” And they answered: “What harm will this do to our lord?” Their lord said to them: “O wicked servants, why have you cast away the weapons I gave you? And why is it dearer to you to love this vanity than to serve me, your lord, whose natural servants you are? Go, then, after that deceiver, as you desire, since you can no longer serve me; and see what his deception will profit you.” And he cast them away from himself.

This means: that lord is almighty God, governing all peoples under his power, who armed every human being with reason and understanding, commanding each to be zealous and [Col. 0411B] watchful in the instruments of virtues, shaking off perversity and negligence. But when human beings take up the way of truth, intending to proceed in the divine commandments, many temptations meet them. Thus they attend to the devil, deceiver of the whole world and most wicked artificer of many victories, set not in the way of truth but in the deception of snares.

Therefore some of them, loving injustice more than righteousness and seduced by the devil, devote themselves more to imitating the vices of the ancient seducer than to embracing the virtues of God. They turn the understanding which they ought to direct toward divine commandments toward the vices of earthly iniquity, submitting themselves to the devil. Their leaders, like companions and fellow servants, often confront them through the sacred Scriptures, reproach their deeds, and rebuke them for following diabolical inventions and bringing divine vengeance upon themselves. [Col. 0411C]

But they very often mock their admonitions and, through pride, assert that they sin only in small matters and offend their God very little. Therefore, when they persevere in that hardening, they receive the divine sentence: for those servants of iniquity are charged with having suffocated the understanding given them from above, and with having preferred the deceptions of the ancient seducer to their Creator, whom they ought diligently to have served. Thus, despised by God, they are assigned to diabolical illusions according to their works—because they refused to serve God—where they are compelled to consider what that most wicked deception [Col. 0411D] has profited them. For, thus cast away, they incur damnation, because, setting aside divine commandments, they strove to follow the devil more than God.

For I do not wish human beings to despise me, whom they ought to know in faith. If they reject me and examine the creature subject to them, thereby imitating the ancient seducer, then I also permit it to happen to them, with both the creature and the devil, according to the desire of their heart, so that they may thus discover what profits them from the creature they worshipped or what the devil whom they followed contributes to them.

And, O foolish people, why do you ask the creature about the time of your life? None of you can either know, avoid, or overstep the span of life appointed by me for you to live. [Col. 0412A] For, O human being, when your welfare in both worldly and spiritual matters has been completed, you will change this present age and pass into that which will find no end.

For when a human being is of such strength that he burns in me more ardently than others, so that he does not lie sluggish in the conscience of the earthly dregs of foul-smelling sins but avoids the snares of the ancient serpent, I do not remove his spirit from his body before he brings his sweet fruits, in the sweetest fragrance, to a good end. But one whom I see to be of such frailty that he is tender and weak, unable amid the grievous pain of his body and the enticement of the worst plotter to bear my yoke, I take from this age before he begins to wither in the season of his decaying mind. For I know all things.

I wish to give all justice to [Col. 0412B] humankind for its warning, so that none may be able to excuse himself. I warn and exhort people to do justice when I strike them with the judgment of death as if they were already to die, though they will still live longer. I do this because no one can have or arrange for himself another span of time except according to the fruit I see in that person and according to my will by which I permit him to live. Thus Job also testifies through me when he says: “You have appointed his bounds, which cannot be passed” (Job 16).

This means: You who are above all and foresee all things before they happen have also, in the hiddenness of your majesty, appointed the bounds of human life, so that no knowledge, prudence, or cunning in any matter can pass them, [Col. 0412C] at any human age—whether infancy, youth, or old age—except according to the providence of your hidden purposes, you who willed human beings to be made for the glory of your name.

For I, O human being, knew you before the establishment of the world. Yet I wish to examine your days in your works, discern their fruit, and weigh each of your works carefully and most keenly. Whoever I suddenly remove from temporal life has completed the usefulness of that life, so that, if that person’s life were prolonged further, it would no longer bring any abundance of good fruits. Rather, having only the lukewarmness of fleshly faith, it would emit merely a smoke like the empty sound of words and would not touch me with the inward contact of its heart. Therefore I do not grant that person a reprieve in this life, but remove him from this age before [Col. 0412D] he falls into the lukewarmness of such barrenness.

But my speech is directed to you, O human being. Why do you despise me? Did I not send my prophets to you, give my Son to the wood of the cross for your salvation, and send my apostles to you so that they might show you, through the Gospel, the way of truth? Thus you cannot excuse yourself from possessing every good thing through me. Why then do you now set me aside?

But I no longer wish to tolerate the error of this perversity: namely, that you seek signs of your actions in stars, fire, birds, or any other such creature. For all who first devised this error by a diabolical vision, despising God, completely rejected his commandments; [Col. 0413A] and therefore they themselves were rejected. But I shine above every creature in the brightness of my divinity, so that my miracles are manifest to you in my saints. Therefore I no longer wish you to practise this error of divination any further, but to look to me.

O fool, consider who I am; consider that I am the highest good. From me I grant you every good thing when you diligently seek me. And whom do you believe me to be? I am God above all and in all. But you wish me to be regarded as a peasant who fears his lord. How? You wish me to do your will, while you despise my commandments. But God is not thus. What is this? For he has neither a notion of beginning nor fear of an end.

The heavens resound in my praises, beholding me and obeying me according to the justice by which they were established through me. The sun also, moon, and stars appear in the clouds of heaven according to their ordained course; likewise, the gusts of the winds and the rains run in the air as appointed for them. All these things obey their Creator according to his command. But you, O human being, do not fulfil my commandments; rather, you follow your own will, as though the justice of the law had neither been set before you nor shown to you. [Col. 0413B] For you are in such obstinacy, although you are ash, that the justice of my law does not suffice you—the law ploughed and cultivated in the blood of my Son, and well trodden in my saints of both the Old and New Testament.

But in great foolishness you wish to seize hold of me when you insult me in this manner, saying: “If it pleases God that I should be righteous and good, why does he not make me upright?” You wish thus to capture me as though a wanton kid wished to capture a stag, only to be forcefully driven back and pierced by the stag’s most powerful horns. So too, because you wish wantonly to play with me in your conduct, I crush you by my just judgment with the commandments of my law, as though with horns. These are trumpets sounding in your ears; but you do not follow them. Instead, you run after a wolf, which you suppose you have tamed so that it cannot harm you. But the hungry wolf devours you, saying: “This sheep wandered from the road and refused to follow its shepherd, but ran after me; therefore I wish to swallow it, because it chose me and abandoned its shepherd.”

O human being, God is just; therefore he disposed all that he made in heaven and on earth by a just ordering. [Col. 0414A] For I am the great physician of all illnesses, acting like a physician who sees a sick person eagerly desiring a remedy. What is this? If the illness is slight, he easily cures it; but if it is grave, he says to the sick person: “I require silver and gold from you. If you give them to me, I will help you.” Thus I too act, O human being. I wipe away lesser sins through groaning, tears, and people’s good will. But in more serious offences I command: “O human being, repent and amend your conduct, and I will show you my mercy and give you eternal life.”

Do not examine stars and other creatures regarding matters that come before you; do not worship the devil, invoke him, or seek anything from him. For if you wish [Col. 0414B] to know more than it is fitting for you to know, you will be deceived by the ancient seducer, because when the first human being sought more than he ought to seek, he was deceived by him and went to destruction.

Yet the devil did not know humanity’s redemption, when the Son of God killed death and shattered hell. For the devil conquered humankind through a woman in the beginning; but God crushed the devil through a woman at the end of times. She bore the Son of God, who wondrously reduced diabolical works to nothing, as my beloved John testifies, saying: “For this purpose the Son of God appeared: that he might destroy the works of the devil” (1 John 3).

What is this? For the health and salvation of human beings the greatest brightness appeared, namely the Son of God, putting on the poverty [Col. 0414C] of a human body. Yet like a burning star shining in shadowy clouds, he was placed in the winepress, where wine free from the dregs of leaven was to be pressed out, because he, the cornerstone, fell upon the winepress and pressed out such wine as gave the greatest fragrance of sweetness.

For he, shining as a radiant human being in the human race without the flood of polluted blood, trampled beneath the foot of his warfare the mouth of the ancient serpent. He dissolved from the liver of that serpent’s iniquity all its darts, which were full both of fury and lust, and rendered it wholly contemptible. Therefore whoever has knowledge in the Holy Spirit and wings in faith must not transgress my admonition, but must receive it by embracing it in the taste of his soul.

## FOURTH VISION

[Col. 0413]

### Summary

The soul’s lament as it returns from the way of error to Mother Zion through God’s grace. On the soul’s punishments; the tabernacle which it entered; its brave resistance, with God’s help, to diabolic storms; the storms introduced by diabolical persuasion and the reason they arise; how anger, hatred, and pride are restrained; the soul’s lament as it leaves its tabernacle in fear; how God’s knowledge is clouded by no obscurity; how no injustice can be found in the beauty of God’s justice; idols and their abandonment; Ezekiel on the same matter; the inequality of human seed and the diversity of people generated from it; Moses’ words on the same subject; why the contracted and deformed are born; how the child is enlivened in its mother’s womb and, after emerging, is strengthened and sustained by the soul; how the soul displays its powers according to the powers of the body; how a human being has three paths within; on intellect and will; a comparison concerning fire and bread; how, in the tabernacle of the will—that is, in the mind—all the soul’s powers are warmed and joined to one another; on reason; on sense; how the soul is mistress and the flesh handmaid; a comparison of the soul with a tree; how the soul, inclined to sins, abandons them when pierced by God’s gift; how the soul, tempted by diabolical snares, expels the devil’s darts from itself through heavenly inspiration; how the soul, leaving the dwelling of the body, awaits its sentence in judgment with great trembling; God’s words to human beings, that they should obey divine commandments and, casting away evil, faithfully accomplish good in the love of God; on the Catholic faith; words of Isaiah.

[Col. 0415A] Then I saw a vast and most serene brightness, as though blazing with innumerable eyes and having four corners turned toward the four regions of the world. Signifying the hidden mystery of the heavenly Creator, it was revealed to me in a great mystery; and within it there also appeared another brightness, like the dawn, bearing within itself the radiance of a purple gleam.

And behold, I saw people on earth carrying milk in earthen vessels and making cheeses from it. One part of it was thick, from which firm cheeses were made; another part was thin, from which weak cheeses were curdled; and another part was mixed with corruption, from which bitter cheeses came forth. Thus I saw, as it were, a woman having in her womb what was like the complete form of a human being.

And behold, through the hidden ordering of the heavenly Maker, that same form gave a movement of living motion; and a fiery sphere, having none of the features of a human body, took possession of the heart of that form, touched its brain, and poured itself through all its limbs. Then, when that human form, thus enlivened, came forth from the woman’s womb, it changed its colour according to the motions which the sphere had within that human form.

And I saw that many storms assailed a certain such sphere remaining in a human body and bent it down to the earth; but, gathering its strength again and rising manfully, it stoutly resisted them. With groaning it lamented thus:

“Where am I, a stranger? In the shadow of death. And by what road do I go? By the road of error. And what consolation do I have? That which strangers have.

“For I ought to have had a tabernacle adorned with squared stones brighter than sun and stars; for neither the setting sun nor setting stars ought to have shone in it. Rather, angelic glory ought to have been in it, since its foundation ought to have been topaz, all its structure gems, its stairways set in crystal, and its streets paved with gold.

“For I ought to have been a companion of angels, since I am a living breath which God sent into dry clay. Therefore I ought to know God and feel him. But alas! When my tabernacle understood that it could see with its eyes into every path, it directed its instrument toward the north. Ah, ah! There I was captured and stripped of the eyes and joy of knowledge, my whole garment torn; and thus, driven from my inheritance, I was led into a foreign place lacking every beauty and honour, where I was subjected to the worst servitude.

[Col. 0415D] “Those who seized me struck me with blows and made me eat with swine. Sending me into a desert place, they set before me for food exceedingly bitter herbs dipped in honey. Afterwards they stretched me over a winepress and afflicted me with many tortures. Then they stripped me of my garments, inflicted many wounds upon me, and gave me over to poisoning, where the worst and most venomous serpents—scorpions, asps, and their like—captured me and sprinkled me all over with their venom, so that I became wholly weak and enfeebled from it.

“Therefore they mocked me, saying: ‘Where is your honour now?’

“Ah! Then I trembled all over, and with a great groan of sorrow said silently to myself: ‘O where am I? Ah, how did I come here? What comforter shall I seek in this captivity? How shall I break these chains? O what eye will be able to see my wounds? What nostrils will endure this foul stench? What hand will anoint them with oil? Ah, who will show mercy to my pain?

“‘Therefore let heaven hear my cry; let the earth tremble at my grief; and let everything living bow in pity toward my captivity, because most bitter pain weighs upon me. For I am a stranger without consolation and without help. Who will comfort me, since even my mother has forsaken me because I strayed from the way of salvation? Who will help me except God?’

[Col. 0416B] “But when I remember you, O Mother Zion, in whom I ought to have dwelt, I behold the bitter services to which I am subjected. And when I recall every kind of music that is in you, I attend to my wounds. But when I remember the joy and gladness of your glory, then I detest the poisons with which I have been infected.

“O where shall I turn? Where shall I flee? My pain is beyond number; for if I persist in these evils, I shall be the companion of those with whom I shamefully lived in the land of Babylon. And where are you, O Zion, my mother? Alas for me, because I departed unhappily from you. For if I did not know you, I would bear my pain more lightly.

“Now I shall flee my most wicked companions, because unhappy Babylon placed me in a leaden balance and crushed me under enormous beams, so that I can scarcely breathe. But when I pour out my tears and groans to you, O my mother, unhappy Babylon sends forth such a din of sounding waters that you do not heed my voice. Therefore with great concern I shall seek narrow paths by which I may escape my most wicked companions and my unhappy captivity.”

When I had said these things, I slipped away onto a narrow path, where I hid myself in a small opening toward the north, weeping most bitterly because I had lost my mother. There I considered all my pain and all my wounds, and, weeping and weeping, I poured forth such streams of tears that every pain and every bruise of my wounds grew wet, drenched by those tears.

[Col. 0416D] And behold, a most sweet fragrance, like a gentle breeze sent forth by my mother, filled my nostrils. O how many groans and tears I then poured out when I sensed that small consolation near at hand! And with abundant weeping I gave such cries of joy that the mountain in whose opening I had hidden was shaken by it.

And I said: “O mother, O Mother Zion, what at last will become of me? Where now is your noble daughter? O how long, how long shall I be deprived of your motherly sweetness—you who had gently nourished me amid many delights?” And I delighted in those tears as though I saw my mother.

But my enemies, hearing my cries, said: “Where is she whom until now we have kept in our company according to our will, and who has until now fulfilled all our will? Behold, she now calls upon the dwellers of heaven. Therefore let us summon all our arts, guarding her with such zeal and care that she cannot escape us anywhere, for we first made her wholly subject to ourselves. If we do this, she will follow us again.”

[Col. 0417B] But, secretly leaving the opening in which I had hidden, I desired to go to a certain height where my enemies could not find me. Yet they set before me a sea of such heat that I could in no way ford it. There was also a bridge there, so small and narrow that I could not cross by it. At the end of that sea, a height of mountains with such lofty peaks appeared that I sensed no path could be made there.

And I said: “O what shall I, wretched one, now do? I had for a little while sensed the sweetness of my mother, and therefore thought that she wished to bring me back to herself. But ah! Will she leave me again? Ah, where shall I turn? For if I now return to my former captivity, I shall be even more a mockery to my enemies than before, because I faithfully cried out to my mother, and because I briefly tasted the sweetness of her gentleness, only now to be abandoned by her again.”

Yet through that sweetness which I had previously sensed coming from my mother, I still had such strength that I turned eastward and began again to attempt the narrowest paths. But those paths were so enclosed by thorns, briars, and other such obstacles that I could scarcely set any footstep upon them. Nevertheless, passing through them at last with great labour and sweat, I incurred such exhaustion from that effort that I could scarcely breathe.

[Col. 0417D] Finally, escaping with utmost weariness to the summit of the mountain in which I had earlier hidden, I bent myself toward its valley. As I wished to descend, asps, scorpions, dragons, and other such serpents came together against me and sent out their hisses. Terrified, I uttered very great cries, saying: “O mother, where are you? I would suffer less if I had not first felt the sweetness of your visitation, for now I shall again fall into that captivity in which I long lay. Where, then, is your help now?”

Then I heard my mother’s voice saying to me:

“O daughter, run: for wings have been given you for flight by the strongest Giver, whom none can resist. Therefore swiftly fly over all these adversities.”

Strengthened by much consolation, I took up those wings and swiftly leapt over all those poisonous and deadly things.

[Col. 0418A] And I came to a certain tabernacle whose interior was wholly made of the strongest steel. Entering it, I performed works of light, whereas I had formerly done works of darkness. In that tabernacle, on the north side, I set up a column of unpolished iron, from which I hung fans of diverse feathers moving this way and that; and, finding manna, I ate it.

To the east I built a stronghold of squared stones; lighting a fire within it, I drank wine scented with myrrh together with new wine. But to the south I constructed a tower of squared stones, in which I hung shields of red colour and placed in its windows trumpets made of ivory. In the middle of that tower I poured out honey, from which I made precious ointment with other spices, so that a most powerful fragrance spread from it through the whole enclosure of the tabernacle.

But on the west side I placed no work, because that side faced the world.

Meanwhile, while I was occupied with this labour, my enemies seized their quivers and attacked my tabernacle with their arrows. Yet because of my absorption in the work I was doing, I did not heed their madness until they had filled the doors of the tabernacle with arrows. Still, none of the arrows injured the door or could penetrate the steel of the tabernacle; therefore I could not be harmed by them.

[Col. 0418C] Perceiving this, they sent out a great flood of waters in order to cast down both me and my tabernacle; yet they achieved nothing by this malice. Therefore I boldly mocked them, saying: “The craftsman who built this tabernacle was wiser and stronger than you. Gather up your arrows and lay them aside, for henceforth they will be able to obtain no victory of your will over me. Behold what wounds they display! With much pain and labour I fought very many battles against you when you wished to hand me over to death; yet you could not, because, armed with the strongest weapons, I brandished sharp swords against you and stoutly defended myself from you by them. Depart, then, depart, for you will no longer possess me.”

But I, frail and untaught, also saw that many storms rushing upon another sphere wished to cast it down, but could not, because it resisted strongly and gave them no place for their madness. Yet it said in complaint:

[Col. 0418D] “Although I am little and poor, I have nevertheless received a great office. Oh, what am I? And what is the complaint of my cry? I am a living breath placed in a human being, in the tabernacle of marrow, veins, bones, and flesh, so that I give life and growth to that same tabernacle and carry it everywhere in its movements.

“But alas! Its sensuality brings forth filthiness, lustfulness, shameless conduct, and every kind of vice. Ah, with what great groaning I lament this! For when I possess the prosperity of life in the works of my tabernacle, diabolical persuasion confronts me, entangling me in every respect and raising me into a breath of exaltation, so that I often say: ‘I wish to act according to the desire of the powers of my earth. For in my tabernacle I understand all works.’ But I am so hindered by its concupiscence that I do not discern my actions before I feel grievous wounds in myself.

[Col. 0419A] “O what lament I then utter! And I say: ‘O God, did you not create me? Behold, vile earth oppresses me. And do I thus flee in it? How? When my tabernacle has carnal concupiscence, then I have pleasure in the work while I carry it out.’

“But reason, which is strong within me together with knowledge, shows me that I was created by God; and in that reason I also feel that Adam, after transgressing the divine command, hid himself in fear. So I too hide myself from God’s face in fear when I perceive in my tabernacle works contrary to God. But when I weigh upon myself the leaden balance of sin, I despise all those works that burn in carnal desires.

“Alas, wandering one that I am! How shall I be able to stand amid these dangers? And when diabolical persuasion attacks me, saying: ‘Is this good which you do not know, do not see, and cannot do? What then will become of you?’ And when it again says: ‘Why do you abandon what you know, understand, and can do?’ What shall I then do?

[Col. 0419B] “In full sorrow I shall reply: ‘Ah, wretched me! For harmful poisons were breathed upon me through Adam, when he transgressed the divine command, was cast out onto the earth, and assembled carnal tabernacles. For through the taste which he tasted in the apple through disobedience, harmful sweetness enters blood and flesh and thus produces the pollution of vices. Hence I feel the sin of flesh within myself; but I neglect the most pure God, because I have been made drunk through guilt.

“‘But I ought not follow what the appetite of my tabernacle has within itself. For because Adam, in his first appearance, was created pure and simple by God, I fear God, knowing that through him I too was created pure and simple. But now, through the evil habit of vices, I am turned into unrest. O in all these things I am a stranger and wanderer!’

“Therefore storms of diverse sounds utter many lies which rise within me, saying: ‘Who are you? What do you say? What kind of struggles are these that you undertake? You are unhappy. For you do not know whether your work is good or evil. Where at last will you go, and who will preserve you? What are those errors which drive you to madness? Will you accomplish what delights you, or flee what distresses you? Oh, what will you do, since you know this and do not know that? For what delights you is not permitted to you, while what distresses you is imposed upon you by God’s command. And how do you know whether these things are so? It would be better for you if you had not existed.’”

[Col. 0419D] After those storms had thus risen in me, I begin to walk another way, which is burdensome to my flesh, because I begin to do justice. But again I doubt within myself whether this is from the gift of the Holy Spirit or not, and I say: “This is useless.” Then I wish to fly above the clouds. How? I wish to ascend beyond my understanding and begin things which I cannot complete.

But when I attempt these things, I stir up the greatest sadness within myself, so that I complete no work either on the height of holiness or on the plain of good will; instead, I feel within myself the unrest of doubt, despair, sorrow, and oppression in all things. And when diabolical persuasion thus disturbs me, O what calamity then overwhelms me! For every evil that exists or can exist—in reproach, cursing, the death of body and soul, shameful words against the purity, salvation, and height that are in God—all these things confront unhappy me.

[Col. 0420A] Therefore this iniquity also rises against me: that every happiness and every good, whether in humanity or in God, becomes troublesome and grievous to me, setting death rather than life before me. Ah, what an unhappy struggle thus assails me from labour to labour, pain to pain, schism to schism, taking every happiness from me!

But from what does the evil of these errors arise? From this, namely: the ancient serpent possesses cunning, deceitful craftiness, and the deadly venom of iniquity. In its cunning it brings upon me obstinacy in sins, taking my understanding away from fear of the Lord, so that I do not fear to sin, saying: “Who is God? I do not know who God is.” By its deceitful craftiness it brings me a hardening, so that I am hardened in evil. But by the deadly venom of iniquity it takes away spiritual joy from me, so that I cannot rejoice even in God; thus it induces in me the doubt of despair—namely, I doubt whether I can be saved or not.

[Col. 0420C] “O what are these tabernacles which endure such great dangers in diabolical deception?”

But when through God’s gift I remember what was created by God, then amid these oppressions I answer those diabolical persuasions in this manner: “I shall not strike frail earth; rather, I shall wage the strongest battles. How? When my tabernacle wishes to perform works of injustice, I shall defend myself by crushing marrow, blood, and flesh in the wisdom of patience, just as a strong lion defends itself and as a serpent hides in its lair, fleeing the stroke of death. For I ought neither to receive the devil’s arrows nor to perform the will of the flesh. How?

[Col. 0420D] “When anger wishes to rage around my tabernacle, I look to the goodness of God, which anger never touched. Thus I become more pleasant than the air which by its mildness moistens the dryness of the earth, possessing spiritual joy when the virtues begin to display their strength in me. Thus I perceive the goodness of God.

“But when hatred attempts to blacken me, I look to the mercy and martyrdom of the Son of God. Thus I restrain my flesh, receiving in faithful remembrance the sweet fragrance of roses which rise from thorns; and thus I acknowledge my Redeemer.

“But when pride strives to set up within me the tower of its vanity without the foundation of rock, and to raise in me that height which wishes to have no equal but always to seem higher than others—O who will then help me? For the ancient serpent, who fell into death because it wished to be above all, attempts to cast me down.

“Then I say in sorrow: ‘Where is my King and my God? What good can I do without God? Nothing.’ Thus I look to God, who gave me life, and run to that most blessed Virgin who crushed the pride of the ancient cavern. Thus, having become the strongest stone in God’s building, the most rapacious wolf, strangled by the hook of divinity, will henceforth be unable to overcome me.

[Col. 0421A] “Thus I recognize the sweetest good—namely humility—in the height of God and, among all, in the remembrance of the humility of the most blessed Virgin. I sense the sweetness of unfailing balm; rejoicing in God’s sweetness, I am as though amid the fragrance of every spice. I also cast down the other vices by the surpassing strength of humility.”

Then I, little and poor, saw that another sphere, drawing itself out from the features of its form, loosened its knots and extracted itself from them with groaning, sorrowfully burst apart its seat, and said: “I shall go forth from my tabernacle. But where shall I, wretched and full of grief, go? Along dreadful and terrifying paths to judgment, where I shall be judged. For I shall show the works that I performed in my tabernacle, and there I shall receive recompense according to my merits. O what fear! O what anguish I shall have there!”

As it thus loosened itself, certain spirits, both bright and shadowy, came—companions of its conduct according to the manner in which it had moved in its seat—awaiting its dissolution, so that, when it had been released, they might take it away with them.

[Col. 0421C] And I heard a living voice saying to them: “Let it be led from place to place according to its works.”

Again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “The blessed and ineffable Trinity revealed itself to the world when the Father sent into the world his Only-begotten, conceived of the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin, so that human beings, born amid much diversity and bound by many sins, might through him be brought back to the way of truth; so that, freed from the bonds of bodily mass, they might carry good and holy works with them and attain the joys of the heavenly inheritance.

“That you may grasp and judge this more deeply and clearly, O human being: you see the vast and most serene brightness, as though blazing with innumerable eyes and having four corners turned toward the four regions of the world. It signifies God’s knowledge—great in mysteries and pure in manifestations—shining with the deepest clarity and extending the keenest rays of fourfold steadfastness toward the four quarters of the world. There it most keenly foresees both those who come to be rejected and those who come to be gathered, showing the mystery of heavenly majesty; this, as you see, is displayed to you in the figure of supreme height and depth.

[Col. 0421D] “Within it there also appears another brightness, like dawn, containing in itself the radiance of purple splendour, because God’s knowledge also shows this: that the Father’s Only-begotten, taking flesh from a virgin, deigned to pour out his blood in the brightness of faith for the salvation of humankind. In this knowledge of God, good and evil are shown, because it is clouded by no obscurity of any thing.

“But you, O human being, say: ‘What can a human being do, when God foreknew everything that he would do?’ To this I answer:

“O fool, in the wickedness of your heart you imitate him who, first rejecting the way of truth, set falsehood against truth when he wished to make himself equal to the highest goodness. Who can conceal the beginning and end of all things from him who is, was, and will remain? But who are you? You are ash-dust. And what did you know when you did not exist? Yet, though you have a lamentable beginning and a miserable end, you contradict what you neither know nor ought to know: namely, the incomprehensible beauty of God’s justice, in which no suspicion of injustice is found, ever has been found, or ever will be found.

[Col. 0422B] “O fool, where do you suppose the father of iniquity is, whom you imitate? What is this? Pride inflates you above the stars and above other creatures, and you wish to be raised above the angels, who fulfil God’s commands in all things and above all things. But you will fall as he fell, who set falsehood against truth. For he loved falsehood, and therefore, enveloped in death, fell into the abyss.

“Therefore, O human being, attend. When you neither consider the love by which God freed you, nor heed how many good things God always bestows upon you, nor consider how he recalls you from death, you frequently fall into sins, where you love death more than life. But if at last you call to mind those Scriptures and teachings which your ancient and faithful fathers set before you—namely, that you ought to avoid evil and do good—if then you say from the inmost heart, ‘I have sinned grievously; therefore I must return with worthy repentance to my Father who created me,’ then your Father graciously receives you and, placing you in his bosom, embraces you with sweet arms.

[Col. 0422C] “But now you disdain to know that blessedness set before you by God, and refuse to hear or practise God’s justice. Would you not, if it were possible, call God’s judgment more unjust than just? Therefore, if you had not been redeemed by the blood of the Son of God, you would lie lost in perdition. But God’s judgment is true and just. Therefore, O human being, what advantage do you gain by rending yourself over my judgment?

“In the choir of angels and in my chosen vineyard is the praise of those who praise and say: ‘Glory to you, Lord, who are just and true.’ Nor is my judgment contradicted by them, because they are just. But what did it profit the devil to oppose himself to me? When he saw that he possessed much brightness, he wished to exalt himself above all; and an innumerable host of proud spirits consented with him. Divine power, in the zeal of its justice, cast them all down together with him. So also all are cast down who, in perseverance in evil, attempt to put God’s justice aside, because they labour to turn the highest good into the perversity of wickedness. Therefore God establishes nothing unjust, but has ordered everything right in the equity of his goodness.

[Col. 0423A] “Moreover, those human beings who rejected God in their unbelief, making idols for themselves, into which the devil entered and mocked them, arose in the madness of such vanity after the human race had passed on from those to whom Adam and Eve had told how they had been made by God and how they had been expelled from Paradise. Others followed them in the same perversity: they worshipped God’s creature rather than their Creator himself, and thought that things which do not live governed their life.

“Therefore let those still polluted in that same unbelief abandon their folly and faithfully turn to him who crushed the devil’s snares, laying aside the oldness of ignorance and embracing newness of life, as my servant Ezekiel exhorts, saying: ‘Cast away from yourselves all your transgressions in which you have transgressed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit’ (Ezek. 18).
