[Col. 0423B] “This means: O you who wish to persevere in uprightness in the sun of justice, whose paths blessed sheep run, cast from the conscience of your heart the questioning of those hidden matters which are useless to you in necessary and saving teaching—matters in which you wished to fly in vain loftiness, when you were plunged into the precipitous pit where no order dwells, but rather that dreadful confusion which does not know God. When you have done this, proceed upon the way of truth for your salvation, where you will find in your heart the newness of the radiant heaven and possess it as a life-giving breath in your spirit.

[Col. 0423C] “You also see people on earth carrying milk in earthen vessels and making cheeses from it. These are people in the world, both men and women, having human seed in their bodies, from which the race of diverse peoples is begotten. One part is thick, from which well-formed cheeses are made, because that seed, soundly and beneficially matured and tempered in its strength, produces vigorous people. Great brightness of both spiritual and bodily gifts is given to them in great fathers and exalted persons, so that in attaining prudence, discernment, and usefulness in life, they flourish clearly in their works before both God and human beings, because the devil finds no place in them.

“There is another, thin part from which weak cheeses are curdled, because this seed, imperfectly matured and tempered in its tenderness, produces weak people, who are generally found foolish, lukewarm, and useless in their works, both before God and in the world, and who do not seek God vigorously.

[Col. 0423D] “There is also a part mixed with corruption, from which bitter cheeses are made, because that seed, badly produced in the weakness of mixture and uselessly commingled, makes malformed people, who often possess bitterness, difficulty, and oppression of heart, from which they cannot raise their mind to higher things. Yet many of these become useful. Nevertheless, they endure many tempests and disturbances in both their hearts and their conduct, but emerge victorious; for if they yielded to their unrest, they would make themselves lukewarm and useless.

“Therefore God, restraining them, helps them and leads them to the way of salvation, as it is written: ‘I will kill, and I will make alive; I will strike, and I will heal; and there is none who can deliver from my hand’ (Deut. 32 [printed ‘Dan. XXXII’]).

[Col. 0424A] “This means: I, who am and have neither beginning nor end, destroy wicked people in their deeds—those who are weakened in vices through the filthiness of the devil and deceived in the regions of the unhappy seedbed by diabolical caverns. O how crafty is the viper’s jaw, which so inflates them that death enters into them! Therefore I take away from them the prosperity of this age, where they are killed by many hardships which they cannot overcome, but which are always present to them by just judgment.

“But I, who am cast down by no malice, often also make them live miserably in another condition: there, living within them, I draw their living breath upward from earthly things lest it perish in them. I also sometimes afflict them with blows, through much infirmity in the labour of their life—those who through pride wish to raise their minds to a height harmful to themselves, thinking that no one can cast them down. And I, who am present everywhere, sometimes raise them upward to true health, lest they be consumed in deceptive dangers through deceptive vanities.

[Col. 0424B] “But in all these matters there is no human being or other creature who can turn aside such works of mine by their own cunning or insolent power, because there is none able to resist my will and justice.

“Often also, as you see, in forgetfulness of me and in mockery of the devil, intercourse between male and female is committed, and there the deformity of people being born is found. Because their parents transgressed my commandments, they may return to me in penitence, afflicted in their own children. I also often permit this marvellous creation to occur in people for my glory and that of my saints, so that, when those who are deformed in this way are restored to health through the assistance of my elect, my name may be glorified by human beings all the more ardently because of it.

“But those who bind themselves by this law, so that they seek the honour of virginity, ascend like the dawn to heavenly secrets, because for love of my Son they cut away from themselves the pleasures of their bodies.

[Col. 0424C] “But what you see is like a woman having in her womb the complete form of a human being. This signifies that after a woman has conceived human seed, a child is formed with the completeness of its limbs in the hidden chamber of her womb.

“And behold, through the hidden ordering of the heavenly Maker, that same form gives a movement of living motion. For when, by the hidden and secret command and will of God, the child has received spirit in the mother’s womb at the divinely arranged fitting and proper time, it shows that it lives by the movement of its body, just as the earth opens itself and brings forth the flowers and fruits that belong to it when dew falls upon it.

[Col. 0424D] “Thus, as though a fiery sphere having none of the features of a human body takes possession of the heart of that form, the soul, burning in the fire of profound knowledge, discerns diverse things within the circuit of its comprehension. Having no form of human limbs, because it is neither bodily nor perishable as the human body is, it strengthens the human heart. The heart, existing as the foundation of the body, governs the whole body and, like the firmament of heaven, holds the lower things together and covers the higher. It also touches the human brain, because in its powers it tastes not only earthly but also heavenly things when it wisely knows God. It pours itself through all the human limbs, because it gives to the whole body the vigour of marrow, veins, and every limb, as a tree from its root imparts sap and greenness to all its branches.

[Col. 0425A] “Then, when that human form, enlivened in this manner, comes forth from the woman’s womb, it also changes its colour according to the motions which that sphere has in the same human form. For after a human being has received the living spirit in the mother’s womb, is thus born, and gives the motions of its activity, its merits correspond to those works which the soul performs with the body: from good deeds it clothes itself in brightness, and from evil deeds in darkness.”

It likewise displays its powers according to the powers of the body: in a human being’s infancy it brings forth simplicity, and in youth strength; but in full maturity, when all a person’s veins are full, it manifests its strongest powers in wisdom—just as a tree, tender in its first budding and then showing fruit within itself, at last brings it forth in the fullness of usefulness. But afterward, in a person’s old age, [Col. 0425C] when his marrow and veins have already begun to bend toward weakness, the soul displays lighter powers, as though wearied by human knowledge; just as the sap of a tree, when winter is now at hand, contracts within its branches and leaves, and the tree itself begins in its old age to bend.

Now a human being has three paths within himself. What are they? Soul, body, and senses: human life is exercised in these. How? The soul gives life to the body and breathes forth the senses; the body draws the soul to itself and opens the senses; the senses touch the soul and attract the body. For the soul furnishes life to the body, as fire pours light into darkness. It has two principal powers, namely understanding and will, as though two arms—not because the soul has arms with which to move itself, but because it manifests itself in these powers, as the sun declares itself by its radiance.

Therefore, O human being, you whom the burden of marrow does not weigh down, attend to the knowledge of the Scriptures. Understanding is fixed to the soul as an arm is to the body. For as an arm, to which the hand with its fingers is joined, is extended from the body, so understanding, together with the activity of the other powers of the soul by which it understands every human action, proceeds with complete certainty from the soul. For above the other powers of the soul it understands whatever is in human deeds, whether good or evil; so that through it, as through a teacher, all things are understood. For in this way the soul examines all things, just as wheat is cleansed from every impurity, investigating [Col. 0426A] whether they are useful or useless, lovable or hateful, or whether they pertain to life or to death. Hence, as food without salt is tasteless, so the other powers of the soul without understanding are insipid and undiscerning.

And it is in the soul as the shoulder-blade is in the body, the marrow in the brain, among the soul’s other powers; and, strong like the body’s shoulder, it understands both divinity and humanity in God. It is a certain bending of the arm, and likewise possesses right faith in its work; this is also the bending of the hand, by which it then distinguishes various works in judgment, as though with fingers. Yet it does not act as the other powers of the soul act. What does this mean?

For will heats the work, the mind receives it, [Col. 0426B] and reason brings it forth; but understanding comprehends the work, showing good and evil—just as angels possess understanding, loving good and hating evil. And as the body has a heart, so the soul has understanding, which exercises its power in one part of the soul, just as will does in another. How? For will possesses a great power of the soul. How?

The soul stands in a corner of the house—that is, in the firm support of the heart—like someone standing in a corner of his house, who, surveying the whole house, governs all the household implements, raising his right arm to mark out and indicate whatever is useful to his house, and turning himself toward the east. Thus too the soul acts through the streets of the entire body, looking toward the sunrise. For it places will, as its right arm, within [Col. 0426C] the support of the veins and marrow and within the movement of the whole body, because will performs whatever work there may be, whether good or evil.

For will is like fire, cooking every work as in an oven. Bread is baked so that people, nourished by it, may be strengthened and able to live. Thus will is the strength of every work, because it grinds in deception, adds leaven in vigor, and pounds in hardness; and so, preparing its work like bread in reflection, it bakes it into completion by the full operation of its ardor. In this manner it provides people with greater food in work than in bread. For a person’s food sometimes ceases within him; but the work of will continues within him [Col. 0426D] until his soul is separated from the body. And whatever great diversity there may be in that work—namely, from infancy, from youth, from full maturity, from decrepit bending—it nevertheless proceeds in the will and manifests its perfection in it.

But will has in the human breast a certain tent, namely the mind, which understanding, will itself, and every power of the soul breathe upon with their strength; and all these are warmed and joined to one another in that same tent. How? If anger arises, the gall is swollen and, sending smoke into the tent, brings anger to completion. But if base pleasure raises itself up, the fire of lust is kindled in its material, and that wantonness which pertains to sin is lifted up and gathered together in the same tent.

[Col. 0427A] But there is another, lovable joy, which is kindled in this tent by the Holy Spirit; the soul rejoices with it, receives it faithfully, and accomplishes a good work in heavenly desires. There is also a certain sadness, from which, in that same tent, torpor is born out of those humors that are around the gall, producing indignation, hardening, and stubbornness in human beings and depressing the soul—unless it is swiftly rescued by the aid of God’s grace.

And when contrary causes encounter that tent, it is frequently stirred into hatred and the other deadly things which kill the soul and prepare great ruin in destruction. But when the will chooses, it moves the instruments of its tent and sets them forth in fervent heat, whether they be good or evil. If [Col. 0427B] those instruments please the will, it cooks its food there and offers it to the human being to taste. Hence in this very tent a vast multitude of good and evil arises, just as when an army gathers in some place. But when the commander of the army arrives, if that army pleases him, he receives it; if it displeases him, he orders it to depart. So too does the will act. How? If good or evil rises up in the inmost breast of the heart, the will either brings it to completion or neglects it.

But in understanding and in will, reason is shown as the sound of the soul; it accomplishes every work, whether it be God’s or humanity’s. For sound lifts a word on high; and as wind lifts an eagle so that it can fly, so the soul sends forth the sound of reason both in hearing [Col. 0427C] and in human understanding, so that its powers may be understood and every work brought to completion.

The body, moreover, is the tent and support of all the soul’s powers, because the soul, remaining in the body, works with the body, and the body with it, whether the work be good or evil.

The senses are that to which the work of the soul’s inward powers adheres, so that those powers are understood through the senses in the fruits of every work; and the senses are subject to them. For the powers lead the senses to a work; the senses do not impose a work upon the powers, because the senses are their shadow, acting according to what pleases them.

Moreover, the outward human being first awakens with sensation in the mother’s womb before birth, while the other powers of the soul [Col. 0427D] still remain hidden. What does this mean? Dawn announces the daylight; so too human sensation declares all the powers of the soul together with reason. And as the Law and the Prophets hang upon the two commandments of God, so human senses flourish in the soul and in its powers. What does this mean? The Law was established for human salvation, and the Prophets reveal God’s hidden things; thus human sensation drives away whatever is harmful from a person and lays bare the inward things of the soul.

For the soul breathes forth sensation. How? It gives life to the human being with a living face, and endows him with sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch; so that a person touched by sensation may be fully alert in every matter. For sensation is the sign of all the powers of the soul, just as the body is the vessel of the soul. How? Sensation encloses all the soul’s powers. What [Col. 0428A] does this mean? A human being is recognized in the face, sees with the eyes, hears with the ears, opens the mouth to speak, feels with the hands, and walks with the feet. Therefore sensation in a human being is like precious stones, and like a precious treasure sealed in a vessel. But just as the vessel is seen and the treasure within it is known, so the other powers of the soul are understood in sensation.

Now the soul is the mistress, but the flesh the servant. How? The soul governs the whole body in giving it life; the body receives the governance of that life, because if the soul did not give life to the body, the body would dissolve in decay. But when a person knowingly performs an evil work, this is as bitter to the soul as poison is to the body when that body knowingly takes it. But the soul rejoices in a good work, just as the body delights in sweet food.

And [Col. 0428B] the soul enters into the body as sap enters a tree. What does this mean? By sap a tree becomes green, produces flowers, and afterward bears fruit; so too does the body through the soul. And how is the fruit of the tree then brought to maturity? By the temperateness of the air. How? The sun warms it, rain waters it, and so it is perfected in the temperateness of the air. What does this mean? The mercy of God’s grace enlightens the human being like the sun; the breathing of the Holy Spirit waters him like rain; and thus discernment, like a good temperateness of the air, leads him to the perfection of good fruits.

Moreover, the soul is in the body as sap in a tree, and its powers are like the form of the tree. How? Understanding in the soul is like the greenness of branches and leaves in a tree; will is like flowers [Col. 0428C] in it; the mind is like its first emerging fruit; reason is like fruit perfected in maturity; and sensation is like the extension of its breadth. In this way a human body is made firm and sustained by the soul.

Therefore, O human being, understand what you are in your soul—you who cast aside your good understanding and wish to be compared to beasts. But when you see these things, O human being, consider also that you see a certain such sphere remaining in a human body, while many whirlwinds assailing it bend it down to the earth. This means that, as long as a human being lives in soul and body, many invisible temptations disturb the human soul, repeatedly inclining it through the pleasure of the flesh toward the sins of earthly [Col. 0428D] desires. But gathering its powers again, it raises itself manfully and resists them strongly. For when a faithful and watchful person has sinned, he is often pierced by God’s gift, abandons his sins, places his hope in God, rejects the devil’s devices, and faithfully seeks his Creator—as the faithful soul, lamenting its miseries, also truthfully shows above.

But what you see—that very many whirlwinds rush against another sphere and wish to cast it down, yet are unable—means that very many devilish snares attack this soul and try to draw it into the sins of many crimes, but cannot prevail against it by their deceptions, because it resists firmly and gives them no place for their madness. Strengthening itself by heavenly inspiration, it drives [Col. 0429A] the missiles of deceitful deceptions away from itself and has recourse to its Savior, as it also declares above in the words of its lament, as has been shown.

And the other sphere which, as you see, contracts itself from the outlines of its form and loosens its knots means that this soul, abandoning the limbs of its bodily dwelling, leaves their jointed connection when the time for the dissolution of its dwelling comes near. With groaning it draws itself away from them and sorrowfully bursts its seat; for, withdrawing itself from its body in anguish, it allows the place of its habitation to fall amid great trembling, fearing the impending judgment of the heavenly Judge, because it will then experience the merits of its works under God’s just judgment, as it likewise reveals above in its lament.

Therefore [Col. 0429B] when a certain spirit is thus dissolved, bright and shadowy spirits come, companions of its way of life according to the manner in which it has conducted itself in its dwelling. For in that dissolution, when the human soul leaves its dwelling, angelic spirits, both good and evil, are present according to God’s just and true ordering. They have been observers of its works, according to the way it worked with its body while in its body, and they await its dissolution so that, after it has been released, they may lead it away with them. For they await the sentence of the just Judge concerning that soul at its separation from the body, so that, released from the body, they may lead it where the heavenly Judge has judged according to the merits of its works—as has also, O human being, been faithfully [Col. 0429C] shown beforehand.

Therefore, O my beloved children, open your eyes and ears, and obey my commands. Why do you despise your Father, who delivered you from death? The choirs of angels sing: “You are just, O Lord,” because God’s justice has no stain whatever; and he delivered the human being not by power but by compassion, when he sent his Son into the world for humanity’s redemption. For no pollution of dregs defiles the sun; likewise, no perversity of injustice can touch God.

But you, O human being, behold good and evil in contemplative knowledge. And what are you when you are filthy amid a multitude of carnal desires? And what are you when the most brilliant gems of virtues shine within you? The first angel despised good and desired evil; therefore he received evil in the death of eternal perdition, and was buried in death because he rejected what is good. But the good angels despised evil and loved good, seeing the fall of the devil, who wished to suppress truth and establish falsehood. Therefore they burned in the love of God, possessing the firm foundation of every good, so that they desire nothing except what pleases God, never ceasing in his praise.

But the first human being knew God and loved him in simplicity; receiving his command, he submitted himself to obedience. Later he bent himself toward evil, practicing disobedience. For when the devil suggested evil to him, he abandoned good and committed evil, and was cast out of paradise [Col. 0430A]. Therefore evil must be rejected in the perdition of death, and good embraced in the love of life.

But you, O human being, when you remember good and evil, are as though placed at a crossroads. If then you despise the darkness of evil, wishing to look upon him whose creature you are and whom you confessed in holy baptism, where Adam’s old guilt was cast down; and if you wish to flee the devil and his malice and follow the true God and his commandments, then consider how you have been taught to turn from evil and do good; and remember that the heavenly Father did not spare his Only-Begotten Son, but sent him for your deliverance. Pray to God that he may help you, and he, hearing you, will say: “These eyes please me.”

And if you then cast away weariness, running strongly in God’s commandments, he hears the cry [Col. 0430B] of your prayers everywhere. For you ought to tame your flesh and subject it to the rule of the soul. But you say: “I feel such great and heavy burdens in my flesh that I cannot overcome myself. But since God is good, may he make me good. How could I tame my flesh, being human? God is good; let him accomplish every good thing in me. For when it pleases him, he will be able to make me good.”

But I answer you: Since God is good, why do you despise knowing his goodness? For he gave up his Son for you, who delivered you from death through many afflictions and great labors. But when you say that you cannot perform good works, you say this in the injustice of iniquity. For you have eyes for seeing, ears for hearing, a heart for thinking, hands for working, and feet for walking; so that with your whole body [Col. 0430C] you can raise yourself up or bend down, sleep or keep watch, eat and fast. Thus God created you. Therefore resist the desires of your flesh, and God will help you.

For when you set yourself against the devil like a strong warrior against his enemy, then God delights in your contest, wishing you to invoke him steadfastly at every hour and in all your distresses. But when you do not wish to tame your flesh, you make it feast upon vices and sins, because you remove from it the bridle of the fear of the Lord, by which you ought to restrain it lest it go to perdition. Therefore you look toward the devil as he himself looked toward iniquity when [Col. 0430D] he fell into death. And he, rejoicing in your perdition, says: “Behold, a human being like us.” Then he falls upon you and establishes his ways in you, in the shadow of death, as pleases him.

But God knows what good you are able to do; therefore the Law was set before you according to what you are able to labor at. From the beginning of the world to its consummation, God wishes to take delight in his elect, so that, most faithfully adorned in the brightness of virtues, they may be crowned. How? A human being should resist the pleasure of his flesh in such a way that he does not dissolve into the delights of this world; nor should he live so securely as though he were remaining in his own house, because he is a pilgrim and his Father awaits him, if he wishes to return to him in heaven, where he knows him to be.

Therefore, O human being, if you turn your eyes toward [Col. 0431A] the two paths—that is, toward good and evil—then you are instructed, and you understand great and small things. How? Through faith you understand one God in divinity and humanity; and you also see that the devil’s works are evil. When you have thus come to know just and unjust paths, you are questioned through me: “Which path do you desire to take?” If you then wish to enter good paths, and if you faithfully hear my words, pray to God with constant and sincere prayer that he may help you and not forsake you, because you are frail in your flesh. Bow your head in humility; shake out those things in your works that are evil, and hastily cast them away from yourself. This is what God requires of you.

And if someone set before you gold and lead and said, “Stretch out your hand to whichever you wish,” you would seize the gold most eagerly and [Col. 0431B] leave the lead, because you would love gold more than lead. So you ought to attend more to the heavenly homeland than to the abasement of sins. But if you fall into sins, immediately rise through confession and pure repentance, before death rises in you. For your Father wishes you to cry out, weep, and seek help, lest you remain in the filth of sins. But if you receive wounds, seek a physician lest you die. Does not God often send storms upon people so that they may invoke him all the more attentively?

But you, O human being, say: “I cannot perform good works.” Yet I say: “You can.” And you ask, “How?” I answer: “By understanding and reason.” You will say: “I have no desire within me.” I answer: “Learn [Col. 0431C] to fight against yourself.” And you say: “I cannot fight against myself unless God helps me.” Hear, then, how you are to fight against yourself: when evil rises within you and you do not know how to cast it away, then, aided by the touch of my grace—for my grace touches you in the paths of your inward eyes—cry out, pray, confess, and weep, so that God may help you, remove evil from you, and grant you strength in good. For you possess this through the knowledge by which you understand God through the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

For if you were a worker for some human master, whenever you had to do something difficult for your body, would you not endure many things laboriously for your earthly wages? Why, then, do you not serve God for the sake of heavenly reward—God who gave you both soul and body? If [Col. 0431D] you wished to possess some temporal thing, how greatly you would labor in order to possess it, even for a little time. But now it disgusts you to seek what has no end. For as an ox is driven by a goad, so you must train your body by the fear of the Lord; for if you do this, God will not cast you away.

If some tyrant took you captive, you would immediately turn to one who could help you, entreat and beseech him, and promise him your possessions so that he might help you. Do likewise, O human being, when iniquity seizes you: turn to God, entreat him, pray, promise your amendment, and God will help you. But you, O human being, are blind for seeing, deaf for hearing, and foolish-hearted for defending yourself, because you account the understanding [Col. 0432A] God has poured into you and the five senses of your body which he gave you as nothing and vanity. Do you not possess understanding and knowledge? The kingdom of God may be bought, but it cannot be acquired in jest.

Therefore listen, O people, and do not despise entrance into the heavenly Jerusalem. Do not touch death and deny God while confessing the devil. Do not increase in sins and fail in good deeds. For you refuse to hear God when you refuse to walk in his commandments, and you run to the devil when you strive to fulfill your flesh’s desire. Therefore come to your senses and be strengthened, because this is necessary for you.

But let a faithful person consider his pain and seek a physician before he rushes into death. If he examines his pain and seeks a physician, the physician, once found, will show [Col. 0432B] him the bitter juice of a remedy, through which he can be healed: these are bitter words by which it is tested whether his repentance proceeds from the root of his heart or from the wind of his instability. And when he has tested this, he gives him the wine of compunction and repentance, to wash away the stench of his wounds; and he also offers him the oil of mercy, in order to anoint those same wounds unto healing. Then he also commands him to be diligent regarding his healing, saying: “See that you remain zealous and steadfast in this medicine, and do not grow weary of it, for your wounds are grave.”

But many scarcely undertake repentance for their sins, and although they perform it with much labor, they do so because of fear of death. Yet I stretch out my hand to them and turn that bitterness into sweetness for them, so that they accomplish that repentance for love of me with great tranquility, though they began it with great difficulty. But one who neglects repentance for his sins because he says it is difficult for him to chastise his body is wretched: he does not wish to look into himself, seek any physician, or have his wounds healed. Instead, he conceals the foulest bruise within himself and covers death with pretense lest it be seen. Therefore he is sluggish in tasting repentance, unwilling to look toward the oil of mercy or seek the consolation of redemption; and thus he hastens toward death because he loved death and did not seek the kingdom of God.

Therefore, O faithful people, run to God’s commands lest [Col. 0432D] condemnation by death seize you. Imitate the new Adam and cast off the old human being. For the kingdom of God is open to one who runs, but it is closed to one who lies upon the ground. Yet wretched are those who venerate the devil while disregarding God. How? Those who do not worship the one God in Trinity, nor desire to know the Trinity in unity. Therefore one who wishes to be saved must not doubt in the right and catholic faith. What does this mean? He does not worship the Father who denies the Son; he does not love the Son who does not know the Father; he does not possess the Son who rejects the Holy Spirit; nor does he receive the Holy Spirit who does not venerate the Father and the Son. Therefore unity in Trinity and Trinity in unity must be understood.

O human being, do you live without heart and blood? Likewise, neither the Father without the Son nor without [Col. 0433A] the Holy Spirit, nor the Son without the Father nor without the Holy Spirit, nor the Holy Spirit without them, is to be believed to exist. But the Father sent his Son into the world for humanity’s redemption and drew him back to himself, just as a person sends forth the thoughts of his heart and gathers them back to himself again.

Therefore Isaiah speaks, by the will of heavenly majesty, concerning this saving mission of the Only-Begotten Son of God, saying: “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it fell upon Israel” (Isa. 9). This means: the Word through whom all things were made, namely the Only-Begotten Son of God, who according to his divinity was always in the Father’s heart without beginning of time—the Lord, namely the heavenly Father, sent him into Jacob through the mouths of the prophets, when they faithfully foretold that this same Son of God would come into the world for the salvation [Col. 0434A] of human beings. Thus, forewarned and fortified by them, people might prudently supplant the devil and wisely avoid the wiles of his deceptions.

And thus the same Word fell upon Israel when this same Only-Begotten Son of God came into the lofty purity of the Virgin, upon whom no man had set his foot, but who kept her flower inviolate, so that he, born of a virgin, might lead back to the true way those who through deceptive blindness did not know the light of truth, and restore them to unfailing salvation. Therefore whoever possesses knowledge in the Holy Spirit and wings in faith should not transgress my admonition, but receive it by embracing it in the taste of his soul.

## FIFTH VISION

[Col. 0433]

### SUMMARY

Concerning the Synagogue, mother of the incarnation of the Son of God. Words of Solomon. Words of Isaiah the prophet. On the Synagogue’s differing color. On her blindness, and on what Abraham in her heart, Moses in her breast, and the remaining prophets in her womb signify. On her great size, like a tower, with a circle like the dawn upon her head. Words of Ezekiel. A comparison involving Samson, Saul, and David concerning the same matter.

[Col. 0433B] After these things I saw what seemed to be a female figure, pale from the crown of the head to the navel, black from the navel to the feet, and blood-stained in the feet; about her feet she had a cloud of the purest and brightest white. She was bereft of eyes, and held her hands beneath her armpits. She stood beside the altar which is before the eyes of God, but did not touch it. Abraham stood in her heart, Moses in her breast, and the remaining prophets in her womb, each displaying his own signs and admiring the beauty of the new bride. This figure appeared of such enormous size, like the vast tower of some city, having on its head, as it were, a circle like the dawn.

And again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: God imposed the severity [Col. 0433C] of the Law upon the ancient people when he commanded circumcision to Abraham; afterward he changed it into the grace of sweetness when he gave his Son, the truth of the Gospel, to believers. In this truth he soothed with the oil of mercy those wounded by the yoke of the Law.

Therefore you see what seems to be a female figure, pale from the crown of the head to the navel: this is the Synagogue, mother of the incarnation of the Son of God, which from the beginning of her rising children to their strength foresaw God’s mysteries under a shadow, yet did not fully disclose them. For she is not the ruddy dawn which speaks openly, but beholds it from afar in great wonder, as is said of her in the Song of Songs: “Who is this that comes up from the wilderness, abounding in delights, [Col. 0433D] and leaning upon her beloved?” (Song 8).

This means: Who is this new bride, who raises herself in most numerous good works through the wildernesses of the nations—who have abandoned the lawful precepts of wisdom and worship idols—ascending to heavenly desires more abundantly enriched by the delights of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and thus panting with great zeal and leaning upon her bridegroom, namely the Son of God? For she is the one endowed by the Son of God, shining in splendid virtues and abounding in the streams of the Scriptures.

And this same Synagogue, in great wonder concerning the children of that new bride, asks my servant Isaiah thus: “Who are these that fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows?” (Isa. 60). This means: Who are these who, withdrawing in their minds from earthly and carnal desires, fly to heavenly things with full longing and full devotion, and in dove-like simplicity, without the bitterness of gall, strengthen the senses of their bodies and with great ardor seek the defense of the most steadfast rock, which is the Only-Begotten Son of God? These are they who, for love of heaven, tread earthly kingdoms underfoot and seek heavenly ones.

Therefore the Synagogue marveled at the new bride, which is the Church, because she did not recognize herself as adorned with such similar virtues as she saw in the Church; for the Church is surrounded by angelic protections, lest the devil tear her apart and cast her down, while the Synagogue, abandoned by God, lies in vices.

Therefore you also see her black from the navel to the feet: that is, from the strength of her expansion to the completion of her duration, she was foul in the violation of the Law and in transgressing the covenant of her fathers, because in many ways she neglected the divine commands, following the pleasure of her flesh. And she is bloodstained in her feet, but around her feet she has a most white and pure cloud [Col. 0434D], because at her consummation she killed the Prophet of prophets, where she herself also fell and collapsed. Yet in that same consummation, most radiant and lucid faith rises in the minds of believers; for where the Synagogue came to an end, the Church rose, [Col. 0435A] when, after the death of the Son of God, apostolic teaching spread itself through the whole world.

That image is also blind, holding its hands beneath its armpits, because the Synagogue did not look upon the true light, when it held the Only-begotten Son of God in contempt. Therefore it covers up its works of righteousness, without casting them away from itself in weariness of good work and sluggishness, and carelessly hides them as though they did not exist. It stands beside the altar, which is before the eyes of God, but does not touch it, because it knows only the outer bark of the Law of God, which it received by divine command and divine inspection; but it did not touch it inwardly, because it abhorred it rather than loved it, neglecting to offer God sacrifices and the incense of devout prayers.

But Abraham stands in its heart, because he was the beginning of circumcision in the Synagogue [Col. 0435B]; and Moses is in its breast, because he brought the divine Law into the inmost hearts of human beings; and the remaining prophets are in its belly—that is, in the institution divinely delivered to it—as overseers of the divine commands. Each displays his own signs and admires the beauty of the new bride, because they showed the mighty things of their prophecy in wondrous signs and gazed in great astonishment upon the splendid nobility of the Church.

She herself appears of such magnitude as the highest tower of some city, because, receiving the greatness of the divine commands, she proclaimed the fortification and defence of a noble and chosen city. Upon her head she has, as it were, a circle resembling the dawn [Col. 0435C], because the Church in her arising displayed the miracle of the incarnation of the Only-begotten Son of God and revealed the bright virtues and mysteries that follow. For she was crowned, as it were, in the first morning, when she received the divine commands, signifying Adam, who first received God’s command but afterwards fell into death through his transgression. So too did the Jews, who first received the divine Law but afterwards rejected the Son of God in their unbelief.

But just as humanity, through the death of the Only-begotten Son of God, was delivered from the perdition of death near the last time, so too, before the last day, the Synagogue, stirred by divine mercy, will abandon unbelief and truly attain the knowledge of God. What is this? Does not dawn rise before the sun? But dawn departs, while the brightness of the sun remains. What is this? The Old Testament has departed, and the truth of the Gospel remains, [Col. 0435D] because what the ancients observed carnally in legal observances, the new people practise spiritually in the New Testament: what those people showed in the flesh, these accomplish in the spirit.

For circumcision has not perished, because it has been transferred into baptism: as they were marked in one member, so these are marked in all their members. Thus the ancient commands have not perished, because they have been transferred to a better state. At the end of time too the Synagogue will faithfully transfer itself to the Church.

For, O Synagogue, while you wandered in many iniquities—so that you defiled yourself with Baal and other such beings, tearing apart the observance of the Law by most shameful practices [Col. 0436A], and lying naked in your sins—I did what my servant Ezekiel says, declaring: “I spread my garment over you, covered your shame, swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you” (Ezek. 16).

This means: I, the Son of the Most High, in the will of my Father, extended my incarnation over you, O Synagogue—that is, for your salvation—taking away your sins, which you committed in many acts of forgetfulness. And I established for you the remedy of salvation, so that I made known the paths of my covenant for your salvation, when I opened to you the true faith through apostolic teaching, in order that you might observe my commandments as a woman ought to be subject to the authority of her husband. For I removed from you the harshness of the outward Law and gave you the sweetness of spiritual teaching; and through myself I showed you all my mysteries in spiritual teachings [Col. 0436B]. But you abandoned me, the righteous one, and joined yourself to the devil.

But you, O human being, understand: as Samson was abandoned by his wife and so was deprived of his sight, so the Synagogue abandoned the Son of God when, hardened, it despised him and rejected his teaching. But after his hair had grown again—that is, after the Church of God had been strengthened—the Son of God in his strength cast down the Synagogue and disinherited its children, when they too were broken by zeal for God through the Gentiles who did not know God. For it had subjected itself to many errors of every kind of confusion and schism, and had defiled itself in transgressions of every iniquity.

And just as David at last recalled his wife, whom he had first betrothed to himself and who had defiled herself with another man [Col. 0436C], so too the Son of God will at last receive the Synagogue—which was first joined to him in his incarnation, but, abandoning the grace of baptism, followed the devil—near the end of time, when it abandons the errors of its unbelief and returns to the light of truth.

For the devil seized the Synagogue in its blindness and handed it over to unbelief amid many errors; nor will he cease to do this until the son of perdition. And when that one has fallen in the exaltation of his pride, as Saul perished when slain on Mount Gilboa—he who had driven David from his land—just as the son of iniquity will try to drive my Son out in his elect, then, Antichrist having been cast down, my Son will call the Synagogue back to the true faith [Col. 0436D], just as David received his first wife after Saul’s death. For when, at the end of time, people see that the one through whom they had been deceived has been defeated, they will hasten back to the way of salvation.

But it was not fitting that the truth of the Gospel should foreshadow the shadow of the Law, because it is fitting that carnal things should come first and spiritual things follow. A servant indeed foretells that his lord will come; the lord does not precede his servant in servitude. Thus the Synagogue came first in the shadow of signification, and the Church followed in the light of truth. Therefore whoever has knowledge in the Holy Spirit and wings in faith should not transgress my admonition, but should receive it by embracing it in the taste of his soul.

## Sixth Vision

[Col. 0437]

**Summary.—**That God wonderfully created and ordered his creature. On the appearance of the angels and its meaning. On the appearance of the archangels and its meaning. On the appearance of the Virtues and its meaning. On the appearance of the Powers and its meaning. On the appearance of the Principalities and its meaning. On the appearance of the Dominions and its meaning. On the appearance of the Thrones and its meaning. On the appearance of the Cherubim and its meaning. On the appearance of the Seraphim and its meaning. That all these hosts, with wondrous voices, resound those miracles which God performs in blessed souls. The Psalmist on the same matter.

[Col. 0437A] Then I saw, in the height of the heavenly mysteries, two hosts of heavenly spirits shining with great brightness. Those in the first host seemed to have wings upon their breasts and bore before them faces like human faces, in which human countenances appeared as though in pure water. Those in the other host likewise seemed to have wings upon their breasts and displayed within themselves faces like human faces, in which the image of the Son of Man shone as though in a mirror. But I could discern no other form either in these or in those.

These hosts encircled five other hosts in the manner of a crown. Those in the first of these five hosts seemed to have human faces, shining with great splendour from the shoulder downward. [Col. 0437B] Those in the second were of such brightness that I could not look upon them. Those in the third appeared like white marble and had heads like human heads; above them burning torches were seen, and from the shoulders downward they were enclosed as though by an iron cloud. Those in the fourth, having faces like human faces and feet like human feet, wore helmets upon their heads and were clothed in marble tunics. Finally, those in the fifth showed no human form in themselves, but reddened like dawn. I saw no other form in them.

These hosts in turn encircled two others in the manner of a crown. Those in the first of these hosts appeared full of eyes and wings [Col. 0437C]; in every eye there appeared a mirror, and in that mirror a human face; and they raised their wings to the height above. Those in the second burned like fire and had very many wings, in which they displayed, as though in a mirror, all the orders of ecclesiastical constitution marked out. I saw no other form either in these or in those.

And all these hosts, in every kind of musical instrument, with wondrous voices resounded the marvels which God works in blessed souls; through these they magnificently glorified God. And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

“The almighty and ineffable God, who existed before the ages, had no beginning, and will not cease to exist after the end of the ages, wonderfully created every creature by his will [Col. 0437D], and wonderfully ordered it by his will. How? He appointed some creatures to cling to earthly things, and others to dwell in heavenly things. He likewise disposed the blessed angelic spirits both for the salvation of human beings and for the honour of his name.

[Col. 0438A] “How? For he established some so that they might aid human needs, and others so that the judgments of his mysteries might be disclosed to human beings through them. Therefore you see in the height of the heavenly mysteries two hosts of heavenly spirits shining with great brightness, because—as you are shown in the height of those hidden things which bodily sight does not penetrate but the sight of the inward person beholds—these two companies signify that the body and soul of a human being ought to serve God, where they themselves possess the brightness of eternal blessedness with the heavenly citizens.

“And those in the first host seem to have wings upon their breasts and display in themselves faces like human faces, in which human countenances appear as though in pure water. These are the angels, [Col. 0438B] spreading the desires of the depth of their understanding as though wings—not because they have wings like birds, but because they swiftly fulfil the will of God in their desires, as a person swiftly flies in his thoughts. Thus through their faces they display in themselves the beauty of rationality, where God also clearly searches human works. For as a servant who hears his lord’s words fulfils them according to his will, so they observe the will of God in human beings and show him their actions within themselves.

“Therefore those in the other host likewise seem to have wings on their breasts and display in themselves faces like human faces, in which the image of the Son of Man shines as though in a mirror [Col. 0438C]. These are the archangels: they likewise contemplate the will of God in the desires of their understanding and display in themselves the beauty of rationality; they most purely magnify the incarnate Word of God, because, knowing the mysteries of God, they often foreshadowed by their signs the mysteries of the incarnation of the Son of God.

“But you can discern no other form in either these or those, because in both angels and archangels there are many secret mysteries which human understanding, burdened with a mortal body, cannot grasp.

“That these hosts surround five other hosts in the manner of a crown means that the body and soul of a human being, encompassing the five human senses by the power of their strength, ought to direct those cleansed through the five wounds of my Son toward the uprightness of inward commandments [Col. 0438D].

“Thus those in the first of these hosts seem to have human faces, shining with great splendour from the shoulders downward. These are the Virtues, ascending into believers’ hearts and building in them, in burning charity, a lofty tower, which is their works. Thus in their rationality they display the works of chosen people, and by their strength they lead them with great radiance of blessedness to a good end.

[Col. 0439A] “How? Namely, when the elect, possessing the brightness of inward perception, cast away all the wickedness of their evils because of the illumination by which they are enlightened in these Virtues according to my will, and fight strongly against the devil’s snares, these Virtues unceasingly show me, their Creator, the struggles which they thus wage against the devilish host.

“For human beings have within themselves struggles of confession and denial. How? This one confesses me, and that one denies me. But in this struggle there is such a question: ‘Is there a God, or is there not?’ [Col. 0439B] Then this question has in a human being the following answer of the Holy Spirit: ‘There is a God who created you and also redeemed you.’ And as long as this answer to the question is in a human being, God’s strength will not fail that person, because repentance adheres to this question and answer. But where this question is not in a human being, there is not this answer of the Holy Spirit either, because that person expels God’s gift from himself and, without the question of repentance, casts himself headlong into death. The Virtues offer God the struggles of these battles, because they are such a seal before God as shows with what intention God is worshipped or denied.

“Those in the second host are of such brightness [Col. 0439C] that you cannot look upon them. These are the Powers, signifying that no weakness of mortality can comprehend the serenity and beauty of God’s power or make itself like it, because God’s power is unfailing.

“But those in the third host appear as white marble and have human heads, above which burning torches are seen, while from the shoulders downward they are surrounded as though by an iron cloud. These are the Principalities, prefiguring that those who, by God’s gift, are princes of human beings in the world should put on the unalloyed strength of justice, lest they fall into the instability of changeableness. They should look to their head, Christ the Son of God, and direct their governments according to his will to the needs of human beings [Col. 0439D], attending above themselves to the grace of the Holy Spirit in the burning of truth, so that they may persevere firm and steadfast in the strength of equity unto their consummation.

“Thus also those in the fourth host, having faces like human faces and feet like human feet, wear helmets on their heads and are clothed in marble tunics. These are the Dominions, showing that he who is Lord of all raised from earth to heaven human rationality, which lay defiled in human dust, when he sent his Son to earth. The Son trampled the ancient seducer underfoot by his uprightness, so that the faithful may faithfully imitate him, who is their head, setting their hope upon heavenly things and fortifying themselves by a strong desire for good works.

“But those in the fifth host [Col. 0440A], showing no human form in themselves, redden like dawn. These are the Thrones, showing that the Godhead inclined itself to humanity when the Only-begotten Son of God put on a human body for human salvation. He had in himself no contagion of human sins, because, conceived by the Holy Spirit, he received flesh in the dawn—that is, in the blessed Virgin—without any stain of all defilement.

“But you see no other form in them, because there are many mysteries of the heavenly secrets which human frailty cannot grasp.

“That these hosts also surround two others in the manner of a crown means that those faithful persons who direct the five senses of their bodies toward heavenly things, knowing that they have been redeemed through the five wounds of the Son of God [Col. 0440B], attain to love of God and neighbour with every effort and turning of their minds, when they disregard the pleasure of their hearts and place their hope in eternal things alone.

“Therefore those in the first of these hosts appear full of eyes and wings; in every eye a mirror appears, and in that mirror a human face; and they raise their wings to the height above. These are the Cherubim, signifying the knowledge of God. Seeing in that knowledge the mysteries of heavenly secrets, they fulfil their desires according to God’s will. Thus, possessing the purest clarity in the depth of their knowledge, they wonderfully foresee therein those who, knowing the true God [Col. 0440C], direct the intention of their hearts’ desires toward him who is above all, as wings of good and just uplift, loving eternal things more than pursuing transitory ones, as they themselves show in the lifting up of their desires.

“But those in the other host burn like fire and have very many wings. In those wings they display, as though in a mirror, all the orders of ecclesiastical constitution marked out. These are the Seraphim, signifying that, just as they burn in the love of God, having the greatest desire for the vision of him, so also in their desires they display both secular and spiritual ranks, which flourish with great purity in ecclesiastical mysteries, because God’s secrets wonderfully appear in them. Thus all who, loving the heavenly life in the sincerity of a pure heart, seek it should ardently love God and embrace him with all desire, so that they may attain the joys of those whom they imitate so faithfully.

[Col. 0440D] “But that you see no other form either in these or in those means that there are many secrets in the blessed spirits which are not to be disclosed to a human being, because, so long as one remains mortal, one cannot perfectly discern heavenly things.

“But all these hosts, as you hear, resound in wondrous melodies in every kind of musical sound the marvels which God works in blessed souls, and through these magnify God greatly. For the blessed spirits, in the strength of God, utter with inexpressible sounds the greatest joys through those wonderful works in heaven which God accomplishes in his saints [Col. 0441A]. Through them they most gloriously magnify God, seeking him in the depth of holiness and rejoicing in the joy of salvation, as David, my servant and beholder of heavenly mysteries, testifies when he says: ‘A voice of exultation and salvation is in the tents of the righteous’ (Ps. 117).

“This means: the sound of joy and the prosperity in which the flesh is trampled down and the spirit lifted up, when unfailing salvation is known in the dwellings of those who cast away injustice and practise justice. Though, at the devil’s urging, they could do what is evil, through divine inspiration they accomplish what is good.

“What is this? A human being often displays unseemly exultation within himself [Col. 0442A] when he has committed the sin which he improperly desired to commit; but he has no salvation there, because he did what was contrary to the divine command. But that person will have the dance of exultation together with the prosperity of true salvation who vigorously accomplishes the good he ardently desired, loving, while dwelling in the body, the dwelling-place of those who, running the way of truth, have turned aside from the error of falsehood. Therefore whoever has knowledge in the Holy Spirit and wings in faith should not make light of my admonition, but should receive it by embracing it in the taste of his soul. Amen.”

## Second Book

[Col. 0441]

## First Vision

**Summary.—**On the omnipotence of God. The words of Job on the same matter. That the Word, before and after assuming humanity, is indivisibly and eternally with the Father. Why the Son of God is called the Word. That by the power of God’s Word every creature was raised up and humanity revived unto salvation. That God’s incomprehensible power fashioned the world and brought forth diverse species. That, when the other creatures had been created, humankind was made from the mud of the earth. That Adam, having received the sweet command of brightest obedience, did not obey at the devil’s counsel. That Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the other prophets struck back the world’s darkness by their signs. That John, the chief prophet, shining with miracles, foretold the Son of God. That when the Word of God was incarnate, that great and ancient counsel was made visible. That a human being ought not investigate God’s secrets beyond what he wills to disclose. That the Son of God, born into the world, overcame the devil by his death and restored the elect to their inheritance. The words of Hosea on the same matter. That the body of the Son of God, lying in the tomb for three days, rose again, and that the way of truth from death to life was shown to humankind. That the Son of God, rising from death, often appeared to his disciples to strengthen them. That, when the Son of God ascended to the Father, his bride was founded with diverse ornaments.

[Col. 0441B] And I, an unlearned human being, not instructed in letters after the manner of strong lions, nor taught through their infusion, but remaining in softness, a frail rib, imbued with mystical inspiration, saw something like a most radiant fire, incomprehensible, unquenchable, wholly living and wholly life itself. Within itself it had a flame of an airy colour, which burned ardently with a gentle breath; and it clung to that radiant fire as inseparably as the entrails cling within a human being.

And I saw that the flashing flame glowed, and behold: dark air, round and of great magnitude, suddenly arose. Upon it that flame struck certain blows, drawing a spark from it each time, until the air was brought to perfection; and so heaven and earth shone forth in complete formation. Then that same flame [Col. 0441C], in that fire and heat, extended itself toward a small clod of muddy earth lying in the depth of the air, warming it; and so it made flesh and blood, and breathed into it, so that it became a living soul.

When this was done, that radiant fire, through the same flame burning ardently with a gentle breath, offered the human being a most white flower hanging in that flame, as dew hangs on grass. The person perceived its fragrance through the nostrils, but did not taste it with the mouth or touch it with the hands, and so turned away and fell into densest darkness, from which the person could not rise.

[Col. 0442B] Those darknesses grew in that air, spreading ever more widely. Then three great stars, joined together in their brilliance, appeared in those darknesses; after them came many other stars, both small and great, shining with very great splendour; and then a certain very great star, radiating marvellous brightness and directing its splendour toward the aforesaid flame.

There also appeared upon the earth a brightness like dawn, into which the higher flame was wondrously infused, yet without being separated from the aforesaid radiant fire; and in that brightness of dawn a great will was kindled. When I wished to examine more carefully this kindling of the will, a secret seal was set upon me in this vision, and I heard a voice from on high saying to me: “Of this mystery you will be unable to see anything further, except what is granted you for the miracle of faith.”

And I saw a most splendid human being come forth from that same brightness of dawn [Col. 0442C]. He poured out his brightness upon the aforesaid darkness and was reflected by it; and, turned into the redness of blood and the pallor of whiteness, he struck the darknesses with such strength that the human being lying in them appeared shining through that drawing, and so rose up and came forth.

Thus that splendid human being who came forth from the dawn, appearing in such brightness as human speech cannot express, stretched forth into the loftiest height of innumerable glory, where he radiated magnificently in the fullness of every abundance and fragrance.

[Col. 0443A] And I heard a voice from the aforesaid living fire saying to me:

“You who are frail earth and, under a feminine name, untaught in all the instruction of carnal masters—namely, in reading letters according to the understanding of the learned—but touched only by my light, which touches you inwardly with a burning like the burning sun: cry out, declare, and write these mysteries of mine which you see and hear in mystical vision. Therefore do not be timid, but speak those things which you understand in the Spirit, as I speak them through you, so that those may be put to shame who ought to show my people the way of uprightness but, because of the perversity of their conduct, refuse openly to declare the justice which they know, unwilling to abstain from their evil desires, which cling to them as though ruling them, causing them to flee the face of the Lord and to blush to speak the truth.

[Col. 0443B] “Therefore, O little one, though you are inwardly taught by mystical inspiration and are nevertheless suppressed by the male form because of Eve’s transgression, speak the fiery work shown to you in most certain vision. For the living God, who created all things through his Word, has through that same incarnate Word restored to faithful salvation the wretched human creature which plunged itself into darkness.

“What is this? That most radiant fire which you see signifies almighty and living God, who in his most bright serenity is never darkened by any iniquity, remaining incomprehensible because he cannot be divided by any division, nor comprehended as he is by the beginning or end or any spark of knowledge of his creature. He is unquenchable, because he is that fullness which no end has ever touched; wholly living, because nothing at all is hidden from him that he does not know; and wholly life, because everything that lives receives life from him. As Job, inspired through me, shows when he says: ‘Who does not know that the hand of the Lord has made all these things, in whose hand is the soul of every living thing and the spirit of all human flesh?’ (Job 12).

[Col. 0443C] “What is this? No creature is so dull in its nature as not to know the reciprocal ordering of its fullness in those causes in which it fruitfully subsists. How? Heaven has light, light has air, air has birds, and earth nourishes growing things; growing things have fruit, fruit has animals. All these testify that the strongest hand—that is, the greatest power—of the Lord of all established them, he who has so worked all things in the possibility of his power that nothing is lacking to them in their uses.

[Col. 0443D] “And in the omnipotence of that same Maker is the movement of all living earthly things: of beasts which seek earth in earthly things and do not have in themselves the rationality of God’s breath; and the stirring of spirits which inhabit human flesh, in whom are rationality, discernment, and wisdom. How? The soul moves about in earthly affairs, labouring amid many varieties according to what carnal habits demand. But the spirit raises itself in two ways: either having sighing, groaning, and desire toward God, or seeking lordship, governance, and choice in diverse matters as though by command, because it has discernment in rationality.

[Col. 0444A] “Thus the human being also contains within himself a likeness of heaven and earth. He has a sphere in which clarity, breath, and rationality appear, as the luminaries are marked in heaven. He has a spirit moving swiftly through every perception and motion, as birds do in the air; likewise, he has a receptacle of moisture, in which moisture is marked, and generation and childbirth appear, as growing things, fruit-bearing things, and animals appear in the earth. What is this? O human being, you are wholly in every creature and forget your Creator; the creature subject to you obeys him as has been appointed for it, while you transgress his commands.

“But you see that the same fire has within itself a flame of airy colour, which burns ardently with a gentle breath and is present in that radiant fire as inseparably as entrails are in a human being [Col. 0444B]. This is the infinite Word, established in eternity before the times of created things, which, in the burning of charity, in the course of passing times, was to be incarnate wondrously, without the defilement and burden of sin, through the power of the sweetness of the Holy Spirit in the dawn of blessed virginity. Yet, just as before assuming flesh it was indivisibly in the Father, so after assuming humanity it remained inseparably in him; for as a human being is not without the vital touch in the path of the inner organs, so his living Word was not to be separated at all from the Father.

“And why is it called the Word? Because, just as by a local word—which, in the earthly dust of a human being, is transitory—the commands of a teacher are intelligently understood by those who know and foresee the command of the one commanding; so also, through the non-local Word, which is imperishable through the unquenchable life that lives in eternity, the power of the Father is truly known by the diverse creatures of the world who perceive and understand him at the origin in which they were created. And as authority and honour of a human being are known through an official word, so the holiness and goodness of the Father shine forth through the divine Word.

[Col. 0444C] “That you see how the flashing flame glows means that the Word of God displays its power as though burning forth, when every creature was created through it; and it glowed when it was incarnate in the dawn and whiteness of virginity. From it all virtues flowed forth in the knowledge of God, when the human being came to life again in the salvation of souls.

“But dark, round air of great magnitude suddenly arose. This is the material of things in the darkness of imperfection, not yet illuminated by the fullness of creatures. It is round because it is under the incomprehensible power of God, whose divinity is absent nowhere; yet, rising in God’s greatest power as though in the blink of an eye, it was raised in the heavenly will. Upon it that flame struck certain blows as a craftsman would, drawing a spark from it again and again until the same air was brought to perfection, because heaven and earth shone forth in full formation. For he who surpasses every creature, the heavenly Word, showed from his material the strength of his power in the creation of creatures that hold service [Col. 0445A], drawing forth diverse species of creatures shining in the wondrous beginning of their formation, as a craftsman suitably hammers out his forms from bronze, until those creatures shone in the beauty of their fullness, possessing above and below the beauty and stability of their perfect creation, because higher things shone from lower things and lower things from higher things.

“That afterwards the same flame extended itself, in that fire and heat, toward a small clod of muddy earth lying in the depth of the air means that, when the other creatures had been created, the Word of God, in the Father’s strong will and in the love of the Holy Spirit’s heavenly sweetness, looked upon the frail material of the soft and tender fragility of humanity—of all humans, both evil and good, who were to be begotten—held in the depth of its insensibility and heaviness [Col. 0445B], and not yet stirred by an effective and life-giving breath. Cherishing and warming it, it made flesh and blood by infusing heat into it by its power. For earth is the human being’s carnal material, nourishing the person with its fruit as a mother does her children with milk. And God breathed into it, so that the human being became a living soul, because he stirred it by heavenly power and wonderfully brought forth from it a human being endowed with discernment in soul and body.

Then that radiant fire, through that flame burning ardently with a gentle breath, offered to that same man a most white flower hanging in that flame [Col. 0445C], as dew hangs upon grass. For when Adam had been created, the Father, who is the most radiant light, gave through his Word in the Holy Spirit to Adam himself the sweet commandment of most brilliant obedience, adhering to that same Word amid an abundant shower of fruitful power. For through that Word the most gentle moisture of holiness dripped from the Father in the Holy Spirit, producing the greatest and most plentiful fruit, just as pure moisture descending upon grass makes it fruitful for much sprouting.

Man indeed perceived its fragrance with his nostrils, but did not taste it with his mouth, nor handle it in his conduct. For he drew in the commandment of the law with the understanding of wisdom as though through his nostrils; but he did not perfectly admit into his mouth the power of its inward perfection, nor [Col. 0445D] fulfil it by the work of his hands in the fullness of blessedness. Thus he turned away and fell into the densest darkness, from which he was unable to raise himself; because, at the devil’s suggestion, he turned his back upon the divine commandment and fell into the abyss of death, since he did not seek God either in faith or in deed. Therefore, burdened by sins, he could not rise to the true knowledge of him until he came who obeyed his Father wholly and without sin.

But those darknesses increased, spreading more and more widely in that air: the power of death in the world continually grew in the breadth of vices, as human knowledge moved into the diversity of manifold vices and foul sins arising through error. But the three great stars which appeared in those darknesses, joined to one another in their brightness [Col. 0446A], followed by many others, both small and great, shining with abundant splendor—these are, as a figure of the heavenly Trinity, the great luminaries, namely Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, mutually embracing one another both in faithful action and in kinship of flesh, and striking back the darknesses of the world by their proclamations. After them came very many other prophets, greater and lesser, shining in great and wonderful miracles.

Then there appeared a certain very great star, glittering with wondrous brightness and directing its radiance toward the aforesaid flame. This is the chief prophet John, namely the Baptist, gleaming in mighty deeds by most faithful and brilliant works, and showing in them the true Word, that is, the Son of God; for he did not yield to iniquity [Col. 0446B], but vigorously and bravely trampled it down by works of righteousness.

But the brightness which appears in that earth like the dawn, into which the higher flame is wondrously infused, yet not separated from the aforesaid radiant fire, means this: God planted in the place of generated things a great splendor of glowing light, sending his Word into it with perfect will, yet not separated from him; and he gave him as abundant fruit and brought him forth as a great fountain, from which every faithful throat that drinks no longer dries up with thirst. Hence a supreme will was kindled in that brightness of dawn, because in the clarity of rosy serenity the power of the great and ancient counsel was made known, so that [Col. 0446C] all the foregoing legions and ranks of heavenly spirits wondered at this in most radiant felicity.

But you, O human being, while you desire more fully to know, in a human fashion, the exalted character of this counsel, the enclosure of hiddenness is set before you. For you must not search out God’s secrets beyond what it pleases the divine majesty to reveal for the sake of those who faithfully believe in love.

And the most splendid man whom you see coming forth from the brightness of dawn, pouring out his brilliance upon the darknesses and being reflected back by them, who, changed into the redness of blood and the pallor of whiteness, struck back those darknesses with such strength that the man lying in them shone forth at his very touch and thus rose and went out—this signifies the Word of God [Col. 0446D], incarnate inviolate in the whiteness of uncorrupted virginity and born without pain, yet not separated from the Father. How so? When the Son of God was born in the world from his mother, he appeared in heaven in the Father; and therefore the angels immediately trembled and, exulting, sang honey-sweet praises.

That Son of God, having lived in the world without the stain of sin, sent the most radiant teaching of blessedness and salvation into the darknesses of unbelief. But, rejected by the unbelieving people and led to his Passion, he shed his rosy blood and bodily tasted the gloom of death. Having thereby overcome the devil, he delivered from hell his elect who had been held and cast down in it; and by the touch of his redemption he mercifully restored them to their inheritance, which they had lost in Adam [Col. 0447A].

When they came into their inheritance, drums and lyres were awakened, and every harmony of musicians in innumerable beauty; for the human being who had lain in perdition, now raised up in blessedness, had escaped death, freed by heavenly power. As I spoke through my servant Hosea:

> The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is hidden.  
> The pains of a woman in labor shall come upon him;  
> he is an unwise son.  
> For he will not now stand in the breaking of children.  
> From the hand of death I will free them;  
> from death I will redeem them.  
> I will be your death, O death;  
> I will be your bite, O hell.  
> (Hos. 13)

What is this? The perversity of the devil’s wickedness is bound with the efficacy of a binding, so that it does not deserve to be released from the zeal of God’s wrath; for he never saw him thinking rightly, nor do those who faithfully fear God behold him [Col. 0447B]. For he always raises himself against God, calling himself God, always erring against God and, because of this, opposing the Christian name.

Therefore his malice has sunk so deeply that his sin, which he impiously committed in most contemptible pride, is not worthy of any healing restoration unto salvation. Thus he will remain in enduring pain, like a woman in the affliction of laboring desperation who distrusts that she can live when her womb is opened. For this misery will always remain upon him: he was cast out from blessedness, because the wisdom of children has fled from one who does not return to himself, as the prodigal son returned to himself and, leaving his iniquity, went back to his father.

Therefore he will never trust in that contrition by which the children of salvation, in the death of the heavenly Son, crush the death of most savage iniquity—the death which that cunning serpent caused to boil up when he suggested to the first human being the deceitfulness which man did not know [Col. 0447C]. But because the children of the Savior despise the deadly poison of that suggestion and look to their salvation, I will free them from the slavery of idols: from the slavery, I say, of idols which possess deception in the power of perdition, and in which unbelievers exchange the honor of their Creator, entangling themselves in the devil’s snare and carrying out their works according to his will.

And therefore I will redeem from infernal punishment the souls of those who worship me, namely the souls of saints and righteous persons. For no human being can be rescued from the bonds of the devil, in which he is bound with a most harsh death because of transgression of God’s commandments, except through the redemption of him who is to redeem his elect by his own blood [Col. 0447D].

Where I shall slay you unto destruction, O death: for that by which you think you live I shall draw out from you, so that you will be called a useless corpse. For you will lie cast down in your strongest powers, just as a body abandoned by the soul is utterly laid low unto destruction. For the fountain of living water will choke you, when blessed souls are mercifully snatched up into heavenly blessedness through the new man, who will be innocent of poisonous deception. [Col. 0448A] Hence, also, to your confusion, I will be your bite, O hell, when my power in great strength strips from you those spoils which you deceitfully seized. Thus you also, O death, justly despoiled, will never afterward appear full in your riches, but, pierced with wounds and lying prostrate in foulness, will bear your confusion forever.

But as you see that radiant man who came forth from the dawn appearing in such great brightness as human tongue cannot utter, it is shown that the most august body of the Son of God, born from the most beautiful Virgin and laid away in the tomb for three days, was illumined by paternal brightness to signify that there are three persons in one divinity; and thus it received the Spirit and rose in most shining immortality [Col. 0448B], which no human being can explain by thought or word. The Father showed him to the heavenly choirs with his wounds uncovered, saying: “This is my beloved Son” (Matt. 3), whom I sent to die for the people.

For this reason, beyond human understanding, innumerable joy was renewed among them, because the blind forgetfulness through which God had not been known was so cast down that human rationality, which had lain prostrate at the devil’s persuasion, was raised to the knowledge of God. For through the highest blessedness the way of truth was shown to humanity, in which it was brought back from death to life.

But just as the children of Israel, freed from Egypt, crossed the wilderness for forty years and reached the land flowing with milk and honey [Col. 0448C], so the Son of God, rising from death, graciously showed himself for forty days to his disciples and to the blessed women who longed after him and greatly desired to see him, in order to confirm them in faith, lest they should doubt and say: “We have not seen the Lord; therefore we cannot believe that he himself is our salvation.” Rather, he often revealed himself to them, strengthening them lest they fall.

And his stretching forth into the most exalted height of innumerable glory, where he radiates wondrously in the fullness of every abundance and fragrance, means that this same Son of God ascended to the Father, with whom, together with the Son and the Holy Spirit, there is the most exalted and surpassing height of unutterable joy and gladness [Col. 0448D].
