There the same Son appears gloriously in the abundance of most resplendent holiness and blessedness to his faithful people, who believe with pure and simple heart that he is true God and true man.

Then too the new bride of the same Lamb was presented to him in diverse adornments, with which she must be adorned in every kind of virtue, in the most valiant struggle of all the faithful people who are to fight against the cunning serpent. But whoever sees with watchful eyes and hears with attentive ears, let that person offer to my mystical words, which flow forth from me who live, the kiss of an embrace.

## SECOND VISION

[Col. 0449]

**SUMMARY.—**On the meaning of the mysteries of God. On the three persons. That humanity must never forget ardently to invoke one God in three persons. On the three powers of a stone. John on God’s charity. On the three causes of the human word. On the three powers of a flame. The words of Solomon. On the unity of essence.

[Col. 0449A] Then I saw a most brilliant light, and within it the human form of sapphire color, wholly aflame with a most sweet glowing fire. That brilliant light suffused all that glowing fire, and that glowing fire all that shining light; and the most brilliant light and glowing fire suffused the whole human form, being one light in one power and might.

Again I heard that living light saying to me: “This is the meaning of God’s mysteries: that it may be discerned and understood what that fullness is which has no beginning and lacks nothing, which by its most mighty power planted all the streams of the strong. For if the Lord were empty of his own power, what then would his work be? Certainly vain; and therefore, in the perfect work one perceives who its craftsman is [Col. 0449B].

“Accordingly, you see the most brilliant light which has no beginning and can lack nothing: it signifies the Father. And, within it, the human form of sapphire color, without any stain of the imperfection of envy and iniquity, declares the Son, begotten of the Father before times according to divinity, but afterward incarnate in the world in time according to humanity. The form is wholly aflame with the most sweet glowing fire; and this fire, without contact with any dry and dark mortality, signifies the Holy Spirit, through whom that same Only-begotten One of God was conceived according to the flesh and born in time from the Virgin, pouring the light of true brightness upon the world.

“But the fact that that brilliant light suffuses the whole glowing fire, and that glowing fire [Col. 0449C] the entire shining light, and the brilliant light and glowing fire the whole human form—being one light in one power and might—means that the Father, who is supreme righteousness, is not without the Son or the Holy Spirit; the Holy Spirit, who kindles the hearts of the faithful, is not without the Father and the Son; and the Son, who is the fullness of power, is not without the Father and the Holy Spirit. They are inseparable in the majesty of divinity: the Father is not without the Son, nor the Son without the Father; nor are Father and Son without the Holy Spirit, nor the Holy Spirit without them. These three persons are one God in the one complete divinity of majesty.

“The unity of divinity remains inseparably active in these same three persons, because divinity cannot be divided, but always remains inviolable without any change. Yet the Father is declared through the Son, the Son through the coming-to-be of creatures, and the Holy Spirit through that same incarnate Son. How so? The Father is he who begot the Son before the ages; the Son is he through whom all things were made by the Father in the beginning of creatures; and the Holy Spirit is he who appeared in the form of a dove at the baptism [Col. 0450A] of the Son of God at the end of times.

“Therefore let no human being ever forget to invoke me, the one God, in these three persons. For I showed them to humanity so that humanity might burn all the more intensely in my love, since for love of humanity I sent my own Son into the world, as John, my beloved, testifies, saying:

> In this the love of God appeared among us: that God sent his only-begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him. In this is love: not that we loved God, but that he first loved us and sent his Son as propitiation for our sins.  
> (1 John 4)

“What is this? In God’s loving us, another salvation arose than that which we had at our first beginning, when we were heirs of innocence and holiness. For the heavenly Father showed his love amid our perils when we were set amid punishments, sending his only Word among the children of human beings in perfect holiness, by heavenly power, into the darknesses of the ages. There that Word, having worked every good thing, led back to life by his gentleness those who had been cast down through the uncleanness of transgression and could not return to the holiness which they had lost [Col. 0450B].

“What is this? For through that fountain of life came the paternal love of God’s embrace, which led us out to life and was our helper in dangers: that most deep and sweet charity which teaches us repentance. How so? God mercifully remembered his great work and most precious pearl, namely humanity, whom he formed from the slime of the earth and into whom he breathed the breath of life. How so? He instructed life unto repentance, whose efficacy will never perish. For the cunning serpent deceived humanity by a proud assault, but God cast him down through repentance, which shows humility—something the devil neither knew nor performed, since he did not know how to rise to the straight path.

“Therefore this salvation of charity did not arise from us, since we neither knew nor were able to love God unto salvation. Rather, because he himself, the Creator and Lord of all, so loved the world that for its salvation he sent his Son, the Prince and Savior of the faithful, who washed and wiped away our wounds. From him also flowed the sweetest [Col. 0450D] medicine, from which all the good things of salvation stream.

“Therefore you too, O human being, understand that no instability of change touches God. For the Father is Father, the Son is Son, the Holy Spirit is Holy Spirit: three persons indivisibly active in the unity of divinity. How so? There are three powers in a stone, three in a flame, and three in [Col. 0451A] a word.

“How so? In a stone there are the power of moisture, the power of tangibility, and fiery force. It has the power of moisture so that it may not dissolve and crumble; tangible solidity, so that it may provide habitation and defense; and fiery power, so that it may be warmed and consolidated into its hardness. The moist power signifies the Father, who never dries up or comes to an end in his power. Tangible solidity signifies the Son, who, born of the Virgin, could be touched and grasped. The force of glowing fire signifies the Holy Spirit, who kindles and illumines the hearts of faithful human beings.

“What is this? Just as a person who frequently draws the moist power of a stone into his body is weakened by it to the point of illness, so a person who rashly wishes, through the instability [Col. 0451B] of his thoughts, to behold the Father perishes in faith. And as people make their dwelling in the tangible solidity of a stone, defending themselves from enemies by it, so the Son of God, the true cornerstone, is the dwelling-place of the faithful people, protecting them from malignant spirits. Further, just as glowing fire illumines dark things, burning whatever it rests upon, so the Holy Spirit drives away unbelief, removing every rust of iniquity. And as these three powers are in one stone, so the true Trinity is in one Godhead.

“Likewise, as a flame in one fire has three powers, so the one God is in three persons. How so? A flame consists in shining brightness, inherent strength [Col. 0451C], and fiery heat. It has shining brightness in order to shine, inherent strength in order to be strong, and fiery heat in order to burn. Therefore, in the shining brightness consider the Father, who spreads his brightness to his faithful by paternal kindness. In the inherent strength of the shining flame, in which the flame displays its power, understand the Son, who took a body from the Virgin, in which divinity declared its wonders. And in fiery heat perceive the Holy Spirit, who sweetly burns the minds of believers.

“But where there is neither shining brightness nor inherent strength nor fiery heat, there no flame is seen. So where neither Father nor Son nor Holy Spirit is worshipped, there he is not worthily venerated. Therefore, as these three powers are perceived in one flame, so three persons are to be understood in the unity [Col. 0451D] of divinity.

“Likewise, just as three powers are to be noted in a word, so the Trinity must be considered in the unity of divinity. How so? In a word there are sound, power, and breath. It has sound in order to be heard, power in order to be understood, and breath in order to be completed. In the sound note the Father, who proclaims all things by inexpressible power. In the power, the Son, who was wondrously begotten from the Father. In the breath, the Holy Spirit, who blows where he wills, and all things are brought to completion.

“Where sound is not heard, there power does not work and breath is not raised; thus neither is the Word understood there. So too the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not divided from one another, but work their work in unanimity. Therefore, as these three things are in one word, so the heavenly Trinity is in [Col. 0452A] heavenly unity.

“Thus, just as in a stone the moist power neither exists nor operates without tangible solidity and fiery power, nor tangible solidity without moist power and the glowing vigor of fiery fire, nor the vigor of glowing fire without moist power and tangible solidity; and as in a flame shining brightness neither exists nor operates without inherent strength and fiery heat, nor inherent strength without shining brightness and fiery heat, nor fiery heat without shining brightness and inherent strength; and as in a word sound neither exists nor operates without power and breath, nor power without sound and breath, nor breath without sound and power, but these adhere indivisibly to one another in their work: so too these three persons of the heavenly Trinity remain inseparably active in the majesty of divinity [Col. 0452B] and are not divided from one another.

“Thus, O human being, understand one God in three persons. But in the foolishness of your mind you think God so powerless that he cannot truly subsist in three persons, but can exist only in one, although you do not even see a voice subsisting without three things. What is this? God is certainly the true and one God in three persons, the first and the last.

“But the Father is not without the Son, nor the Son without the Father, nor Father or Son without the Holy Spirit, nor the Holy Spirit without them; for these three persons are inseparable in the unity of divinity. As a word resounds from a human mouth, yet the mouth is not without the word nor the word without life. And where does the word remain [Col. 0452C]? In the human being. Whence does it go forth? From the human being. How? While the human being lives.

“So the Son is in the Father, whom the Father sent for the salvation of human beings sitting in darkness upon the earth, conceived in the Virgin by the Holy Spirit. As he is only-begotten in divinity, so he is only-begotten in virginity; and as he is the Father’s only one, so also he is his mother’s only one. For as the Father begot him alone before times, so the virgin mother bore him alone in time, since she remained a virgin after giving birth.

“Therefore, O human being, understand in these three persons your God, who created you in the strength of his divinity and redeemed you from perdition. Do not forget your Creator, as Solomon also urges you when he says: ‘Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the time [Col. 0452D] of your affliction comes and the years draw near of which you will say: “They do not please me”’ (Eccl. 12).

“What is this? With your rational understanding remember him who made you, while in the days of your foolish self-confidence you think it possible for you to rise according to your desire into the heights, yet cast yourself down into the depths, and while you stand in prosperity fall into utter miseries. For the life which is in you always strives to be brought to completion until that time when it appears perfected. How so? From its first birth an infant rises to full stature, and then remains at mature age, leaving behind the wanton ways of foolish adolescence, only then prudently taking anxious thought, amid great cares, concerning what must be done in its affairs—something it did not at all do while foolish adolescence burned with inconstancy [Col. 0453A].

“So should the faithful person act: let him leave behind the infancy of conduct and climb to the summit of virtues, persevering in their strength; let him forsake the pride of his desire, which sprouts in the madness of vices, and in distress meditate carefully on what is useful to him after abandoning the infancy of childish behavior.

“Therefore, O human being, embrace your God in the strength of your vigor before the person comes who will purge your works, when all things will be made manifest and nothing concealed will remain, when times come which in their duration will not [Col. 0454A] fail. Of these do not say, murmuring with your human understanding, ‘They do not please me,’ nor say that you do not know whether they are in prosperity or affliction; for the human mind is always uncertain in this. Even while doing good, it is anxious whether such works please God or not; and while committing evil, it fears for the salvation of forgiveness.

“But whoever sees with watchful eyes and hears with attentive ears, let that person offer to my mystical words, which flow forth from me who live, the kiss of an embrace.”

## THIRD VISION

[Col. 0453]

**SUMMARY.—**On the building of the Church, which always bears her children in the regeneration of Spirit and water. That the Church at her birth was adorned with apostles and martyrs. That the Church is adorned in the priestly office and the distribution of alms. On the maternal kindness of the Church. That the Church, not yet perfected to the whiteness of her completion, will be brought to perfection about the time of the son of perdition. How the Church offers her children most devoutly in purity. That no perversity of diabolical art can darken the Church. That human understanding cannot fully behold the secrets of the Church. On Mary’s virginity. On the extension of the sacraments of the true Trinity. That each of the faithful has the ministry of angels at hand. On those regenerated in the faith of the Holy Trinity by Mother Church while she herself remains whole. A comparison of balsam, onyx, and carbuncle. That the most blessed Trinity appears in baptism, heaven being opened to the baptized; and, taking away the blackness of their sins, clothes each one in a white garment. On the Church’s lament over the error of her children. That two signs have been given to human beings for their defense. A comparison concerning a young man. Why a double law was not to be given to Adam. That the admonition of the Holy Spirit, appearing in Noah, threatened the ancient serpent; circumcision struck him on the jaw in Abraham; the Church bound him. What the three wings signify. That males who were not circumcised at the time of circumcision were transgressors of the law. As three causes were signified in Adam’s creation, so there are also three causes in a man in begetting children. That a woman who keeps her virginity in the love of God is greatly adorned by God. That a man refusing marital union for the love of God becomes a companion of the Son of God. Words of Isaiah the prophet. That Adam’s fall closed heaven to humanity, and that closure lasted until the Son of God. Words of the Gospel. Words of God exhorting. That in Abraham’s circumcision one member, but in Christ’s baptism all members, are circumcised. Words of the Gospel. That at every time and every age God graciously receives every sex, namely male and female, in baptism. That three persons must be present in honor of the Holy Trinity at a baptism: a priest and two persons who pledge faith for the baptized; and that these must not enter into carnal union with that baptized person. A comparison concerning an infant. That all sins are forgiven in baptism. That although the priest is a sinner, God nevertheless receives the office of baptism from him. A comparison concerning a rich person. In necessity, if a priest is absent, any faithful person is permitted to baptize, provided that the form of baptism is observed.

[Col. 0453B] After this I saw a figure like a woman, of lofty stature like a great city. She had a head crowned with wondrous adornment, and arms from which radiance hung down like sleeves, shining from heaven to earth. Her belly was like a net having many openings, through which a very great multitude of people entered. But she had no legs or feet; she stood only upon her belly before the altar which is before God’s eyes, embracing it with outstretched hands, while her eyes gazed most keenly throughout all heaven.

I could discern no garments upon her, except that she was wholly shining with the most radiant brightness and surrounded by much splendor. Upon her breast was something like a dawn glittering with ruddy radiance; and there I heard a song, sung about her amid a manifold kind of musical instruments, as about a dawn glowing intensely [Col. 0453C]. The figure spread out her brightness like a garment, saying, “It is necessary that I conceive and give birth.” Immediately there came to her, like lightning, a multitude of angels making ranks and seats for human beings within her, through whom that figure was to be completed.

Then I saw black infants creeping near the earth in the air like fish in water, entering the belly of the figure through the openings—which stood open for those wishing to enter. She groaned and drew them upward, and they came forth through her mouth, while she herself remained whole. And behold, that serene light, and in it the human form wholly blazing with glowing fire, appeared to me again according to the vision which I had seen before. Taking the blackest skin from each of them and casting those skins outside the way, it clothed each one in a most white garment and opened the brightest light to them, saying to each one:

“Put off the oldness of injustice and put on the newness of holiness, for the gate of your inheritance has been opened to you. Consider, then, how you have been taught, so that you may know your Father whom you have confessed. I received you, and you confessed [Col. 0454C] me. Therefore now look upon the two ways, one toward the east and the other toward the north. If, then, you look carefully upon me with your inward eyes as you have been taught in faith, I shall receive you into my kingdom. And if you love me perfectly, I shall do whatever you ask.

“But if you despise me, turning yourself away from me and looking backward, unwilling either to know or understand me—if, when I call you back, filthy in sins, to pure repentance, you return to the devil as though he were your father—then perdition will receive you, because you will be judged according to your works. For although I gave you good, you were unwilling to know me.”

The infants who had entered the belly of the figure walked in the splendor that surrounded her. And she, looking most kindly upon them, said in a sad voice: “These my children will again return to dust. Yet I conceive and bear many who weary and oppress me, their mother, with various assaults: attacking me with heretics and schismatics and with wars useless to themselves, with robberies and murders, adulteries and fornications, and with many other similar errors. But very many of them rise again [Col. 0455B] through true repentance unto eternal life, and very many fall through deceitful hardening unto the second death.”

Again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “The full structure of living souls, which is built in the living heavens from stones adorned with the immeasurable beauty of virtues, flourishes most fittingly in her children whom she embraces as a most capacious city: a most great throng of peoples, and, like a broadest net, a vast multitude of fish, in heavenly virtues, according as the work of faithful human beings remains vigorous in the Christian name.”

Accordingly, what you now see as a woman-like figure, of such vast size as to resemble a great city, signifies the Bride of my Son, who continually bears children through the regeneration of Spirit and water. The mightiest warrior has set her in the breadth of virtues to embrace and bring to perfection a great multitude among her elect; and she is like a great tower, since no enemy can prevail to storm her. She drives unbelief away from herself by contrary resistance and faithfully extends herself. In this mortal age, this is understood in that each one of the faithful provides an example to his neighbor, through which they work very many virtues in heaven. But when each of the righteous comes to the children of light, then in them will appear the good work which they performed—a work which cannot be known amid the mortality of earthly dust, because here it is obscured in the shadow of unrest.

And she has a head crowned with wondrous ornament [Col. 0455D], because at her beginning, when she was raised up in the blood of the Lamb, she was fittingly adorned in the apostles and martyrs, being truly betrothed to my Son; for in his blood she faithfully built herself into a faithful edifice of holy souls. Therefore she also has arms, from which a radiance like sleeves descends, shining from heaven down to earth. This is the activity of strength in priests who, with purity of heart and hands, offer upon the holy altar the most holy sacrifice in the sacrament of the body and blood of their Savior, in the power of good works. This is a most resplendent work for those who show mercy, who in generosity always provide assistance to every sorrow, distributing alms to the poor with the gentlest heart, and thus saying in their perfected mind: “This is not my substance, but that of him who created me; because this work, inspired by God, is presented before his eyes in heaven when it is fulfilled on earth through faithful people in the cultivation of the Church.”

But her belly is like a net having many openings, through which a very great multitude of people enters. This is her maternal kindness, open for the catching of faithful souls in the manifold height of virtues, in which believing peoples devoutly live through the faith of true belief. But he who cast his net for the catching of fish is my Son, the bridegroom of his beloved Church, whom he betrothed to himself in his own blood in order to repair the fall of lost humanity.

She does not yet have legs or feet [Col. 0456B], because she has not yet been brought to the strength of her established constitution or to the highest splendor of her completion. For near the time of the son of perdition, who will bring error into the world, she will suffer in her members, most abundantly, the fiery and bloody pressure of most cruel perversity. Through that calamity, having been brought to perfection by bloody wounds, she will swiftly run to the heavenly Jerusalem; and, since as a new bride she has sweetly arisen in the blood of my Son, she will enter by this ardor into life in the fullness of the joy of her offspring.

Yet she stood only upon her belly before the altar which is before the eyes of God, embracing it with outstretched hands. For she is always pregnant and bears her children in true washing, devoutly offering them to God through the most pure prayers of the saints [Col. 0456C]. Through the sweetest fragrance of discernment of hidden and manifest virtues, which are brought forth in the intention of the mind’s eyes, all pretence of simulation and desire for human praise being cast aside—as incense is cleansed of every injury of opposing stench—this good work is a most sweet sacrifice in the sight of God. In it the new bride frequently labors with all longing in the work of fruitful virtues, panting toward heaven and building, in thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and hundredfold fruit, the lofty tower of the heavenly walls.

Accordingly, she directs her eyes most keenly through all heaven, because no perversity can darken [Col. 0456D] the intention which she holds most devoutly in heavenly things: neither any persuasion of diabolical deceit, nor the error of a transgressing people, nor disturbances spread throughout various lands, where mad people cruelly tear one another apart in the unbelief of their frenzy. But the fact that you can see none of her garments means that human understanding, burdened in the weakness of its frailty, cannot perfectly behold her secrets. Yet she shines wholly in most brilliant brightness, surrounded by great splendor, because the true Sun has everywhere suffused her with the brightest inspiration of the Holy Spirit and with the most fitting ornament of virtues.

On her breast there is something like dawn, gleaming with red radiance, because in the hearts of the faithful the integrity of the most blessed Virgin, who bore the Son of God, shines with most ardent devotion. There too you hear, in many kinds of music [Col. 0457A], this song about her sung as though concerning a dawn glowing intensely red; for every voice of believers, as it is poured into your understanding, ought with whole intention to embrace in the Church the virginity of that undefiled virgin.

But the fact that the same figure spreads out her splendor like a garment, saying that she must conceive and bear, means that in the Church the sacrament of confession of the true Trinity is extended. For her garment consists in the protection of faithful peoples, through whom she will rise in the building up of living stones whitened in the font of the most pure washing. As she herself confesses, it is necessary for salvation that she conceive children in blessing and bring them forth in washing through the regeneration of Spirit and water. Therefore there immediately hastens to her [Col. 0457B], like lightning, a multitude of angels who make ranks and seats in her for human beings, through whom that same figure is to be completed. For every believing person has beside him the ministry of blessed spirits, to be feared and loved, preparing ascents through faith and places of repose in highest peace for those faithful persons in whom the happy mother Church is known to be brought to her adornment.

Then you also see black infants close to the earth, creeping in the air like fish in water, and entering the belly of the figure through the openings—which stand open for those wishing to enter. This blackness is that of foolish people who have not yet been washed in the laver of salvation. Loving earthly things, ranging everywhere among them, and placing their dwelling in their instability [Col. 0457C], they finally come to the mother of holiness. Beholding the dignity of her mysteries, they receive her blessing; through it they are drawn away from the devil and restored to God, entering the sacred constitution of ecclesiastical order in which the faithful person must be made blessed unto salvation, when they say within themselves: “I believe in God,” and the remaining things pertaining to blessed faith.

Therefore she groaned, drawing them upward as they came forth from her mouth, though she herself remained whole. For this blessed mother draws deep sighs when baptism with chrism is consecrated in the sanctification of the Holy Spirit, so that a person may be renewed in the true circumcision of Spirit and water [Col. 0457D], to be offered upward to the highest blessedness, which is the head of all. Thus, having become a member of Christ, a person is regenerated for salvation through invocation of the holy Trinity, as though through the mouth of blessed Mary. That same mother suffers no injury, because she will remain forever in the integrity of her virginity. This is the Catholic faith, for she was born in the blood of her bridegroom, the true Lamb, who was born from the most undefiled Virgin without any corruption of integrity.

Thus the Bride too will remain whole, so that no schism will be able to corrupt her. She must often indeed be afflicted by perverse people; but, by the help of her bridegroom, she always protects herself most strongly, like a virgin frequently assaulted in the desires of the flesh through diabolical art and the persuasions of many people [Col. 0458A]. Yet through her prayers, which she pours forth to the Lord, she is vigorously freed from their temptations while preserving her kindness.

So too the Church resisted the most wicked corrupters, namely the errors of heretics—of evil Christians as well as Jews and other unbelievers—who assail her and wish to corrupt her virginity, which is the Catholic faith. Yet she resists them manfully so that she may not be corrupted, because she always was, is, and will remain a virgin, while true faith—the matter of her virginity—remains whole against every error; just as the honor of a chaste virgin remains uncorrupted in the modest substance of her body against every touch of lust.

Therefore the Church is the virginal mother of all Christians [Col. 0458B], because in the hidden work of the Holy Spirit she conceives and bears them, offering them to God, so that they are also called children of God. And as the Holy Spirit overshadowed the most blessed mother, so that without pain she miraculously conceived and bore the Son of God and yet remained a virgin, so the Holy Spirit illumines the Church, the happy mother of believers: without any corruption she simply conceives and bears children, and endures as a virgin.

What is this? As balsam sweats from a tree; as powerful medicines hidden in an onyx vessel flow out from it; and as most brilliant radiance diffuses itself from a carbuncle without any impediment: so the Son of God was born from the Virgin without any obstacle of corruption; and so also the Church [Col. 0458C], his Bride, generates her children without any defilement of error, while remaining a virgin in the integrity of faith.

But the fact that you see how that radiant light, and within it the form of a human being blazing wholly with glowing fire, appears to you again according to the vision you had previously seen, means that the true Trinity in true unity—namely, the most radiant Father and, in the Father, his most sweet Son, who before time remained in the Father according to divinity but in time was conceived according to the flesh by the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin, as was shown to you in the truest vision—is now also shown to you for the confirmation of faith. For that same blessed Trinity appears, when heaven is opened, to those baptized in holy baptism [Col. 0458D], so that the faithful person may receive this faith: how to worship one God in true Trinity, which also truly appeared in the first sacrament of baptism.

And, stripping from each of them the wholly intact skin, and casting the skins outside the way, it clothes each of them in a most white garment and opens to them most brilliant light, speaking to each one words of blessed admonition. This means that divine power, beholding human hearts, mercifully takes away in the laver of baptism the unbelief of their crimes, and casts those crimes outside the Way, which is Christ. For in Christ there is not death but life, through pure confession and washing away of sins in him. Through him every believer is clothed in the brightness of salvation [Col. 0459A], and through him is opened to them the radiance of the blessed inheritance from which the first human being was expelled. Each is admonished through words of truth to put off the old habit of wickedness and to assume the new gift of grace unto salvation.

But the fact that the infants who had entered the belly of the figure walk in the splendor surrounding her means that those whose mother is the happy Church through the font of sacred baptism ought to remain in and preserve the divine law by which the same mother has instructed and adorned them. Otherwise, if they cast it away unfaithfully, they are again defiled by the sins from which they had been cleansed. Therefore she too, looking upon them most kindly, says in a sad voice that these her children will again return to dust. For that blessed mother, loving them with inward love and grieving for them from her inmost bowels [Col. 0459B], laments that those whom she bore in the laver of regeneration, having been made clean in heavenly things, again become filthy in sins by longing after earthly concerns. How? Because many receive faith outwardly but inwardly assail it with various vices, walking rather in the way of error than in the way of truth. Yet very many of them come to their senses from falsehood, while very many remain in wickedness, as that mother also shows in the words cited above.

For two signs of sealed law are known to have been given to human beings: circumcision among the ancient fathers and baptism among the new teachers [Col. 0459C]. Through these, ungrateful people are like an ox under its yoke; for although it may be corrected with the goad, it would nevertheless make a furrow for a cart if it were not bound to the yoke. In the same way, people would not walk in my paths unless they were bound by the yoke of their signs.

It is like this: if a certain young man were walking along a road and his father said to him, “Walk by the straight path,” but did not give him a sword or other weapons of war by which to defend himself if danger met him—what then? He would flee naked; he would neither dare nor be able to defend himself against the danger meeting him and seeking to hinder him from his way, but would hide himself, because he had not been marked with the terrible armor by which he ought to defend himself.

So my people would be naked [Col. 0459D] if they had not been baptized. Thus they appear terrible to their enemies, who see them marked with the chrism of baptism. By this sign they also resist strongly those who wish to destroy them, whether it be a human multitude or a diabolical battle-line.

But a twofold law was not to be given to Adam. How? I gave him a law in the tree, when he saw me in innocence of heart; but he despised me by assenting to the crafty serpent. This was so harmful that no mortal can see me with bodily eyes so long as he remains in this passing age. But because Adam transgressed my command, he and his race were without law until the time that foretold the nobility of my Son.

The admonition of the Holy Spirit appeared in Noah when the human race was hastening toward destruction [Col. 0460A]. There he raised the ark above the flood, because before the ages he foresaw that, after that wicked race which had defiled itself with most foul iniquity, a new offspring had to arise. For after Adam’s departure, his race, ignorant that I am God, wandered about saying: “Who is God? Who is God?” Then every evil arose among them, so that the ancient serpent ran among them with unrestrained power, persuading them to fulfil all his will.

For at that time he was released from the bond that held him, so that before the flood the admonition of the Holy Spirit did not oppose him with threats, as I opposed him in Noah, in whom a new offspring arose, when I instructed my people in such a way that they could not forget that instruction. For the admonition of the Holy Spirit first threatened him in Noah; afterward circumcision struck him on the cheek in Abraham; then the Church bound him in the last age until the world passes away on the last day.

But I permitted the devil to exercise his power in the world before the flood because of the ancient contest in which he conquered Adam, until he filled his belly with the corpse of every wickedness. I permitted this because my judgment is just. Therefore I also raised up the waters of the flood and killed the sinners, reserving Noah in my mystery, whom Satan himself could not despoil because he was above the flood in my will. And in the flood I designated the most upright shoot, namely my Son [Col. 0460C], announcing him beforehand to the new age: he who came silently into the world and made manifest that the holy Trinity must most truly be worshipped. How?

He showed three wings, signifying the holy Trinity: where you, Synagogue, will deny me; where a foreign people will receive me; and where you, Abraham, will be magnified. O Abraham, you are surrounded by circumcision; you are enclosed as by a wall in the Old Testament; you are adorned by the dawn of the sun, the Church. I gave circumcision to you and your race until my Son, who openly forgave human sins, came; and there the carnal circumcision of the old foreskin fell away, when the font of baptism truly bubbled forth in the sanctification of my Son’s washing.

But those of your race who, in the time of circumcision [Col. 0460D], were not circumcised at the time appointed them, whether they were younger or older, transgressed the covenant of my pact—except women, upon whom circumcision was not imposed. For a woman is not to be circumcised, because the maternal tabernacle is hidden in her body and cannot be touched by an external touch; and because she is under the authority of a man, as a servant under her master.

For a man has three causes in his work: desire, strength, and zeal. Desire kindles strength; hence in both there is zeal for labor and their burning will. This is like the fact that in the creation of Adam three causes were designated: the will of God in power formed the human being, and fulfilled this in great mercy when he made the human being in his image and likeness. In God’s will, understand the man’s desire; in God’s power, the man’s strength; and in the mercy of God’s will and power, the zeal of the man’s desire and strength.

In this way the human race is begotten from woman through man [Col. 0461A], because God too made the human being from the clay of the earth. As earth possesses, in the power of seed, the fruit of fields, so woman is set in the moisture of childbirth to bear children. What is this? A woman has a time when the moisture within her is revealed and diffuses itself in her with moist power and warmth. Otherwise she would not willingly receive the man, but, rejecting him, would not consent to his will and would not bear children.

For if she did not have the power of moisture in warmth, she would remain unfruitful, like dry earth that does not bend itself toward any fruitful use. Yet that power of moisture does not always have in a woman, in its warmth, the burning fire of desire, unless she is first touched by a man and knows the burning heat of desire. For desire in her is not as strong and ardent as it is in a man, who is strong as a lion in the desire to beget children. Thus he has the strength of desire and action, while the woman has only this task: that she is subject to the authority of his will, because she is occupied in the procreation of offspring until she brings them forth into the world [Col. 0461B].

But when she desires my Son, longing in his love to preserve her virginity, she is greatly adorned in his bridal chamber, because she despises the heat which she endures for love of him. Refusing to be dissolved by the fire of burning lust, she perseveres in chastity, because in her spiritual betrothal she rejects a carnal husband. With all desire she pants after my Son, casting away remembrance of a carnal man.

O dearest shoots, and O flowers sweeter and more fragrant than all spices, in whom soft and fragile nature rises like dawn to the betrothal of my Son, loving him greatly with chaste love—she is his bride and he her bridegroom—when this race of virgins loves him greatly, to be adorned in the heavenly kingdom with distinguished ornaments. But what now?

[Col. 0461D] When a man’s strength also refuses to enter a partnership of marriage, so that a man restrains himself in his vigorous nature for love of my Son, even while he flowers in the seed of children, binding his members lest they exercise the desire of his flesh, this is most pleasing to me, because in this way the man conquers himself. Therefore I will make him a companion of my Son and set him as a most serene mirror before his face, because he resisted the devil strongly—the devil who had drawn the human race to himself through the unbelief of most wicked filth.

To rescue humanity from his snare, I sent my Son into the world, born from the sweetest Virgin without any stain of sin, bringing the font of salvation. He, the innocent Lamb, consecrated it, so that the foreskin of the old crime might be abolished in it [Col. 0462A]. What is this? The most bitter foreskin is the guilt of Adam’s transgression, which my Son removed when he entered the font of salvation and most nobly dedicated the Christian host, so that the ancient serpent who had deceived the human being might be drowned in that washing.

How? The Son answers to the condition of his Father and also retains his inheritance. What is this? Adam’s race was expelled from the place of delight through his transgression, and through my Son was recalled to life in the baptism of salvation. How? He uttered a voice of blessing over unbelievers who had resisted my commands, so that, terrified, they might seek pardon in a spirit of contrition, as my servant Isaiah testifies according to what he received from me, saying: “The sons of those who humbled you shall come bending to you, and all who reviled you shall worship the tracks of your feet” (Isa. 60).

What is this? O you who are the peace above and the most pure Sun, through you the living root, which is the regeneration of Spirit and water, will bubble forth. Those who had been cast down under the heaviest curse in the filth of most unspeakable uncleanness will diligently come to know you; for in this way, as though bent over, they will scarcely at last rise to truth and justice. How? They will suck the maternal sweetness of the true faith, not knowing it by visible sight but grasping it only by faithful belief.

And who are they? Those born from such matter of sin, who never saw you in burning love; but those who, cruelly oppressing you, stubbornly afflicted you [Col. 0462C], as though you did not rule over them, will love you most sweetly in right understanding. And when they have followed the true faith, they will take hold of you as a king and worship you as Lord; and they will run eagerly, following your most holy paths which you commanded them, so that with hands always raised they may look to you and always watch toward you in good works—in faith, without becoming weary of beholding you. All this will be done by those who formerly shamelessly and irreverently tore you apart and divided themselves from you in hatred and envy, when then they ardently embrace you in the mirror of faith. What is this?

For Adam’s fall closed heaven in my indignation when the human being despised me and listened to the crafty serpent [Col. 0462D]. Therefore all the glory of paradise was closed to him. This closure lasted until the Son of my radiance entered the flowing Jordan by my will. There my voice sounded clearly when I said that he was my beloved Son, in whom I was well pleased. For I willed at the end of times to redeem humanity through my Son, who clung to me by an indissoluble bond of love as a honeycomb clings to honey. For this reason I also sent him to the font, signifying me, the fountain of living water, so that he himself, the fountain of salvation, might raise from eternal death those souls to whom remission of sins would be given in water through the Holy Spirit.

Therefore the Holy Spirit also appeared there, because through him remission of sins is made for believers. By a mystical secret [Col. 0463A], the Holy Spirit showed my only-begotten one in the form of a dove, which has a simple and sincere disposition, because the Holy Spirit too is unfailing justice in simplicity and in the goodness of all good things. And this was fitting, because my Son was born from the Virgin without any stain of guilt, so that the human being who is born with sin from man and woman might be splendidly and gloriously reborn without sin.

As my Son himself says to Nicodemus in the Gospel: “Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born again from water and Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God” (John 3). What is this? I say to you with utterly steadfast certainty, not unstable ambiguity—you who were born from corruption—that a person who arose from the burning heat of desire and is wrapped in a poisonous garment, unless reborn in the true joy of new offspring from the water of sanctification and the spirit of illumination, will be put to shame in the time of his neglect.

How? Because the human being overflows like water with the spirit of his own vital growth. As water cleanses filth, and as spirit gives life to inanimate things, so, unless he is cleansed in true generation, he cannot through the entrance of salvation become heir of the kingdom of his Creator, because he is bound in the sin of the first parent whom the devil deceitfully deceived. How? As a thief secretly enters when he steals the king’s most noble and precious treasure, so twisted conception, prompted by the devil in gluttony, crept in deceitfully, so that he wickedly took away the most beloved jewel of holy innocence and chastity, in which [Col. 0463C] the Holy Spirit dwells. Therefore it must now be cleansed in the sanctification of washing.

For the deadly heat which lust kindled in the accumulation of desire through transgression of the commands of almighty God must be drowned in him who never enviously hides his wonders, but mercifully displays them in incomprehensible mercy. Therefore hear the Son in this ordinance of regeneration, which is the revelation of my kingdom, and learn from him to fulfil my commands. Do this. For this is pleasing to me. Beware lest the ancient serpent deceive you, and you shall not die if you preserve your baptism as it was commanded you in the name of the most blessed Trinity. And as often as you fall, rise through the correction of repentance [Col. 0463D] from your sins, according to my mercy.

O my most beloved children, know the goodness of your Father, who delivered you in himself from the jaws of the devil through pure confession and true pardon, and who bestowed upon you all good things, in which you must labor so that you may possess the heavenly Jerusalem. You lost it through deceitful deception, because no one can recover a lost inheritance except through the sweat of his labor. Yet you can receive your heavenly blessedness, namely your most excellent inheritance, by an easy, not difficult, law. For, as was said, the Holy Spirit drives Satan’s power out of a person in baptism, sanctifying him as a new human being in regeneration, so that he may be able to receive the joys he lost [Col. 0464A]. Therefore whoever desires to be saved through cleansing from his crimes must not refuse to be regenerated.

For I gave to the males of Abraham’s race circumcision of one member, but in my Son I commanded men and women of all peoples the circumcision of all their members. How? The circumcision of baptism arose in the baptism of my Son and will endure until the last day; after that day its holiness will remain in eternity and will not come to an end. Thus those who are circumcised in the laver of baptism will most truly be preserved, if they faithfully preserve this washing by righteous works. For I will receive a human being, whether of weaker or stronger age, if that person keeps my covenant, which he or she has made with me: namely, by believing in me and confessing me in the true Trinity, whether personally or through others who stand surety—for example, an infant or a mute person unable to speak, who requires the words of another’s mouth. And I will not destroy that person eternally, unlike one who refuses to receive this font together with the work of faith, as it is written in the teaching of the Gospel of my Son: “Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; but whoever does not believe will be condemned” (Mark 16).

What is this? The person who, through his knowledge, which is the inward eye, sees what is hidden from outward sight and does not doubt it, truly believes; and this is faith. For what a person sees outwardly, that person knows outwardly; and what is seen inwardly is considered inwardly. Therefore, when human knowledge ardently receives through the mirror of life the incomprehensible divinity which the outward eye cannot behold [Col. 0464C], the desires of the flesh are oppressed and dashed against the rock.

Thus that person’s spirit longs for true height, feeling this regeneration which the Son of Man, conceived by the Holy Spirit, brought. His untouched mother did not receive him from the flesh of a man sweating in lust, but from the hidden place of the Father of all. Coming sweetly, he showed in water the most pure and living mirror, so that through it a person lives in regeneration. For as a human being is born from flesh, divine power creating that person in the form of Adam, so the Holy Spirit restores the life of the soul through the flooding of water when the water receives the human spirit into itself, raising it to life, as it was previously raised in the wave of blood when it was manifested in the bodily vessel. For as a human form is then sensibly formed when one is called a human being, so the human spirit is then made alive in water before the eyes of God, so that God acknowledges it for the inheritance of life [Col. 0464D].

Therefore whoever thus receives the font of salvation with the covenant of righteousness finds life in salvation, because that person has believed faithfully. But one unwilling to believe is dead, because such a person lacks the breathing-places of the spirit by which to fly to the height of heaven, and merely gropes by touch with blind eyes, not living in the shadowed knowledge of the flesh. For such a person lacks the life-giving discipline which God breathed into the human being, rising upward against the will of the flesh. Therefore such a one will be condemned to the death of unbelief, because he or she did not have the laver of salvation [Col. 0465A]. For I have separated neither time nor race from this salvation, but graciously established this calling for every people through my Son.

For at whatever time of the passing hours, a person of whatever sex or age—male or female, infant or aged—comes to baptism with the disposition of devotion, I will receive that person with the aid of mercy. Nor do I refuse the baptismal washing of an infant, as certain false deceivers say, falsely claiming that I reject such an offering. Likewise, in the Old Testament I did not despise an infant’s circumcision, though the child neither asked for it by speech nor received it by will; yet the parents performed it on the child’s behalf. So too [Col. 0465B], in the new grace, I do not reject an infant’s baptism, although the child neither asks for it by speaking nor by consenting, but only has it performed on his or her behalf by the parents.

Yet if that person desires to attain salvation, he or she will in every respect fulfil the faithful promise which those who presented the child at the most holy font pledged on the child’s behalf. There must be three persons in honor of the holy Trinity: namely, the priest who pours water over the child, and two who pledge the words of faith on the child’s behalf. Those who are thus joined to someone baptized in the laver of baptism must not unite with that person in carnal procreation, because they have adhered to that person in spiritual generation.

For at the baptism of my Son I, the Father, thundered. This signifies the priest giving the blessing in the laver [Col. 0465C]. The Holy Spirit was seen in the form of a light bird; this signifies one person, addressing and instructing the one to be baptized in simplicity of heart. And my Son was present in flesh to be baptized; this declares the woman standing by in maternal gentleness because of the most sweet incarnation of that same Only-Begotten.

What now? As an infant is bodily fed on milk and food chewed by another, so that infant will also preserve from the depths of the heart the teaching and faith proposed in baptism. If the infant does not suck its mother’s breasts and does not receive food chewed for it, it dies without delay. So also, if one does not receive the nourishment of the most loving mother Church and does not retain the words proposed in baptism by faithful teachers [Col. 0465D], one does not escape the cruelty of the soul’s death, because one has refused the soul’s salvation and the sweetness of eternal life.

And just as, when that infant cannot grind bodily food with its own teeth, someone else grinds it for the infant to swallow lest it die, so it must also be done when the infant has no words in baptism by which to confess me. Spiritual helpers will be present, to offer that person the food of life—that is, the Catholic faith—lest they be caught in the snare of perpetual death.

How? A lord communicates his will to his servant in the commanding voice, and the servant fulfils it in deed with fear; a mother teaches her daughter in love, and the daughter performs her words in submission. In like manner, those indebted in faith should appropriately speak the words of salvation to the baptized person [Col. 0466A], so that he or she may fulfil them in faithful devotion for love of heavenly things.

For no sinner is weighed down by so heavy a burden of sins that, if he is immersed in holy baptism in the name of the most holy Trinity, I do not truly wipe away all the crimes of his wickedness; just as, when an infant is washed in the laver of regeneration, I truly wash away Adam’s ancient guilt. But do not wonder, O human being, that in the font of baptism a person is justified from all sins, so that he is most mercifully relieved there of the burden of his sins. For the innocent Lamb, who entered the font of baptism without any stain of sin, through the great mystery of his incarnation mercifully took away in baptism the crimes of human sins.

But I examine all things most attentively, both in this age and in eternity, where there is no death of bodies but all things are laid bare. What does this mean? Gehenna is proved in works of death, and eternal life in works that belong to life. How? Death is proved through death: for when a human being dies in sins without repentance and without God’s mercy—because he does not seek it—by God’s just judgment, death is examined in the death of hell. Life likewise is proved through life, so that good works shine in heaven when eternal life rules over them. Thus also those who are baptized in the font of blessing are proved in the holiness of holy regeneration.

And when I am invoked there through the priest’s invocation of blessing, my ears are open to the words of faith, although the one who invokes me there may be bound by sins. For although the priest is a sinner, I receive the office of baptism from him if he faithfully performs it through invocation of my name. Yet his own iniquity will condemn him if he persists in it without repentance. But I do not refuse to receive the celebration of baptism from him when he has invoked me in the words of faith.

What does this mean? If some rich man has a steward who faithfully carries out his office by properly distributing his master’s goods to his soldiers, then, although that same steward is blameworthy in some other matter, his master nevertheless does not disdain to receive his official service from him. He may perhaps say to him, “Wicked servant in your conduct,” and thus deem him unworthy in his own mind; yet he does not disdain to receive from him the service of his justice. So too I, who have very many stewards, do not disdain to receive my sacrament from a priest who, rightly anointed, faithfully remains in his office, although he is blameworthy for his other acts. Yet I judge him opposed to me on account of his other unjust deeds, without therefore scorning to receive from him that which is mine.

But if someone about to be baptized, believing that the separation of his soul and body is near, seeks baptism and cannot obtain a priest by whom to be baptized, then, if someone pours water over him with invocation of the threefold Majesty, he is baptized. Through this pouring he will receive forgiveness of his sins and the grace of heavenly blessedness, because he has been washed in the Catholic faith; nor can this baptism be changed. Yet in this invocation none of these three ineffable Persons is to be omitted. For if any one of them is omitted from invocation there through unbelief, then truth does not work salvation there; rather, falsehood grants deception.

Therefore invocation of this ineffable Trinity must not be absent there. For the Trinity was not absent from the most pure baptism of my Son, but there it wondrously made known its wonders through itself. Therefore let those who desire to be saved receive the regeneration of life for salvation, and let them not neglect to receive it lest they perish. For as an aborted thing is cast away when it perishes without the warmth of life, adhering neither in formation nor in quickening to its mother’s womb, so too those are held in the danger of death without the consolation of the Holy Spirit who are purified neither in mind nor in deed by the sacraments of the Church, which is the mother of all holiness.

Let all peoples hear and understand this, who wish to enter the kingdom of God through regeneration of Spirit and water, according to what has been set before them in the holy Scriptures through the gift of the Holy Spirit. But whoever sees with wakeful eyes and hears with attentive ears, let that person offer the kiss of embrace to these my mystical words, which flow forth from me, the Living One.

## FOURTH VISION

[Col. 0467]

**SUMMARY.**—That every baptized person ought to be adorned and strengthened through the bishop’s anointing. That the immeasurable and unfailing sweetness of the Holy Spirit is given in confirmation. That the ineffable Trinity is manifested in confirmation and declared through the greenest virtues. That the Church, fortified by the anointing of the Holy Spirit, can never be cast down into the error of perversity. The words of Moses on the same subject. That the baptized are adorned by the pontiff in the anointing of chrism. Words from the Book of Kings on the same subject. That one who has been baptized but not confirmed possesses the brightness of baptism, but not the adornment and anointing of his superior teacher. That, in honor of the Holy Spirit, confirmation is to be administered by bishops alone. That one who holds a person for confirmation is not to be joined to that person in carnal procreation. That one who returns to the devil after baptism will be condemned unless he repents; but one who faithfully follows baptism is received by God, while the Church prays to God for her children. Three ways in which the Church resounds like a trumpet. The manifold diversity of the baptized. The words of Ezekiel on the same subject.

[Col. 0467B] Then I saw something like a great round tower, entirely made of whole and white stone, having three windows at its summit. From these shone so great a radiance that even the roof of that tower, which rose as though into a hollow, could be seen more clearly in the brightness of that radiance. The windows themselves were surrounded with most beautiful emeralds.

This tower, moreover, was set, as it were, in the middle of the back of the aforesaid womanly figure, like a tower placed upon a city wall, so that the figure could in no way fall because of its strength. And I saw those infants who had entered the womb of the image, as was said above, shining with much brightness. Some of them were adorned from forehead to feet with a kind of golden color; others possessed brightness only and lacked that color. Again, some of them looked upon a pure and shining splendor, but others upon a troubled and reddish glow tending toward the east.

Of those who beheld that pure and shining splendor, some, having bright eyes and strong feet, walked stoutly in the womb of that image. Others, having weak eyes and feeble feet, were driven this way and that by the wind. Yet these also held a staff in their hands and fluttered before the image; at times they struck it, but only lukewarmly. Some, however, having clear eyes but weak feet, ran here and there in the air before that image. Others had weak eyes but strong feet, and nevertheless walked feebly before the image.

But among those who beheld that troubled and reddish glow, some, well adorned in the aforesaid image, walked briskly; others tore themselves away from it, attacked it, and overthrew its established ordinances. Some of these humbly returned to it through the fruit of repentance; but others remained, through contempt, in the hardened pride of death.

Again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

“As the new bride of the Lamb, after the illumination of the floods which arose in the sun of righteousness, who sanctified the world by his outpouring, is adorned and strengthened in the fiery ardor of the Holy Spirit unto the perfection of her beauty; so also the faithful person who receives regeneration in Spirit and water must be adorned and strengthened through the anointing of a superior teacher, so that, conformed in all his members to the effect of blessedness and bringing forth the fullness of the fruit of highest righteousness, he may perfectly attain the beauty of his adornment.

“Therefore this tower which you see signifies the blazing of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, whom the Father sent into the world for love of his Son, setting the hearts of his disciples aflame in fiery tongues; and thus they were made stronger in the name of the holy and true Trinity. But before the coming of that same fiery Holy Spirit, they sat shut up in their dwelling, thereby showing the enclosure of their bodies, through which they were timid in speaking God’s righteousness and weak in enduring the penalties inflicted by adversaries.

“And because they had seen my Son in the flesh, they loved him in the flesh with the inner eyes of their hearts closed; so that then they did not see the open teaching which afterward they poured out upon the world, when they had become stronger in the Holy Spirit. At his coming they were so confirmed that they shrank from no punishment, but bore it vigorously. For this is the strength of this tower, through which the Church has been so fortified that it can never be overcome by any madness of devilish fury.

“But that you see it great and round, entirely made of whole and white stone, means that the sweetness of the Holy Spirit is immeasurable and, in grace, moves around all creatures; so that no corruption empties it of the integrity of the fullness of righteousness. For it is a torrent that has its course and sends out all the streams of holiness in the brightness of its strength; and no stain of any defilement has ever been found in it, because the Holy Spirit himself is burning and shining brightness, who strongly kindles burning virtues and will never be extinguished. Therefore all darkness flees from him.

“It has three windows at its summit, from which such radiance shines that even the roof of that tower, which rises as though into a hollow, may be seen more clearly in that radiance. For the ineffable Trinity is manifested in the outpouring of the gifts of the Holy Spirit’s excellence, so that from that same most blessed Trinity such brightness of righteousness flows forth through the teaching of the apostles that even the most mighty power of divinity, incomprehensible in the height of its omnipotent majesty, is more openly made known to mortal human beings—yet only insofar as it is recognized to be possible for the faith of a believing and faithful person to receive it.

“Therefore those windows are surrounded by most beautiful emeralds, because that most blessed Trinity has been declared most openly everywhere throughout the entire world through the greenest virtues and sufferings of the apostles, which are said never to have felt the dryness of lukewarm faith. How? Because it is known how, for the faith of truth, most ravenous wolves oppressed them with diverse afflictions. Thus they were made stronger for the battle of conflict, so that through fighting they gained the Church, strengthened it with most powerful virtues for the building up of faith, and adorned it with manifold flashes of virtues.

“And because in the inspiration of the Holy Spirit the Church has been so strengthened through them, she also wills and requires that her children be adorned with the sign of the Holy Spirit in this anointing. For that same Holy Spirit penetrated the hearts of the faithful in a most profound mercy, which is very mystical, so that he came into the world in fiery tongues by the will of God the Father. Therefore a person washed in the baptism of salvation is to be confirmed by the anointing of an excellent teacher, just as the Church is founded firmly upon the firm rock.

“Thus the same tower is set, as it were, in the middle of the back of the aforesaid womanly figure, like a tower set upon a city wall, so that the image could in no way fall because of its strength. For the Holy Spirit worked his wonders wondrously in the greatest strength of the incarnation of him who is the true Bridegroom of the Church, and showed the Church so strong in the defense of her fortress that, through the strength with which she is fortified by his fiery gift, she can never fall into the error of any perversity. For under heavenly protection she will always rejoice in love of her Bridegroom, without spot or wrinkle, since my same only-begotten Son, conceived of the Holy Spirit, was nobly born without stain from a virgin.

“As I spoke to Moses: ‘Behold, there is a place with me; and you shall stand upon the rock. And when my glory passes by, I will put you in the hollow of the rock, and my right hand will protect you until I pass by. Then I will take away my hand, and you shall see my back’ (Exod. 33).

“What does this mean? The miracle is near which will be fulfilled by my will. But first you will struggle in the hardness of the legal commandments, showing their force by outward signification; there you will not find the sweetness and gentleness which will be revealed in my Son. And this hardness of the law, which you will write in my commandment, will stand in the hardness of stony hearts until all that glory is manifested which must be offered to me by you and your imitators up to the manifestation of my Son.

“When this is fulfilled in the law which you now write, I shall be glorified, and I shall place you in the pierced rock. How? I shall place you in the hardness of the law when I establish you over it in my commandment, calling you the teacher of this antiquity, which my Son will pierce. He will expound it more fully than you in mystical words when I send him into the world at the fitting time. Therefore his strength will protect you, because he will bring sharper words than yours and open what was closed in the legal commandments, until he returns to me.

“What does this mean? He will bodily give saving words to the world until he bodily undergoes death in the flesh which he will take from the Virgin. Then I too will remove my hand, because I shall lift him up to myself above the stars, unveiling all his mysteries through the Holy Spirit. And thus you shall see his incarnation—as a person is seen from the back and not clearly from the front—for you will perceive him incarnate, but you will not comprehend his divinity. For your children will see him more when he has returned to me than they understood him when he lived visibly among them.

“And that you see those infants who had entered the womb of the image, as was said above, shining with much brightness, means that those who in the innocence of purity of heart have obtained through the font of regeneration their mother, namely the Church, as has been shown to you, are children of light because their sins have been washed away.

“Some of them are adorned from forehead to feet with a kind of golden color, because from the beginning of good works to the end of holiness they are adorned through the most shining gifts of the Holy Spirit, in the anointing of true faith, by the hand of the pontiff in chrism. How? As gold is adorned with precious stones laid upon it, so too one faithfully baptized is shown adorned in the anointing of baptism with chrism by the hand of a superior teacher, as it is written: ‘The king also crossed the torrent Kidron, and all the people proceeded along the road of the olive-tree which looked toward the wilderness.’

“What does this mean? The Son of the Virgin, who rules the whole world, as an earthly king crossed over before the rest of the people the rushing waters of the most holy laver; and in the admonition of the Holy Spirit he shows, with strong longing, the way of salvation. What does this mean? He left death and passed to life when, in the regeneration of Spirit and water—that is, in the great adornment of the heavenly city Jerusalem—he proclaimed the highest blessedness which never fails.

“Therefore all the people who believed in him proceeded, through inspiration of the Holy Spirit, on that way which was hidden in the anointing of oil, looking toward Adam’s transgression, which had been stripped of the beauty of the inheritance of God’s righteousness, and looking toward this end: that Adam’s offspring might will to return to salvation. For it was necessary that the wounded sin of the first human being should be anointed through priestly office; but this was not necessary for the Son of the Virgin, because he was conceived wholly in holiness, with his mother’s womb neither wounded nor corrupted, but abiding in the honor of integrity. For what has been weakened and confounded by the wounds of the devil’s suggestion must be made rich and adorned by the anointing of oil, so that the consuming bruise wrought by the lust of the flesh may be wiped away.

“Others, as you see, possess brightness only and lack that golden color, because they have been cleansed only in the baptismal washing and have not received in chrism the anointing of their superior priest, which is the sign of the burning Holy Spirit.

“What does this mean? The anointing of confirmation shines especially through the gift of the Holy Spirit in the episcopal office; it is to be administered to the faithful people after regeneration through Spirit and water, when the believing person is to be confirmed upon the firm rock. How? My Son received baptism in his body, thereby sanctifying it in his flesh, in which he is not divided; for he alone is the living Son of the Virgin, and therefore is called the Son of Man, because that Virgin did not conceive him from the womb, but bore him from the integrity of her virginity.

“After the misery of his Passion and the glory of his resurrection, he penetrated heaven in that same flesh, returning to me. Then the Holy Spirit illuminated the world in fiery ardor, confirming all righteousness in the hearts of his disciples when he opened to them what had previously been hidden. How? The Holy Spirit seasoned their hearts as the sun, when it begins to appear from beneath a cloud, displays its burning heat in its splendid light.

“What does this mean? Love for my Son burned secretly in their minds, and thus the heat of the Holy Spirit, penetrating them, displayed the most mighty sun of their teaching. For this is that testimony which the Holy Spirit declared to the Church, so that death cannot withstand God’s righteousness.

“Therefore, O children of truth, hear and understand the confirmation of the Holy Spirit, which he graciously offers you in the sweet anointing of his teaching—he who is the teacher of all anointings. And therefore this anointing, in honor of that same Holy Spirit, is to be administered only by the superior priest, because every ecclesiastical order has been instituted in the Holy Spirit, and therefore this anointing belongs to the Holy Spirit.

“Thus, if a person who has received the mystery of regeneration unto life has not been anointed in this manner, then that person has not received the adornment of ecclesiastical fullness, according to the manner in which the Church is shown adorned through the blazing Holy Spirit, as was shown above. And as the Church is perfected in the gifts of the Holy Spirit, so the faithful person must be confirmed in the anointing of the principal teacher, who is a venerable master in honor of the Holy Spirit, because that same Holy Spirit ardently sets forth and kindles by his heat the most certain teaching for the Christian people.

“Therefore those who have attached themselves to one so anointed in this anointing of the Holy Spirit are not to be joined to him in worldly procreation, because they have been joined to him in the Holy Spirit. What does this mean? Faith brings a person to this anointing, and therefore the one who holds that person in his hands at that time signifies faith, which does not seek carnal things but always tends toward spiritual things. For my eye sees a person as he will come to me in his deeds.

“But if you, O human being, abandon me after baptism and return to the devil, you will be condemned for this by just judgment, because I gave you the great gift of understanding and showed you my mercy in the font of baptism. For all who seek my mercy in baptism find it graciously, because of my Son who came into the world and endured many labors in his body. Therefore, O human being, you must patiently endure the struggles of your soul and body; and because of my Son I shall receive you.

“And no one who faithfully follows baptism in my name is to be repelled from the laver of baptism, because at whatever time a person seeks me, I fervently receive that person. But if afterward that person’s works are evil, those works themselves judge him unto death. Therefore, O human being, overflow in the regeneration of the Savior, be anointed in the anointing of holiness, flee death, and imitate life.

“For the mother of the faithful, who is the Church, faithfully prays in her children that they may escape death and find life. How? She has in her children a groaning voice, which is placed in her until the fullness of her children enters the dwelling-place of the heavenly city. She has this voice in order always to admonish me, who am before all ages, to see and behold that my only-begotten Son has been incarnate, so that for love of him I may spare her children, whom she has received in the regeneration of Spirit and water. For they cannot enter the heavenly kingdom except in salvation.

“Therefore she resounds thus: ‘Fear the Father, love the Son, and burn in the Holy Spirit.’ How? This sound was given to her from me the Father through my Son in the Holy Spirit. It is the voice that resounds in her like a trumpet in a city. Nor does she speak in any other way except thus in her children. Therefore the most mighty God is thus implored through his Son to spare human sins, which through repentance must be endured without perdition, because the Son of God assumed humanity without sin.

“He ought not to have been clothed with polluted flesh conceived from the seed of sin, because God is just and the brightness of the heavenly kingdom is touched by no stain of defilement. And how could a human being stained by immeasurable foulness enter the heavenly kingdom except through my Son, incarnate without defilement, who receives sinners purified in repentance? And who could do this except God? Therefore the Church turns to her children and cherishes them with maternal love.

“But that you see that, of the aforesaid infants, some look upon a pure and shining splendor, while others look upon a troubled and reddish glow tending toward the east, means that among the children of the Church, whom she brings forth in the innocence of her incorruptibility by God’s power, some attend to the purity of spiritual life, shining in most serene virtue and trampling earthly things underfoot for love of the true Sun. Others, although they possess carnal resources disturbed by the manifold diversity of vices, nevertheless burn faithfully in right faith and sigh toward eternal things because of heavenly recompense.

“And among those who behold that pure and shining splendor, some have bright eyes and strong feet and walk powerfully in the womb of the image. For, while they pursue heavenly things, they set in God’s commandments the sight of just discernment and the step of good fulfillment, walking, that is, in the inward embrace of maternal love, so that they do not establish the devotion of their intention in either transitory or eternal things.

“But others have weak eyes and feeble feet, because they possess neither clear intention nor strong performance for the work of perfection; and therefore they are cast this way and that by the wind, because they are scattered into diversity of conduct through varied temptations of pride. Yet they themselves hold staffs in their hands, flutter before the image, and at times strike it, but only lukewarmly. For, placing stubborn confidence in their works, they show themselves to God’s Church by false report and sometimes—yet foolishly—criticize her through worldly cleverness. Since by a feigned pretense they appear wise in the sight of human beings, they become foolish before God through empty glory.

“Some, however, having clear eyes but weak feet, wander here and there in the air before that image. For although divine commandments are known to them through the gaze of discernment, they limp in the foot of fulfillment. Thus they are shown to the Bride of Christ through the restless course of their own instability, seeking wisdom in shadow and imagining that they possess it in their own power before it touches them in their minds or they obtain any of its force.

“Others have weak eyes but strong feet, and nevertheless walk feebly before that same image, because they maintain a weak intention toward good work when they ought to walk strongly in works of righteousness. Yet they do not run straightforwardly in ecclesiastical observances, because they fix their minds more upon earthly than heavenly things. Therefore they are foolish before God, because through worldly cleverness they wish to comprehend what they cannot attain.

“But among those who behold that troubled and reddish glow, some walk strongly, well adorned in the aforesaid image. Although they possess earthly things, yet, bearing in the womb of the Church the adornment of their labors, they do not disdain to place the foot of uprightness in the divine law, when, obedient to God’s commandments, they receive strangers, clothe the naked, and feed the hungry. O how happy these are, because in this way they receive God, and he himself dwells with them.
