For when they deceitfully withdrew from the world, they did not invoke me in their prayers for help, nor did they seek me by testing their own strength, to learn whether they could persevere in this resolve or not [Col. 0499C]. Therefore I allow them to see what their own will, when they trust in themselves, can do to help them. O, they prove foolish and fruitless, because they are useless without the tillage of God’s law and without the fruit-bearing of his word. For they did not inquire what they ought to do when entering the narrow way, just as one examines good soil to see what useful fruit it yields. Therefore let them hear: O human being, if today, while you burn strongly in the lusts of your flesh, you have come forth as a fiery furnace, who gave you such cooling that you could escape so great a conflagration in your pleasure?

Truly, whoever wishes to undertake these things must proceed with the eyes of the inner person, considering how to begin them through me [Col. 0499D] and how to complete them with my help, lest, having begun them foolishly and ended them badly, he go to ruin. So too that ancient enemy, trusting in himself, was cast down in the wrath of my zeal. Likewise those will be rejected who, without considering themselves, put on the Passion of my Son amid the headlong violence of great pride, but afterward reject it superfluously in disgust. Therefore, those who have put it upon themselves should consider how they may love it, as the prophet Jeremiah exhorts in the Holy Spirit, saying: “O all you who pass by the way, attend and see whether there is sorrow like my sorrow; for he has gathered me as grapes, as the Lord spoke, in the day of the wrath of his fury” (Lam. 1).

What is this? O all you who describe vices—that is, in rejecting worldly things and imitating spiritual ones—who pass along that way which is life and truth, which I, the Son of God, am: at the beginning of good works, take heed lest you forget my suffering when you begin to imitate me in my Passion; and in the perfection of righteousness see that the suffering which you impose upon yourselves for love of me may be like my suffering [Col. 0500A]. How? By persevering without failure, unto a good end, in those same miseries that you endure for my sake, just as I persevered in my suffering to die for you. For I was crushed and trampled in the suffering of the cross, as a grape is pressed in the winepress, so that you might eat my body and drink my blood.

The ruler of heaven and earth spoke this in the foreknowledge of his discerning eye, in the judgment by which Adam abandoned life and accepted death [Col. 0500B]. Yet my heavenly Father foresaw that at the end of time, through me, his Son incarnate from the Virgin—who stood against the devil in the strongest powers of righteousness—he would overcome that ancient deceiver and free the human race through the protection of heavenly aid. Therefore, a person of whatever sex or age who puts on my Passion should take heed to hold it firmly, lest, if through the error of negligence that person casts it away, afterward, wishing to retain it, that person may be unable to find it.

Therefore also those who wish to subject their children to my Passion in a life of humility should not do this shamelessly in the presumption of rashness, but wisely, by a discerning examination [Col. 0500C]. They should not compel them, without the consent of their will, to undertake what they themselves cannot bear. How? If you offer your child to me while he does not yet possess knowledge of discerning understanding, but lies in the folly of all his awareness, and yet offer him without his own will, not considering his consent in this matter, you have not rightly offered the ram.

How? If a person offers a ram at my altar but has not firmly tied it by its horns with ropes, will not the ram run away? So likewise, if a father or mother offers his or her child, who is the ram, to my service, and does not attend to that child’s will—which is its horns—by diligent guarding, supplication, entreaty, and exhortation, all the care of which is understood as the ropes binding it [Col. 0500D], since by all these means the child must be drawn to consent in good will, then, if the child has not been tested by these examinations, he will certainly flee either in body or in mind, unless God guards him by his wonders.

But if you, O human being, shut that child up in such severe bodily restraint that he cannot free himself from the pressure of his resisting will, then in every fruit, of body as well as soul, he appears dry to me on account of that captivity unjustly imposed upon him without his consent. Then I say to you, O human being, author of this binding: “I had a green field in my power. O human being, did I give it to you so that you might make it sprout whatever fruit you yourself wished? And if you sow seed in it, can you bring it to fruit?” No. For you neither give dew, nor produce rain, nor grant moisture in greenness, nor bring forth heat in the burning of the sun [Col. 0501A], by all of which fitting fruit must be produced.

Likewise, you can sow a word into a person’s hearing; but into that person’s heart, which is my field, you cannot pour the dew of compunction, the rain of tears, the moisture of devotion, or the warmth of the Holy Spirit—by all of which the fruit of holiness must sprout. And how did you dare so rashly to touch one delicate and sanctified to me in baptism, so as to hand him over, without his will, to the most stringent captivity of binding, to bear my yoke? Thus he has become neither dry nor green, because he is neither dead to the world nor alive to the world [Col. 0501B]. And why have you so oppressed him that he is useless for either? Nor is a miracle of mine to strengthen him so that he may remain in spiritual life to be expected from human beings, because I do not wish his parents to sin in offering him to me without his will.

But if either father or mother wishes to offer a child to my service, before presenting him let that parent say: “I promise God that I shall keep my child under diligent care until he reaches the age of understanding, praying, entreating, and exhorting him to remain devoutly in God’s service. And if he consents to me, I shall quickly offer him to the service of God; but if he does not give me assent [Col. 0501C], I shall be found blameless before the eyes of his majesty.”

But if the child’s parents have guided him by these means until his age of understanding, and if then the child turns away and refuses to consent to them, then they also, since they have shown their devotion toward him as far as they could, should not offer him without his will, nor compel him to enter that service which he himself is unwilling either to bear or to fulfill.

But whoever willingly desires to subject himself to me with a devout mind should be vigorously encouraged to attain this, and should not be drawn back from his good intention through the envy of any malevolent soul. For if anyone draws back from his resolve one of those who desire to follow me, that person commits sacrilege, because he has broken my covenant in that person’s mind [Col. 0501D]; therefore he will render account for it in righteous judgment if he persists inflexibly in this wickedness, because he has turned aside one who wished to serve me. He ought not to have done this, as it is written: “Everything consecrated to the Lord, whether a human being, an animal, or a field, shall not be sold and cannot be redeemed” (Lev. 27).

What is this? When any yearning soul, through the complete function of knowledge, touches the good sense in a person so that the person accomplishes some thing, then that person’s will confirms the matter, saying: “This is fitting for God’s honor.” And so, with good devotion and just reverence, that person promises it to God, offering it through the kiss of the heart—that is, through the will of his or her desires. Then in this manner it is offered to God as a dowry of sanctification [Col. 0502A]. How? Because God, seeing an edifying will in that person, receives the person by the ring of sanctification, just as a man customarily secures his bride to himself through a ring of betrothal in a covenantal bond, so that he may not henceforth dismiss her.

Therefore, when God has received that will in the strength of a person’s soul—of one who so binds himself that he leaves what he has and apportions what he possesses more to God than to himself—then the bond of such consecration will endure, and the person will not abandon this devotion. Why? Because the person’s knowledge has recognized it, that person’s good sense has understood it, and that person’s will has established it for God’s honor. Therefore, whether it is a person who has thus offered himself to God, or an animal subject to a person that has been offered in the same manner to God’s honor, or a fruit-bearing field likewise consecrated to God, it ought neither to be given for a higher price nor retained under a lower recompense [Col. 0502B], lest God’s honor be reckoned as though at a contemptible valuation.

But just as no one ought to be compelled against his will to turn from the worldly path to the spiritual way, so likewise one who has undertaken my service with the devotion of his own will and afterward, despising it, neglects it, must be summoned back by righteous judgment to resume it. How? If that person has just rulers and spiritual teachers who possess my zeal, they ought to summon that person back to my service. First they should do this by supplication, exhortation, and gentle speech, soothing that person; then they should correct that person by blows and by the constraint of cold and hunger and other chastisements like these [Col. 0502C], so that, warned by these miseries, the person may call to mind the punishments of hell and, fearing them, remove from himself the rottenness of his soul and return, thus recalled, to the path he had abandoned. For it is also written of these in the Gospel: “Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled” (Luke 14).

What is this? You who are a spiritual shepherd, a just ruler, and an upright teacher, go forth from your former customs which cling to you from your first parent; go into the narrow and constricted way and into the ordering of the unbending precepts which most righteous men have composed in the weaving of the Holy Spirit. And most keenly, in my zeal [Col. 0502D], observe those living under your command and instruction who have either accepted or vowed, by their own will and not by another person’s unjust coercion, to observe the holy resolve of my covenant. When afterward, despising it, they desire to return to their former vices, compel them by sweet and bitter corrections to enter ecclesiastical discipline, so that the house of my endowment may be filled both by those firmly corrected and by those gently admonished. For some must be called to life by diverse chastisements, and others by various gentle admonitions.

How? As a diligent shepherd carefully seeks his lost sheep, so spiritual teachers should seek with much diligence those subject to them who wander through diverse vices. By their own skill, they should compel them to return to the house of righteousness [Col. 0503A] from which they departed or wished to depart, so that the Church may be filled, in one part, by sheep corrected out of love and, in another, by sheep gently encouraged, and thus be led to the pastures above.

But those who are then so stopped up that they refuse correction—neither because of bodily chastisement inflicted on them by their appointed teachers in my zeal, nor from fear of me, because I am God who does not will iniquity, nor from love for the shed blood of my Son, who suffered for them—yet strive to pollute my most faithful friends, who swiftly run in my ways, with their rottenness: they must be expelled by my friends as wolves, lest they contaminate my flock, as Paul, my friend, exhorts, saying: “Remove the evil from among yourselves” (1 Cor. 5) [Col. 0503B].

What is this? You who stand at the summit of governance and you who remain in the humility of subjection, expel from yourselves that evil which, despising fear of me, opposes me, the Creator of heaven and earth. Expel it by so strong an examination that it may neither take root in your conscience nor set its foot in your fellowship, lest the sweet spices of good works within you become cheapened. But whoever among these wishes to return in repentance and seeks me, his Creator, from the heart—even if he comes at the end of his course—I will nevertheless receive him, because I judge all things justly.

But whoever hides away the treasure of his heart, saying, “Unless I feel that I am dying, I will not turn away from worldly concerns,” and thus delays conversion until the expiration of his soul, and when no longer able to breathe, despairing that he can retain this present life any longer, attempts to renounce the world: that person deceives his own soul, because his conversion is deceitful; he has done this in mockery, and it is received as mockery [Col. 0503C]. But one who, already near death, renounces the world with all the heart because of sins and because of love for me, desiring, so long as he or she lives, to serve me fervently: I truly receive that person’s devotion with all the choirs of angels and grant the glory of life.

For although a person may be entangled in much crime, when that person confronts sins in such a way as to weep bitterly over offenses, and does so with a single eye because that person has provoked me to anger, I raise that person from death to salvation and do not deny the heavenly inheritance, as David the psalmist testifies in my Spirit, saying: “On whatever day I call upon you, behold, I have known that you are my God” (Ps. 55). What is this? On whatever day of my life some brightness of heavenly illumination appears in my mind, while I lie in darkness, through divine grace, so that in the bitterness of repentance for my sins and in the wounds of my burdened heart I call upon you, who grant the remedy of your mercy to all who call upon you with a pure heart: then, in that same visitation, I have known that you are my God, who mercifully accomplish these things [Col. 0503D].

What is this? When through your grace you have brought me to the point of knowing you as my God in works of righteousness, so that in works of iniquity I condemn and restrain myself: then you receive me as one simply seeking you, crying after you with tears and knowing you in the greenness of my soul, because you are the one able to do these things. Then I bruise my body in true repentance and regard it as nothing. And when a person has thus performed repentance, that person will find the remedy for sins. How? Because that person has known God as God. How? Because that person has abandoned sins, and therefore through the eye of repentance will see that those things were vain which had formerly been committed ardently in evil lust [Col. 0504A].

Therefore let no one neglect to seek the remedy of repentance. For if anyone has neglected it while physically healthy, that person should nevertheless strive to find it even at the last time; and I shall receive that person unto salvation. For although the defilements of sins may be great, they are nevertheless washed away through my Son in pure repentance—except in the case of one who has uttered blasphemy against the Holy Spirit without repentance, and one who, hardened, has hurled himself into the death of his body; for these two are as one. Such persons I do not know in the glory of heavenly life, as it is written in the Gospel: “Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven to human beings, but blasphemy of the spirit shall not be forgiven” (Matt. 12) [Col. 0504B].

What is this? Every sin committed in excess of the flesh, in lust, bitterness, or other vices of this kind; or blasphemy found in the worship of idols, where the true God is unknown and a false fabrication is adored; or the invocation of demons, where the true God is known but the devil is nevertheless invoked in human perversity—all these things shall be forgiven to human beings in pure repentance, when, through the compunction of tears from the inmost heart, they faithfully seek the true God [Col. 0504C], who mercifully grants his mercy to all who call upon him. For although people of this kind sin gravely by wandering in sins, nevertheless, if they do not utterly reject God, who reigns in heaven by command and power, they will find the hand of his help.

But if they persist in unbelief so that they never recover from this perversity, but, with fixed heart and consenting soul [Col. 0504D], utterly deny God, saying within themselves: “What is this that is called God? God has neither mercy nor truth, so that he would or could help me”; and if, unrepentant, they despair of being cleansed from their sins or saved in any way: such people blaspheme God. Therefore, if they persist thus through the wickedness of their hardened state, they will not receive remission of blasphemy, because they suffocate the understanding of their heart so that they cannot sigh upward. They regard as nothing the one through whose mercy they ought to be saved, as David also testifies, saying: “The fool has said in his heart: There is no God” (Ps. 13).

What is this? Through foolish speech, one who was empty of wisdom and understanding denied God in the heart and was foolish even in regard to knowing him [Col. 0505A]. How? Because that person was unwilling either to know or to understand the true God, when, in hardened perception, saying: “What is God? There is no God. And what indeed am I? I do not know what I am.” Whoever says these things is foolish, because such a person does not possess the true wisdom by which God is known. But whoever has known, without pretense, God reigning in his power is wise, even though a sinner.

Therefore, whoever holds this fixed in the heart despairs of God’s mercy, saying: “God is nothing; I do not know him; he no longer knows me; and I deny him because he has denied me.” Such a one shall not rise to life and cannot possess any joy, because all creatures abandon that person, since the Creator of them was held to be nothing. Likewise, one who despairs of sins, because on account of their great weight that person does not believe that salvation is possible, is faithless and therefore will not attain life, because such a person opposes the one who gives life to all. But if anyone among all these, led by repentance, truly seeks me, that person will find me, because I reject no one who returns to me with a pure heart [Col. 0505B].

But if the blackest storms of this blasphemy and despair fall upon any person, and that person consents to them neither in heart, nor in will, nor in the relish of a perverse taste, but is greatly tormented in this conflict, then, if that person perseveres by strongly resisting in the same struggle, I come to help more quickly. Let that person not doubt because of these burdens; for I call that person a most valiant fighter against the greatest tempests, and I shall help that person more swiftly and count that person among my friends, because, patiently enduring so many adversities for love of me, that person has overcome nobly.

But just as one who in no way wishes to know me, the true God, with any faith or hope in the heart, does not rise to life, as has been said, so neither does one who has hurled oneself into bodily death. Such a person does not await that separation which I appointed for human beings, but tears himself or herself apart without any hope of mercy [Col. 0505C]. Therefore such a one falls into perdition, because the person kills that by which repentance ought to have been made. For whoever separates from a human being that which I placed in the human being subjects himself or herself to great guilt, as my Son shows in the Gospel, saying: “You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not kill’; but whoever kills shall be liable to judgment” (Matt. 5).

What is this? You who desire to set your foot upon the foundation of the rock, observe that through that sound which comes forth from the root of rationality you have perceived that, in the words of Scripture—which possess that meaning shown by the finger of God—it was made known to those who preceded you in antiquity [Col. 0506A] that they should not divide in a human being what has been joined in that person by divine ordering. What is this? He who forbade Adam the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, saying, “On whatever day you eat from it, you shall die by death” (Gen. 2), also spoke through Moses to Adam’s race: “You shall not kill, nor destroy that which has been made in the image of God.”

But just as Adam, transgressing the commandment, deprived himself and his race of the life of salvation, so also the person who destroys God’s handiwork in a human being cuts off from his or her soul and body the faithful generations of saving works. In this also making himself or herself guilty of judicial sentence, that person goes into the exile of misery. Therefore one who has made so cruel a separation in a human being casts himself or herself into many calamities, separating what is mine, because I joined body and soul together in a human being [Col. 0506B]. And who is there who would dare to separate these?

If one who kills another is in the great burden of sin, what then is the condition of one who hands oneself over to death and casts into dust that by which one ought to have washed away one’s crimes? For whoever kills oneself imitates the lost angel, who, first discovering iniquity, gave himself over to perdition and killed himself in death. How? Because he envied God, who had no beginning and will receive no end, and who governs all things in heaven and on earth. And just as that proud devil did not wish to look upon me when he cast himself into perdition, so neither does the person who violently tears himself apart deem me worthy to be known [Col. 0506C]; therefore that person falls into death, just as the devil fell when he hurled himself into perdition.

For before he fell, he wished to raise his wickedness above the wings of the winds and, like a bird flying in the air, attempted to fly in heavenly places. Therefore, in this presumption, he cast himself down from blessedness into misery. But I formed the human being from the earth, so that the person might ascend from lower things to higher, and, by beginning and completing good works, might build up bright virtues on high to arduous heights. Therefore a person who possesses both body and soul, who can do good and can repent, must not kill oneself, lest afterward that person receive the place where neither work nor repentance is possible, just as the devil, while killing himself, was cast down into Tartarus [Col. 0506D].

But whoever sees with wakeful eyes and hears with attentive ears should give the kiss of embrace to my mystical words which flow forth from me, the living one.

## Sixth Vision

[Col. 0505]

## Summary

Concerning the venerable sacrament of Christ’s body: the Church was joined to Christ in his Passion and adorned with his blood, and the salvation of souls arose. God the Father conquered the ancient serpent through the humility of his Son, not through power. Words of the Psalmist. As the Church grows, she devoutly offers her dowry to God before the angels; the depth of the sacraments is disclosed by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit; and there is a comparison with gold. When the priest approaches the altar to offer sacrifice, a great brightness shines forth with the mystery of the heavenly spirits. In the sacrament of the altar, God the Father recalls his Son’s Passion for the salvation of the people. Why bread, wine, and water are offered in the sacrament of the altar. Words of Joel on the same subject. The present help of God does not leave the priest during the sacrament; serenity remains until the mysteries are completed. When the priest sings, “Holy, holy, holy,” and begins the mysteries of the sacraments, an incomprehensible serenity shines upon those same sacraments. Divine brightness invisibly draws the altar-offering upward, as if in an instant, and sends it back made true flesh and true blood. A comparison of ointment and sapphire concerning the same matter. Why a human being cannot visibly receive this spiritual gift. When the priest faithfully believes in God and offers with humble devotion, the offering becomes flesh and blood. A comparison with a chick and a winged creature. By a true manifestation, the mysteries of Christ’s birth, Passion, burial, resurrection, and ascension appear in the sacrament of the altar as in a mirror. As long as the faithful person says, “Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors,” Christ’s Passion will appear in the mercy of God the Father. The offering never appears as raw flesh unless it is shown to the elect in great necessity. While the hymn of the innocent Lamb is sung, faithful people communicate so that, cleansed from transgression, they may be restored to the eternal inheritance. Words of Solomon in the Song of Songs. How the Lord’s words spoken to the disciples at his supper concerning this mystery are to be understood. Words of David on the same matter. This sacrament, cleansing every stain, must be venerated until the last human being. Further words of David on the same subject. Why bread is offered in the sacrament of the altar. Words of Moses on the same matter. Why wine is offered in the sacrifice of the altar. Words from the Song of Songs on the same matter. Why water must be mingled with wine in the sacrament of the altar. Words of Wisdom. Further words from the book of Wisdom. Adam possessed pure blood before sin; after transgression he spilled it into the stench of impurity. Those who receive Christ’s body and blood are enlivened with great sweetness. Words of Solomon on the same matter. At the priest’s invocation at the altar, the sacrament of Christ’s body and blood is completed. God exercises the power and strength of his will in every creature as he pleases. From the first hour of the day until the ninth, the office of Mass may be performed according to the necessity of the time. All should communicate fasting, except those placed under the oppression of death. The devil fell without another’s suggestion; but humanity, frail and falling at the devil’s persuasion, was raised up by God. In receiving the Lord’s body and blood, not quantity but holiness must be considered. A comparison with manna on the same matter. It must not be doubted that Christ’s true body and true blood are on the altar. In the sacrament of the altar three things are to be offered in the name of the Trinity: bread, wine, and water. A priest who through negligence or forgetfulness omits these three things in the sacrament of the altar is liable to severe punishment. How Christ’s body and blood are to be distributed to the people. The priest is to use these vestments and these words in the sacrament of the altar, as the ancient Fathers established. The Lord’s words to a negligent priest. Because the priest offers these banquets on the altar, he is not to leave the altar fasting from these banquets. In the sacrament of the altar the priest is not to employ many or great speeches, according to the ordinance of earlier teachers. Concerning five kinds of communicants. Concerning those who are bright in body and fiery in soul. Concerning those who appear pale in body and dark in soul. Concerning those who are hairy in body and foul with much impurity in soul. Concerning those who are surrounded in body by very sharp thorns and appear leprous in soul. Concerning those who appear blood-stained in body and foul in soul like a rotten corpse. Concerning those who approach this sacrament with devout mind and pure faith, and those who approach it with the contrary heart and a wavering spirit. Words of the Apostle. The sacrament of the altar must be handled and guarded with great diligence and care by priest and people. The mystical secrets of the Lord’s body and blood are not to be investigated. Ministers of the Church who enter not through the door but by byways imitate the devil and Baal, because they are bitter, deceivers, and unpolished stones, and they strive to wound Christ as crucifiers do. The same ministers of the Church must preserve chastity with every diligence after the example of the apostles and abstain from every impurity. Words of Moses on the same matter. A priest must not have two unions. How the devil is the priest of priests. Words of the Law on the same matter. Words of the Gospel on the same subject. Words of the Apostle on the same matter. Further words of Paul on the same subject. Concerning three kinds of eunuchs. Whoever cannot contain himself is not to become either priest or another minister of priestly office on any pretext. Why those previously married but thereafter separated from one another were permitted in the primitive Church to approach priesthood, and why this is now not permitted. A comparison with a king on the same matter. The immature and unconsecrated must not take up the Church; nor may one presume to seek several offices. From the entire people bearing the Christian name, priests are to be selected who have good understanding, manly courage, and soundness of limbs. Women must not approach the office of the altar. A man must by no means put on women’s clothing, nor a woman men’s clothing, unless compelled by some great necessity. God judges strictly those who fornicate with women, those who in contrary fornication defile themselves with others or with themselves, both women and men, and those who fornicate with beasts. Concerning pollution occurring during sleep. Words of Moses on the same matter. Whoever burns strongly in lust must provide no fuel to his own burning. Burdened by diverse vices, let him flee to God’s mercy in confession. The remedy of purification was prefigured for a long time even among the ancient Fathers. Whoever refuses to confess sins deceives himself. At the hour of death, if a priest is absent, one person should confess to another; if no person can be found, let that person confess to God alone in the presence of the elements. Let no one despair because of the weight of sins. The Gospel on the same matter. Sins must be erased both through almsgiving and through bodily satisfaction. From the book of Wisdom. The elements are pools of human pleasures. Those who give alms and those who receive them must not do this in vain. The poor, the rich, and those seeking the honor of authority are each rewarded according to intention. Priests should exhort and restrain the people concerning confession. Priests who do not show the people the authority of teaching are called not priests but wolves. The elements howl before God over the iniquity of priests, and the heavens receive their iniquity. Priests possess the power of binding and loosing. Words of the Gospel on the same matter. No one is to be bound without a reasonable fault. If someone has been bound, that person should seek release for God’s honor. Rebels unwilling to return to Christ and hardened persons seeking no mercy imitate the ancient serpent. Words of the devil. Human beings were brought back from the darkness of unbelief through the incarnation of the Son of God.

[Col. 0507A] And after these things I saw, when the Son of God hung upon the cross, that the aforesaid female image, like a shining splendor swiftly proceeding from the eternal counsel, was brought to him by divine power [Col. 0508A] and, sprinkled with the blood flowing from his side as it rose upward, was united to him by the will of the heavenly Father in a blessed espousal [Col. 0509A] and nobly endowed with his flesh and blood. And I heard a voice from heaven saying to him: “Let this, my Son, be your bride for the restoration of my people; and let her be their mother, regenerating souls through the salvation of Spirit and water.”

And when that image had already begun in this manner to advance in her powers, I saw, as it were, an altar. Frequently approaching it, she devoutly examined her dowry, humbly displaying it before the heavenly Father and his angels. Therefore, when the priest, clothed in sacred vestments, approached that altar to celebrate the divine sacraments, I saw a great serenity of light suddenly descend from heaven with the ministry of angels, shining all around the whole altar. It remained there until the sacrament had been completed and the priest withdrew from [Col. 0509B] the altar.

Moreover, after the Gospel of peace had been read and the offering to be consecrated had been laid upon the altar, the priest sang the praise of almighty God: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth,” and thus began the mysteries of the ineffable sacraments. Suddenly, with heaven opened, a fiery radiance of immeasurable brightness descended upon that offering and wholly suffused it with its light, just as sunlight illuminates an object which it penetrates with its rays. As it irradiated the offering in this way, it invisibly raised it to the hidden places of heaven and again returned it downward upon the same altar, just as a human being draws breath inward and then breathes it out again. [Col. 0509C] Thus it became true flesh and true blood, although in human sight it appeared as bread and wine.

As I beheld these things, the signs of the birth, Passion, and burial, likewise of the resurrection and ascension, of our Savior, the only-begotten Son of God, immediately appeared as in a mirror, just as they were accomplished in him when the Son of God was in the world. But while the priest sang the hymn of the innocent Lamb, namely, “Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world,” and prepared himself to receive holy communion, the aforesaid fiery radiance withdrew to the heavenly places. Heaven was then closed, and I heard a voice issuing from it: “Eat and drink the body and blood of my Son, for the abolishing of Eve’s transgression, that you may be restored to the rightful inheritance.”

[Col. 0509D] And when other people also approached the priest to receive the sacrament, I observed five kinds among them. Some were bright in body and fiery in soul; others appeared pale in body and dark in soul. Some were hairy in body and foul in soul, drenched in much uncleanness of human defilement. Others were surrounded in body by extremely sharp thorns and appeared leprous in soul. Others appeared blood-stained in body and foul in soul like a rotten corpse. Yet among all these, when some received the same sacraments, some were suffused as with fiery splendor, while others were darkened as with a gloomy cloud.

After the sacraments were completed, [Col. 0510A] when the priest withdrew from the altar, the serenity previously coming from heaven and surrounding the whole altar, as stated, was withdrawn upward into the heavenly secrets.

And again I heard a voice from the heights of heaven saying to me:

“While Christ Jesus, the true Son of God, hung on the wood of his Passion, the Church was joined to him in the hidden place of heavenly mysteries and endowed with his purple blood. She herself demonstrates this when she frequently approaches the altar, asks for her dowry, and considers most attentively with what devotion her children, approaching the divine mysteries, receive them.

“Therefore, you see that when the same Son of God hung upon the cross, the aforesaid female image, like a shining splendor swiftly proceeding from the eternal counsel, was brought to him by divine power [Col. 0510B]; because when that innocent Lamb was raised upon the altar of the cross for human salvation, the Church, appearing suddenly from the divine mystery in heaven through the deepest mystery, in the purity of the brightness of faith and the other virtues, was joined by the supreme Majesty to that only-begotten Son of God.

“What does this mean? When blood flowed from the wounded side of my Son, the salvation of souls immediately arose. For the glory from which the devil and his followers had been expelled was given to humanity when my only-begotten Son, temporarily undergoing death upon the cross, despoiled hell and led faithful souls to heavenly things. Thus faith also began already to increase and be strengthened in his disciples and in those who sincerely followed them, so that they might become heirs of the heavenly kingdom.

“Therefore, sprinkled with the blood flowing from [Col. 0510C] his side as it rose upward, that image was united to him by the will of the heavenly Father in a blessed espousal. For as the strength of the Passion of the Son of God poured forth ardently and wondrously raised itself to the height of heavenly mysteries—just as the scent of fine spices spreads upward—the Church, strengthened thereby in the bright heirs of the eternal kingdom, was faithfully joined to that only-begotten Son of God by the ordinance of the heavenly Father.

“How? As a bride, subject to her bridegroom in the service of submission and obedience, receives from him the gift of fertility together with covenantal love for the begetting of children, so that she may bring them to her inheritance; so the Church, Daughter of God, united in the office of humility and charity, receives from him regeneration by Spirit and [Col. 0510D] water together with the salvation of souls for the restoration of life, and sends them to the heavenly places. Thus she was also nobly endowed with his flesh and blood, because that only-begotten Son of God bestowed his body and blood in most excellent glory upon his faithful, who are both the Church and the children of the Church, so that through him they might possess life in the heavenly city. How?

“Because he gave his flesh and blood for the sanctification of believers; and because the heavenly Father gave him up to the Passion for the redemption of peoples, thereby defeating the ancient serpent through him in humility and righteousness—not choosing to overcome him by his own power and strength. For God is just and does not will iniquity, as [Col. 0511A] the psalmist says:

‘Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked,
nor stood in the way of sinners,
nor sat in the seat of pestilence.’  
(Psalm 1)

“What is this? God is the author of every blessedness and happiness of his creatures, showing many and diverse signs in those same creatures. Thus the incarnation of his Son distilled the sweetest taste amid great sweetness, when the heavenly powers built many edifices in him, through which humanity might return to the heavenly kingdom, which no shadow of death has darkened. Thus it was also made manifest that the heavenly Father himself is the most mighty strength of all virtues. Through his only-begotten Son he courageously killed death and broke hell; and on the last day he will transform the world [Col. 0511B] into another and better newness.

“Therefore, through the outpouring of his heart, he did not walk in the wavering paths of malignant spirits, who abandoned truth and seized falsehood. How? They wished to divide truth by falsehood. How? They wished to oppress the Ancient of Days, who existed before the time of days and hours; and they eagerly desired to make the ancient serpent, who did not exist before the time of times, his companion. But this neither could nor ought to be, because God is one. Therefore the devil is a liar, for he withdrew from God, abandoned life, and found death.

“Likewise, God did not stand in the way in which sinners plant their feet, because rejecting Adam’s way, he did not love Adam’s sin. Rather, he cast Adam, seduced by the devil, out of paradise. Nor did he reign in the power of that iniquity, [Col. 0511C] as the whole human race is entangled in death, sitting in the shadow of death, whenever humanity proudly abandons truth.

“What is this? God did not resist either diabolical presumption or human negligence by such an exercise of power that he cast them down through his own strength. How? If two combatants were engaged and one surpassed the other in stronger powers, surely the stronger would display greater contests of his own ability to the weaker, in order to humiliate him and subject him to himself, unwilling to yield to him in anything. But God did not do this. Rather, through supreme goodness he opposed the work of iniquity by sending his Son into the world; and in his body, with the greatest humility, he brought his lost sheep back to heaven.

“How? When the blood came forth from his body, as soon as it flowed from his opened wounds it appeared in the heavenly mysteries, seeking that the salvation of souls might be sent forth. How? Every creature showed in the Son of God that through his Passion and death humanity’s ruin was restored to life. How? The only-begotten Son of God, being life, offered himself to the Passion on the altar of the cross for the redemption of humankind. There also, as you perceived by a true hearing a voice resounding from the heavenly mysteries, he chose the Church as his bride, so that she might be the mother for the restoration of the salvation of believing peoples—[Col. 0512A] that she might send them to heaven without spiritual blemish through regeneration.

“But when the aforementioned image has advanced in her powers in this way, you see something like an altar, which she frequently approaches. There, devoutly reviewing her dowry, she humbly displays it to the heavenly Father and his angels. For the Church, as has been said, is increasing in blessed and most powerful virtues; and this is immediately shown to you, as it were, by a manifest demonstration. By the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, the sanctification of mystical altars arose in the depth of faithful sighing. There the same Church, continually setting down the footsteps of her examples, contemplates her dowry—that is, the body and blood of the Son of God—with the deepest devotion, and offers it to the Creator of all [Col. 0512B] in the sight of the living and burning lights, namely the heavenly citizens, in the submission of most humble obedience.

“What is this? As the flesh of my only-begotten Son arose in the undefiled womb of the Virgin Mary and was afterward given up for human salvation, so also now his flesh, frequently increased in the incorruptible integrity of the Church, is given for the sanctification of believers. For as a craftsman melts his gold by fire, now joining it and now separating what he has joined, so I, the Father, through the sanctification of the Holy Spirit, now glorify the flesh and blood of my Son in the offering, and now distribute it thus glorified to faithful people for their salvation.

“Therefore, when the priest, clothed in sacred vestments, approaches the altar to celebrate the divine sacraments, [Col. 0512C] you see that a great serenity of light suddenly descends from heaven with the ministry of angels and shines around the whole altar. For when the steward of souls, girded with a consecrated cincture, approaches the life-giving table for the sacrifice of the innocent Lamb, a great brightness of the heavenly inheritance suddenly shines from heaven’s secret place, expelling the density of darkness. With the sending forth of heavenly spirits, it irradiates everywhere that ordered rite of sanctification. For there the refreshment of souls is performed for the salvation of believers.

“How? When the Church, through the priest’s voice, asks for her dowry, which is the body and outpoured blood of my Son, in order that she may be fitted for blessed childbirth in the salvation of souls—because through the shedding of this precious blood she has also received increase in a great multitude of peoples—then I, who am unfailing light, illuminate that place of sanctification in my holiness for the honor of the body and blood of my only-begotten Son. For when the priest begins to invoke me over the sanctification of the altar, so that I may behold that which my Son offered me—bread and wine at the supper of his death, when he was about to depart from the world—I see that my Son himself showed this to me in the hour of his Passion, when he was about to die upon the wood of the cross. In so doing, he signified that I should always hold the same Passion before my sight and should not erase it from my most keen vision whenever the blessed offering of the most holy sacrifice was offered to me by the priestly office [Col. 0513A]. For in the shedding of his blood he offered me bread and the cup, casting down death and raising humanity.

“Moreover, because the dignity of entering and leaving the enclosure of virginal chastity belonged not to human nature but to divine power, therefore this also is possible: that the flesh of my only-begotten Son may be renewed from wheaten bread, and his blood from the wine of the grape with water, in sanctification. As I showed through my faithful servant, the prophet Joel, saying:

‘The threshing floors shall be filled with grain,
and the presses shall overflow with wine and oil.
And I will restore to you the years
which the locust, the grub, the rust, and the caterpillar have eaten—
my great strength which I sent among you.
You shall eat and be satisfied,
and you shall praise the name of your [Col. 0513B] God,
who has done wonders with you;
and my people shall never be put to shame.’  
(Joel 2)

“What is this? Through God’s wonderful ordering, the threshing floors of the faith of the believing Church will be filled with every good thing. For I give the fruit of grain into the flesh of my Son, so that even in the true salvation by which my faithful are called back to their homeland, there may abound those contritions in which they crush the desires of their flesh for my name’s sake. There I also bring the liquid of the grape into the blood of that same only-begotten Son, giving them as well the oil of mercy.

“How? In another manner, namely in your salvation, I will restore to you the cycles of those vanities which the locust [Col. 0513C] of forgetfulness through unbelieving ignorance has devoured—namely, where evils first arose in Adam’s children. They held the fruitfulness of my righteousness so deeply in forgetfulness that, just as someone forgets the food necessary to him after transferring it into the stomach, they tore apart my righteousness in their impiety, just as the locust gnaws fruits. How? Where the locust of negligence removes, through the sloth of the mind, the usefulness of good fruits, there the grub of foulness wraps itself in the dregs of uncleanness. For such people wrap themselves in the filth of unbelief in idols and in other like schisms; in diabolical inquiry, magical arts, and the examination of creatures rather than the Creator; in the chance events of human affairs; and in the basest foulness [Col. 0513D] of murders and fornications. They feed themselves on these things just as the grub is nourished on mud.

“How? Where the grub of disgrace loves the stench of filth, there the rust of bitterness consumes the metals of faithful brightness. For those people, opposing God’s righteousness, labor to obscure it, just as rust generally takes away the beauty of metals. How? Where the rust of corrosiveness infects the splendor of good deeds, there the caterpillar of harmful action spoils the green plants of abundant usefulness. For such people, throwing away from themselves through the malice of their wickedness the most bright virtues—such as simplicity, chastity, and firm constancy—which the Holy Spirit irradiates with every greenness of blessedness, strive to destroy them [Col. 0514A] just as the caterpillar diminishes the usefulness of plants.

“Through all these things is shown my greatest strength, which by the greatness of its power overcame diabolical adversities when I sent it among you for your salvation. How? I, the Father, sent my Son into the world, bodily born of a Virgin, that through him I might redeem you from the ruin of death. Thus I might dwell in you and you in me, when my Son also, going to his Passion, gave you his flesh to eat and his blood to drink. Therefore you will devoutly eat this sacrament for your salvation, happily feeding upon it; and consequently, through the oil of my mercy, you will be satisfied from the hunger of the soul’s destruction. For my [Col. 0514B] Son also brought the medicine for your wounds in repentance. And because the bride of my Son is adorned with all righteousness and truth, you will faithfully praise my name—I who, being one God in the true Trinity, govern you, show my wonders in you, and deliver you immovably from diabolical power. Thus my people, whom I have willed so wonderfully to draw from the jaws of hell, will not be put to shame by the confusion of death in the eternity to come.

“And you see that the aforesaid serenity remains upon the altar until the sacrament has been completed and the priest leaves the altar, because that serenity—namely, of eternal vision—is shown most brightly in those wonderful mysteries until, once the mysteries of that most holy office have been performed, the one who is steward of [Col. 0514C] those sacraments withdraws from that sanctification and completes the secret mysteries. What is this? It is fitting that the divine Majesty should most fully manifest its power in those most blessed sacraments; and while a person remains occupied in the things pertaining to God, God’s help does not leave that person.

“Moreover, after the Gospel of peace has been read and the offering to be consecrated has been placed upon the altar, when the priest sings the praise of almighty God, namely, ‘Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth,’ and thus begins the mysteries of the ineffable sacraments, a fiery radiance of immeasurable brightness suddenly descends upon that same offering with heaven opened. [Col. 0514D] For when, by the power of living breath, the kiss of the King has been uttered and the fruit of the brightness of life—which is to be made bright in sanctification for the building of God’s wall—has been placed there; when that messenger of truth sends forth the sweetest sound in praise of the Creator of all through the triple invocation of the anointing of that Lord of hosts, and thus begins the hidden things of the dawn’s splendor, namely of the incarnate Son of God from the Virgin, then an inaccessible serenity of incomprehensible height suddenly bends down upon the mysteries of the most holy sacrament, the most bright tabernacle having been opened. It wholly suffuses the offering with its brightness, as sunlight illuminates an object which it penetrates with its rays. For the most holy heat, in the Father’s power, so fills the shining circuit of that offering that radiant brightness enters the [Col. 0515A] thing upon which it spreads itself.

“What is this? The bride of my Son offers bread and wine upon my altar with most devout intention. How? Through the priest’s hand, faithfully reminding me to give her, in that offering, the flesh and blood of my Son. How? Because the sufferings of my only-begotten Son always appear in the heavenly secrets, that offering is therefore united to my Son in my burning heat with the deepest wonder, so that it becomes his flesh and blood with the truest certainty. By this the Church is strengthened in most blessed flourishing.

“For while the aforesaid brightness irradiates the offering as has been said, it invisibly raises it up to heaven’s hidden places, because that fiery radiance, while it fills the [Col. 0515B] sacrament itself with illumination, draws it upward by invisible power to those hidden things which the mortal eye cannot see. It then sends it back downward upon the same altar, because with a gaze of condescension it most sweetly lays it upon the table of sanctification. This is like a person drawing breath inward and breathing it outward again: that person sends the breath of living flourishing, by which he lives through God’s wondrous ordering, inward into himself and then sends it out again so that he may live.

“Thus the offering becomes true flesh and true blood, although it appears before human sight as bread and wine. For as God is true and without deception, so the height of this sacrament is a firm height which no one can overthrow, [Col. 0515C] true flesh and blood without deceit. As the soul truly flourishes in flesh and blood while a person lives in the body, so also this mystery exists in bread and wine where it is venerated by true celebration. It appears thus to human beings because, as a human being’s blind eye cannot perfectly see God, so a human being cannot bodily behold these mysteries. As one sees a person’s body but not that person’s spirit, so one can perceive the appearance of bread and wine, but not these sacraments.

“What is this? The brightness which appeared over the body of my Son buried in the tomb, raising it from the sleep of death, also shines upon the altar over the sacrament of the body and blood of that same only-begotten Son [Col. 0515D] of mine. It conceals the sacrament from human sight, so that people cannot see its holiness except under the appearances of bread and wine, according as that offering has been placed upon the altar. Likewise, the divinity that was in the humanity of the Son of God was so covered from human beings that they could see him only as a human being while he lived among them as a human being, though without sin.

“What is this? I who created all things graciously receive the aforesaid offering when the Church offers it to me through the priestly hand. For as the Divinity displayed its wonders in the Virgin’s womb, so it manifests its secrets in this offering. How? The flesh and blood of the Son of God are made manifest. How? When that offering is invisibly drawn upward, as if in an instant, [Col. 0516A] by God’s power and then sent back again, it is so warmed in the heat of the divine Majesty that it becomes the flesh and blood of the only-begotten Son of God.

“This mystery is as though someone wrapped most precious ointment in ordinary bread and placed a sapphire in wine, and I were to change it into a flavor so sweet that you, O human being, could discern in your mouth neither the bread with the ointment nor the wine with the sapphire, but only perceive the sweet flavor, since my Son is sweet and gentle.

“What is this? By this ointment is understood my Son, born of the Virgin, who was anointed with most precious ointment. How? He was clothed in holy humanity, an ointment so precious that it suffuses the death-dealing [Col. 0516B] wounds of human beings with its sweetness, so that when they turn to him, they no longer rot or stink in Adam’s ruin. By this sapphire, however, is signified the divinity present in that same Son of mine. As the cornerstone, he is gentle and humble, because he did not take root from the root of human flesh that comes from man and woman; rather, in my heat he was wondrously incarnate from the most sweet Virgin. Therefore his flesh and blood must be believed to be sweet and pleasant for reception.

“But you, O human being, cannot receive this spiritual gift visibly, as though you ate visible flesh and drank visible blood, because you are the corruption of mud. Rather, as your living spirit is invisible within you, so this living sacrament, invisible in this offering, must be received invisibly [Col. 0516C] by you.

“For just as the body of my Son arose in the Virgin’s womb, so also now the flesh of that same only-begotten Son rises in the sanctification of the altar. What is this? The invisible human spirit receives invisibly this sacrament, which is invisible in this offering; while the visible human body visibly receives this offering, which is visible in the sacrament. Yet they are one sacrament, just as God and man are one Christ, and as a rational soul and mortal flesh in a human being are one human being. Therefore, whoever beholds me in right faith, when receiving this sacrament receives it faithfully for sanctification.

“What is this? My Son was wondrously [Col. 0516D] born of a most inviolate Virgin, whose flesh never boiled over in the delight of lust but remained always untouched, because the vessel of that Virgin was most pure. In it he willed my only-begotten Son to be incarnate. Therefore I did not permit that vessel of the most sweet Virgin to dissolve in the heat of passion, because in it my Son wondrously assumed a human body.”

But the fact that this most blessed Virgin heard the true address in that same secret place through the angelic word, and thereupon became believing and lifted the sighs of her mind upward when she said, “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to your word” (Luke 1), and immediately conceived the Only-Begotten of God when the Holy Spirit came upon her, signifies that almighty God is to be invoked through the words of the priest in the priestly office. Thus [Col. 0517A] the priest, believing faithfully in God and offering him a pure oblation with devotion of heart, utters words of salvation in the service of humility; and heavenly Majesty, receiving that same oblation, by wondrous power transforms it into the flesh and blood of the merciful Redeemer.

How? Because just as my Son first wondrously assumed humanity in the Virgin, so now too this oblation is wondrously made his flesh and blood upon the altar. Therefore this sacrament too is whole and entire, existing invisibly and visibly: just as my Only-Begotten is wholly entire, invisible according to divinity and visible according to humanity while remaining in the world. For as a young bird emerges from an egg, and as a winged little worm arises from a small seed—when the creature flies away, that from which [Col. 0517B] it arose remains—so too in this oblation the truth of the flesh and blood of my Son is to be held by faith, although the same oblation appears before human sight as bread and as wine.

Thus, as you see there, as though in a mirror, the signs of the birth, passion, and burial, and likewise of the resurrection and ascension, of the Savior, the Only-Begotten of God—just as they were accomplished in him when the Son of God was in the world—so, that you may consider this in true manifestation, the mysteries of the one born of the Virgin, suffering upon the cross, buried in the tomb, rising from the dead, and ascending into heaven, namely of him who came to earth for the salvation of humankind, shine with most pure brightness in these same sacraments; just as, when that same Only-Begotten of God dwelt bodily in the world with them, he suffered these things in his body [Col. 0517C] by the Father’s will for the redemption of the human race.

What is this? Before my eyes appears what my Son suffered in the world for love of humankind, because the birth, passion, burial, resurrection, and ascension of my Only-Begotten slew the death of the human race. Therefore these things shine before me in heaven, because I have not forgotten them; rather, until the consummation of the age they shall appear before me like the dawn in great brightness.

What is this? In that passion I foresee, until the end of the world, all those who will believe it and those who will reject it, because it will always shine before me as long as humanity must say what my Son [Col. 0517D] taught his disciples to pray to God, as it is written: “And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors” (Matthew 6).

What is this? You who have all things in your power, behold the shedding of that blood which was poured out for the human race; and forgive us, who are children of transgression, our debts which we ought to have paid to you but did not, because of the hardening of our heart.

What is this? We do not fulfill what we promised in baptism, because we have transgressed your commandments and cast away innocence, just as Adam did not obey you in paradise and corrupted the garment of innocence. But you, who are merciful, do not punish us according to our wickedness; rather, forgive our transgression according to your mercy. And so we too, [Col. 0518A] who are transgressors, although we have much malice within us, nevertheless, out of fear and love for our Savior, forgive from our heart our debtors the injury which they have inflicted upon us.

How? Because those who ought to love us, since we are human, trouble us greatly and thereby do not love you but neglect your commandments. Yet we do not pursue them according to the malice they exercised against us; rather, beholding your just judgment, we do not avenge ourselves upon them as far as we can. So too, O God, be merciful to us, for you are just and good.

Therefore hear, O human being: as long as help must be given to you, and as long as you can help other people, so long the passion of my Son shall appear before me in mercy, [Col. 0518B] and so long too his flesh and blood shall be consecrated upon the altar for reception, for the salvation of believing people and the cleansing of their sins. For when my Only-Begotten was bodily in the world, his body was sustained for the nourishment of his flesh and blood by wheat and wine; therefore now also his flesh and blood are consecrated upon the altar in the oblation of wheat and wine, so that faithful people may thereby be refreshed in soul and body. Since that same Son of mine wondrously redeemed humankind from Adam’s perdition, so now too he mercifully absolves people from the daily evil into which they frequently fall.

For in the consecration of the aforesaid oblation appears everything that my Son suffered bodily in his flesh for the redemption [Col. 0518C] of humankind; and I do not wish to conceal this, because I draw his elect upward to heavenly things, so that through them his body may be brought to completion in the aforesaid members.

Therefore I also wonderfully show forth all these sacraments in this oblation, because when they appear upon the altar, then that same oblation becomes the flesh and blood of my Son, although it appears before human sight as bread and wine; for human frailty is so tender that it would shrink from receiving raw flesh and raw blood. For mortal humanity cannot behold Divinity so long as it is mortal. Therefore this mystery, which wholly belongs to Divinity, is hidden from human beings, so that they receive it invisibly, [Col. 0518D] because that same Only-Begotten of mine, now immortal, dies no more.

Therefore, O human being, I give you his flesh and blood in the oblation of bread and wine, so that through what is visible you may receive in true faith that which is invisible. And you receive this same sacrament with true certainty through divine power; yet it does not appear visibly to you, just as it has at times been shown to my elect in great necessity, when through it they were placed in great affliction. I do all these things for the love and benefit of humankind.

But every creature is subject to my commands; you, O human being, are always rebellious against me. Therefore you are blind and deaf, yet you cannot rebel against me. Do I not do, without your seeing it, [Col. 0519A] what pleases me? You do not see with the eyes of your flesh or hear with its ears how I place a human soul in its body or how I remove it from its body; but your soul shall understand me when it has left its mortal body. So too I give you the flesh of my Son to eat and his blood to drink, and I accomplish this by my power while you, O human being, do not see it.

Therefore, as you see, when that priest sings the chant of the innocent Lamb—“Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world”—and presents himself to receive holy communion, the aforesaid fiery radiance withdraws to heaven. For when that minister proclaims the praise of him who, in the innocence of his gentleness, bore the sins of humankind, and opens the inward parts of his breast [Col. 0519B] to these sacraments with outward devotion, that unconquered brightness which showed its power there withdraws into the heavenly secrets. And thus, when heaven is closed—that is, when those heavenly mysteries withdraw—you hear a voice from on high commanding believing and faithful people to eat and drink with true devotion the flesh and blood of their Savior, who suffered for them and underwent temporal death in order to wash away the defilement which the first parents, by transgressing God’s command, brought into the world; so that, cleansed from this transgression, they may by faith be restored to the rightful inheritance which they lost through disobedience.

For just as the Only-Begotten of God gave his body and blood [Col. 0519C] to his disciples at supper, so now too he gives his flesh and blood to his faithful upon the altar. It is like a person who, after completing the work of his will, gives it to people for their use. For the Son of God, carrying out the commands of his Father, offered himself for the salvation of humankind and gave his body and blood to be eaten and drunk for their sanctification. Thus the bridegroom speaks to his friends in the Song of Songs, saying: “Eat, my friends; drink and be intoxicated, my beloved” (Song of Songs 5).

What is this? Eat in faith, you who have come to friendship with me through holy baptism, because the blood poured out by my Son has wiped away Adam’s fall for you. Chew over the true medicine in the body of my Only-Begotten, so that your repeated sins, [Col. 0519D] when you frequently commit injustice in your works, may mercifully be wiped away.

Therefore drink in hope from this vine which has led you out from eternal punishment, taking, that is, the cup of salvation, so that you may believe boldly and courageously in that grace by which you were redeemed. For you shall be sprinkled with that blood which was poured out for you. And thus be intoxicated in love, you who are most beloved to me, abounding in the streams of the Scriptures, so that with utmost zeal you may withdraw yourselves from carnal desires; and so that I may awaken in you splendid virtues, greatly beloved by me, likewise giving you the body and blood of my Only-Begotten, just as he himself gave this same sacrament to his disciples. As it is written in the Gospel:

“While they were at supper, [Col. 0520A] Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, gave it to his disciples, and said: ‘Take and eat; this is my body.’ And taking the cup, he gave thanks and gave it to his disciples, saying: ‘Drink from this, all of you; this is my blood of the New Testament, which shall be poured out for many for the remission of sins. But I say to you, I shall not henceforth drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father’” (Matthew 26).

What is this? When the Son of God celebrated with his disciples that consummation by which he was about to pass from the world—namely, when he was no longer to remain among earthly affairs as long as he had previously done, but was to persevere in the Father’s will unto the passion of the cross—he received with highest devotion, for the salvation of humankind, bread in remembrance of his body, [Col. 0520B] moving his Father with all desire: so that, just as he had come forth from him and wished to return to him, the Father might also consider whether, if it were possible, that cup which he was to drink might pass from the frailty of his flesh, although this was not to happen.

Therefore he blessed that bread in remembrance of the sweat of his body, when, submitting himself to the Father’s command and willing to die upon the cross, he gave his body and blood to his disciples in the distress of that passion, lest they too forget that he had given them this example. And he broke it for them, because although that passion was harsh for his body, nevertheless, obedient to his Father, he conquered the most cruel death in the death of his body, signifying also that his flesh and blood [Col. 0520C] were to be given in the sacrament of the oblation to those who believe in him.

And he gave it to those same disciples for true salvation, so that they too might do these things in his name, just as he did them for love of them, saying in a most gentle voice: “You who desire humbly to follow me, receive with burning love this example which I leave you—namely, my passion and my works, which I completed at the command of my Father; for he sent me to teach and reveal his kingdom. And faithfully eat what I give you, because it is my body.”

What is this? Eat my body, because you must imitate my works in your spirit and your flesh, when the Holy Spirit inspires them in your heart, just as a person swallows food and puts it into the body. For as you ought to follow me in my works, so you and all who are willing to keep my commands shall also eat my body.

Then [Col. 0520D] the Son of God, taking in salvation the cup of salvation, gave thanks to his Father, because when blood was shed from his side, this grace was given to believers—a grace so strong that it overcame the ancient serpent, liberated lost humanity, and faithfully strengthened the whole Church.

How? Because that same Savior gave his most precious example to his faithful in the sweetness of his love, exhorting them with the gentle inspiration of admonition: “All of you who desire faithfully to follow me, drink confidently from this saving cup, so that you may discipline your body in distress and restrain your blood in sweat for love of me, to strengthen the [Col. 0521A] Church; denying yourselves, just as I submitted myself to suffering and poured out my blood for your redemption, not considering the tenderness of my flesh in this, but accomplishing your salvation.

“For this blood which is poured out for you is not that blood which was sprinkled under a shadow in the Old Testament, but my blood of the New Testament, given for the salvation of peoples.

“How? I, who am the only Son of my mother, namely of the most undefiled Virgin, poured out my blood upon the cross for the redemption of those people who behold me in faith. And just as I then gave it for the liberation of the human race, so now too I give it upon the altar for humankind, namely for the cleansing of those who receive it faithfully. For at the supper of my passion [Col. 0521B] I gave you my body and blood to eat and drink, so that now you too may do the same upon the altar in memory of me.

“Therefore, in the disclosure of truth, I say to you who have faithfully followed me: I shall no longer drink this cup of anguish amid the heaviness which I now suffer from the Jews, until that day when, rising from death and casting death down, I bring the day of salvation, when I shall drink with you—who are mine—this cup of your redemption, showing you the newness of rejoicing, because the destruction of the old sin shall be cast away and that kingdom which my Father prepared for those who love him shall be opened to you.”

What is this? By my death, which I suffered upon the cross, you shall experience the salvation of souls; and after my resurrection, receiving the Paraclete Spirit at my [Col. 0521C] ascension, you shall receive the newness of the new teaching. Thus you shall endure many tribulations because of my name, and I shall endure them with you—not because I shall henceforth suffer any bodily miseries, as I suffered before when I was bodily in the world, but because you endure them in my name, and there I endure them with you; for you are in me and I am in you.

And thus, as has been said, you who have faithfully believed in me shall receive the body and blood of my Son for the abolition of your sins, so that, gladdened by this sacrament, you may attain the strength of heavenly consolation. Thus my servant David cries in the ardor of my will, saying:

“The earth shall be satisfied from the fruit [Col. 0521D] of your works, producing grass for cattle and herb for human service, that you may bring bread forth from the earth, and wine may gladden the heart of humankind; that he may make the face cheerful with oil, and bread may strengthen the human heart” (Psalm 103 [Vulgate]).

What is this? O God, whose magnificence is above all things: from that faith by which you are known in truth—so that it is itself the fruit of virtues in your wisdom—humanity shall be satisfied. That is, the person adhering to faith casts away the hunger of unbelief upon the way of righteousness, whereas before, ignorant of truth, that person had failed from rectitude, fasting.

But now, in the abundance of good works, producing contrition of soul, that person faithfully gives those who are simple an example of humility, considering his or her own frailty. And, rising with the shoot of virtues [Col. 0522A] in the abundance of that security, he offers the verdure of true uprightness in service to those who seek earthly things; because for their benefit he labors at those acts which bring faithful souls to heavenly joys through the service of their fortification and defense—as do those who, by the warfare of their strength and protection, most courageously defend those whom they ought to protect.

And these things precede among human beings by your will, O God, so that, adorned with these virtues, you may wondrously bring forth for them the body of your Son from that fruit which the earth produces in the purity of greenness; just as your Only-Begotten, coming bodily from the womb of virginal chastity, mercifully gave in himself to believers the bread of life.

You shall perform this miracle also so that the blood of that same Only-Begotten of yours [Col. 0522B], which is poured out for the salvation of souls, may gladden the inner power of people—that is, their souls—for the remission of their sins.

How? Because just as the body of your Son was formerly offered upon the cross for the redemption of the human race, so now too his flesh and blood are consecrated upon the altar for the salvation of believers. Therefore, when this has been wondrously accomplished by your will, then this too shall occur: that the sacrament itself may make glad the face, that is, the Church anointed with the oil of mercy. For believers, embracing mercy with the joy of faith, appear beautiful in the eyes of the Lord. Since the salvation of the world, hanging upon the cross, mercifully delivered humankind from the devil’s snare, he also graciously loosed people from the bond of sins, so that they too, believing faithfully in God with the joy of their [Col. 0522C] simple heart, may not cease to help those suffering misery with fervent devotion.

And believers ought to burn with this love, so that that bread which gives life to those tasting it may strengthen their minds, always wavering in instability, lest the intention of their heart decline toward evil, but may rise strongly toward that which is life.

Now this bread is the flesh of my Son, which no darkness of sins obscures and no stain of iniquities clouds; so that those who receive it worthily may be flooded in soul and body with heavenly light and faithfully cleansed from the stains of their inward filth. Therefore let there be no doubt concerning this most sacred flesh; for he who formed the first human being [Col. 0522D] neither from flesh nor from bone is able to work this sacrament in this manner.

Therefore, O virginal birth, you arise, grow, expand, and produce a great branch in many shoots, through which the heavenly Jerusalem shall be built, coming not from male seed but from a mystical breath. For in your birth you are not bound by any stain of sins; rather, you flowered in the wonder-working of virtues. You arose as such a flower from an untilled field that you shall never wither through any accident of mortality, but shall always endure in the fullness of your greenness.

Therefore this sacrament of your body and blood must be venerated in the Church in the office of truth until the last human being comes at the end of the world, who shall truly be saved through this same mystery, because it comes from God’s secret place and brings salvation to believers [Col. 0523A]. Thus David testifies, saying:

“And he commanded the clouds above, and opened the gates of heaven. And he rained manna upon them to eat, and gave them bread of heaven. Humanity ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance” (Psalm 77 [Vulgate]).

What is this? The heavenly Father, through the power of his glory, softened human minds from the height above when, to the patriarchs and prophets, he revealed in the secrecy of his mysteries that through which they truly foretold his Son in the Holy Spirit; and in the legal commandments they wondrously signified him to people through the blood of goats and through other manifestations.

And thus, opening the sweetness and gentleness of his heart, he sent them his Son [Col. 0523B] in the mildness and ardor of love, that through him they might be refreshed from the hunger of their unbelief; giving them the refreshment of heaven, by which, faithfully filled, they might attain the full joy of every felicity and blessedness.

Therefore humanity received in the humanity of the Son of God that bread at whose sweetness the heavenly angels, beholding God, cannot be sufficiently satisfied, when the highest Father sent people these refreshments of blessedness in an abundance of spiritual joy.

Therefore let the faithful person hear with faithful hearing: O faithful people, who are the Church’s offspring, hear and understand the protection of your souls. You are not children of the devil but heirs of the heavenly kingdom; consider how I, the gentlest and most gracious Father, have surrounded you with the great felicities of your [Col. 0523C] salvation. Therefore attend to the goodness of your Father, to how that which is for your salvation has been ordained through me. For although you are lowly ash, nevertheless the humanity of my Son demands your salvation.

How? My Son was born of an incorrupt Virgin, who knew nothing of that pain but remained in the flourishing purity of her integrity, as grass thrives in the glory of its greenness when dew falls upon it from heaven.

And because that Virgin from whom my Son thus assumed flesh without sin was incorrupt, it is therefore fitting that his flesh now be made from that fruit which has no juice of bitterness.

How? The grain of wheat is the strongest and best fruit [Col. 0523D] among other fruits. It has neither sap nor pith in its stalk, as other trees do; but rising in its grass into an ear, it advances toward its fruit and produces no bitter juice through heat or cold, but yields dry flour. So too the flesh of my Son was dry, without every foulness of human pollution through which the human race arises in the lustful embraces of man and woman.

My Only-Begotten was not born thus; rather, he came forth in the flourishing integrity of virginity, just as a grain joined with a grain produces wheat. For as the flourishing stalk of wheat, without pith, bears dry grain in the purity of the ear, so too the blessed Virgin, giving birth without male power, brought forth her most holy Son in the simplicity of innocence; and he drew from that mother no [Col. 0524A] sap of sin, because she too conceived him without a man’s pith.
