Just as the stalk does not give sap to the grain, because it does not flourish from a pith-filled stem, but thrives by sun and rain and gentle air, so too the aforesaid most undefiled Virgin, overshadowed not by a man but by the power of the Most High and flooded with the infusion of the Holy Spirit, brought forth her Only-Begotten in the sweetness of chastity. Although that Virgin was herself born by the will of man and woman, she did not bring forth her Son in that manner; rather, she gave birth in her integrity, without a man’s will, to him who came from heaven, true God and human being, most pure.

Since she bore him most purely in her virginity without defilement, the bread which is now truly consecrated as his flesh, being most pure in [Col. 0524B] its integrity, ought likewise to be received by the faithful in purity of heart and without an admixture of diversity. Thus I showed beforehand to the children of Israel, as it is written in my will:

“Remember this day on which you came out of Egypt and from the house of slavery, because the Lord brought you out from this place with a strong hand, so that you may not eat leavened bread” (Exodus 13).

What is this? You who wish to be imitators of my Son, be mindful of passing from death to life; that is, keep in your memory the salvation of that day which is my Son, on which he trampled death and gave life, and in which you came forth for your salvation from the miserable exile of perdition. You cast away the densest darkness of unbelief, being likewise delivered from the dwelling of diabolical slavery, [Col. 0524C] to which you had been given in Adam’s transgression.

Therefore now look from earthly acts to heavenly things. For I, the Lord, brought you out of evils in divine power; I prevail over all things with such strength that no opposing obstacle withstands my power so as to prevent me from penetrating all things most sharply. Thus, through my Son, I delivered you from this place in which, serving death through your unbelief, you did not labor in good works but lay in your perversity and shamefully persisted in it.

But since you have now been liberated from this oppression in my Only-Begotten, run from strength to strength, taking care not to admit into your conscience that unbelief which does not strengthen your heart in receiving it but rather weighs it down with its bitterness.

What is this? Do not pursue [Col. 0524D] diabolical arts, nor the other inventions which people have devised for themselves amid human contaminations—those of philosophers, pagans, and heretics. Rather imitate my Son in the mirror of faith, who freed you from the prisons of hell when he offered himself for you to the passion of the cross.

But that you may follow his footsteps more cautiously, strengthen your hearts with heavenly bread and receive his body with faithful devotion; for he, coming from heaven, born of the sweet and pure Virgin, and suffering upon the wood for your salvation, gave himself to you. Thus, without the admixture of that bitterness, receive with sincere affection the sweet and pure bread, his body consecrated upon the altar by divine invocation, so that by it you may escape the hunger of the [Col. 0525A] inner person and be able to attain the feasts of eternal blessedness.

Therefore in the wine which flows from the vine, by the same invocation, I wish to show wondrous things through the sacrament of his blood.

What is this? The blood of my Son flowed from his side, as the grape sweats from the vine. But as the grape is trodden underfoot and pressed in the winepress, and most sweet, strong wine flows forth to strengthen blood in the human being, so too, when my Only-Begotten was worn down in the sweat of anguish by blows and scourges and pressed beneath the wood of the cross, the best and most precious blood flowed from his wounds, flooding believing peoples with most health-giving deliverance.

And as the grape differs from other fruits, which have hard rinds and can be [Col. 0525B] eaten, since people are more accustomed to suck grapes than to eat them, so too my Son differed from other people in sins. For they, weighed down beneath the burden of wickedness, are subject to diverse passions; whereas my Only-Begotten, wondrously born from the most chaste Virgin, lacked every contagion of sin.

Therefore, because the grape is of tender substance, I will that wine be consecrated into the blood of that same Son of mine. For as wine sweats from the vine, so my Son came forth from my heart; and that same Only-Begotten is the true vine, with diverse branches proceeding from him, because the faithful are planted in him and through his incarnation become fruitful in good works.

And as this liquid [Col. 0525C] flows from the most sweet and strong fruit of the vine, so all righteousness appears in mercy and truth through the incarnation of that same Son of mine. All who seek him faithfully find these virtues in him.

How? Those who faithfully adhere to him become green and fruitful from him, so that they bear the best fruits in virtues; just as he himself, being sweet and gentle, brought forth most precious shoots in holiness and righteousness and cleansed those who believe in him from every filth of unbelief. As it is written of him in the Song of Songs: “My beloved is to me a cluster of Cyprus in the vineyards of Engaddi” (Song of Songs 1).

What is this? The Son of God, who saves me, an exiled soul, in his passion, also mercifully gives me in his resurrection the cup of life.

How? Just as [Col. 0525D] a cluster of Cyprus contains within itself the strongest fullness of drink, so the Son of God shall never be exhausted in this way, but can always give the drink of life to those who thirst, because he is the salvation of life.

For we who were formerly in deficiency, now strengthened in the manifestation and knowledge of the true sanctification of good works, eat through him the food of life; in it, knowing God, we proceed to life. When in the Old Testament—which, as though through a shadow, did not possess its full meaning but held much diversity in the manifestation of signification—we endured great hunger and could not rise to salvation, now, therefore, filled in him, we also drink in him the saving cup: namely, by faithfully tasting in true faith who God is, whom we cannot see with the outward eyes of [Col. 0526A] mortal flesh but whom we possess inwardly by spiritual understanding. Thus wine displays its strongest power in human veins, though people do not perceive this, but only know within themselves that it is so.

Therefore the bridegroom of souls is a cluster of Cyprus, whose fruit shall not fail.

How? A blind person entering a gate seeks the sight of a guide.

How? Because when a person who lacks the brightness of faith comes to faith, that person enters, through the pressure of the winepress, into the dew of Christ’s blood.

How? Just as through his commands we have life in our soul, so through his gift we have received cleansing in our flesh; for we, born in Adam’s transgression, are unclean, but are sanctified in his blood.

Therefore the betrothal of souls [Col. 0526B] says of him in the Holy Spirit: “My beloved, who is sweet and lovable to my heart, is for me the strongest wine through his blood in full sanctification. For while I am unclean in the planting of the flesh, like a vineyard still lying uncultivated among thorns, he, the fountain of salvation, mercifully washes sinners from their filth and most gloriously sanctifies them in the mystery of his secrets. For as he came sweetly forth from the Father’s heart, so he also sweetly manifests his blood in wine; and as he was wondrously born from the Virgin, so his body is wondrously declared in bread. For he is the cluster which shall never suffer deficiency through any loss.”

Therefore upon the altar he is trodden as in a winepress by the Father’s will, so that the human being, who [Col. 0526C] cannot subsist at all by himself because of the fragility of his weakness, may not fail. For as human blood receives increase from drink, so humanity receives sanctification from the blood of the Son of God. And as human blood, unless watered by drink, would turn to dryness and must be refreshed by drink, so wine in the consecration of the blood of the Son of God shall not fail, but shall always be upon the altar in the sacrament of his mystery.

But you too, O human being, know most attentively that in this consecration water must be mixed with the wine, because blood and water flowed from the side of my Son; so that in the wine his divinity is understood, and in the water his humanity is perceived. Therefore, since in him there is divinity and humanity, water is likewise to be joined to wine in this consecration; for, although wine signifies his divinity, water also displays his humanity, which exists pure and clean, without the admixture of virile blood. For my Only-Begotten One, being the fountain of living water, cleansed human beings in the rebirth of Spirit and water from Adam’s ancient guilt, and transferred them to heavenly things when he came into the world for their salvation, as it is written: “I, like the river Diorix, and like a water-channel, came forth from paradise” (Ecclus. 24).

What is this? When God established man in rationality, he gave him many mysteries, for, sending into him the breath of life, he exalted him by rationality. When that man, deceived, fell into death, I, the Son of God, who came to free him, flowing in the beauty of every irrigation of steadfast love, and issuing forth in the abundance of true and unfailing purity, came out from the secret place of heavenly delight, so that the human being who had perished through his guilt might mercifully be rescued from destruction.

How? So that the innocent blood of innocent innocence might be shed for him amid the constraining sweat of the Passion. How? In Adam’s transgression, when he himself was driven from paradise, his blood, because he was guilty, flooded wholly through the distress of expulsion; and thus, liquefied in that distress, it was suffused with watery sweat. Thus water is known to be mixed with human blood through sweat. Therefore, O human being, when God’s Only-Begotten began to be distressed in the flesh—that is, when he willed to suffer for the human race—his blood sent forth drops of sweat; and afterwards, while he hung on the cross, water flowed with blood from the wound in his side. Therefore, in that sacrament in which the mystery of his Passion is to be celebrated, water must be mixed with wine, because water and blood flowed from the wound in the side of the Son of God.

But in that same sacrifice the wine is to exceed the water, because blood surpasses decay, just as milk exceeds its own liquid, which is whey. Those who celebrate this mystery are to perform it as it has been shown to them; and likewise they exhort people there where, through my inspiration, they hear wisdom, as it is written: “Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mixed for you” (Prov. 9).

What is this? You who wish to cast off foolishness, come away from that ignorance by which you do not know God, and from that fornication through which you were sent into exile; return to your bright homeland, which has been shown beforehand to you through the mirror of faith in the fountain of living water. And in devout reverence eat my bread, which no man sowed in a field and to which the earth gave no greenness, but which came forth from God and remains in him. For as bread is eaten and as earth is trodden underfoot, so the Son of God, the living bread, surpasses the children of men. The Son of God is stable in the power of his divinity, whereas the children of men are unstable in the weakness of their flesh. For the Son of God, while bodily present in the world, did not have in his flesh the soft fluidity of sin; for just as fire, baking bread, dries it and leaves in it no soft moisture, so too God’s Only-Begotten, conceived from the most mighty fire of the Holy Spirit and born of the most chaste Virgin, remained in his body without any contagion of sin. Thus, as bread refreshes a human being, so faithful people are nourished in faith through that same Son of God, because he is the mightiest fruit, which will never fail. Therefore you faithful ones, eating this bread, also drink with pure intention this wine, wholly free of every defilement and not passing into that empty wandering where corruption, swallowing the purity of innocence, changes it into poison.

For in that manner the first human being was clean when he was created, because there was in him no division, but he was clean in his flesh and blood. When he committed transgression, he was deceived, so that thereafter he continually scattered his blood in the stench of adulterous uncleanness. For just as that human being had cast away the honor of innocence, so too his blood lost its blood-red color, overturned in human conception into the fluid of pollution. Yet in that fluid it is without fornication until blood appears; and that blood, taking on another form after its origin, lies in weakness until its marrow finds the fullness of its strength and until sensation rises in it through the awakening of hidden stirring. Then clean flesh and clean blood, purified of poison, appear until harmful heat strikes it, which by its blow casts forth the harmful foam of uncleanness.

But the Son of God was clean from all these things: having clean flesh and clean blood, so that the touch of no harmful heat ever touched him. Remaining in the sanctification and honor of most flourishing chastity, he could be violated by no contagion. Yet, placed in the distress of his Passion, he poured water into the blood of his side, because blood is not without water in its outpouring; rather, it exists so tempered that blood strengthens water and water softens blood.

Therefore, you who desire devoutly to worship God, because you love your salvation, receive this cup of sanctification, which I have tempered for you so that you may not feel the harshness of vengeance in the gentleness of remission. For divinity and humanity are in the heavenly Son: through whose Passion you have been freed from death, and through whose body and blood you are sustained, so that you may possess fellowship in the eternal dwelling.

But I, who am the beginning and the end (Rev. 21), again speak to you, O human being, concerning my noble Son, who is the flower of roses and the lily of the valleys, born of the most chaste Virgin, who bore him while remaining intact. Such was that birth that through it I was appeased regarding the iniquity of the human race’s first parents, who provoked me to indignation by their transgression. Therefore I continually behold that birth whenever I have the body and blood of my Son consecrated daily upon the altar to my name. Thus, through this sacrament you, O human being, are sanctified, eating his flesh and drinking that same blood.

For when the priest performs his office there as it has been appointed for him, invoking me with the most sacred words, then I am present there in the same power in which I was present where my Only-Begotten was made flesh without any division or contagion. Therefore his most pure and sweet body was in every way holy, so that those who now faithfully receive his flesh and blood are made alive with such sweetness that they suffer no contempt of rejection, as is written in the Song of Songs: “Who will give you to me as my brother, sucking the breasts of my mother, so that I may find you outside and kiss you, and now no one may despise me?” (Song 8).

What is this? The sighing and devotion of those established in the Church say in most certain faith: “Who is he who will give you, the bridegroom of the Church, to me, a most wretched human being set amid afflictions, in a most gentle offering? I call you my brother because of your incarnation, sucking mercy and truth—the nourishment by which divinity feeds human beings—which is my mother in my creation, namely, giving me life through the upbringing of growth.” What is this? For your grace is full of nourishment for the Church, since you grant her full abundance in the sacrament of your body and blood, you who are the living bread and the fountain of living water. You do this so that I may find you outwardly in manifest certainty: knowing that you are the Son of God in heaven, I also see you as human on earth—whom my mortal eyes cannot behold in divinity—and so that I may also find you in the bread and wine of the divine mystery, a sacrament without the weight of deception or the ambiguity of fraud. Then in this manner I kiss you: because you were incarnate for my salvation, and because you make me a participant in your body and blood, so that, since you came into the world for me and gave yourself to me, no creature may henceforth despise me, since it always follows your will in submission to you, while I, rebellious against your commandments, am found very often opposed to you.

Now therefore, as you see, O human being, when the priest, with these words established in the Holy Spirit, begins to invoke me at the altar over the offered sacrifice, amen, I tell you: I am present there in my burning heat, and with full desire I accomplish that sacrament.

How? Because, in the effect of that mystery, I spread burning love over that offering, namely from the beginning of the words by which the priest invokes me and makes this memorial: that my Son, amid the distress of his Passion, blessed bread and wine and delivered them to his disciples in the sacrament of his body and blood, so that they too might do the same for the salvation of the people. Truly I tell you: this invocation shall never be made over such an offering in remembrance of my Only-Begotten without the mystery of the body and blood being accomplished there—a mystery which the carnal eye, so long as it is dust, cannot see, unless it discerns it in faith with humble devotion.

How? When a bird sees an egg placed in its nest, it flies ardently over it and, warming it with its heat, brings forth a chick, so that the shell of the egg remains and the chick flies out. What is this? I, the Almighty, when an offering of bread and wine has been made upon an altar dedicated to my name in remembrance of my Son, illuminate it wondrously with my power and glory and transform it into the body and blood of my Only-Begotten.

How? By the very miracle through which my Son received flesh from a virgin, this offering too becomes his flesh and blood in this consecration. Yet the outward appearance of bread and wine is visibly seen by external eyes, while inwardly the holiness of the body and blood of that same Son of mine remains invisible.

How? When my Son was among human beings in the world, he was also with me in heaven; and now, remaining with me in heaven, he is also among human beings on earth—but this is spiritual, not fleshly. So I too, Father of every creature, am present to all, withdrawing myself from none; but you, O human being, withdraw yourself from it. Thus, when you look into water, your face appears in it, yet you cannot exercise any of your powers in it; but when you turn away from it, you no longer appear in it. But I do not appear to creation in such mutability; rather, I am present in true manifestation, and I do not withdraw my power from it, but exercise in it the strength of my will according as it pleases me. Therefore, in the sacrament of the body and blood of my Son I truly manifest my majesty, wondrously exercising my miracles there from the beginning of the priest’s secret words until that mystery is received by the people.

But this priestly office may be performed by the faithful from the first hour of the day until the ninth hour, according as the need of the time may be found in human circumstances. For Adam, rising in the morning, was deceived at the ninth hour; and the Passion of my Son, begun in the twilight of the day, is known to have been completed at the ninth hour: dying on the cross, he gave up his spirit and manfully overcame death by his death. There the Church, standing beside my Only-Begotten, received her dowry; and this is now to be celebrated by the children of that same Church.

This office is to be celebrated by priests in sacrifice while the stomach is fasting, not full, lest the coagulation of foods empty spiritual desire. For the spiritual feast must be received first, and bodily refreshment afterwards; and spirit is to be honored while flesh is to be restored. This sacrament is to be received with spiritual longing, not carnal appetite; therefore it should be received in fasting, not after banquets, except in that necessity when someone is in the expectation of passing from the world. But my Son gave his body and blood to his disciples toward the end of the day, because he brought them the true morning of life. And at the consummation of the age, when death passes away temporarily among human beings, the elect will shine like the sun in my kingdom (Matt. 13).

In this way my Only-Begotten, by his resurrection, showed that the souls of the righteous are withdrawn from hell and that the human race is restored to eternal life—the life which the reprobate angels lost when, desiring death with no one else urging them on, they were deceived by no tempter other than themselves, since they had no taste of sin in themselves as a human being has in the frailty of his body. Hence, when a human being, possessing bodily frailty, was deceived by one who lay in wait, he was also restored to life by one who lifts up; while the devil, having no bodily heaviness, was left in his perversity. But true and health-giving refreshment was given to humanity in receiving the body and blood of my Son, so that, invisibly refreshed in the soul through this sacrament, the person may rise and manfully resist his invisible adversary.

Those who receive this sacrament in a greater or smaller quantity should understand that both the one who receives more and the one who receives less receive one and the same power. For this sacrament consists not in quantity but in holiness; it saves those who receive it according to their faith, as it is written concerning manna: “And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, one more and another less; and they measured by the measure of a gomor. He who had gathered more had no excess, nor did he who had prepared less find less; but each gathered according to what he was able to eat” (Exod. 16).

What is this? The children of election attend to the heavenly sacrament according to what has been commanded them. Desiring ardently to see God, they gather it in their hearts according to the teaching of their chief masters; and according to what they have learned from them, they search it out in their souls—one having more devotion, another less attentiveness, in the secret of his heart. Thus they measure with their estimation, discerning, according to what they feel in their souls, the faith which they have in God—not dividing it but holding it whole—and considering how great and of what kind the devotion is with which they receive the body and blood of their redemption. Yet the same sacrament will not be holier for the one who receives more of it, nor more restricted for the one who receives less; rather, according to the faith of the person who receives it, so it will illumine that person.

Therefore, O human being, it is not to be received in magnitude, for the most mighty God is in both the small and the great offering of this mystery. Thus those who receive it must attend only to this: that they hold the triune and one God in their hearts with firm and entire faith. And so every faithful person, with a sincere and upright heart, gathers the powers of the soul according to what the capacity of faith in that person requires, taking care not to investigate divinity higher or deeper than the mind or thought can grasp, but soberly, as instructed in the Holy Spirit, submitting to the fear of the Lord; for the human being is poor ash.

But you foolish people, do not doubt whether this sacrament, shown to you in this way, is the body and blood of my Son. Remember, then, from what Adam’s flesh and blood were created: namely, from the mud of the earth. What therefore seems more possible to you: for me to make the flesh and blood of my Son from this offering, or to make a human being from the mud of the earth?

But a man pours forth seed from his blood, and a woman receives it. What more do they then contribute? Absolutely nothing, either in the creation or in the flesh of the child. Who forms the human being in flesh and bones, marrow and beautiful face, except I, the Father of all? Yet father and mother have no power to make or create the child, except that in burning lust they cast out their blood; afterwards they have no power whatever to form it. Can you see how these things happen, except that you behold them in their forms?

But you, O human being, say: “I do not see this offering to be flesh and blood as I see a human being to be body and blood.” To this I answer: You saw my Son bodily and in blood, mortal on earth; he is now immortal in heaven. Therefore you cannot now see him with bodily eyes, nor can you see how his flesh and blood are consecrated on the altar. This sacrament is not performed there for the priest’s glory, but for the glory of my Only-Begotten, who performed this office with his disciples at his supper. But as you cannot see me in my brightness while you are mortal, so neither do you see with your fleshly eyes the flesh or blood of my Son fleshly, since you cannot discern things invisible, but only insofar as your mortal sight can visibly grasp those things which are visible.

This sacrament must be offered to me in three materials. How? In bread, wine, and water, for the honor of the Trinity. Therefore, if any one of these three is lacking, the Trinity is not truly worshipped there; for the Father is understood in the wine, the Son in the bread, and the Holy Spirit in the water. Thus, one who offers wine without bread and water worships the Father but denies the Son and the Holy Spirit; or one who gives bread without wine and water has the Son but rejects the Father and the Holy Spirit; or one who uses water without wine and bread attends to the Holy Spirit but refuses the Father and the Son; or one who gives wine and bread without water has the Father and the Son but denies the Holy Spirit; or one who offers wine and water without bread worships the Father and the Holy Spirit but denies the Son; or one who uses bread and water without wine attends to the Son and the Holy Spirit but refuses the Father.

Therefore let there be no division in this sacrament, for I, remaining indivisible, am one inseparable God in three persons, just as thought, will, and deed are in one human being, without which a person does not exist. If there is a deficiency in this sacrifice—so that bread, wine, or water is neglected—then truly the one through whose negligence this happens will be subject to grave vengeance. For if it is done knowingly through the negligence of lukewarmness, or faithlessly through the uncertainty of unbelief, I will cast from my sight the one subject to this guilt, unless, returning to himself by grave repentance, he punish himself severely for it through repentance. Or if it happens unknowingly through the negligence of forgetfulness, then the one guilty in this matter will answer to me for this fault in the correction of penance, because he did not carefully ensure that all things belonging to my sacrifice were present. For when my Son hung on the cross, nothing necessary for salvation was lacking there, because through his shed blood he brought salvation of souls to humanity. Thus nothing should be lacking in this mystery either. For this sacrament is most sacred sanctification in all holiness; therefore this flesh and this blood must be received with every faith and devotion.

Whoever receives this most sacred flesh should not refuse to receive the blood of the same mystery, because my Son is altogether pure and a mirror of virtues; therefore his most noble blood must be received—unless, because of the recipient’s simplicity, the priest fears the danger of spilling it. In that case, let it be done for the recipient according to the simplicity of children, to whom bread as food is granted while wine as drink is withheld: so this most holy flesh is given to such a person, while the flowing blood is withheld, lest greater danger arise from it, and because that most holy flesh is joined to its blood and that blood to its flesh in one holiness. But if that person has such discretion that he can safeguard the mystery, then, when that holy flesh is given to him to eat, the blood of that same flesh is also given to him to drink.

The priest who celebrates this sacrament must be clothed carefully in the vestments which the ancient Fathers, taught by the Holy Spirit, ordained to be worn for this office. He must attend most carefully to the words which the Holy Spirit inspired into those same Fathers for the celebration of this mystery, diligently taking care to omit nothing from them. He must also consider with deepest devotion that example in which my Son took bread and the cup and gave them to his disciples to eat and drink.

But one who, through the negligence of forgetfulness, unknowingly errs in vestments or words belonging to this office must be corrected by grave and salutary penance. Nevertheless, seeking my mercy, that person will find it, because the transgression was not committed by intention or by wickedness of heart. But if someone knowingly transgresses in these sacraments through lack of devotion in the will or through malice of heart, I will say to that offender: “Wicked servant, why were you not properly clothed in the priestly garment, as your ancient and greater teachers instituted for you in the Holy Spirit, signifying the spiritual office in which my angels always minister to me? And why did you neglect the form of those words which the same Fathers handed down to you in the Holy Spirit for consecrating the body and blood of my Son, for the salvation and glory of the human race?” Therefore, whoever is guilty in this matter will answer to me for it unless he punishes himself by grave affliction in repentance.

But the priest who offers these feasts at my altar must not depart fasting from these feasts; rather, he must receive the refreshment of his soul in the body and blood of my Son. If he knows himself burdened by graver weights and unworthy of these feasts, then he must not presume to approach my table or, unwashed from the stench of his crimes, touch my Son—as did those who defiled both the table and the glory of his birth, cruelly cutting off the head of the shining lamp. Therefore, one so defiled must show the variety of his plague to the high priest, namely my Son, and also accuse himself before another mortal priest, who may show him the remedy of consolation with penance; and only then, purified, may he approach his office.

But I, the Father of all, do not will that the secret ordering of the most sacred discourse by which the priest should invoke me at the altar should consist in many and great speeches. Rather, it is to follow the right ordinance of the earlier masters, whom the gift of the Holy Spirit taught to invoke me in right admonition. Nor should it consist in a multiplicity of foolish wisdom, but in simplicity of heart. For I delight not in much speaking, but in the purity of heart of those who devoutly seek me and kindly embrace me in the ardor of love.

At other times, when my elect seek me, I bestow my grace on them according to the diversity of the gifts of the Holy Spirit; but in this sacrament I show myself wholly to them. For my Son is in me and I in him, and the Holy Spirit is in us and we in him, and we are one in divinity, just as body, other parts, and powers are one living human being. Therefore whoever approaches this sacrament must beware of coming in such a way as to offend the glory of Divinity.

But you, O human being, while other people approach the priest to receive this sacrament, observe five kinds among them. For those who desire to receive from their priest the reception of the divine mystery should cleanse the five senses of their bodies from the dregs of their sins and guard them worthily and praiseworthily from creeping uncleanness, so that they may receive it more healthfully.

Therefore, among those whom you see approaching this sacrament, some are radiant in body and fiery in soul. For, possessing the brightness of faith toward this sacrament, they do not doubt that it is the true body and true blood of my Son. Thus, receiving it with this faith, they are sustained and sanctified in their flesh, so that, sanctified by this mystery, after the resurrection they may appear in heaven in that same body; and in their souls they are infused and kindled with the fiery gift of the Holy Spirit, so that, flooded with this illumination, they reject earthly things and desire heavenly ones.

How? As the blaze of a fire is stirred by wind, so these persons are imbued through this sacrament in order that they may burn with heavenly love. But others appear pale in body and dark in soul, because, lukewarm in faith, they do not have firm faith in this sacrament. They are dull in understanding wisdom, like a child whose actions are foolish. Outwardly they hear with the ear, yet in the slowness of their hearts they do not understand what is said to them concerning this sacrament in such a way that they would gladly comprehend it perfectly in faith. Nevertheless, because of the uncertainty within them, they cannot perceive how great its holiness is. Therefore they are surrounded by darkness in their inward person, because they cannot raise their mind upward to that perfection. Conceived in sins, they are weighed down by the burden of bodily frailty from the perfection of that belief; yet they consent more to the spirit, in that they would gladly understand faith if they could overcome the lukewarmness of their heart.

For those not yet weighed down by greater burdens of sins in their deeds must, though as if unwillingly, consent to the spirit, because the soul, still possessing greater power since it has not yet been killed by sins, subjects the body to its own will. These are the struggles between body and soul: the soul wishes to rule the body, because what the flesh has in its desire—sin—is contrary to it; and the body disdains the justice which is in the soul’s desire, because the soul loves life. What is this? What is dead desires what is dead, and what lives loves what lives. How? The flesh loves sin, and the soul loves justice; in this they oppose one another and rarely agree. But as a child is fed and satisfied without labor and without understanding of its own perception, so these people are made alive by this sacrament almost through ignorance, because they disdain it neither through childishness nor through obstinacy, but embrace it simply in heart.

Some, however, are shaggy in body and foul in soul, drenched in much uncleanness of human pollution. For these persons are ugly and shameless in their flesh, defiling themselves with the dregs of vices; and, as a pig rolls itself in mud, so they contaminate their souls by infecting them with the varied filth of sins belonging to human contagion. Since they do not fear to approach unwashed in this pollution the sacrament of the body and blood of my Son, they must be cleansed by severe examination for this presumption. Yet I do not deny them my mercy in this purification, because I foresee worthy repentance arising in their minds.

Others are surrounded in body by very sharp thorns and appear leprous in soul, because, beset in their hearts by anger, hatred, and envy, they drive from themselves gentleness, sweetness, and love with these thorns of iniquity. Thus, desiring evil, abandoning good, and insulting other people in mockery, they render their souls unclean as though with most grievous ulcers. When they approach the divine mystery in this manner, they wound themselves severely. Yet I turn my eyes toward them when, punishing themselves in bitterness, they afterwards seek my grace in repentance.

Others appear blood-red in body and foul in soul like a rotting corpse, because, making divisions among human beings with bloody hand, they make their souls stink as though with the decaying discharge of most cruel perversity. For, not regarding my fear, they destroy by their cruelty what I established in humanity. Therefore, if, contaminated with this defilement, they do not fear to receive the body and blood of my Son, they cast themselves down through grave injury, since they presume to touch this sacrament so unwashed. Yet afterwards the fountain of salvation will pass through them if they strive to wash themselves from this wickedness by worthy repentance.

But of all these, when some receive the same sacraments, some are suffused with a fiery splendor, while others are darkened by a shadowy cloud. For when believers strive to approach the mystery of the body and blood of my Son, those who receive it with a devout mind and pure faith, shining in good works, are illumined by the gift of the Holy Spirit for the salvation both of body and soul. But those who receive it with a contrary heart and wavering mind, sluggish in perverse acts, bring upon themselves inwardly and outwardly the darkness of presumptuous unhappiness to their own harm, because they have rashly presumed, unwashed, to join themselves to this holiness.

For a human being so rebellious and obstinate as not to fear defilement—whether by simple fornication in the inward parts of one’s own body through touch and pleasure; or by contaminating oneself with double fornication, bringing forth one’s seed with a man or with a woman; or by tearing oneself apart through anger, hatred, and envy toward others; or by staining oneself with blood through murder of those encountered—and who thus, unwashed and uncorrected, rashly presumes to approach the body and blood of my Son without the cleansing of confession and without the penance of correction, knowingly and understandingly enters the judicial fire through his guilt.

How? He will be tested in this presumption and sin as gold in a furnace, so that none of the dust of that presumption shall remain in him by which, polluted and uncorrected, he approached communion with the innocent Lamb. For whoever approaches, as has been said, unwashed to the sanctification of the body and blood of my Son and thus receives that sacrament, receives it unto judgment.

How? As my most beloved Paul says: “Therefore whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. But let a human being examine himself, and so eat of that bread and drink of that cup. For whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord. Therefore among you are many weak and feeble, and many sleep” (1 Cor. 11).

What is this? Truly I tell you: whoever eats the bread of life or receives the cup of salvation, which is the sacrament of him who is Lord of heaven and earth, so as to treat it unworthily—being defiled, namely, in sins—will experience guilt in this. How? Because such a person receives the body and blood of his Lord, that is, the Savior of the world, in a biting and death-bringing manner, when, inclined to evil and polluted with uncleanness, forgetful of the fear of the Lord, he thus contaminated approaches the palace of saving redemption.

Therefore he also commits murder there. How? Because he pierces himself with many wounds when, concealing his crimes without wiping them away and without the washing of repentance, he rashly handles this sacrament. Therefore I say to him: “O most wretched and bitter one, how did you dare cast your Lord into the pit of such misery—the Lord whom the citizens of heaven ever long to behold? Therefore you will be examined by bitter repentance in body and soul, so that, if you do not correct your guilt, this punishment may be found in you after the resurrection of the dead.”

Therefore let the person who wishes here to be his own purifier test himself by faithful examination; and thus, with this devotion of self-scrutiny, let him take of that bread of holiness and taste of that cup of sweetness, so that, arriving at unfailing refreshment, he may escape the hunger of his soul’s weakness. For whoever handles this sacrament wrongly and, not cleansing himself from the filth of iniquity, receives it unworthily, brings upon himself a judgment of vengeance, because he eats and drinks it while unpurified; yet by this presumption he is not able [Col. 0537B] to injure or obscure the mystery, but condemns himself. And because you presume to approach this sacrament while foul with vices, therefore there are many sick among your company: namely, those who refuse to seek in this holiness the medicine of the soul, but impose upon themselves a most bitter sickness in these same sacraments, because they receive them for judgment. There are also many weak: namely, those so feeble in the law of God that they in no way wish to consider who he is whom they receive so unworthily. What does this mean? They do not wish to consider how they ought to fear and venerate their Lord, or how they ought to punish with bitter penitence the flesh which they have so nourished in vices. But [Col. 0537C] because they are so negligent, many also sleep in the forgetfulness of this negligence, neither knowing nor wishing to know how they ought to weep for their sins—just as a person in the sleep of slumber neither knows nor understands what, or how, things are in his body. Hence, O human being, when, unpurified by confession or penitence, you receive unwashed the body and blood of my Son, then in a dreadful inquiry into this presumptuous filth of your sins you will be examined in such a way as even new wine is cleansed of the impurity it contains when, in its ferment, it casts it forth from itself.

This same sacrament must also be handled and guarded by priest and people with such diligence and care [Col. 0537D] that no one neglect it so that it is cast down neglected upon the ground. For if through sluggish negligence it falls upon the ground, I avenge that outrage in my zeal, either upon the ground or upon the person, unless that person punishes himself by penitence and bitter scourges; for flesh and blood must make restitution for flesh and blood. How? The flesh and blood of the human being shall mourn in the human being, whose flesh and blood have carelessly handled the flesh and blood of my Son, just as the earth then trembled and people were shaken with fear when my Son, set upon the cross, gave up his spirit. But if you, O human being, in the instability of your heart say within yourself: “How does this offering on the altar become the body and blood of my Son?” then I shall also answer [Col. 0538A] you: “Why do you ask this, O human being, and why do you inquire into these things? Do I demand these things of you? Why do you search my secrets concerning the body and blood of my Son? These are not matters for you to demand; rather, receiving them only in great fear and veneration, guard them diligently, and do not hesitate further about this mystery. For you ought not to test me so rashly. And what are these things to you? Instead, seek me in most certain faith. For when I have examined the whole of your faith, I do not ask you what the body and blood of my Son are, or how this mystery is consecrated upon the altar. And who asks you, O human being, whether you do not feel the heat of fire in fire? No one. So neither seek me rashly in my secrets, lest you be harmed by it. But if you wish to seek them with devotion of soul, then [Col. 0538B] seek them diligently in prayer, weeping, and fasting, just as your ancient Fathers sought them most surely, and they were frequently revealed to them. And when you have searched and found them in this way, then leave what remains to the Holy Spirit.”

But those who approach these sacraments should come not by devious paths but by the straight way, lest, cast away from them, they suffer a great fall of the soul. How? For the most wicked deceiver, who without election and without the consecration of the chief anointing fraudulently usurps for himself the seat of pastoral office, and the most evil robber, who, having expelled his pastor, violently seizes his chair through the sibyls of those who consent with him: such persons either of their own accord will subject themselves to grave vengeance, [Col. 0538C] or through my zeal will bear a severe sentence for it. For in their most evil bitterness they imitate him who, desiring to possess the highest honor in himself, was cast down from every glory of blessedness into death; and they also follow Baal, who so deceived himself that, falsely naming himself God, he was given over to destruction. And if, in this perversity of their falsehood and presumption, they pretend to administer my sacred things, then those who are thereby infected rather than anointed are accounted before me like those whom the people hold up to derision—whom children make into comic characters for themselves in their games and play. But as this is vain among human beings, so also that is mockery before me which such [Col. 0538D] invaders pretend to perform in their deceit. Therefore, because their building is proved crooked, it cannot stand, because it is destined to fall. And so, if they appear to have established anything in sacred orders in my temple, it must be erased, because, having no justice, it is recognized as worthless.

Therefore let them come to their senses from this rashness, lest they become companions in punishment of him who, while seeking more than he ought, was sent from the height into the abyss of the depths. Likewise, that mangler who, lacking the anointing of priestly office, through the madness of his mind approaches my altar so furiously as though I were a buffoon or jester—this person, rashly touching the table consecrated to my name, wishing, that is, to offer the sacred oblation, which is not his office [Col. 0539A] to offer, does not fear to wound my Son with cruel torment. How? As an unbeliever assaults God through his unbelief, and as a madman runs into fire through his madness, so this man, not knowing me as God and not sensing me as burning fire, casts away my fear and does not love my gentleness. Rather, he wounds my Son when with lips not anointed he mangles that word which my Only-Begotten gave to his bride when he bestowed upon her his body and blood as a dowry. Hence it is said to one who attacks him so rashly: “Who touches my Son, so insolent and unanointed?” But the person who approaches my altar in this way, as often as he presumes to invoke my Son by the aforesaid secret word, so often strives to wound him—not that he torments him with any pain in this way, [Col. 0539B] but because he does not fear to touch him so presumptuously. If he remains in this contempt without penitence, he will stand among those in punishments who wounded my Son without cause. Therefore, lest he suffer these torments, let him take upon himself the lamentation of affliction; yet let him no longer presume to approach the ministry of my altar.

But the rest, who strive under the priest to minister in the service of ecclesiastical office, should beware of presuming to approach that ministry apart from the norm of justice; lest, if they fraudulently usurp that uprightness for themselves, then, found misshapen and unpolished, they be cast out by just judgment from the construction of the Church’s building. For I will that my ministers appear clean before me, without deceit and without filth. How? Let them approach my altar by rightful election, and then also stand before me there without impurity. How? Let them not look toward worldly coupling, because they have chosen the spiritual. How? Because they have entered my service. But if any of them indulges the burning desire of his flesh, let him mortify his body by abstinence and fasting, and chastise himself with cold and scourges. But if at last he slips into a woman’s pollution, let him flee that contamination as burning fire and deadly poison, and wipe away his wounds by bitter penitence; for I will that I be served in chastity. How? Because my Son too was most chaste, and in himself displayed all these ecclesiastical orders. How? [Col. 0539D] Namely, by serving, praying, and offering. How? For circumcision touched him in its service, prophecy showed him by its cry, he himself preached to human beings in his own person, and finally he offered himself as a living sacrifice upon the altar of the cross. And because he gave himself as a holocaust in chastity, so those who strive to offer him a holocaust at the altar should imitate his chastity. They should not only uphold chastity in others, but also preserve it in themselves. How? As the priest ought to guard himself from contact with a woman, so too he should restrain himself even from himself—namely, beware lest by the touch of his own hands he draw pollution from himself, so that the tumult of lust may not grievously rage within him. For Adam’s crime, bringing death upon human beings, stirred up in them [Col. 0540A] the sensations of fornication; and therefore people should restrain their flesh, lest they shamefully lie subject to the falls of death. How? Because my Son overcame death and gave them life. Since he assumed flesh in the integrity of virginal chastity, those who desire to serve him ought therefore also to be chaste, as it is written by divine command: “Be ready for the third day, and do not approach your wives” (Exod. XIX).

What does this mean? You who wish to serve God alone, be ready with the will of your heart for the day of that serenity, when the holy and ineffable Trinity, truly appearing, manifests its wonders in a great miracle. And therefore, if you wish worthily to approach God there, beware lest you join yourselves in carnal affection—that is, in carnal unions—lest you mingle your blood with the blood of one of more fragile constitution. You, O priests and my other ministers who serve under a spiritual name, ought to beware of this; for not even the apostles whom you follow divided themselves in different directions, nor did they leave you such an example. For I do not will that there be two unions in priests, namely, of spiritual and carnal devotion; because the priest will join to himself the justice of God, so that it is his wife, with whom he will nourish and teach the other peoples, as a father is accustomed to rear and instruct his children. And how would it be fitting for a priest to practice two unions in due measure, when they are contrary to one another in their difference? How? One is carnal and the other spiritual.

[Col. 0540C] And when the priest is shepherd and father of those people who have carnal marriage, if he himself then possessed it in the same way, who ought then to be his priest? He could have no other priest set over him than the devil, who ought to be his priest, because he too would have imitated the one who hides poison beneath honey. How? For as the devil hides evil beneath good, so priests of this kind, who follow their shamefulness rather than love chastity, strive to conceal carnal union beneath spiritual marriage, like poison beneath honey. But because my Son is wholly in chastity, those who touch [Col. 0540D] his body and blood upon the altar ought likewise to love chastity, as it is written: “A priest shall not take as wife a prostitute or a vile harlot, nor a woman repudiated by her husband, because he is consecrated to his God and offers the loaves of presentation” (Lev. XXI).

What does this mean? The one appointed to offer sacrifice to God should not love the injustice of the devil, who is the common author of every filth of all iniquity. Nor should he cast down his faculties so vilely that, while wishing to bear my yoke, he follows the will of his flesh against the justice of God and against the examples of the ancient saints by shamefully embracing it; lest he thus fulfill in dishonorable deeds that impurity rejected by those same ancient Fathers, who recognized that it came from the breath of the ancient serpent. Therefore, abandoning these [Col. 0541A] defilements, let him be a lover of God’s justice, because he is consecrated to his God in holiness—that is, withdrawn from carnal desires in the acts that produce children. Hence, being sober and undefiled, he can offer that bread which is set upon the table of consecration for the salvation of human beings. What does this mean? Namely, because that sacrifice, which is the life of the living, the refreshment of souls, and the mirror of all virtues—which are made clear through holy innocence in the form of chastity—is most clean from every defilement. Therefore those who are to offer this sacrifice must likewise be without the filth of pollutions, abstaining also from feasting and drunkenness, from jesting, laughter, and frivolous or disorderly behavior. Rather, let them be in that reverence which befits the successors of the ancient Fathers from whom they are planted, [Col. 0541B] and in that dignity which becomes honorable patrons. Let them also live in such a way that they are not double in two persons—that is, that they do not walk at once in the worldly and spiritual ways—because it is difficult to serve two masters at the same time, as my Son also testifies in the Gospel, saying: “No one can serve two masters” (Matt. VI).

What does this mean? No one clothed in a mortal tunic is able, because of the frailty of his mind and body, to render service to two masters at once with equal obedience. What does this mean? Because he cannot serve at the same time the lord of uprightness and the lord of injustice. Why? Because uprightness rejects injustice, and injustice assaults uprightness. So too a priest [Col. 0541C] cannot at once and with equal devotion have a handmaid and a mistress, namely carnal coupling and spiritual fellowship; for these two cannot together exist in perfection. For what is carnal assaults what is spiritual, and the spiritual suppresses what is carnal. Paul, my friend, knowing this, shows by my will that this is so when he says: “Therefore a bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife” (1 Tim. III).

What does this mean? It is necessary that he who stands above other people in the office of spiritual teaching order his life so that no scandal of offense or reproach may be found in him. How? Because a priest ought not to have two persons, so that he is at once the husband of a carnal wife and the husband of a spiritual spouse; rather, he shall be husband of one wife, namely the Church in holiness, who is one in my Son, because one Church arose in him. Yet though she is one, she has very many husbands, because she enters into marriage with the priests of my Son, who daily carry out his office; nevertheless, she remains a virgin in her integrity, because in her faith is incorrupt. Therefore Paul, my vessel, did not say that this wife should belong to one husband, because she is joined to those priests who arise in this same my Only-Begotten until the last day, until those marriages also come which will never fail through any instability of mortality. [Col. 0542A] And those also who minister most closely under priests in the service of my altar are husbands of the same wife, as that same Paul, presenting to people through me faithful teaching, said: “Let deacons be husbands of one wife, ruling well their children and their households” (ibid.).

What does this mean? Those who assist priests in the service of their aid should be husbands in a faithful union with one wife. And what is that wife? Namely, the most chaste bride, who can be injured by no corruption, just as a woman is corrupted when she loses the flower and innocence of virginity which she possesses at the beginning of her betrothal, while she remains still uncorrupted with her bridegroom. Hence these espousers should conduct themselves with this wife of justice so faithfully that [Col. 0542B] they may provide good examples of virtues to those regenerated by their help in spirit and water, and may labor with faithful care in their office, which belongs to the protection of the Church’s dwelling, just as a worldly person directs all the devotion of his management to his children and household.

For Paul, my friend, showed this bride to priests and the other ministers of my altar, so that they might choose her as wife for themselves and not seek a carnal spouse. For neither Paul himself nor the other disciples, sons of my Son, nor the remaining Fathers—that is, their followers—gave them this example in their own persons, to take a carnal spouse and abandon her whom they had previously chosen as their spiritual wife. For a priest so obstinate in sin as to take a woman unlawfully according to the desire of his flesh commits adultery, because he abandons his rightful wife—that is, the Church, to whom he had been betrothed in spiritual office—and shamefully takes another according to the pleasure of his mind. But although it may be difficult for him to restrain himself in this burning, nevertheless, for the sake of heavenly love let him hold himself back from these desires, as my Son also exhorts in the Gospel, saying: “There are eunuchs who were born thus from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made by people, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who can receive this receive it” (Matt. XIX).

What does this mean? There are some people who came forth from [Col. 0542D] their mother’s womb such that, because of the coldness or weakness of their body, they cannot have spouses. Hence on account of this continence they will receive no benefit of reward, except only that they will not suffer penalties for the deed of that sin, because they will suffer no penalties for a sin they did not commit. There are other people who have been weakened in their bodies through the will of certain persons so that they cannot exercise the pleasure of their flesh in this marital act. Yet these also, though continent in this way, do not deserve the glory of praise for it, because, although they cannot perform this work of burning desire, they nevertheless often feel within their will the heat of shamefulness. There are still others, namely those undertaking the spiritual life, who deny themselves [Col. 0543A] what they could easily perform with their bodies, because for the glory of the heavenly inheritance they scorn carnal coupling and do not wish to possess it. Therefore they will receive from it the greatest praise together with the reward of blessed recompense. Hence my priests, and all who belong to the office of my altar, ought with their whole will to imitate them, so that they may receive the crown of continence with the greatest rejoicing of heavenly joy. Therefore, whoever can receive this example in the intention of his heart, so that by full desire for blessedness he can overcome his body and reject carnal desires, let him receive heavenly fellowship with most ardent devotion, faithfully relinquishing carnal coupling in the restraint of his flesh.

But whoever cannot contain himself, because he burns in the desire of his flesh, should become neither priest nor another minister of priestly rank, whether for the sake of a proud position or an appetite for riches, lest, if he later falls into the pleasure of his flesh, he suffer great harm to himself. For those accustomed to approach the ministry of my altar shall keep their bodies from contact with women; they shall not join themselves in marriages for any occasion, but shall keep themselves chaste both by their own will and by the uprightness of my service; otherwise they ought to avoid holy service at my altar. Yet although this service is found sometimes to have been permitted to certain people who had formerly [Col. 0543C] been subject to the world, this is seen to have occurred in those who placed themselves under the carnal yoke before, not after, undertaking my service. Yet after that yoke was subsequently cut off from them, the Holy Spirit then worked in them proclamations of praise through his wonders. This was permitted as a marvel at the beginning of the rising Church because of the scarcity of priests. But now that she is mature and well strengthened, and her ministers have multiplied, it must be guarded against, in accordance with what ecclesiastical discipline indicates concerning the same matter.

This accords with the example that, at the beginning of the world’s birth, males were permitted, because of the scarcity of people, to take women of near kinship for themselves; but, once they had multiplied, this was to be forbidden even to them. For unshaped and unpolished stones are accustomed to be laid in the foundation of a building, although afterward beautiful and well-fitted stones are required in the wall of its sides. So too, in the infancy of the Church, priests were placed in that office according to what persons could then be found; but now among the spiritual people there is found a full number of those fit for priestly office, so that they are not occupied with the worldly burden of earthly coupling. For it is not fitting that the master of a household, who undertakes the obligation of worldly marriage, should be called my messenger in priesthood.

Hence hear this comparison. A certain king, strong in much power, had gathered a small army. When he had inspected it carefully and saw that it was untrained [Col. 0544A] for the exercise of labor, he selected from it one person, with several others of the common people whom he judged suitable for administration, and set them over that army, because the eminent stock of this nobility was not yet mature. But when afterward that army had begun to increase, and when noble persons in it had already reached maturity, that king arranged every right in that army well and in order, and appointed over it commanders and governors from among those nobler persons, according to the respective demands of justice.

What does this mean? The heavenly King, whose power is above all, had assembled a small host of believers in the planting of the Church. Searching it by most penetrating inquiry, he saw that it was still infirm and weak for bearing bodily sufferings for his name; and therefore, cleansing from the filth of temporal things Peter—who was one of them and had previously lived in earthly affairs—and, after him, certain others who had also at one time tasted the sap of earth, because he foreknew them to be discerning and faithful, fit both for the care of souls and the sustenance of bodies in his planting, he set them, as embracers of the catholic faith, over the office of binding and loosing. For the glowing dawn, burning up human contaminations in the heat of chastity, had not yet widely spread the flowers of its sweetness among human beings. But when the multitude of the Church’s offspring had already been broadly sown throughout the regions of the whole world, and the glory of ecclesiastical honor had been nobly strengthened, that same heavenly King inspired human beings with both worldly and spiritual gifts in a most gracious and fitting ordering, and established priests and the other ministers of divine offices who, most honorably preserving their sobriety and chastity in accordance with God’s justice, observed ecclesiastical law.

Therefore, O human being, because many have now arisen among spiritual people who labor to fight against the world and against the devil, and who hasten to approach my altar in chastity and restraint of their bodies, I will that my priests appear before me free from the contamination of earthly coupling. For although priests in the Old Testament were commanded to abstain from contact with women when they approached my altar, this has been brought to full perfection for my priests in the New Testament: what those ancient priests observed in chastity, as it were, for one hour, these new priests fulfill from the beginning of their youth to the end of their old age. And since I did not wish to receive from the former a sacrifice polluted by union with a woman, much more do I will that my Son be handled by the new priests in the office of chastity.

Let no one immature and unconsecrated take charge of a church; nor let anyone presume to seek several churches. For if someone presumes, in the age of childhood or without consecration to priestly office, to take charge of a church, or, having one, attempts also to subject several to himself, he thereby becomes a transgressor of justice and will be examined under the judgment of most severe discipline, [Col. 0545A] like one who does not fear to fornicate before lawful age or without lawful betrothal, or who, having a lawful wife, hastens to defile himself with others in adultery. Moreover, from all the people who are in the Christian name, priests of wise intelligence and manly spirit are to be chosen; yet they must come to my service in proper order, with just anointing and a willing mind. Yet those ought not to approach the office of my altar who are impaired by weakness in any of their members, because in the kingdom of heaven no blemish of diverse wounds will appear in human souls. Therefore I do not will that those deprived of any of their members serve at my altar. Yet although they are weak in their bodies, [Col. 0545B] they will not on account of this deprivation of their limbs be separated from the kingdom of heaven, provided that they possess health of soul and seek me in purity of good works. Nevertheless, I do not will that they perform the ministry of my altar; rather, let them humbly perform the efficacy of good works.

Likewise, women should not approach the same office of my altar, because they are a weak and frail dwelling, appointed to bear children and, when they have borne them, to nourish them diligently. But a woman conceives a child not through herself but from a man, just as the earth is ploughed not through itself but through a farmer. Therefore, as the earth cannot plough itself, so a woman is not to be compared with a priest in the office of consecrating [Col. 0545C] the body and blood of my Son, although she may sound forth in praise of her Creator, just as the earth receives rain for the watering of its fruits. And as the earth produces every fruit, so in woman every fruit of good work is accomplished. How? Because she can receive the high priest as bridegroom. How? A virgin betrothed to my Son receives him as bridegroom, because she has closed her body to a carnal husband; and therefore in my bridegroom she has priesthood and every ministry of my altar, and possesses with him all his riches. Likewise, a widow may be called the bride of that same my Son, when, rejecting a carnal husband, she flees beneath the wings of his protection. And as a bridegroom greatly loves his bride, so my Son most sweetly embraces [Col. 0545D] his brides who run diligently to him in the love of chastity.

Nor should a man in any way be clothed in women’s dress, nor should a woman use a man’s garment, so that the two persons may thus be distinguished: namely, that the man may show manly strength in himself and the woman may show womanly weakness in herself. For this has been so in my ordering from the beginning of the human race, unless either a man is in danger of death or a woman in danger of chastity. Then, if on that occasion a man according to a woman, or a woman according to a man, humbly changes clothing in fear of death, they will find my mercy concerning their act if they seek it, because they did it not rashly but in danger to their safety. And because a woman ought not to be clothed in male attire, neither will she approach the office of my altar, because she does not display a male person either in her hair or in her clothing.

Those who approach my altar, then, should appear chaste before me. And not only they, but also all others who desire to receive the sacrament of the body and blood of my Son, lest they cast themselves headlong into a ruinous fall. But many are found, both among spiritual persons and among seculars, who defile themselves not only by fornication with women but also, contaminating themselves in contrary fornication, impose upon themselves the gravest burden of strict judgment. How? A man who sins with another man in the manner of a woman sins bitterly [Col. 0546B] against God and against that union by which God joined male and female. Hence both appear before God polluted, black, and lustful; horrible and offensive to God and people, and guilty of death, because against their Creator they destroy the creature that is within them. How? God joined man and woman—that is, he coupled together what is strong and what is weak, so that each might be sustained by the other. But these contrary adulterers, when they transfer their male strength into the softness of contrariety, rejecting the right institution of male and female, follow Satan most shamefully in his perversity, he who wished in his pride to tear apart and divide him who is undivided. For they establish in themselves an alien and contrary adultery by their perverse practices, and therefore appear before me polluted and dishonorable.

But whoever sins in this contrary fornication with a woman is a most ravenous wolf in this perversity. How? For just as that person would be contrary and offensive to people who, possessing the most beautiful and cleanest foods, cast them away and ate the excrement which comes out in human evacuation, so these too are unworthy and unclean before me, because they abandon in a woman the right institution of union and seek in her an alien transgression. Likewise, a woman who adopts these devilish practices, pretending to unite herself to another woman in a male office, appears most vile before me, together with the woman who submits herself to her in such a dishonorable deed. For when they ought to have modesty concerning their passion, they have shamelessly usurped an alien right. And because they have transformed themselves into an alien manner, they are altered and contemptible to me.

Those males also who bring forth their seed by touching their foreskin bring upon themselves a great fall of soul, because in this unrest they are altogether shaken; and therefore they appear before me like unclean animals that devour their young. For perversely shaking out their seed, they lead it into dishonorable pollution. Women who imitate them by immodest touch, when in the stimulus [Col. 0547A] of burning lust they weary themselves in the constraint of their bodies, are likewise very culpable for it, because when they ought to restrain themselves in chastity, they defile themselves in impurity. Therefore both women and men who shake their seed out from themselves by their own bodily touch infect themselves in their souls with sores and wounds in this filth, because for love of me they refuse to restrain themselves in the office of chastity.

What does this mean? When a person feels the goad of his flesh pricking him, let him run into the cave of continence, take hold of the shield of chastity, and thus defend himself from impurity. How? Let him cast tares out from the wheat: that is, let him separate the tumult of lust from the sweetness of chastity. Hence whoever thus casts the taste of lust away from himself is very sweet and beloved to me. But you, O people, cast away chastity and love lust, since you are not only fornicators with human beings but also fornicators with beasts: you cast your seed not into that which lives but into that which is dead; you abandon your partner and desire that which has been subjected to you in servitude. Therefore the elements cry out over you, saying: “Alas, alas! Our rulers mingle themselves with us in the mingling of their seed.” And thus, in your deeds, they show that they experience sorrow because of my indignation. Why, then, do you turn your rational understanding into brutish folly, when you know that you are human beings? Did I create you for union with beasts? By no means. And because you join yourselves [Col. 0547C] to them, most bitter fellowship in unspeakable crimes will fall upon you, because you despise my institution in the union of male and female. For whoever so transforms himself in his deeds that he does what he desires to do—namely, so abandons himself as to spill his seed with a beast—brings upon himself the greatest ruin, just as Satan cast himself down through his own opposition when he wished to make himself like God. Therefore, all of you who defile yourselves by perverse practice in various pollutions of this sort, resist your desires; chastising your bodies, perform most bitter and true penitence with great weeping and fasting, mortification [Col. 0547D] of your flesh, and severe scourges, lest, remaining unrepentant, you cast yourselves into the accumulation of a most cruel guilt.

I desire not only that people cleanse themselves from waking impurity, but also that they duly purify themselves from that pollution which may occur to them while asleep. For if, while a man is sleeping, an emission of seed should arise in his dreams, I do not wish him, while that burning heat still rages, to approach the sacrament of the service of my altar, until that heat has subsided in him; as it is written: “If there be among you a man who is defiled by a nocturnal emission, he shall go outside the camp; and he shall not return until he has washed with water toward evening, and after sunset he shall return to the camp” (Deut. XXIII).

What does this mean? If there is among you who labor in my service [Col. 0548A] a man who is defiled by night in the sleep of his slumber, let him separate himself from the congregation of holiness belonging to my altar, so that he does not presume to join himself to that mystery before, when the harmful heat has departed, he has been cleansed by the washing of repentance, in confession and compunction of heart, from the burning of his lust. Then, when that repentance which has thus illumined his heart has been completed, let him return, in the love of chastity, to those who faithfully guard themselves from the impurity of defilement, and let him approach that sacrament, which is wholly in holiness, worthily and honorably.

But the man who burns intensely with lust both while sleeping and while awake must beware lest he furnish fuel to his own burning. How? Namely, he [Col. 0548B] should not inflame himself with foods that offer him the sap of lust; rather, let him humbly abstain from those meats which came forth naked from their mothers, that is, from beasts, without a covering. For in them is a fervor of heat which is not so great in the flesh of birds, which does not come forth without a covering, but is born from an egg when its shell-covering is broken. Therefore there is less burning in it. Let him also abstain from immoderate wine, lest, through excessive drinking, his veins, filled with harmful blood, become shamefully heated in the ardor of burning.

But if anyone suffers from an excess of these causes and cannot resist himself by his own powers, let him seek me with most devout intention and show me the wounds of his heart by a most humble disclosure. How? Namely, let him disclose them to me by humble confession before a priest. And [Col. 0548C] why is this so? Because true confession is a second resurrection. How? In the fall of the old Adam the human race was killed; the new Adam raised it up in his death. Therefore, in the death of that same new Adam arose the resurrection of souls, so that a man ought to confess his sins—which the old Adam did not do, since he covered over his transgression rather than confessing it. How? He did not confess it in repentance, but covered it by accusing the woman. Therefore confession was established so that, after people have fallen, they may be raised from their fall through it.

And thus whoever has confessed his sins to a priest in pure confession and in love of me rises from death to life, just as she too was rescued from [Col. 0548D] death who, at the banquet before my Son, cleansed herself from her filth by tearful repentance. This remedy of cleansing was also long prefigured in the ancient fathers. How? Before the law of grace, the patriarchs and prophets were the consolation of humankind; under the law, the high priests and priests were their instruction; afterward the apostles came and brought true righteousness in my Son, so that many people, running to them, devoutly implored their help. And so, from Adam to the apostolic mission of the apostles, there were always those who, through heavenly inspiration, aided human miseries by their consolation and instruction.

Moreover, as the apostles showed people by their preaching and by many miracles, a human being [Col. 0549A] who, falling into death through diabolical persuasion, could never raise himself by his own power, was rescued from death through my Son. How? Because, while he was in the world, he endured many labors in his body and finally was placed upon the cross for the redemption of the world. Faithful people ought to imitate this for their salvation together with their priests. How? Let them seek the help of my Son; for when, after baptism, they have renewed the old crime of Adam, they cannot rise from their fall by themselves. Therefore let them seek counsel as from patriarchs and prophets, and receive help from apostles, where they will faithfully display their sins, their wounds laid bare, in true and pure disclosure. How? With most devout heart and mouth they will confess their sins to the priest, who is the minister of my Son. [Col. 0549B] Then that priest, bestowing upon them a remedy in their repentance, will bury their sins in the death of my Only-Begotten. And they, afterward rising to life in this manner, will also glorify the resurrection of my Son.

But whoever refuses to lay bare the wounds of his sins, and silently attempts to heal them by himself without the aid of another, following what he finds his own heart then desires, deceives himself, because he wishes to be his own priest. Therefore he cannot rise without another’s help, since neither was humanity raised to salvation by itself, but was saved through my Son. Hence whoever desires salvation must not despair of confessing his sins even at the end of his life.

But if anyone, placed in the hour of death, seeks remedies [Col. 0549C] for the wounds of his sins and nevertheless cannot have a priest to whom he may confess his sins, let him disclose them to another person whom he has available at that time. Or, if so suddenly he can have no person at all, let him reveal them to me, before the elements with which he also committed them, from the inmost affection of his heart; and I, seeing the devotion of his heart, do not reject his repentance. Therefore let no one despair because of the burdens of his iniquity, for if he despaired of my mercy, he would not rise to life. But whoever has struggled with despair and at last reduced it to nothing has freed himself, because, being strong, he has conquered manfully.
