But one who, through the swelling pride [Col. 0549D] of his mind, does not seek the remedy of his salvation is not to be helped, because, when he could have found me, he refused to seek me. Therefore, while a person has time, let him not neglect himself, but seek the refuge of pure confession, as my Son also commanded in the Gospel, saying: “Go and show yourself to the priest, and offer your gift which Moses commanded, as a testimony to them” (Matt. VIII).

What does this mean? You who are filthy in sins, when you desire to be cleansed from them, go with good intention and show them in pure confession to the priest who is my minister; and offer with devout heart the gift of true repentance, which he prefigured by God’s will who was cleansed by divine power from the many floods of earthly iniquity, so that those who had formerly seen you [Col. 0550A] filthy in evil deeds may testify that you are now cleansed from them in the bitterness of repentance, as though in the furnace of testing.

Therefore, O human being, if a sinner concealed his deeds in the secrecy of his heart, who then would be a witness of that repentance against the accuser? No one. Therefore let a person disclose his sins, so that he may have a witness to his repentance. But whoever desires to complete repentance for his sins should take almsgiving as his aid. How? When the human body fails through its weakness in the labor of repentance, let almsgiving run to its assistance. And because it is difficult for a person to repent harshly and as justice requires, let him take almsgiving as a mother to himself, so that with her he may accomplish what is laborious to his body.

[Col. 0550B] For just as a mother does not cease to assist her child’s need, even though he may seem already grown up, so almsgiving assists the frailty of the body in a person’s repentance, although that same person may appear strong in the mortification of his body through repentance. Yet let a person physically punish in himself those evil works which he committed in his body through the desire of his flesh, so that the deed which had been dear and sweet to his flesh may faithfully be wiped away from him through the bitterness of repentance. For the bitterness of repentance, with the help of almsgiving, ought to heal in people the deadly wounds of sins.

How? Because when a person constrains himself by chastisement, he should also enlarge himself through almsgiving. How? Because almsgiving [Col. 0550C] signifies my mercy. How? When a faithful person assists the poor from his substance for love of me, he keeps my commandments, because he bestows his mercy upon the needy for the honor of my name, just as I do not withhold my grace from those who seek me in purity of heart.

But whoever in this way aids the poor with the relief of alms, moved by compassion, is very dear to me, because he has bowels of mercy, fulfilling what is written: “Place your treasure in the commandments of the Most High, and almsgiving will profit you more than gold” (Ecclus. XXIX). What does this mean? With just and right consideration, take from the material of your money, which is in your bosom and in the embrace [Col. 0550D] of your heart, and divide it according to the commandments of him who is above all, because God commanded that you turn away from evil and do good. Therefore you ought thus to abound in your inmost heart through your good will, lest you be among the lost sheep; rather, sanctify yourself before God by giving from your substance to refresh those who are failing, for then too God will not hold back his mercy from you in your miseries.

If you do this, then that compassion which you have toward one who possesses no treasure brings you greater profit than if, climbing a great mountain, you possessed much gold money in your pride. How? It is better for you to give a little to the little ones in humility than to possess the kingdom of the world with great [Col. 0551A] pleasure; for then mercy would fail you in God’s recompense because of the weight of your pride, since there you would have no bowels of compassion for the poor. Hence the elements are the reservoirs of human pleasures, and they reveal human habits. How? Because they bring God’s vengeance upon those who sin.

Therefore, O human being, abandon the vanity of shipwrecked avarice, for your most just inheritance is in eternal life. Leave evil and do good, so that you may abandon the ill will of hardness. And, that you may obtain mercy, give from your substance to the needy, in this imitating God, who is merciful.

Therefore also, O human being, no liar can deny that you who thus [Col. 0551B] assist the poor fulfill my will in this. How? As I bestow my grace upon you, so you too ought to give your alms to the poor. But those who receive alms must not take them in vain or according to avarice. What does this mean? Many people love idleness and do not wish to labor bodily so that they may feed themselves; nor do they strive to do good works spiritually so that they may help their souls. Rather, they are like beasts, having no understanding of righteousness either in soul or body. Therefore they appear unworthy before my eyes if they persist in the lukewarmness of this depravity without correction and without repentance.

But there are also many who, suffering bodily need, receive alms humbly in fear [Col. 0551C] and pray and labor for those who bestow mercy upon them, while avoiding the wicked works of most unclean filth. Among these are also many from whom I withhold earthly riches because I wish to give them heavenly riches. Those who willingly endure poverty for my name’s sake are very dear to me; but those who would gladly have worldly riches for their own covetousness, yet cannot have them, lose the reward of this labor. But whoever seeks riches in order to fulfill my will, and not his own covetousness, will receive from me the reward of honor for his good will.

Likewise, one who seeks the power of honor for the display of his own pride [Col. 0551D] and not for the glory of my name is to me like a rotting corpse. But one who seeks it so that he may uphold not his own pride but my honor will appear glorious in my kingdom for that very reason. Therefore priests who hold the office of spiritual governance ought to undertake their teaching not for themselves but for me, so that they may preside over my people more securely and devoutly. How? They ought to teach, admonish, exhort, and restrain my people, so that they may keep the law of God worthily and praiseworthily.

And this the shepherds must always ponder: when by exhortation they move the people, they must urge them not to persist in their sins without confession and repentance, but to trample evil works underfoot and perform good ones. If the people do not obey [Col. 0552A] their priests in this admonition, then the people will bear their guilt and the priests will have delivered themselves from the fall caused by this negligence. But if priests do not show the people the authority of their teaching, then they are not called priests but are termed ravening wolves, because they carry out their office in plunder. Just as a wolf cruelly tears apart a sheep, so they follow their own will more than they love the guarding of their sheep.

And because they live perversely, they fear to sow true doctrine among the people, consenting to iniquity as though to a certain lord of their own—which is carnal desire—and shutting the door of their heart against equity as though against a member of their own household—which is God’s justice. Therefore, O shepherds, howl and lament [Col. 0552B] your crimes, which send forth a dreadful cry in your iniquity, so that even the elements take up their outcry and roar with them before me.

For how dare you, in your office, touch your Lord with bloodstained hands, in contrary filth and adulterous iniquity? Truly, in your uncleanness you shake the foundation of the earth. How? Namely, when, filthy with such great crimes, you do not fear to touch your God, I oppress the earth with great grief, avenging the flesh and blood of my Son. For not only do you cruelly shake the earth in this horror, but you also foul heaven most grievously by your uncleanness. How? When, in the stench of your uncleanness, you touch the Lord your God, just as a pig [Col. 0552C] defiles pearls in dung, then the heavens, receiving your iniquity, send upon the earth the vengeance of my judgment according to my will.

For when, with true justice and divine law, you ought to go before my people, shining in good works, so that my people, walking after you, might not strike their foot in any offense, you sometimes defile my people with greater iniquity than they themselves would defile themselves; in you they have an evil and most evil example. You ought to be so radiant a gem that believers, walking in your light, could recognize the way of uprightness. But you offer them an example of death, so that in your iniquity they cannot [Col. 0552D] find a limit. And how can you be their shepherds when you so lead them astray? How then will you answer for them, when you cannot give an answer even for yourselves? Therefore weep and howl before the time of death removes you.

And why do you not consider your honor, which has been given you above other people? What does this mean? In my Son you received above others the keys of heaven, which consist in the judgment of right discernment and just judgment in knowledge of the Scriptures, when you rightly consider what it is that you ought to bind. What does this mean? When people stubbornly oppose me in my law, you ought to instill in them fear of my judgment. And if they then do not correct their fault, extend your binding over them. How? Because they are rebellious, [Col. 0553A] you will bind them openly in my words and declare that binding to them, since by their obstinacy they are bound before me also, as my Son showed the first shepherd of the Church, saying: “I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. And whatever you bind upon earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose upon earth shall be loosed in heaven” (Matt. XVI).

What does this mean? I, who have power over heaven and earth, will give to you, who have devoutly imitated me through my grace, those judgments which concern the dignity of the heavenly kingdom. Thus what you bind upon earth by just judgment, according to the sins which you see people commit on earth, is not to be violated. For after I have drawn a human soul from its body, you will not extend your judgment over it, because [Col. 0553B] that judgment is mine: let it be bound in its wickedness and, in the heavenly places—that is, separated and cast out from heaven—since in the dwelling above no iniquity is permitted to have freedom or place.

But this bond, which you first imposed in rebellion, when afterward you recognize repentance in the offenders, shall be loosed upon earth and in the heavenly mysteries. Then, after a person’s death, you will pray for his soul; and you will then be able to absolve it from the knots of its binding, because God does not reject the groaning of a devout heart.

But you, O priests, who have received this power through my Son: bind no one in my words without a culpable cause, because of the rage of [Col. 0553C] your hearts; rather, you must consider most keenly whom you ought thus to bind. For one whom neither shame before people, nor fear of me, nor your prayers nor commandments can restrain from willing to persist in his iniquity, you shall remove from my Church by ecclesiastical censure in my words. But do not bind the innocent; for if you bind him, you cast yourselves into the knot of dreadful guilt.

Yet if someone has been bound improperly in this way, though innocent, he nevertheless ought to seek release with the humblest obedience of submission for the honor of my name, lest, if he proves contemptuous, he incur the guilt of pride. But let this binding be such: a person who refuses to obey either me or the commands of his superiors in his perversities is to be separated in my word from heavenly things, just as Adam, disobedient to me in my command, was cast out of paradise; nor is he to be received into the fellowship of the faithful except in the repentance of obedience, just as the human race was called back to the heavenly homeland in the martyrdom of my obedient Son.

But one who is so rebellious that he refuses to return in the office of humility, if he persists thus in his obstinacy, will have fellowship with those who, refusing to cast off their stony heart and remaining in their unbelief, refused to have the glory of ecclesiastical blessedness. For one who is [Col. 0554A] so hardened that he takes no care to seek mercy for his wickedness imitates the ancient serpent, who despised mercy and, having deceived the first human being in paradise, thus spoke within himself:

“Although I have been cast from heaven when I could not prevail in resisting the army of the Most High, with my angels, in battle—because I was defeated by him—yet now I have found the human being upon earth, and by exercising my wrath upon him I shall take strong vengeance for myself. For in the human being upon earth I shall accomplish what I wished to do in heaven: namely, that I might be like the Most High. And if God is just, this power will not be taken from me, because the human being will consent to me and will not obey God.”

As the devil spoke these things within himself, he marshaled all his arts against the human being so that the latter [Col. 0554B] might withdraw from God; and the human being followed the devil. Thus the devil bound him so strongly to himself that the human being worshiped him as God and denied God his Creator.

But when the human being lay in such great darkness of unbelief and could not raise himself, for his salvation I sent my Son, in a wondrous manner incarnate of a virgin, being true God and true man. What does this mean? He truly came forth from me, the Father, according to divinity; and he truly took flesh from the Virgin Mother according to humanity.

What does this mean? O human being, you are soft and tender in your body, but you remain hard and inflexible in your unbelief. A stone can be polished for a building [Col. 0554C], but you refuse to be softened unto faith. Yet attend: as a person who possesses a most beautiful gem in his treasure-chest sets it in metal so that it may appear to people, so I, having my Son in my heart, willed that he be incarnate from a Virgin, so that he might bestow the salvation of life upon believers.

If I had given him a carnal father, who then would he have been? Plainly, not my Son but my servant; but this ought not to have been. Born from a Virgin, he ate, drank, and rested in sleep, and endured other bodily miseries; nevertheless, he did not experience the taste of sin in his flesh, because he took flesh not in falsehood but in truth.

What does this mean? Other human beings are born in the transgression of Adam and Eve through the taste of pleasure, which is in falsehood [Col. 0554D] and not in truth. My Son was not born so; rather, in holiness he was born of the most chaste Virgin for the redemption of human beings. For one like another could not free his like from its bond, unless one greater came who could rescue him. What does this mean? A person born in sins could not free a sinful person from the perdition of death. Therefore my Son came without sin, because, having overcome death, he mercifully rescued humanity from death. But whoever sees with watchful eyes and hears with attentive ears, let him offer the kiss of an embrace to my mystical words, which flow forth from me, the living one.

## SEVENTH VISION

[Col. 0555]

### SUMMARY

That God, dispensing all things justly and manifesting in justice the diverse gifts of the Holy Spirit, strengthens faithful people in good works so that they cannot be overcome by the devil. Concerning the multitude of the faithful and the divine law spread out before them. That the devil’s deceptions lie open to people on the path of this world. That the devil openly and fraudulently offers people riches and pleasures, which those who desire them purchase. That some vigorously resist and reject diabolical persuasion, while others, living lukewarmly, consent to it. The words of Ezekiel on the same matter. That the devil, filled with every wickedness and with the venom of his manifold art, labors to deceive the five senses of human beings. That the devil’s pride was cast down in the incarnation of the Son of God. What his eyes, ears, and nostrils signify. What his hands, feet, and tail signify. That the power of almighty God has so crushed the devil’s strength that he cannot exercise his wickedness according to his will. That in the four quarters of the world the devil sends forth the fire of wicked persuasion against every class of different human beings. David’s words on the same matter. How the devil, through fiery persuasions, attacks different kinds of spiritual and secular persons with manifold temptations. Concerning their three battle-lines. Concerning the temptation of secular persons. Concerning six modes of temptation among spiritual persons. Concerning the unbaptized. What the arrows of his mouth, the smoke of his breast, and the moisture of his loins signify. What the whirlwind of his navel and the filth of frogs from his belly signify. That the devil agitates foolish people through wicked unbelief, making them think true what he fraudulently shows them. That heretics who worship the devil as God are to be avoided and cast out from the Church; they are the devil’s entrails and the precursor seed of the son of perdition. That those who despise God’s hearing are deserted by God’s grace, but those who seek are mercifully aided. Solomon’s words on the same matter. That true worshipers of God, who with all effort trample earthly things underfoot, cast down the ancient serpent by mighty crushing.

[Col. 0555A] Then I saw a burning light as great as some great and lofty mountain, divided at its summit as though into many tongues. Before that light stood a certain multitude of people clothed in white, and before them there appeared something like a veil, transparent as crystal, stretched from their breasts down to their feet.

And before that multitude, as though upon a certain road, there lay on its back a worm of wonderful size and length, which seemed of such horror and fury as no human being could express. At its left side was something like a marketplace, where the riches of people, worldly delights, and markets of diverse things appeared. There also certain people, running with great speed, engaged in no [Col. 0555B] trade; while others, moving slowly, were occupied there in selling and buying.

That worm was black, hairy, ulcerous, and full of pustules. It bore five varieties descending like belts from its head through its belly to its feet: one appeared green, another white, another red, one saffron-colored, and one black, all full of deadly venom. But its head was so crushed that even its left jaw already seemed to be dissolving. Its eyes were bloody outwardly and fiery inwardly; its ears were round and bristly; its nostrils and mouth were like the nostrils and mouth of a viper; its hands were like human hands, its feet like a viper’s feet, and its tail appeared short and horrible.

A chain had been placed around its neck [Col. 0555C] which bound both its hands and feet, and this chain, fastened with great strength to the stone of the abyss, so firmly constrained it that it could move itself neither here nor there according to the wickedness of its will.

From its mouth many flames came forth and divided into four directions. One part rose to the clouds, another extended among secular people, another among spiritual people, and another descended to the abyss. [Col. 0556A] The flame that sought the clouds fought against those people who wished to ascend to heaven. Three battle-lines of these appeared: one line advanced near the clouds, one in the region between clouds and earth, and one near the earth. All cried out repeatedly, “Let us go on to heaven!” But, cast about here and there by that flame, some did not fall, others scarcely supported themselves upon their feet, while others fell to the earth but rose again and strove toward heaven.

The flame which spread among secular people burned some of them and turned them into most hideous blackness; it pierced others so sharply that it bent them wherever it wished. Yet some, rescuing themselves from it and going toward those seeking heaven, cried out anew: “O faithful ones, grant us help!” Others, however, remained thus pierced.

The flame which spread among spiritual persons covered them with its darkness. I considered them also in six modes: some that same flame injured by cruel burning; those whom it could not injure it fiercely blew upon with the green, white, red, saffron-colored, or black deadly venom that flowed from the worm’s head down to its feet.

But the flame which sought the abyss contained within itself the various punishments of those who, not washed in the fountain of baptism and ignorant of the light of truth and faith, had worshiped Satan as God. I also saw very sharp, whistling arrows issuing from its mouth; black [Col. 0556C] smoke breathing out from its breast; burning moisture boiling from its loins; a hot whirlwind blowing from its navel; and, from the end of its belly, something like the filth of frogs bubbling forth. All these brought great unrest to people.

And a most foul mist issuing from it with a most evil stench infected many people with its perversity. But behold, a great multitude of people shining in great brightness came; everywhere they strongly trampled upon that worm and cruelly tormented it, though they themselves could be injured neither by its flames nor by its venom.

[Col. 0557A] And again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

God, who justly and rightly disposes all things, calls faithful peoples to the glory of the heavenly inheritance. But the ancient deceiver, lying in ambush and attempting to hinder them, stirs up against them the arts of his wickedness. Yet, conquered by them, he receives the confusion of his presumption, when they possess the heavenly homeland and he undergoes infernal horrors.

Therefore you see a burning light as great as a great and lofty mountain, divided at its summit as though into many tongues. This is the justice of God, burning in the faith of believers, displaying in the strength of its power the greatness of sanctities and the height of glory, and wonderfully revealing in that same glory the diverse gifts of the Holy Spirit.

And the multitude [Col. 0557B] of people clothed in white standing before that light is the throng of people shining in faith, well and honorably ordered through their good works, in the presence of God’s justice. Before them there appears a veil transparent as crystal, stretched from their breasts down to their feet, because before their eyes they always have the divine law, strong and radiant, from the intention of good actions to their completion. In these they are so strengthened that they cannot be overcome by the cunning and deception of fraudulent persuasions.

But the fact that before that multitude, as though on a road, [Col. 0557C] a worm of wonderful size and length lies upon its back means that, openly known before human awareness upon the way of this world—which is set before both good and evil persons for walking—the ancient serpent appears cast down, not in his own form but in the signification of a mystery: great in malice and long in snares. He gapes upward to cast down through his deception those who strive toward heavenly things; yet he lies fallen because his powers have been crushed through the Son of God, so that he cannot stand in them. Although he seems of such horror and fury as no human being can express, mortal human estimation cannot set forth the venomous rage and malicious efforts in the manifold diversity of his nature.

[Col. 0557D] Therefore, at his left is something like a marketplace, where human riches, worldly pleasures, and markets of diverse things appear. For in death, understood as the left side of that traitor, a marketplace is seen: namely, his most wicked works of death. There, in corruptible riches, pride and vainglory, and, in transitory pleasures, wantonness and desire, seethe like the buying and selling in a market of many varieties of earthly covetousness.

Thus, one who openly recoils from diabolical terror may secretly be deceived by these things, when the many persuasions of vices are gently offered to him—as diverse wares are shown to people by a merchant, so that, delighted by them, they may purchase more eagerly what they see offered [Col. 0558A] to them. For the devil fraudulently offers his arts to people; but those who then desire them purchase them. How? They cast away their good conscience as though selling it, and incur upon themselves the deadly wounds of their souls as though buying them.

But there certain people run with great speed and conduct no trade, because, knowing God, they bear the treasure of good will and the spices of virtues and gain them for themselves most vigorously. Passing swiftly through worldly pleasures and diabolical filths in God’s commandments, they despise the sweetness of their flesh.

But others move slowly and attend there to selling and buying, because, having slowness in good works, through the lukewarmness of their body they extinguish within themselves heavenly desire as though [Col. 0558B] selling it, and nourish within themselves the pleasure of their flesh as though buying it. Therefore the former will receive the reward of good action, while the latter will endure the punishments of their iniquity, as Ezekiel shows when he says: “The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him” (Ezek. XVIII).

What does this mean? The radiant works of a pure person bathe that person in holiness, and, like a thousand eyes looking upward and into the depths, surround him everywhere, lifting him upward to great honor and to the mortification of his own pleasure, as the Holy Spirit inspires him, just as a wing raises a bird upward in the air wherever it pleases.

But the viperous venom of wickedness belongs to the most savage viper, which foams against heaven, wrapping a pearl [Col. 0558C] in mud and raging against the most beautiful of all fair things. The one who faithlessly follows it, however, it casts away from the most noble work of God’s finger, from every honor, and from the blessedness of the heavenly vision; making him an exile, it cuts him off from the living fruit and from the root of the righteous tree.

The fact that you see that worm black, bristling, ulcerous, and full of pustules signifies that the same ancient serpent abounds in the blackness of the darkness of unbelief, in the hairs of hidden deceptions, in the ulcers of polluting uncleannesses, and in the pustules of caverns of fury. It also has within itself five varieties descending from its head through its belly to its feet in the manner of belts [Col. 0558D], because it never ceases to breathe upon the five senses of human beings with diverse passions of vices—from that deception when it first strove to fill itself, up to that consummation when its madness will reach its end. Yet, while feigning a deceptive rectitude, it draws people down into the slopes of its unclean arts. Of these varieties, one appears green, another white, another red, one saffron-yellow, and one black—all full of deadly venom: for in the green they display worldly sadness; in the white, foolish irreverence; in the red, the glory of deceit; in the saffron-yellow, biting detraction; and in the black, shameful pretence, together with the fullness of other perversities that bring death to the souls of those who assent to them.

But the fact that its head is so [Col. 0559A] crushed that even its left jaw now seems to be coming apart signifies that its pride was so cast down in the incarnation of the Son of God that even the adversity of death is now unable to exercise the strength of its bitterness. Its eyes appear bloody outwardly and fiery inwardly, because the intention of its perversity, as it were outwardly, inflicts bloody wickedness upon human bodies and, as it were inwardly, drives a fiery dart into their souls. Its ears are round and bristling, because it surrounds a person, as it were in a circle, with the hairs of its arts, in order to cast that person down very swiftly if it discovers anything in him that belongs to itself. Its nostrils and mouth appear like the nostrils and mouth of a viper, because it displays indiscreet and foul habits to people [Col. 0559B], through which, piercing them in many vices, it cruelly kills them. But its hands look like human hands, because it practises the contrivances of its arts in human deeds. Its feet are like a viper’s feet, because it does not cease to inflict diabolical lacerations upon human paths through its snares. Its tail appears short and horrible: this is its power in the brief yet utterly evil time of the son of perdition, who in raging desires to seize more than he can accomplish.

And the fact that a chain has been placed around its neck, binding both its hands and feet, signifies that diabolical strength has been so broken and crushed by the power of almighty God that its most evil deeds and most wicked paths—by which it seduces people—have been pressed down in its crushing [Col. 0559C]. Thus that chain, most firmly fastened to the stone of the abyss, binds it so strongly that it cannot move itself either this way or that according to the wickedness of its will. For the power of God, abiding without failure in the most steadfast eternity, oppresses the devil with such strength for the salvation of souls that he will not be able, by either the external or internal instruments of his most wicked undertaking, to remove the salvation of redemption from faithful souls, so as to prevent them from reaching the place of joy which he himself stubbornly lost.

The fact that many flames burst from its mouth and divide themselves in four directions signifies that, from its most rapacious voracity, it emits the most evil and manifold [Col. 0559D] wrong of the cruelest fire of wicked persuasion, and scatters it in various ways among people in the four quarters of the whole world, so that they may follow it. One part of these rises as far as the clouds, because that diabolical breath draws back by its sharpness those who seek heaven with the whole desire of their minds. Another spreads itself among worldly people, because it deceives, by its variety, those engaged in earthly concerns. Another extends itself among spiritual persons, because it infects by its pretence those labouring in spiritual disciplines. Yet another descends to the abyss, because by its seduction it sends unbelievers who agree with it into infernal torments. For, following the path of falsehood and deceit, they did not hold to the way of rectitude nor offer to the true God the reverence owed to him, as David testifies [Col. 0560A] when he says: “Destruction and misery are in their ways; they have not known the way of peace; there is no fear of God before their eyes” (Ps. 13).

What does this mean? The innocence and most powerful works of God, which contend in the living and most pure spring, so crush those who drive God from their hearts by most wicked and damnable deeds, as a great rain submerges some object so that it no longer appears. Therefore they do not shine in the sight of God, for misery, together with most unhappy habit, is in their paths wherever it extends itself with the food of death. In what way? Namely, by tasting and eating that which is evil. Hence they do not know, in their deeds, the way that rises in the heat of the sun [Col. 0560B], because they taste God’s sweetness neither in honour nor in love, where they reject his fear as though it were fear of a stranger, since they desire neither to see nor to look upon him.

Therefore, as you see, that flame which seeks the clouds fights against those people who wish to go to heaven, because when that most wicked fire perceives the minds of faithful people tending upward, it rages most cruelly against them through its arts, lest they attain those heavenly things which they seek with many sighs. You see three ranks of them, because they do not cease to worship the true and ineffable Trinity, although they are greatly wearied in their struggles. One rank goes near the clouds, because these people, fighting most strongly against the devil, raise their minds from earthly actions so far upward to heavenly things [Col. 0560C], just as a cloud is accustomed to float above the earth. Another runs in the middle region between clouds and earth, because these, restraining themselves with a certain moderation, labour neither with their whole mind for heavenly things nor with their entire desire for earthly things; rather, setting themselves a measure in these matters, they seek inward things without rejecting outward ones. One rank proceeds close to the earth, because these people do not entirely abandon transient things, but adhere to them somewhat, so that, labouring greatly in them, they experience many wearisome passions in them; nevertheless, through heavenly help they prove victorious. Let us all, with repeated cries, proceed shouting toward heaven, because both these and those, amid many sighs of their desires, exhort themselves to tend toward those things that are [Col. 0560D] in the heavenly secrets, even though they are often wearied in this intention by the arts of the ancient serpent.

But they are hurled this way and that by that flame, because they are driven into diverse habits by the blast of diabolical temptation. Yet some do not fall, because, being most valiant fighters, they defend themselves courageously from these illusions. Others scarcely support themselves on their feet, because they set their paths upon the way of rectitude, but, exhausted by many labours, scarcely overcoming diabolical arts, they nevertheless persevere in God’s commandments. Others fall to the ground but rise again and tend toward heaven, because, having fallen into a diversity of vices, they are afterward raised through repentance and place their hope in God together with good works.

[Col. 0561A] The fact that the flame spreading among worldly people burns some of them and turns them into most foul blackness signifies that this same fire of most wicked deceit comes upon those engaged in earthly concerns. Subjecting some of them to its perversity, it infects them with the worst vices of dark iniquity, so that, despising the brightness of true faith and killing themselves with bitter death, they fall to the earth and carry out most abominable deeds in their actions. It pierces others with its sharpness so that it bends them wherever it wishes, because it so subdues them by its wickedness that it inclines them to every vice of its perversity, suggesting to them worldly sweetness in the embrace of burning lust. Thus they possess diverse manners [Col. 0561B] in its manifold rites—namely in speech, hair, clothing, gait, and other things of this kind. Hence they become crooked, neglecting God’s justice, transgressors of the law, and imposing upon themselves no circumcision of the mind. For they seek excess in lust and observe no time of the law established for them by God. Rather, as the sea is stirred into unrest by wind, so they too are moved into diverse vices by the breath of the ancient dragon.

Yet some rescue themselves from it, proceeding toward those who seek heaven. “O faithful ones, give us help,” they shout again, having taken up the cry: for, withdrawing themselves from shameful and harmful custom and imitating those who fix their minds upon heavenly things, they desire to devote their care and seek help from them with heart and voice. But some remain thus transfixed, because entangled in diverse vices they persevere in evils.

But the fact that the flame extending itself among spiritual people covers them in its darkness signifies that the same breath of diabolical persuasion sends its fires against those who ought with all effort to serve the spirit, and darkens them by the perversity of their vices, so that they strive more after flesh than after spirit. You also observe them in six modes, because the ancient enemy tries to pervert both their five outward senses and the inward devotion of their hearts, as a sixth mode. For the same flame harms some, because the devil, sending his arts into them, breathes upon them with carnal [Col. 0561D] desires and pleasures, so that it inflames them toward lust and the pollution of much uncleanness. But those whom it cannot harm, it ardently breathes upon with the green, white, red, saffron-yellow, or black deadly venom that descends from the head of that worm to its feet.

How? When they reject the pleasures of pollutions, it either pours into them worldly sadness like budding greenness, by which they are so oppressed that they have strength neither in spiritual nor worldly affairs; or it introduces into them the irreverence of vices like foolish whiteness, so that they conceal their shame neither before God nor before human beings; or it shows them remembrance of earthly glory like shining redness, whence they have bitterness and anxiety of heart [Col. 0562A]; or it brings upon them detraction of their neighbours like lukewarm saffron, so that they become whisperers and double-tongued; or it lays upon them a pretence of justice like horrible blackness, by which they are miserably darkened in their hearts. All these are deadly plagues, proceeding from the beginning of the deception of that same destroyer until the end when it will finally receive the end of its madness in the world; by these it brings the harmful burning of vices upon people.

But the fact that the flame seeking the abyss contains within itself diverse punishments for those who, unwashed through the font of baptism and ignorant of the light of truth and faith, worship Satan as God, signifies that that fire, cleaving to perdition, inflicts dreadful and bitter torments upon those [Col. 0562B] souls which, not cleansed in the font of salvation and not seeing the brightness of the heavenly inheritance and the faith of the Church’s institution, do not cease to venerate, instead of him who grants people life and salvation, him who lies in wait and strives to send human souls to death.

As you see sharp whistling arrows issuing from its mouth, these are the worst and most wicked piercings proceeding from diabolical fury, raging through many iniquities; and black smoke breathing out from its breast, this is the emission of most foul wrath and envy from its malicious schemes; and burning moisture boiling from its loins, this is the outpouring, from its uncleanness, of most ardent lust among prelates. And you see a hot whirlwind blowing from its navel: this is the stifling, from its voracity, of most burning fornication among subjects [Col. 0562C]. From the extremity of its belly there gushes, as it were, the uncleanness of frogs: this is the foul discharge, in the hardness of despair, from the perdition of its perverse swallowing, when that ancient plotter has brought those who follow it to every desire of its own. All these things create great turmoil among people, because perversities of this kind impose the greatest calamity of most miserable entanglement on those who fix their hope not upon heavenly things but upon earthly.

But the fact that a most foul mist, issuing from it with a most evil stench, infects many people with its perversity signifies that from the same devil proceeds the blackest error of a stinking conscience, which agitates foolish people through wicked credulity. How? From the beheading of John the Baptist, who showed the Son of God to be the remitter of the wounds of sins, a most evil error arose, in which the devil deceives many people through diverse images: they suppose true what he falsely shows them according to their own estimation. Hence many are deceived in this way, because their faith continually wavers in weakness.

But, O my children, if you wish to live justly and devoutly, flee this most wicked error, lest most bitter death seize you in unbelief. Flee also those who dwell in caves, being enclosed companies of the devil. Woe to them, woe to them who persist thus, because they are the devil’s entrails [Col. 0563A] and the forerunning offspring of the son of perdition. Therefore, O my beloved children, avoid them with every devotion and with all the strength of your soul and body, because the ancient serpent feeds and clothes them by its art: they worship it as God and trust in it through deceptive deceit. They are most wicked murderers of themselves, so that they kill those who attach themselves to them simply, before permitting them to turn away from their error. In themselves they are most shameful fornicators, killing their own seed in murder and offering it to the devil; and in their schisms and in the fullness of their vices they assail my Church, while wickedly mocking, in their shameful contrivances, baptism, the sacrament of the body and blood of my Son, and the other institutions which my Church possesses.

But although, through fear of my people, they do not openly oppose these my institutions, nevertheless in their hearts and deeds they regard them as nothing. For, through diabolical illusion, they pretend to possess holiness, in which they are deceived by the devil; for if the devil showed itself openly to them, it would be recognized by them, and they would avoid it. Therefore, by its art it shows them certain things as though good and holy, and thus deceives them. O woe to those who persist thus in this death. But because the devil knows that it has only a short time for its error, it now hastens to perfect unbelief in its members—namely, you most wicked deceivers who labour to overthrow the Catholic faith. You are unstable and weak in avoiding the venomous arrows [Col. 0563C] of human pollution, which you practise against the law according to your own will. Therefore, after you have discharged your lust through the poisonous seed of fornication, you then pray falsely and deceitfully impose holiness upon yourselves—a thing more unworthy in my eyes than stinking mud.

Certainly, the schism that arose at Horeb, where the Jewish people made a graven image and began to play in diabolical mockery—as some still now habitually play wantonly—and the schism that was in Baal, in which many perished, and the schism of fornications, where shameful acts were committed with the Midianites, and all other like things shall fall upon you. For in all these evils you have a share, being worse than the former people, because, seeing the true law of God, you stubbornly reject it. But, O you who desire your salvation, who have received baptism and are the anointed mountain of God, resist Satan and do not wish to descend from the mountain of your salvation.

But a person of such hardness that he despises God’s help in resisting the devil is one against whom the devil does not cease to set its snares, when it sees even in that person the blackness of iniquity arising, which brings such bitterness upon the whole body that the body itself withers in weakness from it. Therefore, when a person begins to chew over evil and to crush himself into despair, as though it were impossible for him to avoid evil and do good, then the devil, seeing this, says: “Behold the person who is like us [Col. 0564A], denying his God and turning himself toward us: he now follows us. Therefore let us all hasten and run swiftly to him, binding him with our arts so that he cannot flee from us. For he wishes to abandon his God and follow us.”

But if a person is assailed by diabolical suggestion in these evils—that is, is polluted by murder, adultery, gluttony, drunkenness, and the excess of every vice—and then persists in these matters without repentance, that person falls into death. But one who, resisting the devil, withdraws from these vices through repentance rises to life. For of one who has followed the desire of his flesh and neglected the good desire of his spirit, the Maker of the world says: “This person despises me and loves his flesh together with sin [Col. 0564B], unwilling to know that he ought to turn himself away from perdition; and therefore he must be rejected.” But of one who has loved the good ardour of his spirit and rejected the pleasure of his flesh, the Creator of the world says: “This one looks toward me and does not nourish his body in filth, desiring to know that he ought to remove himself from death; therefore he is to be helped.”

How? As Solomon says in accordance with my will: “Sinners pursue evil, and good things shall be repaid to the just.” What does this mean? Those rushing into a fall and falling in ruin are assailed on every side by deadly diseases, so that they do not look wisely upon what is true but carelessly reject it. Hence, since they are not worthy to look upon God or to have any happiness in God or in human beings, because they reject God and choose the devil, the evil that they perform brings much adversity upon them. But in the good, right understanding and just thought build on high, so that they receive in their bosom the inheritance of the Father, because they attend to the heavenly light. They are not deceivers in the mockery of the marketplace, concerning how this or that may be sold without comparison, but possess what is true in God.

But the fact that you see a great multitude of people gleaming in much brightness, who everywhere strongly trample the aforesaid worm and afflict it with dreadful torment, signifies that the faithful company of believers, though begotten in human misery, hastens toward heavenly desires in the faith of baptism and in blessed virtues, with much adornment and beauty. Thus, surrounding this ancient seducer in their deeds with most powerful crushing [Col. 0564D], they cast it down and grind it with dreadful torment. Such are virgins, martyrs, and other worshippers of the true God, who with all their effort trample earthly things and desire heavenly things. Yet it cannot harm them by either its flames or its venom, because these people are so fortified in God with strength and steadfastness that they cannot be contaminated either by the open fires or by the hidden persuasions of diabolical iniquity. For with great strength of virtues they abandon vain fabrications and, living justly, cleave to holiness.

But whoever sees with wakeful eyes and hears with attentive ears, let that person offer the kiss of embrace to these my mystical words which flow forth from me who am living.

## BOOK THREE

[Col. 0565]

## FIRST VISION

**SUMMARY.—**The hearts of the faithful ought to fear and revere the greatness, breadth, and height of the fear of the Lord. Every faithful soul that wisely fears God is, through faith, God’s seat. The depth of God’s mysteries is incomprehensible to human beings, except insofar as faith conceives it through God’s gift. In the wisdom of God the Father, through love for his Son, the perfection of all the elect has been reckoned. An example from the Gospel concerning the same matter. What the muddy clay in the breast signifies, and why a human being is not overcome by the angel. Words of Isaiah on the same matter. Words of David. God the Father, in his Son incarnate from the dawn of the Virgin, works, orders, and completes all his works. On the revolving circle. God’s power is higher than a human being ought to know; and why angels praise God without change. God is clear justice, true and just. The virtue, justice, and judgment of God have no end that can be comprehended by human understanding. On the fall of the first angel and those who consented with him: why, how, and whither they fell. Words of Ezekiel on the same matter. The glory of that splendour which the devil lost through pride was preserved in the Father’s secret for another created light. The devil fell without an heir. An example concerning Goliath and David. The faith which was hidden among the ancients came forth into light in the mystery of God the Son incarnate.

[Col. 0565A] And I, a human being taken from other human beings, who am unworthy to be called human on account of transgressing God’s law—although I ought to be just, I am unjust, except that I am God’s creature through his grace, which will also save me—looked toward the east. And behold, there I saw something like a single stone, wholly intact, of immense breadth and height, having an iron colour; and upon it a white cloud. Upon the cloud was placed a round royal throne, on which sat a radiant youth of wonderful glory and such brightness that I could not look clearly upon him at all. He had, as it were, upon his breast black and muddy clay, broad like a human breast, surrounded by precious stones and pearls.

And from that radiant one seated on the throne there extended a great circle, golden in colour like the dawn, whose extent I could in no way comprehend, revolving from the east to the north, west, and south, thus bending back toward the east to that radiant one and having no end. This circle rose so high from the earth that I could not comprehend it, giving out a most terrible brilliance—of stony, steel-blue, and fiery colour on every side—according to its extent, stretching upward into the height of heaven and downward into the depth of the abyss, so that I could see no end of it.

Then I also saw a great star, of exceeding splendour and beauty, coming forth from the secret place of the one seated on the throne; with it came a very great multitude of shining sparks. All of these, led out with that star toward the south, looked upon the one seated on the throne as though he were a stranger; turning away from him, they desired the north more than they wished to look upon him. But immediately, in that turning away of their gaze, they were all extinguished and turned into the blackness of coals. And behold, a whirlwind arose from them; it at once cast them from the south, backward from the one seated on the throne, toward the north, hurling them into the abyss, so that I could see none of them any longer. But I saw the great splendour taken from them suddenly return to the one seated on the throne when they were extinguished.

[Col. 0566A] And I heard the one seated on the throne saying to me: “Write what you see and hear.” And from the inward knowledge of that vision I replied: “I beg you, my Lord, give me understanding, so that I may speak these mysteries in a manner that can be told; do not abandon me, but strengthen me in the dawn of your justice, in which your Son was revealed. Give me how I may and how I ought to set forth the divine counsel that was ordered in the ancient counsel: how you willed your Son to be incarnate, so that he might become human in time. You willed this before every creature in your simplicity and in the fire of the dove, that is, the Holy Spirit, so that your Son, rising wondrously like the bright form of the sun [Col. 0566B], might truly be clothed in humanity at virginity’s beginning, taking a human form for the sake of humankind.”

And again I heard him saying to me: “O how beautiful are your eyes in the divine account, when the dawn rises there in the divine counsel.” And again I replied from the inward knowledge of the vision itself: “In the bosom of my soul I seem to myself like the ash of ashen decay and like dust of instability; therefore I sit trembling in the shadow like a feather. But do not blot me out, a stranger, from the land of the living, for I labour in great sweat in this vision; and also, because of the lowliness of my foolish understanding, which is mine in the flesh, I frequently reckon myself in the least and most lowly place, so that I am not worthy to be called human [Col. 0566C], because I am greatly afraid and do not dare to narrate your mysteries. O good and gentle Father, teach me what your will is, what I ought to utter. O Father who must be feared, O sweetest one, O one full of every grace, do not abandon me, but preserve me in your mercy.”

And again I heard the same one saying to me: “Now say how you have been taught. I wish you to say: Although you are ashes, speak the revelation of the bread who is the Son of God, who is life in fiery love, raising every dead person in soul and body, forgiving sins that have been undone in serene brightness. He is the beginning of the raising up of holiness in a human being, before holiness is awakened in that person. Therefore the magnificent, glorious, and incomprehensible God gave great help by sending his Son into the chastity of virginity, which could possess no variety of stains in its virginity whereby it might be softened. No pollution of flesh could or ought to have been in the mind of the Virgin, because death, the slayer and killer of the human race, was itself unwittingly deceived as if in sleep when the Son of God came in great silence into the dawn—that is, into the humble maiden. Death advanced as though secure, not knowing the life carried by that sweet Virgin, because her virginity was hidden from it. The Virgin herself was poor in earthly possessions, because the divine majesty wished to find her thus. Now write in this way concerning the true knowledge of the Creator in his goodness.”

God, who created all things and ordained humankind for that glory from which the lost angel was cast out with his imitators, is to be revered and feared with the greatest honour and awe by every creature, because it is just that reverence be offered to the Creator of all by his creature, and that God be worshipped above all things with the truest faith. This is most certainly signified by the stone which you see. For it is, in mystery, the greatness of the fear of the Lord, which ought always to arise and endure in the hearts of the faithful through a most pure intention.

But the fact that you see it wholly intact, of immense breadth and height, and having an iron colour signifies that this same firm [Col. 0567C] and great magnitude of the fear of the Lord must be held most firmly. For God must be feared by every creature in total integrity, so that he may be recognized as the one true God, since there is none besides him and none like him. In him is immeasurable breadth, because he is incomprehensible in all things and above all things; and height, because no one can comprehend the holy divinity or attain it with the height of his own understanding, for it is above all things. The fact that it resembles the colour of iron signifies that it is burdensome and hard for human minds to fear God: a thing most weighty to the softness of fragile ash, because the human creature rebels against him.

But the white cloud above that stone is the clear wisdom of the human mind; and the round royal throne placed upon it is the strong and princely faith that encompasses the Christian people, in whom God is faithfully known. For where the fear of the Lord takes root, there also the wisdom of the human mind appears above it; and then, with God bringing help, faith is laid upon this wisdom, in which God himself prepares rest for himself. For when God is feared through the wisdom of the human mind, he is understood in faith, because he is to be touched by these people as a seat touches its lord. Then in them God prepares a seat for himself, being supreme above all things; for he can be comprehended neither by power nor by dominion, but rests in the one pure faith, because he alone is God to be believed above all things.

[Col. 0568A] Therefore the radiant youth seated on the throne, of wonderful glory and such brightness that you could by no means look clearly upon him, having as it were upon his breast black and muddy clay broad as the breast of a great man and surrounded by precious stones and pearls, is the one God reigning above all things, shining in goodness and wonderful in his works. No human being can perfectly behold his immeasurable brightness in the depth of his mystery, except insofar as it is comprehended and borne by faith. Just as a seat contains and surrounds its lord, being so subject to him that it cannot raise itself against its lord, so faith does not desire proudly to gaze into God but touches him only with deepest devotion.

And, as it were, on his breast—that is, in the wisdom of his mystery—through love of his Son, he has the weak, frail, and poor clay that is humankind: black in the blackness of sins, muddy in the pollution of flesh, and broad according to the likeness of a human breast. This is the extension of the deep and great wisdom in which God himself created humankind, looking upon those who are in the salvation of the soul through repentance, whatever crime against God they may commit while in their weakness they kick against him, because they will finally come to him.

These are surrounded by the many ornaments of those who arise among them: precious stones in the great persons who are martyrs and virgins of holiness, and pearls in the innocent and penitent children of redemption. With these, the same clay is greatly adorned, while such virtues shine in a human body as shine in God in every brightness. For he who established the breath and life of human beings looked upon himself. How? Namely, in redemption, when in his foreknowledge he knew that his Son would be incarnate, so that every stained variety of crimes ought to be wiped away in his body.

And thus he also sees the souls which will be justified after an increase of superfluous sins while they are still in their bodies, and which, after the diversity of their errors, will become accustomed to walking in God’s justice: how they stand in God, how they cease from great forgetfulness, and how they return from every vice by which they were wounded [Col. 0568D] when they fell into mortal sins. And just as they see that many peoples have risen from the erring paths in which they walked, full of wounds from most grievous blows, restored from the death of the foulness of crimes, so also many come who are so gravely wounded in the bitterness of the sharp pain of sin that, worn out even by the habit of evil conduct in which they have sinned beyond measure, they can no longer breathe amid the waves in order to perform the deadly work of adultery, murder, and the excess of every evil.

O wretched ones, do they not come like strangers from a far country, as Scripture has in the Gospel, where the younger son said: “I will arise and go to my father, and I will say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven [Col. 0569A] and before thee; I am now no longer worthy to be called thy son; make me as one of thy hired servants” (Luke 15)? This means the following. A person who returns to himself from the fall of sin through the admonition of the Holy Spirit says: “I wish to rise from unbearable sins, which I can by no means endure—from grievous guilt—and I shall return in the remembrance of my mind, weeping and grieving over my sins. Thus I shall come to my father, who is my father because he created me, and I shall say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven—that is, against the heavenly work which I am, whom you formed in your will, touching me thus in creation itself, so that I too ought to have been heavenly in my deeds. But I made myself defiled through most shameful works, sinning also before you, because I abandoned human nature within myself. How?

[Col. 0569B] “Through many abominations; therefore I too am guilty in my own perdition and before your majesty. And I am not worthy to be called your son, because through the wickedness of my heart I brought your creature in myself into a condition other than that in which I was established by you. But now treat me as your redeemed servant, for the wage of the blood of your Son, whom you gave as so great a payment that death can never repay it by any compensation; yet he dismisses sinners through the repentance that arose in the passion of your Son. For I lost the rightful inheritance of the sons in Adam, who, though created a son, was deprived in righteousness of the glory of blessedness. But now repentance ought to redeem the sins of man through the blood of your Son.”

This is what must be said by those who repeat Adam’s fall and afterwards [Col. 0569C] return through repentance, thus attaining salvation. They remember that they have heard many admonitions narrated from the Scriptures, concerning the torment and blood of their Redeemer; and, groaning, they remember that they transgressed despite having heard them—though they ought diligently to have understood how to keep the word of God. For they neglected his law, which had been established for them to keep, refusing, in the institution of the commandment, to consider what they ought to do or abandon through fear of the Lord. Yet they come to the truth, recalling what they heard or knew from God, although they were previously so blinded that they wholly refused to know his righteousness, [Col. 0569D] so as to turn themselves toward setting it before their sins, while they despised it, cast the word of God behind them, and rejected his law. Many of these will abound in good things, so that they are neither satisfied nor find it enough to feast in the house of God, celebrating the divine office and performing his righteousness abundantly. Thus they are always weeping and remembering in sorrow the evils that they committed in former times, while they worshipped unlawful works and passed beyond what was lawful in God’s law.

This is the muddy clay which you see in the breast of the merciful Father. How? The believing people are present to the Son of God, who came forth from the Father’s heart into the world, clinging to him by that intention through which they believe in him. Certainly for this reason they also appear in [Col. 0570A] the breast of the merciful Father: so that neither angel nor any creature may despise humankind, because the incarnate Son of the most high God bears human form in himself. For the blessed angelic choir is indignant with humankind because it is excessively defiled by its sins, whereas the blessed angels are inviolate, without any transgression of righteousness, always gazing most attentively upon the Father’s face. And what is loved by the Father, they too love in the Son. How? Namely, that the Son of God was born as a human being. For I, the Father, set my Son, born of the Virgin, for the salvation and restoration of humankind, as Isaiah, my servant and prophet, announces to you: “Like a shepherd he shall feed his flock; in his arm he shall gather the lambs and lift them in his bosom; he himself shall carry those that are with young” (Isa. 60 [cf. Isa. 40:11]).

This [Col. 0570B] means the following. As a shepherd feeds his flock, so my Son, the good shepherd, shall feed his redeemed flock. How? He feeds it with his law, which he himself planted through me. Therefore, too, in his outstretched power, as in his arm—because this same Son of mine is human—he shall gather innocent lambs from Adam’s guilt through the innocence of baptism, when the old man with his works is stripped from them; and he shall lift them up in his virtues and in his law, in his bosom. How? Namely, because he raises them above the heights of heaven, so that they become his members. Therefore, in the inward secret of the Godhead, humankind appears in its form in a way that neither angels nor any other creature possess, because my Only-Begotten assumed human form in virginal flesh for the redemption of the human race.

[Col. 0570C] He himself shall also carry those with young in his body. How? My Son carries human beings in his blood, so that they are made safe through his five wounds; for whatever they have sinned through their five senses shall be wiped away, after repentance, by supreme righteousness. For he carried them in this way: he was incarnate, suffered five wounds upon the cross, died and was buried, and rose from the dead. He also stretched out his hand to them when he drew them back to himself. How? Namely, because my Son assumed humanity for those who thought that, through Adam’s fall, they had perished forever. This same Only-Begotten of mine also conquered death, [Col. 0570D] so that it could no longer rule over them. Therefore he knows them in the power of his brightness, so that they shall come into the cleansing of repentance.

But that you see them appearing in the Father’s bosom means that the Son of Man is completed with his members in the Father’s secret. How? For when the world is completed, then Christ’s elect, who are his members, are also perfected. O how beautiful he is, as the Psalmist also says: “Fairer in form than the sons of men” (Ps. 44 [45]). This means the following. In him shines the most beautiful beauty of most radiant form, without any stain of sin, without the moisture of human foulness, and without any lust for a deed in the desires of sinners which the flesh of mortal weakness demands. This never touched this man.

And that form [Col. 0571A] of the Son of Man was born in simplicity above other human beings, such that the untouched Virgin bore her child in ignorance of sin, not knowing herself to have a son amid distress. How? Because she felt no contact with sins, she did not know herself to have pain in giving birth; rather, within her the integrity of her body rejoiced. O how fair in form! Yet let people know that there was no greater bodily beauty there except insofar as the ordering of profound wisdom established the human form. For the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one God in three persons, does not delight in beauty of flesh, but in the great humility with which the Son of God clothed himself in humanity.

Moreover, in the form of the Son of Man there was no blemish, such as occurs when a person is at times [Col. 0571B] distorted by an afflicted appearance through bodily irregularity. This belongs to God’s judgment: namely, when a human being’s divided limbs are not rightly ordered, as in the infirmity which is not according to the natural formation of the human body, but according to God’s judgment. Strong nature indeed exists in right formation; weak nature declines into a diversity of formation contrary to form. Such was not the case in my Son, the human being.

But, I say, human beings are greatly diverse in their members: they are black, ugly, defiled, leprous, dropsical, and full of vices; they also have the rust of wickedness through the persuasion of diabolical art; they are foolish and hard of heart in seeing the Lord’s good things, and [Col. 0571C] are liable to accusation and blame because, in great forgetfulness, they ought to have performed righteousness but perform evil, abandoning good and despising the cross and martyrdom of their Lord. Yet God the Father looks upon the formed work of clay with the intention of his goodness, as a father looks upon his children when he lifts them into his bosom. And because he is God, he has the love of a merciful father for his children.

For his inward love of heart toward human beings is such that he sent his Son to the reproach of the cross, like a gentle lamb being led to slaughter as a victim. Thus my Son brought back the lost sheep, which he took from the wolf’s jaws, upon his shoulder, having assumed humanity and carrying it amid great pains when he deigned to die for his sheep.

[Col. 0571D] Among those human beings are many surrounded with ornaments and adorned with the precious array of virtues: martyrs, virgins, innocents, penitents, those subject to their teachers, as has already been said, and those who make themselves conscious of their crimes, tormenting themselves in these through an unconquerable struggle, while they deny in themselves what they are. It is not to be said there who the elect are or where they are, for all are numbered. Who can see into the profound wisdom of the Most High and into the discernment of his knowledge, to know what he has in the number of those to be saved? His judgments are incomprehensible to all human beings. You must run, because the kingdom of God is prepared for you. For according to the zeal of the faithful who work God’s righteousness, [Col. 0572A] who are washed in baptism and known in faith, such also shall be their reward.

But that you see a great circle, golden in colour like the dawn, extending from the one seated on the throne, whose extent you can in no way comprehend, means that from the almighty Father there extends a most powerful authority and his most powerful work, comprehending all things in his power. With it he works in his Son, whom he has always had with himself in the majesty of divinity, ordering and completing through him all his works before the world and in the world from the beginning. He glows with most beautiful brightness like the dawn, because the Son was incarnate in the most wise Virgin, whom the dawn signifies, by the inspiration of God’s finger, which is the Holy Spirit; and in him every work of the Father was also made.

[Col. 0572B] You cannot comprehend by any reasoning the circuit of this glory, because neither his power nor his works, nor any goodness or power in any creature—whether existing, having existed, or yet to be—has any measure by which to measure it. Rather, God is immeasurable and incomprehensible in his power, unconquered and wondrous in his work.

And that same circle turns from east to north, and to west and south, bending back toward the east, to the very one seated on the throne, and has no end: this means that God’s power and work go around, encompassing every creature. How? In the will of the Father, who with the Son and the Holy Spirit is one God, all creatures arose; and all [Col. 0572C] perceive him in his power. How? All perceive him in creation, namely as turning from the east, which is in the rising of all righteousness, and stretching toward the north, in the confusion of the devil; toward the west, where the darkness of death seeks to crush the light of life—yet the light rises again, having conquered the gloom of darkness; and toward the south, where the burning ardour of God’s righteousness is in the hearts of the faithful. Finally, he turns back to the rising of righteousness, as though returning eastward.

What is this? When, through supreme power, God’s work in human beings in this world has been completed according to the time preordained by God, then the circuit of this world also shall be fulfilled, perfected at the end of time on the last day. All God’s works shall shine forth in his elect; while he who sits [Col. 0572D] upon the throne has no end, because God is perfect in power and work, who was, is, and shall remain in divinity without any beginning of time, so that he was not merely but is.

And that this circle rises from the earth to such a height that you cannot comprehend it means that heavenly power is so exalted above every creaturely life in human sense and understanding, and so incomprehensible in all things and above all things, that no creature can measure it by any capacity of perception; for it is far more sublime than can be known by it. Hence the angels also frequently resound with praises of God. For they see him in his power and glory, but cannot, even while beholding him perfectly, comprehend him as if they had reached an end; [Col. 0573A] nor can they ever be overtaken by the weariness of satiety with his greatness and beauty.

But that it gives forth from itself a most terrible radiance, namely of stony, steel-like, and fiery colour, means that divine power displays from itself a hard strength in great severity against concealed, unrepentant, and unpunished iniquity: fearful and, as it were, steely. For God is transparent righteousness, having no injustice of yielding softness—for injustice, as is said, is like dust, which does not please God—but he is that righteousness which, like steel, has strengthened every other righteousness, which yields before his righteousness as iron yields to steel. He is also, as it were, fiery, because he is the judicial fire burning sin on account of [Col. 0573B] every injustice that has never wished to turn to him and seek his mercy.

God is also like a stone in relation to humankind, because he is true and just without any change: as a stone cannot be turned to softness, so he has no change. And he is like steel, namely in efficacy, passing through all things without any change of place or time, because he is God existing above all. He is also like fire, because he kindles, burns, and illuminates all things without the succession of time bringing novelty, because he is God.

And that this radiance extends everywhere, according to its breadth, upward to the height of heaven and downward to the depth of the abyss, [Col. 0573C] so that you cannot see any end of it, means that the strength of God’s power and work, and his righteousness and most upright judgment, have no comprehensible end anywhere in their incomprehensibility, neither in the heights of heaven nor in the depths of the abyss, since they are above all things.

You also see from the secret place of the one seated upon the throne a great star of exceedingly great radiance and beauty coming forth, and with it a very great multitude of falling sparks. This means that by command of the almighty Father the angel Lucifer, who is now Satan, came forth at his origin adorned with great glory and clothed with much brightness and beauty; and with him all the sparks of his host, then shining in the splendour of light but now extinguished in the darkness of gloom. [Col. 0573D] For, inclined toward evil, he did not look upon me alone as perfect; rather, trusting in himself, he thought that he could begin whatever he wished and complete what he had begun. Therefore, the honour due to the one seated on the throne, because he had been created by him, he turned back upon himself; and by this very act he bent himself toward evil.

But that, with that star, all were led southward, gazing upon the one seated on the throne as though he were a stranger, turning themselves away from him and desiring the north more than they wished to look upon him, means that Lucifer and his entire company, though created in the blazing goodness of God, stood as if obliquely—that is, in pride, disdaining the one reigning in heaven. For all of them, having come forth in creation, tasted impiety from the beginning, which turned itself toward perdition: [Col. 0574A] they looked upon God not so as to wish to know him in goodness, but wished to exalt themselves above him as over one alien to them, turning themselves away from knowledge of him in burning pride and striving more toward their own fall than desiring to know God in his glory.

But that immediately, in the very turning away of their gaze, they were all extinguished and transformed into the blackness of coals, means that when they proudly disdained to know God, Lucifer with all his followers was extinguished in his wickedness from the brilliance of radiant splendour with which he had been clothed by divine power. He erased in himself the inner beauty that he ought to have used for good and stretched himself toward swallowing impiety. Thus he was extinguished from eternal brightness so as to fall into eternal perdition.

[Col. 0574B] Therefore all were turned into the blackness of coals whose fire is extinguished: stripped with their leader, the devil, of the brightness of their splendour, they were thus extinguished in the perdition of darkness, deprived of every glory of blessedness, just as a coal lacks every light of fiery spark. But that a whirlwind arose from them and immediately cast them back from the south, away from the one seated on the throne, toward the north, hurling them into the abyss so that you could no longer see any of them, means that the greatest blast of impiety rose in those angels of iniquity when they wished to prevail over God and crush him through pride. It was blown out into the most bitter blackness of perdition and cast them back from the south—that is, from goodness—which is into forgetfulness of God, ruler of all things, [Col. 0574C] as though toward the northern region, so that where they wished proudly to be exalted, there they might find a shameful fall: cast down because of their pride into the abyss of eternal death, which is their perdition, so that they may no longer be seen in any brightness.

Thus I spoke through my servant Ezekiel to the southern forest, which ought ardently to have borne the fruit of righteousness but did not, saying: “Behold, I shall kindle in thee a fire, and I shall burn in thee every green tree and every dry tree; the flame of the kindling shall not be extinguished, and every face from south to north shall be burned therein. And all flesh shall see that I, the Lord, kindled it; it shall not be extinguished” (Ezek. 20).

This means the following. O fool, who raised yourself against me in your pride: I, who [Col. 0574D] have neither beginning nor end, shall cause the fire of my indignation to be kindled in you in my zeal. By it I shall burn up in you all your greenness, by which you wished to begin a work, trusting in your false strength more in yourself than in me; for in your foolish knowledge you chose to be according to your pride. And I shall burn in you all the dryness of your sin and of the other lost ones, when you suggest sin, dry with respect to goodness, to the human being who is ashes; for your suggestion shall receive no salvation in you, but shall become eternal fire in you. No reward of salvation remains for you, nor for those who follow you in your example.

And that kindling of punishments shall not be extinguished in its torments, but shall burn up precipitous pride, as it were in the face of the covetous gaze upon the honour which you conceived the desire [Col. 0575A] to have in yourself. You have been cast out from all your glory, rising from the south in burning, most radiant light and falling into the northern darkness—that is, into hell. And every human being shall see this: namely, the elect and the reprobate shall know Gehenna, for the elect know it because they have escaped it; the reprobate because they shall remain with it in punishments. They shall know that I, the almighty Lord, kindled it in recompense for your evils, O devil, and that it shall not be extinguished in your evils nor in those of your followers.

Thus the perdition of diabolical pride cast Satan and his angels into the outer darkness of eternal torments, without any consolation of light; so that no place in eternal light was found for them. And you, frail human being, horrified [Col. 0575B] and astonished, could see nothing more of them, just as the same Ezekiel, in my Spirit, says to the king of Tyre under a mystical signification: “All who see thee among the nations shall be astonished at thee. Thou hast become nothing, and thou shalt not be for ever” (Ezek. 28).

This means the following. All those upright in heart who see you, O devil, drunk with vices among those nations that embrace you in transgression of God’s law, shall wither in astonishment at your filth: at the way you defile by your suggestion the temple in God’s building, which is the human being.
