Moreover, two of the upper three—those standing to the right and left of the middle figure—and two of the lower three—the middle one and the one to her left—had no women’s veils upon their heads, but stood only with bare white [Col. 0626A] hair. The middle one of the first three, and the one seated on the stone beside the wall, had heads veiled with a white head-covering, as is women’s custom. The middle one of the upper three and the one at her right were dressed in white tunics.

But I saw the following differences among them. The figure standing in the middle of the upper three had upon her head a saffron-coloured circlet like a crown, inscribed on the right side: “Always kindle.” And I saw that a dove flew toward the right side of that figure, breathing with its mouth into the same inscription. The figure said:

“I am suffused with inward mercy, from which springs a stream that in no way wishes to hide money, gold, precious stones, [Col. 0626B] or pearls from the needy, who lack the means necessary for their needs and therefore weep. Now I shall console them and always relieve their poverty, for love of the Son of God, who is sweet and gentle and distributes His goods among the souls of the righteous, touching the wounds of their sins for repentance.”

The other figure, standing at her right, had on her breast something like a lion, like a shining mirror; and from her neck there hung down to her breast something like a pale-coloured serpent in the twisted bend of a rod. She said:

“I behold the shining lion, and for love of him I give. But I flee the fiery serpent; yet I love the serpent hanging upon the wood.”

The third figure, at her left, was clothed in a tunic resembling red hyacinth. At her breast there appeared an angel with one wing on either side, so that the right wing stretched to that figure’s right shoulder and the left wing to her left shoulder. The figure said:

“I have fellowship with angels, nor do I walk with hypocrites who dissemble, but I feast with the righteous.”

The figure in the middle of the lower three was clothed in a saffron-coloured tunic. A most white dove stood upon her right shoulder, breathing with its mouth into her right ear. Upon her breast appeared the monstrous and shapeless head of a human being. Beneath her feet lay forms like human beings, trampled and crushed by her. In her hands she held [Col. 0626D] an unfolded document, inscribed on one side—that is, on the side facing heaven—with seven lines, which I wished to read [Col. 0627A] but could not. She said:

“I wish to be the rod of bitter correction and the scourge against that liar who is the devil’s son, because the devil himself is the persecutor of God’s ineffable justice. Therefore I am a contrary and grievous adversary to him, because I have never been found in his mouth; and I too spit him from my mouth as deadly and lethal poison, because he has never found me in his cunning. He is also for me the worst and most grievous evil of all evils, because every evil arose from him. Therefore I reject and trample him underfoot in God’s beloved justice, which is beloved to me without cease and without end. I am its supporter and guide, because upon me every structure of God’s virtues, which build [Col. 0627B] on high, shall be made firm and stand. O most mighty and most noble God, attend!”

The other figure, standing to her right, had an angelic face and one flying wing on either side, though she appeared in human form like the other virtues. She said:

“I resist the devilish conflict that rises obstinately against me, saying: ‘I cannot endure any tribulation, but I want to remove from myself everything contrary to me. I shall fear no one. Whom should I fear? I do not wish to fear anyone.’ But those who utter this evil will be cast down by me, because I am appointed always to rejoice and always to take joy in all good things. For the Lord Jesus is the remitter and consoler of every pain, since He too endured pain in His body. And because He is also righteous correction, I therefore wish to join myself to Him and always bear Him, casting from myself hatred, envy, and every evil. I also wish always to have a joyful face in your justice, O God.”

But the third figure, standing at her left, was clothed in a white tunic marked with green. In her hands she held a small vessel of pale brilliance, emitting much light like lightning, so that the same light shone upon the face and around the neck of the figure. She said:

“I am blessed. For the Lord Christ Jesus makes and prepares me beautiful and white when I flee that deadly counsel of the devil, who continually broods upon that misfortune: namely, that God be rejected [Col. 0627D] and the devil drawn in through evil works. I flee this Satan; I reject him and always regard him as grievous to me, because I desire that beloved One whom I may continually embrace and possess with joy in all things and above all things.”

The figure seated upon the stone at the end of this wall was clothed in a darkish tunic. On her right shoulder she bore a small cross bearing the image of Jesus Christ, which turned this way and that. And, as though from clouds, a splendor of wondrous brightness shone upon her breast, divided from itself into many rays, as the sun’s radiance divides from itself when it shines through many small openings in some object.

In her right hand she also held a small piece of wood shaped like [Col. 0628A] a fan, from whose top three little branches had miraculously sprouted with blossom. In her lap she had tiny stones of every kind of gem, which she examined with great care and diligence, as a merchant is accustomed carefully to examine his wares. She said:

“I am the mother of virtues; I always possess God’s justice in all things. For amid spiritual warfare and secular tumult, I always await my God within my conscience. I do not condemn, trample underfoot, or despise kings, dukes, governors, and the other secular offices, which have been ordained by the Author of all things. How could it be lawful for ashes to despise ashes? God’s crucified Son turns Himself toward all, moving them according to His justice and mercy. I too wish to hold every one of His ordinances and institutions according to His will.”

But the figure standing upon the wall at that same end had an uncovered head, black and curly hair, and a dark face. She was also clothed in a variegated tunic woven with many colours. I saw her take off her tunic and shoes and stand naked. Immediately her hair and face shone with the beauty of whiteness and newness, like those of a newly born infant; and throughout her body she shone as a pure, bright radiance shines in splendor. Then I saw upon her breast a most brilliant cross with the image of Christ Jesus, set upon a small tree between two flowers, a lily and a rose, which bent themselves somewhat upward toward that cross. [Col. 0628C] And I saw that she shook out forcefully her removed tunic and shoes, so that much dust was shaken from them. She said:

“I put off the Old Testament and put on the noble Son of God with His justices in holiness and truth. Therefore I have been restored in good things and changed from vices. Therefore, O my God, do not remember the sins of my youth and my ignorances, nor take vengeance for my sins.”

And while I considered these things more attentively, He who sat upon the throne again said to me:

“Let none of the faithful who humbly wishes to obey God hesitate to refuse subjection to human teaching authority, because through the Holy Spirit government among the people has been arranged for the effective benefit of the living. It was prefigured among the ancient people as something that would exist in ecclesiastical observances and ought to be held faithfully and firmly.

“Thus, what you see between the northern corner and the western corner—the wall of the aforesaid building, wholly arched on its inner side after the manner of a lattice, yet not open like a lattice but solid—means this: from Abraham and Moses, resisting the devil, as though from the corner facing north, up to the true Trinity openly declared in the true and Catholic faith, when God the Father sent the Son of God into the world and He abundantly poured forth His teaching at the end of time, as though at the corner facing west, there stood a wall: that is, the Israelite people, established in the law of God’s justice and working in the construction [Col. 0629A] of the goodness of the almighty Father. They were restrained and convicted in the Old Testament, because, after the display of severity stirred up in the Lord’s zeal through the ordinances of the ancient prelates, the governments of new dignities were prefigured.

“For the Old Testament extended to the New, producing from itself far greater commandments of the law of the New Testament than had first arisen within it. Thus, from the lesser came the greater: from the lesser teaching of the ancient precepts came the greater and broader teaching of the new, since the Old Testament was only like a foundation first laid. Upon it was built the most profound wisdom of all teaching, manifested in the incarnation of the Son of God, extending from the circumcision of the old law to the new rule of baptism, adorned with greater commandments.

[Col. 0629B] “And that wall—the Jewish people—on the inner side of its understanding, wherein the human soul knows God, is everywhere enclosed with arches. That is, it is enclosed on every side by the signification of the teaching office of its forerunners, who proclaim the commandments of God’s law and show them to it, so that lesser persons may be ordered by greater, as people are ordinarily arranged under those who excel them. This is according to the construction of a lattice, which is the typological prefiguration of the Holy Spirit piercing the hard letters in the incarnation of the Son of God, who most fully showed the lattices of His mercy to those who seek them.

“Yet it is not open by the piercing of the doorkeeper, namely, the Holy Spirit—not laying bare spiritual understanding in the old law as happened later in the lattices of mercy, in the flesh-manifested Son of the Most High. Instead it remains solid in the severity of legal precepts, which were afterward illuminated through the Holy Spirit in the fountain of living water.

[Col. 0629C] “It also has in every arch something like a picture of human beings, because just as this picture displays the image of persons, so a person placed in a triumphal arch—that is, in the dignity of teaching authority—acts in God’s stead. How? Because the most profound and principal wisdom was placed by God’s grace in the mouth of human rationality, so that, in God’s name, a person might exercise the office of teaching through the strictness of the justice and mercy of the Most High.

[Col. 0629D] “But what you see on the exterior side of the same wall, namely two other smaller walls, means that in external affairs, apart from spiritual teaching authority, there is an intervening order of greater and lesser peoples, appointed by God’s command like two walls. For the exterior wall consists of elders through the strength of secular power in my ordering; and the middle wall consists of lesser persons, who stand under the authority both of spiritual and secular persons, as though between the arches of the aforesaid inner wall—which is spiritual teaching authority—and the outer wall, which is secular power, as has been said. Therefore the two walls are placed outside the circumference of the inner arched wall, because secular persons are occupied in earthly affairs, possessing exterior matters more than interior ones; yet they are nevertheless within the line of my ordering. How?

[Col. 0630A] “The inward is understood through the outward. For just as from the visible and exalted person of a human being, a person recognizes how that human being is to be feared, entreated, and loved, so by the same understanding he recognizes how the invisible and most high God is to be feared, venerated, and loved above all things. For through outward and secular lordship, a person is admonished of the inward and spiritual power of divine majesty, which is so closed and hidden from humanity that it cannot be seen by physical eyes except insofar as it is apprehended by faith. And since God is invisible to mortal creatures, at least through visible authority let a person learn to fear and venerate Him, the Most High Founder of His authority. How?

[Col. 0630B] “Divine inspiration gave human minds, through their rationality, that in a rightly ordered society great persons should rule among the peoples and be feared and honoured by them. For God allowed one class to excel and another to be subject so that human beings might be divided in this way and might not kill one another and perish by themselves. Otherwise they would be idle, unable to proceed to the knowledge of God unless they foresaw this through fear and honour among human beings. Thus the Holy Spirit advanced, leading the people toward the inward law of the spirit, by which a person might be ruled within and without, until the springing fountain came forth, appearing to the world in the fullness of justice, [Col. 0630C] governing both body and soul.

“Thus too the care of secular power was instituted for the use of earthly things: that the body might seek refreshment lest it fail; and spiritual teaching authority was instituted for the inward longing of attaining God’s service, so that the soul might yearn for heavenly things. These matters, then, were established by my ordering, according also to what Isaac said to his son Jacob: ‘Be lord of your brothers, and let the sons of your mother bow down before you’ (Gen. 27). This means: You ought to be lord of your brothers, powerful over them in honours and blessedness, blessed in the blessings given to me by God; and all those born as children of your mother’s children, subject to you because of the preeminent ground of your blessing, should bow before you.

“For from you shall go out a great people, from whom a most strong and mighty man shall arise. His brothers shall pursue him in flight, but he, very swiftly in his greatest strength, like a lion tearing himself away from them, shall rule over them with most excellent dominion and press them down in the name of his power—a power which shall never be uprooted in the basest tail, while his brothers become a tail.

[Col. 0630D] “So I too, the heavenly Father, said to my incarnate Son: ‘Be Lord of all those born and begotten from the conceived seed of humankind, whom I created through you; for you, wonderfully born of a Virgin, were not conceived by human seed, but came forth from me through blazing fire, appearing upon earth as true human being, while the seal of the most whole and chaste [Col. 0631A] Virgin remained closed. Therefore you are Lord of those who are your brothers by reason of your incarnation, in which you are human, in the heavenly brightness of divinity. And let bowing—that is, subjection—be rendered to you by the children of your mother, namely of your incarnation; and let human beings born from human beings be subject to you in the service of most dutiful devotion.’

“And because the Son of God is thus Lord of all creatures, through Him also, in the will of the Father and the touch of the Holy Spirit, the arrangement of diverse powers in the world was established. How? Namely, God removed that excess and boastfulness by which people would fail to honour people, so that each person would do whatever pleased him, had God not overthrown this by the immeasurable wisdom of His counsel. Rather, He distinguished people from people: the lesser to be subject to the greater in the service of obedience; the greater diligently and devoutly to assist the lesser in every administration useful to them. So also, in the ascent of the Holy Spirit, it was given to Jacob through his father that he should be lord of his brothers, as has been said.

[Col. 0631B] “But in the fact that he was shown to be lord, it was demonstrated that secular office has the role of exercising lordship over the freedom of others, while, because of the fear of the honour rendered to it by them through its power, it should spare them—not oppressing them under the law of servitudes, but regarding them as in the love of brothers. But in the statement that bowing should occur before him is indicated the service of those who are bound to serve their lords by the bond of servitude, as children of the flesh, having fleshly care.

“But after Jacob had by paternal blessing stolen this lordship from his brother, he afterward established heavenly celebration through the stone which he raised as a memorial and through the tithe which he vowed to give, as was prefigured. This signifies the principal person in spiritual warfare, because every believer ought to ascend from the lowest rank to the highest: through secular power, that is, learning the higher teaching of brighter light, of spiritual life. In it is fulfilled the office of the helmsman according to the course of the immaculate Lamb, who lifted humanity upward with the fullness and goodness of all justice, namely [Col. 0631D] raising up the person cast down by the snares of the perverse ravisher.

“Therefore these two institutions, proceeding respectively toward earthly and heavenly things, are divided into four and four parts, because God gave human beings a great force of rational knowledge, so that in the ascent of the Holy Spirit they might investigate these in themselves in the figure of the four elements, adding more than the aforesaid two modes. This I neither despise nor reject, because one who multiplies in my name what is lesser is worthy of reward, not rejection. These four divisions exist both in secular burdens and in spiritual institutions. How? In secular affairs there are noble and more noble persons, and there are servants [Col. 0632A] and those who render obedience. But in spiritual sacraments there are those who excel and those who are higher, and there are those who obey and those who correct.

“But I do not at all wish those offices, established by my ordering, to be seized by a furtive gift of purchase in a sale; rather, I wish that they be administered for a rational purpose, so that those who receive them may be useful before God and human beings. Yet certain venomous scorpions transgress my justice and seize them with the deadly poison of avarice and pride, not only in secular offices of authority but also in spiritual appointments. The seizure of secular dignities—earthly things acquired through earthly things—must indeed be examined most severely in the wrath of my zeal; but the seizure of spiritual offices is of still greater weight and examination.

[Col. 0632B] “For secular persons are outwardly flesh from flesh, whereas spiritual persons are inwardly joined to the spirit. Yet although secular persons are occupied outwardly with earthly care, under that form they ought in their government to yearn toward the inward things of the spirit. But spiritual persons, placed under the form of religion and contempt for worldly things, ordered inwardly in the heart of the almighty Father, ought much more, under the spiritual name, ardently to imitate His Son in the highest priesthood. For as the Son of God came forth from His Father’s heart, so the Father established within Himself, in His Son, the persons of teachers, who are placed in so distinguished an order for the Church’s benefit and joined to God in right action. [Col. 0632C] How?”

Those who are in compunction and testing of heart, and in mature judgment—who, as is wholly clear to me, have a good conscience—so that they do not perversely and contrarily seek the office of teaching, neither seeking it by diabolical art, nor acquiring it through money or secular power, nor seeking from it the fleeting words of human praise, but accepting it in humility through my true election and that of the people: these are my most beloved and most approved guardians, and my most faithful friends. But those who go backward and acquire it otherwise in darkness—that is, secretly plundering heavenly mysteries by secular, earthly means—flee my face [Col. 0632D] and cruelly kill their own souls. In this they mock me, because they deny me thus and kick against my will. How? Because they despise me, not wishing to attain the authority of teaching through me, so as to raise the inward eyes of their heart to me and say: “Does this please God or not?” Rather, each says within himself: “Even if this is evil before God, nevertheless I shall accept it, trusting in the Lord that, while still living in the body, I may one day repent.” In this way they acquire the office of teaching without me, the living God: they neither ask this of me nor trust that they can attain it by my will; but, aflame in this desire, they flee from my face, thus seizing the office of teaching and suffering shipwreck away from my mercy.

[Col. 0633A] These are not within the heart of the supreme Father, but are outside, in the region of the north, where he who is their prince in these matters resides. They do not wish to seek me, the Creator of all things, but follow their own will, which they treat as God, and abandon me. For they do not wish to know me, nor do I know them. Their own desire suggests to them what they want. And because they refuse to have fear of me, I therefore do not then wish to oppose them in the terror of my wrath, until they are resisted on that day when they can prevail no longer. Left by me in this life, they will answer in the future terrible judgment for what they do: knowing me indeed in faith, but unwilling, in what they commit, to look toward me.

Now, as you see, the aforesaid two smaller [Col. 0633B] walls are as long as the space from the aforesaid northern corner to the western corner. This means that, in the ordering of peoples, greater and lesser, through the extension of human time—from Abraham and Moses, as though from the north, to the manifestation of the Catholic faith in the true Trinity, which faith my Son, sent by me into the world as toward the west, taught—there existed under my law peoples and their chief teachers. They were the preceding seed and example of the people of the New Testament, extending from zeal to my Son born in the flesh. Thus there were, are, and always will be distinctions among human beings, inward and outward, [Col. 0633C] that is, spiritual and secular, greater and lesser. They are joined to those corners on both sides, in the manner of a vault, because under both the Old and the New Testament, from either side of their beginning, peoples are shown as united in honor and teaching; and this is in the likeness of a vault, being well and worthily arranged, by the authority of divine providence, for the condition of the building of the heavenly Jerusalem.

And the fact that the height of these same two smaller walls is three cubits means that, in the elevation of uprightness among the two secular conditions—that is, greater and lesser—there are three classes of people: the more eminent rulers; others free from the yoke of servile attendance; and [Col. 0633D] the common people laid beneath their prelates in subjection. Hence also the width between the inner arched wall and the middle wall is one cubit: this is the extent of rank between the higher persons of spiritual teaching and the lower titles of earthly service, established in the unity of faith according to God for correcting their subjects. And between the outer and that same middle wall there is a width of one palm, like a child’s hand, because between the lower authority of secular rule and the subjection of secular service there is likewise room for just consideration, so that these, with unanimous and simple devotion of childlike innocence, may touch one another in the hand of their united work.

But the fact that within that building you see six figures standing on the pavement of the building before the aforesaid [Col. 0634A] arched wall means that in the work of God’s goodness six virtues are extended, prefiguring the other virtues, just as God created his creatures in six days. That is, the virtues appear as a figure of things to come before the wall—that is, before the Israelite people restrained by the divine law and surrounded by the teaching and defense of their forerunners—while they also tread underfoot the pavement of earthly cares in the same construction of the supreme Father, in this signification: that the Christian host may oppose itself to the devil through them.

Therefore three stand together at the front of that wall near the corner facing north, because the holy and inseparable Trinity, in the power of its majesty, was signified by diverse and hidden figures at the beginning of the Old Testament, begun from Abraham and Moses in opposition to the devil. And three likewise stand together at the end of the same wall beside the corner extending westward, because that same Trinity, reigning in the unity of divinity, was proclaimed by its open name at the end of that declining law, when the Son of God was born in the flesh for the redemption of humankind, tending toward the setting. All of them look upon the picture in the arches of that same wall, because, with equal zeal of devotion, they always attend to the teaching of God’s ordering, signified through his power in the law of both the New and Old Testaments, considering how it is fulfilled in them.

But the fact that, at the very end of that wall, you see another [Col. 0634C] figure seated within the same building upon a single stone, placed like a seat on the pavement, means that in the laying aside of the old law of the ancient people and at the beginning of the new faith, inaugurated in the true Trinity, when God established all steadfast virtues in the Church, this virtue too fittingly appeared in the work of the supreme Father, working in it through humankind until the consummation of the world. Hence she also sits upon the strongest rock, upon the one, namely the Son of God, who is the seat and rest of all the faithful who despise transient things and believe in him with pure faith. She inclines her right side toward the wall, because in the uprightness of rest and in the part of salvation she adheres to this people, which is placed under the teaching ordering [Col. 0634D] of God, so that the greater and the lesser alike may cultivate her in their works. But she turns her face toward the column of the true Trinity, because in every matter she directs her attention to that Trinity with the keenest sight of just discernment, so that, just as the eternal Trinity must be considered inviolably in three persons, so all who worship God may consider it most diligently in their deeds and, in considering it, may not abandon it.

But the fact that at the same end you see another figure standing upon the same wall in a higher place means that, when the shadow of the ancient law was transferred and the true light of justice shone forth in faith in the holy Trinity, this virtue was raised up in chief teaching and among the faithful people at the summit of the heavenly desire for salvation [Col. 0635A]. It stands, fighting against vices, raised up in the Son of God, because it began from him and will remain with him in the heavenly Jerusalem after the end of the age. It too is turned toward the aforesaid column of the true Trinity, because, strengthened through the holy and ineffable Trinity, it leads souls back to their homeland.

The resemblance which you perceive in these figures means that the same virtues are unanimous amid the diversity of God’s gifts. Therefore they are clothed, like the preceding figures, as if in silken garments: around them, as around the other virtues, are the sweetest works which worshippers of God render to them in the divine law, doing them in the justice of truth. They wear white shoes, because in their ardor there is also the brightness of following the example of good deeds among human beings.

But the one at the right, in the middle of the three which you see at the far end of the same wall, possesses such purity and brightness throughout that, because of her great splendor, you cannot perfectly behold any form of her. For that virtue, with the salvation of true strengthening through the gift of the holy Trinity, rising at the end of the holy severity of old, is wholly translucent and pure, lacking every diabolical indignation, in the brightness of the joyful gladness of human unanimity. Thus, because of the multitude of glory and honor which it possesses in heaven, no mortal can by any reasoning behold its immeasurable unanimity—as it were, its form—[Col. 0635C] except insofar as God deigns to reveal it.

And the figure standing upon the wall wears black shoes, because before the incarnation of my Son there was, among humankind, a sign and trace of death both in the higher dignity and in the lower. But the fact that all are without cloaks means that they have together cast off earthly observances and the outward texture of legal institution, looking inward upon true justice. The exception is the middle one of the three who stood in the first part of the same wall, who is clothed in a cloak, because she, laboring under God’s protection at the beginning of the commanded severity, is encompassed by the embrace of God’s love, in which she hides the heavenly treasure after casting away the desire of fleshly things.

And two of the upper three—namely, those standing to the right and [Col. 0635D] left of the middle figure—and two of the lower three—namely, the middle one and the one to her left—have no women’s veils upon their uncovered heads, but stand only with white hair. This means that the law and the prophets, proceeding through the power of the heavenly majesty and showing life and death by their strength, together with the two commandments of twofold love that follow through the same divine power and possess steadfastness of inward circumspection amid opposites and the joy of sweetness in divine things, have faithfully been released from every subjection to any pain or snare of death in the head, that is, in Christ my Son. Yet they shine with uncovered hair in the brightness of virginity, because divinity greatly loved virginal nature in the Virgin Mary.

But the fact that [Col. 0636A] the middle one of the first three and the one seated upon the stone beside the wall have their heads veiled with a white head-covering, according to women’s custom, means that they are gently and sweetly bound, by the aid of heavenly height and the steadfastness of the manner of blessed rest, with the strong bond of subjection, reverencing God, the head of all the faithful, in the whiteness of devout devotion—as a husband ought to be honored by his wife with sincere love. And the middle one of the upper three and the one standing to her right are clothed in white tunics, because by that same power of divine majesty their most radiant and whitest works, established among human beings under the law of the Lord to whom they are joined, flow forth in most sweet blessedness. But the difference which you also see among them means that they have diverse powers in God, though they worship him in harmony.

Therefore the figure standing in the middle of the upper three prefigures abstinence, because in the first struggle she is like a city, a stronghold, and an ornament of the virtues joined to her, restraining herself from sin by gravity of conduct. Thus she searches out and rejects every childish thing in evils, has no wantonness in herself, and appears like a mother in the midst of those virtues which signify the glory of the Trinity at the beginning of the law given to the ancient people. Upon her head she has, in the manner of a crown, a circle of saffron color engraved on the right side, ever kindled, because she is crowned by the supreme [Col. 0636C] Head with the saffron ray of the most splendid sun, namely the Son of God, in whose brightness she is wholly enclosed, desiring none but him, who also ever kindles her in the right-hand part of the soul’s salvation.

Therefore, as you see, a dove flies toward the right of this figure, breathing with its beak into that Scripture. This means that on the right hand of heavenly prosperity there is present the gift of true simplicity, namely the Holy Spirit, kindling in abstinence every good thing through heavenly inspiration for the salvation of souls, as that virtue itself also shows in the aforementioned words of its exhortation.

The other figure on her right signifies generosity, possessing childlike simplicity and having no craftiness or hardness at all toward human sufferings. With it abstinence always withdraws from every harshness in the right hand of good works, thus stretching toward God, because generosity is the beginning of its activity when abstinence first undertakes its work. Upon her breast she has something like a lion, like a shining mirror: in her heart is my Son, Christ Jesus, the mightiest lion, enclosed as a mirror of loving and splendid charity. But the fact that from her neck she bears something like a pale serpent, hanging down upon that same breast in the twisted bend of a rod, means that my most prudent Son endured, as though in the strongest neck—that is, patience—the bending of punishments in the pallor of afflicted flesh, together with the lifting up of the cross, the remedy of all wounds. [Col. 0637A] Generosity imprints this upon its breast through heavenly love, frequently beholding it in human minds, as it also declares in the aforesaid words of its exhortation.

The third figure, at her left, reveals piety, which has in no way hatred, envy, or any human foulness, but always rejoices in and embraces the prosperity of all people. By its freshness and the anointing of generosity, abstinence resists the left-hand side of diabolical suggestion, because piety is the complete work of abstinence in the banner-bearing battle through which it is always victorious. Therefore she is clothed in a tunic resembling red hyacinth, because she is encompassed by the most splendid work under which, with most beautiful endurance, bloody adversities lie hidden: namely, the bearing of all injuries after the passion of my Son, through his example.

But the fact that at her breast an angel appears, having one wing on each side, means that a human being should always imitate the angelic order in his understanding, loving every ordering of God. From both sides—both prosperous and adverse circumstances—he raises himself to flight by the individual and paired wings, that is, in the one God through a twofold virtue: neither lifted beyond measure in good things nor wholly cast down in evils. To fly is to behold God in purity of heart, thus tending upward and not throwing oneself down to earth. Therefore the right wing extends toward the right shoulder of that figure, because human prosperity is offered on the right hand of the salvation [Col. 0637C] of souls as an aid to piety, when my Son brought humankind back to its homeland. And the left wing extends toward her left shoulder, because, on the left hand of the adversity of diabolical snares, the faithful person stretches upward toward the refuge of my Son the wing by which he casts off works of darkness. Through him he is strong against every adversity, imitating the life of the righteous, as this virtue likewise declares in its words, as has been shown above.

The figure in the middle of the lower three also represents truth. For after abstinence and the virtues joined to it, truth arises in all matters, standing with the figures beside it as their tower and defense—that is, signifying a strong protection—as though in the middle of the virtues prefiguring the holy Trinity at the setting of Jewish observance and the dawning of the true faith. Upon her right shoulder a most white dove stands, breathing with its beak into her right ear. This means that, in the higher part of the right hand—that is, the blessed restoration to life through the incarnation of the Son of God—there appears the wondrous virtue of the Holy Spirit, which breathed by its touch into the right hearing, that is, into the hearts of believing people, so that they might understand what God is in his divine power.

But the fact that a monstrous and shapeless human head appears on her breast means that God permits the miseries and persecutions of rulers to exist in the hearts of his elect, just as his Son [Col. 0638A] also chose to suffer at the hands of the chief priests. And since God is in the heart of the faithful person, that person too ought for God’s love patiently to bear persecution for God. And because death was raised up in the fall of the devil, the faithful person must endure many struggles against diabolical wickedness in various afflictions, which are often burdensome and hostile to his body, because it clings to humankind and that ancient serpent always persecutes it. What is this? The desire of the flesh, which that wicked enemy, set in ambush, lies in wait to attack.

But the fact that beneath her feet lie forms like human beings trampled and crushed by her means that beneath the footsteps of truth all diabolical falsehoods enacted in human works are reduced [Col. 0638B] to nothing. For truth has love for the building up of the Church, and all virtues appear and are tested openly in truth. Truth lay hidden and invisible in the heart of the Father before the ages of the world, but appeared visibly at the end of times in the true flesh of the Son of God.

Thus she has in her hands a scroll spread out, inscribed on one side—that is, toward heaven—with seven lines. This means that in every work of truth there is an unfolded fabric of law, established for the Christian people through God’s grace, to be maintained by open worship on the side of heavenly desires and feared on the side of fleshly desires. It displays within itself the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, namely an unconquerable defense against the diabolical snares of death. And you wish to read it but cannot, because, although a human being greatly desires to know the mysteries and secrets in God’s gifts, while burdened by a mortal body it is not possible for him to understand or grasp what God wishes to bring about in his wonders. Yet let that person embrace and comprehend these things in truth, namely by following God’s commands, as this same virtue also shows in its aforesaid words.

The other figure on her right [Col. 0638C] signifies peace, having a heavenly sign and angelic companionship, because in full freshness it brings forth truth. For that same truth, surrounded by outstanding heavenly gifts on the right hand of the salvation of souls, possesses peace through the Son of God. How? As it is written in the angelic song: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will” (Luke 2). Its meaning is this: in the highest God, humanity shines, and God shines in humanity, because the Son of God was wondrously incarnate. Therefore God is praiseworthy and glorious in heaven, by every creature of his. Hence on earth the peace of salvation comes to those people who receive the Father’s will with devotion and faith. For the peace of good will is the will of the Father’s entire goodness, which is his Son, who is God and human.

And how is he peace? He is the peace of human beings, defending them from the snares of the ancient serpent, the first transgressor, who lost the light of life when he was cast down into darkness. That light true peace—that is, the true Son of God—brought to human beings, so that they became sharers in the kingdom of God in the blessed place which the devil lost. And, as you see, the aforesaid virtue has an angelic face, because it flees from every evil with holy intention, as though beholding God in its face with angelic desire. It also has one flying wing on either side, because in both conditions, tranquil and turbulent, it tends upward toward God, producing neither terror nor bitterness, but always remaining in gentle prosperity. It embraces the one God in the unanimity of two wings, because it is overthrown by no storm of instability either in good or in evil, but persists only in tranquility. And it appears in human form like the other virtues, because [Col. 0639B] it shone wonderfully through the Son of God, while all virtues are also proved among human beings through it. Thus it seeks contention or quarrelling in no way, but always opposes itself to the diabolical struggle in gentleness, as is also made plain above in the words of its discourse.

But the third figure standing to her left signifies blessedness, desiring eternal life. By its faithfulness and inward gentleness, truth contradicts the person who consents to every deceptive persuasion of the serpent from the left side, because blessedness is the invincible security of true brightness, in which it does not fear the unhappiness of death. Therefore it is clothed in a white tunic marked with green, because it is surrounded by faithful works whitening in heavenly desire and adorned with manifold gifts flourishing in the freshness of the Holy Spirit.

But the small vessel of pale brightness which it holds in its hands means that, in its work, it shows how a human being may apprehend God through faith in a small receptacle—that is, in the contrite secret of the heart—yet amid the pallor of frail human flesh, because faith must be cultivated purely even in this mortal life, so that human misery does not abandon it. Thus it sends out much light like lightning, so that the light shines upon the face and around the neck of this figure. This means that knowledge of eternal light is spread abroad in the fear and love of God, extending from [Col. 0639D] the inward heart of the human being to the face—that is, to the beginning of a right work, making its intention manifest in a good example—and around the neck, which afterward prudently encompasses strength in every place in the completed work. Then, through blessedness, that work shines before God in the person more brightly than the sun, as is also declared in the aforesaid manifestation of that same virgin.

The figure sitting upon the stone at the end of the wall signifies discernment, because, resting in Christ at the consummation of the ancient observance, it appeared in its fullness as the most careful sifter of all things, retaining what ought to be retained and cutting off what ought to be cut off, so that wheat may be separated from tares. It is clothed in a darkish tunic [Col. 0640A], because it is surrounded by mortification of the flesh, rejecting the frivolity of every vanity.

But the fact that upon its right shoulder it bears a small cross carrying an image of Jesus Christ means that this virtue set its root in the right-hand part of the strength of God’s power, when almighty God sent his Son to be wondrously incarnate and humbly to suffer. Discernment is joined to his love, because it was manifested through him, so that through it all justice may be distinguished. And as God is the dispenser of the fitting stature of a human being, so discernment is his imitator in its office, fulfilling its works in the crucified Son of God, the dispenser, who is in both dignities, namely divinity and humanity. It moves this way and that because, in its grasp of breadth through the signification of the holy cross, it has a circuit among good and evil.

But the fact that a splendor of wondrous brightness seems to shine from clouds into its breast means that from God’s mercy, as from a most shining cloud, the kindling of divine piety is breathed into human minds, producing discernment in them and illuminating them. Therefore it is divided from itself into many rays, just as the sun’s brightness is divided from itself when it shines through small and numerous openings in some object. This means that the Holy Spirit, in heavenly power dividing various rays of his gifts among human beings, pours them forth—brighter than the sun and ineffably discerning—into humble caverns, that is, into the penetrating vision of the souls of his faithful, illuminating their senses and minds, so that [Col. 0640C] they may understand most keenly, in every matter, what they ought fittingly to do in God.

But the small piece of wood which it holds in its right hand in the form of a fan means that discernment, on the right hand of the salvation of souls, always considers its work through the gift of the Holy Spirit in human beings, as in the wood of fragile flesh. Yet it bears this sign in itself, so that, through divine aid, it may drive away from itself the various flies—that is, diabolical persuasions—lest it be scattered by them into diverse vanities. Therefore from its top three little branches wonderfully sprout with flowers, so that faithful people may faithfully believe, above all and in all things, in the holy Trinity ever flowering in its wonders, reigning in the unity of most glorious divinity. They must not rashly investigate heavenly secrets within themselves; but as God justly and discerningly orders all his works among his diverse creatures, so they too, through the power of discernment, should dispense all their deeds well and rightly.

But the fact that it has in its lap tiny stones of every kind of gem, which it examines with much care and diligence as a merchant customarily examines his goods closely, means that in the bosom of human minds it holds everything that is fitting and suitable in their smallest counsels and arts. It carefully and diligently searches out every justice established by God, as though among gems of virtue, so that it may proceed suitably and justly in all things [Col. 0641A] in human hearts, most keenly considering, for the reward of work, where recompense lies in God, as it also proclaims in its words, as has been shown before.

The figure standing at the end upon the wall signifies the salvation of souls, because it shone forth at the decline of the old severity, at the summit of the authority of the new grace. Thus discernment is, as it were, its foundation, with and upon which that salvation of souls appears, arising in the Son of God when he was born of the Virgin for the salvation of humankind. It has an uncovered head and black, curly hair, because it is bare of servitude, remaining in free dignity, since it openly adheres to the Son of God, by whom it has also been mercifully raised up. Yet it bears the blackness of its hair, because in the Jewish people it appeared obscured, lacking true brightness but possessing manifold diversity, like the curly hair of various observances. Its face too is dark, because before the incarnation of the Son of God it was not seen, in the shadow of death, to retain the blessedness of eternal salvation.

It is clothed in a varied tunic woven with many colors, because among the ancient people it was surrounded in many ways by a variety of works mingled with the diversity of many vices. But the fact that you see it standing naked as it puts off its tunic and shoes means that in the passion of my Son, when death had been wiped away, and also after the sound and words of the apostles went forth into the world at the coming of the Holy Spirit, it was awakened in the salvation of souls. Thus, despising evil works and casting away contrary footsteps, it was stripped and strongly denuded of diabolical dominion within itself, saying: “O most shameful devil, you would never have left me if I had not been redeemed in the blood of the Lamb. For you wished to keep me in the pit of hell, but now I have been set free by the grace of God.”

And so its hair and face shine with the beauty of whiteness and newness, as those of a newly born infant. For after the incarnation of my Son a great people grew in the figure of his crimes [Col. 0642A], well illuminated in the inner face of the soul, adhering to true and splendid justice. Thus it sought eternal blessedness, trusting in the whiteness of life and in the liberation of faithful members adhering to Christ their head through new regeneration, and through the true innocence of childhood, saving in heavenly life. Its whole body shines, as a pure and radiant splendor shines into brightness, because through all its members—that is, through the faithful people made subject to it through my Son—it has become pure, clear in dove-like simplicity and in the most radiant beauty of God’s justice.

But the fact that on its breast you see a most splendid cross with an image of Christ Jesus, set upon a little tree between two flowers, lily and rose, which bend somewhat upward toward that same cross, means that this virtue became the strong heart of believing peoples in the passion of Jesus the Savior. By his martyrdom, in the footsteps of his good and upright example, he pressed down and crushed the tree of Adam’s death and perdition. Against it, too, the two Testaments—namely the Old in whiteness and the New in redness—proceeded by God’s ordering, opposing it and bending upward, in the height of spiritual understanding, toward the passion of that same kindly and most noble Redeemer and toward all his justice, away from the perdition of death.

Thus you also see it strongly shake out its discarded tunic and shoes, so that much dust is shaken from them. This means that the salvation of souls displays in the new and righteous works of human beings the tunic of former habit [Col. 0642C] and of all the vices of old sins, removed; and the evil example of Adam’s transgression cast away. It vigorously examines and despises these, and casts from itself the dust of vainglory and of other sins, as it also acknowledges above concerning itself in its prologue.

Whoever has keen ears of inward understanding, let that person pant in the burning love of my mirror toward these words, and write them in the conscience of the mind.

## SEVENTH VISION

[Col. 0641]

### SUMMARY

That the ineffable Trinity, revealed at the end of times, must be believed and worshipped by the faithful with a simple and humble heart, lest anyone, investigating more than is proper because it cannot be comprehended, fall into something worse. That the world was saved in the blood of Christ and the worship of the holy Trinity was declared most manifestly; yet it lies open to the understanding of no one. That the ineffable Trinity appears with the clearest command and power to every creature, except unbelieving hearts, yet penetrates all things like a cutting sword. That divinity cuts down in confusion those who, among the Christian people of the Catholic faith, oppose it in the dryness of unbelief. That divinity casts down the boasting of the Jewish people. That the diabolical schism of the Gentile people, cut off from God, goes to perdition. A parable concerning the same matter. Words of John concerning the same matter. On the distinction and unity of the three persons. On three likenesses of the Trinity. Words from the Book of Kings concerning the same matter.

[Col. 0641D] Then I saw in the western corner of the building shown to me a wondrous, hidden, and most mighty column, having the color of purplish blackness. It was so set upon that corner that it appeared both within and outside the building. It was also of such size that neither its size nor its height [Col. 0642D] was accessible to my understanding; yet it was in a wondrous manner utterly smooth, without any wrinkle. On its outer side it had three steel-colored edges, from its foot to its summit, cutting like a keenest sword. One faced Africa, where a great quantity of rotten straw had been cut down and scattered by it; another faced the northwest, where many little feathers, torn apart by it, had fallen; and the middle one faced the west, where very much rotten timber, cut down by it, lay. Each of these things had been cut down by those same edges because of their rashness.

And again he whom I beheld seated upon the aforesaid throne, and who showed me all these things, said to me: “These mystical, wondrous, and utterly unknown gifts, which appear to you, O most bright human being, in the true light, I show you and grant you to speak and reveal, in order to kindle the fiery hearts of the faithful, who are the purest stones for the building of the heavenly Jerusalem.”

For the holy and ineffable Trinity, of supreme unity, was hidden from those serving beneath the yoke of the Law, but revealed in the new [Col. 0643B] grace to those freed from servitude. With a simple and humble heart, the faithful must believe that God is one and true in three persons; they must not rashly investigate him, lest one who is unwilling to be content with the gift received from the Holy Spirit, while seeking more than is fitting through the rashness of his own pride, fall rather into worse things than find what he improperly desires. The present vision also shows this.

For this column which you see in the western corner of the building shown to you is a figure of the true Trinity: because the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit are one God in Trinity, and that same Trinity exists in unity—a perfect column of every good, penetrating things highest and lowest and governing the whole world. It appears in the western region because the Son [Col. 0643C] of God, incarnate in time as if at sunset, glorified his Father everywhere and promised the Holy Spirit to his disciples. This same Son, by undergoing death in the will of the Father, fulfilled goodness for humankind, so that they too may walk uprightly in the building of the supreme Father, accomplishing true and just works in the Holy Spirit.

But it shows itself wonderful, secret, and exceedingly strong, because God is so wonderful in his creatures that he can by no means be brought to an end by them; so secret that he is not to be obstinately examined by any knowledge or perception of theirs; and so strong that all their strength is directed by him and cannot be compared with his strength.

That it has the color of purple-blackness, and is so set upon that same corner that it appears both within and outside the building, means this: in the will of the Father, his only Son shed his purple blood for the blackness of human sins, and thus by his Passion saved the world and brought true and right faith to believers. For at the passing away of the old observance and the rising of the new sanctification, the worship of the holy Trinity was declared most openly, when it was plainly believed that the heavenly Father sent his Son into the world, conceived of the Holy Spirit—who sought the Father’s glory and not his own, and disclosed the profound consolation of the Holy Spirit—as has been said. Thus this lay hidden in no respect, but was proclaimed both to the faithful who remain in God’s work [Col. 0644A] and to unbelievers set outside the faith.

That it is of such extent that neither its greatness nor its height can be understood by you means that this same Trinity is of such ineffable glory and power that it cannot be bounded, either in the greatness of its majesty or in the height of its divinity, by any circuit or presumption of the wisdom of the human mind. And in a wonderful manner it is utterly smooth, without any wrinkle, because—what is most worthy of wonder—it is most gentle in grace, and always kind and level in the sweetness of justice toward those who come to it, so that no roughness of any injustice is found in it, since it is just and good in the work of salvation.

That it has, on its outer side, three corners of steely color, cutting from its foot to its summit [Col. 0644B] like a sharpest sword, means that, with the opposition of darkness set against it throughout the world, the ineffable Trinity in the unity of divinity appears most openly. It lies hidden from no creature by its rule and power, except unbelieving hearts, from whom it is concealed because of their unbelief. Therefore God’s judgment, with deserved recompense, slays them as they deserve—like strongest steel, yielding to no burning but resisting it. Hence it stretches from highest point to highest point: namely, from the beginning of the world’s creation to its end; and beyond this, in its sharpest divinity, like a cutting sword, it has always penetrated and penetrates powerfully by wisdom and power.

That one corner looks toward the southwest, where [Col. 0644C] much dry straw has been cut away and scattered by it, means that the most righteous divinity of the Trinity cuts down and burns, among the Christian people, every dryness of diversity, contradiction, and rejection that opposes the most upright catholic faith, in its greatest confusion—like hay trampled underfoot and burned in fire, separated from the fruitful grain of wheat. This grain is faith with works in the knowledge of Scripture; and from it everything contrary and useless to that true faith in its belief is scattered and removed, because the foolish people misuse such things like senseless cattle.

And another directs itself toward the northwest wind, where many little feathers, torn apart by it, fall, because that same divinity cast down the proud boasting of the Jewish people. In great arrogance they flew aloft in the height of [Col. 0644D] their own minds, since they wished to be righteous in themselves and not in God—as the Pharisees, who attempted to climb to the heights of heaven, trusting in themselves according to their own confidence. But, by God’s just judgment, they were torn apart on account of the diversity of their conduct and fell in this presumption.

The middle one looks toward the west, where very many rotten logs, thrown down by it, lie scattered. For through the Trinity is cut off the impious and diabolical schism of the Gentile people, who wander at the sunset of unbelief away from the right faith. For just as rotten timber is troublesome and useless for human purposes, so this people is cut off and cast away from the joy of life, pursuing diabolical fabrications rather than divine commands.

[Col. 0645A] Therefore each of these things was cut off by those same corners because of their rashness: in all the causes mentioned above, the true and holy Trinity permits unbelievers—whether they presumptuously wish to tear it apart or obstinately refuse to believe it—to go away from it, cut off into perdition. For they madly and ignorantly assault divinity, refusing to submit to the faith which the Son of God brought in his own person and also transmitted to humankind through his disciples, as this parable says:

A certain lord, possessing a fiery stone, wished through it and through his messengers to entrust a necessary matter to a great multitude of people. But the messengers were not wise or capable of understanding the words of their lord; rather, they were foolish and ignorant in carrying out that command. Meanwhile [Col. 0645B] there arose a tumult, a great storm, a torrent, and a fierce thunderclap, so that the earth was shaken and stones were split. Likewise, a single vessel, lying hidden in the earth, in which very many small vessels were contained, with its back turned toward heaven, was uprooted from the earth with great force, and its womb was turned toward heaven.

Then from that lord, through the stone itself, a most violent blast of fire came, which passed through those messengers with such burning that all their veins grew warm. Every sluggishness of fear was shaken from them with such speed as something poured upon dry skin falls from it most swiftly. At last they remembered everything which they had heard and learned from their lord. They went to [Col. 0645C] a people who had no navels and whose city had been destroyed, and they announced to them their lord’s command. To some of them they restored navels, and, rebuilding their city, returned it to them. But to others they restored neither navels nor city; rather, killing them, they divided them like swine. Thus that stone became known to the whole world, shaking and destroying all false deeds of human flesh.

This means the following. That lord is the almighty Father, with whom is his Only-Begotten Son: namely, that cornerstone conceived from the fiery Holy Spirit and born as a human being from the most inviolate Virgin—indeed, the whitest and most beautiful flower, existing in the whiteness and beauty of all holiness.

For the Son of God was, according to [Col. 0645D] divinity, ineffably before the age of every creature, with the Father and with the fiery Comforter; then, at the appointed time, he was sent by the Father so that, conceived of the Holy Spirit, he might truly be incarnated and born of the Virgin, as has been said, in order to confer upon believers the brightness and beauty of life. When he was incarnate, the heavenly Father graciously announced through him and through his disciples a necessary matter: namely, salvation and deliverance for those who believe in him.

But while that same Son remained bodily with them in the world, his disciples were foolish, ignorant, and dull; slow to understand his words watchfully in the Spirit and to fulfill them in work. They heard them only as if asleep, in simplicity—not yet strengthened, but fearful and terrified like human beings.

Meanwhile came the time of deranged hearts, so that the Jews, making a tumult, sought to stir up many schisms against the Son of God in order to kill him in this great storm. And while they fulfilled all their malice as they desired, then in this sudden and great thunderclap there was perpetrated a homicide so great as none had been before and none would be afterward: so that the earth was shaken—that is, earthly human minds were terrified along with the rest of creation—and so that the stony law of the Jews was split apart in their criminal deed.

Then the first human being, with his race—within whom lay hidden the sign of the remaining creation—lay buried in death, having turned all his intention toward earthly things and having heaven at his back, unwilling to look toward [Col. 0646B] God. He was uprooted by the great power of the Son of God from the earth of death, in which he sleeps with his children, so that, sighing from his whole heart, he turned all his knowledge, as if in a womb, toward the heavenly homeland, because he heard that Christ, the Son of God, had been killed for his sake.

But after the ascension of that same Son of God, the Holy Spirit came from the Father and through the Son, as he had promised. For the whole earth dripped with heavenly sweetness, because heavenly bread had remained in the world: the unbelievers had neglected it fleetingly, as though amid a rumor, but the faithful had received it with all devotion. Therefore, because the Word had been incarnate, the Holy Spirit openly appeared in fiery tongues, since the Son who converted the world to truth by his preaching was conceived of the Holy Spirit.

[Col. 0646C] And because the apostles had been taught through that same Son, the Holy Spirit flooded them with such warmth that they spoke in different tongues in soul and body, for in them the soul ruled the body. They cried out in such a way that the whole world was shaken by their voices.

The same Holy Spirit also took human fear away from them. Thus no such terror remained in them that they would fear human cruelty and fail to speak the word of God. Rather, all such timidity was taken from them with such burning and haste that they became, as it were, dry and no longer soft, but dead to every adversity that might happen to them. Therefore, their understanding having immediately been made perfect, they remembered [Col. 0646D] everything that formerly, slow in faith, they had heedlessly heard and received from Christ. They brought it back to mind as though they had learned it from him at that very hour.

Setting out, they travelled among unbelieving peoples who had no navels—that is, no seal, namely, no knowledge of holy innocence and justice—and whose city, namely the instruments of God’s law, had been destroyed in unbelief. To them they proclaimed words of salvation and true faith in Christ. Thus they brought many from that multitude back to the knowledge of God, leading them to the navel—that is, to the font of baptism—in which they received the holiness lost by proud transgression. They raised up for them the holy city of God’s commandments, rebuilding it, of which the plotting devil had robbed them in Adam [Col. 0647A]; and they restored it to them in faith for salvation.

But those who, because of their unbelief, would not receive the faith of baptism and the protection of God’s command, they passed over in the public proclamation of signs and, condemning them for the hardness and unbelief within them, handed them over to death. For, entangling themselves in their crimes, in the filth of fleshly defilements, and in the allurements of their fornications and adulteries—as a pig wallows in mud—they refused to be converted to the true faith; hence they were divided and separated from life.

Thus the Son of God was manifested by many wonderful signs throughout the whole world: that, according to divinity, he was ineffably begotten from the Father before times, and that later, according to humanity, he was wonderfully incarnate from the Virgin. Thus the hearts of all hearing these things were shaken with great dread and trembling, and the empty and deceitful works which they had done according to their pleasures were reduced to nothing in them through contempt of death, while the true Word of God bore witness to the holy Trinity and to life-giving salvation, which comes through the water of regeneration and restores to life.

As beloved John shows in his exhortatory words, saying: “And the Spirit is he who testifies, because Christ is truth. For there are three who give testimony on earth: spirit, water, and blood; and the three are one. And there are three who give testimony in heaven: Father, Word, and Spirit; and the three are one” (1 John 5).

This means the following. The spirit of a spiritual human being does not proceed from blood or arise from [Col. 0647C] flesh, but runs from God’s hidden place, being invisible to that which is subject to change. Therefore its testimony concerns the Son of God, whose glory is wonderful in the mystical breathing, which no human being can perfectly understand—namely, how that same Only-Begotten of God was received from the Holy Spirit and came into this world. Nor can any human being fully know how the soul passes through the human body and blood, so that they possess one life.

And just as the human spirit, in the surest ground of the knowledge given it by God, passes through everything granted to it by God, because it is not a false and deceptive life but a true and faithful one, so Christ is perfect truth, in which life rose [Col. 0647D] again and the light of salvation shone forth, while death fell away from it because death is deceitful.

And three things signifying the holy Trinity give testimony on earth: they show and confer in the present age the remedy of life-giving salvation, through which one must come to the heavenly things that endure without end—things not yet possessed in the actuality of immortality, but awaited in hope.

For the human spirit has from me testimony within itself that it is not in the full life of salvation’s restoration unless it rises again for me in the water of regeneration, because it failed in that light which shines in me, having been expelled from blessedness through the corrupted conception of sin that grows in blood. Water has that testimony: that it cleanses every filthy thing within itself, and that the deadly destruction of death perishes in it through the purest cleansing. Here it is joined to the spirit before the blood; for as the spirit is spiritual, so water brings spiritual sanctification. Placed between spirit and blood, it strengthens both soul and body through spiritual generation and conveys them to life.

[Col. 0648A] Blood also has this testimony: that it turns back its poisonous paths toward the house of sanctification through the water of salvation, which is the healing power beginning in my Son and enduring in him unto life. For blood contains very guilty sins and a great unrest of injustice, running through wandering paths in twisting sweetness that serves burning lust and chokes innocence by horrible vices. It began to grow through the act of eating at the suggestion of the plotting devil.

And these three are one, because the spirit is not a living human being without the bloodly substance of the body; nor is the bloodly substance of the body a living human being without the soul; nor are these two restored in the grace of the new Law to life except through the water of regeneration. Thus they are one in redemption, and they are not whole in salvation so long as they are separated from this saving water, because rationality lacks the surpassing honor of life, in which redeemed humanity must always resound perfect praise before God, who gave it rationality.

For God by his own will created the human being for that honor which is fulfilled in the body of his Son in eternal life, when the lost human being, redeemed in God by saving grace, revives in the honor of life.

[Col. 0648C] The spirit, invisible to bodily eyes, signifies the Father, beyond estimation by every creature; the water, which cleanses filth, signifies the Word—that is, the Son—who by his Passion wipes away human stains; and the blood, which embraces and warms the human being, represents the Holy Spirit, who raises up and kindles the most radiant virtues in human beings. Thus these three—spirit, water, and blood—are in one, and one is in three; and they are one in salvation, as has been said. They display Trinity in unity and unity in Trinity.

How? The holy and heavenly Trinity gives heavenly testimony: testimony not received from another, but manifested in itself by certain faith.

How? The Father testifies that his only fruitful Word, whom he begot before the ages and through whom all things were created, afterward flowered most gloriously in the Virgin at the predestined time. The Word testifies that he came forth from the Father, bowing himself toward human nature—namely, incarnate in the chastity of virginity. For he came forth from the Father in a spiritual going forth and returned again to the Father in the fruitfulness of flesh, being set here in the middle: invisibly begotten from the Father before times, and bodily conceived of the Holy Spirit in the Virgin’s womb in time.

[Col. 0648D] The Holy Spirit testifies that he kindled the Virgin’s integrity, so that she conceived the Word of God; and that he confirmed the teaching of that Word in fiery tongues when he so flooded the apostles that throughout the whole world [Col. 0649A] they cried aloud the true Trinity.

How? They proclaimed that God the Father fulfilled what he had created: the human being for heavenly blessedness, of which humanity had been despoiled. For humanity was made from the clay of the earth in an upward erectness, but by its own will bent itself downward to the earth. Now, through grace, it has been raised upward again through the incarnate Son of God, illumined and strengthened through the Holy Spirit so that it should not perish in destruction, but should be restored in redemption to eternal brightness.

Thus Father, Son, and Holy Spirit testify that they are not at all divided in power, although they are distinguished in persons, because they work together in the unity of a simple and unchangeable substance.

How? The Father creates all things through the Word—that is, through his Son—in the Holy Spirit; the Son, through whom all things are completed, works in the Father and the Holy Spirit; and the Holy Spirit, through whom all things flourish, works in the Father and the Son. These three persons are so united in inseparable substance that they are not mutually confused with one another.

How? For he who begot is Father; he who was born is Son; and he who proceeds from Father and Son in most ardent greenness, who appeared in the form of an innocent bird over the waters and sanctified them, and flooded the apostles with fiery ardor, is the Holy Spirit. For before the ages of the world the Father possessed the Son; and the Son was with the Father, while the Holy Spirit was eternally coeternal with Father and Son in the unity of divinity.

[Col. 0649C] Hence it must be considered that, if two or even one of these three persons were absent, God would not be in his fullness.

How? Because they are one unity of divinity; if any one of them were absent, God would not be. For although these persons are thus distinct, nevertheless they are one whole, unchangeable substance of immeasurable beauty, abiding in undivided unity.

How? Power, will, ardor: these three points are on the one summit of operation.

How? In power is will, in will is ardor, and they are inseparable, as is the breath of a human being in its issuing forth.

How? The wind, moving with moisture and heat, is an indivisible emission in human breathing, as is your eye in its integrity.

How? The circle of your eye has two transparent parts [Col. 0649D] within itself, yet is one dwelling, governing all things appointed to it.

Hear and understand, O human being. Thus three persons exist in the one unchangeable essence of divinity: the Son in the Father, the Holy Spirit in both; they are one and cooperate inseparably. For the Father does not act without the Son, nor the Son without the Holy Spirit, nor the Holy Spirit without them; neither Father nor Son acts without the Holy Spirit, for they are undivided unity.

Thus God is in three persons without beginning, before the age; before the world’s beginning, the assumption of flesh in the Son had not yet been accomplished, until the preordained time came, when “God sent his Son” in the fullness of that time. Yet when that same Son was incarnate, God remained the same in three persons and willed to be invoked in this way. When that virgin flower [Col. 0650A] blossomed in the integrity of virginity, no person was added thereby to the ineffable Trinity; rather, the Son of God alone put on flesh, assumed without violation.

Therefore these three persons are one God in divinity. Whoever does not believe thus shall be cut off from God’s kingdom, because he divides the integrity of divinity and himself in faith, as it is written: “On the third day a man appeared, coming from Saul’s camp, his garment torn and dust sprinkled upon his head” (2 Kings 1).

This means the following. On that day when the catholic faith arose in the manifestation of the holy Trinity, people sprang up in great schism, coming from the army of the death-dealing cohort, perversely examining what it is impossible for a human being to know. Incarnate through many persuasions of diabolical art, they pretend to ascend above that height, wishing to know more than they ought to know concerning incomprehensible divinity. Therefore they are torn away from the garment of salvation and justice, because they are opposed to God; they are defiled by the diversity of their scattering, having no whole faith in the head of faith, but scattering the one honor of divinity into many sects and diminishing their higher honor in the mockery of schism.

All these will be judged by God, as follows: “David said to the young man who had brought him the news, ‘Where are you from?’ He answered, ‘I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite.’ David said to him, ‘Why were you not afraid to put forth your hand to kill the Lord’s anointed?’ Then David called one of his servants and said, ‘Come near; fall upon him.’ And he struck him, and he died. David said to him, ‘Your blood be upon your head; for your own mouth has spoken against you, saying, “I have killed the Lord’s anointed”’” (ibid.).

[Col. 0650C] This means the following. That victorious one, incomprehensible to every creature, speaks to the childish ignorance which is in the human being—to that childishness, namely, which exalts itself and wishes to know what ought not to be known. In its folly it assaults God, as if rashly announcing to him, “I know you well, Lord.” Thus he answers it: “Whence are you, who have a beginning, that you wish to know wholly that which lacks beginning?”

And folly, which arose in humanity and has a beginning, answers as if in its knowledge: “I am the son of a human being who is an alien, coming here [Col. 0650D] from this accursed land; for the first human being, falling through tasting the fruit, made the journey into this exile from his homeland, and I am his offspring.”

Then God says to him: “Since you are a human being from an accursed land, driven from your homeland as an exile, why were you not afraid, with such presumption, to investigate what you should not know—stifling your work so that it is in no way useful in the light of hope, and touching within it the evil of homicide? For whoever rashly investigates what God did before the world’s creation, or what God will do after the last day, let that person be anathematized from a share in blessed communion. For this is not to be known by one who has a mortal beginning, burdened with sins. Rather, he shall be deprived of the happy salvation of good knowledge, because he obstinately investigated what he ought not [Col. 0651A] to investigate.

“Therefore you, who do these things presumptuously and cruelly by killing, kill within yourself the blessed understanding of royal prophecy; for your soul ought to provide itself pure knowledge, namely faithfully in that fitting simplicity, and to believe in God.”

Then God commands through the zeal of his most pure justice, which has no stain of iniquity, calling him by the most upright unity of his judgments: “Hasten, and crush him away from the good knowledge he possessed, so that he may rest in no happiness of his understanding, because he gave me no rest in my heart.”

Thus the stroke of the Lord’s zeal strikes him, so that not even the smallest spark of any eye remains to him for seeing—that is, knowing—God. Thus he dies to the life-giving consolation of justice, unable to govern himself.

Then God says to him: “May your bloody crime, by which [Col. 0652A] you raise yourself to those heights which you cannot behold, be upon your soul. The evil by which you unjustly rise against me shall trample you down into a low place, from which you cannot raise yourself to the right measure of faith’s proposition; for you refused to walk in right footsteps, but sought a great schism in your own understanding. Let your mouth be left without words of wisdom, for it has spoken against your salvation, when you deceitfully investigated secret and incomprehensible divinity, presuming to know what is not to be known and rashly saying within yourself, ‘I know well what God is.’ By this rashness you killed your inward salvation, when you refused to believe in God cautiously, but proudly raised yourself against him.”

But whoever has the keen ears of inward understanding, let that person pant after these words in the burning love of my mirror and write them in the conscience of his soul.

## EIGHTH VISION

[Col. 0651]

**SUMMARY.**—Words of humility. Words of charity. Words of fear. Words of obedience. Words of faith. Words of hope. Words of chastity. Words of God’s grace for the admonition of humankind. That the humanity of the Savior, sustaining the edifice of the Church, appears in the faith of peoples who work faithfully.
