“And as he attempted to oppose divinity at his first origin, so also his imitator Antichrist will attempt, in the last time, to resist the Lord’s incarnation. Lucifer fell at the beginning of time, and Antichrist will fall at its end. Then it will be known who is the true God, and it will be seen who is he who never fell. As Lucifer had demons as followers, who followed him from heaven’s height into the fall of damnation, so even now he has people on earth who follow him unto destruction [Col. 0677B] and perdition. But we virtues have been appointed against his wiles and his exhalations, which he sends out to swallow souls, so that through us all his arts may be reduced to nothing in the souls of the righteous, and he may appear confounded on every side. Thus God will be known through us, because he ought not to be hidden but made manifest, since he is righteous in all things.”

The first of the figures standing beside this one appeared armed: clad in helmet, breastplate, greaves, and iron gloves; holding a drawn sword in her right hand and a spear in her left. Trampling beneath her feet a horrible dragon, she pierced its mouth through with the iron of her spear, so that it vomited forth most foul foam. And she vigorously brandished, as if to strike, the sword she held.

And she said:

“O most mighty God, who can withstand and oppose you? The ancient serpent, that dragon the devil, cannot do so. Therefore, with your help, I wish to oppose him, so that no one may prevail against me or cast me down—neither strong nor weak, neither ruler nor lowly person, neither noble nor ignoble, neither rich nor poor. I wish to be like the strongest steel, making all weapons fitted for God’s battles utterly invincible; in them I am the sharpest edge, because no one will be able to break through you, most mighty God, through whom I also rose up to cast out the devil. Therefore I shall always be the surest refuge for human frailty, giving their weakness a cutting sword with which to defend itself. O most compassionate [Col. 0677D] and merciful God, help those contrite in heart.”

The other figure appeared three-headed: a head appeared in the natural place of the head and one upon each shoulder, though the middle head rose somewhat above the other two. The middle head and the one at its right shone with such brilliance that their brightness struck back my sight, so that I could not perfectly discern whether they had a male or female form. But the one at the left appeared somewhat dark and, in feminine fashion, veiled with a white covering.

The figure was clothed in a tunic of white silk and most white shoes. It bore upon its breast the sign of the cross, about which a great brightness shone ruddy upon its breast, like a gleaming dawn. In its right hand it wielded a bare sword, which it pressed to its breast and to the cross with great devotion. And I saw inscribed on the forehead of the middle head, “Holiness”; on that of the right head, “Root of goodness”; and on that of the left head, “Not sparing itself.”

And the middle head, looking at the other two, said:

“I was first born of holy humility within her, as an infant is born in its mother. Through her I was also reared and strengthened, as a child is nourished to strength by a nurse. My mother Humility conquers and overcomes all opposing things, which are intolerable even to others.”

And the head at her right, looking toward the principal head, said:

“At my first rising I take root on the mountain of the lofty summit, which is God. Therefore, O Holiness, in order that you may stand, it is necessary [Col. 0678B] that I cling to your inner parts.”

But the one standing at her left, likewise looking toward its own principal head, said:

“O woe, woe, woe! How rigid and inflexible I am, so that I can overcome myself only with such difficulty, O Holiness, through your help! For without me you cannot stand, if I flee. Ah, ah, ah! Woe to the negligent person, for I must nevertheless uproot that most restless thorn which, by pricking me, tries to drive me to destruction—if I do not pull it out before it is wholly fixed in me and before it is cherished in me as though in a rotten corpse. O Holiness, that I may persevere freely in you, I wish to avoid the devil’s most rapacious snare and to break it in the true God.”

And again, he who sat on the throne, as above, revealed these things to me, saying:

[Col. 0678C] “When the Son of God was incarnate, the calling of the new people, raised up to salvation through his teaching in the Holy Spirit, arose; fortified by the strengthening of strong people in the exhortation of the blessed virtues against the most savage enemy, whom no human being can resist unless aided by God’s grace. By God’s help it presents itself as invincible, so that it can be neither uprooted nor destroyed from God by any art of his snares.

“Therefore the tower which you see beyond the aforesaid column of the Savior’s humanity prefigures the Church. Completed by the incarnation of my Son, she arose as a new construction in every good work, in the strength and height of heavenly deeds, like a most strongly fortified tower set against the devil to resist wickedness. [Col. 0678D] Accordingly, she is of most brilliant splendor, placed upon the aforesaid stone wall on the southern side of that building in such a way that she may be seen both within and without the building. For, illumined by the most serene light of the humanity of the Son of God, she has living stones kindled by the heat of the Holy Spirit in this manner in the divine work; so that she may be openly shown, in that building which the supreme Father works through his Only-Begotten, to inward knowledge of the Scriptures and heavenly understanding, to the outward foolishness of worldly things, and to faithful and unbelieving people alike.

“And her breadth, throughout the inner part of her circuit, is five cubits, because she refers to the honor of the same Lamb, namely her Bridegroom, the breadth of every inward contemplation and the intention of all continual meditation through the five senses of her adornment, [Col. 0679A] in the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, together with all those virtues which the true Lamb reveals to her.

“But she appears of such height that you cannot discern her, because the height and depth of divine wisdom and knowledge in the work of the Church are greater than the fragile and mortal human heart can search out by its own estimation.

“But that between this tower and the column of the Savior’s humanity there has been laid only a foundation, with no wall yet built above it, but only a broken and empty place appearing, one cubit in length, as was also previously shown to you, means that concerning the Church, joined in betrothal to my Son, a great proclamation remains still hidden in the knowledge [Col. 0679B] of God, as in a firm foundation. It does not yet shine forth revealed in the complete work of perfection, but lies hidden in human hearts without disclosure. Yet it is one cubit in length, because human minds are in the power of the one true and almighty God. Thus even a person, by understanding, can apprehend in the knowledge of good and evil what is more beneficial to himself, as was shown to you above in an open vision.

“And that this tower has not yet been built to its full completion, though it is continually constructed by many workers with great skill and speed, means that this same Church has not yet attained that course and condition to which she will attain, although with much care and industry, through the swiftness of passing times, she does not cease daily, without delay, to hasten toward the accomplishment of her beauty in her children who pass away and succeed one another.

[Col. 0679C] “Yet around the circuit of her summit she has seven battlements, built with marvelous strength, because she is surrounded in the height of heavenly works by the seven invincible gifts of the Holy Spirit. These are of such power that no adversary can destroy them or proudly reach them by the height of his own mind.

“But that from the inner side of the aforesaid building you see something like a ladder raised to the summit of that tower means that, in that work which the heavenly Father has worked in divine counsel through his Son, many flourish in unanimity upon the steps of the simple ordering of ecclesiastical progress, reaching to the height of heavenly mysteries, in which the Church stands strengthened and made firm.

“And from bottom to top a certain multitude of people stands upon its steps, because from the first times of the Church’s betrothal until that nuptial time when she will openly rejoice with her Bridegroom in the full wall of her children, apostolic lights will shine upon the steps of the ordering of God’s commandments, by which she was built, protecting her from the darkness of unbelief.

[Col. 0680A] “Accordingly, they have fiery faces and white garments, but black shoes. For in their intellectual understanding—that is, in that of the apostolic rulers—conspicuous faith, namely faith in one God, has been enkindled by the burning of the Holy Spirit in them, as though their face were aflame. Thus they also shone before God and the world by the most pure brightness of the garment of good works. Yet their footwear appears black, because they passed through the paths of unbelief and the filth of the many crimes of unbelievers, whom they converted and led by their example to the way of justice, though with great difficulty.

“But that among them there appear some of like appearance but greater stature and brightness means that among those same defenders of the Church are the first founders of the Church itself. In first building her after the Son of God by their preaching, they preserve the same tenor as their followers, who are known especially to imitate them: for as those went before, so these followed after. Yet they excel them in form, because they themselves had no predecessor from whom to draw an example of the new grace, apart from the Son of God, from whose mouth they heard the word of life; and they excel them in brightness because, beyond the others, they saw in person the splendor of his incarnation.

[Col. 0680B] “They also gaze upon the tower itself with great diligence, because they do not cease, in divine love, to attend upon the Bride of God with the solicitude of their mercy, that she may stand perfectly in her strength, as it is written: ‘Your neck is like the tower of David, built with battlements. A thousand shields hang from it, all the armor of the mighty’ (Song of Songs 4).

“This means: As the incarnation of the Son, the supreme ruler—the strongest lion coming from virginal flowering—was established as the strongest instrument of the new grace, so the strength of your faith, O new Bride, enduring incorrupt, has been made the surest defense of the faithful people. How? All the fortifications of your children are present with and cleave to your most mighty powers; they must be nourished by the new illumination of streams dripping with wine and from a most pure fountain, which you possess in this union of strength. It is as the neck is joined to the rest of the body, so that you can neither be destroyed nor scattered, just as the victorious instruments of the true David cannot be overcome.

[Col. 0680D] “How? The virtue of Christ Jesus, Son of God, is the strongest tower. In it the most victorious warfare of the faithful is exercised in most invincible testing; no adversary will boast that he can prevail against them, because they contain within themselves Christ, true God and true man. Through him, in the second regeneration, the whole structure of your children is most fittingly extended unto salvation.

“Therefore that most pure incarnation, foretold by the prophets and adorned with the most precious stones of virtues, was proclaimed throughout the whole world for the salvation of believers, with the battlements of apostolic teaching—that is, with the planters of the justice of the true light—as this parable shows:

“A certain lord, possessing a marble city, thundered into it with a loud voice. He carved its walls within with many carvings, [Col. 0681A] from which he breathed forth the sharpest polishing of unworked stones. When this had been done, the same lord spoke in his single word to the waters of waters, that by their outpouring they should make level places upon the mountains. When this too had been accomplished, he likewise instructed the fire of fire to prepare small dwellings. And when this too had been fulfilled, those same dwellings grew so high that by their swift growth they surpassed that city in height.

“This means: This lord is he whom no other preceded in lordship. He alone is above all things and in all things, because nothing was found before him or after him; and therefore he is Lord of all. He possessed in his power the noble city, namely the choir of prophets, strong and steadfast against the rage of worldly storms. For they were filled by the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, when that same Lord thundered into them with a great voice, so that he stirred up in them that inspiration by which they uttered his mysteries in obscure words. For first a sound is heard, while the word is not yet known; nevertheless the sound of their prophecy was followed by the true Word, the Son—namely, God incarnate.

[Col. 0681B] “This Lord made manifold carvings in their hearts when he poured into their understanding wisdom through the manifold Spirit, so that in spiritual understanding they prophesied the deep things of God, both of the present and of the future age. Through this they uttered most effective words against the contrary ways of human beings, by which they stirred the exceedingly hard hearts of the Jews toward the gentleness and mercy of blessed deeds.

“But when the Word of God was incarnate, the heavenly Father, indicating his Son to the same apostles—who, though human beings, had been separated from the common people as most pure streams are chosen from other waters flowing in the plain—commanded them to flow out over the whole world in the flood of true faith, crushing and breaking down the great schism of contempt, the puffing of pride, and the exaltation of idolatrous worship, so that people, by knowing the true God, might abandon their unbelief through the apostles’ preaching.

“When this faith had been strengthened among the peoples, the same Provider of all things gently instructed, in the Holy Spirit, the fiery minds of his elect, who had been kindled from the fiery hearts of those whom the Holy Spirit, coming in fiery tongues, had touched, [Col. 0681D] so that, becoming despisers of the world in contemplation of heavenly life, they should not refuse to be little ones and poor in spirit, but should gain for themselves heavenly riches through these small dwellings of humility.

“As those who despised transient things imitated these works of humility in lofty zeal, always pondering the most subtle commandments of God—as martyrs, virgins, and other persons who renounced themselves—they ascended in this breaking down of themselves to love of heavenly things, so that they surpassed even the cultivators laboring in the vineyard of the Old Testament by the speed of their good endeavors, since, regarding themselves as nothing, they yearned with all desire for eternal things.

“Therefore a thousand shields—that is, the many perfect defenses of perfect faith in the new grace—hang from the Son of God, [Col. 0682A] while the first shepherds of the Church, drawing their example from him and trampling themselves down for the hope of things above, protect the Catholic faith, strengthened by the shedding of their blood, from the fiery darts of the devil, which wound human souls. The multiple virtues of heavenly military armor in the other elect who follow them also serve the love of God in this world.

“How? Because the ancient serpent breathed into the first human being the most foul stench of contempt for God. Therefore the devil himself is pierced by every fragrance of the spices of chastity—namely continence, the binding force of God’s commandments, fellowship with Christ, the bearing of his yoke, and contempt for the whole world—these heavenly darts opposed to him. Thus, cast out from the city of God, confounded and trodden down in the open condition of his damnation, he is abhorred by the faithful.

[Col. 0682B] “But that on the northern side of that building you see the world and human beings begotten from Adam’s seed moving about between the aforesaid luminous wall of the building’s speculative knowledge and the circumference of the circle extending from the One seated upon the throne means this: in carnal desires, directed toward weakness and occupied with earthly worldly covetousness, the world and worldly people have been set under the guilt of the first parent. On one side, knowledge of good and evil has been set before them, so that they may approach God’s work through good and flee evil; and, on the other side, God’s power has been shown to them, so that they may know themselves to be under his majesty and not doubt that all their deeds are examined by him. [Col. 0682C]

Accordingly, many pass through the building itself, entering and leaving between the tower of the foreknowledge of God’s will and the column of the divinity of His Word, through the aforesaid wall of speculative knowledge, as a cloud spreads here and there. For, admonished by the Old Testament and the new beginning, many undertake the divine work and enter it through speculative knowledge, abandoning carnal desires; and many, following their pleasures, leave it there amid their evil desires. Thus, according to their own will, whether toward good or evil, they let themselves be carried here and there with the swiftness of clouds—that is, in the movement of their thoughts.

But the fact that those who enter the building are clothed in a most white garment [Col. 0682D] means that those who undertake God’s work with good will are clothed in the most pure and radiant garment of true faith, so that through His mercy they may know God. Some of them, exulting with great joy in the sweetness and gentleness of this garment, retain it; for, with a contrite and humbled spirit, instructed in the sweetest and gentlest Catholic faith and suffused with the inward liquid of holiness, they continually rejoice with the inward eyes in heavenly things, most devoutly fulfilling and retaining the things which the Holy Spirit inspires in them. Others, however, made sad as though by its weight and difficulty, wish to put it off; because, as though burdened by a most heavy load and hindered by a most difficult road, inwardly tearing and wearing themselves away through the most restless and bitter habit of unlawful pleasure [Col. 0683A], they strive to cast aside faith in their works and refuse to permit themselves to be moved by the divine commandments.

This virtue, which you heard called the knowledge of God, kindly restrains such persons often and speaks to each of them the true words of its admonition, as has been said above. For the Most High God, foreknowing that the hearts of hard stones in human beings may be softened, bends toward them in His mercy—as was shown to you—frequently warning them to pray to Him inwardly with groaning and tears, that He may free them from the importunity of their wickedness, with which they have been saturated by diabolical persuasion; so that in this repentance they may return to the understanding of good will, remembering the garment of innocence which they received in the regeneration of Spirit and water.

But the fact that you see [Col. 0683B] certain of them, chastened by these words, retain the same garment with much sweat, although it appears difficult to them, means that, warned by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, they take up in their minds the faith which they receive as a heavy and difficult road; yet, though with much labor, neither despairing nor growing numb from weariness, they finally complete it. Others, mocking those same words and furiously stripping off and casting away the garment itself, return to the world from which they came; searching into many matters, they learn many useless things belonging to worldly vanities. These are those who hold the law of God and His righteousness in derision, strip themselves of the Catholic faith amid the vanities of their errors, deny it by evil works pertaining to death, and turn themselves toward [Col. 0683C] the vanities of this world, which they had previously pretended to abandon. Seeking lustful deeds in perverse acts, they learn the burning taste of the age and corrupt it by diabolical mockeries according to the devil’s deception.

Some of these finally return to the same building and, taking up again the garment which they had cast aside, put it on. For these return from the path of their error to the divine work; casting away the schism of the devil which they had accepted according to his will, they again take up, confessing with a pure and simple heart, the habit of true faith which they received in baptism and which, in their errors, they had cast away while deriding the true God. Others, unwilling to return, remain shamefully stripped in the world [Col. 0683D], because, despising a return to God through pure repentance, they are despoiled of the garment of innocence. Therefore, naked of the good of faithful works but full of the evil of the vices of diabolical arts, they lead their lives without repentance amid the wickedness of worldly vanities, to death, with the greatest confusion both in this present age and in that to come.

But the fact that you see certain most filthy and black persons, as though stirred by madness, coming from the north and rushing into the building itself, attacking the aforesaid tower in bacchanalian frenzy, and hissing into it like serpents, means that certain wicked persons, under the shifting heat of joyous delirium, defiled by the blackness of diabolical vision, look upon God. They do not seek through the gift of the Holy [Col. 0684A] Spirit the office which they desire, but, blown upon and incited by diabolical art and sent from the region of damnation, they enter the divine work through cunning. By secretly pilfering, openly seizing, and recklessly raging in madness through the most accursed money of horrible diabolical blackness, they swallow up offices established by God; and, troubling the Church in this way by insane fury, they emit into it the hisses of the ancient serpent’s deception.

How? By diabolical cunning they blow upon unwary people until, through deadly purchase, they overcome them according to their will. They defile the Church with this hiss of boastfulness while they thus steal powers which have been established by My ordinance. Since they do these things, they are cast away from My sight without repentance, and I do not acknowledge them in these [Col. 0684B] deeds; for they acquired them through themselves and not through Me, as Hosea, My servant, shows when he says: “They have reigned, but not by Me; they have become princes, and I did not know it. They made for themselves idols from their silver and gold, that they might perish” (Hos. VIII).

This means: Human beings, following their own will, calculate and establish within themselves whatever their private appetite determines. What is this? The desiring desire that is in them persuades them to rule over human beings by a stolen and seized honor, neither sought nor received nor established from Me. Yet I sometimes permit this to occur, so that judicial punishment may come upon them because of their own wills, since in this they did not seek Me. And what benefit does this bring them? In it they possess not greenness but dryness [Col. 0684C]; and because this is not planted, but useless grass grows in them without a trunk. Fruitless grasses easily grow from the earth by themselves; fruitful plants, however, are sown and planted with great labor.

So I permit that at times a human being’s earthly desire, without a root, may easily flourish in evil without seeking the planting of good, because it does not have the greenness of summer. I also permit at times that his right desire, well rooted in good, may bear fruit through many miseries, loving the watering of holiness, because it lacks the harshness of winter. Thus, vile people often also surpass in authority a common and useful people, just as useless plants are sometimes taller than useful ones. They are established only in their own desires, not planted by Me [Col. 0684D], nor rooted by the touch of the knowledge of My gift or of My ordinance. Yet I permit this by a just judgment, because they did not seek it from Me but established it within themselves; therefore they will answer to Me for this in My judgment.

For they make into a contrary vanity both the blessedness of the best teaching—which they ought to examine in their mind, free from every unworthiness of unbelief, as silver is purified from every falsehood—and the usefulness of the deepest wisdom, which they ought to order in their will by most splendid faith, always seeing how God must be worshipped, venerated, and confessed. How? They bend it down into the greatest misery, offering their understanding, which they have from God, to the insatiable [Col. 0685A] desires of their flesh, as though their own foul and putrid flesh were a god. They refuse to lift their eyes to God who formed them; rather, they regard their own will as God, because they live according to it, arranging and establishing matters within themselves.

They do this not in order to possess that field which bears the food of eternal life, but so that they may be far from it and perish eternally without repentance; for the one whom they worship as God is dead, just as they too are dead—both sellers and buyers of spiritual things—desiring to be that which they did not seek from Me. For how could one who seizes authority through mad desire, so as to make the rational gift of the Holy Spirit salable, be saved through such a sale? A person who [Col. 0685B] sells his property to strangers ought no longer to use it. And how should that merchant use the salvation he purchased, which he did not wish to receive from God but hastened to acquire with money—though God, by His right judgment, permitted it to happen that he might acquire it?

For God, angered with some people, permits them to steal that thing, for which, nevertheless, by a hidden judgment He punishes them in the present and not in the future; so that, since they loved in forgetfulness of the Holy Spirit, they may be confounded within themselves, and through this confusion may be brought to return to God in repentance. When they have done this, they receive forgiveness in the future. Others He tolerates in this matter, not tormenting them in the present but deferring it to the future for a just reason, because they regard their own will as God; therefore in the future He shows them what profit their will brings them in bitter torments. [Col. 0685C] Others, again, He punishes both in the present and in the future, because their clear understanding voluntarily makes itself vile and contemptible within them, imitating the devil in his evils. He also permits others to come to this point, so that the evil itself may be confounded in their repentance when, severely punishing themselves for the injustice committed, they cast it away like a putrid corpse. But He mercifully resists some, lest they attain it; for if they reached it, they would deserve to be grievously tormented in the pains of hell, from which they could not escape.

Whoever sells or usurps for himself a chair of authority by the counsel of his father, which is money—for money becomes [Col. 0685D] his father in the marketplace—acquires perdition from that dignity; and both the one who gave and the one who received must be cast away. For if someone’s beast were secretly stolen and sold to another, the one from whom it was taken reclaims it when found, with every right; but the one who sold it and the one who bought it must each surrender it without objection. Thus, too, if the dignity of authority, which ought to be possessed according to My justice, is plundered by anyone through a clandestine gift and perversely scattered among others, it is required back by Me in strict judgment. Therefore both the person who put it on the market and the person who bought it unworthily will, by just judgment, lack its benefit, because they have made the temple consecrated to My name into a gift of robbery.

How? [Col. 0686A] They have put into the marketplace, by their own decision, the wisdom and counsel which they had from Me in their heart, receiving from this money of iniquity through the perdition of others. Therefore they will cast away that commerce in bitter repentance, or they will answer to Me for it in the fire of dreadful burning. For whoever, buying with dead money a living dignity which the Spirit gives life to in spiritual heights, strives to lead it into the stench of bubbling corruption, will be thrust down through the very perversity of this presumption into perdition—unless he quickly repents. Thus Peter, the son of the dove, inflamed by the Holy Spirit, a deserter of error and one who had left all things, says to the passing whirlwind that wished in its most foul blackness to swallow up the light: “May your money be with you unto perdition, because you thought that the gift of God [Col. 0686B] could be possessed with money. For you have neither part nor lot in this matter. For your heart is not right before God” (Acts VIII).

This means: May the money of your deceitful confidence, which you hold as master over another’s property—while it holds you as its slave, indeed as nothing—be with you in the perdition of hellfire, if without repentance you retain this gift of the fiery Holy Spirit, bought through the crime of money. For in the transient knowledge of your soul you deceitfully thought that the kindling of that most piercing Inspector could be possessed with money; you despaired of being able to have it by God’s gift. But if you repent on this account, you will give up what you bought and will perceive as lost the money you paid for it, because you wished to trade for what is eternal with mud, from Him who formed you [Col. 0686C] from clay.

But while you persist in that purchase, you will have no share of light in the fellowship of the heavenly angels, because in the utterance of your tongue you revealed the rapacity of your heart, desiring something other than that which the citizens of eternal brightness desire. Therefore your heart in this perversity is unjust before God, since you wish to have by the purchase of money what must be freely given by God.

Therefore, deserters of this divine covenant, because they ought to seek it by the free gift of the Holy Spirit and do not do so, are by My just judgment compared to vain images. For just as those things, being works of hands, are empty of fellowship with truth, though they are worshipped as God by unbelievers, so these persons, deprived of the illumination of the Holy Spirit through the contrary gifts of earth, become deceitful teachers [Col. 0686D]. They are not chosen in the sighing of their souls, as though unworthy of that office; rather, receiving it from human beings in blazing pride, they do not consider My will in this matter. Therefore I do not know whence they are, and they are as strangers to Me; for because of this injustice, if they persist thus, they are cast away from Me. But if they repent with all their heart, looking upon them, I shall cause the angels to rejoice over them.

But although those who desire these dignities with perverse ardor act unjustly, and those who strive to seize them by their wickedness must not be approved, as has been said, the offices themselves are good, well established by God for the benefit of human beings. They must not be resisted proudly and obstinately, but rather obeyed in My love. Therefore, no believer who wishes worthily to obey God [Col. 0687A] should set himself against the authority set over him, because it imitates God’s honor by guarding and feeding His sheep, so that the honor of the sheep themselves may not be dissipated to the stranger who is a thief and robber. For just as no one ought to oppose God, so no one ought foolishly to resist His authority.

Therefore every person, living in soul and body, ought to obey the dignities higher than himself, whether they maintain bodily or spiritual jurisdictions; he ought to be subject to them, so that the law established for human beings may be directed by fear of their authority, lest, wandering astray in the undisciplined liberty of their own will, they establish a law for themselves according to whatever they wish and thus err in the way of the Lord. It is in order that they may not err that authority is from God.

How? The governments of human beings have been arranged by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit [Col. 0687B], so that through them people may learn to fear the Lord. If people pervert them into their contrary according to their own pleasure, this nevertheless is not in God’s will, but in His hidden permission, so that their desire may be fulfilled in perverse ardor to their own harm by just judgment. Therefore the dignities of powers, inspired by God for the benefit of human beings and justly ordered by Him because of their great necessity, exist lest God’s people, living like cattle without government, should proceed through every byway of their instability.

Thus, whoever resists them, unwilling through the impulse of pride to obey them in humble subjection, as is just, does not contradict human beings but obstinately opposes Me, the Creator who justly disposes all things, according to Adam’s transgression. On account of this rebellion he heaps upon himself the darkness of damnation, just as Adam was expelled from joy into miseries. But this does not apply to one who, walking humbly in My zeal, does not consent to the perverse wickedness of human beings. Such a one rather increases than diminishes the justice of God’s justice, if he does this fittingly and at the proper time. Rather, it applies to the person who wishes improperly to oppress the dignities themselves through haughty pride, since they have been manifested by My ordinance for the benefit of the living, as has been said. Whoever kicks proudly against them resists My inspiration, although some, in the madness of their ignorance, not considering My fear, thrust themselves into those same dignities through the iniquity of their will, transgressing the divine commandment [Col. 0687D]. By just judgment I permit this to occur as they desire, so that through the most equitable examination they will answer for it in grievous repentance or in the fire of hell.

But the fact that you see some of these becoming clean, having ceased from this folly, while others persevere in the same wickedness and filth, means that some of them, returning to their senses from their perversity through divine inspiration, deserve to be cleansed and saved through pure and true repentance; whereas others, hardened and without repentance, remain in the same cunning and uncleanness until the end of their lives, and thus, suffocated, die miserably and cruelly in the torments of a dreadful death.

But the fact that within the aforesaid building, toward the aforesaid tower of the Church, you behold standing, as it were, seven marble columns of white [Col. 0688A] color, turned into a wondrous roundness, means that in the work of the omnipotent Father, for the protection and adornment of the new Bride, the Holy Spirit has revealed seven most bright supports of His inspiration, which by their strength wipe away every adversity of storms, making manifest the supreme power that has neither beginning nor end in the roundness of eternity. They are seven cubits high, because, surpassing every strength and height of all human understanding, those gifts show that He who created all things must be worshipped in the purest faith. At their summit they have, as it were, an iron and round platform, suitably raised a little upward in height, because in the excellence of their brightness they signify the invincible and incomprehensible power of divinity, covering and sustaining in the heavens, by its most elegant rectitude, those who here have separated themselves from carnal pleasures through the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

But the fact that at the top of this platform you see, as it were, a most beautiful image standing means that this virtue was in the Most High Father before every creature, ordering in His counsel all the instruments of creatures established in heaven and on earth. It is the great ornament shining in God, the broadest step among the steps of the other virtues in Him, and joined to Him in the rejoicing embrace of burning love. It looks toward human beings in the world because it always governs and guards with its protection those [Col. 0688C] who wish to follow it, loving them greatly because they stand firm in it.

For that image signifies the wisdom of God, because all things have been created and are governed by God through it. Its head shines with such brightness as lightning that you cannot fully contemplate it, because divinity is terrible and gentle to every creature, seeing and considering all things, just as the human eye judges things set before it; yet no human being can penetrate it to an end in the depth of its mystery. Thus it suitably clasps its hands to its breast: this is the power of wisdom, which wisely restrains itself, directing every work in such a way that no one can resist it in anything, whether by prudence or power. Its feet are hidden from your sight in the platform, because its depths, hidden in the Father’s heart, lie open to no human being; its secrets are bare and manifest to God alone.

The fact that it has upon its head a circle in the form of a crown, shining with much brilliance, means that the majesty of God, without beginning or end, shines with incomparable honor, divinity radiating with such splendor that the gaze of mortal minds is dazzled by it. But the fact that it is clothed in a tunic of golden color means that the work of wisdom is often considered as though in the purest gold. Therefore, from its breast downward to its feet, it is adorned with one descending girdle, ornamented with most precious gems: green, white, red, and a brazen color gleaming through purple splendor [Col. 0689A]. For from the beginning of the world, when wisdom first brought its work into open manifestation, it has extended itself as by one path unto the end of the ages, adorned in holy and righteous commands: first, with the planting of the green shoot of patriarchs and prophets, who amid the miseries and groans of their labor most earnestly begged for the Son of God to become incarnate; then adorned by the most white virginity in the Virgin Mary; afterward by the most steadfast and red faith of martyrs; and finally by the purple and radiant charity of contemplation, by which God and neighbor must be loved through the warmth of the Holy Spirit. This will proceed to the end of the world without ceasing through its admonition, ever flowing forth while the world endures, as this virtue also declares in its exhortation, as has been said.

But the fact that again you see three other images on the floor of the same building means that these virtues, treading earthly things underfoot and pursuing heavenly things in the divine work, signify three instruments through which the Church seeks eternal things in her children: namely, the nourishment of teachers, the battle of the faithful against the devil, and their return from consent to vices. One of them leans upon the aforesaid columns, because ecclesiastical teachers, instructed through the gift of the Holy Spirit, receive rest in its strength. The other two stand alongside it in front of it, because love of God and neighbor is contained in the united and companionable activity of their exhortation [Col. 0689C]. Therefore they all direct themselves toward the column of the Savior’s humanity and toward the aforesaid tower, because with equal unanimity they show that the Son of God, true God and true man, must be most devoutly worshipped and adored in the Church, elevating justice through justice; that is, they signify that in the ancient saints the Most High God wrought the salvation of souls through the incarnation of His Son.

But the image that leans upon these columns prefigures the justice of God, because after wisdom it works through the Holy Spirit in human beings with all its justices. It appears of such breadth that it may be said to equal the breadth of five people standing beside it: this is the expanse of the five senses of human capacity, with which it moves in the breadth of God’s law, containing and preserving, for those who love it, the commands of life established by God. It is also of such height that you cannot perfectly discern its length; indeed, it looks throughout the entire building, because, surpassing human understanding in its breadth, it stretches upward to heavenly things. Thus it also looked down from heaven in the incarnation of the Savior, when that Savior—the Son of God—came forth from the Father, who is true justice. Therefore it directs its gaze toward all ecclesiastical instruments, because they are fashioned and sustained through it, as higher bulwarks are joined to the strongest tower through which they may stand firm.

Accordingly, possessing a great head [Col. 0690A] and clear eyes, it looks most keenly into heaven, because the greatest and highest goodness of justice declared to human beings the most radiant vision through the incarnate Son of God, when He manifested Himself in a human body to earthly and darkened eyes while contemplating heavenly things through the redemption of souls. It is wholly white and translucent like a most serene cloud, because it dwells in the brightness and purity of the minds of righteous people, who direct all their effort toward being most faithfully subject to God’s justice. Therefore it likens itself to clouds, because it prepares for itself a pleasing dwelling in the hearts of the righteous.

But the fact that you see no other human form within it means that it remains heavenly and not earthly, as has also been explained to you: it does not adhere to human [Col. 0690B] works by which people are burdened, but to those which lead them to the justification of life. For God is righteous, and this virtue, opposed to the devil in God’s work, faithfully exhorts the other virtues above.

The first image of those which stand alongside one another before the aforesaid image signifies fortitude, because after the justice of God fortitude arises like a prince in the presence of the highest King, resisting in all human beings, by a right and holy work, every snare of adversaries. It appears armed, namely with the strength of almighty God, because, strong in faith, it strongly resists diabolical subjection. Therefore it is clothed with a helmet—that is, heavenly strength for the salvation of believers—and with a breastplate, which is the law of Christians [Col. 0690C], and which no arrow of diabolical craft destroys through the justice it contains. It also has greaves, that is, the right paths frequented in the teaching of the principal masters, and iron gloves, which are the strongest and keenest works that the faithful accomplish in Christ.

It also holds an unsheathed sword in its right hand: that is, the naked and open admonition of God in divine Scripture, made manifest in good works, which the true Son of God uncovered in mystical signification when He showed the inward sweetness of the kernel in the unveiling of the law. It holds a spear in its left hand, by which it signifies that it has confidence in eternal things in this action also, when it is attacked by unbelieving people through carnal desires and the pleasure of the flesh. The fact that it tramples beneath its feet a horrible dragon means that through the path of uprightness it subjects the ancient and dreadful serpent to its power. It also pierces the serpent’s mouth with the iron of its spear, so that the serpent vomits out most unclean foam: for, piercing the jaws of most filthy and diabolical lust with the keenest boldness of chastity, it wrests from it the foaming of burning lust by which the serpent defiles human beings.

Therefore it strongly brandishes the sword it holds as though to strike, because God has manifested His penetrating word in extended strength to destroy all the unbelief of idols and other schisms that belong to incredulity, as this virtue also shows in its admonition.

The other image signifies holiness, because [Col. 0691A] when the devil is resisted through fortitude, holiness arises in good people for the adornment of the heavenly army. It has three heads, because through this threefold dignity it is brought to its state, so that a head appears in the natural place of the head and upon each shoulder. For in righteous and worthy action God, the head of all true exultation, must be feared and venerated both in prosperity and adversity, by which a human being may be made joyful or sorrowful. Yet the middle head rises somewhat above the other two, because He who is judge of good and evil surpasses all things by His equity.

But the fact that the middle head and the head at its right shine with such splendor that their brightness dazzles your sight, so that you cannot perfectly discern whether they have masculine or feminine form [Col. 0691B], means that holiness, standing at the summit of honor and in the realm of eternal prosperity and sweetness, is so flooded with the brilliance of divine grace that the depth of its mystery surpasses human understanding. Because of the heaviness of mortality, humanity cannot behold either its freedom or its subjection in Christ, except insofar as it flourishes in Him.

But the head that appears at the left is somewhat dark and veiled in a white covering according to feminine custom, because this perfection, which firmly restrains itself for love of God, has, in that adversity in which it is attacked by diabolical assault and human action, an anxiety and concern about how it may defend itself with divine help. In the most humble subjection, in the whiteness and beauty [Col. 0691C] of Christian combat, it commends itself to the highest Redeemer through the groans of faithful hearts.

The fact that the same image is clothed in a tunic of white silk means that it appears wrapped in the work of most radiant and gentle zeal, in which perfect holiness imitates My Son. It is also equipped with most white shoes, because through Christ’s death it shines in human minds with the brightness of regeneration by Spirit and water [Col. 0692A], so that they too may imitate His death. On its breast it bears the sign of the cross, around which a great splendor glows upon the same breast like a shining dawn, because in the purpose of the minds of the faithful, who most diligently embrace it, it meditates upon the remembrance of the Passion of Christ Jesus. By this most serene brightness of faith, everywhere marking those same minds, it also shows that He who, obedient to the Father, suffered in His holy humanity according to the Father’s will, came forth born without the stain of sin in the most beautiful dawn of the sun, which is the Virgin Mary.

The fact that it holds a naked sword in its right hand, applying it to its breast and to the same cross with great devotion, means that it shows in good and holy work how it loves Scriptures laid bare through the Holy Spirit in the remembrance of the minds of the elect—for they too most sweetly remember the Passion of their Redeemer. Thus you also see written on the forehead of the middle head, “holiness,” because holiness is known in the inward countenance, which is that of the soul, with joy of life and without any shameful indignation. On the forehead of the right head is written, “root of good,” because it is openly the beginning and foundation of the salvation found in holiness. On the forehead of the left head is written, “sparing not itself,” because, rejecting apart from the body the softness and vanity of carnal pleasures, it always restrains itself in severity, joins to itself the ornaments of the other virtues, and strives to be perfected and to endure.

The middle head looks toward the other two, and they toward it; they confer their usefulness upon one another, because, standing firmly in the unanimity [Col. 0692C] of inward vision and love, so that none of them can endure without the help of another, they direct their words and admonitions toward the advancement of human beings, as has been said. But whoever has the sharp ears of inward understanding, let him pant after these words in the burning love of My mirror and inscribe them in the conscience of his soul.

## TENTH VISION

[Col. 0691]

### SUMMARY

Words of the Son of Man. That a human being who has knowledge of good and evil is without excuse. Admonition to married persons. A comparison concerning a field. That a human being ought not to investigate what he ought not to know, as is evident from the examples. That no one should suddenly take up the way of holiness, as is seen in the examples set forth below. Admonition to virgins and continent persons concerning how they ought to undertake holiness. Concerning the inward continence of the mind, as is evident in the examples below. A comparison concerning a treasure. Words of constancy. Words of heavenly desire. Words of compunction of heart. Words of contempt for the world. Words of concord. That works which God performs in human beings are strengthened in the height of justice and the strength of the gifts of the Holy Spirit. That every action accomplished in the faithful by faith and work is united by divine providence to the fear of the Lord. That the Son of God governs one who wishes to persevere in good work, lest he fall into error—He who by His humility destroyed death. That the shadow of the law came to an end in the birth and Passion of the Son of God. The things God has done in the Church can be seen and known by human beings; future things, however, can be known only by faith or divine revelation. That God, mercifully regarding humanity, admonishes it to seek the heavenly homeland by imitating the saints. Concerning the state of constancy, heavenly desire, compunction of heart, contempt, and concord. Concerning their appearance. Concerning constancy. Concerning heavenly desire. Concerning compunction of heart. Concerning contempt of the world. Concerning concord. That good work is unfolded in the watchful strength of faith, and that in the perfection of work it is shown with what devotion each person worships God. That through the strength of faith God cast the ancient serpent down into the depth of eternal confusion. Pagans, Jews, and false Christians who deny the true faith are in God’s power, although they have been cast out from the Church set on high. Words of John on the same subject. That God brings to fulfillment, on the last day, the Church gathered from every part of the world according to what He predestined, the devil having been confounded.

[Col. 0691D] And after these things, at the summit of the eastern corner of the building previously shown, where the aforesaid two parts of its wall—that is, the bright and the stone-built—were joined together [Col. 0692D], I saw, as it were, seven steps of purest white marble [Col. 0693A], which seemed to curve, like a vault, toward that great stone upon which the aforesaid Bright One appeared seated on the throne. And upon those steps a seat had been placed, upon which a certain young man sat. He had a manly and noble countenance, though of a pale complexion, and darkish hair flowing down to his shoulders; he was clothed in a purple tunic. He appeared to me from his head as far as his navel; but from the navel downward he was obscured from my sight. And looking out upon the world, he cried with the greatest strength to the people who were in it, saying:

“O foolish people, who languish tepidly and shamefully within yourselves, unwilling even to open one eye to see what you are in the goodness of your spirit, but ever burning to do the evil [Col. 0693B] which the concupiscence of your flesh possesses; refusing to abide in a good conscience and in the right contemplation of your minds, as though you had no understanding of good and evil, nor this glory, that you should know how to avoid evil and accomplish good: hear me, the Son of Man, speaking to you.

“O human being, consider what you were when you were a coagulation in your mother’s womb. For then, in being given life, you were unaware of yourself and powerless. But then spirit, motion, and sensation were given to you, so that, living, you might move, and moving yourself, might understand the fruit of what is useful. For since you possess knowledge of good and evil and the power to act, you cannot excuse yourself from possessing every good thing from these within yourself: so that, instructed by the highest inspiration, you may love God in truth [Col. 0693C] and justice, and resist yourself in the concupiscence and delight of unrighteousness, tormenting yourself in these things. And in this manner honor my martyrdom, resisting yourself in these ardors, that is, bearing my cross in your own body—fleeing unlawful desires when it pleases you to sin.

“And why do you have so great a power, namely, to avoid evil and do good? Because of the knowledge of good and evil, by which you understand that you are human, you will answer to me. Yet you despise good and do evil, burning in carnal desires, because good seems burdensome to you, whereas evil is easily stirred up within you. And although this is so, you do not wish to constrain yourself, but to sin freely. What did I do when I suffered for you on the cross in the weakness of the flesh, when I trembled and was distressed—I, [Col. 0693D] the Son of Man? Therefore I require of you a martyrdom against yourself, which you undergo amid the pleasure of your flesh, your other disturbances, and your unlawful desires that oppose my will, and in other such wickednesses that follow these; in these you cannot excuse yourself from knowing when you act well and when badly.

“But I do not reject the bond of chaste lawful union, which by divine counsel was established for the multiplication and begetting of the children of Adam, when this is done by those to whom it is lawfully permitted without injury, in the true desire for offspring and not in the false pleasure of the flesh, according as it has been commanded them in the divine law—namely, those given to the world and not set apart in spirit. Therefore you must love, against yourself, the good which you have from me [Col. 0694A]. You are heavenly in spirit and earthly in flesh. Therefore you must love what is heavenly and trample down what is earthly. In the work of heavenly things I show you the reward above; but in the will of your flesh, when you wish to accomplish what is unjust, there I show you my martyrdom and the punishments I endured for you, so that you may resist yourself in contrary desires for love of my passion. You have very great understanding in yourself, and very great account will likewise be required of you. Much has been given to you, and much will likewise be required of you. But in all these things I am your head and helper. For, touched by the touch from above, if you call upon me, you will hear an answer from me; if you knock at the door, it shall be opened to you. In the spirit of most penetrating [Col. 0694B] knowledge with which you have been endowed, you possess within yourself everything that is useful to you. And because this is within you, therefore my eyes, seeing with the utmost keenness, will consider what they find within you.

“Therefore from your conscience I require the wounds and sorrow of your heart, by which you restrain yourself when you perceive that your own will is drawing you toward sin. And when you have so burned within it that, wholly melted, you can scarcely sigh—behold, then I look upon you. What will you then do? If, in that labor, with wounded heart and streaming eyes, shaken by fear of my judgment, you call upon me, and if you then persevere in that cry, that I may help you against the wickednesses of your flesh and the combats of evil spirits, I will do everything that you desire to be done for you [Col. 0694C], and I will make the dwelling-place of my habitation in you.

“Now therefore, my son, consider with how much labor and sweat work is done in a field before it is sown with seed; but after it has been sown with seed, it yields its fruit. Therefore attend to and consider these things. Do I not refuse to grant the earth that it should produce fruit without the sweat of labor? Yet when it pleases me, it is so abundantly filled with fruits that people have sufficiency in the greatest abundance, sometimes even an excess; and when I will it, it is so reduced that people sometimes scarcely live because of extreme hunger, and sometimes many, weakened among them, perish. In this manner I deal with human beings established through me: namely, to the person who willingly receives the seed of my word with a good heart, I abundantly grant the great gifts of the Holy Spirit, as to a good field [Col. 0694D]. But the one who at times receives my word and at times refuses to receive it is like a field which is green at one time but withers at another. Yet this person does not altogether perish, because although he suffers hunger in his soul, he nevertheless has some, however little, greenness. But he wholly dies who desires to receive my words with no intention at all and who is unwilling in any way to stir his heart to good either through the admonition of the Holy Spirit or through human teaching. You marvel at these things, O human being, and wish to know why they happen thus.

“But just as you cannot behold divinity with mortal sight, so neither can you grasp its secrets with mortal understanding, except insofar as this is possible for you by its own permission. But you, with your wavering mind, turn hither and [Col. 0695A] thither. Thus, as water is absorbed by the heat of a burning furnace, so your spirit is overwhelmed by the restlessness of your foolish mind. For you desire to know things that ought not to be known by human flesh conceived from human seed in sins. Raise your finger, then, and touch the clouds. What now? But this cannot be done; likewise neither can that be done while you investigate what ought not to be known by you.

“But just as grasses cannot comprehend their fields, because they lack sense and understanding, knowing neither what they themselves are, nor what the field is, nor what they accomplish by their fruit, although they fill and surround the fields for usefulness; and just as gnats, ants, and the other smaller animals do not desire to rule over other creatures like themselves, or to know or understand the power or significance [Col. 0695B] of a lion or of other greater animals: so neither will you be able to know what is in the knowledge of God. What did you do, or where were you, when heaven and earth were created? He who created them did not then need your help, nor does he now. Why do you investigate God’s judgment when you have been touched from above by the rain of salvation? Show me how you labor in the field of your heart and how you cultivate it. If that labor pleases me, I shall give you the best fruit according to your labor, and your fruit shall come with its reward. Do I give the earth’s fruit without labor? Likewise I do not deal with you, O human being, without the sweat that I require of you. For through me you have within yourself those things by which you can labor. Therefore diligently exercise yourself in labor, and you will attain fruit from it. [Col. 0695C] And when you have fruit, you will receive reward from it.

“But what is this? Many now seek me with a devout, pure, and simple heart, and, having found me, retain me.

“But many, jesting and playing, wish to approach me without labor of mind and thought. They do not wish to deliberate beforehand what they ought to do—namely, by calling upon me and considering the condition of their own body—but wish only to seize hold of me. As though awakened from a heavy sleep, they suddenly, by a movement of pretense and deception, take up the way of holiness as they imagine it within themselves: some in the rejection of worldly business, others in continence from the flesh, others in the chastity of virginity, taking my yoke upon their shoulders. They suppose that everything they wish is possible for them, unwilling to consider who they are or what [Col. 0695D] they can accomplish, and unwilling to know who formed them or who their God is. They wish merely to have him as their servant, to perform their every wish. Thus I do not wish to give my gift or sow an empty field in that person who, in such vanity, does not know himself in alienation of ignorance before me. Hence his foot will often slip.

“And I say to him: ‘O human being, why did you not inspect the field of your mind, in order to uproot useless weeds, thorns, and briars—by calling upon me and considering yourself—before you came to me like one drunken, mad, and ignorant of yourself? For you cannot accomplish any bright work without my help. For after this rashness, by which you sought me as though in sleep, when you have become weary in [Col. 0696A] my service and remember that sleep in which you formerly slept amid your habitual sins, you will return, mad and ignorant of good, to those former crimes, deprived of the help and consolation of the Spirit, the Paraclete.’

“But what did you seek as leader and helper for these things? Certainly your own deceitful and deceivable mind, which foolishly led you into barrenness, without greenness and without remembrance of your understanding, forgetting that you could do no good without me. And what then do you have? Certainly then you will fall miserable and empty before me and before the people, and you will be trampled like useless dust. For what is possible to you against me? Nothing. And what can you do by my help? You can perform works most bright, more splendid than the brilliance of the sun, and sweeter in inward taste than [Col. 0696B] honey and milk, when they are made manifest to a people that longs for them. For when you seek me with the innermost understanding of your soul, as you were taught in baptism through faith, do I not give all that you desire?

“But after their fall many seek me with groaning and sorrow—though they ought to have sought me before they fell. To these I stretch out my hand, saying: ‘Why did you not seek me before the fall? Where was I? And where did you seek me? Did I reject you when you sought me?’

“And I say: ‘O human being, if you were standing beside a bridge over very deep water, and, through empty boasting and forgetfulness of your heart—by which you despised me in all things, thinking all that you wished possible to you, as though you needed no help from me—you rashly said within yourself, [Col. 0696C] “I wish to avoid this bridge and walk through the water,” would you act prudently? But if you did it presumptuously and foolishly, would you not breathe out your spirit in that very creature which was created subject to you for your benefit? Yet, lest this happen to you, you take precautions because of the present and visible fear of water that would swallow you in death. Or if you saw a great felled tree falling, would you not flee lest it crush you? Or if you saw lions or bears coming to meet you, would you not, if you could, hide yourself in the ground because of the fear you would conceive? And when you flee bodily injury in this way, why do you not avoid the most terrible death of the soul by fearing your Creator? Have you ever seen or heard of anyone resisting me? For whoever is not with me shall be scattered; [Col. 0696D] and he upon whom I fall shall be broken.

“What were you when heaven and earth were created, which carry out their powers as has been established for them? Yet you, formed by God’s counsel and touched by his illumination, transgress his commands. O great madness! Through the creature that serves you in subjection, you despise your God. You tread the earth and look upon heaven, which, fearing their Creator, obey him and fulfill his command; what do you, most foolish one, utterly fail to do, when you will neither know him in your thought or work nor look toward him, so as to acknowledge him as is fitting? Therefore, unless you repent, hell will swallow you in just judgment, as it did him who, hardened, was cast down from heaven and whom you have imitated. Nevertheless, when you have fallen, seek me faithfully, crying out [Col. 0697A], and I shall receive and raise you up. But you, O human being, so often wish to touch the highest things, though you cannot even comprehend the lowest.

“Therefore hear me speaking to you: if, instructed by me, you desire to bear my yoke in the rejection of worldly concerns or in continence from the flesh, before you undertake this first cry out, and persevere in this by seeking me, and I will help you. But if, touched by my admonition, you desire to imitate me by looking to me in the chastity of virginity—for just as a flower springs from an untilled field, so I, the Son of God, was born from a virgin without male seed—show me the field of your mind in great humility, and address me amid the abundance of your inward tears, and say:

“‘O my God, I, an unworthy human being, do not have from myself this ability [Col. 0697B] to accomplish the preservation of my virginity unless you, Lord, help me; for I am wholly guilty in the uprising of burning sap from which I sprout amid many miseries, often returning to the source of my frailty. Thus I cannot by my own strength overcome myself in tasting the sweetness of my flesh, since I am a tree conceived and born in sins. Therefore, Lord, give me in your strength a fiery gift which may extinguish in me this tinder and this burning of perversity, so that with upright sighs I may drink from the water of the living fountain, which may cause me to rejoice in life—I who am ashes and dust, looking more toward works of darkness than toward works of light.’

“And if you then are zealous and steadfast in this supplication, I shall prepare in you that field [Col. 0697C] which Isaac set before his son when he said: ‘Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a full field, which the Lord has blessed’ (Gen. 27); and I shall bless this same field of mine in your heart. And as he further said: ‘Be lord over your brothers, and let the sons of your mother bow down before you’ (ibid.), so likewise you shall be an exalted generation before the common people. And I shall sow into that field roses and lilies and other excellent spices of virtues, and water it with the continual rain of the inspiration of the Holy Spirit; and, uprooting barrenness, I shall cut evil away from it, so that, turning my eyes about, I may feed them upon the greenness and flowering of this incorrupt field. This is mine and through me, not yours, O human being, nor through you. For I am the flower of the field (Song 2), because as a field produces a flower without a plow [Col. 0697D], so I, the Son of Man, was begotten of a virgin without male union. Therefore this gift is mine and not yours, because you were conceived in sins and born from corruption in sins. But if you faithfully ask this gift from me, you will confidently obtain it from me, and I shall grant you fellowship with me before my Father in virginity.

“Yet, because of the frailty of your body, you cannot possess this without the labor of the heat that is in you; for the human nature of your frailty often betrays itself in you, and you cannot avoid this because you are flesh from flesh. But in this you must bear my cross and imitate my martyrdom: namely, by constraining yourself, so that through me you may conquer yourself. This is always pleasing to me, because I know you to be a fragile vessel; and then I desire to share and sympathize with your sufferings. [Col. 0698A] And if you sometimes fall even in these matters, rise swiftly, do repentance from the heart, and, receiving you, I shall save you.

“But some, deceived by the devil and persisting in evil, think themselves sanctified because they restrain their outward person from marriage, while rejecting the circumcision of the mind, where they abound in unclean thoughts, and even rejecting the circumcision of the spirit, where they bring forth evil in their speech and deeds. They do not wish to know that this is shameful, but observe only tepidly that their flesh may remain untouched by intercourse, wholly refusing the integrity of their spirit. Therefore, being unworthy before me, they are cast outside both the carnal and spiritual law, because they have lived according to God’s justice neither in flesh nor in spirit. For they have kept neither the law of marriage established for them [Col. 0698B], nor preserved, in love of virginity, that which is greater than what was commanded in the law. Therefore they are unworthy in my eyes, because I do not know who they are. For I have not seen them walking in the commandment of the law, nor have I seen them favoring in this matter what was greater than what was commanded them. Hence they are rejected from my sight.

“I compare them to barren earth producing thorns, briars, and wretched grasses, fit for no human use, which in their height and color liken themselves to roses, lilies, and other useful flowers and herbs that possess useful juice, sweet fruit, and good fragrance for medicinal purposes. And again I compare them to copper: outwardly it resembles gold, but inwardly retains the deception and hypocrisy [Col. 0698C] of gold. For in this manner these people outwardly show themselves to resemble the prudent virgins, but inwardly are full of deceit and indignation. Thus before me they are like a lukewarm wind, whose heat and cold have no vigor at all; for they are neither useful in the heat of their spirit, persevering in virginal continence as they began, nor capable in the cold of worldly life of living in secular affairs as they propose. For they neither sin outside the law as tax collectors, nor within the law as unjust persons; but lukewarm in themselves, they are neither perfectly just nor unjust.

“But as the offspring of unclean animals is cast away before it senses itself to be alive, or before it is strengthened in the strength of its maturity, so this people is cast into death, because it neither knows itself to live [Col. 0698D] unto life nor understands within itself the strength of the virtues that are in the house of wisdom. Therefore I blow them out from my mouth, because they are unworthy of my sight if they persist thus without repentance. But now, O human being, look within yourself.

“For if someone gave you a treasure because he loved you greatly, and said to you, ‘Trade with this and become rich, so that thereby it may also be known who he is who gave you this treasure,’ then you ought to think most carefully how you might make gain from it usefully, saying within yourself: ‘The treasure of my lord must appear in me with the finest profit, so that he too may be praised in it.’ And when you had usefully increased and multiplied it in this way, a good report would reach the ears of him who had given you the treasure. Therefore he himself, remembering you because of this, would love you more and bestow greater [Col. 0699A] gifts upon you.

“So too does your Creator. He gave you the excellent living treasure, namely understanding, loving you greatly because you are his creature. And through the words of the law established by him, he commanded you to make gain by your understanding through good works and become rich in virtues, so that he, the good giver, may thereby be more diligently known and praised. Therefore at every hour you ought to consider how this very great gift that you have received, being made useful both to others and to yourself in works of justice, may render forth from you the splendor of holiness, so that people, stirred by your good example, may offer God the honor of praise for it. And when you have humbly multiplied it in every righteousness, praise and thanksgiving increase toward the knowledge of God, who in the Holy Spirit inspired these virtues in you. Therefore he himself, turning the mercy of his grace toward you [Col. 0699B], will through the sweetness of his love make you burn yet more abundantly in love for him, so that, filled with the consolation of the Holy Spirit, you may wisely discern everything that is good and perform greater good works, glorifying your Father with most ardent love, who kindly gave you these things.

“Let my sheep hear these words, and let all who have ears of the inward spirit receive them, because it pleases me that people who know and love me should thus act, so that they themselves may understand within themselves what they ought to do in the gifts of the Holy Spirit.”

But in that same eastern region I saw, upon the pavement of the aforesaid building before the same young man, three figures standing beside one another and gazing upon him with the utmost devotion [Col. 0699C]. Toward the north, between that great circle extending from the aforesaid Bright One seated on the throne and the same building, I perceived something like a wheel hanging in the air, and in it a human figure visible as far as the breast and looking with the greatest keenness upon the world. Before the corner of the same building turning toward the south, another figure appeared within the building upon the pavement, turning herself toward the aforesaid young man with great joy. And these figures had this appearance: like the other virtues I had seen before, all were clothed in silken garments. All likewise had their heads covered with white veils, except the one standing in the middle at the right of the aforesaid three, who seemed to have white hair and an uncovered head. [Col. 0699D] None of them was wrapped in a mantle, except that same middle one of the three, who was clothed in a white mantle. Yet all wore white tunics, except the one appearing in the wheel, who had a darkish tunic; and except the one in the middle on the left among those same three, who wore a pale-colored tunic. All were likewise shod with white footwear, except the middle one of the three, whose foot-coverings appeared black and painted in varied colors. Such was their dissimilarity.

In the breast of the figure who stood in the middle of the aforesaid three beside one another, two little windows appeared, and above them a stag turned toward the right of that same figure, so that it had placed its forefeet upon the right-hand window and its hind feet upon the left, as if making itself ready to run.

[Col. 0700A] And that same figure said: “I am most strong, a pillar not moved by the lightness of instability, nor able to be stirred by a blast of wind like a leaf of a tree which is moved by it and driven now here, now there; rather, I must endure upon the true stone, which is the true Son of God. And who can move me? Who can harm me? Neither powerful nor weak ruler, neither noble nor base, rich nor poor, will be able to prevent me from persevering in the true God, who shall not be moved for ever. Nor shall I be moved, because I have been founded upon the strongest foundation. For I do not wish to be with flatterers, who are scattered in every direction by the wind of temptation, never remaining in the rest of stability but always falling toward lower and worse things. But I am not thus, because I have been placed upon the firm [Col. 0700B] rock.”

But the figure on her right, looking upon the aforesaid stag, said: “As the stag longs for the springs of waters, so my soul longs for you, O God” (Ps. 41 [42]). “Therefore I desire to leap over mountains and hills, and over the weakness of the sweetness of transitory life, looking only with a simple heart toward the fountain of living water, for he is filled with innumerable glory, and no one can be satisfied with his sweetness to the point of weariness from satiety.”

But the figure standing at her left, looking at the aforesaid little windows, said: “I ever behold, I ever hold the true and eternal light; nor shall I be able to be sated, by thinking, looking upward, and gazing, with the everlasting sweetness that is in God above.”

But [Col. 0700C] the figure which appeared in the wheel toward the north had a green little branch in her right hand, while the wheel itself continually revolved, the same figure remaining immovable in it. Around the circumference of the wheel was written: “If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also shall my servant be” (John 12). And upon the breast of the figure was inscribed: “I am the sacrifice of praise in the provinces.” And the figure itself said: “To the one who conquers I will give to eat of the tree of life which is in the paradise of my God, because the fountain of salvation, submerging death, has poured its streams into me and made me green in redemption.”

The figure that appeared before the corner facing south had such splendor in her face that I could not gaze upon her perfectly. But on each side she had a wing [Col. 0700D] of white color, whose breadth exceeded the length of a certain figure, and she said: “Who is of such strength as to try to resist God? And who has such audacity as to dare to strip and corrupt me in the shamefulness of hatred and envy? God is just and one in sincere power and glory. I always wish to embrace him with a pure heart and joyful countenance, and always to rejoice in all his just acts. I do not wish to be changeable, but to endure ever in one mind and continually praise God. Therefore neither devil nor malevolent human being shall be able to soften me or cast me down into this frenzy of deceit, so as to prevent me from always persevering as an imitator of peace in right unanimity. When the world has passed away, I shall appear more brightly in the heavenly vision.”

After this I saw, and behold, the entire pavement [Col. 0701A] of the aforesaid building appeared wholly like white glass, giving forth from itself a most serene brightness. Moreover, the splendor of that Bright One seated on the throne, who showed me all these things, shone through that pavement even to the abyss. Between the circle extending from the one seated on the throne and this building, earth then appeared, sloping somewhat downward, so that the building itself seemed to stand upon a mountain.

And the Bright One seated on the throne again said to me: “The Son of the living God, born of the Virgin, is himself the cornerstone, whom those rejected who ought to have built in the law of God for their salvation; but they refused to do this, loving darkness rather than light and death rather than life. He reigns mightily in those who, burning by the touch of the Holy Spirit, beneficially trample down their outward selves and with all striving draw themselves toward the inward things of the spirit in the fullness of virtues and good works [Col. 0701B].
