“Therefore, too, at the summit of the eastern corner of the building previously shown, where the aforesaid two parts of its wall—that is, the bright and the stone-built—are joined, you see, as it were, seven steps of purest white stone. For in the height of justice flowing forth from the true East, who is the cornerstone in the divine work, where the two unions of necessary fortification—namely, contemplative knowledge and human work—cleave to one another in the unanimity of repose, there is a sevenfold ascent of purest strength, full of most upright [Col. 0701C] action, which God works and accomplishes in the human being, just as he worked in six days and rested on the seventh.

“These steps seem fittingly to curve like a vault toward that great stone on which the aforesaid Bright One seated on the throne appears, because every action accomplished through faith and works in faithful people is joined, by the authority of God’s providence, in a most worthy effect of harmonious arrangement to the fear of the Lord, over which he himself, who rules all things, presides in strongest omnipotence. Therefore a seat has been placed upon those steps: that is, over the works which God performs in human beings is the most firm support of protection, governing and aiding them. For whoever wishes to persevere with him shall not fall into error, because he is the strongest [Col. 0701D] support on which all justice is established.

“And seated upon the seat is a certain young man: the Son of Man, the Son of God, who in most steadfast rule reigns in all justice with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God. He has a manly and noble countenance because he, the strongest lion, destroyed death with noble face, coming visibly without sin and born of a virgin. Yet he is of pale complexion, because among earthly things he did not seek earthly honor, but appeared most humble, lowly, and poor in holy humility.

“Thus he has darkish hair descending to his shoulders, because the Jewish people, not seeking the brightness of faith revealed in the incarnation of this same Son of God, languished stubbornly and unbelievingly under the shadow [Col. 0702A] of the outward understanding of the law. Yet, having arisen at the head of justice and reached as far as the shoulder of strength, where the perfect work flourished in the humanity of the Son of God, it there came to its end in its unbelief. And he is clothed in a purple tunic because, pouring out his blood in love, he redeemed the human being who had perished.

“And your seeing him from his head to his navel means that, from his incarnation until the present time, the works he has performed in the Church are manifest to the faithful. But from the navel downward he is obscured from your sight, because the things which are to come in that same Church from this time until the completion of this age can neither be seen nor known except insofar as they are perceived by divine revelation and Catholic faith [Col. 0702B], since the greatest flashes of virtues that are to be manifested in people before the last day still lie hidden and unknown to human beings.

“And he looks upon the world because the same Son of God, directing the gaze of his mercy toward human beings, speaks to them the most faithful words of his admonition on account of past and future things, that they may imitate the heavenly warfare in his saints, fleeing the perils of sins, and that, battling most strongly, they may attain heavenly blessedness by opposing in their deeds the punishments of the ungodly.

“But your seeing in that same eastern region, upon the pavement of the aforesaid building before that same young man, three figures standing beside one another and gazing upon him with the utmost devotion means that, in the rising of justice, which presses down carnal [Col. 0702C] desires, when the Son of God appeared in the flesh by the ordinance of the almighty Father, these three virtues, united in devotion, were manifested through the power of the most steadfast Trinity and directed their gaze toward him, because they desire and seek him in faithful people.

“Thus also you perceive toward the north, between that great circle extending from the aforesaid Bright One seated on the throne and the building itself, something like a wheel hanging in the air, and in it a human figure visible as far as the breast and looking upon the world with the greatest keenness. This is because, against the arts of the devil, between the hidden power of God and his spiritual edification, the circuit of his mercy, as though hanging in the air, turns in the minds [Col. 0702D] of human beings—now touching the power of God’s justice, now strongly confirming his work in them. In it Christian perfection appears in contempt of the world as far as the breast of its strength, because this virtue, trusting in God through the power of the strongest contest, most keenly warns people living secular lives in the world to imitate, in the rejection of earthly things, the example of the Son of God who has gone before, breathing strongly toward him with most steadfast intention.

“Therefore, too, before the corner of the same building turning toward the south, another figure appears within the building upon the pavement and turns herself toward the aforesaid young man with great joy. For, so that the fall of humankind might be restored to life through the goodness of the heavenly Father in the ardor [Col. 0703A] of fruitfulness, this virtue, trampling down worldly things in the fullness of the divine work and openly making herself manifest in the sweetness of her affection, directs herself toward the Son of God in the fellowship of the angelic order with the joy of faithful people, because she flourished by heavenly power in the incarnation of that same Savior. But these figures have one likeness, because with equal devotion they manifest God in human beings who harmoniously magnify him in their works.”

Accordingly, just as all the other virtues that you saw earlier are clothed in silken garments, so they are not unlike the remaining virtues that were most truly shown to you above in their powers; rather, in the gentle business of the most delightful work of faithful people, they are always alike directed upward toward God. And the fact that all are covered with white veils upon their heads means that, together, in the bright resolve of the lawful institution, they are occupied before God with the great binding-together of the head of all things, as a woman is customarily veiled before her husband—except for the one standing on the right of the middle one of the aforesaid three, who seems to have white hair upon an uncovered head. For she, strengthened by that same prosperity of power manifested through the heavenly Trinity, burdened by no anxiety of this age, seeks only in the brightness of heavenly longing “to be dissolved and to be with Christ.” Therefore none of them is wrapped about with a mantle, because they are stripped of every office of servitude by which they might be hindered from always looking toward heaven and panting after God in the office of their freedom, desiring nothing except what is separated from earthly things—save the middle one of the three, who is clothed in a white mantle. By this is indicated the beauty of the blessed Law’s discriminating work in divine support; and this virtue is so covered by the mantle as a person is covered by his own mantle.

But the fact that all are clothed in white tunics means that they walk in the brightness of good works, without the blackness of depraved habits, unlike those darkened by blinded unbelief amid wickedness and vices—except for the one appearing in the wheel, who has a somewhat black tunic. For she is surrounded in the turning movement of divine mercy by those deeds which, in their strictness, are hard for the flesh; and except for the one standing on the left of the middle one of those same three, who wears a tunic of pale colour. She herself, in adversity, is encircled and fortified for her defence by the protection of the highest Majesty, and, with the tearful sorrow of grieving work, sighs continually to God, weeping and wailing amid these things.

Accordingly, all are also furnished with white footwear, because in the death of my Son they prepare the shining way of peace in human minds, so that people may desire heavenly things—except for the middle one of the three, whose foot-clothing appears black and painted in diverse colours. For she, remaining under God’s protection yet enduring the great schisms of unbelievers who stray from the way of truth in the mockery of blackness, is nevertheless adorned with the straight path of faith. Without dissenting from the mortification of my Son, she presses upward through many assaults of diabolical arts and through the diverse tribulations of human conduct, persevering in her strength and beauty.

Yet there is a difference among them. For although they are of one mind and joined to one another in their activity, each individually displays her own powers in the people subject to her, in the fervour of heavenly brightness.

Thus the image in the middle of the three standing beside her signifies Constancy. She is the pillar and defence of the virtues that cling to her, manifesting the holy Trinity in the midst of this number, and showing people that they should be constant in good works. For Christ also, God and man, brought to a good end the works that he performed in the world; and this virtue, existing as the support of the inward virtues in people, brings them to God with great discipline.

Therefore two little windows appear in her breast. This is the manifestation of heavenly things, displayed in human hearts through the two mirrors of faith, because the divinity and the humanity in the Son of God must be believed. Through him that virtue, perfected in people, will not be moved from the strength of its uprightness.

But above those windows a stag appears, turned toward the right of that image, because above this faith—that the Son of God is believed to be God and man—he himself is most firmly set by the faith of the faithful people. By the course of his swiftness he signifies heavenly longing and turns toward the right of Constancy, because eternal life is found in perseverance in good work. Thus he places his forefeet upon the right window and his hind feet upon the left: for neither that he is true God is to be despised in the tranquillity of faith, nor that he is true man is one to be distrusted in the assault upon that same faith by anyone who truly loves God.

Accordingly, he also makes himself ready as though to run, because the salvation of souls is found in his course. Hastening amid great pains toward the Passion of the Cross, he bestowed life upon those who persevere in truth, as this virtue also indicates above in the words of her confession.

But the second image, which is on her right, prefigures heavenly longing, always looking toward heaven and tending toward salvation. By it Constancy, not seeking the prosperity of transitory things, desires rather the happiness of eternal things.

Therefore she also looks upon the aforesaid stag, because, constantly attending to the Son of God in his most radiant work, she cannot be satisfied with his sweetest embraces, as she also affirms above in the utterance of her longing.

The third image, standing on her left, shows compunction of heart and recollection of mind, grieving and weeping over its exile in continual contrition. Through its blessed outpouring Constancy, turning aside from the opposition of the left side—which is the destruction of the soul—hastens from death to life.

Accordingly, she too looks upon the aforesaid windows, because, directing her whole intention in the hearts of the faithful toward the Son of God reigning both in humanity and in divinity, she delights to enjoy his sweetness in continual vision, as she also demonstrates clearly in the open declaration of her words.

But the image that appears in the wheel toward the north represents Christ’s perfection and contempt for the world. For the fullness of the virtues was most openly made known by the Son of God in the rejection of worldly things: living among people and not craving earthly things, he vigorously urged his followers, with all ardour, to pant after heavenly things.

She holds a green branch in her right hand, because in the blessedness of the soul’s salvation she contains the work of the most verdant and beautiful shoot of the blessed virtues, which is suffused with the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

Therefore the wheel itself continually turns, while the same image remains motionless within it. For God’s mercy, bending toward people in pious compassion and sympathizing with their miseries, is always yielding to those who seek it; but Christ’s perfection in contempt for the world has no movement of instability, and always tends toward those things which have no defect of changeableness.

And the words written around the circumference of the wheel—“If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also my servant shall be” (John 12)—mean that the mercy of God, flexible everywhere, contains this: whoever renders obedience to the Son of God by imitating his example will rejoice in heavenly blessedness, attaining with him without end the fellowship of the angels.

Accordingly, there appears engraved upon the breast of the image: “I am a sacrifice of praise among the provinces.” For Christ, wisely teaching contempt for worldly things, intimates through the hidden counsel of his heart to the hearts of his elect that every faithful soul reveres and adores with inward devotion him who was offered as a sacrifice to the Father upon the wood of the Cross. And throughout the whole world the voice and tongue of all the faithful do not cease to resound with his glory and praise because of the reward of life, as she herself also openly proclaims in her utterance.

The image appearing before the corner that faces south signifies Concord, fleeing the rage of evil spirits but embracing the fellowship of the blessed angels. For love of God’s sake she avoids the divisions of unbelievers and pants after the vision of perpetual peace.

Therefore there is such splendour in her face that you cannot look upon her perfectly, because, lacking deadly hatred and envy, she prepares in human souls a brightness greater than the mortal mind, burdened by its frail body, can grasp.

But the fact that she has on each side a white wing, whose breadth exceeds the length of the image, means that, both in prosperity and adversity, joining themselves to the sweat of righteous labour, that virtue extends the protection of its most shining goodness. It possesses more in the breadth of its expansion in the charity of heavenly things than it has in the length of the human race as it is born. For when the world is ended, flying above the heavens of heavens, it will appear more in its brightness then than it does now. There nothing earthly and nothing transitory is sought; rather, that which is heavenly and eternal is loved in sweetest embrace, and there all things will endure bright and joyful, every cloud of wickedness having been wiped away, as is faithfully declared in the words professed by this virtue.

What you see—the entire pavement of the building appearing like white glass and giving forth from itself a most serene brightness—means that the strength of true faith, bearing and explaining the work and city of God, is wholly pure and level in the whiteness and mirror of simplicity. This faith, with all the works belonging to it, watches and builds in the city of God, so that God may be touched at the beginning of people’s good works through the brightness of a most serene intention, and may be most openly known at their end through the salvation of the soul. For when the work has been carried out, faith itself reveals with what devotion each soul sought God.

Accordingly, the splendour of that radiant One seated upon the throne, who shows you all these things, shines through the pavement down to the abyss. For the grace of almighty God, ruler of all things, who makes known to you what you perceive in this vision, has through the strength of faith reduced the devil to nothing in the destruction of death.

How? God cast the ancient serpent and the death of eternal perdition into the depths of perpetual confusion through the most pure faith that is in the regeneration of Spirit and water, powerfully passing through the darkness of unbelief when the Son of God admonished his faithful people to send out into the world the words of teaching received from him.

But the fact that, between that circle extending from the One seated upon the throne and this building, only earth appears, sloping a little downward, so that the building seems to stand upon a mountain, means that between the strength of almighty God’s power and the chosen work of his goodness there are very many people who deny true faith and pursue temporal rather than eternal things: pagans, Jews, and false Christians, always descending from evil to evil. They do not look upward, amid transient things, toward the mirror of Catholic faith; rather, in their pleasures they labour to drag wicked work down into the depths of sins.

Thus the greatest and most beautiful work of God appears openly, amid the darkness of this misery, to every person who seeks it in the height of supreme goodness, as John, the beloved Evangelist, testifies in the divine revelation, saying: “And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city Jerusalem coming down out of heaven, having the glory of God” (Revelation 21).

This means: the Spirit raises the spirit. How? In his power the Holy Spirit draws the human mind away from the weight of the flesh, so that it may fly in the vision of the eyes of that spirit which sees inward things and is not darkened by the blindness of carnal pleasures.

What is this? The Holy Spirit raises the human spirit up to the mountain of heavenly desires, so that it may clearly consider the works that must be accomplished in the spirit. This is the greatness of God’s works, beneath which a thousand arts of diabolical activity are laid, so that it rules over them as a mountain rises above the level plain of the earth. It is an immovable foundation, like a mountain that does not depart from its place; it is also of such height that mortal man cannot describe it in his understanding, because it surpasses all human prudence, which rises from earthly minds and earthly qualities.

And so the works of the Spirit are shown to the faithful and holy soul. Likewise, the heavenly Jerusalem, without the work of fleshly hands, is to be built spiritually through the work given by the Holy Spirit. It appears in the greatness and height of holy works in the spirit, so that the same city is adorned by the good works which are done in people through the touch of the Holy Spirit. For set thus upon a mountain and built with innumerable edifices, she gathers within herself the noblest stones—the holy souls who are in the vision of peace—purged of every rottenness of sin.

Accordingly, she shines like gold with those precious stones, because in good people Wisdom displays the work of her brightness. But those works, accomplished in the uprightness of justice and by which the heavenly Jerusalem herself is adorned and perfected—whence did they arise? Plainly, from the height of heaven. For as dew descends from the clouds and drenches the earth with its moisture, so good works descend from God into people and are watered by the infusion of the Holy Spirit; thus the faithful person, producing good and sweet fruit, gains the fellowship of the heavenly city.

Therefore heavenly works, coming from heaven into people through the gift of the Holy Spirit, possess brightness in him from whom they also flowed forth. How? Because the brightness of God shines in the good works of righteous people, so that he is known, adored, and worshipped all the more ardently on earth through the virtues by which that city, thus made, is adorned with her ornaments. For when a person does good works with God’s assistance, he venerates God in his wonders.

Thus this revelation is seen and known through the eyes of the spirit: through the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, upright works performed in people appear before God in the heights.

Therefore, as has been shown beforehand, God works from the east and from the north and from the west toward the south. There, through his Son in love for the Church, he brings to that final effect—the Last Day—everything that had been predestined before the foundation of the world. So too, carrying out this work of his by himself, he brings it back to himself, confirmed and adorned with the aforesaid towers and virtues in mystical signification, and completed in supreme perfection.

How? The justice of righteous action, signified after Adam’s fall in Noah, tends toward the Last Day, surrounded by many miracles which God has not ceased to display in his elect at diverse times: in preparation in Noah, in manifestation in Abraham and Moses, and in operation in his Son.

How? Before the ages it was in the heart of the heavenly Father that he wished to send his Son into the world at the end of the ages for the true salvation and redemption of fallen humanity. Born of a Virgin, he completed in perfect action all that the ancient saints, filled with the Holy Spirit, had foretold—just as a person’s arm first bends itself toward work, and then the hand acts.

What is this? When Adam was cast from the earth of flourishing, justice, that is, the righteous judgment of God, first began to move in Noah, as at the first joint of the shoulder. Thus it stretched toward stronger things in Abraham and Moses, as toward the more flexible parts according to the joint of the arm, and finally reached perfect work in the Son of God. Through him all signs and prophecies of the old Law were fulfilled in open action; and through him all the virtues by which the heavenly Jerusalem will be adorned in her children were manifested with the fullest certainty in the regeneration of Spirit and water, just as the hand, through its fingers, brings the work it performs to complete manifestation.

In this way I complete my work for my glory and for your confusion, O devil: opposing you by the strength of my arm in the north, the north country, and the west, and also resisting you according to the sun’s course from the east and south. Thus I overthrow you in the west, so that you may be confounded in every region. For in my Church, which is the mountain of strength, I perform the work of justice and holiness for your destruction, O most hideous deceiver, so that you, utterly conquered, may perish—you who wished my people to perish.

Whoever has keen ears of inward understanding, let that person pant after these words in the burning love of my mirror, and write them in the conscience of his soul.

## ELEVENTH VISION

[Col. 0707]

### SUMMARY

Concerning the five most savage courses of temporal kingdoms. Concerning the fiery dog. Concerning the tawny lion. Concerning the pale horse. Concerning the black pig. Concerning the grey wolf. Concerning the hill with five peaks, and what the five beasts’ ropes signify. Job’s words on the same matter. That the Church shines from her perfection in the beauty of justice until the time of Antichrist. That then the Church’s faith is, as it were, in doubt, apart from the testimony of Enoch and Elijah. That before the end of the world, through their testimony, the Bridegroom of the Church will shine with purest brightness, the son of perdition having been defeated and the faith of truth made manifest. David’s words on the same matter. That, as justice grows cold, the Church will lamentably endure many diverse sufferings and persecutions. That Antichrist, tearing apart the faithful with dreadful terror, pours into people the stench of his cruelty and the frenzy of his biting savagery. That the son of perdition will try to bend by most cruel persecutions those whom he cannot bend by flatteries. That at the consummation of the world the Church will be drenched in most noble blood, until the two witnesses of truth. That we are in the seventh millennium. Why God speaks new secrets and many mysteries hitherto hidden through one who is unlearned and does not speak. God’s exhortation to teachers not to despise this discourse, but to raise it as a most victorious standard against the son of iniquity. The Holy Spirit’s words to the Church concerning the last time. The Gospel concerning the same. That, when the world is disturbed, the four elements will be washed clean and the Church will be completed in her children, lest members be lacking to the head. That the course of the world is now in the seventh number; that, after toil, the seals of the Scriptures are brought forth openly and gently, as in this book; and that there is no other number—the remainder is not for humanity to know. Why God willed his Son to become incarnate. Concerning Antichrist and his mother. That, instructed by his mother in magical arts, he exercises his will in diverse creatures by God’s permission. Concerning his power and the various miracles he seems to perform. Moses’ words concerning the vision of God. That some, deceived by the devil, deceitfully display portents in creatures, but cannot transform them into another kind. That Antichrist deceives his followers in diverse ways, and why this is permitted him. Concerning Antichrist’s feigned death; concerning the writing of cursing: whoever contradicts it will be killed. John’s words. Why Enoch and Elijah are reserved for that time. Their words to the children of God. Concerning their true signs, by which Antichrist’s false signs are rejected. That, their course completed by God’s permission, they will receive the reward of their labours. That all the Church’s members will be shaken with terror by Antichrist’s presumptuous arrogance, as he thinks himself able to penetrate heavenly secrets. That God’s power, by manifest strength, casts down the son of perdition after the manner of the devil into eternal damnation. That infernal stench and mist will fill the place of his exaltation, so that those deceived may return. That, after the son of perdition has been cast down, Christ’s bride will shine in the brightness of wondrous beauty, as those who have wandered return to the way of truth. That no one but God can know the day of judgment. The example of Samson.

[Col. 0709A] Then I looked toward the north, and behold, five beasts stood there. One was like a fiery dog, but was not burning; one like a tawny lion; another like a pale horse; another like a black pig; another like a grey wolf. And they faced toward the west.

And in the west, before those beasts, there appeared something like a hill having five peaks, so that from the mouth of each beast one rope extended to each peak of that hill. All were of a somewhat black colour, especially that rope which was stretched from the wolf’s mouth, which appeared partly black and partly white.

And behold, in the east I again saw upon that same corner the young man whom I had earlier seen upon the corner where the radiant and stony wall of the building joined, clothed in a purple tunic. But now he appeared to me from the navel downward. From the navel to that place at which a man is distinguished, he shone like the dawn; there lay what seemed to be a lyre with its strings crosswise; from that place down to the heels of his feet—that is, to the measure of two fingers laid transversely, touching the heel above—he was shadowy; and from that measure through his whole feet he appeared whiter than milk.

But that female image also, which I had previously beheld before the altar that is before the eyes of God, was now shown to me here again. Yet I saw her too from the navel of the belly downward. From the navel to the place at which a woman is recognized, she had variegated and scaly spots. But in the place of female intercourse there appeared a monstrous and utterly black head, having fiery eyes, ears like the ears of an ass, and nostrils and mouth like the nostrils and mouth of a lion. It gnashed with a great gape and horribly sharpened, as though of iron, its dreadful teeth.

But from that head down to her knees, the image was white and red, as though bruised by much crushing. From the knees to two white bands lying crosswise above and touching the heels of the feet, she appeared blood-red.

And behold, that monstrous head moved itself from its place with such a crash that the whole female image was shaken by it in all her members. A great mass, as it were, of much filth was joined to that head; and from it the head, raising itself above a certain mountain, attempted to ascend to the height of heaven.

And behold, a blow like a thunderclap, coming suddenly, struck back that head with such force that it fell from that mountain and breathed out its spirit into death. Thereupon a stinking mist suddenly enveloped the whole mountain. In it that head was wrapped in such foulness that the people standing by were turned to the greatest terror; and that mist remained somewhat longer about the mountain.

Seeing this, the assembled people, shaken with great fear, said to one another: “Alas! Alas! What is this? What does this seem to us to be? Ah, wretched us! Who will help us? Or who will free us? For we do not know how we have been deceived. O almighty God, have mercy upon us! Let us return, then; let us return! Let us hasten to the testament of Christ’s Gospel, for ah, ah, ah! we have been bitterly deceived.”

And behold, the feet of the aforesaid female image appeared white, giving forth brightness upon brightness beyond that of the sun.

And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “Although all things that are on earth tend toward their end, so that the world, placed in the failing of its powers, bends toward its outcome, oppressed by many miseries and calamities, nevertheless the bride of my Son, though she is greatly wearied in her children both by the forerunners of the son of perdition and by the destroyer himself, will by no means be crushed, although she is greatly attacked by them.

[Col. 0710C] “For she will rise up stronger and more powerful at the end of the ages, and will be rendered more beautiful and brighter, so that in this manner she may proceed more sweetly and delightfully to the embraces of her beloved. This too is mystically signified by the vision that you behold.

“For you see toward the north, and behold, five beasts stand there, which are five most savage courses of temporal kingdoms, raging fiercely within themselves in carnal desires, in which the stain of sin is not absent.

“One is like a fiery dog but is not burning, because the course of those times will have people harshly biting in the constitution of their own order, appearing in their own estimation like fire, but not burning in God’s justice.

“And one is like a tawny lion, because that course will sustain warlike people, stirring up many wars but not discerning God’s uprightness in them. For in the tawny colour those kingdoms will begin to incur the weariness of weakness.

“Another is like a pale horse, because those times will produce people wanton in the flood of sin, who in the swiftness of their pleasure leap over the activity of good virtues. Then the heart of those kingdoms will be broken in the pallor of their ruin, because it will then lose the red glow of its strength.

“But another is like a black pig, because that course has rulers who create within themselves a great blackness of sorrow and roll themselves in the mud of impurity: namely, setting aside the divine Law amid many oppositions of fornications and other similar abominations, and devising many schisms against the divine commandments in matters of holiness.

“But another is like a grey wolf, because those times will have people heaping up for themselves many plunderings, both in positions of power and in their other successes. In these struggles, showing themselves neither black nor white but, as it were, grey in their cunning, they will cast down the heads of those kingdoms by dividing them. For then the time will come for the ensnaring of many souls, when the error of errors will be raised up from hell to heaven, so that the children of light will be placed in the winepress of their martyrdoms. They will not deny the Son of God, but will reject the son of perdition, who will attempt to carry out his wishes through diabolical arts.

“And these beasts turn toward the west, because these transient times fall with the setting sun. For as it rises and sets, so do people also: this one is born, and that one dies.

“Accordingly, there also appears in the west before those beasts something like a hill with five peaks, because the authority set in place in those courses amid carnal lusts is shown as proclaimed in five exaltations. Thus one rope extends from the mouth of each beast to each peak of that hill, because from the beginning of those times the long course stretches to every height of appointed power. All are of somewhat black colour except the rope stretched from the wolf’s mouth, which appears partly black and partly white, because these long courses exist amid the varied stubbornness of human pleasure.

“But that course set in the voracity of plunder extends many iniquities in its black part. Yet from it come forth, in great whiteness of justice, those who will confront the son of perdition in order to resist him amid terrifying miracles, as my servant Job shows concerning a righteous man performing justice, when he says: ‘The innocent shall be stirred up against the hypocrite; and the righteous shall hold to his way, and he who has clean hands shall add strength’ (Job 17).

“This means: the one innocent of bloody deed—that is, murder, fornication, and similar evil works—is stirred up like a burning spark against him who always lies in his works. How? For he names honey, but devours poison; and he calls someone a friend whom he suffocates like an enemy. That is, he speaks sweet words but has malice within himself; he speaks gently to his friend, but strives to kill him in an ambush.

“But one who has a rod, driving unworthy beasts away from himself out of the straight path of his heart, also has bright paths before the shining sun. For he is raised up in God as a bright spark and clear light, like a shining torch. Thus, surrounding himself with most strong and pure works, he adds to them a strong breastplate and a cutting sword, driving vices away from himself and joining virtues to himself.

“Therefore you again see in the east, upon the same corner, that young man whom you had earlier seen upon the corner where the radiant and stony wall of that building joined, clothed in a purple tunic. For the rising of justice, the Son of Man, presiding over the strength of the union of contemplative knowledge and human work that builds upward in the Father’s goodness—when this Son of Man, in the will of his Father, pays [luit; printed ludit] his blood for the salvation of the world, as was shown to you—now also sits there in the same height and is again manifested to you for the confirmation of truth through the mysteries of his miracles.

“Yet now he appears to you from the navel downward, because from the strength of his members, which is his elect, where now he himself, the Bridegroom of the Church, flourishes, down to their completion, you see many wondrous and obscure signs. Thus, from the navel to that place where a man is distinguished, he shines like the dawn, because from that perfection—when his faithful members now possess the perfection of strength—to the time of the son of perdition, who will feign himself a man of power, he will show the brightness of justice in the uprightness of those who devoutly worship him.

“Therefore there lies there what seems to be a lyre with its strings crosswise. This means that in the persecution in which the son of iniquity will inflict many torments on the elect, the joy of the songs of those who, because of the dreadful torments they suffer in their bodies, are now released from bodily bonds and pass into rest.

“But from that place down to the heels of his feet—that is, to the measure of two fingers laid transversely, touching his heel above—he is shadowy. This means that from the persecution which the faithful are to suffer from the son of the devil to the teaching of the two witnesses, namely Enoch and Elijah, who despise earthly things and devote their labours to heavenly longings, the faith of the Church’s institution is to be held as though in doubt. People will say with much grief: ‘What is said about Jesus? Is it true, or otherwise?’

“But from that measure touching the heel above, through his whole feet, he appears whiter than milk. This means that, through the testimony of those witnesses awaiting eternal rewards, after the son of perdition has been defeated, before the end of the world the Son will shine in Catholic faith most white and beautiful. Then the truth will openly be known through him, and the falsehood in the son of iniquity will in every respect be rejected, as David my servant also testifies where he says: ‘But the king shall rejoice in God; all who swear by him shall be praised, because the mouth of those speaking iniquity has been stopped’ (Psalm 62).

“This means: profound knowledge, which is a great state in humanity—namely, touching the beautiful form of human tongues by God’s will and disposition—strenuously makes harmony at God’s altar, because it knows God. And the blessed run in the praises of sounding minds, making a torrent the path of words in the most pure fountain of the mightiest Ruler, when, in the time of perdition, the gaping hisses of diabolical arts which foully infect human minds are destroyed.

“But that female image also which you had earlier beheld before the altar that is before the eyes of God is now shown to you here again. For the bride of the Son of God, persisting in the most pure prayers of the saints and most devoutly offering them to heavenly scrutiny, as was shown to you, is now also disclosed to you in these same mysteries for the confirmation of justice.

“Yet now you see her too from the navel of the belly downward, because from that creation through which she is now advanced in ecclesiastical dignity to the fullness of her children, she is manifested to you through many mysteries of miracles for the protection of many.

“For from the navel to the place at which a woman is recognized, she has variegated and scaly spots. This means that from that strength by which she now flourishes worthily and praiseworthily in her children to that time when the son of perdition will attempt to carry out the arts that the devil instilled into the first woman, she will lamentably and miserably endure diversity and hardness amid the onslaught of many vices, both sexual sins and deadly, predatory evils. How? Because those who ought to love her will fiercely persecute her.”

Accordingly, at the place of female knowledge there appears also a monstrous, utterly black head; because when the son of perdition comes raging with the arts of the first seduction, in monstrous obscenities and blackest iniquities [Col. 0713D], having fiery eyes, ears like an ass’s ears, and nostrils and mouth like a lion’s nostrils and mouth: he will introduce into human beings the furious operations of most wicked fire and the most shameful sounds of contradiction, causing God to be denied; thus pouring the foulest stench into their senses and, with most cruel rapacity, tearing apart ecclesiastical institutions—namely, gnashing with a great gaping mouth and horribly sharpening, as it were, iron and dreadful teeth. For with the most voracious maw of vices he most wickedly fastens upon those who agree with him the force and madness of his biting. From that head down to those knees she is white and red, and as if bruised by much crushing; because from the dreadful deception by which the son of perdition will first try gently and softly to seduce people, until that time [Col. 0714A] when he will try to bend and bow them more cruelly, the Church in her children will endure the whiteness of true faith, but in herself the distress of bloody stupor and the greatest afflictions of diverse sufferings. Yet from those knees to the two bands, which stretch crosswise, touching the upper part of the heel of the feet, and are seen as white, she appears blood-red; because, when she has now endured, as it were, the motion of her oppression, she will suffer most wicked persecutions and most cruel effusions of blood in those who have despised that destroyer, until the two witnesses of truth, who will most strongly uphold the Church, display near the consummation of the world the brightness of justice and uprightness.

What is this? When the son of perdition has deceptively gained confidence and strength in his contrary teaching, [Col. 0714B] then the Church too, in the course of her hastening, will be drenched in most noble blood; and there she herself will then be fully built into a heavenly dwelling. For you, O streets of Jerusalem, will then shine in the finest gold through the blood of the saints, because the devil will then be extinguished, since he has persecuted the members of the heavenly King; so that, through his own great terror, he will be reduced to nothing.

But, O human beings who desire to dwell in those things, flee him, and worship God who created you. For in six days God completed His works, and on the seventh He rested from His work. What is this? The six days are the six numbers of the age; but in the sixth new miracles were brought forth into the world, so that on the sixth day too God completed His works. But now the world, in the seventh number [Col. 0714C] of the age before the last day, is as on the seventh day. How? The prophets completed their voices; my Son also fulfilled my will in the world; and the Gospel has openly been preached throughout the whole world. It has also remained well founded through me during the period of the periods of the complete number, and through more years of that complete number, despite much diversity in human customs. But now the Catholic faith wavers among the peoples, and the Gospel limps in human beings; even the strongest volumes, which the most approved teachers expounded with much diligence, dissolve in shameful weariness, and the food of life, the divine Scriptures, has now grown lukewarm. Therefore I now speak through a human being who does not speak from the Scriptures [Col. 0714D] and has not been taught by an earthly master; but I who am, expound through her new secrets and many mysteries that have hitherto lain hidden in books—just as a person first prepares clay for himself and then distinguishes from it whatever forms he wishes according to his will.

O fruitful teachers of good gain, redeem your souls and cry out this word boldly; do not be unbelieving toward it. For if you despise it, you despise not it but me, who am true. You ought to nourish my people under my law, taking care until the appointed time of that healing, when every care for all labours shall fail. Yet concerning this time you have periods of periods of predetermined predestination, running toward that time [Col. 0715A] when the son of perdition will come. Therefore be strong and be fortified, my elect, taking heed lest you fall into the snare of death; rather raise the most victorious banner of these words and rush upon the son of iniquity. For amid the error of those paths that precede and follow the son of perdition, whom you call Antichrist, imitate the footsteps of him who taught you the way of truth when he appeared in the flesh in the world with great humility and not with pride. Therefore hear and understand. For the Spirit speaks to the Church concerning the time of the final error.

Death will rush into the Church at that very hour when, at the end of times, the accursed one, the son of cursing, comes—he who is the curse of curses—as my Son testifies in the Gospel concerning the city of most evil error, saying: “And you, Capernaum, will you perhaps be exalted unto heaven? You shall descend unto hell” (Matthew 11). [Col. 0715B] This means: O you cave of iniquity, being a pit of concealment and possessing the wings of hypocrites’ pretence, how could you stand upon the height of walls, when your eye beholds the wickednesses of vices that hide burning light amid filth, saying: “Who is like the parricide in hypocrisy, whom fools call ruler?” Will you have heaven in miraculous signs when you dip your finger in the abyss? How? Your works will seek the bottom of hell, in whose voracity you will lie swallowed up; so that even hell will vomit forth that stench in which the world will see the bitterness of death in the destroyer [Col. 0715C] of destructions.

But there ought not to be a head without a belly and without the other members. The head of the Church is the Son of God; the belly and the other following members are the Church with her children. Yet the Church is not yet perfect in her members and children; but on the last day, when the number of the elect is fulfilled, then the Church too will be complete. And then, on the final day, there will be a disturbance of the world, when I, God, shall cleanse the four elements together with what is mortal in human flesh; and then, at the consummation of the age, there will be full joy for the offspring of the Church.

For, as was said beforehand, God completed His works in six days. The five days are the five numbers of the age; in the sixth, new miracles were proclaimed on earth, just as on the sixth day the first human being [Col. 0715D] was formed. But now the sixth number is finished and the seventh number has been reached, in which the course of the world is now set as on the seventh day of rest, because the labour which formerly the strongest teachers undertook in the depth of the sealed-up seals of the holy Scriptures is now open and must openly be brought forth, in the simplicity of words such as the words of this book, as if on the seventh day of rest. For six days are for work, and the seventh is for rest. There is no other number of days. What remains is not for you, O human being, to know, but lies in the Father’s secret. But you, O human beings, in this time have a period of periods in your course before that murderer comes who will desire to pervert the Catholic faith. But what will happen thereafter—neither the time nor the moment is for you to know, [Col. 0716A] just as you cannot know what comes after the seven days of the week. The Father alone knows this, who has placed these matters in his own power. Concerning the days of the week or the periods of the times of the age, you, O human being, need know no more.

But after the five numbers of the age I brought forth heavenly miracles for the world, just as on the five days another creation had been made before humankind, which is subject to humankind. Thus too the fullness of unbelievers and Jews had come about; the diverse schisms of diverse evils among both gentile and Jewish peoples had boiled over; the law and prophecy had already sweated; and all peoples had been tested both in evils and in goods before my only-begotten Son took flesh from a virgin [Col. 0716B]. For it had not been decreed that he should be sent until all these things had first occurred, so that all justice might be proved in him and all injustice might take offence at him. If my Son had come earlier, this would have been done, as it were, foolishly—like a person who imprudently wishes to gather crops before they are ripe. Or if his incarnation had been postponed until the very end of the world, he would then come suddenly like a bird-catcher who deceitfully catches birds when they do not know how they have entered his net.

But my Son came at that time as when the day, after the ninth hour, is already turning toward evening: that is, when the day’s greatest strength has already departed and cold begins to be present. So, after the five numbers of the world, my Son came to the world when the world was already running toward its setting [Col. 0716C]. What then? Coming, he opened the marrow of the law, where he changed the water of the law into the wine of the Gospel, and where he caused the greatest streams of virtues to flow forth. He accomplished this by coming at so fitting a time, so that the ecclesiastical virtues kindled by the Holy Spirit might be strengthened in people by firm roots, and so that virginity, which he brought in himself, might spring up and spread into most worthy shoots of flowers.

But the mad murderer, namely the son of perdition, will come in a very short time, when the day is departing and the sun is hidden in its setting—that is, when the final time is already falling and the world abandons its course. But hear this testimony, O my faithful ones, and [Col. 0716D] understand it devoutly for your protection, lest the error of that destroyer, coming suddenly while you are unaware, cast you headlong into the ruin of unbelief and perdition. Therefore arm yourselves and prepare yourselves for the most mighty battle, forewarned in this manner by the most faithful fortifications.

For when that time comes in which that most wicked deceiver will appear horribly, the mother who will bear this deceiver into the world was, from childhood in her girlhood, full of vices through diabolical arts and reared in a desert of rejection among most wicked people. There—without her parents’ knowing it, and without the knowledge of those among whom she lives, because the devil persuades her to go there—he deceives and fashions her according to his own will, as though he were a holy angel. Therefore she separates herself from people so that she may more easily be concealed. Hence she secretly joins herself with some men, though few, in the most wicked robbery of fornication; and in such zeal for shamefulness she defiles herself with them, as though a holy angel commanded her to accomplish the heat of that perversity. Thus, in the most burning ardour of that fornication, she conceives the son of perdition, not knowing from the seed of which of those men she has conceived him. But Lucifer, the serpent of old, delighting in that shamefulness, breathes upon this conception with his arts by my just judgment and possesses it wholly with all his powers in that mother’s womb, so that that destroyer comes forth from his mother’s womb full of the diabolical spirit. Then she avoids her customary fornication and openly tells the foolish and senseless people [Col. 0717B] that she has no husband and does not know the father of her child; but she calls the fornication she committed holy. Hence the people consider and call her holy.

Thus the son of perdition is reared by diabolical arts until a more vigorous age, always withdrawing himself from the people who know him. But at times his mother displays him by certain magical arts both to people who worship God and to those who do not, causing him to be seen and loved by them. When he reaches full age, he will openly teach a contrary doctrine, opposing me and my elect, and acquiring such strength that in his great power he will attempt to raise himself above the clouds. For by my just judgment I permit him to exercise his will in diverse creatures, [Col. 0717C] because, just as the devil said in the beginning, “I shall be like the Most High” (Isaiah 14), and fell, so I also permit that same devil to fall at the last time when in this his son he says, “I am the Saviour of the world.” And just as every generation of the faithful recognized that Lucifer was a liar when he wished in the beginning of days to be like God, so every faithful person will see that the son of iniquity is a liar when, before the last day, he makes himself like the Son of God.

He is indeed the most evil beast, killing people who deny him; allying himself with kings, leaders, princes, and the rich; casting down humility and raising up pride; and subjecting the world to himself by diabolical art [Col. 0717D]. For his power extends to the edge of the wind, so that he seems to stir the air, bring fire down from heaven, and produce lightning, thunder, and hail; even to overturn mountains, dry up waters, take their greenness from woods, and restore to them again the sap of their verdure. For he displays such illusions in diverse creatures, namely in their moisture, greenness, and dryness. Nor does he cease to practise his deceptions upon human beings. How? He will seem to inflict sickness upon the healthy and health upon the sick, to cast out demons, and sometimes to raise the dead. How? When at some time someone has departed from life whose soul is in the power of that devil, he will sometimes display his illusions around the corpse of the departed person, by my permission [Col. 0718A], making that corpse move as if alive. Yet he will sometimes be permitted to do this only for a very brief hour and not for a longer space, lest by this presumption the glory of God be mocked and held of no account.

Some who see this will trust in him; others, wishing nevertheless to retain their former faith, will always desire him to be favourable to them. Yet, not wishing to injure them more harshly, he inflicts certain illnesses upon them. When they seek medicine and the assistance of physicians and cannot be healed, they will run to him, trying whether he can heal them. When he sees them coming to him, he removes from them the weakness that he had inflicted. Therefore, loving him greatly, they will believe in him. Thus many will be deceived when they darken the eyes of the inward person [Col. 0718B], through which they ought to look toward me; wishing, in the testing of their mind, to know as though some novelty those things which they see with external eyes and touch with their hands, while despising those invisible things which remain in me and must be grasped by true faith. For mortal eyes cannot see me; rather, I show my miracles in shadow to those to whom I will. But no one will see me while remaining in a mortal body, except in the shadowing of my mysteries, as I spoke to my servant Moses, as it is written: “For no human being shall see me and be able to live” (Exodus 33).

This means: A mortal person cannot direct the gaze of mortal nature upon the brightness of my divinity while continuing to possess mortal life in corruptible ash [Col. 0718C], amid the change of passing time—that is, while leaving one life and passing to another—because all living things have been made firm through me, and because I live and there is no change in me. For as a gnat cannot live if it throws itself into a flame of fire, so neither could a mortal human being endure if he saw the flashing brilliance of my divinity. But while mortal people are burdened by the weight of their mortality, I show myself to them in shadow, just as a painter makes known invisible things to people through images in his painting. If, O human being, you love me, I shall embrace you and warm you with the heat of the Holy Spirit. For when you look upon me with good intention and recognize me in your faith, then I too [Col. 0718D] shall be with you. But those who despise me turn themselves toward the devil, because they are unwilling to know me. Therefore I reject them.

The devil mocks and deceives these same people however he pleases, so that they think true whatever he shows them. He instils this very art of deception into those who trust in him, so that in this art they deceitfully display to people diverse portents in creatures according to their own will. Nevertheless, they cannot transform either the elements or other creatures made by God into another form; rather, only by their deceptions do they fashion certain monstrosities, like certain clouds, in those who believe them. For Adam too, when he sought more than he ought to have, lost the glory of Paradise. Thus these people too lose the sight and hearing of the inward person, because they abandon God and worship the devil [Col. 0719A].

In this manner the son of perdition works the deceptions of his arts in the elements, showing in them beauty, sweetness, and pleasantness according to the desires of the people he deceives. But this power is promised to him so that the faithful may see in right faith that the devil has no power in good things, but only in the evils of eternal death. Whatever this son of iniquity does, he does in power, pride, and cruelty, having no mercy, humility, or discernment. Rather, with command and great astonishment he drives people to follow him. For he wins over very many peoples [Col. 0719B], telling them to carry out their desires freely, not binding themselves excessively by vigils or fasts, and proposing to them that they should love only their God, whom he pretends to be, so that thus, freed from hell, they may reach life. Therefore, deceived in this manner, they say: “Oh, woe to those miserable people who lived before these times, because they afflicted their lives with dreadful torments, alas, not knowing the mercy of our God!”

For he shows them treasures and riches, permits them to feast according to their desires, and confirms his teaching through deceptive signs, so that they think they ought in no way to restrain and chastise their bodies. He also commands them to observe circumcision and Judaism in accordance with Jewish customs [Col. 0719C], making lighter for them, according to their wishes, the stricter precepts of the Law which the Gospel transforms into grace through worthy penitence. And he says, “Whoever turns to me, that person’s sins will be wiped out, and he will live with me forever.” He also rejects the baptism and Gospel of my Son, and derides all those commandments handed down to the Church. Again, in diabolical mockery, he says to those who serve him: “See who and what sort of madman he was who, through his lies, established these observances for a simple people.

“But I desire to die for you and for your glory, and to rise from death. Thus I shall free my people from hell, so that henceforth you may live gloriously with me in my kingdom”—which that deceiver had first pretended to accomplish. [Col. 0719D] Then he tells his beloved followers to strike him with a sword and wrap him in a clean shroud until the day of his resurrection. Thus they are deceived into thinking that they kill him and fulfil his commands in this way. Afterwards, pretending to rise again, he produces the writing of dire cursing as though it were the salvation of souls; handing it to people as a sign, he orders them to worship him. But if any believer, through love for my name, refuses, he will be consumed by him with the dreadful torture of torments. Therefore all who see or hear these things will be shaken by the greatest astonishment and doubt, as my beloved John also shows, saying: “And I saw one of his heads as if slain unto death, and the wound of his death was healed; and the whole earth wondered after the beast” (Apoc. [Col. 0720A] 12).

This means: I, the lover of God’s mysteries, saw the deceitful and accursed one surrounding all the holiness of the saints with the greatest and innumerable iniquities and wearying it with manifold vices. By his lying acts he will imitate the shedding of his blood in being killed and thus dying—not falling in his body, but in a deceitful shadow, as though he had been struck and were dying. Therefore, amid the error of his deceptive wounds, having pretended as though dead, he will pretend as though he has risen from the sleep of death. Thus he will seize all people throughout the earth in marvellous and terrible astonishment at the horror of this accursed one, just as the people were amazed at the greatness and strength of Goliath when they saw him standing armed against them in battle. And so, as you see, the pillars of my elect will seem to be shaken with the great stupefaction of fear by both these torments and the contrary, monstrous, and terrible signs which the son of perdition will produce [Col. 0720B], giving forth the groan of lamentable distress.

Yet I shall send out my two witnesses, whom I have reserved until that time in the secret of my will—namely Enoch and Elijah—that they may oppose him and lead the erring back to the way of truth. They will show the faithful the most strong and powerful virtues, because when the words of their testimony in the mouth of each equally agree with one another, those hearing will put faith in them. For this reason these two witnesses of truth have been reserved by me for so long: so that when they come forth, their speech [Col. 0720C] may be held and made firm in the hearts of my elect, and so that from this the shoot of my Church may endure in great humility.

And they will say to the children of God whose names are in the book of life: “O you upright in heart and elect in the glorious praise of the blessed graces of life, hear and understand what we declare to you confidently. This accursed one was sent by the devil in order to lead into error the souls that subject themselves to his commands. We were removed from this world, kept in the secrets of God that are hidden from human beings, so that we were not amid human anxiety and distress. For we have been reserved for this purpose and sent to you: to oppose the errors of that destroyer. Therefore see whether we are like you either in bodily stature or in age.”

And all who wish to know and confess the true God will follow these two ancient and truthful witnesses, who bear the banner of God’s justice, abandoning wicked error. For they will shine in great proclamations before God and before the people, passing through streets, marketplaces, cities, and every other place wherever the son of perdition has breathed forth his contrary doctrine [Col. 0720D], and performing in them many signs in the Holy Spirit, so that all people who see them will be led into the greatest astonishment. These great signs will be given them, established upon the firm rock, so that those contrary and false signs may be cast away. For as lightning burns and consumes, so the son of perdition will act in his perverse iniquity and wickedness, burning peoples by magical arts like the fire of lightning [Col. 0721A]. But Enoch and Elijah, with right doctrine as with a thunderbolt, will terrify and cast down his whole host, thus establishing the faithful.

Nevertheless, when they are at last killed by him under the permission of my will, they will obtain in heaven the reward of their labours. Then the flowers of their teaching will fall, because their voices will no longer be heard in the world; yet they will show good fruit in the elect, who despise the words and frenzy of diabolical art and are well established in hope of the heavenly inheritance, as Solomon shows concerning the good and upright person, saying: “In the house of the just is much strength, and in the fruits of the wicked is disturbance” (Proverbs 15). This means: In the keen dwelling where there is no destruction or misfortune [Col. 0721B] is the special mirror of God’s eye in the upright person, in which that same eye sees the strength of his miracles as in the stroke of a striking sword. But in advancing deeds, like the growing fruits of the proud heart which builds ruins in its own pleasures, there will be that sadness, because the proud heart does not trust in the hope that flourishes in heavenly fullness.

But, as you see that monstrous head has moved itself from its place with such a crash that the whole aforesaid female image is shaken thereby in all its members: this means that when the son of perdition, being the head of iniquity, raises himself in much proud arrogance from the small error of wickedness fastened within him and seizes a greater error—namely, wishing to be exalted above all [Col. 0721C]—that is, when his deceptions are about to receive their end, the whole Church in all her children, both greater and lesser, will be cast into the greatest fear, awaiting the madness of his presumption.

And as it were a great mass of much dregs is joined to that head, whence it raises itself upon a certain mountain and attempts to ascend to the height of the heavens. This is because the greatest arts of diabolical snares, bringing much uncleanness and attending upon that same son of iniquity, supply him with the wings of pride and raise him to such presumption that he thinks he can penetrate even the heavenly secrets. How? For when he has fulfilled the whole will of the deceiving devil, so that by God’s just judgment he will no longer at all be permitted to possess such great power of iniquity and cruelty [Col. 0721D], he will gather his whole host and tell those who believe in him that he wishes to go to heaven. But as the devil did not know that the Son of God would be born for the redemption and salvation of souls, so this most wicked one, while involving himself in the deadly evil of all evils, will not know that the mightiest blow of God’s hand is coming upon him.

And behold, like a sudden stroke of thunder, it strikes that head with such force that it casts it down from that mountain and makes it send forth its spirit into death. For the power of God, manifesting itself, casts down that same son of perdition by such might of its zeal that he falls from the pride by which he had raised himself against God, by the great headlong plunge of his presumption; and, utterly consumed, [Col. 0722A] he vomits out his vital breath into the death of eternal damnation. For just as the temptations of my Son ended when, tempted by the devil, he said, “Go away, most foul Satan,” and Satan fled terrified, so too these temptations which the son of iniquity inflicts upon the Church will receive their end in this zeal of mine.

Then suddenly a stinking mist envelops that entire mountain, in which that head is wrapped in such filth that the people standing by are cast into the greatest terror. For a most unclean, intolerable, and hellish stench will fill the whole place of his exaltation, in which that most wicked accuser had seethed with such uncleanness and stench that, by God’s just judgment, neither his beginning nor his end will henceforth be held in memory [Col. 0722B]. For when those peoples see his corpse lying voiceless on the ground and drenched in much corruption, they will know that they have been deceived, while that mist remains somewhat longer around the mountain. For that stench, embracing his diabolical exaltation, shows it to be unclean, so that those deceived by him, seeing that stench and uncleanness, may turn away from their error and return to truth. For the people standing by, seeing these things, are shaken with great fear, because the sight produces the greatest horror, so that they utter mournful cries and tearful complaints and say that they have gravely erred.

And behold, the feet of the aforesaid female image appear white, giving forth a brightness beyond the brightness of the sun. This means that the strength of the foundation and [Col. 0722C] the support of the bride of my Son will display much brightness of faith and demonstrate that beauty which surpasses every beauty of earthly splendour. When the son of perdition has been cast down, as has been said, many of those who had erred will return to truth. But after the fall of that impious one, let no mortal human being ask when the last day will come in the dissolution of the world; for he cannot know it, because the Father has kept it hidden in the secrecy of his counsel. Therefore prepare yourselves for judgment, O human beings.

But as was said before, the son of perdition with his father the devil and all his arts will, at the last time, be overcome in great confusion by my Son, the mightiest warrior; just as Samson’s strongest enemies were cast down in his prefiguration, as it is written in Sacred History: “And when he had violently shaken the columns, the house fell upon all the princes and the rest of the multitude who were there; and by dying he killed far more than he had killed while alive” (Judges 16). This means: The Synagogue was first joined to the Son of God, namely to the strongest Samson. To her he imparted, in his wonderful teaching, those hidden things concealed in the Old Testament, benignly opening for her the inward sweetness of the Law, which was stronger than a lion. But she deceived him, causing his secrets to be mocked; she was unwilling to look to his teaching and despised it with the great arrogance of pride. Therefore, moved by this, he foretold that the kingdom of God would be taken away from her and given to another people. Thus, ascending to the city of Jerusalem amid many signs and a very great crowd, after the unbelief of those who spread their garments in the way had been slain [Col. 0723A], he fulfilled through miracles what he had promised to those by whom he had been betrayed through his bride.

And in that ardour he abandoned his bride when he foretold that her house would be left desolate. But the father of that bride, namely diabolical deception, joined her to another husband—that is, to unbelief. Then the Son of God sent out the cunning foxes, namely the apostles, who burned the harvests of his enemies with the fire of the Holy Spirit—that is, who turned the legal precepts toward spiritual understanding. Thus the Synagogue was burned with her father, namely by the overthrow of the Synagogue’s perverse unbelief. Then he killed the unbelievers with great signs and astounding miracles, so that all trembled in great astonishment when they said that they feared the Romans would come and take away their place and nation. Therefore they assembled their council to destroy him; but he hid himself on the mountain in prayer, saying that, if it were possible, that cup might pass from him. But Judas Iscariot betrayed him, handing him over into the most cruel hands of his enemies.

And he hid the power of his strength, which he had in his hair—that is, in his Father—which is unknown to all people except insofar as it is grasped in faith, just as hairs are seen upon a person’s head. Later, when he willed to suffer, he showed the power of his strength, namely by taking up the jawbone of an ass when he told the daughters of Jerusalem not to weep for him but for themselves; thus killing them—that is, most truthfully foretelling to them the terror of the evils to come [Col. 0723C]. And when he was wearied on the cross and thirsty, the fountain of true faith flowed from the gentile people; he did not disdain to drink from it, also saying that thus it was finished. Therefore, when he gave up his spirit, he afterwards descended into Gehenna, namely to the harlot woman, while his enemies besieged him by setting guards at his tomb. But rising from death, he sought the heavenly kingdom with the two gates—that is, with his special elect—and with the common people whom he freed from hell.

But thus the most beautiful bride, namely the Church, joined to him, most diligently asked him how she might come to know his strength. Yet he opened his powers to her not suddenly, but gradually and with discernment. How?

As soon as they had first received the Catholic faith in the Old Law and in the New, some of them thought that they ought to walk on until complete amendment with the binding of moist sinews that had not yet attained perfect dryness. Hence the Church, still unformed, said to many crowds: “This is the strength of my bridegroom.” And the people, hearing this, [Col. 0724A] wished by a sudden impulse to worship God only in hearing words, and not to live in the meaning of the Holy Spirit. But thus his strength was not recognized.

Then virginity, like new ropes that had never been used in work—just as virginity had not previously been held in glory—was nobly raised up. This binding indeed touched the Son of God strongly, yet did not fully reveal him. But the Church, raising herself on high, said: “O my friends, these are the greatest powers of my bridegroom.” And immediately, amid a great tumult, a large people rushed upon him, saying: “In his greatest strength we have seized him.” Yet not even thus were his powers made manifest.

Afterward the Church was strengthened in the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, as in his seven locks, these [Col. 0724B] being fastened by a strong nail in the firmament of the apostolic preachers. Therefore, with the net of faith woven in this way, the Church cried: “O how strong is my bridegroom in his seven locks!” And all peoples who heard her rushed upon him, thinking that he possessed no greater powers. But in this manner also his strength was not known.

Thereupon the Church shed many tears, because she did not know the strength of the Holy Trinity, saying that she had indeed seen the humanity of the Son of God, but had not yet perfectly understood his divinity. Therefore he, moved in his beloved John, disclosed the secrets of the Holy Trinity—as much as it was permitted for a human being to know—in the honor of the Father and in the burning ardor of the Holy Spirit. And thus, reclining his head in the bosom of his bride, he will rest there until the greatest [Col. 0724C] schisms that are to occur in the son of perdition; there his strength will be cut off when his locks are shorn, when people at that time will strive to follow the son of perdition rather than himself, saying: “What is this, O God, that we see such and so great miracles?” Thus his strength is effaced, when true faith now seems to be obscured in the blindness of unbelief.

But his powers will rise again when Enoch and Elijah appear. Therefore, violently shaking pride and presumption, he will cast down the son of perdition with all his diabolical arts and his other vices. And he will crush diabolical vices much more harshly when the Church, bearing the Christian name, passes from the present and temporal age to eternity, than [Col. 0724D] he did formerly while divine worship still flourished temporally in the world. What does this mean? Because, when the world itself is already coming to its end, then both diabolical persecutions and the most powerful workings of virtues will also cease temporally among human beings.

But whoever has keen ears of inner understanding, let that person, in the burning love of my mirror, pant after these words and write them in the conscience of his or her mind.

## TWELFTH VISION

[Col. 0723]

**SUMMARY.—**That in the last time the world will be dissolved by many calamities, as a human being is dissolved in the hour of death. That all creatures are suddenly moved, and whatever is mortal in air, water, or earth gives up life, and whatever foulness is in them will vanish. That the bodies of the dead, wherever they may be, rise again in the integrity of their bodies and sex. Concerning those rising again who are marked and those who are not marked. That the Son, to whom [Col. 0725] the Father gave power to execute judgment, will come to judgment in the form of humanity. The Gospel concerning this same matter. That those who are marked are swiftly caught up without difficulty to meet the just Judge, and their works will appear. That all the flowers—patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, monks, and other prelates—will shine. That meanwhile the heavens restrain their praises in silence when the Son pronounces the judicial sentence, with each person’s conscience laid open. Concerning the good and the evil who are to be judged. Concerning unbelievers who, already judged, do not come to the judgment. That, once the judgment has ended, the greatest repose of tranquillity arises. That eternal glory receives the elect with great praises, but hell swallows the reprobate with great howling. The Gospel concerning this same matter. How, when the judgment is ended, the elements, the sun, moon, and stars are changed for the better, and there will be no night. John’s words concerning the same matter.

[Col. 0725A] After these things I saw, and behold, all the elements and all creatures were shaken by a dreadful motion: fire, air, and water burst forth and caused the earth to move; lightning flashed and thunder crashed; mountains and forests fell, so that everything mortal gave up its life. And all the elements were cleansed, so that whatever had been filthy in them vanished in such a manner that it would appear no more.

And I heard a voice crying out with a great shout throughout the whole circuit of the earth and saying: “O you children of humankind who lie in the earth, all arise!” And behold, all human bones, wherever they were in the regions of the earth, were gathered as though in one moment, covered with their flesh, and all human beings rose with their limbs and bodies whole, in their own sex: the good shining in brightness [Col. 0725B] and the evil appearing in blackness, so that each person’s work was openly visible in that person.

And some of them were marked in faith, but others were not, so that among those marked some had before their faces what looked like a golden brightness, while others had something like a shadow; this was their mark. But suddenly a great radiance shone forth from the east. There, in a cloud, I saw the Son of Man coming with angelic choirs, in the countenance in which he had been in the world, his wounds stripped bare and open; and I saw him sitting above the seat of a throne flaming but not burning, with beneath him this greatest storm of the world’s purification.

And those who had been marked were caught up as if in a whirlwind to meet him in the air, where I had previously seen that brightness which signifies the secret of the heavenly Creator, [Col. 0725C] the good being there separated from the evil. But he, in a gentle voice, as the Gospel declares, blessed the just with the heavenly kingdom; and in a terrible voice, as it is likewise written, assigned the unjust to infernal punishments. Yet no other inquiry or answer concerning their works was made there than that which the Gospel’s voice shows, since each person’s work, whether good or evil, appeared manifestly in that person.

But those who had not been marked stood far away in the northern region with the diabolical company; nor did they come to this judgment. Yet, seeing all these things as if in a whirlwind, they awaited the end of the judgment and uttered bitter groans within themselves. And thus, when the judgment had been completed, lightning, thunder, winds, and storms ceased; and whatever in the elements was transitory [Col. 0725D] suddenly vanished, and the greatest tranquillity came to be.

Then the elect, suddenly made resplendent beyond the brightness of the sun, sought the heavenly places with the Son of God and the blessed companies of angels in great joy, while the reprobate, with the devil and his angels, [Col. 0726A] were moving toward infernal places with great howling. Thus heaven received the elect and hell swallowed the reprobate. But suddenly such joys and such praises arose in heaven, and such sadness and such howlings in the lake of the abyss, beyond what human understanding can utter.

And immediately all the elements shone in the greatest serenity, as though their blackest skin had been stripped away: so that fire no longer had heat, air density, water violent swelling, or earth any fragility.
