The sun also, moon, and stars, like abundant ornament in the firmament, gleamed with great brilliance and beauty; and they remained fixed without the motion of their circuit, so that day and night were no longer distinguished. Thus there was no night, but day. And it was finished.

Again [Col. 0726B] I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “These mysteries show the last times, in which temporal times will be changed into the eternity of that radiance which is without end. For the last times will be wearied by many dangers, and the setting of the world will be shown by various signs. For, as you see, on that final day the whole globe of the earth will be shaken by terrors and battered by storms, so that whatever in it is perishable and mortal will be ended by these calamities. For then, the course of the world having been completed, it will no longer be able to endure, but will be consummated according to the divine ordinance.

“For as a human being, when he or she is about to end, is overcome and cast down by many illnesses, and is dissolved with much pain even in the very hour of death, [Col. 0726C] so great adversities will precede the end of the world and dissolve it at its end with diverse terrors, because the elements will then display their terrors, since they will no longer be able to exercise them.

“By a sudden and unexpected motion at this end, the elements are loosened, all creatures are moved, fire bursts forth, air is dissolved, water pours out, earth is shaken, lightning burns fiercely, thunder crashes, mountains are split, forests fall, and whatever is mortal in air, water, or earth gives up life. For fire moves the whole air, and water fills the whole earth; and in this way all things are cleansed, so that whatever foulness is in the world vanishes as though it had not been, just as salt dissolves when it is put into water.

[Col. 0726D] “But, at the divine command, when the summons to rise again has been received, the bones of the dead, wherever they may be, are joined together in their proper place as in the twinkling of an eye and are covered with their flesh. They are delayed in no way, but whether they have been consumed by fire, water, bird, or [Col. 0727A] beast, they are restored most swiftly. Thus the earth gives them back as salt sweats out from water, because my eye knows all things and nothing can be hidden from me.

“Thus all human beings rise in soul and body, with no contraction or cutting off of their limbs, but in the integrity both of their body and of their sex, as in the twinkling of an eye: the elect bearing the brightness of their good works and the reprobate carrying the blackness of their unhappy deeds, so that their works are not hidden there but openly appear in them.

“And some of them are marked in faith, while others are not, so that the consciences of those who have faith shine through the works of faith in the brightness of wisdom, whereas those of others appear in the darkness of their neglect. [Col. 0727B] By these they are openly distinguished, because the former fulfilled faith in works, while the latter extinguished it in themselves. But some do not have the mark of faith, because they did not wish to have knowledge of the living and true God either in the Old Law or in the New Grace.

“And then, in the brightness of eternal light, yet in a cloud by which heavenly glory is hidden from the reprobate, the Son of God will come to judge the human race itself, surrounded by the heavenly army, in the form of his humanity and passion which, in the Father’s will, he suffered for the salvation of humankind. For the Father gave him this: that, because he had visibly dwelt in the world, he should judge the visible things of the world, as he himself shows in the Gospel, saying: ‘And he gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man’ [Col. 0727C] (John 5).

“This means: the Father bears witness concerning his Son. What does this mean? The Father gave authority to the Son, because he, always remaining with the Father in divinity, but receiving humanity from his mother according to his humanity, also received from the Father that every creature should perceive him as the Son of God, just as every creature subsists, created by God in the creation of its own form. Therefore all works are discerned by the Son, whatever their rank or lowliness, and he places them according to where they are to be placed. For because he was a tangible and visible human being in the world, he also discerns according to justice those things which were visible in the world, appearing terrible in judicial power to the unjust but gentle [Col. 0727D] to the just; judging them in such a way that even the elements feel their purification.

“Then those also who are marked are caught up to meet the just Judge, not with difficulty but with great speed, so that, because they had faith believing in God, the works of faith also appear manifestly in them. There too the knowledge of God does not fail to know their deeds, both good and evil, as was shown to you. For there good and evil are separated, because their works are unlike.

“For there it appears most certainly, in both the evil and the good, how they sought God in infancy, childhood, youth, old age, or decrepit age. There too shine all the flowers of my Son: namely, the patriarchs and prophets who lived before his incarnation, [Col. 0728A] and the apostles who dwelt with him in the world; and the martyrs, confessors, virgins, widows, all of whom faithfully imitated him; and those who were set over my Church in secular as well as spiritual matters; also anchorites and monks, who made themselves lowly through the chastisement and mortification of their flesh for the name of my Son, showing this in their clothing as they imitated the angelic order with great humility and charity.

“But whoever seeks me in the contemplative life because they say that this life is more glorious than that one is before me as nothing. But whoever seeks me in humility, in that manner of life which has been given by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, that person I shall exalt to the foremost places in the heavenly homeland.

“Then the heavens again restrain their praises in silence [Col. 0728B] while the Son of God pronounces the judicial sentence upon both just and unjust. They listen with reverent honor to how he judges them: gently granting heavenly joys to the just and terribly sending the unjust to infernal punishments. But there will be no greater excuses or examination of their deeds than this: that the consciences of human beings, both good and evil, are naked and open there.

“The just who receive there the words of the most equitable Judge have indeed done many works of justice; nevertheless, while they lived in the world, they did not possess them in the fullness of perfection, and therefore they must now be judged in them. But the unjust who feel judicial severity there have indeed perpetrated evil deeds; yet they did not do them in ignorance of the divine majesty [Col. 0728C] which is in the iniquity of unbelief already condemned. Therefore they will not escape that Judge’s sentence, because all things must be weighed in an equal balance.

“But those who are not marked in faith, because they did not believe in God, meanwhile remain in the northern region—that is, of perdition—with the diabolical company, and do not come to this judgment. Yet, seeing it in shadow and awaiting its end, they groan greatly within themselves, because they persevered in unbelief and did not know the true God. For before baptism they neither worshipped the living God in the Old Testament nor, under the Gospel, received the remedy of baptism; but they persevered under the curse of Adam’s fall, [Col. 0728D] bearing the punishments of condemnation. Therefore they are found already judged in the unbelief of their crimes.

“And so, when the judgment has ended, the terrors of the elements, lightning, thunder, and winds in storms cease; and everything perishable and transitory falls away and will appear no more, as snow ceases to be when it melts in the heat of the sun. By divine dispensation the greatest quiet of tranquillity thus arises.

“And so the elect, possessing the brightness of eternity, seek heavenly joys in great glory together with their head, namely my Son, and with the glorious heavenly army. And the reprobate proceed, with the devil and his angels, to eternal punishments in much affliction, where they eternally see the eternal death prepared for them, because they followed their own desires rather than [Col. 0729A] my commandments. Thus heaven receives the elect into the glory of eternity because they loved the ruler of the heavens, and hell swallows the reprobate because they did not cast off the devil. So great are the praises of all joys resounding in heavenly glory, and so great the howlings of all groans arising in hell, beyond what human understanding can grasp. For the former possess eternal life, while the latter have eternal death, as my Son says in the Gospel: ‘And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life’ (Matt. 25).

“This means: those who stink in the enticement of all evils and do not thirst to draw what is just from highest goodness are plunged, by the path of their unbelief and wickedness, into the punishments of eternal [Col. 0729B] perdition, receiving infernal torments according to their works. But the builders of the radiance of the heavenly Jerusalem, who faithfully attend to the gates of the daughter Zion, will shine in the light of eternal life, which the most chaste Virgin wonderfully brought to believers in the fruitfulness of her virginity.

“And, as you see, after all these things have been accomplished, the elements will shine in the greatest brightness and beauty, with every hindrance of blackness and filth removed. For fire will then gleam like the dawn without heat; air will shine most pure without density; water will stand clear and gentle without the force of overflowing or submersion; and earth will appear strongest and most level, without any fragility or unevenness, [Col. 0730A] all these things having been transformed into great tranquillity and beauty.

“But the sun, moon, and stars also, like most precious stones in gold, will gleam in the firmament with much brightness and the greatest splendor. Nor will they any longer have the restless movement of their revolution by which day is distinguished from night, because, the world having ended, they are now in immutability. Therefore no darkness of night will henceforth appear, because then there is unending day, as my beloved John also testifies, saying: ‘And night shall be no more; and they shall need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will give them light’ (Rev. 22).

“This means: one who has a treasure sometimes withdraws it and sometimes brings it forth; so too night hides light, while day drives away darkness, bringing light to human beings. [Col. 0730B] It will not be so in the transformation of times, because then the shadow of night will be driven away. Thus the darkness of night will henceforth not appear, because that transformation will no longer need the light which human beings kindle to drive away the shadows of darkness. Nor will the sun then embrace mutability, though it now contains the times held in shadow. For then day will be without any change, because then the ruler of all things, by the brightness of his divinity, which no mutability obscures, illuminates those who in the world escaped darkness through his grace.”

But whoever has keen ears of inner understanding, let that person, in the burning love of my mirror, pant after these words and write them in the conscience of his or her mind.

## THIRTEENTH VISION

[Col. 0729]

**SUMMARY.—**A symphony concerning Saint Mary. Concerning the nine orders of heavenly spirits. Concerning the patriarchs and prophets. Concerning the apostles. Concerning the martyrs. Concerning the confessors. Concerning the virgins. The voice of harmony in lament for those recalled to the same ranks. In exhortation of the virtues and contradiction of diabolical arts. That God, because of his ineffable grace, must be praised without ceasing in heart and mouth. That symphony must be rendered in unanimity and concord. That the word signifies the body, symphony the spirit, harmony divinity, and the Word the humanity of the Son. That by the symphony of rationality the sluggish soul is aroused to watchfulness. That symphony softens hard hearts, induces the moisture of compunction, and calls upon the Holy Spirit. That the faithful person ought unceasingly to rejoice with every devotion. David’s words concerning the same matter.

[Col. 0729C] Then I saw a most luminous air, in which I heard, in all the meanings stated above, in a wondrous manner diverse kinds of music: in the praises of the citizens of heavenly joys, strongly persevering in the way of truth; in the laments of those recalled to the praises of those same joys; and in the exhortation of the virtues, exhorting themselves toward the salvation of peoples, against whom diabolical snares struggle. Yet the virtues themselves crush those snares, so that faithful human beings finally pass from sins to the heavenly realms through repentance.

And that sound, like the voice of a multitude symphonizing in harmony in praise of the heavenly ranks, said:

“O most radiant jewel, the serene beauty of the sun has been poured into you: a fountain leaping from the heart of the Father, which is his only Word, through whom he created the first matter of the world [Col. 0729D] and which Eve disturbed. This Word fashioned a human being in you, and you are that shining jewel from whom the Word himself brought forth all virtues, just as [Col. 0730C] in the first matter he brought forth all creatures.

“O sweetest branch, flowering from the root of Jesse, how great is the power that divinity looked upon the most beautiful daughter, as an eagle fixes its eye upon the sun, when the heavenly Father regarded the brightness of the Virgin and willed that his Word be incarnate in her. For, when the Virgin’s mind was enlightened in God’s mystical mystery, a wonderfully bright flower came forth from that Virgin.”

And again it said:

“O most glorious living light: O angels, who beneath divinity behold the divine eyes with the mystical obscurity of every creature in burning desires, and therefore can never be satiated! How glorious a form your joys possess, which in you remains untouched by every wicked deed, first arising in your lost fellow angel, [Col. 0730D] who wished to fly above the inwardly hidden pinnacle of God. Therefore that crooked one was plunged into ruin; but the counsel of God’s finger established the instruments of his fall, the instruments of his suggestive [Col. 0731A] counsel.

“For, O you angels who guard peoples, whose form shines in your faces; and O you archangels who receive the souls of the just; and you virtues, powers, principalities, dominions, and thrones, who are reckoned in the fifth secret number; and O you cherubim and seraphim, seal of God’s secrets: praise be to you, who behold the chamber of the ancient heart in the fountain. For you see the inner power of the Father, which breathes from his heart like a face.”

Again it said:

“O admirable men, who passed through hidden things, beholding through the eyes of the spirit and announcing in luminous shadow the sharp and living light, doubling in the branch which alone flowered from the entrance of rooted light: you ancient saints foretold the salvation of exiled souls immersed in death. You moved about like wheels, speaking wondrously of the mysteries of the mountain touching heaven, which passes through by anointing many waters, when among you also arose a shining lamp, which, running before that mountain, gives light.

[Col. 0731B] “O blessed roots, with whom the work of miracles—and not the work of crimes—was planted by the torrent in the path of transparent shadow! And O you ruminating fiery voice, running before the polishing stone which overturns the abyss: rejoice in your head. Rejoice in him whom many on earth did not see, though they called upon him ardently.”

And again it said:

“O host of warriors of the flower of the unthorned branch, you sound that circles the regions of the world, of minds gone mad, feasting with pigs: you conquered them through the helper poured in by the one who set roots in the tabernacles of the Father’s Word, full of work. You too are the noble people of the Savior, entering the way of the regeneration of water through the Lamb, who sent you with the sword among most savage dogs. They destroyed their glory in the works of their own fingers, setting what was not handmade under the subjection of their hands, in which they did not find him.

[Col. 0731C] “For, O most luminous company of apostles, rising in true knowledge and opening the enclosure of the devil’s teaching, washing captives in the fountain of living water: you are a most brilliant light in blackest darkness, and the strongest race of pillars, sustaining the Bride of the Lamb in all her ornaments. Through her joy, she herself, mother and virgin, is the foremost standard-bearer. For the spotless Lamb is the bridegroom, and his bride is spotless.”

Again it said:

“O most victorious triumphers, who, in the outpouring of your blood, entered the blood of the Lamb, greeting the building up of the Church, feasting with the slain calf! O how great is your reward, because while living you despised your bodies, imitating the Lamb of God and adorning his punishment, by which he brought you into the restoration of the inheritance.

“You flowers of roses, who are blessed in the greatest joys through the outpouring of your blood, fragrant and sweating in the purchase that flowed from the inward mind of counsel, abiding before the age in him in whom there was no establishment: from the head let honor be in your fellowship, you who are the instrument of the Church and who [Col. 0732A] poured forth abundantly in the wounds of your blood.”

And again it said:

“O most powerful successors of the lion, ruling between temple and altar in his ministry, as angels resound in praises and stand by peoples in help: you are among those who always do these things, having care for the office of the Lamb. O imitators of the exalted person in most precious and most glorious signification, how great is your adornment, where the human being proceeds, loosing and binding in God the sluggish and the wandering, even adorning the white and the black, and remitting great burdens. For you also possess the offices of the angelic order, and you know beforehand where the strongest foundations must be established. Therefore great is your honor.”

Again it said:

“O beautiful faces gazing upon God and building at dawn! O blessed virgins, how noble you are, in whom the King beheld himself, when in you he marked beforehand all heavenly adornments; and you are also a most sweet garden, fragrant in every ornament. O most noble greenness, rooted in the sun and shining in a white serenity in the wheel, which no earthly eminence comprehends: you are surrounded by the embraces of divine mysteries. You redden as dawn and burn as the flame of the sun.”

Then that sound, like the voice of a multitude in harmonious lament for those to be recalled to the same ranks, lamented thus:

[Col. 0732B] “O this is a lamenting voice of greatest sorrow. Ah, ah! A certain wondrous victory has risen in God’s wondrous desire, in which the delight of the flesh secretly hides itself. Alas, alas! Where will did not know crimes and where human desire fled wantonness, because so few come to you.

“Therefore mourn, mourn in these things, O innocence: you who did not lose integrity in good modesty and did not swallow there the avarice of the throat of the ancient serpent, because people attend to you so negligently. O living fountain, how great is your sweetness, who did not lose the faces of these persons in yourself, but keenly foresaw how you would draw away from the angelic fall those who thought themselves to possess that which may not so stand.

[Col. 0732C] “Therefore rejoice, daughter Zion, because God restores many to you, whom the serpent wished to cut off from you, and who now shine in greater light than would previously have been caused by them. For the living light says of these: ‘I caused the crooked serpent to stumble in his suggestion, which was not as full as he thought. Therefore I swore by myself that in these matters I did more and more than in them. O serpent, your joy would betray you, because in your suggestion I cut off that which was never found in your cruelty, O most shameful deceiver.’”

Again that sound, like the voice of a multitude, in the exhortation of the virtues to help human beings and in contradiction of the opposing diabolical arts—the virtues overcoming vices, and human beings at last returning through divine inspiration to repentance—cried out thus in harmony:

“We are virtues in God, and we remain in God. We serve the King of kings and separate evil from good. For we appeared in the first battle, where we were victorious when he fell who wished to fly above himself. Therefore let us now also fight, [Col. 0733A] helping those who invoke us, trampling down diabolical arts, and leading to blessed dwellings those who are willing to imitate us.”

### LAMENT OF SOULS PLACED IN THE FLESH

“O we are exiles. What have we done, turning aside toward sins? We ought to have been daughters of the King, but we fell into the shadow of sins. O living sun, carry us upon your shoulders into the most just inheritance which we lost in Adam. O King of kings, we fight in your battle.”

### INVOCATION OF THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“O sweet divinity, and O gentle life, in which I shall bear the splendid garment, receiving what I lost at my first appearance: I sigh toward you and call upon all the virtues.”

### RESPONSE OF THE VIRTUES

“O happy soul and O sweet [Col. 0733B] creature of God, built in the deep height of God’s wisdom, you love greatly.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“O gladly will I come to you, that you may give me the kiss of the heart.”

### THE VIRTUES

“We must fight with you, O daughter of the King.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“O grievous labor and O hard burden that I bear in the garment of this life, because it is too heavy for me to fight against the flesh.”

### THE VIRTUES

“O soul established by God’s will, and O happy instrument, why are you so weak against that which God crushed in virginal nature? You ought to overcome the devil in us.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“Help me by assisting me, that I may be able to stand.”

[Col. 0733C]

### THE KNOWLEDGE OF GOD

“See what it is with which you are clothed, daughter of salvation; be steadfast, and you will never fall.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“O I do not know what I should do or where I should flee! Alas for me, I cannot fulfill that with which I am clothed! Certainly I wish to cast it off.”

### THE VIRTUES

“O unhappy conscience, O wretched soul, why do you hide your face from your Creator?”

### THE KNOWLEDGE OF GOD

“You do not know, see, or understand him who established you.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“God created the world; I do him no injury if I wish to use it.”

### THE DEVIL

“Foolish one, foolish one, what profit is it to you to labor? Look upon the world, and it will embrace you with great honor.”

### THE VIRTUES

“Alas, alas! Let us virtues lament and mourn, because the Lord’s sheep flees from life.”

[Col. 0733D]

### HUMILITY

“I, Humility, queen of the virtues, say: Come to me, all virtues, and I shall nourish you in seeking the lost drachma and crowning her, happy in perseverance.”

### THE VIRTUES

“O glorious queen and O sweetest mediatrix, we shall gladly come.”

### HUMILITY

“Therefore, most beloved daughters, I hold you in the royal chamber. O daughters of Israel, God raised you up beneath the tree; therefore at this time remember his planting. Rejoice, then, daughters of Zion.”

### THE DEVIL

“What is this power, that there is no one besides God? But I say: Whoever wishes to follow me and my will, I shall give that person everything; but you, with your followers, have nothing that you can give, because you all do not even know what you are.”

[Col. 0734A]

### HUMILITY

“I, with my companions, know well that you are that ancient dragon who wished to fly above the summit, but God himself hurled you down into the depth of the abyss.”

### THE VIRTUES

“But we all dwell on high.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“O royal virtues, how beautiful and how shining you are in the highest sun, and how sweet is your dwelling! And therefore, alas for me, because I fled from you.”

### THE VIRTUES

“O fugitive, come, come to us, and God will receive you.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“Ah, ah! Burning delight swallowed me up in sins, and therefore I did not dare to enter to you.”

### THE VIRTUES

“Do not fear or flee, because the good shepherd seeks his lost sheep in you.”

[Col. 0734B]

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“Now it is necessary that you receive me, because I stink in the wounds with which the ancient serpent defiled me.”

### THE VIRTUES

“Run to us and follow those footsteps in which you will never fall in our fellowship, and God will heal you.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“I, a sinner who fled from life, full of ulcers, shall come to you so that you may give me the shield of redemption.”

### THE VIRTUES

“O fugitive soul, be strong and put on the armor of light.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“O entire army of the queen of virtues, and O her white lilies with rosy purple, bend down to me, because I have lived as an exile, estranged from you; help me, that I may rise in the blood of the Son of God. And O [Col. 0734C] true medicine, Humility, give me aid, because pride, wounding me by laying many scars upon me through many vices. Now I flee to you; therefore receive me.”

### HUMILITY

“O all virtues, receive the mourning sinner in her scars for the sake of Christ’s wounds, and lead her to me.”

### THE VIRTUES

“We wish to bring you back and do not wish to abandon you, and the whole heavenly army rejoices over you. Therefore it is fitting that we sound forth in symphony.”

### HUMILITY

“O wretched daughter, I wish to embrace you, because the great physician suffered hard and bitter wounds for you.”

### THE DEVIL

“Who are you, or whence do you come? You embraced [Col. 0734D] me, and I led you out; but now, in your return, you put me to shame. Yet I shall cast you down in my battle.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“I have learned that all your ways are evil, and therefore I fled from you; but now, O deceiver, I fight against you.”

### THE FAITHFUL SOUL

“Therefore, you, queen Humility, help me with your remedy.”

### HUMILITY

“O Victory, who overcame him likewise in heaven, run with your companions and bind this devil, all of you.”

### VICTORY TO THE VIRTUES

“O strongest and most glorious soldiers, come and help me conquer this deceiver.”

### THE VIRTUES

“O sweetest warrior at the torrent-fountain [Col. 0735A] that swallowed the ravening wolf, O glorious crowned one, we gladly fight with you against the deceiver of souls.”

### HUMILITY

“Bind him, then, O radiant virtues!”

VIRTUES. O our queen, we will obey you, and we will fulfil your commands in all things.

VICTORY. Rejoice, O companions, because the ancient serpent has been bound.

VIRTUES. Praise to you, Christ, king of the angels. O God, who are you, who held within yourself this great counsel, by which you destroyed the infernal draught among tax collectors and sinners, who now shine in heavenly goodness? Therefore, O king, let praise be to you. O almighty Father, from you flows a fountain in fiery ardour: lead your children into the straight wind of the waters’ sails, so that we too may thus lead them into the heavenly Jerusalem. [Col. 0735B] And these voices were like the voice of a multitude, when a multitude raises its voices on high. Their sound passed through me in such a way that I understood them without the difficulty of slowness. And I heard a voice from that same luminous air saying to me:

Praises must be given to the heavenly Creator with the unceasing voice of heart and mouth, since by his grace he establishes in heavenly seats not only those who stand upright and erect, but also those who have fallen and are bent low. Therefore you see, O human being, the most luminous air, signifying the brightness of the joy of the heavenly citizens. In it I hear, in all the meanings previously mentioned, a marvellously diverse kind of music: in the praises of the citizens of heavenly joys, who persevere strongly in the way of truth; [Col. 0735C] and in the lamentations of those called back to the praises of those same joys. For just as air encompasses and sustains the things beneath heaven, so, as you hear in all the wondrous works of God shown beforehand to you, sweet and delightful symphony resounds in joy: it proclaims the miracles of the elect dwelling in the heavenly city and persevering in God with sweet devotion; and, in lamentations, the bending low of those whom the ancient serpent attempts to destroy, yet whom divine power strongly leads to the fellowship of blessed joys. It brings forth in them those mysteries unknown to human minds inclined toward the earth, and does so in the exhortation of virtues exhorting themselves for the salvation of peoples against whom the snares of the devil contend, but which the virtues themselves crush, [Col. 0735D] so that faithful persons at last pass from sins to heavenly things through repentance. For there the virtues resist vices in the minds of believers for their redemption—vices by which they are wearied through the devil’s breath. But when these have been overcome with most powerful strength, persons who have slipped into sins return to repentance by divine prompting, when they investigate and bewail their former deeds, and consider and guard against those that follow.

Accordingly, that sound, like the voice of a multitude, makes harmony in praises concerning the heavenly ranks, because symphony, in unanimity and concord, meditates upon the glory and honour of the heavenly citizens, so that it raises upward what the word openly brings forth. Thus the word signifies the body, while symphony [Col. 0736A] manifests the spirit; for heavenly harmony proclaims divinity, while the word declares the humanity of the Son of God. And just as the power of God flies everywhere and encompasses all things, nor does any obstacle resist it, so the rational faculty of the human being has great power to sound forth in living voices and to awaken lethargic souls to vigilance in symphony. David demonstrates this in the symphony of his prophecy, and Jeremiah shows it in his lament with a mournful voice. So you too, O human being—who are a poor and fragile creature—hear in symphony the sound from the fiery ardour of virginal chastity; the sound in the embraces of the flowering rod of words; the sound from the sharpness of living lights shining in the heavenly city; the sound from the prophecy of profound sayings; the sound from the expansion [Col. 0736B] of the apostolate of wondrous words; the sound from the shedding of blood by those faithfully offering themselves; the sound from the priestly office of mysteries; and the sound from the virginal rank flowering in heavenly verdure. For God’s faithful creature resounds to the heavenly Creator in a voice of exultation and joy, and offers him frequent thanks. But you also hear the sound, like the voice of a multitude, resounding in harmony in the lamentations of those recalled to these same ranks. For symphony rejoices not only in the unanimity of exultation of those who strongly persevere in the way of uprightness, but also exults in the concord of the restoration of those who have fallen from the way of justice and are finally raised to true blessedness; for the good shepherd brought back the lost sheep to the flock with joy.

Likewise, as you hear, that sound, like the voice of a multitude, cries out in harmony in the exhortation of virtues aiding human beings and in the opposition to hostile diabolical devices, when virtues overcome vices and people at last return to repentance by divine inspiration. For there is a sweet union in the virtues that draw faithful persons to true blessedness, but a dreadful accumulation in the vices of diabolical snares. Yet this is not such that virtues do not overcome vices; rather, virtues wholly weaken them and lead those who agree with them, through the help of heavenly assistance, to eternal recompense by true repentance, as has also been shown to you in the voices of their harmony.

[Col. 0736D] For symphony softens hard hearts, brings into them the moisture of compunction, and calls upon the Holy Spirit. Therefore the voices you hear are like the voice of a multitude when a multitude lifts up its voices on high, because praises of jubilation uttered in the simplicity of unanimity and charity lead the faithful to that unanimity where there is no discord, making those placed upon earth yearn with heart and mouth for heavenly recompense. And their sound passes through you in such a way that you understand them without the difficulty of slowness, because wherever divine grace has worked, it removes every darkness of overshadowing, making pure and bright those things which are obscure to bodily senses in the weakness of flesh.

Therefore whoever faithfully understands God should offer him tireless praises [Col. 0737A] and unceasingly rejoice before him with faithful devotion, just as David my servant, suffused by me with the spirit of depth and height, exhorts when he says: “Praise him with the sound of the trumpet; praise him with psaltery and lyre. Praise him with timbrel and dance; praise him with strings and organ. Praise him with well-sounding cymbals; praise him with cymbals of jubilation; let every spirit praise the Lord” (Psalm 150).

This means: You who know, worship, and love God with simple intention and pure devotion, praise him with the sound of the trumpet—that is, with the faculty of reason—because when the fallen angel, together with those agreeing with him, fell into destruction, the companies of blessed spirits persevered reasonably in truth and clung to God with faithful love. And praise [Col. 0737B] him with the psaltery of profound devotion and with the lyre of honey-sweet song; for with the trumpet sounding comes the psaltery, and with the psaltery sounding comes the lyre. Thus, after the blessed angels persevering in the love of truth, and then after humankind was created, prophets arose with wondrous voices; the apostles followed them with most sweet words. And praise him with the timbrel of mortification and with the dance of exultation, because after the lyre comes the timbrel, and after the timbrel the dance exults. Thus, when the apostles preached words of salvation, martyrs endured diverse punishments in their bodies for the honour of God; from these there afterwards arose true teachers of the priestly office. And praise him with the strings of human redemption and with the organ of divine protection, because, when the dance exults, [Col. 0737C] the voices of strings and organ reveal themselves. Thus, when true teachers in the office of blessedness showed the truth, virgins came forth, who loved the Son of God as true man, as it were on strings, and worshipped him as true God, as it were on an organ, believing him true man and true God. What does this mean? Because when the Son of God assumed flesh for the salvation of human beings, he did not lose the glory of divinity. Therefore blessed virgins, choosing him as their bridegroom, apprehended him with faithful devotion as true man in betrothal and true God in chastity.

But praise him with well-sounding cymbals—that is, in those affirmations which make a good sound in true joy—when people lying in the depths [Col. 0737D] of sins, pricked by divine inspiration toward heavenly height, raise themselves upward from the depths. And praise him with cymbals of jubilation, namely in affirmations of divine praise, where powerful virtues, most strongly achieving victory, crush vices in human beings and lead them, persevering in good works with strong desire, to the blessedness of true recompense. Therefore let every spirit that has goodwill to believe in God and honour him praise the Lord—that is, him who is Lord of all—for it is fitting that one who desires life should glorify him who is life.

And again I heard a voice from the aforementioned luminous air saying: “O highest King, praise be to you, who accomplish these things in a simple and unlearned person.” But again [Col. 0738A] a voice from heaven cried out with the greatest outcry, saying:

Hear and attend, all you who desire to possess heavenly recompense and blessedness. O you people who have believing hearts and await heavenly recompense: receive these words and place them in your inmost hearts, and do not reject this admonition at the time of your visitation. For I, the witness of truth, the living and true God who speaks and does not keep silent, say—and say again—who will prevail against me? Whoever attempts it, I shall cast down. Therefore let no human being lay hold of a mountain that he cannot move, but remain in the valley of humility. But who crosses paths without water? One who tosses himself into a whirlwind and distributes fruits without refreshment. And how would my tabernacle [Col. 0738B] be there? Yet my tabernacle is there where the Holy Spirit pours out his irrigation. What does this mean? I am in the midst. How? Whoever worthily grasps me will fall neither into height nor depth nor breadth. What does this mean? Because I am that charity which blazing pride does not cast down, profound falls do not shatter, and the breadth of evils does not crush.

Can I not build upon the height of the sun’s footstool? The strong, who display their strength in valleys, despise me; the dull cast me away amid the sounds of whirlwinds; the wise refuse my food; and each person prepares a tower for himself according to his own will. But I shall confound these persons in one who is small and lowly, just as I cast down Goliath by a boy and overcame Holofernes through Judith. [Col. 0738C] Therefore whoever rejects the mystical words of this book, I shall stretch my bow over him, pierce him with the arrows of my quiver, throw his crown from his head, and make him like those who fell at Horeb when they murmured against me. And whoever utters curses against this prophecy, the curse uttered by Isaac shall come upon him. But whoever embraces it, holds it in his heart, and brings it forth upon level paths shall be filled with the blessing of heavenly dew. Whoever tastes it and commits it to memory shall become a mountain of myrrh, incense, and every spice, and an enlargement of many blessings, ascending from blessing to blessing [Col. 0738D] like Abraham; and, as a newly wedded bride of the Lamb, he shall join it to himself as a pillar before God, and the shadow of the Lord’s hand shall protect him. But if anyone rashly hides these words of God’s finger, diminishes them through his madness, or diverts them to another place for the sake of some human notion and thus mocks them, that person shall be rejected, and God’s finger shall crush him.

Praise, praise God, O blessed wombs, in all those wonders which God established in the gentle form of the lofty appearance which he foresaw in the first appearance of the rib of that man whom God created from clay. But whoever has keen ears of inward understanding should pant, in the burning love of my mirror, for these words and write them in the conscience of his mind. Amen.

[Col. 0739]

# THE BOOK OF DIVINE WORKS OF SAINT HILDEGARD, THE SIMPLE PERSON

(Baluze, *Miscellanies*, ed. Mansi, vol. II, p. 337.)

## JOHN DOMINIC MANSI TO THE READERS

In an elegant ancient manuscript from my library, adorned with gold and colours and dating from the twelfth century, or at least the beginning of the thirteenth, I found this volume bearing the title *The Book of Divine Works of the Simple Person*. Nor did I need laborious investigation to discover its author, since in reading it I encountered the word *Scivias*, which I knew to be distinctive of Saint Hildegard, the German virgin celebrated in the twelfth century for divine revelations; and I found, indeed, that Trithemius, in *On Ecclesiastical Writers*, identifies a work written by her under that title. The same Trithemius also gives the opening of that writing, which occurs in our manuscript in precisely the same words. Thus no further doubt concerning its author remained.

There was, however, still reason to wonder whether it might be the same work that had appeared in print more than once. I therefore consulted the Paris edition published in 1513 under the care of Jacques Lefèvre; comparison showed that it was a different work from ours, especially because the titles on the two sides differ, as do the openings of the books. Finally, the editions already published testify that they were written by their author when she was forty-three years old, whereas this work, the most holy virgin herself testifies, was given by her in the sixty-fifth year of her age. The former belongs, moreover, to the year 1141, this one to 1163. Finally, the printed work is divided into three books, whereas the work now published by me is one book only, as Trithemius also indicates, though it is divided into three parts.

Some ambiguity nevertheless remained, because at the beginning of the work here published these words are read: “And it came to pass in the sixth year after the true vision of unfailing light had shown to me, a human being most ignorant of the diversity of manifold dispositions, the marvellous and true visions concerning which I had laboured for five years, etc. [lacuna] That first year was the beginning of the present visions; but I link this year with the year 1163 of Christ, and with the forty-fifth year of her age.” If the earlier vision lasted five years, and if an interval of six years came between it and the beginning of the second, we rightly infer that the beginning of the earlier vision should be placed in the year 1152, and in the fifty-fifth year of Hildegard’s age. But how can this accord with the date of the earlier printed vision, which marks its beginning in the year 1141, the forty-second year of Hildegard’s age? Add eleven years to 1141 and to the forty-second year of her age, and you will reach the year 1152 of Christ and the fifty-third year of her age.

This knot could scarcely—indeed, hardly at all—be untied unless we posit three visions. The first, which was printed, began in 1141; when it ended, we do not know. It was followed by another, begun in 1152 of Christ, in Hildegard’s fifty-third year, and this is indicated in the vision now published in print. This second vision lasted five years, that is, until 1157 of Christ, when Hildegard was fifty-eight. It was followed by a pause of six years, which brings us to the beginning of the present vision, fittingly connected with the year 1163 of Christ, when Hildegard had begun her seventieth year.

Having dealt with these chronological difficulties, I must now say a few things about the work itself. It abounds remarkably in physical realities—or in their figures, images, and likenesses—for explaining both the divine dogmas of the Catholic faith and the most holy mysteries, and those human matters concerned with ordering and governing our conduct: fleeing vices and practising every virtue. Throughout it the glory of God is narrated and his attributes and perfections celebrated: his goodness, mercy, wisdom, omnipotence, providence, and justice in creating, preserving, and directing all things severally to their own end; in the restoration of the human race; in the sanctification and reward of the righteous; and in the punishments of the wicked to be endured in the other, eternal life according to the measure of their offences.

This work has always been held in such high esteem that fair-minded judges have always thought that any trouble and labour involved in reading and meditating upon it is relieved by such an abundance of most delightful fruit that it seems almost entirely removed or scarcely felt. What did the Council of Trier, held in the presence of the supreme pontiff Saint Eugenius III, not decree concerning Saint Hildegard, her revelations, and her writings? For, as Trithemius says in the *Chronicle of Hirsau*: “Saint Father Bernard was present there; through his mediation the supreme pontiff, together with all the others, was moved not to allow so distinguished a lamp to be concealed in silence, but himself to confirm by his authority so great a grace as the Lord had revealed in his own time.” The holy pontiff, favourably assenting to this, visited the devoted virgin of Christ by a letter of greeting, in which he gloriously granted her, by apostolic authority, permission to speak and write whatever she had learned through the Holy Spirit; and he encouraged her [Col. 0741] to write down without fear what had been revealed to her. Severinus Binius includes such a letter of Pope Eugenius to Hildegard in his account of the Council of Trier; Manrique cites it in the *Cistercian Annals*, under the year of Christ 1148, p. 101. You may read almost the same things in Baronius’s *Ecclesiastical Annals*, vol. XII, under 1148, and in Surius’s *Life of Saint Hildegard*.

Why say more? William Cave himself, in his *Literary History of Ecclesiastical Writers*, under the year 1170, p. 684, says this of Saint Hildegard: “Endowed with rare gifts of mind, distinguished by exceptional piety toward God and zeal for religion, she began, while already forty years old, to become renowned through divinely granted visions and prophecies. Pope Eugenius III, and leading bishops and abbots of France and Germany, among them Saint Bernard, stirred by the report of this matter, subjected her prophetic visions to a more searching examination in 1148; they found them unfeigned and confirmed them at the Council of Trier. Popes Anastasius IV and Adrian IV afterwards upheld the same judgement; in letters addressed to her, they commended both themselves and the Roman Church to her prayers.” Whatever therefore Casimir Oudin, in his *Commentary on Ecclesiastical Writers*, vol. II, col. 1571 ff., and persons of similar bran may babble, let a work most worthy of being brought into the hands of all learned people come to light and at last be read by them more attentively, with greater profit and love of truth.

# THE BOOK OF DIVINE WORKS OF THE SIMPLE PERSON BEGINS

[Col. 0741]

[Col. 0741A] And it came to pass in the sixth year after the true vision of unfailing light had shown to me—a human being most ignorant of the diversity of manifold dispositions—the marvellous and true visions concerning which I had laboured for five years, which first year was the beginning of the present visions: when I was sixty-five years old, I saw a vision of such great mystery and power that I trembled all over and, because of the frailty of my body, began to be ill from it. I scarcely completed this vision at last through seven years of writing. Therefore, in the year 1163 of the Lord’s Incarnation, while the disturbance of the apostolic see had not yet been calmed, under Frederick, emperor of Roman dignity, a voice from heaven came to me, saying:

“O poor little form, daughter of very many labours, worn out by many grave bodily infirmities, yet suffused with the depth of God’s mysteries: commit in stable writing for the usefulness of humankind those things which you see with inward eyes and perceive with the inward ears of your soul, so that through them people may understand their Creator and not refuse to venerate him with worthy honour. Therefore write these things not according to your own heart, but according to my testimony—I who am life without beginning and end. [Col. 0742A] They were neither discovered by you nor premeditated by any other human being, but ordained beforehand by me before the beginning of the world. For just as I foreknew humanity before it was created, so I also foresaw those things necessary for it.”

Therefore I, a poor and weak little form, with the testimony of that man whom, as I said in my earlier visions, I had secretly sought and found, and also with the testimony of the same girl of whom I made mention in the preceding visions, crushed by very many infirmities, at last turned my trembling hands to writing. While doing so, I looked upward to the true and living light to learn what I should write. For everything which I had written from the beginning of my visions, or afterwards knew, I saw in heavenly mysteries while wakeful in body and mind, with the inward eyes of my spirit, and heard with inward ears—not in dreams nor in ecstasy, as I stated in my earlier visions. Nor, with truth as witness, did I put forth anything from human understanding, but only those things which I received in heavenly secrets. Again I heard a voice from heaven teaching me thus, and it said: “Write therefore according to me in this manner.”

# PART ONE

[Col. 0741]

# FIRST VISION

[Col. 0741C] Description of the marvellous vision upon which the following work depends, and within it a subtle description of the appearance and attributes or circumstances of a certain divine image appearing in human form.

I. And I saw, as though in the midst of the southern air, a beautiful and marvellous image in the mystery of God, like a human form. Its face was of such beauty and brightness that I could more easily gaze upon the sun than [Col. 0742C] upon it. A broad circle, golden in colour, surrounded the head of that face. In the same circle, above that head, there appeared another face, like that of an old man, whose chin and beard touched the crown of this head. From either side of the neck of this form there extended a wing, which rose above the aforesaid circle and there joined the other. [Col. 0743A] At the summit of the arched curve of this right wing I saw something like an eagle’s head, with fiery eyes in which the radiance of angels appeared as in a mirror. At the summit of the arched curve of the left wing was something like a human face, shining like the flashing of stars. These faces were turned toward the east. From each shoulder of this image a wing extended down to the knees. It wore a tunic like the brilliance of the sun, and held in its hands a lamb, shining like daylight. It trampled beneath its feet a certain monster, horrible in form, poisonous and black in colour, and a serpent that had fixed its mouth in the monster’s right ear, bending the rest of its body across the monster’s head and extending its tail down its left side to its feet. And this image spoke.

Words of this image, through which charity is understood: it calls itself the fiery life of God’s substance and narrates the manifold effects of its power in the various natures or qualities of creation.

II. “I am the supreme and fiery power that kindles every living spark; I have breathed forth no mortal things, but judge them as they are. Flying around the encircling circuit with my higher wings—that is, with wisdom—I have rightly ordered it. I, the fiery life of divine substance, blaze over the beauty of the fields; I shine in the waters; I burn in sun, moon, and stars; and with the airy wind, by a certain invisible life that sustains all things, I give life to everything. For the air lives in greenness and flowers; waters flow as though they lived; the sun too lives in its light, and when the moon has come to its waning it is kindled by the sun’s light, so that it may seem to live anew; likewise the stars shine in their light as though living. I also established the columns that bear the whole globe of the earth. Likewise I established those winds which have wings subject to them, namely gentler winds, which by their gentleness restrain the stronger winds lest they show themselves dangerously—just as the body covers and contains the soul lest it breathe out. And just as the breath of the soul, strengthening the body, holds it together lest it fail, so the stronger winds animate those subject to them, that they may suitably perform their office. Therefore I, fiery power, lie hidden in these things, and they blaze from me, just as breath continually moves a human being and as flame in fire is wind-driven.

“All these things live in their essence and were not found in death, because I am life. I am also rationality, possessing the wind of the sounding Word, through whom every creature was made; and I breathed into all these things, so that none of them is mortal in its kind, because I am life. For I am whole life, not cut from stones, not budding from branches, nor rooted in male power; rather, every living thing is rooted in me. For rationality is the root, but the sounding Word flowers in it. Therefore, since God is rational, how could he fail to work, when all his work blooms forth—[Col. 0744A] humanity, which he made in his image and likeness and in which he marked all creatures according to measure? For it was always in eternity that God willed his work, namely humanity, to be made; and when he completed that work, he gave it all creatures so that it might work with them, just as God himself had made his work, namely humanity.

“I am also the ministering power, because every living thing burns from me; and I am equal life in eternity, neither arisen nor to end. This life, moving and working itself, is God; and yet this life is one in three powers. Eternity is therefore called the Father, the Word the Son, and the breath connecting these two the Holy Spirit, just as God has also marked this in the human being, in whom are body, soul, [Col. 0744B] and rationality. That I blaze over the beauty of the fields means the earth, which is the material from which God made humanity. That I shine in the waters pertains to the soul, because as water permeates the whole earth, so the soul passes through the whole body. That I burn in sun and moon is rationality; and the stars are the innumerable words of rationality. And that, with the airy wind, by a certain invisible life sustaining all things, I vivify everything, means that by air and wind those things which proceed in growth subsist in vegetative life, removed from nothingness into what they are.”

That in the human being made in his image and likeness God marked every creature; that after the Fall he restored humanity through his incarnation solely out of the charity of his goodness and placed it in the blessedness which the fallen angel lost; and that this is shown by the mystical meaning of the preceding vision.

III. And again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “God, who created all things, made humanity in his image and likeness and marked in it both higher and lower creatures. He loved it with such great love that he destined it for the place from which the falling angel had been cast out and ordained it for the glory and honour which that angel had lost in blessedness. This vision which you see demonstrates it. For what you see, as though in the midst of the southern air, a beautiful and marvellous image in the mystery of God, like a human form, means that in the strength [Col. 0744D] of unfailing divinity there is charity—beautiful in election and marvellous in the gifts of the heavenly Father’s secrets—showing humanity, because when the Son of God clothed himself with flesh, he redeemed lost humanity in the service of charity. Its face is of such beauty and brightness that you can more easily look upon the sun than upon it, because the generosity of charity stands in such eminence and flashing splendour of its gifts that it transcends all understanding of human knowledge, by which a person can understand diverse things in the soul, so completely that such a person cannot grasp it in understanding at all. Yet it is shown here in a sign so that through it he who is not visibly seen by visible eyes may be known in faith.”

That devout faith embraces the excellence of divine charity, and through it God is known as one in the Trinity; and that by the merit of this faith God himself protects human beings and leads them back to heavenly things.

IV. And the broad, golden-coloured circle surrounds the head of that face because the Catholic faith, spread throughout the whole world and rising in the first dawn with surpassing splendour, embraces with all devotion the excellence of the generosity of true charity, where God redeemed humanity in the humanity of his Son and strengthened it through the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. Thus God, who was God in divinity without temporal beginning before the ages, is known as one in Trinity. That another face, like that of an old man, appears in that circle above the same head means that the goodness of divinity, surpassing all things and without beginning or end, helps the faithful, [Col. 0745B] so that the chin and beard of that face touch the crown of this head: divinity, ordering and protecting all things, possesses the height of supreme charity, where the Son of God in his humanity leads lost people back to heavenly things.

That the love of God and neighbour, strengthened by the power of faith, cannot be separated.

V. From either side of the neck of this form a wing extends, rising above the aforesaid circle and joining one another there, because love of God and neighbour, proceeding through the power of charity in the unity of faith and enclosing that same faith within themselves through supreme desire, are not separated from one another, while holy divinity obscures from human beings the innumerable brightness of its glory as long as they remain in the shadow of death, deprived of the heavenly garment which they lost in Adam.

That everyone subject to God with humble devotion, enkindled by the assistance of the Holy Spirit, overcomes both himself insofar as he is sinful and the devil; and that angels, rejoicing at the good deeds of the righteous, praise God’s omnipotence.

VI. At the summit of the arched curve of this right wing, you see something like an eagle’s head, with fiery eyes in which a multitude of angels appears as in a mirror. This means that, in the height of triumphant submission, when anyone subject to God overcomes himself and the devil, that person becomes exalted in [Col. 0745D] the blessedness of divine protection. When that person raises the mind upward, enkindled by the Holy Spirit, and fixes intention upon God, the blessed spirits appear clearly within that person and offer God the devotion of that person’s heart. For spiritual persons are signified by the eagle: with every devotion of their hearts they frequently behold God in contemplation, like angels. Therefore the blessed spirits, continually beholding God, rejoice in the good works of the righteous, show them in themselves, and thus, persevering in God’s praise, never grow weary, because they can never bring him to an end. Who could count the innumerable wonders which God performs in the power of his possibility? No one. For the angels possess a radiance like many mirrors [Col. 0746A] in which they see that no one works as God does or has such power; therefore no one is like him, because he has no time.

That from eternity all things were in God without spatial location; and, through his creating, proceeded distinctly in number, order, place, and time.

VII. All things which God has made he possessed in his presence before the beginning of time. For in pure and holy divinity all visible and invisible things appeared before the ages without moment or time, just as trees or another creature near waters are seen in those waters, although they are not bodily in them, yet their entire form appears in them. But when God said, “Let it be,” they were immediately clothed in form—[Col. 0746B] those things which his foreknowledge beheld before the ages without bodies. For just as everything before a mirror shines in it, so all God’s works appeared in holy divinity without the ages of time. And how could God be without the work of his foreknowledge, when every one of his works, after being clothed with a body, is complete in the office allotted to it, which holy divinity foreknew would be present to itself in knowing, understanding, and serving? For just as the ray of every light shows every creaturely form through shadow, so the pure foreknowledge of God beheld every form of creatures before they were embodied, since the work which God was to make shone in his foreknowledge before that work was embodied according to this likeness: as a person sees the brightness of the sun before being able to behold its substance. [Col. 0746C] And as the brightness of the sun indicates the sun itself, so angels show God by praising him; and as it cannot be that the sun exists without its light, so neither is divinity without the praise of angels. God’s foreknowledge preceded, and his work followed; and if God’s foreknowledge had not preceded, his work would not have appeared, just as, if a person’s face is not seen, that person’s body is not known; but when a person’s face is seen, that person’s body is praised. Therefore God’s foreknowledge and his work are in him.

That the devil and angels who deserted justice, though formerly of great power, were reduced through their ingratitude or pride to being unable to do anything in any creature except insofar as they are permitted by heavenly will.

VIII. But there was a certain innumerable multitude of angels who wished to exist from themselves, because, when they saw their own great and glorious brightness in its supreme radiance, they forgot their Creator. And before they had even begun to praise him, they reckoned within themselves that the splendor of their honor was so great that no one could resist them; and therefore they wished also to obscure God. For when they saw that they could never bring him to an end by their marvels, they abhorred him; and when they ought to have praised him, through a deceitful opinion they said that in their [Col. 0747A] great brightness they would choose another god. Hence they fell into darkness, reduced to such incapacity that they can accomplish nothing in any creature except insofar as their Creator permits them.

For when God had adorned the first angel, who was called Lucifer, with all the ornaments of creatures which he had given to all creatures, so that even his whole host derived splendor from him, that angel, going contrary to God, became more horrible than all horrors, because the holy Divinity in its zeal cast him into the place that is without light.

That a human being, directing himself toward imitation of his Creator, as though drawn away from a certain beastly irrationality, begins to shine with the radiance of rational nature.

IX. But that at the summit of the arched curvature of the [Col. 0747B] left wing there is, as it were, a human face radiating like the brightness of stars, means this: at the height of victorious humility, when a human being crushes in humility earthly concerns that oppose him as though on his left, and turns himself to the defense of his Creator, he bears the appearance of a human being, because he begins to live honorably—not according to cattle, but according to what human nature teaches him. Thus, in these righteous works also, he shows the good intention of his heart to shine forth like outstanding splendor.

That at God’s word, “Let there be light,” rational light—that is, angels—were created; and that, when some of these fell from blessedness, the Lord made another rational life covered with flesh—that is, the human being—to possess the place and glory of the fallen.

[Col. 0747C] X. For when God said, “Let there be light,” rational light arose—namely, the angels: both those who remained with him in truth and those who fell into outer darkness without any light, because they denied that the true light, which before time and without beginning was in brightness, was God; and because they wished to make something that could not exist like him. Then God caused another life, covered with a body, to arise: the human being. To him he gave both the place and the glory of the lost angel, so that in praise of God this one might accomplish what that one had refused to do.

In this human face are shown those who, though bodily devoted to the world, nevertheless continually serve God in spirit; and who, although they are held in the world in a worldly manner, do not on that account forget the things of the spirit in God’s service. These faces are turned toward the east, because both spiritual and secular persons who desire to serve God and preserve their souls in life ought to turn themselves toward the rising of holy conduct and blessedness.

That God, gathering to himself in the strength of his love those predestined for him, instructs them by the infusion of the gifts of the Holy Spirit in all necessary matters.

XI. Moreover, from each shoulder of this image a wing extends to its knees, because in the strength of love the Son of God gathered righteous persons and sinners to himself; and he sustained them both with shoulders, because they had lived rightly, and with knees, because he had recalled them from the way of injustice; and he made them companions of the citizens above, just as a human being supports with both knees and [Col. 0748A] shoulders the things that he carries.

For in the knowledge of love a human being is brought, in soul and body, to the fullness of integrity, although he is often moved from the state of upright stability. When the gifts of the Holy Spirit pour down upon him in pure and holy abundance, they instruct him abundantly in heavenly and spiritual matters. In earthly matters also, for the use of bodily necessity, they instruct him in another way—matters in which he nevertheless understands himself to be weak, infirm, and mortal, though fortified with these manifold gifts.

That the Son of God, assuming human nature without the stain of sin and appearing in the flesh, called tax collectors and sinners to repentance and justified them through faith in him.

XII. But that the figure is clothed in a tunic like the splendor of the sun means that the Son of God, in love, clothed himself with a human body free from every contagion of sin, in the likeness of the sun’s beauty. For just as the sun shines above other creatures at such a height that no human being can touch it, so no human knowledge can grasp how the humanity of the Son of God is, except by believing.

And he holds in his hands a lamb, splendid like the light of day, because love brought forth in the works of the Son of God the gentleness of true faith, shining above all things: there he chose martyrs, confessors, and penitents from tax collectors and sinners; and there he made righteous persons from the impious, as Paul from Saul, so that they might fly upon the wings of the winds—that is, into the [Col. 0748C] heavenly harmony.

Thus love accomplished its work gradually and distinctly, so that no weakness but every fullness might be in it. A human being does not do this; for when he has only a small ability to accomplish something, he scarcely endures until he completes it without being seen by others. Let the human being consider this within himself: even a bird emerging from an egg, lacking wings, does not yet hasten to fly; but after it has received wings, it flies wherever it sees fit.

That imitation of the love of the Son of God, who crushed the devil by his cross, even now tramples down in his faithful discord and the other vices, as well as the ancient deceiver of the human race himself, and reduces them to nothing.

XIII. But that a certain monster of horrible [Col. 0748D] form, poisonous and black in color, tramples a serpent beneath its feet means that true love crushes through the footsteps of the Son of God the injury of discord—twisted by many vices, horrible through many perversities, poisonous in deception, and black in destruction—as well as the ancient serpent lying in wait for all the faithful; indeed, the Son of God himself reduced that serpent to nothing on the cross.

The serpent fixes its mouth into the right ear of this same monster, bends the rest of its body crosswise around the monster’s head, and stretches its tail along the monster’s left side down to its feet. This means that the devil sometimes, while pretending that he is doing good, implants his deception in discord; and, lightly adding the entire race of vices here and there at its beginning, nevertheless shows at their end that discord possesses the perversity of a most evil consummation. For the serpent, being more cunning in deceit than other creeping things, destroys in that same cunning everything it can and turns itself toward what is worst. The various colors within it also signify this.

So Satan acted: when he recognized his own beauty, he wished to be like his Creator; and he also instilled this into the human being through hearing, as though through the serpent’s head. Nor will he cease to do this until the last day, which is like his tail.

Love, therefore, is in the wheel of eternity without time, as heat is in fire. For God foreknew in his eternity all creatures, which he brought forth in the fullness of love so that the human being might lack no refreshment or service [Col. 0749B] in them, because he joined them to the human being as flames to fire. God established the first angel with many ornaments, as has also been said; but when that angel beheld himself, he hated his Lord and wished to be Lord. Yet God cast him into the pit of the abyss. Then this same transgressor offered evil counsel to the human being, and the human being consented.

That Adam and Eve, consenting to the devil’s persuasion, who envied them, lost the glory of the heavenly garment—that is, immortality.

XIV. For when God created the human being, he clothed him in a heavenly garment, so that he flashed forth in great brightness. But when the devil looked upon the woman, he knew that she would become the mother of a great world; and in the same malice by which he had departed from God, he brought it about that he would overcome God in this work of his, so that he might turn God’s own work, the human being, into his fellowship. Then, when the woman felt herself changed by tasting the fruit, she gave the fruit to her husband; and thus they both lost the heavenly garment.

That God, having mercy on them, expelled them from paradise into this exile to punish the guilt of transgression; and that whoever violates the marital fidelity instituted by God between them is to be punished by severe vengeance unless he repents.

XV. But when God afterwards said, “Adam, where are you?” he thereby signified that he remembered having made him in his own image and likeness, and that he wished to draw him back to himself. He also covered his nakedness by means of his servile labor, and sent him into exile, so that in place of a shining garment he received a sheep’s skin, just as paradise was exchanged for this exile.

For God joined woman to man with an oath of fidelity, so that this fidelity should never be destroyed between them, but that they should consent as one, like body and soul, which God joined into one. Therefore, whoever destroys this fidelity and thus remains unrepentant and without amendment will be turned into the land of Babylon—that is, the land of confusion and barrenness. It will remain without the beautiful greenness of the field, that is, without God’s blessing; and God’s vengeance will fall upon that person, down to the final line of consanguinity which proceeded from his fervent blood, because this sin affects that human being.

[Col. 0750A] That, in the preaching of the incarnate Son of God, the promise which God made to Abraham was fulfilled in the rising spiritual people: that his seed would be multiplied according to the number of the stars of heaven.

XVI. And just as Adam is the progenitor of the entire human race, so through the Son of God, who was incarnate in virginal nature, there proceeded a spiritual people which will ascend, as God promised Abraham through an angel: namely, that his seed would become like the stars of heaven. As it is written: “Look up to heaven, and count the stars, if you can.” And he said to him: “So shall your seed be.” Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness (Gen. V).

This is plainly understood as follows. You who worship and revere God with good will, examine the hidden things of God and consider the reward of the merits of those who shine before God day and night—if, however, this is possible for a human being weighed down by bodily burden. For as long as a human being savors the things of the flesh, he cannot fully grasp the things of the spirit.

And a truthful declaration is made to one who strives to worship God in the right sighing of his heart: “In this manner the seed of your heart will be multiplied and made bright, which you sowed in the good field watered by the grace of the Holy Spirit; it will also rise and shine manifoldly before the highest God in blessed virtues, just as the stars shine in the firmament.” Therefore, whoever faithfully believes the divine promise, possessing toward God the loftiness of true faith, so that he despises all earthly things and strives upward toward heavenly things, will be counted righteous among the children [Col. 0750C] of God, because he loved truth and had no deceit in his heart.

That God chose the Virgin Mary from the lineage of Abraham, who believed and obeyed him, and that Christ, founder and ruler of the new—that is, spiritual—generation, would be born from her bodily.

XVII. For God knew that Abraham’s mind was without the serpent’s deceit, because he performed what he did to injure no one. Hence God chose from his lineage the sleeping earth, wholly ignorant of that taste by which the same ancient serpent deceived the first woman.

This earth, prefigured through Aaron’s rod, was the Virgin Mary, who became the king’s closed chamber in great humility. For when she received from the throne this message—that the highest King wished to dwell within her enclosure—she looked upon the earth from which she had been created and said that she was God’s handmaid. The first deceived woman did not do this, when she desired to possess what she ought not to possess.

Moreover, Abraham’s obedience, in which God tested his faith when he showed him a ram hanging in thorns, prefigured the obedience of the blessed Virgin, who, believing the word of God’s messenger, desired that it might be done to her according to that messenger’s word. Therefore the Son of God clothed himself in flesh within her, he whom the ram hanging in the brambles had prefigured.

And when God said that the race of this Abraham would be multiplied according to the stars of heaven, he foresaw in this the race that was to be counted into the full number of the heavenly fellowship. Because Abraham faithfully believed God in all things, he was therefore called the father [Col. 0751A] of those who shall be heirs of the kingdom of heaven. Therefore every person who fears and loves God should open the devotion of his heart through these words, and should know that these things are for the salvation of human bodies and souls—not from a human being, but through me, who am set over them.

## SECOND VISION

[Col. 0751]

[Col. 0751A] Description of the sphere of the whole world, with its circles, planets, and winds, in the form of a wheel appearing in the breast of the image described in the first vision.

I. Then, in the breast of the aforesaid image, which, as stated above, I had seen as though in the midst of the southern air, there appeared a wheel of wondrous vision, with its signs of approximately this form: like that instrument which twenty-eight years earlier I had seen symbolically in the shape of an egg, as is shown in the third vision of the book *Scivias*. Thus, at its uppermost part, around the circumference of its roundness, there appeared a circle resembling bright fire; beneath it another circle, like a circle of black fire. The circle of bright fire exceeded that circle of black fire by twice its density; and these two circles were joined together as though they were one circle.

Below the same circle of black fire was another circle resembling pure ether, everywhere of as great a density as the circles of the two aforesaid fires appeared to be. But beneath that circle of pure ether was another, like a circle of watery air, whose density throughout its roundness was as great as the density of the aforesaid circle of bright fire. And beneath the same circle of watery air there appeared another circle, as though of strong, white, bright air, having in its firmness the character of a sinew in a human body; it was everywhere around its circumference of the same density as that of the aforesaid circle of black fire. These two circles also were so joined together that they appeared as though they were one circle.

Below this circle—namely, that of strong, white, bright air—there was marked, as it were, another thin air, which seemed above to bear clouds, at times raised and bright, at times lowered and shadowy, and to diffuse itself as though throughout the whole aforesaid wheel. All these six circles were joined to one another without any interval. The uppermost circle seemed to pour the others through with its fire; but the watery one watered all the others with its moisture.

And from, as it were, the beginning of the eastern side of that wheel to, as it were, the end of its western side, a line extended toward its northern part, as though separating the northern region from the other regions. Also, in the middle of the sign of the aforesaid thin air, a globe was marked. It stood everywhere around its circumference at an equal distance from the sign of the strong, white, bright air; and it was as broad across as the depth of the space from the summit of the highest circle to the edge of the clouds, or from the edge [Col. 0752A] of the clouds to the summit of that globe.

In the middle of this wheel there appeared an image of a human being, whose crown above and soles below reached to the aforesaid circle, as though of strong, white, bright air. On the right side, the tips of the fingers of his right hand, and on the left side the tips of the fingers of his left hand, were extended on both sides to that circle marked in its roundness, because the image had stretched out its arms in this way.

Toward these same directions four heads also appeared: namely, as though the head of a leopard and of a wolf, and as though the head of a lion and of a bear. Above the crown of the aforesaid image, in the sign of pure ether, I saw something like a leopard’s head emitting, as it were, breath from its mouth. On the right side of its mouth this breath curved somewhat lengthwise and became a crab’s head with two claws, as though with two feet; but on the left side of its mouth, likewise bending somewhat lengthwise, it ended in a stag’s head.

From the mouth of this crab’s head another breath, as it were, went forth as far as the midpoint of the space between the heads of the leopard and the aforesaid lion. But from the mouth of the stag’s head another breath, as it were, came as far as the midpoint of the space between the heads of the leopard and the bear.
