And my whole ordering was so festive that I displayed it in none other than my Son, sent from me, who completed all my ordinances through his teaching and through his apostles with manifest work—ordinances which the prophets had formerly seen in shadow. Then too the seventh day of my rest shone forth in the Church, so that thereafter I might work nothing else in open deed, neither through preaching nor signs of miracles nor visions of ancient saints, except to make manifest in my Son the works of life and very many secrets, future, past, and present; and so that I might benignly admonish my elect to imitate the Incarnation of that same Son of mine, which flowered in the first shoot.

“And he blessed the seventh day and sanctified it” (ibid.), because on it he had ceased from all work which God created in order to make. I blessed and sanctified this seventh day in the salvation of souls when I sent my Son to be incarnate in the Virgin’s womb. And I blessed and sanctified it because I take great delight in this day: namely, in those who, like flowers of roses and lilies, freed from the yoke of the law, begin freely—through my inspiration alone—to restrain themselves, just as the Incarnation of my Son, which I formerly promised in prophecy, is not subject to the commandment of the law.

And I ceased to work in such a manner in the Church, which now shines in holy work and is perfected in a full ordering, because my Son, who is my seventh work, proceeding in humanity from the Virgin’s womb, accomplished all these things with me in the Holy Spirit, according to what he says in the Gospel: “All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me” (Matt. 28).

This must be understood thus: To me, who am the Son of the Virgin, all power has been given by God the Father, by hereditary right: to act in heaven and judge on earth those things which are to be done and judged. Yet I do not exceed my Father’s will, but behold it in all things, because I am in the Father and he is in me.

And again, in another sense:

How these same matters, according to the tropological sense, are fulfilled in the advancement and perfection of each believer.

XLIX. “Thus the heavens and the earth and all their adornment were perfected” (Gen. 2).

This must be understood thus: Those heavenly and earthly virtues and all their adornment are perfected in righteousness and truth with good works in the human being.

“And God completed on the seventh day the work which he had made, and rested on the seventh day from all the work which he had accomplished” (ibid.). [Col. 0955A] Through the seventh day, which is his Son, in whom all fullness of good work arose, God completes in the human being a good work with all perfect virtues, as a craftsman sets precious stones into the work he is making; for all good works in the person who acts through the grace of the Holy Spirit are fully adorned.

Then God also rests in his Son from every work—namely, from that work in which the human being is now perfect—because the person has begun to work according to the works in the Son of God, who was the seventh work, in the womb of the Virgin Mary.

“And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it he had ceased from all the work which God created in order to make” (ibid.). God blessed the seventh day in the perfection of good works: that is, the human being who is a member of his Son in him. How? Namely, so that the person may imitate the inward blessing, that is, that same Son who came forth from God’s heart, and thus return to life through the examples of him who became obedient to God the Father.

He also sanctifies the aforesaid heavenly works in that human being when he grants the person glory and honor with himself, so that the person may forgive the neighbor every debt whenever he wills. And from this severity of the Father of works he now ceases—the severity by which, before the Incarnation of his Son, he permitted no one to enter the heavenly kingdom. But now, in that same Son, he opens the entrance to heavenly joys when, through that same Son, he forgives each debt to the human being who confesses it from the heart. Therefore let the faithful person understand these things faithfully and not despise in them him who is true.

PART THREE.

[Col. 0955]

SIXTH VISION.

[Col. 0955B] A mystical vision concerning a structure shown in the form of a city; also concerning a mountain and a mirror shining upon it; a cloud white above and black below; and the other things appearing in the same vision.

I. And again I saw something like a square structure of a great city, surrounded on either side as though by a wall of a certain brilliance and certain darknesses, and likewise adorned, as it were, with mountains and images. I also saw, in the middle of its eastern region, something like a great and lofty mountain of hard white stone, having the appearance of that from which fire is cast forth. On its summit there shone something like a mirror of such brightness and purity that it seemed even to surpass the sun’s radiance. In it there also appeared something like a dove with wings outspread, as though prepared to fly.

This same mirror, containing within itself very many hidden wonders, emitted from itself a radiance of great breadth and height, in which many mysteries and numerous forms of diverse images appeared. For within this radiance, on the southern side, there appeared something like a cloud, white above but black beneath. Above it shone, as it were, a very great multitude of angels: some appeared fiery, some bright, some like stars. All of them were moved by a certain wind flying like burning lamps; and it was full of voices sounding like the noise of the sea. This wind extended its voices in its zeal, and through it sent fire into the aforesaid blackness of the cloud; [Col. 0955C] whereupon it burned in blackness without flame. Then it immediately blew into it and made it vanish and collapse like thick smoke.

Thus it cast that falling cloud from the south, over the aforesaid mountain, toward the north into a certain boundless abyss, so that thereafter it could not raise itself up, except that it sometimes sends a kind of mist over the earth. And I heard, as it were, trumpets crying aloud from heaven: [Col. 0955D] “What is this—that one strong in his powers has fallen?” And so the white portion of the aforesaid cloud shone more brightly than before; nor could anyone thereafter resist the wind which, in three modes of its voices, had cast down the blackness of the aforesaid cloud. And again I heard a voice from heaven saying:

On God’s foreknowledge, predestination, and ordination: he knows all things beforehand from eternity, creates all things in time, and examines the works of rational creatures by strict judgment.

II. God knows all things in his foreknowledge, because before creatures came to be in their forms he knew them beforehand; nor was anything hidden from him that proceeds from the beginning of the world to its end. The present vision also declares this. For you see something like a square structure of a great city, signifying the stable and firm work of divine predestination, surrounded on either side, as it were, by a certain radiance and certain darknesses as by a wall, because the faithful are assigned to glory and the unfaithful to punishments, separated from one another by just judgment. It is likewise adorned as though with certain mountains and images—that is, fortified and exalted with great marvels of miracles and virtues—because God, making all his works true and just, has strengthened them with such power that they cannot be destroyed by any assault of failure.

But that you see, as though in the middle of the eastern region, a great and lofty mountain of hard white stone, having the appearance of that from which fire is cast forth, [Col. 0956B] signifies that God is, in the strength of justice, great in power, lofty in glory, hard in severity, and white in gentleness, because he accomplishes all his judgments in the burning heat of equity. For he is just and utterly crushes injustice, because heaven and earth are founded upon him and he sustains the firmament with all creatures, just as a cornerstone holds together the whole building.

On its summit a mirror shines, as it were, with such brightness and purity that it seems even to surpass the sun’s radiance, because in God’s excellence his foreknowledge is so luminous and clear that it surpasses every brightness of creatures. In it there also appears something like a dove with outspread wings, as though prepared to fly, because in that same foreknowledge the divine ordination, spreading itself out, has proceeded toward its manifestation. For when God willed it, he caused every creature to come forth.

And just as elsewhere there are two wings for flight, and one sitting upon a mountain considers where one wishes to fly, so divine ordination too, possessing two wings in angels and human beings, sits in its power as if upon a mountain, ordering all things. It is like a man who silently orders all that he wills; and, fortifying the human being with the defenses of angels, gave that person will and work as wings for flight. And in the old law he was silent as if saying nothing, because the whole law was figurative. For it had foreseen in all things that the figure in which there was living breath and knowledge should know what it ought to do when, through the living wind—that is, the soul—it looked either to the right or to the left: if it flew to the right, it would receive the reward of life; but if it turned to the left, it would there be subject to due punishments.

Therefore God holds this ordination beneath the covering of his wings, so that, protecting with his right hand, he receives the one who flies toward him, saying: “In you I shall rejoice, because you made me; therefore my soul clings after you,” and grants that person many ornaments. But he permits the one who refuses to cling to him to perish, as was said above.

Moreover, when the Son of God assumed the garment of flesh, which adhered to holy divinity and through which he might bring his work, not yet completed, to its fulfillment in his humanity, he immediately flew mightily among human beings—at which the angels marveled. No other human being could do this except the incarnate Word of God. And through that same garment he sanctified them, so that, looking to him, they might deny themselves and, with him, fly in their outspread wings toward heavenly desires.

On how the knowledge of God, containing many unknown and secret things within itself, brings forth the manifestation of its wonders according to its pleasure; and what is signified by the threefold rank of angels appearing in this vision.

[Col. 0957D] III. The aforesaid mirror, containing within itself very many hidden wonders, emits from itself a radiance of great breadth and height, signifying that the knowledge of God, containing many unknown and secret things in itself, produces, according to its pleasure, the manifestation of its wonders by expanding and elevating it. In it many mysteries and numerous forms of diverse images appear, because when the manifestation of God’s wonders opens itself, things formerly unknown and unseen will come forth into open manifestation.

For in that same radiance there appears toward the southern region something like a cloud, white above but black beneath, signifying that in the manifestation of God’s burning justice the intention of the blessed spirits is laid bare as praiseworthy, but that of the reprobate as accursed. Above it shines, as it were, a vast multitude of angels: some appear fiery, some bright, and some like stars. Those who appear fiery are in the strongest powers, so that they can in no way be moved, because God willed them to be before his face, that they might always behold it.

But those shown as bright are now moved in the offices of the works of human beings, which are God’s work. The works of these offices stand before God in the sight of those same angels, because they always consider them and offer their good odor to God, choosing useful things and casting away useless ones. Those who appear like stars sympathize with human nature and present it to God as a written record; they accompany human beings, speak to them in the words of rationality as God wills, and praise God for their good works, but turn themselves away from evil ones.

On the Spirit of God stirring up his zeal through the blessed angels to repel and suppress the presumption of the reprobate angels; and on the tireless harmony of the good angels, who praise God with an immeasurable and ever-new wonder beyond human understanding.

IV. And they are all set in motion by a certain wind, like burning lamps in flight, because the living Spirit of God, burning in truth, moves these angelic spirits to His zeal against His enemies. He is also full of voices, which sound like the sound of the sea, because He possesses the fullness and perfection of every praise by which both angelic and human creation are poured out into the praise of God [Col. 0958C]. And, as you see, this same wind extends its voices in its zeal, because the Spirit of God turns the voices of the righteousness of His judgments toward the punishment of the reprobate.

And through it He sent fire into the aforesaid blackness of the said cloud, so that it blazed into blackness without flame, while the blessed spirits, seeing the undertaking of the lost angels, hastened to the honor of God. They likewise poured out the fire of vengeance fiercely upon the utterly evil unbelief of intention of those same enemies of His: upon those who burned, not toward correction, but toward greater accursedness, without any light of salvation, and who were unwilling to render their Creator the honor due to Him. For because they wished to exist without the radiance of praise to their Creator [Col. 0958D], they were reckoned as nothing, just as unwritten parchment is empty and has no honor of writing.

He also immediately blew upon it and made it vanish and collapse like thick smoke, because that same zeal, through the blessed spirits, annihilated, weakened, and cast down the attempt of the reprobate that desired to ascend on high. For the multitudes of good angels gaze upon God; with every harmony of praise they know Him; and with wondrous uniqueness they praise His mysteries, which always were and are in Him. Nor can they omit this in any way, because no earthly body weighs them down. They also declare the Godhead with the living sounds of exalted voices, which exceed the number of the sands of the sea, the number of all fruits that spring up from the earth [Col. 0959A], the number of sounds uttered by all animals, every radiance that shines in the waters through sun, moon, and stars, and every sound of the ether produced by the blasts of winds that raise and uphold the four elements.

Yet in all these voices of their praise the blessed spirits cannot comprehend the Godhead without limit. Therefore they continually make newness in their voices. The aforesaid zeal also cast that collapsing thing backward from the south, beyond the aforesaid mountain, into the north, into a certain infinite abyss, so that thereafter it cannot raise itself up, except that it sometimes sends a kind of mist over the earth. This shows that He [Col. 0959B], through the power of the angels’ holiness, drove back the now-wavering intention of the malignant spirits from the place of blessedness, from the sight of the ever-living One, into the unhappiness of perdition and unceasing calamity. He reduced them to such crushing defeat that thereafter they cannot rebel against God, although they do not cease to assail human beings with their most wicked suggestions.

That a certain part of the blessed spirits, remaining hidden in heaven and always attending upon the countenance of their Creator, is seldom sent outward; whereas another part, designated by the name “angels,” continually goes forth for various offices and, when necessary, appears to human beings; and that every rational creature ought always to seek not its own glory but that of its Creator.

[Col. 0959C] V. There is also a certain multitude of angels, hidden with God in heaven, upon whom the Godhead has poured His light, and which is obscure to human creatures except insofar as it is known through luminous signs. This multitude is more rational with God than with humankind, and rarely appears to human beings. But angels who perform offices among human beings reveal themselves through certain signs when it pleases God, because God has appointed some to various offices and made them ministers with created beings. Yet, although they have differing offices, all venerate one God by worshipping and knowing Him.

But if knowledge, together with the sound of praise, did not fly toward Him from whom it comes, but wished to exist of itself [Col. 0959D], how could it stand, since it does not exist through itself? For rationality always directs the sound of praise toward another, and thus rejoices; because if it wished to sound from itself, it could not be glorified. This is what Satan did when he began to live: he did not look to his Creator with praise, but, wishing to exist through himself, fell, cut off from the Godhead and trampled down, just as straw separated from grain is trampled down.

Therefore let every creature that lives look to its Creator and not seek to possess glory from itself. For a human being cannot possess from himself the full joy of benefit unless he receives it from another; and when through another he understands the joy of benefit, he will consequently have great exultation in his heart. Hence the soul [Col. 0960A] also remembers that it was created by God and looks to Him in faith, just as a person looks at his own face in a mirror to see how it has been formed.

For almighty God established His work in such a way that it looks to Him with praises, because He made it in great honor, also ordaining that the blessed spirits should cast out those opposed to true blessedness, saying: “Let us cast away from us those who wish to terrify us.” Hence it is written in the will of God:

Words of the Psalmist from Psalm 92, bearing on the same matter, and the sense in which they should be understood.

VI. “The rivers have lifted up, O Lord; the rivers have lifted up their voice. The rivers have lifted up their waves, because of the voices of many waters” (Ps. 92 [93]). [Col. 0960B] The meaning of this statement is to be understood thus: In Your zeal the angelic spirits rose up, O Lord of all creatures, and like waves raised their powers in the overwhelming of Your enemies. Again, the hosts of those same spirits stretched their strength aloft, offering God voices of exceedingly many sounding praises; for angelic companies are like rivers of living water, which the wind of God’s Spirit moves to the glory of His praise, when those same voices fought against the black dragon.

For Michael struck that serpent with the voices of the trumpets of God’s hidden judgment, because it desired to know the brightness of the Godhead; and by God’s power he cast it into the pit of hell, which has no obstruction at its bottom. There also its followers, who had agreed with it and held it as their master, fell with it [Col. 0960C]. Yet it received more punishments than all of them, because it wished to look to no one but itself, whereas they looked to it.

After the fall of this ancient enemy, the heavenly choirs praised God because their accuser had fallen and because his place was no longer found in heaven. Then too they knew the wonders of God with a greater radiance than they had previously seen them, understanding likewise that henceforth such a battle would not occur in heaven and that no one would thereafter fall from heaven. Yet in the pure Godhead they knew that the number of fallen spirits would be filled up by vessels of clay. Therefore, because of this joy—that they knew the number of those who had fallen would thus be restored—they consigned that fall to such forgetfulness as though it had never been.

For almighty God established the heavenly host in diverse orders, as befitted Him, so that each order holds its own offices and each order is a contemplative seal for another order. In every such mirror are divine mysteries which these same orders cannot fully see, know, taste, or bring to completion [Col. 0960D]. Therefore, marveling, they ascend from praise to praise and from glory to glory, and thus are always new, because they cannot bring all these things to an end. They too are spirit and life from God. Hence they never fail in divine praises, always behold the fiery brightness of God, and, from the brightness of the Godhead, flash forth like flame.

Let the faithful receive these words with the devoted affection of their hearts, because they have been set forth for the benefit of believers through Him who is first and last [Col. 0961A].

## SEVENTH VISION

[Col. 0961]

[Col. 0961A] A mystical vision concerning a marble stone, like a mountain, standing in the eastern part of the building of the city previously shown; also concerning an innumerable multitude of human beings appearing in both the eastern and southern regions of the same building; and concerning the wondrous form and appearance of two images placed beside the eastern corner.

[Col. 0961B] I. After this, at the eastern corner—that is, where the east begins—I saw what seemed to be a marble stone, like a great, high, and whole mountain. In it only a gate, like that of a great city, appeared to have been cut; a certain bright radiance coming from the rising of the sun flooded it entirely, and extended no further. From this same stone almost as far as the other eastern extremity, which lay toward the south, there appeared what seemed to be human figures—children, young men, and old men—like stars seen through a cloud. They gave forth a sound reaching to the west, like the sea when it is moved to flood by the wind.

A certain splendor coming from above, surpassing every beauty estimable by human judgment [Col. 0961C], flooded them with a ray of its own and afterward drew that ray back to itself. Beside this aforesaid eastern extremity stood two other images close together. The former of them had the head and breast of a leopard, arms like a human being’s, but hands resembling a bear’s feet; I saw no other form in it. It was clothed in a stone tunic and moved neither this way nor that, but turned its gaze toward the north.

The other image, which was closer to the said corner, had a human face and hands folded together, and showed within itself the feet of a hawk. It wore what seemed to be a wooden tunic, which appeared white from its top down to its navel; reddish from the navel [Col. 0961D] down to its loins; grayish from the loins down to its knees; and turbid from the knees down to the ends of its feet. It also held a sword placed crosswise, as it were, above its loins; and, remaining motionless, it had turned its gaze toward the west.

Then I saw what seemed to be countless other human figures flowing like a cloud through the whole southern region. Some bore on their heads things like golden crowns; others held very richly adorned palms in their hands; others, things like pipes; others, like zithers; and others, like organs. The sound of these instruments rang out like the sweet sound of clouds. And again I heard a voice from heaven speaking to me.

[Col. 0962A] That almighty God, unaltered by any change, condemned the proud angels by just judgment; and, mercifully aiding deceived humankind, after sending beforehand in the Old Testament many wondrous heralds of its future salvation, finally accomplished its deliverance through many miracles in the New Testament; and that prophecy, divinely given for instruction and correction, has never been and never will be absent from any age of the world.

II. After the host of lost angels fell, God appointed humankind to the glory they had lost. But when humanity also fell, He redeemed it at the great price of blessed deliverance, having many times promised in the Old Testament many marvelous messengers by whom He would restore it to life; and having performed in the New Testament very many miracles through its deliverance [Col. 0962B].

Therefore, at the eastern corner—that is, where the east begins—you see what seems to be a marble stone like a great, high, and whole mountain. This signifies that from the beginning of creatures, when the world was created, God has stood as a most firm rock, mighty and exalted in the wholeness of steadfastness, having no change in Himself. In it only a gate, like that of a great city, appears cut out; a bright radiance coming from the rising of the sun floods it entirely and extends no farther. This is because God’s will, like a gate open toward every good, is touched by the ordering of the most pure Godhead, which does not proceed beyond what has been ordained; for the will and ordering of God so agree with one another that neither surpasses the other.

For God, by the merciful goodness of His will, appointed humanity in the place which the ancient serpent had lost. When humanity wavered into perversity, He cleansed it by the waters of the Flood, and by righteous examination renewed the world in Noah. Hence, from that same stone almost to the other eastern extremity [Col. 0962C], which lies toward the south, human figures—children, young men, and old men—appear like stars through a cloud and send forth sound as far as the west, like the sea when moved to overflow by the wind. This is because prophecy began in the first work of God, namely Adam, from the divine strength up to the point where the old law, appearing with severity, received its end when the burning of justice and truth came.

Thus prophecy shone, from generation to generation through the various ages of humankind, like light through darkness; nor will it cease from its sound until the end of the world, uttering voices of manifold meanings as it is imbued with the inspiration of the Holy Spirit and diverse mysteries. For prophecy is in humankind as the soul is in the body: just as the soul is hidden within the body [Col. 0963A], and the body is governed through it, so prophecy comes from the Spirit of God, who surpasses every creature, is invisible, and through prophecy all who decline are reproved and those who stray are brought back to the way of righteousness, as David, My servant, also speaks through My inspiration, saying:

Words of David from the first verse of Psalm 44, that is, “My heart has uttered a good word,” bearing on the same matter and on both generations of Christ, and the manner in which they should be understood.

III. “My heart has uttered a good word; I speak my works to the King.” The meaning of this statement also is to be understood thus. I, who am Father of all, plainly show that before every creature My inward power uttered a good word: namely, that I begot My Son, through whom all things were made very good [Col. 0963B]. Therefore I also say—without changing into something different—I who am, revealing My works to Him who will reign throughout the world. For all My works that have been made from the beginning are known to My Son.

Prophecy also uttered in its power a good word when it declared those wonderful works, saying that this same Word, through whom all things were made, was to be clothed in flesh; when it showed that He would be King of kings; and when it showed that the whole, unbroken earth ought to bring forth this righteous shoot—the earth not crushed by the work of a man. Prophecy knew this through the infusion of the Holy Spirit: namely, in certain old men, certain young men, and certain children, who spoke by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit in many signs concerning this same shoot, which is the Word of God.

For God created the male from earth and changed him into flesh of blood; but the woman, taken from that man, remained flesh from flesh, not to be changed into another thing [Col. 0963C]. And these people knew in the spirit of prophecy that a woman, through the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, would bear the Son of God, just as a flower grows from the most sweet air. This was also prefigured in Aaron’s rod, which, cut from a tree, showed the Virgin Mary: a man was so cut off from her mind that she was never touched by the pleasure of any union, but through the burning power of the Holy Spirit brought forth one man, who encompassed all creatures, because, proceeding from Him, they had received taste; and therefore all obeyed His voice.

For the prophets had said that a woman should come forth to give birth through the work of charity, like a rod from the stock of Jesse; and they ascribed this virginal birth to the King, namely the Son of God. When this woman encompassed the Son of God, the people who saw and heard Him in the likeness of their own image loved Him more than if they had not seen Him; for what people see in a shadow they cannot know fully. Hence, when the prophets spoke in the sound of shadow, these things sometimes passed over them as a shadow; yet all these things were afterward formed among human beings, because the sound of prophecy proceeds from the hidden mysteries of the Godhead [Col. 0963D].

[Col. 0964A] That the first of the two images standing at the eastern extremity of the shown building, appearing almost wholly in a beast-like guise, signifies the time before the Flood, in which human beings lived without law and without knowledge of the true God, according to a cruel manner more bestial than human.

IV. As you see, beside the aforesaid eastern extremity two other images stand close together. They signify that, as the rising of righteousness manifested in Abel had already begun to totter, God revealed two periods, joined together in proximity, of human beings with different customs: one before the Flood without law, the other after the Flood under law.

The former has a head and breast like a leopard, arms like a human being’s, and hands resembling a bear’s feet [Col. 0964B]; you see no other form in it. This is because that time before the Flood, which was without law, displayed in human customs the power and strength of various beastly natures. For then human beings were entangled in every vice through the first diabolical deception, consigning God to forgetfulness and living according to the taste of their own will. At times they acted in their arms like human beings; at other times, in the works of their hands, they imitated the nature and rapacity of cruel beasts.

Therefore people neglected moral decency and did not strive to live according to human discipline, but remained wholly deformed in this way. It is clothed in a stone tunic, moves neither this way nor that, and turns its gaze toward the north, because those who lived in the aforesaid time surrounded themselves with the hardness and weight of sins and did not turn from evil to good. In their knowledge they saw indeed that they performed evil and shameful deeds in which the ancient serpent rejoices, yet they did not wish to abandon them.

For when God created heaven and earth, He divided the earth so that one part of it is immutable and another mutable; from the latter God also formed humankind. Human beings are likewise mutable through waking and sleeping. For when one is awake, one does not have, according to the course of the sun, the light of one’s eyes as light; thus one is like a person whose soul is darkened as in night [Col. 0964C].

Concerning the strength, cruelty, and impure customs of human beings before the Flood, and how, through the devil’s art, all but a few departed from the worship of God.

V. God placed humankind in the land of the living, which is not illuminated by the sphere of the sun but is flooded with the living light of eternity. Yet humanity, having transgressed the divine command, was sent back into the land of mutability. Humanity produced two sons: one offered sacrifice to God; the other, having killed his brother, became guilty of death. The one who offered sacrifice to God and heard the voice of God was slain. Hence great mourning arose.

For in that first creation human beings had such strength and such power that they even overcame the strongest beasts. Thus they often delighted to play with them [Col. 0965A], and the beasts themselves, fearing human beings and restraining their ferocity, submitted to them; yet for this reason they did not change their nature. But human beings, changing the beautiful form of their rationality, mingled themselves with beasts. What was thus generated, if it resembled a human more than a brute animal, they hated and neglected; but if it had more the form of a brute animal than that of a human, they embraced it with the kiss of love.

The customs of those human beings then existed in two modes: now according to cattle, just as the leopard and the bear belong to the manners of human beings and beasts. Therefore they did not possess the most beautiful feathers of rationality, by which they might pant toward God with upright faith and hope, because those feathers had failed in them because of the aforesaid sins. The ancient serpent suggested this to them so that the glory of their rationality might perish—a glory which it tore apart with great hatred in humankind.

For the devil said within himself: “What is this that the Most High has made? It consents more to my counsel than to His own. Therefore I shall overcome Him in its formation.” Thus human beings in the first age, polluted by the serpent’s foam, acted according to the taste of their earthly vessel and not according to the breath of the soul. Nor did they wish to know anything except what they saw formed, saying: “What good is a wind to me, which is neither formed nor speaks to me? What speaks to me [Col. 0965B] and runs to me—that I shall hold!”

For the devil’s art breathed into certain great animals and spoke to human beings through them: “I am the one who created you.” In this way it suggested to human beings that they should be polluted through those animals, in order to overthrow within them the sound of the voice of rationality by which they ought to praise God, so that they might not praise God—as it neither wished to do itself nor seeks to wish.

But a few, who had heard the first-formed human being, who had told them how he had been formed by God, placed in the place of delight, and gone out from it, tasted their human nature. They did not mingle themselves with cattle; as God had appointed them, they lived uprightly and soberly in their own nature. Because of the trouble and burden of the common people, who were polluted in the manner described above [Col. 0965C], they fled to high mountains. There they were so strengthened by the breath of the soul that they were not free to sin, but continually sighed, saying: “Where shall we seek Him who created us?”

The aforesaid peoples mocked them, saying: “What is it that these men worship, which they neither see with their eyes nor touch with their hands?” They also mocked Noah’s building. But God spoke to these few through His mystical miracles, just as He had spoken to Abel, the son of the first human being.

That God, unable to endure the iniquities and crimes of human beings in that age, exterminated the whole human race and every living thing, except those enclosed by the ark, through the waters of the Flood; concerning the alteration of the sun, moon, stars, and earth from the qualities they possessed before the Flood; and that at the end of the world fire will consume the earth to the same depth that the waters penetrated by their inundation [Col. 0966A].

VI. After the earth had been filled with this contrary people, I, who am, no longer enduring these criminal sins, decreed that the human race should be drowned in the waters, except for the few who had not known them. The earth was not dried out until the whole deceived people had been submerged. For the waters flooded the entire earth so that it became like mud, and human corpses were immersed in it in such a way that they could not afterward be found; though some animal carcasses, because of their lightness, appeared on the surface of the waters.

Nor was the earth dried before the sun, together with the courses of moon and stars and all their offices, had completed its rising and setting; nor before all these had drawn the waters back to their appointed places, as they had been set at the beginning [Col. 0966B]. Thus the earth was baked by the heat of the sun into a different condition from that in which it had formerly appeared.

For after Adam’s fall and before the Flood, the sun, moon, stars, and other heavenly bodies were somewhat disturbed by an excessive and powerful heat, and human beings then were so strong in their bodies that they could endure that heat. Even now the fervor of great heat sometimes displays this, when the aforesaid stars are at times troubled by it. For after the Flood they were so flooded by the waters that they appear brighter in their coldness and heat than they had before the Flood, while the earth and human beings afterward remained in greater weakness and infirmity than formerly.

For in the Flood water, flooding the whole earth down to the bottom of the penetrable earth, changed it into mud; and on the Last Day it will burn to that same depth, because afterward humanity will have no need of it. God exercises His judgments upon humanity through water and fire, so that, since He composed humanity by these things, humanity may also be brought low by the same. And as God floods the whole earth with water’s moisture and composes and strengthens it with the heat of fire, so He moistens human beings with the moisture of the body and strengthens them by the fiery heat of the soul [Col. 0966C].

But those whom the Lord had preserved after the Flood for the begetting of a new race, terrified by the dreadful judgment of God which they had seen, burned in the fear of God and began to offer their sacrifices in honor of God [Col. 0966D].

That through the alteration of the elements human strength too was diminished after the Flood; concerning their temporary correction through terror at that judgment; and concerning the rainbow, first set then in the clouds as a covenant or sign between God and human beings.

VII. But afterward, generation after generation proceeded with lesser strength than human beings had possessed before the Flood, as stated above. For when the earth was altered, human strength too was altered and made weaker, because they had followed the ancient deceiver, who had changed his glory into serpentine habits. For the serpent is cunning in deceiving whomever it wishes to deceive and in fleeing from the person from whom it seeks to flee.

So too the ancient enemy acts when he deceives with the deceit of the death-dealing poison of unbelief the person he overcomes; and when he quickly flees from the one by whom he is conquered, because he is trampled down by that person, just as he was cast from heaven [Col. 0967A]. This age thus flourished in the fear of the Lord, resisting the ancient serpent so that, through its breath, forgetfulness of God might not be poured into humanity as it had been before the Flood.

For after the Flood God made a new earth with a new people, placing the rainbow in the clouds as a sign that the waters should no longer drown the entire earth and all peoples. He also showed that all His enemies should know how great a power He held over them in His dreadful judgment. For God’s judgment possesses great power for striking His enemies, who wish to destroy the truth of the Godhead; and after the fall of the son of perdition, He will bring about the end of all mortal human beings with fire and great storms, so that thereafter nothing mortal shall in any way appear [Col. 0967B].

That the other image signifies the period after the Flood under the Law; and that the variations of its diverse garb signify the divisions of time from the Flood to the coming of the Lord, or to the end of the world, as well as the qualities of the customs of human beings existing or yet to exist in them.

VIII. But the other image, which is nearer to the said corner, has a human face and hands folded together, but shows within itself the feet of a hawk. It signifies that period after the Flood which existed under the Law in human customs, proceeding to that point at which the severity of the same Law faltered. In that period the intention and works of people who looked more toward fleshly than spiritual things were idle without labor; and in their walking they ordained harshness rather than gentleness, because the Law spared no one but sharply punished the offender.

It is clothed, as it were, in a wooden tunic, because the aforesaid period had drawn to itself the old Law, which neglected spiritual fruits [Col. 0967C]. It appears white from its top to its navel, because the time before Noah—who knew his Creator, knew himself to be human, first began the building of holiness, and offered gifts to God—was, as it were, white up to Abraham, who arose as the navel of strength. For human beings had been so terrified through the gulf of waters that thereafter for a time they gathered themselves to the fear of God through uprightness.

From its navel down to its loins it is reddish, signifying the time extending from Abraham to Moses, burning in circumcision. For as dawn precedes the sun, so Abraham, through the sign of circumcision in which he crushed lust, preceded the humanity of the Son of God. From its loins down to its knees it is grayish, showing that the time from Moses the lawgiver to the Babylonian exile proceeded in the hardness and severity of the Law according to the flesh, and there began to bend itself toward many vanities.

From the knees [Col. 0968A] down to the ends of its feet it is turbid, signifying the time extending from the Babylonian exile to the abolition of that Law, when the Son of God came and fulfilled it wholly in Himself. This time appeared turbid in negligence and torpor, because the same Law, already reckoned disgraceful and considered nothing, like troubled water, was tending carnally toward its fall. For those who seemed at that time to be under the Law did not wish to know the rising sun of righteousness; rather, they said that they wished to look only at the letters written on tablets and affirmed that nothing else was to be understood in them.

Therefore I, who judge all things justly, sent against them certain peoples to capture them and scatter them into distant regions: I did this through My judgments, which I had extended over them in Egypt and elsewhere when they trusted in themselves [Col. 0968B] and did what they wished. They will remain in this hardness of unbelief until the ancient serpent moves its eye in a certain wandering and lost man. Hidden divinity will so kill that man that neither angel nor human being will know the blow; and then this same people of the Law will look to Me amid great afflictions, mourning and lamenting that it has been deceived for so long. But how long human beings will afterward remain in the transitory world is unknown to angel and human being.

The aforesaid image holds a sword placed crosswise, as it were, above its loins, because it shows itself to have existed in circumcision, as it were in a fleshly passage. Yet from the navel of the vital parts down to the loins a human being sins through their motion, when the human mind moves them to sin. It also declares the judgments of God, which possess pure justice: namely, that God sheds the blood of the murderer who dismembers a human being, and also crushes by righteous judgment the person who turns himself away from the murderer into other evils.

Remaining motionless, it turns its gaze toward the west, because the people who lived in the same period, while the old Law flourished, did not move themselves toward spiritual understanding. They knew the fall of the ancient serpent and saw many dangers, yet held the salvation of their souls in torpor and negligence [Col. 0968C].

For the fiery dragon, seeing that God had preserved certain persons whom the flood of waters had not devoured, emitted great wrath through its breath, saying furiously within itself: “I shall stir up all my arts and sift them out one by one, so that I may deceive through certain impediments those whom the Flood did not drown, and thus bring them again under my subjection” [Col. 0968D].

Concerning the significance of sacrifices, circumcision, and the Law, which preceded through prophecy in the Fathers the incarnate Son of God; concerning the preaching of the prophets; and concerning the fact that humankind could not be saved unless the Word became flesh; also concerning the devil’s suggestions by which he deceives human beings through delusion, and the modes of help by which God always resists him.

IX. Thus this period extends from Noah after the Flood down to the incarnation of my Son, who turned those believing in himself toward spiritual understanding; and there another period proceeded toward life, not according to the flesh but according to the spirit. For in Noah I displayed many miracles, just as in my first manifestation in Adam I performed very many miracles; for, as I foresaw in Adam all human beings who would be born, so also in Noah I foreshadowed the resurrection of a new age. From this stock there arose most powerful and swift prophets, who sharpened their tongues and boldly uttered what they saw in the Holy Spirit: namely, that God would send into the world his Word, which had been in him before the ages. And this was incarnated in such a way that the whole world might marvel at it; and their tongues swiftly traversed the world for this miracle, when they declared that one beautiful above the sons of men would come to earth.

But reason dictates, and action is performed in accordance with the dictation; for if the dictation did not proceed, the action would not follow. For God decreed the world and humanity in his Word. The Word, which is without beginning, decreed a certain work, by which it put on the world as a garment, so that when humanity had sinned, if it confessed God, he might draw it back to himself with that same garment. Therefore, if that same Word had not put on this garment, humanity would not be saved, just as the lost angel will not be saved. And how could it be that God lacked the power to restore to his place one who had departed from him, if that being confessed in repentance? For just as it pleased almighty God to make humanity, so it also pleased him to redeem the one who trusts in him.

Therefore he breathed forth prophecy secretly and sent it veiled, until he should complete his work; yet before he brought it to fulfillment, he showed it through preceding signs. For he displayed the ark to Noah, gave circumcision to Abraham, and taught the law to Moses, so that the movement of lust, which moves like the tongue of a serpent, might be confounded by these; and so that, as the devil had deceived humanity through animals before the Holy of Holies came, that same devil might be trampled down through animals in the ceremonies of God.

And these three signs—sacrifice, circumcision, and law—went before the Son of God; and he willed that they should suffer and come to an end in himself, according to the words of the inspiration of the prophets, who spoke both of God and of all the evils of the north. For as long as the ancient serpent wishes to fight against God, just as he also fought against him in heaven, he attacks human beings, persuading them to oppose God as well and to worship as God that which they handle with eyes and hands, as he showed them in Baal and other idols.

But just as no one can comprehend God and no one can bring his work to completion, so neither can the devil know a human being unless first, through his own suggestion, that person pants after him; and then the devil greatly rejoices in his wickedness that he conquers God’s work by thus deceiving it. For when he knows that a human being can act, he does not yet know what that person wishes to do; and when he understands that the person is yearning for God, so that he places his works in God, because he was created through him, the devil immediately approaches by his suggestion, saying: “Since you have the ability to do whatever you wish, why do you seek your work from another? And what harm will it do you if you perform works which you are able to perform, when the one whom you call your Creator made his work as he wished?” And thus, by suggesting this, he deceives the person.

Therefore the north wind signifies this suggestion and persuasion; for as it destroys and overturns an entire house, so this diabolical blast leads a human being’s right understanding into such forgetfulness that he forgets God’s inspiration and cannot sigh toward God. It also cuts off the breath of that soul which ought to pant toward God and kindles it toward sins which it can commit through its body. For in the blast of this foul suggestion the devil trusts that he can draw even the souls of rational human beings to himself, just as a worm lying in mud produces other worms from the juice of its own filth.

For he led human beings into these perverse and foul works, so that they bent their knees to Baal and to other idols, from whose mouth an unclean spirit sounded and spoke, teaching them incestuous deeds. For at the beginning peoples proceeded from generation to generation, whose horrible minds withdrew from God because of the taste of their flesh. Yet, as was said before, through the ark God brought forth righteousness; through circumcision, which was like steel, he wounded death, so that even the lust breathed out by the serpent was laid bare through it; but through the law, which he wrote with his finger, he confounded it. In this he recalled that he had made humanity with his finger, with the ministry of humanity—that is, with the creature which God had first given it—preceding: from this, taking clean animals, humanity first offered sacrifice to almighty God.

What Abel began, the law wholly completed, signifying that the person who offers as sacrifice an animal by which he is nourished should offer himself as a sacrifice to God. And as the sun has the moon subject to itself, both waxing and waning, so the Son of God, the true Sun, had the law in himself: it grew in him when he fulfilled it, and it came to its end in him when he offered himself to God the Father. And as at his death an eclipse of the sun occurred, and the sun then shone again over the whole world, so that same Son of God willed that humanity should shine according to him, looking upon his death and considering in it what it ought to do.

And as a plough with beasts turns over the earth, into which seed is sown that yields abundant fruit on which people feed, so the people under the law possessed written letters in God’s commandments, but were not satisfied with their fruit, because they did not know what was hidden in the letters. But the Son of God revealed through the seeds of his words to believers that, nourished by his flesh and blood, they possess life; and he manifested through himself what was hidden in divine mysteries.

[Col. 0971A]

**Concerning the innumerable multitude of the faithful who, in diverse ways in this life, both in labours and in the mortification of vices, fight manfully for God’s honour and their own salvation, and receive diverse rewards from God’s gift according to their merits.**

X. But what you see as innumerable other images of human beings throughout the whole southern region, flowing like a cloud in the air, means that the multitude of believers who have imitated and imitate the Son of God in burning righteousness, lifting their minds to heavenly things, have ascended and are ascending from virtue to virtue.

Some of them bear on their heads crowns, as it were, because, when they raise their minds upward, they place upon their souls the adornment of heavenly rewards through the just and holy desires of their hearts; for good desires are the beginning of a good undertaking. Others hold in their hands richly adorned palms, because they show in their works the victory of the good contest. Others hold pipes—that is, the rewards which they have deserved in the fear and love of God through their teaching. Others hold lyres: namely, the rewards of the hard and narrow way which leads to life. Others hold organs, because the manifold virtues which tend toward God in praises appear in them.

And the sound of these instruments resounds like the sweet sound of clouds, because the praises which ring out in the aforesaid dignities and rewards of virtues harmonize, through the desirable merit of those working in virtue and lifting their minds to heavenly things; for according as human beings merit by doing good uprightly, their rewards shall be in recompense.

Thus the minds of the faithful, as has been said, run like clouds: in the soul’s desire, by which the blessed person seeks from God a work to perform, one is never satisfied, just as streams flowing from the sea do not cease from their floods. And because holy desires, which are the beginning of all good things, are implanted in them in this way, as was said above, God crowns them with the heavenly host, because they cleave to him so that in no way will they be separated from him.

For God’s ordering in creatures first signified that a human being ought to be revived in spiritual life. For when in the law he commanded certain animals to be bound, killed, and burned, and their blood to be sprinkled, he foreshadowed that certain human beings, running like clouds and looking to him, would be tormented in his love, killed, and thus offered in sacrifice. And because these people suck the breasts of virtues, so that they may flee lust and other vices, they bear the victory of palms when they even pour out their blood before they fall from the net of righteousness through works of unbelief. Thus they torment themselves in two ways: by fighting against their bodies and by pouring out their blood through God’s ordinance. Hence they are also likened to the angels who always stand before God.

But those who exercise their office through the teaching of almighty God, teaching others, resound with the pipes of holiness when through the voice of reason they sing righteousness into human minds. For just as speech dictates and sound resounds, and through sound speech is heard and carried round so that it may be heard, so through a pipe the voice is multiplied. Thus, in the fear and love of God, the teacher’s voice ought to be multiplied among people, where it gathers the faithful and puts the unbelieving to flight.

In this way others also arise, who despise and reject themselves, binding themselves in the modesty of virginity, regarding worldly pleasure as punishment, persevering in angelic praises, and flying to God like an eagle in the full desire of their hearts. They are like the dawn that precedes the sun, always beholding God with the eyes of dove-like simplicity. Therefore through lyres they render to God, to whom they are thus joined, praises which human knowledge cannot at all explain.

[Col. 0972B] Yet there are others who gather innumerable virtues to themselves like sheaves in God’s commandments, and serve humility, the queen of virtues, through organs, when they cast themselves down, as it were, to the ground in God’s fear and love. For humility opens heaven to those who imitate it and closes it to those who neglect it, so that it cannot be opened by any persecution of enemies; and it casts pride down into hell, which is the inheritance of people of arrogant minds. And it reigns in heaven with those who serve alongside it.

For just as organs are turned to the sound of praise through their different kinds of tones, so God has established human praises in likeness to the angels; for as the heavenly host overcame pride in God’s sight, so people who restrain themselves from evils continually overcome pride within themselves. For humanity is the work of the right hand of almighty God, which that hand has wrought, and it will fill the choir of the lost angels; and therefore it is also under the protection of the good angels.

And God greatly delights in these two orders, angels and human beings: in the praises of angels and in the holy works of human beings. For with these he accomplishes, according to his will, all things which were thus foreknown in eternity. But the angel is steadfast before God, whereas humanity is unstable; therefore the work of humanity fittingly fails, but the praises of angels do not fail. Heaven and earth also touch God, since they were made through him and exist for God’s glory. But because humanity is mortal, divine revelations which are sometimes made manifest to prophets and wise persons are often clouded like a shadow.

But when humanity, from mutable, has become immutable, then it shall see by knowing the brightness of God and shall remain with God, as David, my servant, says in my will:

**Words of David from Psalm 62 [63], bearing upon the same matter, and the sense in which they should be understood.**

XI. “And I shall rejoice in the covering of your wings; my soul has clung after you; your right hand has upheld me.”

The meaning of this saying should be understood thus: In the defense of your protections, O God, I shall rejoice when I have been freed from the burden of sins; and because my soul desired through good works to come after you, therefore the power of your strength gathered me as I drew deep sighs and cried out to you, so that henceforth I may be safe from my enemies.

For I am a work which you have made, since before the antiquity of days you had in your ordering that you would make me in this manner, so that every creature might be at my service. And when you created me, you gave me power to act according to you, just as you had made me; therefore I am yours. And you put on immaculate flesh, as befitted you the Creator, and thus extended the hem of your garment.

Therefore you also moved heaven with praises and surrounded it, in the encompassing circle of angels, with the variety of every adornment. They cannot fully marvel when they surround themselves, as in the encircling of a girdle of praises, that you made humanity thus: because, when he vanished from heavenly glory, you girded humanity with the girdle of praise of the one who refused heavenly glory, and strengthened it with your garment so that henceforth it might not vanish in praise.

But the angels also marvel because from mortal Adam you took your garment. Yet you did this so that the same transgressor might live again and so that divine brightness—which cannot be exhausted by any inquiry of experience—might shine clearly to the heavenly angel, saying: “You are always in my sight and therefore do not need recalling, unlike the one whom you found through my garment, since he had not utterly denied me when he had been deceived by another. For when he sought my likeness, he became mortal; therefore he had to be recalled through the sufferings of my garment, lest the fellowship of your brotherhood perish in him. For although I created you without flesh and him with flesh, yet I made both of you male.”

In this way the hidden Divinity, wholly just and not perfectly seen by anyone except insofar as it deigns to reveal itself, showed itself to the angel who had remained in heavenly things without falling. For in the grasp of its right hand it has this fullness: that no one who looks upon it with the pupil of the eye of faith perishes. For those who do not look upon it with the eye of faith vanish from its sight, as the lost angel and those consenting to him also perished. For when God had created all things, he also ordered all things well: rewards of merits for those who look toward him, and judgment upon those who refuse to look toward him, as has been said.

**That all things were created through the Word, begotten from the Father without beginning, and that humanity was redeemed through that same Word made flesh in the Virgin.**

XII. And all these things were revealed through the incarnate Son of God, because those who believe in him will be saved, while those who turn away from him will be condemned. For he proceeded not from the root of the earth but from an inviolate Virgin by the Father’s will: before his Incarnation creating all things with the Father, and after his Incarnation saving the humanity he had formed, because he put on the sinless form of a human being and redeemed through the human being whom he had created. No one else could do this except the one who had created humanity.

For when Adam was a simple and radiant son, he both kept watch and slept, so that through the spirit he might have wisdom and through sleep his flesh might rest. Thus he was brought into the immutable land of delight, so that through the spirit he might know immortality and might not deny invisible things through the outward sight of his eyes. Immortal life indeed has no cloudy light, unlike the formed eye, which sees for a short time because darkness comes upon it again. Humanity suffers this because its eye is covered with a cloudy skin.

The pupil of the eye shows the vision of the inner eyes, which is unknown to the flesh; but the eyelid signifies the man of flesh, which is poured outwardly. Thus every human work is completed in two modes of knowledge. The knowledge of inward sight teaches humanity divine things, but the flesh obstructs this; blinded knowledge, however, performs nocturnal works according to the sight of the serpent, which does not see light. Hence it turns away from works of light all whom it can, as it did in Adam, when it disturbed in him the light of living knowledge.

Knowledge in Adam was also like prophecy, and this endured until the Son of God became human, so that he might illuminate it through himself, just as the sun illuminates the whole earth; and so that he might spiritually fulfill in himself all things which have been foretold—those recognized as having been done before the law and under the law—when he offered his whole self to the heavenly Father, as is also written:

**Words of David from Psalm 103 [104], bearing upon this same matter, and how they are to be understood.**

XIII. “You make the cloud your ascent; you walk upon the wings of the winds.”

The meaning of this saying should be understood thus: Lord God, you are the one who makes the just and upright desires of the faithful your ascent, so that you reign in their hearts; and you also direct your ways above the words and writings of teachers, where you surpass them because you walk without stain, sensing no fault in yourself.

Therefore clouds are your ascent, which you made as a ladder for yourself when, through your garment, O Son of God, you ascended them—that garment which you assumed from the one and most inviolate Virgin, whose enclosure no one ever opened or touched. For as dew enters the earth, so you entered her; and you were rooted not in the stock of a man but in divinity, just as a ray of the sun warms the earth so that it brings forth its shoot.

And from her, just as into her, you came forth without any corruption or pain, as if in sleep; just as Eve was taken from the sleeping man, and that same man saw her without a wound and with joy. So too the one Virgin embraced her Son joyfully in her bosom. And Eve was created not from seed but from the flesh of the man, because God created her by the same power by which he sent his Son into the Virgin. Nor were any others afterward found like Eve, virgin and mother, or Mary, mother and virgin.

In this way God put on the form of humanity and covered his divinity with it; this is visible to the angels in heaven, which is his dwelling-place. Hence humanity also, which he formed in height, breadth, and depth, is his dwelling-place.

**That the Son of God, in what he did or suffered in the flesh, fulfilled everything which before the law and in the law had been signified concerning him by typical deeds or foretold in mystical words; and that after his Ascension, strengthening the twelve apostles by the sending of the Spirit after the pattern of the twelve winds or twelve signs of heaven, and illuminating the world through their preaching, he turned all things to the better.**

XIV. This incarnate Son of God fulfilled in himself all the preceding miracles which had gone before him, as was said above. For in his infancy, when Herod was deceived by the Magi while seeking to destroy him, he showed the fall of the ancient serpent, which had endeavoured to disturb heavenly things. In his childhood he showed the period from Adam to Noah, when, in contrast to Adam’s ignorance, he possessed great wisdom in himself, so that no stain of sin touched him. There too the devil’s estimation, by which he thought humanity wholly lost, was deceived, because he did not know that God had put on human form.

For all who then saw and heard him marvelled, saying: “We have never seen or heard such things as are in this boy”: namely, that in simple and untaught childhood wisdom of great depth appears. In saying this they did not know that he was the root of the knowledge of angels and human beings, nor that he was the one from whom angels and human beings are rooted.

He also raised up in his humanity what had failed through Adam: namely, the revelation of righteousness; for he ascribed all his work to his Father. And as a tree brings forth its large branches from the greenness of its root, so he completed all his works in the divinity from which he was rooted in humanity, because he came from it and is with it without any division.

He also restored for the better, in his flesh, the foul works of human beings; and through his teaching, with the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, he clothed them in holiness. Thus he recalled to the life of righteousness those who were, as it were, drowned in a flood and dead in sins, as had been foreshadowed under Noah.

The same Son of God, appearing in the flesh as a young man, declared in himself the period from Noah to Abraham, to whom circumcision was commanded. For by entering the water and sanctifying it in his body, and by performing great miracles, he showed that human beings living after the Flood more holy than before the Flood, and renouncing the incestuous acts which they had formerly loved, ceased from the injustice of forgetting God, so that the nakedness of incestuous action might be brought to shame.

For chastity in that same Son of God trampled down lust, bound it with the cord of teaching, and compelled it to serve him through abstinence from sins. For the Son of God, showing and teaching all righteousness through himself, fulfilled it in his humanity through the cutting away of sins, as circumcision also showed, which was performed in one place to shame the serpent.

But when afterward he had fulfilled in himself the fleshly commandments given through Moses, having endured the binding of chains and the other reproaches, and having become a living sacrifice on the cross for his sheep, he departed from the age, as day is separated from night; for after he had performed very many signs and shown many hidden miracles through himself, he was taken from the earth.

In his passion and death he also manifested the Babylonian power, when the children of Israel were led into captivity, just as he himself was handed over to the Gentiles to be crucified. Then his disciples became sad, just as the aforesaid captives, laying aside joy, changed their instruments into mournful sounds. Yet, rising from death and appearing to his disciples with very many proofs, he thereby signified the return of those captives.

And when he commanded those same disciples to go into the whole world to baptize believers, and after his Ascension strengthened them by the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, so that, defeated by diverse tribulations from adversaries, they should not fall, but should overcome them by glorious miracles, he showed that the old law had ended according to the flesh and had itself been changed into spiritual life.

He taught them also as much as they were able to receive, because they could not yet see him as he is in his divinity; just as a person looks upon another’s form but cannot behold that person’s soul. For when the Father drew him back into his heart, whence he had gone out and where he had never been absent, as a person draws back his breath into himself, all the hosts of angels and all heavenly mysteries openly beheld him as God and human being.

Therefore he touched his disciples with that fire in which he was conceived in his mother’s womb, and poured into them, in fiery tongues, a most powerful force stronger than that of a lion, which does not fear beasts but catches them, so that they might not fear human beings but might capture them. For the Holy Spirit changed them into another life which they had not previously known, and so raised them by his breath that they did not know themselves to be human beings.

He visited them in a greater and stronger measure than he visited anyone before or afterward. For the prophets spoke very many things through the Holy Spirit, and many performed very many miracles after those disciples; nevertheless, none of them saw fiery tongues. Because they saw fiery tongues with their outward eyes, they were inwardly strengthened so that every fearful stirring of dangers was removed from their veins, and they had terror or fear in no danger. Divine power had implanted this strength in them in the fiery tongues.

For it befitted the almighty Father to preserve this number of twelve, whom he had joined to his Son, so that these same disciples might teach others what they had heard from him. Thus God also established the firmament and composed its stability with the blasts of the twelve winds and the twelve signs of the moving months. And as the same firmament performs all its offices with fire, so they were strengthened by the fire of the Holy Spirit in all miracles; for their teaching went out like the blast of winds into all the earth and shone like the sun, and their martyrdoms burned as with the south wind.

For the months complete their course with all the things which sustain the firmament; and with these truthful human beings God completed all his signs in the catholic faith, and through his Son brought back to heaven the number ten, which is humanity, signified by the drachma which Wisdom found. Thus the Only-Begotten of God and Son of the Virgin, whose name is Star of the Sea, from whom all rivers flow and to whom they return again—just as all salvations of souls come from that same Only-Begotten of God and remain again in him—fulfilled through himself all the things previously mentioned, which were before him in the law or before the law.

He also changed all things for the better, walking thus upon the wings of the winds: that is, surpassing the aforesaid wonderful deeds of the patriarchs and the words of the prophets, as well as the teachings and writings of all teachers; and, in his humanity, flying above every creature that is human. He received every creature from his Father as an inheritance, as he also spoke to his disciples, saying:

**Words of Christ in the Gospel concerning the authority delivered to him by the Father, and how they should be understood.**

XV. “All things have been delivered to me by my Father” (Matt. 11).

The meaning of this saying should be understood thus: I, who am the Word and Son of God, came forth from my Father, by whom all things that he had predestined were delivered to me, so that I might bring them forth into forms, just as words express thoughts lying hidden in the heart. To him I return, the dispensation of my Incarnation having been completed: namely, the work which he entrusted to me in that same eternity in which I always remained inseparably with him before the ages. He sent me because of the number which he had established and which had to be filled.

And just as I received from him the power of creating in the heights, so also in the lower regions of the world I received power to restore what had been created and had perished. For in God’s true foreknowledge all things that were to be lay hidden eternally; afterward he created them through his Word, namely his Son, to whom he also entrusted the power of freeing and governing what he had created. Thus all things were delivered to his Son, who before the ages was coeternal and consubstantial with the Father in divinity.

**That the words of the prophets before the Lord’s Incarnation could not be understood because they were obscure and unknown; but that Christ, living in the world according to them and fulfilling them, made them intelligible; and that through the water of baptism both original and actual sins are washed away in faith in the Trinity.**

XVI. For the Son of God walked upon the wings of the winds, because the prophets were wings of the Holy Spirit’s words: as the Holy Spirit inspired them, so they prophesied by speaking those things. And in this they furnished an example to the same Son of God, because, as they had foretold concerning him, so he acted while remaining in the world and carried humanity, as was said above, upon his shoulder to heaven and to paradisal places.

God established the heavenly dwelling and the paradisal place in this way, like a person who builds dwellings for his dependents. Into these same places the Son of God carried with himself, at his Father’s command, the souls of the faithful rescued from the infernal regions, as one first takes possession of his city with a few people and afterward fills it with a great multitude.

Thus almighty God had foreshadowed all these things before the Incarnation of his Son and had granted humanity creation for its work. But only humanity, standing upright, looks upward to heaven with its sight; all other animals are bent toward the earth and subject to humanity. Thus humanity is imperishable through the rational spirit but perishable with worms through the flesh.

And prophecy was like the words of infants, whose words cannot be understood; but after they have grown more mature, their words are understood. So prophecy before the incarnate Son of God was unknown and not understood, but in Christ it was opened, because he is the root of all good branches. For the root first brings forth grass, the grass a shoot, then the shoot branches; the branches flowers, and the flowers fruit. Thus the root signifies Adam; the grass, the patriarchs; the shoot, the prophets; the branches, the wise; the flowers, the legal commandments; and the fruit, the incarnate Son of God, who through water brought faithful believers into remission of sins.

For through water he cleansed every blasphemy of sins which arose in Adam; and just as fire is extinguished through water, so original guilt and other sins are washed away in the laver of baptism. And because the Holy Spirit came into the water, he cleansed humanity through the circumcision of sins. He also sanctified its soul, which had become poisonous through the deception of the ancient serpent, so that henceforth it might be his tabernacle in the communion of true faith.

Therefore David speaks by my inspiration concerning one who is not washed in baptism for the remission of sins:

**Words of David from Psalm 103 [104], concerning those who through unbelief do not receive remission of offenses in baptism, and those who are cleansed in it through faith.**

XVII. “You have made darkness, and night has come; in it all the beasts of the forest shall pass through.”

The meaning of this saying should be understood thus: O God and ruler, who dispose all things justly, by your righteous judgment you have appointed the darkness of punishments for the vengeance of evils; from this also night has arisen, which is the destruction of the reprobate. For while unbelievers are in the darkness of unbelief, they incur the darkness of death. Thus they then fall eternally into perdition; and in that night without the light of faith all pass through who are fierce in tyranny and fruitless in unbelief, because, while they do not lay aside unbelief and do not run to you, God, through the grace of baptism, they shall go into oblivion as though they had never existed.

But the faithful person is one who, having laid aside the darkness of unbelief and banished the night of eternal damnation, passes beyond every beastly habit and fruitless action, turning to the life brought by him who is Life, renouncing the devil, and cleansing himself in the laver of baptism. For the Son of God proclaimed to his disciples that humanity must be regenerated in water; otherwise it would not be raised to heaven unless first cleansed from sins through water and the Holy Spirit. For when a human being is sown from the father, sent into the mother, and generated from her, in baptism that person receives the inspiration of the Holy Spirit and thus becomes a participant in holiness. But the unbeliever is cast out from holiness and sent into places of punishment.

Let the faithful receive these words with the devoted affection of the heart, because they were set forth for the benefit of believers through him who is the first and the last.

## EIGHTH VISION

[Col. 0979]

[Col. 0979B] **A brief vision concerning three images; a description of their state or appearance; and the orders of saints appearing before them.**

I. I also saw, as it were, in the midst of the aforesaid southern region, three images: two standing in a certain most pure fountain, enclosed and adorned above by a round, perforated stone, as though rooted in it, just as trees are sometimes seen growing in water. One was surrounded by a purple radiance and the other by a white radiance, so that I could not look upon them fully. But the third stood outside that same fountain, above the aforesaid stone of it, clothed in a white garment; and her face shone with such brilliance that the brightness itself reflected upon my face. Before them the blessed orders of saints appeared like clouds, gazing attentively upon them.

**Words of the first image, namely the virtue of Charity, recounting the magnificence of her works in angels and human beings and in the teaching of prophets and apostles, and exalting with the highest praise the excellence of the virtues of Wisdom and Humility.**
II. And the first image said:

“I am Charity, the radiance of the living God; and Wisdom has wrought her work with me, while Humility, rooted in the living fountain, has been my helper, and Peace clings to her. Through the radiance which I am, the living light of the blessed angels flashes forth; for as a ray shines from light, so this radiance shines upon the blessed angels, and it could not but shine, just as light cannot exist without brightness.

“For I wrote man, who was rooted in me as a shadow, just as the shadow of any object is seen in water. Thus I am also a living fountain, because all things that were made existed in me as a shadow; and according to this shadow man was made with fire and water, just as I too am fire and living water. Therefore man also has it in his soul to arrange each thing according to his will. Every animal has a shadow; and that which lives in it moves to and fro within it as a shadow.
