Thoughts exist in the rational animal, but not in brute animals, since they merely live and possess senses by which they recognize what they ought to flee and what they ought to seek; but only the soul breathed by God is rational.

“My radiance also overshadowed the prophets, who through holy inspiration foretold things to come; for in God, all things which He willed to do were shadows before they came to be. But rationality speaks with sound; sound is as it were a thought, and a word as it were a work. From this shadow the writing *Scivias* proceeded through the form of a woman, who was like a shadow of strength and health, since these powers were not working in her.

“The living fountain, therefore, is the Spirit of God, whom He distributes through all His works. These works also live from Him, possessing vital life through Him, just as the shadow of all things appears in water; and there is nothing that plainly sees that from which it lives, but it senses only that by which it is moved. And as water makes that which is in it flow, so the living soul is a breath, ever remaining in a human being and making that person, through knowing, thinking, speaking, and acting, flow forth as it were.

[Col. 0980C] “Within this shadow Wisdom measured all things in equal proportion, lest one thing exceed another in its weight, and lest one could be moved contrary to another. For she surpasses and restrains all the malice of diabolical art, because she was before the beginning of all beginnings, and after their end she shall remain in her most mighty power, and no one will be able to resist her. For she summoned no one to her aid and had need of no one, because she was first and last; nor did she receive an answer from anyone, because she was first and brought about the establishment of all things.

“And in herself and through herself she established all things devoutly and gently; nor can they be destroyed by any enemy, because she most excellently saw the beginning and end of her works. She composed all things completely, so that all things are also governed through her. She also beheld her work, which she ordered into a right constitution in the shadow of living water, when through the aforesaid unlearned feminine form she disclosed certain natural powers of diverse things, certain writings concerning the merits of life, and other profound mysteries. Seeing these in true vision, that woman was greatly weakened.

“But before all these things, Wisdom had drawn the words of the prophets, the words of other wise persons, and also those of the Gospels from the living fountain; she entrusted them equally to the disciples of the Son of God, so that rivers of living water might be poured out through them over the whole world, by which human beings, as if drawn in a net, might be brought back to salvation.

[Col. 0981A] “The springing fountain is the purity of the living God, and His radiance shines in it. In that splendor God embraces all things with great love; their shadow appeared in the springing fountain before God commanded them to come forth in their forms. And in me, Charity, all things shone forth, and my brightness displayed the formation of things, just as a shadow indicates a form. In Humility, who is my helper, the creature came forth at God’s command; and in that same Humility God inclined Himself toward me, so that He might raise the dry leaves that had fallen into that blessedness by which He can do all that He wills. For He had formed them from the earth, and therefore after their fall He delivered them.

“For man is wholly God’s workmanship: he looks toward heaven, treads the earth underfoot in dominion, and commands all creatures, because through the soul he beholds the height of heaven. Therefore through it he is heavenly, but through his visible body he is earthly. Thus God gathered in Humility the human being lying in the depths, in opposition to him who was cast from heaven into confusion. For when the ancient serpent sought by pride to rend the harmony of the angels, God held it fast in His mighty power so that it should not be torn apart by that serpent’s fury. For Satan, possessing great glory on high, reckoned within himself that he could do whatever he wished. lest he thereby lose the glory of the stars; yet he wished to possess everything, and therefore, while he coveted everything, he lost all that he possessed.”

[Col. 0981C] **That whatever God has wrought, He has accomplished in Charity, Humility, and Peace; and exposition of the foregoing vision, shown beneath the images of these three virtues.**

III. Again I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

“Everything whatsoever God has wrought, He has accomplished in Charity, Humility, and Peace, so that man too may love Charity, embrace Humility, and hold fast Peace, lest he go to destruction with him who mocked these virtues at his first arising.

“For you see, as if in the midst of the aforesaid southern region, three images: namely, two standing in a certain most pure fountain, enclosed and adorned above by a round, perforated stone, as though rooted in it, just as trees sometimes appear to grow in water. These are the three virtues, in the strength of burning justice, in the name of the Holy Trinity: the first is Charity, the second Humility, and the third Peace.

“Charity and Humility exist in the most pure Godhead, from which rivers of blessedness flow, because these two virtues show forth, for the deliverance and raising-up of man who lay crushed in the depths of sins, the only Son of God proclaimed throughout the whole world. When His body, pierced on the cross and buried, rose through the marvelous power of divinity, He showed Himself to be the stone of strength and honor, because He referred all the miracles which that same Son of God performed in the world to the glory of His Father.

[Col. 0982A] “Nor are these virtues separated from divinity, just as a root is not severed from a tree; for God, who is Charity, maintains Humility in all His works and judgments. Charity and Humility, descending to earth with the same Son of God, brought Him back as He returned to heaven.

“One is surrounded with purple radiance, the other with white brightness, so that you cannot look fully upon them. This signifies that Charity burns in heavenly love like purple, while Humility shakes earthly filth from herself in the whiteness of uprightness. Although it is difficult for a mortal human being to imitate these in every respect while living in the flesh, nevertheless one should not neglect to love God above all things and to humble oneself in all things for the reward of eternal things.

“But the third image stands outside that same fountain upon its aforesaid stone. This means that Peace, which abides in heaven, also guards earthly affairs, which are outside heavenly things, because the Son of God, being the true cornerstone, brought Peace when He illumined the whole world by His birth, and when the angels in their praiseworthy song recognized Him as God and man.

“Her face shines with such brilliance that this brightness strikes back upon your own face, because Peace, which arose through the Son of God, cannot be held on earth as it is in the heights. Heavenly things are always in the stability of unanimity, but earthly things, cast to and fro in their instability, are often changed. Yet man, who is God’s work, will praise Him; for the human soul will be in praise, as an angel is. While man lives in the world, he cultivates the earth as he wills and desires, and he displays God, because he has been marked according to Him.

[Col. 0982C] “And before them appear the blessed orders of saints as in a cloud, whom they attentively behold, because through Charity and Humility one comes to the glory of heavenly exaltation. The minds of the faithful flow like clouds from virtue to virtue; and there Charity and Humility, considering them with careful discernment and protection, ardently and gently kindle them toward the desires of heaven.

“For Charity is the adornment of God’s works, just as a ring is adorned by a noble stone. But Humility openly revealed herself in the humanity of the Son of God, who arose from the unblemished star of the sea. He did not fear the fall of the first man, nor was He frightened by the first man’s expulsion, because no sin touched Him: He was wholly rooted in divinity. But certain persons who saw Him and went with Him dried up and fell like dry leaves. Yet He caused others to sprout in their place, and He took counsel from no human being concerning how He should overcome His enemies, who had fallen from Him by their own will.

“Nor was He idle, as the first man in his fall had ceased from good works; for He renewed man into a more glorious life than that in which he had previously been placed. Nor did He incline Himself toward the seat of pride, as the devil did, who deceived man with the pestilence of disobedience. Nor did He fear how He would take man away from him, because He foreknew that the devil’s head was to be crushed by mighty strength.

[Col. 0983A] “And adorned and endowed with the aforesaid virtues, the Church was led into the king’s chamber, as it is written:

**Words of David from Psalm XLIV, commending the Church adorned with the varied cultivation of virtues.**

IV. ‘The queen stood at your right hand in garments of gold, surrounded by variety.’

The meaning of this statement is to be understood thus:

“O Son of the Father, in the espousal of the catholic faith the Church stood, endowed for the prosperity of heavenly desires with Your humanity, which was drenched in the redness of Your blood. She was also wrapped in the manifold virtues which she brought from Your Father’s house when she placed herself in the embrace of Your love.

“For this espousal proceeded from the will of almighty God, who accomplished it with a radiant work, gathering man from highest to lowest and adorning him with the garment of justice, when the Son of God willed to suffer in the flesh for the redemption of man.

[Col. 0984A] “For man is the work of God’s right hand; through him the Church is clothed and called to royal nuptials. Humility brought these about when God Most High looked down upon the depths of the earth and gathered the Church from the common people, so that he who had fallen might rise through repentance and renew himself in holy conduct, adorned with a diversity of virtues like the freshness of flowers.

“Pride, however, is always corrupt, because it oppresses, divides, and takes away every thing. Humility takes or removes nothing from anyone, but retains everything in Charity. In Humility God inclined Himself to earth, and through her He gathered all the virtues. For the virtues tend toward the Son of God, just as a virgin, rejecting a man, calls Christ her bridegroom; and they are joined to Humility when she leads them to the nuptials of the King.

“Let the faithful receive these words with the devotion of their hearts, because they have been set forth for the benefit of believers through Him who is first and last.”

## VISION NINE

[Col. 0983]

[Col. 0983B] **Vision of two images shining with marvelous brightness, with a description of their appearance; and of darkness occupying the entire western side of the building, and of fire with sulphur and other darkness bending itself as far as the middle of the northern side.**

[Col. 0983C] I. Then, near the northern corner facing east, I saw an image whose face and feet radiated with such brightness that the same radiance struck back upon my sight. It wore a garment as though of white silk, and over it had a green tunic, which appeared everywhere adorned with diverse pearls. It bore, as it were, earrings at its ears, necklaces on its breast, and bracelets on its arms; all these seemed to be of most pure gold, adorned with precious stones.

But as if in the middle of that same northern region, I saw another image standing erect and of marvelous form. At its summit, where the place of its head should have been, there shone such radiant brightness that it struck back upon my sight. In the middle of its belly there appeared a human head with gray hair and a beard; its feet resembled the feet of a lion.

It also had six wings. Two rose upward from its shoulders, bent back, joined one another, and covered the aforesaid brightness. Two extended downward from those shoulders to the crown of the aforesaid head. Two descended from the loins of the same image to the ankles of its feet, spreading themselves somewhat as if for flight. The rest of the body was entirely covered with scales like those of fish, not feathers of birds.

In the two wings extending to the crown of the aforesaid head appeared five mirrors. One was at the top of the right wing, in which was written, “The Way and the Truth”; one in its middle, bearing the inscription, “I am the door of all God’s mysteries”; and one at its end, containing the inscription, “I am the manifestation of all good things.” At the top of the left wing was one bearing the inscription, “I am the mirror in which the intention of the elect is considered”; and one at the end of that wing was inscribed, “Tell us whether you are he who is to reign among the people of Israel.” This image had turned its back toward the north.

Throughout the entire western region I saw something like utterly foul, smoking darkness. But near the corner of that region facing north, blackest fire, boiling with sulphur and densest darkness, bent and extended almost to the middle of the northern quarter. And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

**That the first of the two images signifies Wisdom, and that the manifold beauty of her appearance signifies every kind of creature which God created in diverse natures and species of things.**

II. “Almighty God, who created all things through Wisdom, reveals His marvelous works by diverse signs; and, being wonderful in His gifts, He distributes them to each creature as He wills. Desiring also to lead man back to the blessedness of heaven, He suitably shows him, in marvelous figures and as He wills, those things which are in heavenly, earthly, and infernal dwellings.

“Therefore, near the northern corner facing east, you see an image whose face and feet radiate with such brightness that the same radiance strikes back upon your sight. For where folly ends and justice arises, the Wisdom of true blessedness is made manifest. Her beginning and end surpass human understanding, because by the same light of foreknowledge through which she beheld the beginning of her work, she also foresaw its end.

[Col. 0985A] “She wears a garment as though of white silk, because, embracing man in the whiteness and sweetness of love, she also displays the Son of God incarnate in the beauty of virginity. How this occurred is unknown to man; divinity alone knows it.

“And she has over it a green tunic, appearing everywhere adorned with diverse pearls, because Wisdom does not reject even the outward creatures—those flying in the air, walking or creeping on the earth, and swimming in the waters—whose spirits perish with their flesh. Rather, she gives them life and preserves them, because they render service to man, who is nourished by them. They themselves also are like ornaments among the pearls of this same Wisdom, since they do not exceed their own nature, as man often does by transgressing the right path appointed for him.

“Thus she bears earrings at her ears, necklaces on her breast, and bracelets on her arms, all seeming to be of most pure gold and adorned with precious stones, because all creatures obey her and remember her commands. Therefore her works are fortified by the comprehensiveness of fullness, so that no creature is so imperfect that it lacks anything in its nature; rather, each possesses within itself the fullness of complete perfection and usefulness. Thus all things which proceeded through Wisdom are in her like most pure and elegant adornment, shining with the most splendid brightness of her essence.

[Col. 0985C] “Moreover, the person who fulfills the precepts of God’s commandments is Wisdom’s white and sweet garment, and her green clothing through good intention and the fresh vigor of works adorned with manifold virtues. The adornment of her ears is shown when such a person turns away from hearing evil whisperings; the protection of her breast, when unlawful desires are neglected; and the honor and strength of her arms, when one is defended from sin. For all these arise from purity of faith, adorned with the most profound holy gifts of the Spirit and the most just writings of teachers, when the faithful person fulfills them through good works.”

[Col. 0985D] **That the second image signifies almighty God; and what the brightness in the place of its head, the human head appearing in the middle of its belly, and its lion-like feet signify.**

III. “But as if in the middle of that same northern region you see another image, standing erect and having a marvelous form. Against the strength and unjust presumption of the ancient serpent, it signifies almighty God, invincible in His majesty and wonderful in His powers, because no one can pursue the depth of His mysteries to their end.

“At its summit, where the place of its head should be, such radiant brightness shines that it strikes back upon your sight, because no one burdened with a mortal body can see the exaltation of divinity which illumines all things. Not even angels, ever standing before His gaze and continually desiring to behold Him, can reach Him to the end. For God is that radiance which neither began to be nor will cease.

[Col. 0986A] “In the middle of its belly there appears a human head with gray hair and a beard, signifying that, in the perfection of God’s works, there was from of old a plan for human salvation, displaying within itself the great dignity of uprightness, which no one can count or comprehend. Just as a man cannot discern the beginning and end of a wheel that has an even circle, so no man can bring to completion that which angels cannot comprehend, because eternity existed before them, equally willing and accomplishing, and had need of nothing, because it was always full.

“Thus the same head has the form of a human head, because God made man in His image and likeness and gave him power to work what is good, to praise his Creator, and not to forget Him. For no one is like God, nor can be; but he who wished to make himself like God was destroyed, because this ought not to have been.

“When God wished powerfully to show His strength, He looked upon the Virgin’s womb; and as on the seventh day He rested from all His work and afterwards appointed man to work, so He caused His Son to rest in the Virgin’s womb, to whom He entrusted all His work.

[Col. 0986C] “For the Holy Spirit touched the Virgin’s flesh with His gentle warmth, without any burning of a man’s carnal motion, as dew gently falls upon grass, so that the flower—that is, the Son of God—might assume the form of man in the flesh of that Virgin. He also endured many offenses with great patience for mankind. In His circumcision He signified that man was to be cleansed through baptism; in His Passion and death, that he was to be redeemed from grievous sins; and in His Ascension, that he was to be joined to the heavenly kingdom. In these ways He will complete the number of the blessed until the dreadful time of judgment.

“The feet of the aforesaid image resemble the feet of a lion, signifying that God conceals His divinity from men while they are mortal, though He shows them many good things in the commandments of the Law and in other creatures. At last, through His Son, He will draw all these things to Himself, as with lions’ feet, and examine them, so that the whole earth will be shaken and the firmament overturned. Then mortal man, coming to his end, will render an account of his works, and will see the immortal Son of God.”

**How the same image appeared clothed about with six wings, and what those wings signify.**

IV. “It also has six wings, which are the works of the six days, in which man praises God by invoking Him and attends to himself with God’s help. Two rise upward from the shoulders, bend back, join one another, and cover the aforesaid brightness. They signify love of God and neighbor; rising upward through the strength of good works, and laying aside severity, they condescend to the needs of their neighbors.

[Col. 0987A] “They also comprehend the mysteries of God’s secrets, because these wings further reveal the heavenly host of spirits above, whom God placed before His face, making them mirrors of His miracles. They behold His face, yet cannot bring Him to an end by any solemnity of praise or any limit.

“By the two wings extending downward from the aforesaid shoulders to the crown of the aforesaid head are signified the Old and New Testaments. They bear the strength of God’s commandments and extend themselves downward toward the ancient counsel: in the Old Testament the prophets foretold the Son of God, whom in the New the children of the Church received through the devotion of faith.

“He also manifests the power of God, which has the ability to create and do what it wills, just as a bird flies with outspread wings into height, breadth, and depth. For God established all heavenly secrets upon a straight path, so that their splendor never ceases and in His truth they never have an end, just as truth has no shadow of falsehood.

“By the two wings descending from the loins of the same image to the ankles of its feet, and spreading themselves a little as if for flight, are shown the present age and the future age. In the present age one generation passes away and another follows; in the future, the stability of unfailing life will come. Near the end of the world this will be revealed, with very many terrors and signs flying before that end as it were.

[Col. 0987C] “Into the loins, the greed of the devil’s throat sends the taste of sins and carnal desires, where food descends and is expelled, and where fleshly concupiscence grows in sins. But divine protection defends them and grants them chastity together with the raising up of good works. For God afterwards restrained the incestuous acts which had arisen in the first humans through the motion of the serpent’s tongue, through one man who, with the mighty wings of virginal nature, shattered in human minds the service of lust contrary to the laws of the flesh.”

[Col. 0987D] **What it signifies that this image appears wholly covered with fish-scales rather than birds’ feathers; that the Son of God entered the world in flesh without the devil’s knowledge; and why the Father willed Him to endure such great sufferings.**

V. “Thus the rest of its body being entirely covered with scales like those of fish, and not feathers of birds, signifies this: just as the form of fish differs from that of birds, and just as it is hidden how fish are born and grow, while the waters in which they live run in swift courses and the fish swiftly flow with them, so the Son of God also was born wholly in holiness. In a different nature—that is, separated from other men—He was wholly holy in justice. In that justice He bore man into heaven upon the outspread wings of all good works, as had often been prefigured in the old Law by the signs of sacrifices, and was afterwards fulfilled through Him in virginal nature.

“For as soon as Adam ate the deadly fruit, he conceived a taste for sins, so that he could sin. Therefore the glory of paradise departed from him and he was sent into exile. Immediately the devil also brought forth lust against God and overturned human procreation with shameful confusion. In his deceit he thought that a human being, so filthy amid such things, could not enter the kingdom of heaven, because the people of fornication could not be God’s people, nor could God be their God.

[Col. 0988A] “The devil rejoiced greatly in the filthiness of fleshly motion and said within himself: ‘I have cast man down from his glorious place and sent him into the greatest filth; therefore God has no share in him, because He is altogether clean and neither wills nor receives any filthiness. Therefore man will remain in my place.’

“But God hid from the ancient serpent how He intended to deliver man. Through His Son He washed away the filth that had boiled up through that serpent’s deceit and erased through Him the wounds that lust had inflicted upon man. God did this in the midst of His power, in which He was before all beginnings, and in the midst of the night of the infernal pit; just as He had signified it in the middle of the night through the smiting angel.

“It was in the midst of His power because He was mighty to do whatever He willed; and in the midst of night because the ancient enemy, in proud opinion, thought that he had captured men as he pleased and possessed so great a multitude of them as though he held them in the middle of his own heart.

[Col. 0988C] “Then, as has been said, the Son of God came secretly, without the devil’s knowledge, and through His humanity broke the devil’s hook by which he caught human beings. Having conquered His enemies, He hung that hook upon the banner of the Cross as a sign of triumph, and displayed it to His Father together with all the host of the heavenly army. Therefore that same army raised a song of new praise, rejoicing that so great a multitude of blessed souls had been delivered from so savage a captivity, because the aforesaid Son of God had placed them in the abode of blessedness.

“And why did almighty God permit His only Son, who owed no debt through sins, to suffer such great passions? Namely, so that the ancient deceiver might have no ground of accusation against God, because man had willingly consented to him and had followed all his commands. For if a sinful man were killed for other men, the evil spirit would say that he could free no one, because he himself would have to answer for his own sins, in which he had consented to the devil. Therefore he would have no power to draw away the rope of captivity either from himself or from others. Hence the living God gave His Son, whose form was like Adam’s form, so that through the garment of His humanity He might redeem man.”

[Col. 0989A] **What the five mirrors appearing in different places in the two middle wings of the same image signify, and how the writing displayed in them is to be understood.**

VI. “And in the two wings which extend themselves toward the crown of the aforesaid head appear five mirrors, because in the Old and New Testaments, which look toward the dignity of the ancient counsel, five luminaries of different times are shown: the first in Abel, the second in Noah, the third in Abraham, the fourth in Moses, and the fifth in the Son of God. All these shine upon men as the way of truth; and the Son of God Himself opened through His Passion the enclosure of heavenly joys.

“One is at the top of the right wing, in which is written: ‘The Way and the Truth.’ This signifies the lofty mysteries of God’s miracles, which no human being can fully comprehend through knowledge, except so far as one grasps them within the circle of faith; just as a shadow in a mirror does nothing beyond what is displayed to it by the form. These mysteries show the peoples the way of justice and the truth of uprightness, so that man, fearing God, may come to heavenly things—as the works and end of Abel also declare.

[Col. 0989B] “And one is in its middle, bearing the inscription: ‘I am the door of all God’s mysteries.’ For in the perfection of saving protection the manifestation of God’s secrets is revealed, showing that almighty God extends Himself through His miracles over the breadth of all creation. From the first man to the last He accomplishes manifold signs of miracles: by prophesying, announcing, and doing. Nor will He cease in these things until He completes all that He will do, just as in the first creation He did not rest before He had wholly completed the creature, as He also prefigured through diverse signs in Noah.

“And one is at its end, in which is contained the inscription: ‘I am the manifestation of all good things.’ For at this end the end of the devil’s mockery is foreshown, and the beginning of all good things prefigured. It also signifies that the Son of God would assume human form from a simple virgin and accomplish every good thing through Himself. This the book of life, which shall never be erased, announces; in it too the heavenly Jerusalem is described with all its virtues, which no one can recount. Nor can anyone bring God’s wonders to their end. Abraham faithfully prefigured all these things in the circumcision which he performed at God’s command.

[Col. 0989D] “And at the top of the left wing is one bearing the inscription: ‘I am the mirror in which the intention of the elect is considered.’ For at the beginning of justice, when heavenly protection was oppressing wickedness through the strength of its elect, their devotion appeared so simple and pure that they resisted diabolical arts and offered themselves to God as a living sacrifice. Therefore Satan, cast backward, knew God to be so strong against His enemies that, terrified even in the depths of hell, he trembled before Him in every way.

“Thus many who slept in the northern region through the deadly fruit awoke in the mirror of the fear of God through repentance: murderers, adulterers, robbers, liars, and all other sinners, beseeching God to deliver them from the ancient enemy. God is greatly praised in their repentance, because all ranks of penitents and faithful persons recognize God as great in His power, since He so delivers them and blots out their sins. Therefore He greatly delights in them: though they had been mortal like night in sins, through repentance He made them like a pure day.

[Col. 0990A] “Thus, having been delivered from the devil in this way, they love Him far more than they would if they had not needed deliverance through repentance; nor afterward will they grow numb in His love. Therefore the fear of God is necessary both for simple and innocent elect persons and for sinners alike, because they must have the fear of God before they taste His love. Hence their intentions appear like writing in the aforesaid mirror, and God always beholds them.

“And one is at the end of the same wing, bearing the inscription: ‘Tell us whether you are he who is to reign among the people of Israel.’ For where the Old Testament ended and the New began, My Only-Begotten appeared. He cast Satan like a stone into the lower pit of hell, so that he can breathe in no gusty blast of his will, as he did before. In this act My same Son showed His elect eternal rewards, as I spoke to Moses, saying:

[Col. 0990C] **Words of God speaking to Moses in Exodus: ‘I will show you every good thing,’ and how they are to be understood concerning the mystery of the Lord’s Incarnation.**
VII. “I will show you all good things, and I will be called by the name of the Lord before you; and I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be gracious to whom it pleases me.” And again he says: “You cannot see my face; for no man shall see me and live.” And again: “Behold,” he says, “there is a place beside me; you shall stand upon the rock. And when my glory passes by, I will place you in a cleft of the rock, and I will protect you with my right hand until I have passed by; then I will remove my hand, and you shall see my back parts” (Exod. XXXIII).

The meaning of this passage is to be understood thus: I, who am the Lord of all, because I exist through myself, will show you, who worship me with a pure heart, the blessedness of eternal life, which is every good thing. And I, the Lord, who am the creator of all creatures, will be called before you when you, Israel, see the garment of my Son, which I promised to Adam when I called him by his name and gave him a dark garment, because he was darkened.

For this reason no human being burdened with human sins can see my countenance so long as he remains mortal, because through the devil’s suggestion he is blackened by the darkness of the north; and just as all bright things are turned away from the north, so the brightness of the true light withdrew from Adam when, by the counsel of the ancient serpent, he looked toward the north. Therefore, because none of mortals could perfectly behold my glory, I showed my miracles by speaking through my prophets, who spoke in shadow—a shadow formed from light, yet darker than its own light, just as every shadow is darker than the substance from which it proceeds.

The sun, moon, and all the stars were likewise obscured to humankind, so that they could not see their naked brightness; and every breath of the winds was veiled from their sight. Therefore it was spoken, as it were, in shadow, as was said above: “Tell us whether you are the one who is to reign over the people Israel.” For the Holy Spirit, prophesying in his people, declared what had been prefigured by the first calling by which Adam was called: that the liberator of humankind would come.

Then the Son of God came clothed in humanity. Human beings could not see the brightness of his divinity when they looked upon him as though he were merely another man. Yet he showed himself to them as living in a way different from that of other people—namely, without any taste of sin—although he ate, drank, slept, and clothed himself, having no stain of wrongdoing. But the Jews and many others, seeing him, doubted that he was the Son of God; thus they obscured their own knowledge and did not receive his wonders in faith. Instead they became hard as stones, as a serpent hides in the hollow of a rock.

Nevertheless, by his right hand he will hold fast very many Jews and pagans, with an innumerable host of those to be saved, until all his wonders have passed by. Then he will lift the hand of his great work and show all his friends his back parts, so that all may know [Col. 0991C] how he fought with the devil. And then, O Israel, you will confidently believe in him, whose miracles you fled—as Adam fled the brightness of eternal life—by not believing in him. Then he will be beneath your tongue like a honeycomb, and like food of milk in the manifestation of his works, which you will gather to yourself and grasp with your arm, saying in a mournful voice: “Ah, ah—how long we have been deceived!” And thus will be fulfilled what was written by my inspiration:

Further words of David from Psalm XCII, where he says: “Wonderful are the liftings up of the sea; wonderful is the Lord on high,” and how this should be understood.

VIII. “Wonderful are the liftings up of the sea; wonderful is the Lord on high.” The meaning of this passage is to be understood thus. God, who is the way and the truth, placed all the adornments of the firmament beneath the hidden mysteries of his right ordering, together with the wonderful liftings up of the sea; and with the wonderful lifting up of the sea he inundated the adornments of the firmament. He placed them in some respect, according to heavenly mysteries, in the likeness of a mirror. But as a shadow in a mirror can do nothing apart from its form, so the adornments of the firmament cannot accomplish anything by themselves except through heavenly secrets.

For the adornments of the firmament shine forth from the highest mysteries, just as radiance proceeds from fire: fire is the material of radiance, and radiance passes away, while fire remains. Thus too the adornments of the firmament pass away, but heavenly harmony endures. Therefore the Lord is wonderful in the heights of heaven [Col. 0992A], because no transient thing can perfectly behold things that will never pass away, since transient things exist in a perfection that fails.

Yet God showed heavenly things to human beings through the ornaments and signs of the firmament, so that in the mirror of faith they might recognize his wonders through them. If they could not see those adornments, their knowledge would be blind. Thus too the north, deprived of all light, never shone after the devil’s fall; because he mocked the honor of the Most High, he retained no light. The wonderful liftings up of the sea also occur when people, who surge about in instability here and there, set aflame by the Holy Spirit, lift themselves from earthly things to heavenly ones. And thus the Lord is wonderful in the lofty virtues, when he strengthens them toward every good thing so that thereafter they refuse to submit themselves to the filth of vices. Hence Scripture also says:

Further words of the same writer from the same Psalm, where he says: “For he has established the circle of the earth, which shall not be moved.”

IX. “For he has established the circle of the earth, which shall not be moved.” The meaning of this passage is to be understood thus: God filled the circle of the earth with a complete work, and therefore it shall not be moved; for if it were not filled with creatures, it would be shaken and moved by a certain emptiness. Every creature fills its own place, which bears it by serving it. But God works his wonders in humankind and entrusted the circle of the earth to humanity for the need of the body.

He also established the Church, spread throughout the whole circle of the earth [Col. 0992C], which no storm of opponents will destroy, although it is often wearied by very many tribulations. For God continually accomplishes his wonders within it, and he will not cease until the number of his elect is completed together with the heavenly harmony. But the countenance of Divinity is above this harmony. Harmony itself cannot be bounded by any end, nor can it do anything of itself, but only through the manifestation of the countenance of Divinity—just as a shadow appearing in a mirror does nothing by itself, but through the form from which it proceeds.

Those who behold God are called heavens; those who prophesy him are also heavens; and that in which the Son of God showed himself in humanity was likewise heaven. Those are called heavens who shine from the splendor of God’s countenance as sparks shine from fire, and in whom God overcame all his enemies. But when God created heaven and earth, he placed humankind between them, so that humanity might rule over them. This middle corresponds to that middle in which the Son of God is in the midst of the Father’s heart; for as counsel proceeds from the human heart, so the Son proceeded from God the Father. For the heart possesses counsel, and counsel is in the heart; and they are one, nor can any division be there.

That the fact that the aforesaid image had turned its back toward the north signifies that God concealed from the devil and all evil spirits the counsel of the incarnation of his Son and of human redemption.

X. And this image had turned its back toward the north [Col. 0993A], because almighty God concealed from all the friends of the north what he wished to do with his Son. And just as he cast them backward so that they might see no light, so they saw the work of the Son of God in no knowledge; and because God had ordered all these things by an ancient counsel, they were hidden from them.

For by the force of God’s zeal the devil was plunged into the abyss, and every light was taken from him, so that he now sees no gleam of blessedness, because he is utterly blinded. For he desired to possess the likeness of him who is from no one, but exists through himself. And although he now feels God’s judgments in a useless fear and answers to them—namely, those judgments that punish what belongs to him—yet in fear of God’s judgments he knows that he cannot resist God at all. But nevertheless he cuts off the branches of God’s work, as he did in the first human beings, seducing those who consent to him from their whole heart. Therefore they too go to destruction, in which this same enemy always roars in order to devour souls and never ceases from this fury through any weariness.

But God shows human beings his hidden divinity through great proclamations and many signs, and through wisdom reveals many things to them in creatures, by which they may know the secrets of his divinity, just as a human being paints many forms with colors through skill. And just as the ancient serpent could not resist God in his fall, so he could not prevent God from restoring, through his Son and with the souls of the righteous, the heavenly choir from which they fell, in greater praise. They will not be able fully to know the work of this Son of God before the last day; and then they will suffer great confusion before the heavenly host, because their place will be filled with a greater blessing than it had previously possessed.

For, as stated above, the Son of God went forth more beautiful than others upon an alien way, being the offspring of virginal nature; for the first virgin was corrupted by the serpent’s counsel. But the Virgin Mary was wholly holy: she conceived the Son by the Holy Spirit, gave birth as a virgin, and remained a virgin. This birth had been predestined by the ancient counsel and lay hidden wholly spiritually in divinity; it did not fly into human knowledge, because it was not manifold but one in divinity, where the same Son of God was begotten of the Father before the antiquity of days, since the Father always held in his will that he should become human.

Coming in the alien nature of humanity, he overthrew the left side of Leviathan when, through works of chastity, he drew a thousand sinful vices from its throat. For abstinence and contrition for sins are the wings of chastity, on which virgins and penitents, because their sins of carnal desires have been forgiven, fly to the espousal of the Lamb. For the Son of God, the Son of the Virgin, crowned with virginity, received penitents who ran to him.

From the beginning of the garment of his humanity, he worked in humankind all spiritual things, which he will also accomplish until the last day. These are in the midst of his power—not by the number of days, but by the force of his work—and he holds them in a just balance, so that he cannot be overcome by any deception. For in his humanity he flew upon the wings of the winds; and as an eagle looks into the sun, so he looked upon the face of the Father. For just as Abraham received circumcision of the flesh, by which spiritual life, signified by water, is understood—as fish live in water—so the human soul is circumcised through baptism and is spiritually reborn to life in water, in which it will live eternally in the seat of blessedness, as is also said concerning the throne of God’s majesty.

Words of David from Psalm CI, where it is written: “The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven,” with the sense in which these words are to be understood; and a brief recapitulation of the Lord’s incarnation.

[Col. 0994B] XI. “The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, and his kingdom shall rule over all.” The meaning of this passage is to be understood thus: The Son of God, who is Lord of human beings, Lord of angels, and Lord of all powers, prepared his throne in the heaven of blessedness, just as a human being’s thought works the instrument of his work according to his desire. And as he accomplishes every work according to his will, so this same Son did not depart from his Father in that matter, as Adam did when he fell into the pit of death.

Therefore his kingdom will rule over all, namely in heaven and on earth, where he will trample his enemies underfoot as the footstool of his feet. For his flesh was never touched on earth by the taste of sin, and thus no pain overcame him; but through harsh and bitter suffering he overcame all earthly things. Who, moreover, was fitting to free humankind except the fiery Son of God, who descended from heaven to earth and ascended from earth to heaven, and who distils heavenly grace upon his people by the dew of divinity, like a drop of honey, so that the faithful may never be overcome by one another?

For the Father accomplished every good work in his Son, which could not be done in anyone else, because he, as said above, never departed from the Father, just as the brightness of the sun is not separated from the sun. Therefore he came to earth for the liberation of humankind and redeemed humanity, whom no one else could redeem, because the Father had ordained that he should come thus, as the prophet David, inspired by the Holy Spirit, says:

Further words of the same writer from Psalm LXXI, where it is read: “He descends like rain upon fleece,” and that this too should be referred to the Lord’s incarnation.

XII. “He will descend like rain upon fleece, and like droplets falling upon the earth.” The meaning of this passage is to be understood thus: Adam became mortal through the devil’s counsel, by transgressing God’s commands. Therefore the Son of God descended, like the dew of sweetness, into the womb of the Virgin, who was sweet, gentle, and humble in her conduct like a sheep, so that he might raise humankind from death—just as, when the earth is overturned by the plough, fruit is raised by rain.

[Col. 0995A] For the plough is the commandment of the law, which this same Son of God gave to human beings in his humanity, so that through knowledge of this commandment they might be raised to life; and so that, according to his example, they might overturn carnal desires within themselves as with a plough, and thus become fruitful through examples of holy works, advancing day by day as he himself had gone before them. In this way he sent droplets upon them and made of them a field full of virtues, which he blessed and filled with the fruits of every good thing: chastity, continence, patience, and the other beatitudes.

That the darkness seen in the western region, and likewise the fire with sulphur and other denser darkness displayed in the northern part of the aforesaid building, signify the penal places in the outer world where the souls of sinners are tortured, and also signify the inward blindness of those same sinners, by which they are darkened through unbelief.

XIII. Across the whole western region you see, as it were, most dreadful smoking darkness, because there are penal places there, containing various kinds of torments. For when a person descends through the slopes of sins toward the setting, he draws to himself the blindness of unbelief, emitting an evil vapor through wickedness; and thus, falling into the punishments of that darkness, he casts himself into confusion when he neglects his Creator.

But near the corner of that same region which faces north, exceedingly black fire, boiling with sulphur and the densest darkness, curves and extends almost to the middle of the northern side [Col. 0995C], because that same place is the penal deep and the lake of destruction for the souls of those who, despising God, refused to know him through good works. Therefore sharp fire, with the bitterness of sulphur and inextricable darkness, steams there and spreads itself to its appointed places, so that human knowledge cannot perfectly know the diversity of those punishments so long as a person lives in the mortal world.

Likewise, when a person reaches the setting of unbelief, which looks toward destruction, so that he loves neither righteous works nor God, the fire of perversity, meeting him with bitterness and blindness of character, brings him to the fullness of misery and submersion, so that, having no hope of life, destruction draws him wholly into itself. For the person who follows folly and abominates the wisdom through which God created all things condemns himself: having no restraint in evils, he thinks nothing of the life to come, neither desires to know whether there is another life, nor keenly considers how changeable he is.

A person can comprehend his infancy and childhood, youth and mature age; but what becomes of him in old age, or how he will be changed, he cannot comprehend at all. Through the rationality of his soul he knows that he has a beginning; but how it is that the soul does not die and has no end, he cannot know or comprehend at all.

[Col. 0996A] That God made all things through wisdom in order to confute the devil’s malice; that, though invisible to humanity, he might be understood through faith and known through his work; and that he had within himself before time the ordering of his whole work, which he created in time—also establishing humankind after his own pattern, so that one might first arrange in thought within oneself whatever one would afterward carry out in action.

XIV. Therefore God established the firmament through wisdom and fastened it with the powers of the stars as with nails, just as a person secures a house with nails lest it fall. The stars also attend the moon, which is kindled from the sun and, in its waning, distils light upon the stars. Wisdom, indeed, in its ancient counsel made the moon fruitful for humankind together with the sun, when it pours in the moisture of earth; for humankind is every creature. But the sun signifies divinity, while the moon signifies the innumerable multitude of the human race; and all these are ornaments of wisdom.

The firmament is also the seat of all its adornments, just as a person has a seat, namely the earth, which supports him. God set it with its ornament for his own praise, as wisdom had preordained. Therefore creation was, as it were, a garment for wisdom, because wisdom touched its work just as a person feels his own garment. But if a person had been created so as to be able to lack garments, he would then have had no need of work and would have been honored by no service, except that the body alone would be the covering of the soul and would be moved through the soul.

God too cannot be seen, but is known through creation, just as the human body cannot be seen because of garments [Col. 0996C]. And as the inward brightness of the sun is not perceived, so God is not seen by a mortal creature, but is understood through faith, just as the sun’s outer circle is looked upon by watchful eyes. Every work that wisdom established, it established against the devil’s malice, because he always hated and hates all its work, until the end of the full number, when, struck by him with such great strength, he will perish and will no longer attempt to wage war against God.

Every ordering of wisdom is sweet and gentle, because when it has been splashed with filth, wisdom washes its garment in the blood of the merciful Lamb. Therefore it is to be loved above all the adornments of creatures and appears lovely to all holy souls, because they will never grow weary in the embrace of its gaze.

As wisdom also ordained, the spirit lives and is awake in a human being and will by no means come to an end. So long as a person lives in the body, thoughts multiply in him beyond number, just as the sound of praise in angels is innumerable. Thought also lives in a person’s youth; he sends it forth by the word of rationality and works through it, but that work by no means lives in itself, because it had a beginning. But eternity lives in itself and has never appeared in diminution, because before time it was eternally life.

When the soul is changed into immortality, it is afterward no longer called soul, because then it accomplishes nothing with the human being through thoughts; but thereafter it is among the praises of the angels, who are spirits. Therefore it too will then be called spirit, because it will no longer labor with the body of flesh. A human being is rightly called life because, while living through breath, he is life; and when changed through the death of the flesh into immortality, he will be in life. After the last day, with body and soul, he is life in eternity, because when God formed humanity, he enclosed his hidden mysteries within humanity: humanity was made in God’s likeness by knowing, thinking, and working.

For Divinity had within itself the ordering of all its work—how it ought to be made—and according to this established humanity able to think, so that one might first dictate all one’s works in one’s heart before doing them; for humanity is the enclosure of God’s wonders. God orders, humanity thinks, and the angel possesses knowledge [Col. 0998A], in which it always resounds with the voice of praise and love for God’s honor, desiring nothing except to behold God and praise him.

Before time God held within himself, without any cessation, the work that he was going to do. Thus humanity, which is the enclosure of his miracles, knows him with the eye of faith and embraces him with the kiss of knowledge, though it cannot see him with bodily eyes, and acts in accordance with him. The angel also offers God the chosen works of humanity with a sweet odor, which the human being sends upward through good will; and the angel likewise shows the just Judge worthless works that look more toward another path than toward God. Let the faithful receive these words with the devotion of the heart, for they have been set forth for the profit of believers through him who is first and last.

## TENTH VISION

[Col. 0997]

[Col. 0997B] The final vision, in which a wheel of great size is shown and carefully described as to its appearance; and the image of Charity is again seen under another form.

I. Then, beside the mountain which, as stated above, I saw as though in the middle of the eastern region, I saw something like a wheel of marvellous size, having the appearance of a white cloud and turned toward the east. Across its middle—that is, from its left side to its right side—it was divided by a line of dark color, like a human breath. Thus the half of the same wheel that was above this line was further marked by another line, glowing like dawn, descending from the summit of the wheel to the middle of the aforesaid line.

The upper half of this wheel, from its left side to its middle, gave forth, as it were, a green color; from its right side to its middle, a red color shone, so that these two colors were divided between themselves by an equal measure of space. But the half of the same wheel below the aforesaid transverse line showed a pale color mingled with a certain blackness.

And behold, in the middle of that wheel, on the aforesaid line, I again saw sitting the image previously named to me as Charity, though she now appeared in an adornment different from that in which I had seen her before. For her face shone like the sun; her tunic gleamed like purple; she wore around her neck a golden necklace adorned with precious stones; and she was clothed in shoes emitting the brightness of lightning.

Before the face of this same image there also appeared something like a tablet, transparent as crystal, on which was written: “I will reveal a beautiful form of silvery color, because divinity, which lacks a beginning, possesses great brightness; but everything that has a beginning is uncertain amid terrors and cannot comprehend God’s secrets in full knowledge.” This image looked upon the aforesaid tablet. Therefore the line on which she sat moved; and at once, where that line of the aforesaid wheel seemed joined to its left side, the outer part of the wheel became for a short distance somewhat watery; then, somewhat beyond the middle of the half of the wheel below the aforesaid transverse line, it became reddish; afterward pure and bright; and finally, near the end of that half, where the aforesaid line was fastened to the wheel, it became like a troubled and stormy tempest. And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me:

That God could not truly be called one if he had one like himself by nature; that the aforesaid character of the wheel shows God himself, lacking beginning and end, prepared for every good; and how the whole description of the same wheel pertains to eternity or God’s power, or to the salvation of souls.

II. O human being, hear and understand the words of him who was and who is without the office of changing times, because within him was the ancient counsel by which he willed to make diverse works. He saw these, before the antiquity of days, as though a ray of the sun, because they were to be. For God is one, and nothing can compare itself with this unity. Yet he foreknew that a work which he was to make would attempt to arrogate to itself the likeness of this unity. Therefore he set before it the obstacle of repulsion, because he is that unity which has no likeness to itself; otherwise it could not be called unity. Thus he casts away from himself one who perversely desires this likeness.

So every rational soul in a human being, which exists from him who is the true God, may choose what pleases it and reject what displeases it, because it knows what is good or harmful for itself. But although God is one, he nevertheless foreknew in the power of his heart a work that he multiplied magnificently. God himself is the living fire through whom souls breathe; he existed before the beginning and is also the beginning and the time of times. The present vision makes all this manifest.

For beside the mountain which, as stated above, you see as though in the middle of the eastern region, you see something like a wheel of marvellous size, having the appearance of a white cloud and turned toward the east. It shows God as without beginning and end, gentle in his works, and prepared for every good. It is divided across the middle, from its left side to its right side, by a dark-colored line like human breath, because the will of God is perfectly apparent through the beginning of the passing world and through its end tending toward eternity, when he separated temporal things from those that are eternal.

Thus another line, glowing like dawn, descends from the summit of the wheel to the middle of the aforesaid line, marking the half of the wheel above that line. By this is shown that the divine ordering—directed toward every good, appearing wonderfully before the beginning of the world, after its end, and within the times of the world, as by an unfailing brightness—manifests that the fullness of God’s perfection, which exceeds temporal things through his will in heavenly things, is prepared for all righteousness.

Therefore the upper half of that wheel gives forth, from its left side to its middle, something like a green color, because when God was about to bring creatures forth into their forms for labor, as they had been foreknown by him, he held them, as it were, in the greenness of his will. From its right side to its middle a red color shines, because after the world’s end God will change for the better those things that pass from the transient age into life; and, rendering to the souls of the faithful the reward of their shining labors, will permit neither labor nor failure ever again to rule over them. “Thus these two colors are divided between themselves by an equal measure of space,” because just as eternity before the beginning of the world lacks a beginning, so likewise, once the world has ended, it lacks an end; but the beginning and end of the world are enclosed, as it were, by one circle of comprehension.

“The half of the same wheel which is drawn beneath the aforesaid transverse line shows a pale color mixed with a certain blackness,” because it signifies the passing times of worldly things, which have beginning and end, over which unceasing eternity, bounded by no end, rules; and which, while the world endures, often grievously bear now the pallor of distress, now the blackness of tribulations.

But all these things described above also refer in another way to the salvation of human souls, so that the power of God is joined to the highest strength, which consists in the perfection of shining righteousness; for God’s power and strength cleave to one another. God’s power is round in the equality of moderation, because it lacks beginning and end and, in broad possibility, can do all that it wills. It shines white in the gentleness of heavenly judgments, because no change, no alternation of increase or decrease, touches God; no time ever divides him. Rather, always without beginning, unharmed and unchangeable, he remains, granting life to all things that exist and gathering those who worship him in purity to the highest blessedness.

The fullness of his power, ordering all things in just moderation and unknown to human beings in its height and depth, shows eternal and temporal things as though in a circle having neither beginning nor end. Thus the perfection of God’s power, which manifests the eternity of the divine ordering, and his providence shining in eternal things, extending from the eternity of that power to the fullness of divine ordering, reveals itself in its works and declares that the souls of the blessed will remain in heavenly glory.

The eternity of the perfection of God’s power, in dispositions that were yet to come, shows the fullness of creatures as the greenness of a germ that will come and proceed, when heaven and earth did not yet exist; just as the gifts of the Holy Spirit bring greenness to the human heart so that it may bear good fruit. But in those things which will attain the end of the world and the stability of immutability, it shows a glowing brightness, because then all things will be perfect and will no longer suffer any defect, with the souls of the saints lifted up to heavenly things. Thus, just as God’s eternity had no beginning before the beginning of the world, so after its end it will be bounded by no limit, where the blessed will then rejoice without end in heaven.

Moreover, the perfection of God’s power, enclosing beneath eternity all temporal things that possess diverse modes, shows that all things are subject to God and declares that those who neglect God are sent to infernal places, because all things that appear to resist God will be examined.

Why the virtue Charity is seen adorned in this vision differently from the preceding one.

III. That you again see, in the middle of the same wheel, seated upon the aforesaid line, the image previously named Charity to you, though now appearing in an adornment different from that in which you had seen her, means this: in that perfection by which God’s power subjects all things to itself, Charity is joined to the will of God as though at rest, because Charity fulfills every will of God. She is adorned now with this, now with that ornament, because the virtues at work in human beings show Charity as adorned with a certain beauty, since every good thing is done through Charity.

For her face shines like the sun, admonishing a person to fix every intention of the heart upon the true sun. Her tunic shines like purple, so that a person, making for oneself a garment from the bowels of mercy, may help each petitioner as far as possible. She has a golden necklace adorned with precious stones around her neck, signifying that a person, taking upon oneself the yoke of submission, should adorn it with blessed virtues, so that, humbled in all things, one may show oneself truly subject to God, just as the Son of God obeyed his Father in all things unto the death of the flesh. She is clothed also in shoes giving forth the brightness of lightning, so that all a person’s paths may be in the light of truth and so that, following Christ’s footsteps, one may faithfully offer others examples of uprightness.

Concerning the tablet transparent as crystal which appears before the image of Charity; what it signifies that, as this image looks upon the tablet, the line of her seat moves; and a brief repetition concerning the creation of heaven, earth, angels, and humankind.

IV. But before the face of this same image there also appears something like a tablet, transparent as crystal, bearing the inscription that the Godhead which lacks a beginning, with nothing subject to it as a beginning, can comprehend all things fully. For before the gaze of Charity the foreknowledge of God is displayed, [Col. 1001B] because Charity and the foreknowledge of God agree as one. For foreknowledge, transparent without any obscurity, bounded neither by beginning nor by end, nor delimited by mortal creature, shows that the person who wishes to be subject to Charity, who loves the things that are in God and beholds God in purity of faith, proposing to Him nothing perishable, establishes a dwelling for himself in the higher joys, because God foresaw that he would come there.

And this image looks upon the aforesaid tablet; hence also the line on which it sits is moved. For when the charity of God beheld His foreknowledge—in which all things that would come to be in creatures appeared, although the creatures to be created did not yet exist—the will of God, to which Charity was joined as if in repose, moved itself [Col. 1001C] to form creatures; and so heaven and earth, and the other creatures that are in them, arose at God's command. For when the angels came first, some of them, neglecting their Creator, fell irrevocably, while others remained steadfast in His service and love.

Therefore, after the other creatures God created humankind, so that it might find prepared for itself all things it needed. He illuminated it with the breath of life and fortified this wonderfully made being in two ways: namely, that it might be fire and flame—fire indeed in the soul, and flame, blazing from it, in rationality. The flame of rationality knows where it acts with the kiss of choice, which is the knowledge of good and evil. By this it does not burn in a person in respect of that which it does not choose for its work, but flees with reluctance from what it does not wish to do, unless the craftsman strikes it so that it may burn a little there where he himself wishes to bend it; and where it sometimes burns by choice, there the craftsman often causes it to cease.

God placed these two powers in an earthen vessel, so that it might perform what was useful to itself. And just as fire contains flame within itself, so the rational human being has powers for action; and these two aforesaid powers are in the earthen vessel, and that earthen vessel itself exists with them. But if fire and flame burned in no thing, where could their heat be seen? Therefore the aforesaid powers must have a work, namely the earthen vessel, in which soul and rationality exercise their works. Wind too is more forceful [Col. 1002A] and fills the remaining creatures with which human beings work, so that humanity itself would not exist if the other creatures did not exist.

And God is fire and living spirit; and He made a great work, from which His Son took a garment. By it, concealing His divinity, He performed very many miracles; and with it He passed through the world until He drew to Himself the tenth number which had been lost. God also established this same work against him who desired the north, and through it utterly overcame him, striking him so upon the jaw that he can no longer raise his head as he formerly did.

For the Godhead clothed the good angels in its brightness and ordered them about itself, so that it might restrain by the chastening of its zeal the work which looked to itself and, following its own will, departed from its Creator; [Col. 1002B] because rationality, when it acts according to the will of the flesh, draws God's vengeance upon itself. But that which looks to its Creator, saying, “You are my God,” the fire of the Holy Spirit kindles to multiply its praises, just as sparks of fire are multiplied.

Moreover, rationality consists in two parts of choice: what it chooses it gathers to itself, and the other it rejects. For in one choice it cannot have two things that are opposed to one another. Whoever serves another despises himself; and whoever works for himself does not, through what he does, serve another; therefore these do not agree as one. The rational human being first chooses and desires, [Col. 1002C] and afterwards acts accordingly in some matter. But an irrational animal lives as it has been constituted and can do no more, because it does not possess the eye of knowledge in rationality; rather, it turns itself toward the material of its own nature. But the human being dwells with God through faith.

### On God's vengeance upon transgressors of the natural law through the waters of the Flood, and on the differing condition of the times from the beginning until the Lord's Incarnation

V. But what you see—namely, that immediately where this same line appears joined to the aforesaid wheel on its left side, the outer part of that wheel becomes somewhat watery for a short distance—means this: after My will had been joined to My power for the procreation of creatures and had brought forth creatures, the judgments of this same power of Mine appeared in the outpouring of the waters [Col. 1002D] in the Flood. For when the first man begot children, their descendants plunged themselves from evil into evil. Adam indeed and his children rightly propagated according to human nature because of fear of Me; but their descendants most wickedly violated themselves against human nature. Since I was unwilling to endure this any longer, I drowned them in the Flood.

Therefore the devil, terrified, trembled, because he saw as invincible My strength by which humankind had thus been destroyed. And then, somewhat beyond the middle of the middle of that same wheel, which is drawn crosswise beneath the aforesaid line, it is reddish and afterwards becomes pure and bright. For from the Flood until the Incarnation of My Son—whom, when the strength of the ages had passed, I sent powerfully at their end in the silence [Col. 1003A] of My will—the judgments of My power passed into the redness of justice. For after the Flood too, through the various ages of days, people took up the brightness of My fear in their deeds.

For the structure of justice arose in Noah; circumcision in Abraham; the giving of the Law in Moses; and prophecy in the prophets. All these restrained idolatry, as day drives away night; within them all times run their course, just as human works appear in human beings. But when all these were tending toward their setting, as when the sun sets, and while the people thus advanced by generation, I beheld the fullness of that number of which it is written by My inspiration:

### The words of Paul on the fullness of time, in which God sent His Son, made of a woman; who in His coming fulfilled and brought to completion the mystical sayings and deeds of the ancients, and who, enlightening the world through His teaching and through the preaching of the apostles or teachers of the Church, changed all things for the better

VI. “When the fullness of time had come, God sent His Son, made of a woman, made under the law, so that He might redeem those who were under the law, in order that we might receive adoption as sons” (Gal. IV).

The meaning of this statement is to be understood as follows. God the Father, who lacks beginning and end, in the fullness of time eternally foreordained, sent His Son to earth for the redemption of fallen humanity, prefigured by very many signs and miracles. This seems aptly intimated to us by Noah’s ark. [Col. 1003C] For it signifies the Church, tossed in the present age by the assaults of varied temptations, which He has now joined to His Son for the restoration of its children through the grace of faith.

This ark, set upon the summit of the mountains, may also signify the eternity of almighty God, who long beforehand foresaw all creatures before they came to be, such as they now distinctly appear, each in its kind, through His word. That heavenly city too, which is the dwelling-place of God's children, presents a tower built with most elegant workmanship; by its most beautiful ornament the supremely faithful obedience of Abraham is signified, and God's Son and the countless tokens of His miracles are set before us.

For the Law given through Moses required unwearied obedience, without which it could in no way stand: just as [Col. 1003D] a house cannot stand without columns to support it, nor a person without the heart by which he is governed. Obedience is a kind of fire, and the Law is its brightness. And as Abraham, leaving his home and native land at the Lord’s command, was first transformed by circumcision, so the Son of God, conceived and born by the fire of the Holy Spirit from the most inviolate Virgin, without any taint of blood, spiritually transformed through Himself the Law given through Moses into a better state.

Those begotten from the blood of sinners, whom the blood of legal sacrifices could not free, it befitted the mercy of their Creator that He alone should free at the inestimable price of His own blood. And just as a human being customarily offers God a sacrifice from the creature granted to him, so the Son of God clothed Himself in flesh taken from humanity, in order to offer it to God the Father on humanity’s behalf.

Thus the Son of God, coming into the world, set pure and bright teaching before human beings; and, illuminating all the things aforesaid, changed them into another form, so that idols were turned toward the living God and prophecy into a spiritual way. For just as a human word is uttered in the breath of its spirit, so God's Only-Begotten was sent from the Father into the chamber of the Virgin and conceived of the Holy Spirit. And so, having assumed flesh and been born from that same Virgin, He made manifest through Himself all things past and future, and changed into better things all human acts recounted and heard of: destroying what was useless and preserving what was useful. Thus [Col. 1004B] He acted in the host of good angels, whom after the fall of the lost He glorified still more.

For before His birth all things were as if in darkness; after He assumed flesh, He illuminated them like the sun. For He Himself was the Law, fulfilling it and transforming it into what was better, and obeying the commands of His Father—which Adam had neglected to do. In this same Son of God justice and peace are joined. Justice, through which the world, darkened in sins by the serpent’s foam, is subdued through His humanity; for He, as a warrior, resists injustice with justice and peace: with justice surrounded by divine commands, and with peace fortified by the grace of God sparing humanity. And He gathered His elect to Himself in that likeness in which the blessed angels remained steadfast with God.

When He ascended bodily into heaven, the Holy Spirit kindled them with fiery tongues, so that they were illuminated in inward knowledge and might thus join others to themselves, so that they too would perform very many miracles and signs, adorned with the catholic faith and sanctified by good works. [Col. 1004C] Thus the teaching of the Son of God, bearing much fruit and ascending from virtue to virtue, proceeded in purity; and a very great people, shining in the light of faith, submitted itself to Him. Thus many who had been darkened in Adam’s fall through forgetfulness and unbelief were enlightened with true faith and most holy works.

And it was necessary that the Son of God should come at the end of the ages, because the ancient serpent had violated the whole human being by deception, mockery, and blasphemy. [Col. 1004D] But it was also necessary that the presence of the humanity of the body of this same Only-Begotten of God should perform its work, which it began to perform through the highest rulers governing the Church, through other prelates of that same Church, then through their priests and subjects, through hermits who maintain the virginal order, through the host of spiritual persons who are in the order of angels and who worship God in the trumpet of praise according to angelic praise, through penitents who cry to Him through imitators of God, through good married persons obedient to the commands of their teachers, and through the continent, who reject themselves and leave the world.

For the Son of God thus worked from royal seats; and as, in the presence of His body, [Col. 1005A] He returned to His Father and showed Himself to Him, so, gathering the upright works of all these, He showed them to His Father. These aforesaid orders, established through the teaching of the Son of God, burned with great zeal as they ascended from virtue to virtue, just as the day burns more fiercely through the heat of the sun from the first hour to the ninth.

### That these times decline from the original strength of apostolic discipline into a kind of feminine weakness, and that all things deteriorate, both in the disturbance of the elements and in the corruption of morals

VII. Afterwards, through the teaching of the apostles and the virtues of the other saints, they became pure and bright until these days, which have descended from their strength into a kind of feminine [Col. 1005B] weakness. For then every good custom which had first been planted in human beings through the grace of the Holy Spirit from apostolic times onward was led into the darkness of the darts by which the ancient serpent deceived the world.

For the apostles had strengthened their teaching as though with steel, enclosed it with the enclosure of heaven, and imposed upon it the reins of the fear of God, lest it be brought into mockery; rather, that it might be maintained in daily vigor. And because they ordered their teaching according to the course of the sun, they sanctified it by abstinence from foods and by praise and prayer.

But the ancient serpent, searching within himself, inquired how he might destroy and extinguish this law, because he saw himself wholly deceived; and because through the fact that he had turned human conception into sin, he knew that he had a time for warfare against the children of humankind. [Col. 1005C] Hence he inflamed a certain judge of royal name with the burning lust of transgression, so that he summoned to himself many abominable vanities as if he worshipped them. He continued thus until the hand of the Lord struck him, just as it crushed Nero and other tyrants in all their honor.

Then the greenness of the virtues dried up, all justice declined into failure, and therefore the greenness of the earth declined in all its growth. For the upper air was changed into a different condition from that in which it had formerly been constituted, so that summer afterwards often had an unnatural cold, and winter an unnatural heat; [Col. 1005D] and there were many times such drought and such moisture, together with certain other preceding signs which the Son of God, when His disciples asked, foretold would come upon the earth before the day of judgment, that many said the day of judgment was imminent.

### Certain hidden words of the Son, interceding with the Father on account of the affliction which He endures in His body, which is the Church, from certain members abandoning justice; and on account of the completion of the number of the elect eternally ordained; and how these words are to be understood according to the differing conditions of times from the beginning of the world to the present

VIII. Therefore the Son speaks to the Father, saying: “In the beginning all creatures were green; in the middle [Col. 1006A] flowers bloomed; afterwards the greenness declined.” And the warrior saw this and said: “I know this time. But the golden number is not yet full. Therefore look upon the paternal mirror. I endure weariness in my body; my little ones also fail. Now remember that the fullness which was made at the beginning ought not to have dried up. And then You had within Yourself that Your eye would never yield, until You saw my body full of gems.
