For it wearies me that all my members go into derision. Father, look: I show You my wounds. Therefore now, all people, bend your knees to your Father, that He may stretch out His hand to you.”

The meaning of this statement is to be understood as follows. In the beginning, namely before the Flood, [Col. 1006B] the earth’s greenness was so great that it produced its fruits without human labor. At that time human beings, possessing neither worldly discipline nor devotion to God in perfection, labored only for earthly things and their pleasures.

But after the Flood, as if in the middle of time—that is, the middle between the Flood and the coming of the Son of God into the world—flowers, with new sap and every kind of shoot, blossomed differently than they had before, because the earth was then ripened by the moisture of the waters and the heat of the sun. And as the flowers of fruits then sprang up more abundantly than before, so human knowledge, kindled in wisdom by the Holy Spirit, advanced until the new star that showed the King of kings. Thus wisdom burned from the fire of the Holy Spirit, [Col. 1006C] through whom the Word of God was made flesh in the Virgin’s womb. This the aforesaid star also showed, in which the Holy Spirit revealed to the nations the work that He had accomplished in the Virgin’s womb. And the brightness of the flame of the Holy Spirit is the sound of the Word, which created all things.

For the Holy Spirit made the Virgin’s womb fruitful, came upon the disciples of the Son of God in fiery tongues, and, after those same fiery tongues, worked many miracles with those same disciples and their followers. Therefore this same age, ascending from virtue to virtue, was called the masculine age, and so it endured for many years in vigorous healing.

Afterwards the greenness declined from its strength and was changed into feminine [Col. 1006D] weakness, setting aside all justice and submitting itself to the foolishness of human morals, because in these days every person does what pleases himself. Thus the Church is desolate among them, like a widow deprived of the consolation of her husband’s care; it has no straight staff of governance upon which people may lean.

But perverse hirelings, because of avarice for money, cast My little ones down into valleys and prevent them from ascending to hills and mountains. They take from them nobility, inheritance, estates, and riches. They act like rapacious wolves that lie in wait for the tracks of sheep: the sheep they seize they tear to pieces, and those they cannot tear to pieces they drive away. By deceitful deception they devour My little ones through greater judges [Col. 1007A] and unjust tyrants.

Therefore these days are a prison of devilish artifice, because for a long time I endured My people’s being mocked through the tyranny of enemies. For the ropes were loosened for them so that they might afflict human beings with diverse punishments, just as I often chastised those rebellious against Me in the Old Testament. I also permitted certain airy spirits, in a great storm, to terrify some people in these same days; and thus I struck them and afflicted them with very many plagues of punishment and with great weakness and bodily infirmity, because they do not cease from their restless ways.

They place envy and hatred in their bosom, reckoning the losses of others as gain to themselves; they strip others of the cloak of honorableness and usefulness and clothe them in every wickedness and bloodshed. [Col. 1007B] Yet they are often judged through the creation which I made for human use: they are suffocated by fire and water; by wind and air the fruits of the earth are taken from them; and sun and moon appear to them out of season, because they do not complete their courses as they were established by God but exceed them. Thus the earth sometimes moves, like a chariot thrown apart by some impact.

In this way these days will complete their course in the foul morals of human beings, by shedding blood, destroying every honorable constitution of the Church, polluting golden justice with the brass and lead of iniquity, and weighing every human will in the diversity of wickedness. But before the end of these days [Col. 1007C] of feminine weakness, justice—which the Son of God entrusted to His disciples with the ring of betrothal when He sent them into all the earth—will rise and display its garments, received from the apostles, polluted and torn through the iniquity of the peoples.

### A mystical description of how the apostles adorned with manifold garments of glory the justice received from the Lord for preaching throughout the world, according both to the diversity of their natural dispositions and to the distribution of graces poured into them from heaven; and on the excellence of the teaching of the Apostle Paul, and why he was raised by the sublimity of revelations and depressed by the burden of weakness

[Col. 1007D] IX. For Matthew, gentle in his disposition and not possessing a profound intellect, taught people mildly and softly. Confirming indeed the teaching of the apostles, he set it before his own teaching as a mistress. Thus he converted a great multitude to God in the true faith by preaching that dripped sweetly like a honeycomb. Because of the sweetness of his character, the peoples licked up his teaching as an infant sucks milk; and therefore the Holy Spirit touched him, so that he faithfully wrote of the Incarnation of the Son of God.

He prepared from the silk of devout intention a shirt—that is, well-ordered contrition—bright as the light of day; and with it he clothed justice, when he did not turn aside from martyrdom for justice’s sake. But Thomas had strong and vigorous dispositions suited to human needs. [Col. 1008A] He did not lightly turn himself to every matter, nor did he readily assent to anything; rather, he believed what he saw, and grasped whatever was inwardly invisible only through the showing of signs. For this is why signs are known through works: bodily things are seen bodily, spiritual things are apprehended spiritually, and by holiness of works a person is known to be spiritual.

Thus he converted a great multitude to God and clothed justice with a long garment of green silk over a shirt. It shone like a ray of the sun, when he adorned it with the uprightness of good intention and made it shine in all things, converting the hearts of unbelievers from idols to God and offering himself through his martyrdom to the Ruler of all.

But Peter wove a tunic from fine linen and purple when he displayed uprightness, gentleness, and vigor; and with it he clothed justice with ecclesiastical orders, when he subjected himself to many tribulations in body and soul. [Col. 1008B]

Matthias, gentle and humble, possessing dove-like manners and fleeing the diversity of human temperaments, envy, and hatred, was a vessel of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in those who do not allow their minds to run through public places and inquire into diverse matters. Before believers and unbelievers alike, humbly and as though unaware, he performed many signs and wonders; and he desired martyrdom as a feast.

Therefore he prepared for justice a royal seat upon which it might sit honorably, having eagles’ heads and lions’ feet upon its four columns; because he flew in humility through the four regions [Col. 1008C] of the world and could not be conquered by any injury. Spreading his preaching widely, patiently enduring very many reproaches, he brought all his work manfully to completion. Therefore people gladly listened to him and loved him greatly, and he made justice sit upon the seat which he had prepared through his humility.

For God chose the twelve apostles in the alternation of different dispositions, just as He had also chosen twelve prophets, because God is wondrous.

Then He found one spark and kindled it with His fire—namely Paul—in whom He also performed many wonders. For He completes His signs in the fierce and vigorous as well as in the gentle, lest people reject them by saying that He works His miracles only in the good. For the Holy Spirit adorned through Paul the entire teaching of the apostles. Paul bore a mountain of lofty mind and was fierce as a leopard, snarling at everything [Col. 1008D] which he wished to overcome, because he thought himself able to accomplish all that he wished.

The Holy Spirit found in him a spark of faithfulness, because he carried on persecution not from envy and hatred but from love of the old Law. God had created beasts before humanity, and had made humanity in His image and likeness after the beasts. He first gave the old Law according to beasts, which He afterwards transformed, through the humanity of His Son, into a spiritual understanding according to the exercise of the angels’ praise. For as He first formed humanity and then sent into it the breath of life, so He first set forth the old Law and later changed it for the better by the new Law.

Thus, finding Paul in excessive zeal, God threw him down in the old Law and thereby showed him that he was to bear the name of His Son in the new Law. Raising Paul’s spirit to the height, He showed him the wonders by which He contended against him; yet his soul remained hidden within him, so that he scarcely felt himself alive, just as a soul remaining in a body sends forth its thoughts. For if God had gently revealed His miracles to him, Paul would, because of his fierceness of mind, have returned to his former zeal. Therefore [Col. 1009B] God constrained him greatly and drenched his whole body with toil.

His infirmity was twofold: all the veins of his body were pervaded with sickness, and the fiery darts of the devil wearied him through a certain sweetness of the flesh. But because he had seen God's wonders in spirit, he had an exceedingly strong power in his spirit; and because he had seen many secret and hidden mysteries beyond what is permitted a human being to speak, his words and preaching were like nails fixed on high that support a house. For the Son of God, whom the Virgin Mary bore, chose this man from the tribe of Benjamin. Therefore he labored more than all others who had been bodily with Him in preaching.

A woman adorns herself for the honor and glory of her husband, so that she may seem all the more beautiful to him. Thus a human being should understand how to adorn his own soul before the highest King: when a person possesses Charity, he puts on for himself a golden garment; when he loves chastity, he adorns his face with precious pearls; and when he takes upon himself abstinence from foods, he clothes himself in purple and fine linen. [Col. 1009C] Therefore the person who wishes to abstain from sins should avoid meats—though they are to be eaten for the restoration of health—because meats often draw human flesh into sins.

Paul, however, had no commandment concerning virginity in the Law; hence he did not impose it on people but gave counsel, because commandment belongs to fear, but counsel to love. Therefore the commandment of fear, heard outwardly, is often transgressed; but the counsel of love, which all the veins of a person perceive in desire, is firmly kept. But because counsel was first disturbed through the serpent, God became human from the ancient counsel, in whom Charity burned so that it illumined the whole world.

Therefore Paul too gave, from hidden counsel, counsel concerning virginity and not a command, which no human being ought to establish by command, because God brought it to perfection in Himself. Thus chastity, possessing no legal commandment of service or fear, is alone free in God without any fear.

[Col. 1010A] Therefore Paul is the wheel of the chariot of justice: as a wheel carries a chariot and a chariot carries every burden, so Paul’s teaching bears the law of Christ. For the new Law is woven from the old Law, in which Moses enclosed circumcision and offerings; the Holy Spirit renewed all these into new holiness, and Paul fastened them with a new fire in the appended little chain of the necklace of justice.

He sanctified every work in upright honorableness: namely, that marriage should be in the fear of God; that those who live rightly should be continent; that a person should not afflict himself by abstinence beyond what he could endure by God's grace; and that virginity should adorn itself with the crown of the highest King, because it is taken from God. For just as God formed the first human being without any moisture of flesh, [Col. 1010B] so He Himself took His garment from virginity without any sweat of sin.

In these three states—marriage, continence, and virginity—Paul gathered all virtues and the entire life of the saints and adorned the teaching of the apostles with an elegant color. He also made the shoes of justice from purple silk when he entirely left the world and labored more than all his fellow disciples by traveling through the ways of the churches. He adorned them with purest gold, shining like stars, when through good works he set before all believers examples shining in holiness; there too he hastened to give his body to suffering.

But James, called the brother of the Lord, gentle in character, was mild. He offered his teaching inwardly to God alone and did not seek empty glory; rather, running with great zeal in the straight paths, he cleansed the muddy streets of unbelief. [Col. 1010C] He also converted people to the true faith and sweetly declared how the Son of God, born from the Virgin, should be taught. Demonstrating this in sweet words, he confirmed it also by holy works and very many signs.

Accordingly, by the sweet sound of his words he prepared earrings for justice. The left earring was of hyacinth and had the color of a pure cloud, signifying that the Son of God lived in the world without sin, wiping away and washing human sins. But the right earring was of reddish hyacinth, showing the Passion [Col. 1010D] of the same Son of God, through whom the devil was conquered. Therefore James also submitted himself to martyrdom.

Simon was wise and vigorous, preached bitter torments to the innumerable sins of unbelievers, and performed great signs in steadfast faith. Thus people gladly listened to him, and he prepared a rushing path to faith because he set before them fear of death. In this way, through great proclamation, he made a necklace of justice out of emerald, red stones, beads, and pearls: through the defense of his vigorous character he made the necklace, upon which he set the emerald through the greenness of prophecy and the red stones, with the other beads and pearls, through fear of punishments. Nor did he fear the torment of martyrdom, [Col. 1011A] but endured it patiently.

Paul aided him; and although he had made the shoes of justice, he hung from that same necklace a most elegant little chain made of purest gold and most firmly adorned without defect with twelve stones and most precious pearls. Descending to the feet of this same justice, it had at its end two formed heads: on its right side, one of reddish sardius, like the head of a goat; on its left, one of gold, like the head of a leopard, so that the goat’s head seemed to oppose the leopard’s head.

For he joined his teaching to the defense of the teaching of the other apostles and adorned it irreproachably with good works, with apostolic teachings, and with the other virtues, so that it might endure without failing until the end of uprightness, until the world is ended. There also, about that same end, two powers will appear as if in the two heads: one ascending upward to salvation in laborious constraint through Enoch and Elijah; the other hurrying snarling toward perdition through Antichrist, in the pretense of glorious miracles and virtues. Thus too they show that those who strive toward heavenly things crush those who hasten toward diabolical deception. [Col. 1011B]

But James, the brother of John, wove a woman’s veil of white silk and gold embroidery by preaching the Incarnation and Passion of the Son of God, while destroying idols through very many miracles. With this he adorned the head of justice that was thus surrounded, so that the whole Church might give praise to God; there too he bowed himself to the martyrdom of beheading. [Col. 1011C]

John, however, by the miracles which God showed him, made a girdle of green silk, bringing forth chastity with a green and sweet intention; into it he set twelve stones of prophetic virtues, with many pearls of good will. At its mouth he placed a green color like the branch from which balsam exudes, because he joined to chastity’s enduring greenness the fragrance of virtues; and he girded Justice with it when, at the people’s prayers, he proclaimed, “In the beginning was the Word.” But Philip, being gentle and appearing humble in his teaching, drew many people to himself. Therefore he also fashioned bracelets [Col. 1011D] of gold, upon which he placed emeralds, reddish jacinths, and most noble pearls, so that the gold itself could scarcely be seen because of the multitude of these stones. For, displaying in his teaching and works the greenness, labor, and innocence of virtues, he concealed inwardly, as far as he could, his good will; and he placed these bracelets around the arms of Justice when by his martyrdom he completed his good works.

Bartholomew, moreover, could neither be wearied in his great zeal for preaching nor wished to cease from it. Therefore, from gold and another most beautiful material, he made electrum with raised engraving and intermingled precious stones. Extending it broadly, he drew it from the aforesaid bracelets as far as the elbows of the arms of Justice; and [Col. 1012A] he also divided it, from the same bracelets to the aforesaid elbows, into three distinct places, joining those divisions with certain slender golden chains. For from the good will which he had in faith, he exalted the words of his preaching together with the hidden secrets of God’s mysteries and with chosen virtues, and extended them as far as holy action. Correctly distinguishing three persons in one God, he faithfully and most fittingly affirmed the true Trinity, invisibly and ineffably joined together; thus drawing human minds to himself, wholly subjecting his body to suffering, and encircling the arms of Justice with marvelous adornment.

Andrew also made a ring of the purest gold and set in it an excellent topaz. He made known that the Son of God [Col. 1012B] is the spouse of Justice, when he adorned sincere faith in the Church through the beauty of virtues; and he put this ring on the finger of Justice when he allowed himself to be suspended upon the cross.

Thaddaeus too was prudent and subtle, and he studied to investigate human dispositions; therefore he converted very many to the profit of faith, because they could not overcome him. Conquering the serpent’s deceit through holy works, he displayed many miracles before the people. He also made a cloak of reddish silk and diligently endeavored to adorn it. He placed it around the adornment of Justice, because he ordered works of charity in the splendor of the other virtues, brought them to their true beauty, and covered Justice with them, when he also subjected himself bodily to suffering.

But Peter, [Col. 1012C] seeing her thus clothed, and although he had dressed her in a tunic, nevertheless fashioned a crown of the finest gold, which he adorned with most precious stones and jewels and placed upon the head of Justice. For by preaching the glory of the Son of God faithfully and fearlessly, and showing it adorned with every virtue and hidden mystery, he embellished Justice with the crown of holiness and honor; and, hanging upon the cross, fittingly bestowed it upon her head by his martyrdom. In this manner Justice was clothed by the apostles.

### A brief recapitulation of the foregoing: how, in these days lacking manly strength, all ecclesiastical institutions fall into deterioration; and the testimony of the Psalmist where he says, “Righteous art thou, O Lord,” why it is introduced and how it is to be understood

**X.** But she herself, having a face shining like the splendor of the sun, because she is always radiant and unchangeable before God, calls upon the heavenly Judge with a mighty cry, and shows, as has been said, that her garments have been defiled by wicked people. For these days of feminine weakness lack manly strength, so that all ecclesiastical institutions, whether secular or spiritual, decline for the worse and now stand in a manner other than that in which the apostles and the other ancient Fathers established them. By all these things the Church at first shone like the sun, and Justice was crowned, just as [Col. 1013A] a king is named for his dominion over a kingdom and honored for his diadem and royal garments.

For the Justice of God is crowned and adorned through ecclesiastical ordinances and through all things pertaining to them; and it is itself the substance of all lawful justifications, which were instituted by almighty God and kindled by the fire of the Holy Spirit, just as a house is exalted by those dwelling in it. Hence it is written: “Righteous art thou, O Lord, and upright is thy judgment” (Psal. CXVIII). The sense of this statement is to be understood thus: Thou art righteous in all thy judgments, O Lord, who rulest all things; because thou art that Justice which is never darkened by any iniquity, but displays its work as a set-up banner goes before its leader.

The work of Justice is heaven and earth with the rest of creation; and Justice is God, who shows truth through the good report of holy works, which are fixed in that Justice as branches in a tree. Therefore God’s judgment is also upright in equity, because it has no darkness of falsehood; for it treads that down as most foul mud, stinking in its rottenness. Therefore the Justice of God cries out over the mountains, and its voice sounds to heaven, and complains that the mountain of holiness, first established in the Church, now lies destroyed upon the mountain of holiness. For I, the Justice of God, say with a mournful voice:

### The complaint or cry of Justice to God the Judge against wicked and impious people, defiled by diverse crimes, who, rejecting the ancient institutions of the Fathers, strip her and leave her destitute of the ornaments of her glory

**XI.** My crown has been darkened by the schism of erring minds, because each person has established a law for himself according to his own will; and those who ought to have a master and endure his rod wish to be masters. Governing themselves by arrogant ordinance and calling useful whatever they choose, they thus become faithless because they trust in themselves; and neither from themselves nor from others do they attain in this way the salvation of life, which no one except God can give. For through all these things my crown has been darkened, because those who do such things do not behold me in that brightness [Col. 1013D] in which I proceeded from God.

My tunic too has been sprinkled with the dust of earth. It is defiled by those who, abandoning the world, put on the tunic of the Son of God by a holy and good manner of life, yet join themselves to harlots, as is known to be written concerning the younger son in the Gospel. They have been yoked to Christ’s yoke by imitation of circumcision and of the priests’ legal institution; but by transgression they prove adulterers. They do not cry out with the younger son, who returns to his father saying, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before thee” (Luc. XV); rather, they hold the evil of adultery as though it had been established for them by custom.

Therefore they stain my tunic with the dust of sins and do not shake that same dust from it through repentance; rather, like worms, they warm themselves in the rottenness [Col. 1014A] of sins. Hence they are blind, deaf, and mute: they do not proclaim my office or judge my judgment. Instead they swallow up avarice and do not heal wounds, because they are full of wounds; and they are deaf to the Scripture which speaks to them, neither hearing it nor teaching it to others.

In these ways there is weariness in all the established orders of the Church, and she herself walks as though without a staff, because almost all her institutions have now failed. For when the sun is darkened in a cloud, there is no joy of pleasantness in creatures; nor is there joy among peoples when they are without a king. The institutions of ecclesiastical orders have been darkened because they wish merely to be named as institutions without works; therefore true joy is not in them, just as it is not in faith without works. Truly this will not endure or remain thus, because God’s judgment threatens those who fulfill all their own desires in their own possession as though they were without God.

For I, who arose in the ancient counsel, cry out to the judgment of God, making complaint concerning those who have taken my cloak from me and stripped me of all my ornaments. I summon their judges against them to aid me, in the same calling by which the Creator of all called woman when he took her from man, so that he might make for him a helper like himself. For just as woman is subject to man and bears children, so human beings ought through me to hear God’s commandments and obey them. Since they do not do this [Col. 1014C] but neglect me, every time I am struck by them, God’s judgment surrounds them—as happened in ancient time through the Flood, and as happened many times under the old law and the new law, as indeed still happens often.

For I am called Justice, and the Church arose from me through the regeneration of Spirit and water; and we are one, just as God and man are one. Therefore I shall cry out to most fierce judges, who will avenge me upon the furious bites of those who pursue me as wolves pursue lambs. These sinners also do not feast upon the fatted calf, but are like the Samaritans who wished to remain in two laws. Therefore they will be turned into the mockery of the prophet Elijah, who, as though deriding those who worshipped Baal, told them to cry with a louder voice. For if Baal were God, perhaps he was speaking, or at an inn, or on a journey, or perhaps asleep and needing to be awakened. Thus they have also been deceived, because God’s grace is far from them: they do not keep the commandments which they receive, but cast them behind them, saying, “When we wish, we shall observe the commandments of our God, because correction pleases him only for a little while.”

### That God, seeing these losses of Justice in the unfailing light of his brightness, does not consign them to oblivion, although he overlooks human sins for the sake of repentance; and his words concerning this

**XII.** The man who is a strong warrior against the diabolical battle-lines and [Col. 1015A] against every wickedness sees these unseemly days, which are harmful to all equity, in the unfailing light of his brightness; nor does he consign them to oblivion, although he overlooks human sins in order that people may repent. And he says:

“I know in my hidden judgments this time which declines from good and falls into evil. For I do not so negligently disregard the iniquities of human beings, which run their course through the varied courses of successive times, that I fail to examine them with the scourges of just correction. But the golden number—namely, those martyrs who, shining like gold in the redness of their blood, were slain in the early Church for the true faith—is not yet complete. For they await those martyrs who, at the end of time, amid the error of perdition, for the dishonoring of my name, will give their bodies over to the suffering of martyrdom,” as John, my beloved, testifies, saying:

### Testimony fitting to this from the Apocalypse of John the Apostle, and the sense in which it is to be understood

**XIII.** “And it was said to them that they should rest yet for a little time, until their fellow-servants and their brethren, who are to be slain as they also were, should be completed” (Apoc. VII).

The meaning of this statement is to be understood thus. By divine inspiration it was shown to those who had subjected themselves to temporal death for the love of God that their bodies should rest in the dust of dissolution for yet a little time—that is, until that predestination is fulfilled, until those who will be servants of God, serving God in all truth, are completed in every perfection; [Col. 1015C] and until they and their brethren, since they too will be passible in their bodies as those martyrs were, are worn down by very many tribulations for the Son of God and undergo bodily death.

For the blood-stained voice of the martyrs, who knew neither sins nor why they were killed, rises to God; but the splendor of divinity shines upon them, so that in that same splendor of divinity it foresees an innumerable multitude to come. For the brightness of eternal life is given to them, in which they know the answer shown to them. Their cry is not darkened by the filthy works of sinners, because they were innocent and because their blood was shed for the Incarnation of the Son of God, where they also testified that the Lamb would shed [Col. 1015D] his blood.

Those who are killed for faith and justice are called their fellow-servants; but their brethren are those who will be destroyed by Antichrist at the end of time, just as the infants were destroyed by Herod, who denied the Son of God—as Antichrist too will deny him. For the voice of a human being’s shed blood rises upward through his soul, crying out and complaining that it has been expelled from the seal of the body in which God had placed it; and thereafter that soul receives the reward of its works, whether in glory or in punishments. The first voice of blood began to cry to God in Abel, because Cain had precipitately and presumptuously destroyed the construction of God’s work. Therefore the Son of God again says:

### [Col. 1016A] Another complaint of the Son to the Father concerning the tribulation which he suffers in his body from those who kick against him through malice; concerning little ones who fail from good by embracing vanity; and concerning how angels, though they shine with immeasurable brightness, nevertheless behold and approve the holy works of human beings as a mirror of praise

**XIV.** Therefore do thou, O paternal mirror—which is the brightness of divinity, in which the host of angels shines, just as those forms which are shown in a mirror—look and show how many injuries I suffer from those who neglect me. For that same mirror always shines upon the angels. In my body, that is, in my members who kick against me through malice when they ought to cleave to me in uprightness, I endure the weariness of perversity, because I find nowhere in them where I may rest through the greenness of good works.

My little ones also, who ought to walk in humility and cast away all worldly pomp, fail in that which is nothing because they embrace the vanity of pride, thinking themselves holy and carrying their works in the praises of human glory. Because in this transitory praise they fall away from heavenly praise, they do not heed the praise of angels. For angels frequently praise holy divinity, always finding a new praise in God because they cannot bring him to an end. For he is the most bright light, which can in no way be extinguished, so that the angelic company is made bright by him.

For an angel is praise without a carnal work; but a human being is praise with a carnal work, and angels praise that person’s works. In the praises by which they praise God, they also approve the holy works of human beings and behold them as a mirror of praise. For God wonderfully composed the human being from soul and body; and the human being does not lack the brightness of angels when he is in their fellowship, because God also ordained that divinity and humanity should be gloriously praised in one God.

Hereby the devil is mocked: though he was an angel, he wished to be God; but God, as it were, deceived him when he created from the mud of earth the human being, who is soul and body in one—not a human being if soul is without body, nor if body is without soul. The soul works with the body, and the body with the soul. For the body is an enclosure in which the soul [Col. 1016D] is shut up, and often constrains the soul so that it yields to the body and cannot restrain it from performing the work which it seeks, because it is occupied with it. The taste of the flesh displeases the soul, yet it is often accomplished through the veins against her will, in which she works. But when a human being desires another life, opposed to the flesh’s concupiscence, the soul grasps and accomplishes it by a swift course, because with its whole desire it tastes that life within itself.

### That Justice, honesty of morals, and the dignity of virtues, strengthened by prophets from the days of the Flood to the Lord’s advent, and thereafter shining for a long time through apostles and doctors in the Church, though now corrupted after these days languishing in injustice, will again be reformed in human beings before the end, after many tribulations

**XV.** But these days which languish in injustice are signified, as has been said, by the fiery but non-burning dog in the book *Scivias*. Others, stronger in strength, will follow them, in which certain people, looking upon uprightness and putting off the aforesaid frivolity, will turn themselves to Justice.

Therefore, from the Incarnation of the Son of God, Justice ascended through the many courses of days to the heights of holiness, as though by certain ladders, in the Catholic faith. It was poured over, as it were, with the purest gold of good works and shone brilliantly in that same faith; it was stained by no unworthiness of depraved works, but remained unconquered. But after those days had passed for a very great length of time, even to the aforesaid [Col. 1017B] days of feminine frivolity, it began in that same faith to incline by certain descending degradations and to be darkened by certain shadows of injustice.

For Justice, moral honesty, and the other dignities of virtues gradually grew among human beings from the days of the Flood, and gradually ascended to their heights as far as the days of the prophets. The prophets so strengthened them that they gave their greatest splendor until the Son of God. Thereafter they endured in the apostles and other doctors, in the same dignity and splendor, through a very great length of days, almost until the rise of the aforesaid secular judge, a worshipper of adultery rather than of the fear of God. Before his beginning they gradually began to decrease and incline toward worse things, just as they had gradually risen upward from the Flood to the prophets.

From the days of that judge arose the root of iniquity and forgetfulness of Justice and moral honesty. Spreading and propagating, these proceeded as though in feminine weakness until another ruler, bearing a spiritual name, who possessed the prudence and malice of the serpent, and whom God’s judgment killed. In his days the aforesaid iniquity and the superfluous habits of human vices began, by divine examination, to grow hot, boil, and cast forth foam for purification. Hence they are now cultivated so sharply and bitterly, and cleansed of their foam, that human beings are moved in these dangers by great mourning and sadness. But the days of mourning and sadness are not yet present.

### That the heavenly Judge, meanwhile regarding Justice’s complaint, will bring his vengeance upon transgressors against equity—and especially upon wicked prelates of the Church—through many judgments of adversity, until, cleansed by due examination, they return to their senses through repentance; and thus every order, restored to uprightness, will return to the honor of its dignity

**XVI.** After Justice has directed her complaint to the heavenly Judge, as has been said above, he, receiving the voices of her complaint, will in his just judgment permit his vengeance to come upon the transgressors against uprightness, and the tyranny of their enemies to rage against them. These enemies will say to one another: “How long shall we endure and tolerate these rapacious wolves, [Col. 1018A] who ought to be physicians and are not? Yet because they possess authority to speak, bind, and loose, they seize us as most savage beasts. Their crimes fall upon us, and through them the whole Church withers; for they do not proclaim what is just and they destroy the law, as wolves devour lambs. They are ravenous in gluttony, commit very many adulteries, and for such sins judge us without mercy. They are also plunderers of churches, and through avarice swallow up whatever they can; by their offices they make us poor and needy, and defile both themselves and us.

“Therefore let us judge and divide them by a just judgment, since they are deceivers rather than teachers. Let us do this also lest we perish, because if they continue thus they will throw the whole region into disorder by subjecting it to themselves. Now let us tell them either to fulfill their habit and office according to just religious observance, as the ancient Fathers established them, or to withdraw from us and leave what they possess. We do not wish these men to reign over us with estates, fields, and the other secular things over which we have been appointed rulers. How is it fitting that tonsured men, with their stoles and chasubles, should have more soldiers and more weapons than we? Is it suitable that a cleric should be a soldier and a soldier a cleric? Therefore let us take from them what they possess not rightly but unjustly.

“But [Col. 1018C] let us carefully consider what has been offered with great discernment for the souls of the dead, and leave that to them, for this is not plunder. Almighty Father has rightly divided all things: heaven for heavenly beings, earth for earthly beings. Thus there should be a just division among the children of men: spiritual people should possess what pertains to them, and secular people what suits them, so that neither party oppresses the other by plunder. God did not command that tunic and cloak should be given to one son and the other remain naked; rather, he commanded that this one should receive the cloak and that one the tunic.

“Therefore secular people should have the cloak, because of the extent of secular care and because of their children, who always increase and multiply; but the tunic should be granted to the spiritual people, lest they lack food or clothing and lest they possess more than is necessary. Therefore we judge and determine that all the aforesaid things should be rightly divided; and wherever the cloak is found with the tunic among spiritual persons, there the cloak should be taken away and given to the needy, lest they be consumed by poverty.”

Thus at last they will endeavor through this judicial decree to accomplish all these things according to their own purposes. But pontifical dignities and all those living under them in spiritual habit will at first labor greatly to resist them with the shutting of heaven. Yet when they finally perceive that they have been unable to resist them either by the power of binding or loosing, by the confirmation of their offerings, by the clamor of arms, by flatteries, or by threats, they will be terrified by divine judgment. Casting off the empty and proud confidence which they had always previously placed in themselves, and returning to themselves, [Col. 1019A] they will humble themselves before them, cry out in lamentation, and say:

“Because we cast away almighty God in the order of our office, this confusion has been brought upon us: we are oppressed and humiliated by those whom we ought to have oppressed and humbled. For God has taken from us the cord of subjection over those of whom we were appointed rulers and over those who were subject to us by discipline, and he permits them to rule over us. Therefore let us consider that we suffer the just judgments of God, because we wished to subject the kingdoms of the world to ourselves, though we ourselves ought to have been under God’s yoke; and because we fulfilled every pleasure of carnal concupiscence so that no one dared rebuke us for it.

“For God commanded the Jewish people to offer sacrifices of animals to their Creator; but they, despising his commands, turned themselves to every carnal sense. Therefore foreign nations were brought against them. But he commanded us to offer a living and spiritual sacrifice; yet we did not fear to handle it with polluted hands. When he crowned us with the diadem of his scepter, we exalted ourselves above all things and fulfilled the concupiscences of our flesh in every way. Therefore our enemies rage against us, just as the enemies of earlier [Col. 1019C] transgressors ruled over them.”

Then both the greater and lesser persons of each people will order the clergy and arrange what is necessary for them so that they lack neither food nor clothing and thereafter suffer no such reproaches from secular people. These things will begin among both the spiritual and secular people as at the first hour of the day; then, as at the third hour, they will be brought into full operation; finally, as at the sixth, they will be completed altogether. All ranks of people will be considered as though after the sixth hour and will be arranged otherwise than they now are, so that each order may stand in its own uprightness, free persons return to the honor of their freedom, and servants [Col. 1019D] to the due servitude of their subjection.

### That, when God’s vengeance has been appeased through the correction of transgressors, the order of Justice and the tranquility of peace will shine before the end of the world, as they did before the Lord’s first advent; and that some part of the Jews will be converted, rejoice, and confess that he has come whom they now deny has come

**XVII.** Yet amid all this, as the lion marked in the book *Scivias* shows, hard and cruel wars will repeatedly arise after the fear of God has been cast away; very many people will fall in slaughter, and very many cities will collapse in destruction. For as a man overcomes feminine softness by his strength, and as a lion surpasses the other beasts, so in those days the cruelty of certain people will consume the peace of others by divine judgment. God will then grant the cruelty of punishments to his enemies for the purging of iniquities, as he has always done from the beginning of the world.

When human beings have been purified by the aforesaid afflictions, they will become weary of the aforesaid conflicts. Through fear of God they will lay hold of Justice in all ecclesiastical institutions pleasing to God, add many good things to them, and do this in times of peace, war, and every kind of labor. Then Justice will rightly be called a bride, though she had been led as a concubine into the bed of the true King. Her concern had been sometimes to observe certain legal commands by pretense, and sometimes to join herself to the custom of a depraved fellowship. Therefore [Col. 1020B] the King will reject her; for the aforesaid days were like a concubine, in which people observed ecclesiastical commands in certain institutions but wholly abandoned them in others.

For almighty God, who is the true Solomon, will adorn his bride, Justice, with all ornaments—that is, with all ecclesiastical orders—so that her ornaments will appear openly. The concubine had so obscured them in her that at times they could not be seen. Thus those days will show the destruction of useless days, and consolation will remove desolation, just as the new law changed the old law and as a time of healing brought a time of falling toward better things. For if the aforesaid evils remained unshaken in the frivolity and scandal of their custom, truth would be so darkened that the towers of the heavenly Jerusalem would be shaken and every ecclesiastical institution polluted, as though human beings were without the true God.

For transgressors against Justice will then be in such disgrace as a woman who, abandoning a lawful marriage, commits adultery. They had committed adultery, as it were, by transgressing ecclesiastical commandments; and therefore they will endure affliction and contempt, as a woman abandoned by her husband lacks his consolation. New and unknown ordinances of Justice and peace will then come, so that people will wonder and say that they had neither heard nor known such things before. Peace will be given them before the day of judgment, as peace also preceded the first advent of the Son of God. Yet, for fear of the judgment to come, they will be unable to rejoice wholly; rather, they will seek from almighty God all Justice in the Catholic faith, while Jews too rejoice and say that he is now present whose coming they presently deny.

For that peace which preceded the advent of the Incarnation of the Son of God will be brought to full completion in those days. Strong men will then arise in great prophecy, and every shoot of Justice will flower in the sons and daughters of human beings, as was foretold through my servant the prophet according to my will: “In that day the Branch of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth sublime, and joy for those who have been saved from Israel” (Isa. IV). [Col. 1021A] The meaning of this statement is to be understood thus:

### Words of Isaiah the prophet testifying to the Lord’s first advent, which will be especially fulfilled in the world through the illumination of the Jews, who, blinded by the scandal of Christ in his Passion, had withered from the greenness of faith and good works

**XVIII.** On that day, when the angels sang that peace had been given to human beings, my Son was born of a virgin, magnified by those same angels, and glorified also by the shepherds who sought him with devout affection. The fruit of the earth, to which peace had been restored and to which the air supplied sweetness, was abundant; and there was joy among the sons of Jacob who had been delivered from the past tribulation of evils, because they had earlier been crushed by many tribulations under a just judgment.

But when the light [Col. 1021B] of true faith illuminates the hearts of the faithful, my Son will be magnified in them, because they will believe that he came forth from me and will glorify him when they confess that he has returned to me in glory. Therefore the fruit of good works will also be exalted in them. Their exultation will increase when, rescued from diabolical power and freed from Tartarean punishments, they are numbered among the children of God.

But the flourishing of the vineyard of Sabaoth, which proceeded from the flower of Aaron’s rod, did not grow hot through the serpent’s foam when my Son suffered on the cross; it withered because the eyes of the Jews were weighed down in the shadow of death. Hearing the words of prophecy, they rejected them together with the true flower, whom the whole earth recognized when he expired upon the cross. Therefore they also killed themselves and thus withered in both the Old and the New Testament. For the Old Testament is like winter, which hides all greenness within itself; but the New is like summer, which produces grasses and flowers.

### The words of the same Lord Christ which, while he was being led to death, he spoke in answer to those lamenting him concerning the green and dry wood; and how they are to be understood

**XIX.** Therefore he also said to those lamenting him: “For if they do these things in the green wood, what will be done in the dry?” (Luc. XXIII.) The meaning of this statement is to be understood thus: He himself was the green wood, because he brought forth every greenness of virtue; yet he was rejected by unbelievers. But Antichrist is the dry wood, because, trampling down every greenness of Justice, he makes dry those things which are green in uprightness; and therefore he will be brought to nothing.

The green wood also was those days in which human beings had regard for the restoration of all sorrows and feared no dread of the future judgment of the end time. The dry wood, however, will be when the falling away of which Paul, my chosen vessel, speaks appears before the son of perdition; then every pain that comes upon them will shake heaven and earth. For heaven and earth will be moved in the future judgment, as was foreshadowed in the green wood when, at his death, the wheel of the firmament—which bears many signs within itself—withdrew the splendor of its light, as is also shown in the aforesaid words of the prophets.

### [Col. 1022A] How great and diverse the joys in the Church will be, through Justice’s restored state, abundance of temporal things, and plenty of spiritual goods, which people will enjoy for some time in the next-to-last days; while that part of Jews and heretics who persist in evil rejoices in ruinous presumption at Antichrist’s near advent
XX. In the days therefore mentioned above, very gentle clouds with very mild air will touch the earth and cause it to sweat forth the verdure of fruitfulness, because people will then make themselves ready for every kind of righteousness. For in the aforesaid time of feminine weakness the earth’s fruitfulness failed, because the elements, violated by human sins, were then deprived in every respect of their functions. Princes also, together with the rest of the people, will rightly order the justice of God, and will prohibit all [Col. 1022B] weapons prepared for the killing of men, preserving only those implements by which the earth is cultivated and those which serve the necessities of human use. If anyone transgresses this, he will be killed by his own sword and cast into a deserted place.

And as the clouds will then send forth a mild and proper rain for the fruit of righteous growth, so too the Holy Spirit will pour the dew of his grace, together with prophecy, wisdom, and holiness, upon the people, so that they will then appear as if transformed into another manner of good conduct. For the old Law was a shadow of spiritual life, since it was wholly marked out through creation: just as in winter no fruit hidden in the earth is seen, [Col. 1022C] because it has not yet been formed. Nor did that Law possess summer, because the Son of God had not yet appeared incarnate; but when he came, it was wholly transformed into spiritual meaning and displayed the fruit of eternal life in the precepts of the Gospel, just as summer too produces flowers and fruits.

For in those days there will be a true summer through the power of God, because then all things will stand in truth: priests, namely, and monks, likewise virgins and the continent, and the remaining orders will stand in their uprightness, living justly and well and casting aside every exaltation and superfluity of riches. For as through the moderation of clouds and air the necessary usefulness of fruits will then be produced, so the shoot of spiritual life will then be revealed through the grace of God. Prophecy, [Col. 1022D] as has been said, will then be open, and wisdom delightful and strong; and all the faithful will behold themselves in these things as in a mirror. Then also true angels will attach themselves familiarly to human beings, seeing in them a new and holy manner of life, whereas now they often withdraw from them because of their foul-smelling sins.

But then the righteous will rejoice as they make their way toward the land of promise and await the hope of the eternal reward; yet they will not rejoice fully, because they will see the future judgment drawing near. They will do this after the likeness of pilgrims who are journeying toward their homeland and do not have full joy while they are still in pilgrimage. But the Jews and heretics will rejoice greatly then, saying: “Our glory is near, and those who [Col. 1023A] wearied and expelled us will be trampled down.”

Nevertheless, very many pagans, seeing the abundance of the Christians’ honor and riches, will then join themselves to the Christians; and, having been baptized, they will preach Christ with them, as happened in the time of the apostles. They will say to the Jews and heretics: “What you call your glory will be eternal death, and him whom you call your prince—you will see his end with the greatest terror and danger. Then, beholding that day, you will turn to us: the day which the offspring of the dawn, namely Mary, star of the sea, showed to us.”

Those days indeed will be strong and praiseworthy in peace and stability, like armed soldiers lying upon a rock, lying in wait for their enemies and pursuing them to destruction; and they will announce the coming of the last day, because whatever the prophets foretold of goodness or grace will be fulfilled in them. Wisdom, piety, and holiness too will be established in them. For if the Son of God had not been foretold by the prophets, and had come as in the blink of an eye, he would quickly have been consigned to oblivion, just as the lost man too, coming as though secretly, will be destroyed very swiftly.

That this same tranquillity of peace and abundance of fruits, when human beings attribute them to themselves and not to God, and begin again to grow sluggish in religion, will be followed by tribulations so great as have never before raged in the world.

XXI. Yet in those same days the aforesaid justice and religion will sometimes decline in human beings through the weariness of weakness, [Col. 1023C] but they will quickly recover their strength. At times too iniquity will rise and fall again; at times wars, famine, plague, and mortality will rage and then vanish again. None of these things will then remain long in one state and course, but they will move now this way, now that, so that they appear at one time and slip away at another.

But in those very days, amid all these things, as the horse in the book *Scivias* shows, wantonness of behavior, boastfulness of spirit, fullness of pleasures, and other vanities without reverence will often arise among people. For, resting in the quiet of peace and abounding in plenty of crops, they will be terrified by no invasion of wars and constrained by no scarcity of produce. But attributing these things to themselves, [Col. 1023D] they will not render due honor in them to God, from whom all good things proceed. Therefore dangers so great as had not been seen before will follow that tranquillity and abundance.

For when people, as has been said, are settled in such quiet, fearing no dangers, other days of every sorrow will come, in which the lamentable voice of the prophets and the voice of the Son of God will be fulfilled: people, through fear of continual afflictions, desiring death and saying, “Why were we born?” and wishing that the mountains might fall upon them. The earlier days of sorrows and calamities had at times some refreshment and recovery; but these days, full of every sorrow and iniquity, will not cease from evils. Rather, sorrow [Col. 1024A] will be heaped upon sorrow and iniquity upon iniquity in them; every hour murder and injustice will be reckoned as nothing; and just as animals are slaughtered for eating, so human beings in those same days will be killed in the fury of others.

For when the pagan nations see Christians living in peace and rich in possessions, having cruel confidence in their own strength they will say: “Let us attack the Christians with our weapons, for they are without arms and without power; we can seize and kill them like sheep for slaughter.” Thus they will summon from far-off regions a most ferocious and most unclean nation, to which they will join themselves in fornication, uncleanness, and every evil. They will attack the Christian people everywhere with plundering and battles, [Col. 1024B] and will destroy many regions and cities. They will defile ecclesiastical disciplines with very many vanities and impurities, and will contaminate all whom they can in the same manner.

Thus those days will make clear that still other, most evil days are to come, and will reveal the coming of the lost man. For as one who is unclean and continually defiles himself in uncleanness is not thereby satisfied, so those days too will be full of impurities and will not be able to be satisfied with them. David, foreseeing this, said in a clear voice:

The words of David from Psalm XXI, spoken in the person of Christ and the Church, announcing the persecutions of the wicked, and how they are to be understood.

XXII. “They divided my garments among themselves, and over [Col. 1024C] my clothing they cast lots.” Although, because of the certainty of future events, this speaks literally of past events, it must nevertheless be understood thus of future ones. Through great slaughter caused by unbelief, unbelievers will divide according to their own wills the arrangements of secular dignities and functions with which I had been clothed in the Church as with garments. And upon those who, as it were, were my clothing and nearer to me in spiritual life, they will cast very many vanities, when they turn them away from the uprightness of their paths, reduce all the rights of churches to nothing through destruction, and impose upon them laws of iniquity so as utterly to crush them.

But David himself answers these evils, saying: “But you, O Lord, do not remove your help far from me; look to my defense” (*Ps.* XXI). The meaning of this sentence must be understood thus: I, the Church, who ought to be the bride of your Son, O heavenly Father, although I am now weakened, cry out to you, O Father of all, asking you not to delay in helping me. For my members, which are the members of your Son, are going to destruction and dispersal; therefore bend as swiftly as possible the eyes of your mercy to defend both me and them, lest, neglected by you, we be utterly crushed.

Likewise, the Son’s intercession to the Father for the liberation of his body, which is the Church.

XXIII. But the Son also speaks to the Father in these same words: “O Father, I was always with you, and you sent me, clothing me with flesh; and so I walked on earth, [Col. 1025A] and I fulfilled whatever you commanded me, because I am your truth. Therefore you placed all my enemies under my feet, and I stand over them because they are on the left side and do not belong to you; for your true work is at your right hand. I also work with you that which you had ordained before the beginning of days; and I judge my enemies, just as the Lord crushes the footstool of his feet.

“Therefore bend your help toward me, vindicating me against my enemies, for I, your Son, walk upon the asp and the basilisk. Therefore look also to the protection of me and of my members, because I have brought to fulfillment every work that you willed and laid upon me; and thus I am in you, and you are in me, and we are one.”

And again the same Son says to the Father: “Now remember that the fullness which was made in the beginning ought not to have withered. For at the beginning of the world you beheld the end of the world, and you did not consign it to oblivion, as you forget those who go to destruction. And the fullness of the generation of human beings, foreseen and made in the first time and in the first human being, ought not yet to have withered in failure; for it was not in you that human beings should utterly fail in their generations before the appointed time.

“And when you created the human being, you had in yourself—that is, in your ancient counsel—that your eye, namely your knowledge, foreseeing all things fully and disposing all things rightly, would never depart from what had been ordained in you: namely, that humanity should wholly perish through [Col. 1025C] any intemperance of its own, or that the world should fail, until you should see my body in its members—for the faithful are my members by your ordering—full of gems: that is, perfect in all those who trust in you through me and worship you, shining like gems in virtues.”

That at that time, when the Christian people have been brought to repentance and worn down by many afflictions for their sins, divine grace will aid them through many miracles, as it did his ancient people; and, after their enemies are subdued, it will add a very great multitude of pagans to their faith.

XXIV. Finally, when the unbelieving and horrible nations, as has been said above, have attacked the resources and possessions [Col. 1025D] of churches on every side and have striven to destroy them utterly—as vultures and hawks clutch what they hold beneath their wings and claws—and when the Christian people, worn down in every way by repentance for their sins and not terrified even by bodily death, attempt to resist them in arms, a most powerful wind will come from the north with a great mist and exceedingly dense dust. By divine judgment it will send its blasts against them, so that their throats will be filled with mist and their eyes with dust, in such a way that, laying aside their ferocity, they will be changed into the greatest astonishment.

For holy Divinity will then perform signs and miracles among the Christian people, as it also did with Moses in the pillar of cloud. And just as [Col. 1026A] Michael the archangel fought in defense of Christians against pagans, so the faithful sons of God, proceeding under his protection, will rush upon their enemies and by the power of God will become their victors: some they will deliver to death, while others they will drive out of their territories.

Therefore a very great multitude of pagans will then be added to the Christians in true faith, saying: “The God of the Christians is the true God, who has done such signs among them.” And the victors, whom God will hold in his protection, will praise God, saying: “Let us praise the Lord our God; for he has truly been magnified in us, because in his name we are victors. Thus our strength also is his praise, because through him we have overcome both his enemies and ours, [Col. 1026B] when we believed faithfully in him.”

And again they will say: “Let us also heed the Lord’s words in the Gospel. A pagan nation will rise against a Christian nation, as has happened among us. Therefore let us rebuild the cities and villages near us that have been destroyed, and make them stronger and more fortified than they had been before, lest we henceforth be crushed by evils of this kind as we are now crushed.” And they will accomplish this bravely and generously with all their strength and all their resources.

That in those days, as the Roman emperors fall away from their former strength, the empire will gradually diminish and fail in their hands; the insignia of apostolic honor will also be divided, and different masters or archbishops will be set over different places.

XXV. [Col. 1026C] But in those days the emperors of Roman dignity, declining from the strength by which they had formerly held the Roman Empire vigorously, will become weak in their glory, so that by divine judgment the empire will gradually diminish and fail in their hands. For, being slovenly, lukewarm, servile, and base in their habits, they will be useless in every respect. They will indeed wish to be honored by the people, but will not seek the people’s prosperity; therefore they will not be able to be honored and revered.

For this reason kings and princes of many peoples who had formerly been subject to the Roman Empire will separate themselves from it and will no longer endure to be subject to it. Thus the Roman Empire will be scattered into decline. For [Col. 1026D] every nation and every people will then set up for itself a king whom it will obey, saying that the extent of the Roman Empire had formerly been more a burden to it than an honor.

But after the imperial scepter has been divided in this way and cannot be restored, the mitre of apostolic honor too will be divided. Since neither rulers nor other persons of either spiritual or secular rank will then find any religious devotion in the apostolic name, they will diminish the dignity of that name. They will set over themselves, under another name, other masters and archbishops in different regions. Thus the apostolic see at that time, diminished from the breadth of honor of its former dignity, will scarcely retain under its mitre even Rome and a few places adjoining it.

These things will happen partly [Col. 1027A] through incursions of wars, and partly will be carried out by the common counsel and agreement of both spiritual and secular peoples. They will urge that every secular prince fortify and rule his kingdom and people, and that every archbishop or other spiritual teacher bind his subjects to the uprightness of discipline, lest they again be afflicted by those evils by which, through divine ordinance, they were formerly afflicted.

That then, when iniquity is again restrained and justice grows strong, the discipline of honorable conduct and the laws of ancient customs will sprout anew and be observed; there will be many prophets, and the hidden things of Scripture will be opened to the wise—while meanwhile very many heresies boil up everywhere, announcing the near coming of Antichrist.

XXVI. [Col. 1027B] Then iniquity will again lie somewhat weakened, though it will sometimes attempt to rise; but in the meantime justice will stand in its uprightness. Thus people of those days will return, in honorable conduct, to ancient customs and to the disciplines of ancient people; they will hold and observe them, as the ancients were accustomed to hold and preserve them.

Then too every king and prince, and every bishop of ecclesiastical dignity, will correct himself through another, when he sees another observing justice and living honorably; and every nation will receive correction from another when it hears that nation advancing toward good things and rising to uprightness. The air too will again be mild, the fruits of the earth useful, and people healthy and strong.

In those days there will also be many prophecies and very many wise persons, so that the secrets of the prophets and of other Scriptures will then be fully opened to the wise. Their sons and daughters will prophesy, as was foretold long ago; and this will happen in such purity of truth that aerial spirits will not then be able to mock them. In the same Spirit [Col. 1027C] they will prophesy in which the prophets formerly announced the secrets of God, and in a likeness to the teaching of the apostles, whose teaching was beyond all human understanding.

Meanwhile, so many heresies and so many foul practices, with other evils, will boil up that they will show Antichrist to be near. People of those days will say that such crimes and impurities had never before existed as will have appeared in their days. This is also indicated by the pig described in the book *Scivias*: when justice reigns at times, iniquity attacks it; and when iniquity is vigorous at times, justice confounds it, because the world never remains in one condition.

On the character of the judgments of divine power to be manifested near the end of the world, and on the fact that then the greater part of humankind, abandoning the sincerity of the Catholic faith, will turn to the son of perdition.

XXVII. Now, O human being, what you see—namely, that the aforesaid outer part of the above-mentioned wheel finally appears like a cloudy and stormy tempest, that is, near the end of that same half, where the aforesaid line is attached to the wheel—shows that [Col. 1028A] the judgments of God’s power will be cloudy and stormy in those days. For near the end of that strength in which the world now flourishes, they will find neither purity nor tranquillity of Catholic faith in the hearts of unbelieving people. This is where God’s will is joined to his power, so that it lies in God’s will when, by his power, the world and the things that are in the world shall end.

For people of that time will flee the sincerity and stability of the true faith and will depart from the true God, turning to the son of perdition. He will throw all ecclesiastical institutions into confusion and bring the greatest storms of adversity upon the faithful who resist him. For after people have suffered many tribulations in the invasions of foreign nations and in themselves through the division of the empire, [Col. 1028B] and have now, as it were, settled into peace, many heresies and many conflicts against ecclesiastical dignity will suddenly boil up again.

On the conception and birth of Antichrist; on his being filled from the beginning with a diabolical spirit, concealed and nourished in hidden places, and instructed in every magical art until he reaches manhood; and on the great disturbance and uncertainty that will then exist in worldly affairs, times, and the Church.

XXVIII. At that time an unclean woman will conceive an unclean son. For the ancient serpent who swallowed Adam will so fill him, with all his host, that no good thing will enter him or be able to exist in him. He will be nourished in hidden and various places so that people may not know him, [Col. 1028C] and will be instructed in every diabolical art. He will be concealed until the full days of his age, and will not reveal the perversities that are in him until he knows himself to be full and overflowing in every iniquity.

But from the beginning of his birth many conflicts and many things contrary to rightful orderings will boil up; burning justice will be darkened away from its uprightness, and charity will be extinguished among human beings. Bitterness and harshness will arise among them, and such great heresies will come to pass that heretics will openly and without hesitation preach their errors. There will be such doubt and uncertainty in the Catholic faith of Christians that people will be uncertain which God they should invoke.

Very many signs [Col. 1028D] will appear in the sun, moon, stars, waters, and other elements and creatures, so that, as if in a picture, they will foretell coming evils through their portents. Consequently, such sadness will seize people at that time that they will regard death as almost nothing. But those who are then perfect in the Catholic faith will wait in great contrition to see what God may wish to ordain.

And these tribulations will proceed in this manner until the son of perdition opens his mouth to contrary teaching. But when he has uttered the words of his falsehood and deceptions, heaven and earth will tremble. The chain of the necklace of justice which Paul made descend to the feet of that same Power, as has been said above, will then for the first time be moved, as though touched by a great blast of wind, because up to that time it will remain unshaken and unmoved.

For Paul strengthened his teaching so firmly through many miracles and adorned it so worthily with most profound words that it will endure thus even to the end of the world, as this same chain, descending to the feet of that Justice as if to the end of the world, also shows. Through truth, in the elevation of his spirit, he also spoke to believers concerning the second coming of the Son of God and the deadly assault of the son of perdition, saying:

Testimonies from Paul’s Epistle to the Thessalonians, announcing the end of the world, the coming, works, and judgment of Antichrist, and how they ought to be understood.

XXIX. “Do not be alarmed, either by spirit [Col. 1029B] or by word or by letter supposedly sent by us, as though the day of the Lord were at hand. Let no one deceive you in any way, for unless the falling-away comes first and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself above everything called God or worshiped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as though he were God” (II Thess. II).

The meaning of this statement must be understood thus: You who belong to God and believe his words, be cautious, lest you be shaken in your hearts by any terror—whether by spiritual deception, by wordy seduction, or by writings seeming to be truthfully directed to you—as though that day were present on which the Creator of all will lay bare the secrets of hearts. Beware also lest anyone incline you, by deceptive and phantasmal acts, into seduction on any pretext.

For unless that time comes in which ecclesiastical exaltation will be scattered and true faith trampled down—this is understood as the falling-away, which will occur in the time of the wicked son whose mother is unclean and does not know by whom she conceived—and unless he is revealed who will be the man of sin, because from his beginning he will be wholly filled with sins and thus will be a sinner, rehearsing and gathering together all sins; and unless the son of most cruel perdition is revealed, because he will remain wholly in perdition, teaching people things contrary to God—he whom the seducer of humankind will inflame as he himself first began to rage when he wished to be like God—therefore he will oppose all who worship God [Col. 1029D] and exalt himself above every creature, calling himself God and commanding that he be worshiped as though God: do not believe that the day of the Lord is at hand, namely the day on which he will judge the whole world when the world reaches its end.

Again Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, says: “For the mystery of iniquity is already at work; only let him who now restrains it continue to restrain it, until he is removed from the midst” (*ibid.*). The meaning of this statement must be understood thus: The hidden prompting is already manifest in the works of heretics, among whom the persuader of iniquity sends forth his darts, wishing to oppress the truth of the true faith. Therefore let this be the endeavor of the faithful person, with right intention and good effort: whoever holds the apostolic and truly Catholic faith, let him now hold it unshaken with firm stability, until he is removed from the middle—that which lies between his beginning and his end. For around the times of the son of perdition, faith, declining from its strength, will already be bent and weakened.

For whoever possesses ecclesiastical exaltation in God and right faith holds something great, because through it he will enter the heavenly kingdom; but whoever does not have faith holds nothing, because he will go to perdition. Thus also the human being exists in the midst of God’s power: for God was before the human being was formed, and after the human being comes bodily to an end, God endures in his power.

That the ancient enemy, who conquered the first human being by deceiving him and was conquered again through the human being Christ, will suppose that through another human being he can conquer again; and that, by God’s just permission, he will pour his whole malice into Antichrist, so that Antichrist will strive to attack the Catholic faith and destroy Christ’s teaching.

XXX. For the ancient enemy, whom the strength of divinity cast into the lake of the abyss as lead falls into raging waters, because he wished to establish iniquity when God is just and true and has no equal—for God, eternally subsisting through himself, made all things from nothing—because he had overcome the first human being, supposes that through another human being, namely Antichrist, he can accomplish what he began long ago when he attempted to fight against God.

For Antichrist, filled by the devil, when he opens his mouth to perverse teaching as has been said, will destroy everything that God established in the old [Col. 1030C] and new Law. He will declare that incest and similar acts are not sins. For he will say that it is no sin if flesh warms flesh, just as it is no sin if a person is warmed by fire. He will also assert that all precepts of chastity were made through ignorance, because when one human being is warm and another cold, they ought to be tempered mutually by warmth and cold.

Again he will say to the faithful: “Your law of continence has been established against the order of nature, namely, that a person ought not to be warm, though fire is in his breath and sets the whole human body aflame. And how can that person be cold against his own nature? On what grounds, then, should a person refrain from warming another flesh? For that man whom you call your teacher gave you a law [Col. 1030D] exceeding due measure, because he commanded you to see things in this way.

“But I say: remain in these two modes, namely warmth and cold, and warm one another. Consider that the aforesaid man gave you unjust precepts, because although he commanded that people should not warm one another, they themselves nevertheless cultivated their own nature carnally. Therefore see that you are no longer deceived by unjust teaching; for in me lies what you can or cannot do. Nor did your teacher set before you right propositions, since he wished you to be like a spirit not clothed with flesh and not acting—although the born flesh of human beings was not so created, flesh which is infused and formed through fire. For if children were not created, they would not have the capacity of acting.

“Therefore know what you are. For he who first taught you deceived you and helped you in nothing; but I fill you so that you may know yourselves and know what you are, because I created you and am wholly in all things. But he, assigning all his works to another rather than to himself, spoke nothing from himself because he could do nothing from himself; whereas I speak from myself and can do all things through myself.”

By these and similar words this unhappy son of perdition will deceive people, teaching them to live according to the fiery taste of the flesh and to fulfill every desire of their flesh. Both the old and the new Law invite human beings to chastity, provided, that is, that chastity does not exceed its measure. In this way Lucifer, through him, will deny God’s justice and, thinking that he can accomplish through him everything he begins to do, will suppose that Jordan flows into his mouth—so that baptism may thereafter no longer be named. Rather, he will cast it backward, just as he himself was cast down through baptism. Thus, by ruling in this manner, he will suppose that he has subjected such a number of people to himself that the Son of God will have only a small number of faithful by comparison with his own number.

Why Antichrist is called by the Apostle the man of sin and the son of perdition; a pertinent testimony from John’s Apocalypse, how it is to be understood; and the fact that the devil has had followers both in the Old and New Testament, deceiving some through idols and others through heretics.

XXXI. The aforesaid man of sin is called a man because he will accomplish every evil, and because all those evils [Col. 1031C] will be poured upon him. He is called the son of perdition because death and perdition will rule over him. As has been said, by seducing a multitude of peoples through perverse and most abominable means, he will draw them to himself and cause himself to be worshiped as God, as John too, describing his savagery under the image of a beast, says in the manifestation of truth: “And all who dwell on the earth worshiped it, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb” (Apoc. XIII).
